6.3.s:
adhyāya 1
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ .. 1.1 ..
6.3.d:
अध्याय 1
श्रीगणेशाय नमः .. 1.1 ..
6.3.m: Chapter 1 / Om, salutations to Gaṇeśa. (1.1)

6.3.s:
oṃ namaḥ śrīpuruṣottamāya .
oṃ namaḥ śrīnarmadāyai .
oṃ namo hariharahiraṇyagarbhebhyo namo vyāsavālmīkiśukaparāśarebhyo namo gurugobrāhmaṇebhyaḥ .
oṃ majjanmātaṅgagaṇḍacyutamadamadirāmodamattālimālaṃ snānaiḥ siddhāṅganānāṃ kucayugavigalatkuṅkumāsaṅgapiṅgam .
sāyaṃ prātarmunīnāṃ kusumacayasamācchannatīrasthavṛkṣaṃ pāyādvo narmadāmbhaḥ karimakarakarākrāntarahaṃstaraṃgam .. 1.2 ..
6.3.d:
ओं नमः श्रीपुरुषोत्तमाय .
ओं नमः श्रीनर्मदायै .
ओं नमो हरिहरहिरण्यगर्भेभ्यो नमो व्यासवाल्मीकिशुकपराशरेभ्यो नमो गुरुगोब्राह्मणेभ्यः .
ओं मज्जन्मातङ्गगण्डच्युतमदमदिरामोदमत्तालिमालं स्नानैः सिद्धाङ्गनानां कुचयुगविगलत्कुङ्कुमासङ्गपिङ्गम् .
सायं प्रातर्मुनीनां कुसुमचयसमाच्छन्नतीरस्थवृक्षं पायाद्वो नर्मदाम्भः करिमकरकराक्रान्तरहंस्तरंगम् .. 1.2 ..
6.3.m: Om, salutations to Śrī Puruṣottama. / Om, salutations to the auspicious Narmadā. / Om, salutations to Hari, Hara, and Hiraṇyagarbha; salutations to Vyāsa, Vālmīki, Śuka, and Parāśara; salutations to the spiritual teachers, cows, and brahmins. / Om. May the waters of the Narmadā protect you— / whose swarms of bees are intoxicated by the fragrance of the rut-wine dripping from the temples of bathing elephants; / which are turned yellowish-red by contact with the saffron melting from the pairs of breasts of Siddha women during their baths; / whose trees on the banks are covered with heaps of flowers by sages evening and morning; / and whose wave-currents are struck by the trunks of elephants and makaras. (1.2)

6.3.s:
ubhayataṭapuṇyatīrthā prakṣālitasakalalalokaduritaughā .
devamunimanujavandyā haratu sadā narmadā duritam .. 1.3 ..
6.3.d:
उभयतटपुण्यतीर्था प्रक्षालितसकलललोकदुरितौघा .
देवमुनिमनुजवन्द्या हरतु सदा नर्मदा दुरितम् .. 1.3 ..
6.3.m: Endowed with holy sacred fords on both banks, washing away the flood of sins of all the worlds, / praised by gods, sages, and mortals—may the Narmadā always remove sin! (1.3)

6.3.s:
nāśayatu duritamakhilaṃ bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhavacca bhuvi bhavinām .
sakalapavitri tava sudhā puṇyajalā narmadā bhavati .. 1.4 ..
6.3.d:
नाशयतु दुरितमखिलं भूतं भव्यं भवच्च भुवि भविनाम् .
सकलपवित्रि तव सुधा पुण्यजला नर्मदा भवति .. 1.4 ..
6.3.m: May she destroy all sin—past, future, and present—of living beings on earth! / O purifier of all, your holy water, Narmadā, becomes nectar. (1.4)

6.3.s:
taṭapulinaṃ śivadevā yasyā yatayo'pi kāmayante vā .
muninivahavihitasevā śivāya mama jāyatāṃ revā .. 1.5 ..
6.3.d:
तटपुलिनं शिवदेवा यस्या यतयोऽपि कामयन्ते वा .
मुनिनिवहविहितसेवा शिवाय मम जायतां रेवा .. 1.5 ..
6.3.m: Whose sandy bank even gods devoted to Śiva and ascetics desire, / and who is served by hosts of sages—may the Revā bring about my welfare! (1.5)

6.3.s:
nārāyaṇaṃ namaskṛtvā naraṃ caiva narottamam .
devīṃ sarasvatīṃ vyāsaṃ tato jayamudīrayet .. 1.6 ..
6.3.d:
नारायणं नमस्कृत्वा नरं चैव नरोत्तमम् .
देवीं सरस्वतीं व्यासं ततो जयमुदीरयेत् .. 1.6 ..
6.3.m: Having bowed down to Nārāyaṇa and Nara, the best among mortals, / and to the goddess Sarasvatī and Vyāsa, one should then recite the ‘Victory.’ (1.6)

6.3.s:
naimiṣe puṇyanilaye nānāṛṣiniṣevite .
śaunakaḥ satramāsīnaḥ sūta papraccha vistarāt .. 1.7 ..
6.3.d:
नैमिषे पुण्यनिलये नानाऋषिनिषेविते .
शौनकः सत्रमासीनः सूत पप्रच्छ विस्तरात् .. 1.7 ..
6.3.m: In Naimiṣa, the sacred abode frequented by various seers, / Śaunaka, seated at a sacrificial session, questioned Sūta at length: (1.7)

6.3.s:
manye'haṃ dharmanaipuṇyaṃ tvayi sūta sadārcitam .
puṇyāmṛtakathāvaktā vyāsasaśiṣyastvameva hi .. 1.8 ..
6.3.d:
मन्येऽहं धर्मनैपुण्यं त्वयि सूत सदार्चितम् .
पुण्यामृतकथावक्ता व्याससशिष्यस्त्वमेव हि .. 1.8 ..
6.3.m: “I consider that skill in righteousness is ever revered in you, Sūta; / for you are the narrator of holy, nectar-like stories, indeed the disciple of Vyāsa. (1.8)

6.3.s:
atastvāṃ paripṛcchāmi dharmatīrthāśrayaṃ kave .
bahūni santi tīrthāni bahuśo me śrutāni ca .. 1.9 ..
6.3.d:
अतस्त्वां परिपृच्छामि धर्मतीर्थाश्रयं कवे .
बहूनि सन्ति तीर्थानि बहुशो मे श्रुतानि च .. 1.9 ..
6.3.m: Therefore I ask you, O wise poet, concerning the refuge of righteous sacred fords. / There are many sacred fords, and many of them have been heard by me. (1.9)

6.3.s:
śrutā divyanadī brāhmī tathā viṣṇunadī mayā .
tṛtīyā na mayā kvāpi śrutā raudrī saridvarā .. 1.10 ..
6.3.d:
श्रुता दिव्यनदी ब्राह्मी तथा विष्णुनदी मया .
तृतीया न मया क्वापि श्रुता रौद्री सरिद्वरा .. 1.10 ..
6.3.m: I have heard of the divine river belonging to Brahmā, as well as the river belonging to Viṣṇu; / but nowhere have I heard of the third, the best of rivers, belonging to Rudra. (1.10)

6.3.s:
tāṃ vedagarbhāṃ vikhyātāṃ vibudhaughābhivanditām .
vada me tvaṃ mahāprājña tīrthapūgapariṣkṛtām .. 1.11 ..
6.3.d:
तां वेदगर्भां विख्यातां विबुधौघाभिवन्दिताम् .
वद मे त्वं महाप्राज्ञ तीर्थपूगपरिष्कृताम् .. 1.11 ..
6.3.m: Tell me, O greatly wise one, of her who holds the Vedas within her, who is celebrated, saluted by hosts of gods, / and adorned with an abundance of sacred fords. (1.11)

6.3.s:
kaṃ deśamāśritā revā kathaṃ śrīrudrasaṃbhavā .
tatsaṃśritāni tīrthāni yāni tāni vadasva me .. 1.12 ..
6.3.d:
कं देशमाश्रिता रेवा कथं श्रीरुद्रसंभवा .
तत्संश्रितानि तीर्थानि यानि तानि वदस्व मे .. 1.12 ..
6.3.m: Which land has the Revā resorted to? How was she born from the glorious Rudra? / And whatever sacred fords belong to her, please tell them to me.” (1.12)

6.3.s:
sūta uvāca -
sādhu pṛṣṭaṃ kulapate caritraṃ narmadāśritam .
citraṃ pavitraṃ doṣaghnaṃ śrutamuktaṃ ca sattama .. 1.13 ..
6.3.d:
सूत उवाच -
साधु पृष्टं कुलपते चरित्रं नर्मदाश्रितम् .
चित्रं पवित्रं दोषघ्नं श्रुतमुक्तं च सत्तम .. 1.13 ..
6.3.m: Sūta said: / “Well asked, O head of the clan, concerning the history pertaining to the Narmadā, / wonderful, purifying, destroying faults, as heard and proclaimed, O best of good men! (1.13)

6.3.s:
vedopavedavedāṅgādīnyabhivyasya pūritaḥ .
aṣṭādaśapurāṇānāṃ vaktā satyavatīsutaḥ .. 1.14 ..
6.3.d:
वेदोपवेदवेदाङ्गादीन्यभिव्यस्य पूरितः .
अष्टादशपुराणानां वक्ता सत्यवतीसुतः .. 1.14 ..
6.3.m: Having arranged the Vedas, Upavedas, Vedāṅgas, and the rest, the son of Satyavatī was fulfilled; / he is the proclaimer of the eighteen Purāṇas. (1.14)

6.3.s:
taṃ namaskṛtya vakṣyāmi purāṇāni yathākramam .
yeṣāmabhivyāharaṇādabhivṛddhirvṛṣāyuṣoḥ .. 1.15 ..
6.3.d:
तं नमस्कृत्य वक्ष्यामि पुराणानि यथाक्रमम् .
येषामभिव्याहरणादभिवृद्धिर्वृषायुषोः .. 1.15 ..
6.3.m: Having bowed to him, I shall speak of the Purāṇas in due order, / by whose recitation righteousness and life-span increase. (1.15)

6.3.s:
śrutiḥ smṛtiśca viprāṇāṃ cakṣuṣī parikīrtite .
kāṇastatraikayā hīno dvābhyāmandhaḥ prakīrtitaḥ .. 1.16 ..
6.3.d:
श्रुतिः स्मृतिश्च विप्राणां चक्षुषी परिकीर्तिते .
काणस्तत्रैकया हीनो द्वाभ्यामन्धः प्रकीर्तितः .. 1.16 ..
6.3.m: Revelation and tradition are declared to be the two eyes of brahmins; / a man lacking one of them is one-eyed, and lacking both, he is declared blind. (1.16)

6.3.s:
śrutismṛtipurāṇāni viduṣāṃ locanatrayam .
yastribhirnayanaiḥ paśyetso'ṃśo māheśvaro mataḥ .. 1.17 ..
6.3.d:
श्रुतिस्मृतिपुराणानि विदुषां लोचनत्रयम् .
यस्त्रिभिर्नयनैः पश्येत्सोऽंशो माहेश्वरो मतः .. 1.17 ..
6.3.m: Revelation, tradition, and the Purāṇas are the three eyes of learned men; / he who sees with three eyes is considered a portion of Maheśvara. (1.17)

6.3.s:
ātmano vedavidyā ca īśvareṇa vinirmitā .
śaunakīyā ca paurāṇī dharmaśāstrātmikā ca yā .. 1.18 ..
6.3.d:
आत्मनो वेदविद्या च ईश्वरेण विनिर्मिता .
शौनकीया च पौराणी धर्मशास्त्रात्मिका च या .. 1.18 ..
6.3.m: The knowledge of the Veda was fashioned by the Lord for oneself, / as well as the Śaunakīya, the Paurāṇic, and that which has the nature of Dharmaśāstra. (1.18)

6.3.s:
tisro vidyā imā mukhyāḥ sarvaśāstravinirṇaye .
purāṇaṃ pañcamo veda iti brahmānuśāsanam .. 1.19 ..
6.3.d:
तिस्रो विद्या इमा मुख्याः सर्वशास्त्रविनिर्णये .
पुराणं पञ्चमो वेद इति ब्रह्मानुशासनम् .. 1.19 ..
6.3.m: These three lores are primary in determining all sacred teachings. / ‘The Purāṇa is the fifth Veda’—such is the ordinance of Brahmā. (1.19)

6.3.s:
yo na veda purāṇaṃ hi na sa vedātra kiṃcana .
katamaḥ sa hi dharmo'sti kiṃ vā jñānaṃ tathāvidham .. 1.20 ..
6.3.d:
यो न वेद पुराणं हि न स वेदात्र किंचन .
कतमः स हि धर्मोऽस्ति किं वा ज्ञानं तथाविधम् .. 1.20 ..
6.3.m: He who does not know the Purāṇa knows nothing here at all. / What kind of righteousness is that, or what kind of knowledge is that— (1.20)

6.3.s:
anyadvā tatkimatrāha purāṇe yanna dṛśyate .
vedāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ pūrvaṃ purāṇe nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 1.21 ..
6.3.d:
अन्यद्वा तत्किमत्राह पुराणे यन्न दृश्यते .
वेदाः प्रतिष्ठिताः पूर्वं पुराणे नात्र संशयः .. 1.21 ..
6.3.m: or what else is there in this world that is not seen in the Purāṇa? / Formerly, the Vedas were established in the Purāṇa; there is no doubt about this. (1.21)

6.3.s:
bibhetyalpaśrutādvedo māmayaṃ pratariṣyati .
itihāsapurāṇaiśca kṛto'yaṃ niścayaḥ purā .. 1.22 ..
6.3.d:
बिभेत्यल्पश्रुताद्वेदो मामयं प्रतरिष्यति .
इतिहासपुराणैश्च कृतोऽयं निश्चयः पुरा .. 1.22 ..
6.3.m: The Veda fears one of little learning: ‘Lest this man deceive me.’ / And through the Itihāsas and Purāṇas this determination was made of old. (1.22)

6.3.s:
ātmā purāṇaṃ vedānāṃ pṛthagaṃgāni tāni ṣaṭ .
yacca dṛṣṭaṃ hi vedeṣu taddṛṣṭaṃ smṛtibhiḥ kila .. 1.23 ..
6.3.d:
आत्मा पुराणं वेदानां पृथगंगानि तानि षट् .
यच्च दृष्टं हि वेदेषु तद्दृष्टं स्मृतिभिः किल .. 1.23 ..
6.3.m: The Purāṇa is the soul of the Vedas; those six limbs are separate. / And what is seen in the Vedas is indeed seen through the Smṛtis; (1.23)

6.3.s:
ubhābhyāṃ yattu dṛṣṭaṃ hi tatpurāṇeṣu gīyate .
purāṇaṃ sarvaśāstrāṇāṃ prathamaṃ brahmaṇaḥ smṛtam .. 1.24 ..
6.3.d:
उभाभ्यां यत्तु दृष्टं हि तत्पुराणेषु गीयते .
पुराणं सर्वशास्त्राणां प्रथमं ब्रह्मणः स्मृतम् .. 1.24 ..
6.3.m: and what is seen by both is sung in the Purāṇas. / The Purāṇa is remembered as the first of all sacred teachings from Brahmā. (1.24)

6.3.s:
anantaraṃ ca vaktrebhyo vedāstasya vinirgatāḥ .
purāṇamekamevāsīdasmin kalpāntare mune .. 1.25 ..
6.3.d:
अनन्तरं च वक्त्रेभ्यो वेदास्तस्य विनिर्गताः .
पुराणमेकमेवासीदस्मिन् कल्पान्तरे मुने .. 1.25 ..
6.3.m: And afterwards the Vedas emerged from his mouths. / There was only one single Purāṇa in that other kalpa, O sage, (1.25)

6.3.s:
trivargasādhanaṃ puṇyaṃ śatakoṭipravistaram .
smṛtvā jagāda ca munīnprati devaścaturmukhaḥ .. 1.26 ..
6.3.d:
त्रिवर्गसाधनं पुण्यं शतकोटिप्रविस्तरम् .
स्मृत्वा जगाद च मुनीन्प्रति देवश्चतुर्मुखः .. 1.26 ..
6.3.m: which achieved the three aims of life, holy, extending to a billion verses. / Remembering it, the four-faced god spoke to the sages; (1.26)

6.3.s:
pravṛttiḥ sarvaśāstrāṇāṃ purāṇasyābhavattataḥ .
kālenāgrahaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā purāṇasya tato muniḥ .. 1.27 ..
6.3.d:
प्रवृत्तिः सर्वशास्त्राणां पुराणस्याभवत्ततः .
कालेनाग्रहणं दृष्ट्वा पुराणस्य ततो मुनिः .. 1.27 ..
6.3.m: from that occurred the emergence of all the sacred texts and the Purāṇa. / Then the sage, seeing the inability to grasp the Purāṇa in the course of time, (1.27)

6.3.s:
vyāsarūpaṃ vibhuḥ kṛtvā saṃharetsa yuge yuge .
aṣṭalakṣapramāṇe tu dvāpare dvāpare sadā .. 1.28 ..
6.3.d:
व्यासरूपं विभुः कृत्वा संहरेत्स युगे युगे .
अष्टलक्षप्रमाणे तु द्वापरे द्वापरे सदा .. 1.28 ..
6.3.m: the all-pervading lord, having assumed the form of Vyāsa, condenses it age after age / to the measure of eight hundred thousand verses in every Dvāpara. (1.28)

6.3.s:
tadaṣṭādaśadhā kṛtvā bhūloke'smin prabhāṣyate .
adyāpi devaloke tacchatakoṭipravistaram .. 1.29 ..
6.3.d:
तदष्टादशधा कृत्वा भूलोकेऽस्मिन् प्रभाष्यते .
अद्यापि देवलोके तच्छतकोटिप्रविस्तरम् .. 1.29 ..
6.3.m: Having made it eighteenfold, it is proclaimed in this mortal world. / Even today, in the world of the gods, it extends to a billion verses, (1.29)

6.3.s:
tathātra caturlakṣaṃ saṃkṣepeṇa niveśitam .
purāṇāni daśāṣṭau ca sāmprataṃ tadihocyate .
nāmatastāni vakṣyāmi śṛṇu tvamṛṣisattama .. 1.30 ..
6.3.d:
तथात्र चतुर्लक्षं संक्षेपेण निवेशितम् .
पुराणानि दशाष्टौ च साम्प्रतं तदिहोच्यते .
नामतस्तानि वक्ष्यामि शृणु त्वमृषिसत्तम .. 1.30 ..
6.3.m: while here it has been concisely arranged into four hundred thousand. / The eighteen Purāṇas are now stated here; / I shall speak of them by name: listen, O best of seers! (1.30)

6.3.s:
sargaśca pratisargaśca vaṃśo manvantarāṇi ca .
vaṃśānucaritaṃ caiva purāṇaṃ pañcalakṣaṇam .. 1.31 ..
6.3.d:
सर्गश्च प्रतिसर्गश्च वंशो मन्वन्तराणि च .
वंशानुचरितं चैव पुराणं पञ्चलक्षणम् .. 1.31 ..
6.3.m: Creation, secondary creation, lineage, the Manu-periods, / and the history of lineages: this is the fivefold characteristic of a Purāṇa. (1.31)

6.3.s:
brāhmaṃ purāṇaṃ tatrādyaṃ saṃhitāyāṃ vibhūṣitam .
ślokānāṃ daśasāhasraṃ nānāpuṇyakathāyutam .. 1.32 ..
6.3.d:
ब्राह्मं पुराणं तत्राद्यं संहितायां विभूषितम् .
श्लोकानां दशसाहस्रं नानापुण्यकथायुतम् .. 1.32 ..
6.3.m: Among them, the first is the Brahma Purāṇa, adorned in a collection / of ten thousand verses, containing various holy stories. (1.32)

6.3.s:
pādmaṃ ca pañcapañcāśatsahasrāṇi nigadyate .
tṛtīyaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃnāma trayoviṃśatisaṃkhyayā .. 1.33 ..
6.3.d:
पाद्मं च पञ्चपञ्चाशत्सहस्राणि निगद्यते .
तृतीयं वैष्णवंनाम त्रयोविंशतिसंख्यया .. 1.33 ..
6.3.m: The Padma Purāṇa is said to have fifty-five thousand verses; / the third, named Viṣṇu Purāṇa, has twenty-three thousand in number. (1.33)

6.3.s:
caturthaṃ vāyunā proktaṃ vāyavīyamiti smṛtam .
śivabhaktisamāyogācchaivaṃ taccāparākhyayā .. 1.34 ..
6.3.d:
चतुर्थं वायुना प्रोक्तं वायवीयमिति स्मृतम् .
शिवभक्तिसमायोगाच्छैवं तच्चापराख्यया .. 1.34 ..
6.3.m: The fourth, spoken by Vāyu, is remembered as the Vāyavīya; / on account of its union with devotion to Śiva, it is also known by another name as Śaiva. (1.34)

6.3.s:
caturviṃśatisaṃkhyātaṃ sahasrāṇi tu śaunaka .
caturbhiḥ parvabhiḥ proktaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ pañcamaṃ tathā .. 1.35 ..
6.3.d:
चतुर्विंशतिसंख्यातं सहस्राणि तु शौनक .
चतुर्भिः पर्वभिः प्रोक्तं भविष्यं पञ्चमं तथा .. 1.35 ..
6.3.m: It is counted as twenty-four thousand verses, O Śaunaka; / and the Bhaviṣya Purāṇa is proclaimed as the fifth, in four sections. (1.35)

6.3.s:
caturdaśasahasrāṇi tathā pañca śatāni tat .
mārkaṇḍaṃ navasāhasraṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ tatparikīrtitam .. 1.36 ..
6.3.d:
चतुर्दशसहस्राणि तथा पञ्च शतानि तत् .
मार्कण्डं नवसाहस्रं षष्ठं तत्परिकीर्तितम् .. 1.36 ..
6.3.m: It has fourteen thousand and five hundred verses. / The Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa is declared as the sixth, with nine thousand verses. (1.36)

6.3.s:
āgneyaṃ saptamaṃ proktaṃ sahasrāṇi tu ṣoḍaśa .
aṣṭamaṃ nāradīyaṃ tu proktaṃ vai pañcaviṃśatiḥ .. 1.37 ..
6.3.d:
आग्नेयं सप्तमं प्रोक्तं सहस्राणि तु षोडश .
अष्टमं नारदीयं तु प्रोक्तं वै पञ्चविंशतिः .. 1.37 ..
6.3.m: The Āgneya is proclaimed as the seventh, with sixteen thousand verses; / and the Nāradīya is spoken of as the eighth, with twenty-five thousand. (1.37)

6.3.s:
navamaṃ bhagavannāma bhāgadvayavibhūṣitam .
tadaṣṭādaśasāhasraṃ procyate granthasaṃkhyayā .. 1.38 ..
6.3.d:
नवमं भगवन्नाम भागद्वयविभूषितम् .
तदष्टादशसाहस्रं प्रोच्यते ग्रन्थसंख्यया .. 1.38 ..
6.3.m: The ninth is named Bhāgavata, adorned with two parts; / it is declared to have eighteen thousand in text count. (1.38)

6.3.s:
daśamaṃ brahmavaivartaṃ tāvatsaṃkhyamihocyate .
laiṅgamekādaśaṃ jñeyaṃ tathaikādaśasaṃkhyayā .. 1.39 ..
6.3.d:
दशमं ब्रह्मवैवर्तं तावत्संख्यमिहोच्यते .
लैङ्गमेकादशं ज्ञेयं तथैकादशसंख्यया .. 1.39 ..
6.3.m: The tenth, the Brahmavaivarta, is said here to be of the same count; / the Liṅga is to be known as the eleventh, having likewise eleven thousand in number. (1.39)

6.3.s:
bhāgadvayaṃ viracitaṃ talliṅgamṛṣipuṃgava .
caturviṃśatisāhasraṃ vārāhaṃ dvādaśaṃ viduḥ .. 1.40 ..
6.3.d:
भागद्वयं विरचितं तल्लिङ्गमृषिपुंगव .
चतुर्विंशतिसाहस्रं वाराहं द्वादशं विदुः .. 1.40 ..
6.3.m: That Liṅgapurāṇa is composed in two parts, O best of seers; / the Vārāha, the twelfth, they know to be twenty-four thousand [verses].

6.3.s:
vibhaktaṃ saptabhiḥ khaṇḍaiḥ skāndaṃ bhāgyavatāṃ vara .
tadekāśītisāhasraṃ saṃkhyayā vai nirūpitam .. 1.41 ..
6.3.d:
विभक्तं सप्तभिः खण्डैः स्कान्दं भाग्यवतां वर .
तदेकाशीतिसाहस्रं संख्यया वै निरूपितम् .. 1.41 ..
6.3.m: Divided into seven sections is the Skānda, O best of the fortunate; / it is indeed determined by measure to be eighty-one thousand [verses].

6.3.s:
tatastu vāmanaṃ nāma caturdaśatamaṃ smṛtam .
saṃkhyayā daśasāhasraṃ proktaṃ kulapate purā .. 1.42 ..
6.3.d:
ततस्तु वामनं नाम चतुर्दशतमं स्मृतम् .
संख्यया दशसाहस्रं प्रोक्तं कुलपते पुरा .. 1.42 ..
6.3.m: Then the fourteenth is remembered as the Vāmana by name; / in measure it was proclaimed of old, O patriarch, to be ten thousand [verses].

6.3.s:
kaurmaṃ pañcadaśaṃ prāhurbhāgadvayavibhūṣitam .
daśasaptasahasrāṇi purā sāṃkhyapate kalau .. 1.43 ..
6.3.d:
कौर्मं पञ्चदशं प्राहुर्भागद्वयविभूषितम् .
दशसप्तसहस्राणि पुरा सांख्यपते कलौ .. 1.43 ..
6.3.m: They say the Kaurma is the fifteenth, adorned with two parts; / [it contains] seventeen thousand [verses] of old in the Kali [age], O lord of Sāṅkhya.

6.3.s:
mātsyaṃ matsyena yatproktaṃ manave ṣoḍaśaṃ kramāt .
taccaturdaśasāhasraṃ saṃkhyayā vadatāṃ vara .. 1.44 ..
6.3.d:
मात्स्यं मत्स्येन यत्प्रोक्तं मनवे षोडशं क्रमात् .
तच्चतुर्दशसाहस्रं संख्यया वदतां वर .. 1.44 ..
6.3.m: The Mātsya, which was spoken by the Fish to Manu, is the sixteenth in order; / that is fourteen thousand in number, O best of speakers.

6.3.s:
gāruḍaṃ saptadaśamaṃ smṛtaṃ caikonaviṃśatiḥ .
aṣṭādaśaṃ tu brahmāṇḍaṃ bhāgadvayavibhūṣitam .. 1.45 ..
6.3.d:
गारुडं सप्तदशमं स्मृतं चैकोनविंशतिः .
अष्टादशं तु ब्रह्माण्डं भागद्वयविभूषितम् .. 1.45 ..
6.3.m: The Gāruḍa is remembered as the seventeenth, and [has] nineteen [thousand verses]; / the eighteenth is the Brahmāṇḍa, adorned with two parts,

6.3.s:
tacca dvādaśasāhasraṃ śatamaṣṭasamanvitam .
tathaivopapurāṇāni yāni coktāni vedhasā .. 1.46 ..
6.3.d:
तच्च द्वादशसाहस्रं शतमष्टसमन्वितम् .
तथैवोपपुराणानि यानि चोक्तानि वेधसा .. 1.46 ..
6.3.m: and that contains twelve thousand and eight hundred [verses]. / Likewise the secondary Purāṇas, which were also spoken by Brahmā:

6.3.s:
idaṃ brahmapurāṇasya sulabhaṃ sauramuttamam .
saṃhitādvayasaṃyuktaṃ puṇyaṃ śivakathāśrayam .. 1.47 ..
6.3.d:
इदं ब्रह्मपुराणस्य सुलभं सौरमुत्तमम् .
संहिताद्वयसंयुक्तं पुण्यं शिवकथाश्रयम् .. 1.47 ..
6.3.m: This easily obtainable, excellent Saura belongs to the Brahmapurāṇa, / joined with two collections, holy, resting upon tales of Śiva.

6.3.s:
ādyā sanatkumāroktā dvitīyā sūryabhāṣitā .
sanatkumāranāmnā hi tadvikhyātaṃ mahāmune .. 1.48 ..
6.3.d:
आद्या सनत्कुमारोक्ता द्वितीया सूर्यभाषिता .
सनत्कुमारनाम्ना हि तद्विख्यातं महामुने .. 1.48 ..
6.3.m: The first was spoken by Sanatkumāra, the second uttered by the Sun; / it is renowned indeed by the name of Sanatkumāra, O great sage.

6.3.s:
dvitīyaṃ nārasiṃhaṃ ca purāṇe pādmasaṃjñite .
śaukeyaṃ hi tṛtīyaṃ tu purāṇe vaiṣṇave matam .. 1.49 ..
6.3.d:
द्वितीयं नारसिंहं च पुराणे पाद्मसंज्ञिते .
शौकेयं हि तृतीयं तु पुराणे वैष्णवे मतम् .. 1.49 ..
6.3.m: The second is the Nārasiṃha, belonging to the Purāṇa named Padma; / the third is considered the Śaukeya, belonging to the Vaiṣṇava Purāṇa.

6.3.s:
bārhaspatyaṃ caturthaṃ ca vāyavyaṃ saṃmataṃ sadā .
daurvāsasaṃ pañcamaṃ ca smṛtaṃ bhāgavate sadā .. 1.50 ..
6.3.d:
बार्हस्पत्यं चतुर्थं च वायव्यं संमतं सदा .
दौर्वाससं पञ्चमं च स्मृतं भागवते सदा .. 1.50 ..
6.3.m: The fourth is the Bārhaspatya, always agreed to belong to the Vāyavya; / the fifth is remembered as the Daurvāsasa, always [belonging] to the Bhāgavata.

6.3.s:
bhaviṣye nāradoktaṃ ca sūribhiḥ kathitaṃ purā .
kāpilaṃ mānavaṃ caiva tathaivośanaseritam .. 1.51 ..
6.3.d:
भविष्ये नारदोक्तं च सूरिभिः कथितं पुरा .
कापिलं मानवं चैव तथैवोशनसेरितम् .. 1.51 ..
6.3.m: In the Bhaviṣya is the one spoken by Nārada, declared of old by the wise; / also the Kāpila and the Mānava, and likewise the one uttered by Uśanas,

6.3.s:
brahmāṇḍaṃ vāruṇaṃ cātha kālikādvayameva ca .
māheśvaraṃ tathā sāmbaṃ sauraṃ sarvārthasaṃcayam .. 1.52 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रह्माण्डं वारुणं चाथ कालिकाद्वयमेव च .
माहेश्वरं तथा साम्बं सौरं सर्वार्थसंचयम् .. 1.52 ..
6.3.m: the Brahmāṇḍa, and the Vāruṇa, and then the pair of Kālikās, / the Māheśvara, likewise the Sāmba, and the Saura that holds all matters,

6.3.s:
pārāśaraṃ bhāgavataṃ kaurmaṃ cāṣṭādaśaṃ kramāt .
etānyupapurāṇāni mayoktāni yathākramam .. 1.53 ..
6.3.d:
पाराशरं भागवतं कौर्मं चाष्टादशं क्रमात् .
एतान्युपपुराणानि मयोक्तानि यथाक्रमम् .. 1.53 ..
6.3.m: the Pārāśara, the Bhāgavata, and the Kaurma as the eighteenth in sequence. / These secondary Purāṇas have been spoken by me in proper order.

6.3.s:
purāṇasaṃhitāmetāṃ yaḥ paṭhedvā śṛṇoti ca .
so'nantapuṇyabhāgī syānmṛto brahmapuraṃ vrajet .. 1.54 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe purāṇasaṃhitāvarṇanāṃ prathamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
6.3.d:
पुराणसंहितामेतां यः पठेद्वा शृणोति च .
सोऽनन्तपुण्यभागी स्यान्मृतो ब्रह्मपुरं व्रजेत् .. 1.54 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे पुराणसंहितावर्णनां प्रथमोऽध्यायः ..
6.3.m:
Whoever recites or hears this collection of Purāṇas / shall possess infinite merit and, when deceased, go to the city of Brahmā.
Thus ends the first chapter, the description of the collection of Purāṇas, in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth [section], the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses].

6.3.s:
adhyāya 2
sūta uvāca .. 2.1 ..
6.3.d:
अध्याय 2
सूत उवाच .. 2.1 ..
6.3.m: Chapter 2 / Sūta said:

6.3.s:
narmadāyāstu māhātmyaṃ kṛṣṇadvaipāyano'bravīt .
tatte'haṃ sampravakṣyāmi yattvayā paripṛcchitam .. 2.2 ..
6.3.d:
नर्मदायास्तु माहात्म्यं कृष्णद्वैपायनोऽब्रवीत् .
तत्तेऽहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि यत्त्वया परिपृच्छितम् .. 2.2 ..
6.3.m: Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana declared the māhātmya of the Narmadā; / that which was asked by you, I shall relate completely to you.

6.3.s:
vistaraṃ narmadāyāstu tīrthānāṃ munisattama .
ko'nyaḥ śakto'sti vai vaktumṛte brahmāṇamīśvaram .. 2.3 ..
6.3.d:
विस्तरं नर्मदायास्तु तीर्थानां मुनिसत्तम .
कोऽन्यः शक्तोऽस्ति वै वक्तुमृते ब्रह्माणमीश्वरम् .. 2.3 ..
6.3.m: Who else indeed is capable of declaring the extent / of the sacred fords of the Narmadā, O best of sages, except Brahmā and Īśvara?

6.3.s:
etameva purā praśnaṃ pṛṣṭavāñjanamejayaḥ .
vaiśaṃpāyanasaṃjñaṃ tu śiṣyaṃ dvaipāyanasya ha .. 2.4 ..
6.3.d:
एतमेव पुरा प्रश्नं पृष्टवाञ्जनमेजयः .
वैशंपायनसंज्ञं तु शिष्यं द्वैपायनस्य ह .. 2.4 ..
6.3.m: This very question Janamejaya asked of old / to the pupil of Dvaipāyana named Vaiśaṃpāyana.

6.3.s:
revātīrthāśritaṃ puṇyaṃ tatte vakṣyāmi śaunaka .
purā pārīkṣito rājā yajñādīkṣāsu dīkṣitaḥ .. 2.5 ..
6.3.d:
रेवातीर्थाश्रितं पुण्यं तत्ते वक्ष्यामि शौनक .
पुरा पारीक्षितो राजा यज्ञादीक्षासु दीक्षितः .. 2.5 ..
6.3.m: The holy [māhātmya] concerning the sacred fords of the Revā I shall tell you, O Śaunaka. / Formerly, King [Janamejaya], the son of Parīkṣit, was consecrated in the rites of sacrifice.

6.3.s:
saṃbhṛte tu havirdravye vartamāneṣu karmasu .
āsīneṣu dvijāgryeṣu hūyamāne hutāśane .. 2.6 ..
6.3.d:
संभृते तु हविर्द्रव्ये वर्तमानेषु कर्मसु .
आसीनेषु द्विजाग्र्येषु हूयमाने हुताशने .. 2.6 ..
6.3.m: When the sacrificial materials had been gathered and the rituals were underway, / when the foremost twice-born were seated and the fire was being offered into,

6.3.s:
vartamānāsu sarvatra tathā dharmakathāsu ca .
śrūyamāṇe tathā śabde janairukte tvaharniśam .. 2.7 ..
6.3.d:
वर्तमानासु सर्वत्र तथा धर्मकथासु च .
श्रूयमाणे तथा शब्दे जनैरुक्ते त्वहर्निशम् .. 2.7 ..
6.3.m: and discourses on dharma were going on everywhere, / while day and night the words spoken by the people were heard

6.3.s:
yajñabhūmau kulapate dīyatāṃ bhujyatāmiti .
vividhāṃśca vinodānvai kurvāṇeṣu vinodiṣu .. 2.8 ..
6.3.d:
यज्ञभूमौ कुलपते दीयतां भुज्यतामिति .
विविधांश्च विनोदान्वै कुर्वाणेषु विनोदिषु .. 2.8 ..
6.3.m: in the sacrificial arena, O patriarch: 'Give!' and 'Eat!', / and while entertainers were performing various entertainments—

6.3.s:
evaṃvidhe vartamāne yajñe svargasadaḥsame .
vaiśaṃpāyanamāsīnaṃ papraccha janamejayaḥ .. 2.9 ..
6.3.d:
एवंविधे वर्तमाने यज्ञे स्वर्गसदःसमे .
वैशंपायनमासीनं पप्रच्छ जनमेजयः .. 2.9 ..
6.3.m: while such a sacrifice was taking place, resembling an assembly of heaven, / Janamejaya questioned Vaiśaṃpāyana who was seated.

6.3.s:
janamejaya uvāca -
dvaipāyanaprasādena jñānavānasi me mataḥ .
vaiśaṃpāyana tasmāttvāṃ pṛcchāmi ṛṣisannidhau .. 2.10 ..
6.3.d:
जनमेजय उवाच -
द्वैपायनप्रसादेन ज्ञानवानसि मे मतः .
वैशंपायन तस्मात्त्वां पृच्छामि ऋषिसन्निधौ .. 2.10 ..
6.3.m: Janamejaya said: / By the grace of Dvaipāyana you are endowed with knowledge, in my view; / therefore I ask you, Vaiśaṃpāyana, in the presence of the seers.

6.3.s:
brūhi me tvaṃ purāvṛttaṃ pitṛṇāṃ tīrthasevanam .
ciraṃ nānāvidhānkleśān prāptāsta iti me śrutam .. 2.11 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रूहि मे त्वं पुरावृत्तं पितृणां तीर्थसेवनम् .
चिरं नानाविधान्क्लेशान् प्राप्तास्त इति मे श्रुतम् .. 2.11 ..
6.3.m: Tell me the ancient account of the attendance at sacred fords by my ancestors; / I have heard that they suffered various afflictions for a long time.

6.3.s:
kathaṃ dyūtajitāḥ pārthā mama pūrvapitāmahāḥ .
āsamudrāṃ mahīṃ vipra bhramantastīrthalobhataḥ .. 2.12 ..
6.3.d:
कथं द्यूतजिताः पार्था मम पूर्वपितामहाः .
आसमुद्रां महीं विप्र भ्रमन्तस्तीर्थलोभतः .. 2.12 ..
6.3.m: How was it that the sons of Pṛthā, my ancient grandfathers, defeated at dice, / wandered over the earth as far as the ocean, O brahmin, out of a desire for sacred fords?

6.3.s:
kena te sahitāstāta bhūmibhāgānanekaśaḥ .
ceruḥ kathaya tatsarvaṃ sarvajño'si mato mama .. 2.13 ..
6.3.d:
केन ते सहितास्तात भूमिभागाननेकशः .
चेरुः कथय तत्सर्वं सर्वज्ञोऽसि मतो मम .. 2.13 ..
6.3.m: Accompanied by whom, dear sir, did they wander through many regions of the earth? / Relate all that; you are regarded by me as omniscient.

6.3.s: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca .. 2.14 ..
6.3.d: वैशंपायन उवाच .. 2.14 ..
6.3.m: Vaiśaṃpāyana said:

6.3.s:
kathayiṣyāmi bhūnātha yatpṛṣṭaṃ tu tvayā'nagha .
namaskṛtya virūpākṣaṃ vedavyāsaṃ mahākavim .. 2.15 ..
6.3.d:
कथयिष्यामि भूनाथ यत्पृष्टं तु त्वयाऽनघ .
नमस्कृत्य विरूपाक्षं वेदव्यासं महाकविम् .. 2.15 ..
6.3.m: I shall relate, O lord of the earth, what has been asked by you, O sinless one, / having bowed down to Virūpākṣa and to the great poet Veda Vyāsa.

6.3.s:
pitāmahāstu te pañca pāṇḍavāḥ saha kṛṣṇayā .
uṣitvā brāhmaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ kāmyake vana uttame .. 2.16 ..
6.3.d:
पितामहास्तु ते पञ्च पाण्डवाः सह कृष्णया .
उषित्वा ब्राह्मणैः सार्धं काम्यके वन उत्तमे .. 2.16 ..
6.3.m: Your grandfathers, the five Pāṇḍavas together with Kṛṣṇā, / dwelt with brahmins in the excellent Kāmyaka forest.

6.3.s:
pradhānoddālake tatra kaśyapo'tha mahāmatiḥ .
vibhāṇḍakaśca rājendra muruścaiva mahāmuniḥ .. 2.17 ..
6.3.d:
प्रधानोद्दालके तत्र कश्यपोऽथ महामतिः .
विभाण्डकश्च राजेन्द्र मुरुश्चैव महामुनिः .. 2.17 ..
6.3.m: Chief among them was Uddālaka, then the broad-minded Kaśyapa, / Vibhāṇḍaka, O best of kings, and the great sage Muru,

6.3.s:
pulastyo lomaśaścaiva tathānye putrapautriṇaḥ .
snātvā niḥśeṣatīrtheṣu gatāste vindhyaparvatam .. 2.18 ..
6.3.d:
पुलस्त्यो लोमशश्चैव तथान्ये पुत्रपौत्रिणः .
स्नात्वा निःशेषतीर्थेषु गतास्ते विन्ध्यपर्वतम् .. 2.18 ..
6.3.m: Pulastya, and Lomaśa, and likewise others with sons and grandsons; / having bathed at all the sacred fords, they went to the Vindhya mountain.

6.3.s:
te ca tatrāśramaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvairvṛkṣaiḥ samākulam .
campakaiḥ karṇakāraiśca punnāgairnāgakesaraiḥ .. 2.19 ..
6.3.d:
ते च तत्राश्रमं पुण्यं सर्वैर्वृक्षैः समाकुलम् .
चम्पकैः कर्णकारैश्च पुन्नागैर्नागकेसरैः .. 2.19 ..
6.3.m: And there [they saw] a holy hermitage filled with every kind of tree: / campakas, karṇikāras, punnāgas, and nāgakesaras,

6.3.s:
bakulaiḥ kovidāraiśca dāḍimairupaśobhitam .
puṣpitairarjunaiścaiva bilvapāṭalaketakaiḥ .. 2.20 ..
6.3.d:
बकुलैः कोविदारैश्च दाडिमैरुपशोभितम् .
पुष्पितैरर्जुनैश्चैव बिल्वपाटलकेतकैः .. 2.20 ..
6.3.m: adorned with bakulas, kovidāras, and pomegranates, / with flowering arjunas, bilvas, pāṭalas, and ketakas,

6.3.s:
kadambāmramadhūkaiśca nimbajambīratindukaiḥ .
nālikeraiḥ kapitthaiśca kharjūrapanasaistathā .. 2.21 ..
6.3.d:
कदम्बाम्रमधूकैश्च निम्बजम्बीरतिन्दुकैः .
नालिकेरैः कपित्थैश्च खर्जूरपनसैस्तथा .. 2.21 ..
6.3.m: with kadambas, mangoes, and madhūkas, nimba, jambīra, and tinduka trees, / with coconuts, kapitthas, dates, and jackfruits,

6.3.s:
nānādrumalatākīrṇaṃ nānāvallībhirāvṛtam .
sapuṣpaṃ phalitaṃ kāntaṃ vanaṃ caitrarathaṃ yathā .. 2.22 ..
6.3.d:
नानाद्रुमलताकीर्णं नानावल्लीभिरावृतम् .
सपुष्पं फलितं कान्तं वनं चैत्ररथं यथा .. 2.22 ..
6.3.m: overgrown with various trees and creepers, covered with manifold climbing plants, / flowering, fruitful, charming like the Caitraratha grove,

6.3.s:
jalāśrayaistu vipulaiḥ padminīkhaṇḍamaṇḍitam .
sitotpalaiśca saṃchannaṃ nīlapītaiḥ sitāruṇaiḥ .. 2.23 ..
6.3.d:
जलाश्रयैस्तु विपुलैः पद्मिनीखण्डमण्डितम् .
सितोत्पलैश्च संछन्नं नीलपीतैः सितारुणैः .. 2.23 ..
6.3.m: adorned with groups of lotuses in expansive bodies of water, / and veiled with white water-lilies, blue, yellow, white, and red,

6.3.s:
haṃsakāraṇḍavākīrṇaṃ cakravākopaśobhitam .
āḍīkākabalākābhiḥ sevitaṃ kokilādibhiḥ .. 2.24 ..
6.3.d:
हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णं चक्रवाकोपशोभितम् .
आडीकाकबलाकाभिः सेवितं कोकिलादिभिः .. 2.24 ..
6.3.m: crowded with swans and kāraṇḍavas, graced with cakravākas, / frequented by water-fowls, storks, cranes, cuckoos, and others,

6.3.s:
siṃhairvyāghrairvarāhaiśca gajaiścaiva mahotkaṭaiḥ .
mahiṣaiśca mahākāyaiḥ kuraṅgaiścitrakaiḥ śaśaiḥ .. 2.25 ..
6.3.d:
सिंहैर्व्याघ्रैर्वराहैश्च गजैश्चैव महोत्कटैः .
महिषैश्च महाकायैः कुरङ्गैश्चित्रकैः शशैः .. 2.25 ..
6.3.m: with lions, tigers, boars, and fiercely haughty elephants, / with giant buffaloes, deer, leopards, and hares,

6.3.s:
gaṇḍakaiścaiva khaḍgaiśca gomāyusurabhī yutam .
sāraṅgairmallakaiścaiva dvipadaiśca catuṣpadaiḥ .. 2.26 ..
6.3.d:
गण्डकैश्चैव खड्गैश्च गोमायुसुरभी युतम् .
सारङ्गैर्मल्लकैश्चैव द्विपदैश्च चतुष्पदैः .. 2.26 ..
6.3.m: with rhinoceroses, jackals, and cattle, / with sāraṅga deer, mallakas, two-footed and four-footed beasts,

6.3.s:
tathāca kokilākīrṇaṃ manaḥkāntaṃ suśobhitam .
jīvaṃjīvakasaṃghaiśca nānāpakṣisamāyutam .. 2.27 ..
6.3.d:
तथाच कोकिलाकीर्णं मनःकान्तं सुशोभितम् .
जीवंजीवकसंघैश्च नानापक्षिसमायुतम् .. 2.27 ..
6.3.m: and also crowded with cuckoos, captivating the mind, exceedingly fair, / with flocks of jīvañjīvaka pheasants, accompanied by manifold birds,

6.3.s:
duḥkhaśokavinirmuktaṃ sattvotkaṭamanoramam .
kṣuttṛṣārahitaṃ kāntaṃ sarvavyādhivivarjitam .. 2.28 ..
6.3.d:
दुःखशोकविनिर्मुक्तं सत्त्वोत्कटमनोरमम् .
क्षुत्तृषारहितं कान्तं सर्वव्याधिविवर्जितम् .. 2.28 ..
6.3.m: free from sorrow and distress, enchanting with noble creatures, / devoid of hunger and thirst, lovely, entirely free from disease.

6.3.s:
siṃhīstanaṃ pibantyatra kuraṃgāḥ snehasaṃyutam .
mārjāramūṣakau cobhāvavalehata unmukhau .. 2.29 ..
6.3.d:
सिंहीस्तनं पिबन्त्यत्र कुरंगाः स्नेहसंयुतम् .
मार्जारमूषकौ चोभाववलेहत उन्मुखौ .. 2.29 ..
6.3.m: There deer drink affectionately from the lioness's teat, / and a cat and a mouse both look up and lick each other.

6.3.s:
pañcāsyāḥ potakebhāśca bhoginastu kalāpinaḥ .
dṛṣṭvā tadvipinaṃ ramyaṃ praviṣṭāḥ pāṇḍunandanāḥ .. 2.30 ..
6.3.d:
पञ्चास्याः पोतकेभाश्च भोगिनस्तु कलापिनः .
दृष्ट्वा तद्विपिनं रम्यं प्रविष्टाः पाण्डुनन्दनाः .. 2.30 ..
6.3.m: Lions with elephant calves, and snakes with peacocks— / having seen that delightful forest, the sons of Pāṇḍu entered.

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍaṃ dṛṣṭavāṃstatra taruṇādityasannibham .
ṛṣibhiḥ sevyamānaṃ tu nānāśāstraviśāradaiḥ .. 2.31 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डं दृष्टवांस्तत्र तरुणादित्यसन्निभम् .
ऋषिभिः सेव्यमानं तु नानाशास्त्रविशारदैः .. 2.31 ..
6.3.m: There he saw Mārkaṇḍa resembling the morning sun, / attended upon by seers skilled in various sacred scriptures,

6.3.s:
kulīnaiḥ sattvasampannaiḥ śaucācārasamanvitaiḥ .
dhīsaṃgataiḥ kṣamāyuktaistrisaṃdhyaṃ japatatparaiḥ .. 2.32 ..
6.3.d:
कुलीनैः सत्त्वसम्पन्नैः शौचाचारसमन्वितैः .
धीसंगतैः क्षमायुक्तैस्त्रिसंध्यं जपतत्परैः .. 2.32 ..
6.3.m: born of noble families, endowed with pure essence, accompanied by purity and good conduct, / endowed with wisdom, possessed of forbearance, devoted to chanting during the three junctions of the day,

6.3.s:
ṛgyajuḥsāmavihitairmantrairhomaparāyaṇaiḥ .
kecitpañcāgnimadhyasthāḥ kecidekāntasaṃsthitāḥ .. 2.33 ..
6.3.d:
ऋग्यजुःसामविहितैर्मन्त्रैर्होमपरायणैः .
केचित्पञ्चाग्निमध्यस्थाः केचिदेकान्तसंस्थिताः .. 2.33 ..
6.3.m: devoted to oblations with the mantras prescribed in the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma Vedas; / some standing in the midst of five fires, some remaining in solitude,

6.3.s:
ūrdhvabāhunirālambā ādityabhramaṇāḥ pare .
sāyaṃprātarbhujaścānye ekāhārāstathā pare .. 2.34 ..
6.3.d:
ऊर्ध्वबाहुनिरालम्बा आदित्यभ्रमणाः परे .
सायंप्रातर्भुजश्चान्ये एकाहारास्तथा परे .. 2.34 ..
6.3.m: with raised arms without support, others following the movement of the sun, / others eating in the evening and morning, and others eating once a day,

6.3.s:
dvādaśāhāttathā cānye anye māsārdhabhojanāḥ .
darśe darśe tathā cānye anye śaivālabhojanāḥ .. 2.35 ..
6.3.d:
द्वादशाहात्तथा चान्ये अन्ये मासार्धभोजनाः .
दर्शे दर्शे तथा चान्ये अन्ये शैवालभोजनाः .. 2.35 ..
6.3.m: and others [eating] after twelve days, others taking food every half-month, / others at every new moon, and others subsisting on moss.

6.3.s:
piṇyākamapare'bhujan kecitpālāśabhojanāḥ .
apare niyatāhārā vāyubhakṣyāmbubhojanāḥ .. 2.36 ..
6.3.d:
पिण्याकमपरेऽभुजन् केचित्पालाशभोजनाः .
अपरे नियताहारा वायुभक्ष्याम्बुभोजनाः .. 2.36 ..
6.3.m: Others ate oilcake, some subsisted on palāśa leaves, / others of restrained diet, feeding on wind or consuming water—

6.3.s:
evaṃbhūtaistathā vṛddhaiḥ sevyate munipuṃgavaiḥ .
tato dharmasutaḥ śrīmānāśramaṃ taṃ praviśya saḥ .. 2.37 ..
6.3.d:
एवंभूतैस्तथा वृद्धैः सेव्यते मुनिपुंगवैः .
ततो धर्मसुतः श्रीमानाश्रमं तं प्रविश्य सः .. 2.37 ..
6.3.m: by such eminent aged sages he was attended upon. / Then that glorious son of Dharma entered that hermitage;

6.3.s:
dṛṣṭvā munivaraṃ śāntaṃ dhyāyamānaṃ paraṃ padam .
prādakṣiṇyena sahasā daṇḍavatpatito'grataḥ .. 2.38 ..
6.3.d:
दृष्ट्वा मुनिवरं शान्तं ध्यायमानं परं पदम् .
प्रादक्षिण्येन सहसा दण्डवत्पतितोऽग्रतः .. 2.38 ..
6.3.m: having seen that best of sages, tranquil, meditating on the supreme abode, / he circumambulated him clockwise and quickly fell down like a staff before him.

6.3.s:
bhaktyānupatitaṃ dṛṣṭvā cirādādāya locanam .
ko bhavānityuvācedaṃ dharmaṃ dhīmānapṛcchata .. 2.39 ..
6.3.d:
भक्त्यानुपतितं दृष्ट्वा चिरादादाय लोचनम् .
को भवानित्युवाचेदं धर्मं धीमानपृच्छत .. 2.39 ..
6.3.m: Seeing him fallen down in devotion, [the sage] opened his eyes after a long time. / 'Who are you?' he said; the wise one questioned Dharma's son:

6.3.s:
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā dārakastatsamīpagaḥ .
āhāyaṃ dharmarājaste darśanārthaṃ samāgataḥ .. 2.40 ..
6.3.d:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा दारकस्तत्समीपगः .
आहायं धर्मराजस्ते दर्शनार्थं समागतः .. 2.40 ..
6.3.m: Hearing his word, a boy standing near him / said: 'This is the King of Dharma, who has arrived for your darśana.'

6.3.s:
tacchrutvādārakeṇoktaṃ vacanaṃ prāha sādaraḥ .
ehyehi vatsavatseti kiṃcitsthānāccalanmuniḥ .
taṃ tu snehādupāghrāya āsane upaveśayat .. 2.41 ..
6.3.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वादारकेणोक्तं वचनं प्राह सादरः .
एह्येहि वत्सवत्सेति किंचित्स्थानाच्चलन्मुनिः .
तं तु स्नेहादुपाघ्राय आसने उपवेशयत् .. 2.41 ..
6.3.m: Hearing the word spoken by the boy, he said with respect, / 'Come, come, child, child!' moving slightly from his seat; / smelling him affectionately, the sage had him seated on a seat.

6.3.s:
upaviṣṭe sabhāyāṃ tu pūjāṃ kṛtvā yathāvidhi .
vanyairdhānyaiḥ phalairmūlai rasaiścaiva pṛthagvidhaiḥ .. 2.42 ..
6.3.d:
उपविष्टे सभायां तु पूजां कृत्वा यथाविधि .
वन्यैर्धान्यैः फलैर्मूलै रसैश्चैव पृथग्विधैः .. 2.42 ..
6.3.m: When he was seated in the assembly, after performing worship according to the rule / with wild grains, fruits, roots, and various kinds of juices,

6.3.s:
pāṇḍavā brāhmaṇaiḥ sārddhaṃ yathāyogyaṃ prapūjitāḥ .
muhūrtādatha viśramya dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ .. 2.43 ..
6.3.d:
पाण्डवा ब्राह्मणैः सार्द्धं यथायोग्यं प्रपूजिताः .
मुहूर्तादथ विश्रम्य धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः .. 2.43 ..
6.3.m: the Pāṇḍavas together with the brahmins were appropriately honored. / Then, having rested for a moment, Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma,

6.3.s:
pṛcchati sma muniśreṣṭhaṃ kautūhalasamanvitaḥ .
bhagavansarvalokānāṃ dīrghāyustvaṃ mato mama .. 2.44 ..
6.3.d:
पृच्छति स्म मुनिश्रेष्ठं कौतूहलसमन्वितः .
भगवन्सर्वलोकानां दीर्घायुस्त्वं मतो मम .. 2.44 ..
6.3.m: asked that best of sages, filled with curiosity: / 'O Lord, among all the worlds you are considered long-lived by me;

6.3.s:
saptakalpānaśeṣeṇa kathayasva mamānagha .
kalpakṣaye'pi lokasya sthāvarasyetarasya ca .. 2.45 ..
6.3.d:
सप्तकल्पानशेषेण कथयस्व ममानघ .
कल्पक्षयेऽपि लोकस्य स्थावरस्येतरस्य च .. 2.45 ..
6.3.m: tell me completely of the seven aeons, O sinless one. / Even at the end of an aeon, of the world, both motionless and moving,

6.3.s:
na vinaṣṭo'si viprendra kathaṃ vā kena hetunā .
gaṅgādyāḥ saritaḥ sarvāḥ samudrāntāśca yā mune .. 2.46 ..
6.3.d:
न विनष्टोऽसि विप्रेन्द्र कथं वा केन हेतुना .
गङ्गाद्याः सरितः सर्वाः समुद्रान्ताश्च या मुने .. 2.46 ..
6.3.m: you were not destroyed, O foremost among vipras! How or for what reason? / All the rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā that reach the sea, O sage—

6.3.s:
tāsāṃ madhye sthitāḥ kāḥ svitkāścaiva pralayaṃ gatāḥ .
kā nu puṇyajalā nityaṃ kānu na kṣayamāgatā .. 2.47 ..
6.3.d:
तासां मध्ये स्थिताः काः स्वित्काश्चैव प्रलयं गताः .
का नु पुण्यजला नित्यं कानु न क्षयमागता .. 2.47 ..
6.3.m: among them, which remained and which went to dissolution? / Which indeed has sacred waters eternally, and which did not meet destruction?

6.3.s:
etatkathaya me tāta prasannenāntarātmanā .
śrotumicchāmyaśeṣeṇa ṛṣibhiḥ saha bāndhavaiḥ .. 2.48 ..
6.3.d:
एतत्कथय मे तात प्रसन्नेनान्तरात्मना .
श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यशेषेण ऋषिभिः सह बान्धवैः .. 2.48 ..
6.3.m: Tell me this, O father, with a gracious inner self; / I wish to hear it completely, along with the seers and my kinsmen.'

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
sādhusādhu mahāprājña dharmaputra yudhiṣṭhira .
kathayāmi yathā nyāyaṃ yatpṛcchasi mamānagha .. 2.49 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
साधुसाधु महाप्राज्ञ धर्मपुत्र युधिष्ठिर .
कथयामि यथा न्यायं यत्पृच्छसि ममानघ .. 2.49 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / 'Well said, well said, O wise one, O Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Dharma! / I shall tell according to the rule what you ask me, O sinless one.

6.3.s:
sarvapāpaharaṃ puṇyaṃ purāṇaṃ rudrabhāṣitam .
yaḥ śṛṇoti naro bhaktyā tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu .. 2.50 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वपापहरं पुण्यं पुराणं रुद्रभाषितम् .
यः शृणोति नरो भक्त्या तस्य पुण्यफलं शृणु .. 2.50 ..
6.3.m: The sacred Purāṇa spoken by Rudra, which destroys all sins— / hear the holy fruit of the man who listens to it with devotion:

6.3.s:
aśvamedha sahasreṇa vājapeyaśatena ca .
tatphalaṃ samavāpnoti rājannāstyatra saṃśayaḥ .. 2.51 ..
6.3.d:
अश्वमेध सहस्रेण वाजपेयशतेन च .
तत्फलं समवाप्नोति राजन्नास्त्यत्र संशयः .. 2.51 ..
6.3.m: with a thousand horse-sacrifices and a hundred vājapeya sacrifices, / he obtains that same fruit, O king; there is no doubt about this.

6.3.s:
brahmaghnaśca surāpī ca steyī goghnaśca yo naraḥ .
mucyate sarvapāpebhyo rudrasya vacanaṃ yathā .. 2.52 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रह्मघ्नश्च सुरापी च स्तेयी गोघ्नश्च यो नरः .
मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो रुद्रस्य वचनं यथा .. 2.52 ..
6.3.m: The killer of a brahmin, the drinker of liquor, the thief, and the man who slays a cow / is freed from all sins, according to the word of Rudra.

6.3.s:
gaṅgā tu saritāṃ śreṣṭhā tathā caiva sarasvatī .
kāverī devikā caiva sindhuḥ sālakuṭī tathā .. 2.53 ..
6.3.d:
गङ्गा तु सरितां श्रेष्ठा तथा चैव सरस्वती .
कावेरी देविका चैव सिन्धुः सालकुटी तथा .. 2.53 ..
6.3.m: The Gaṅgā is the foremost among rivers, and likewise the Sarasvatī, / the Kāverī, the Devikā, the Sindhu, and the Sālakuṭī,

6.3.s:
sarayūḥ śatarudrā ca mahī carmilayā saha .
godāvarī tathā puṇyā tathaiva yamunā nadī .. 2.54 ..
6.3.d:
सरयूः शतरुद्रा च मही चर्मिलया सह .
गोदावरी तथा पुण्या तथैव यमुना नदी .. 2.54 ..
6.3.m: the Sarayū, the Śatarudrā, the Mahī along with the Carmilā, / and the sacred Godāvarī, and likewise the river Yamunā,

6.3.s:
payoṣṇī ca śatadruśca tathā dharmanadī śubhā .
etāścānyāśca saritaḥ sarvapāpaharāḥ smṛtāḥ .. 2.55 ..
6.3.d:
पयोष्णी च शतद्रुश्च तथा धर्मनदी शुभा .
एताश्चान्याश्च सरितः सर्वपापहराः स्मृताः .. 2.55 ..
6.3.m: the Payoṣṇī, the Śatadru, and the auspicious Dharmanadī— / these and other rivers are traditionally remembered as destroyers of all sins.

6.3.s:
kiṃ tu te kāraṇaṃ tāta vakṣyāmi nṛpasattama .
samudrāḥ saritaḥ sarvāḥ kalpe kalpe kṣayaṃ gatāḥ .. 2.56 ..
6.3.d:
किं तु ते कारणं तात वक्ष्यामि नृपसत्तम .
समुद्राः सरितः सर्वाः कल्पे कल्पे क्षयं गताः .. 2.56 ..
6.3.m: However, I shall tell you the reason, O father, O best among kings: / the oceans and all the rivers met destruction aeon after aeon.

6.3.s:
saptakalpakṣaye kṣīṇe na mṛtā tena narmadā .
narmadaikaiva rājendra paraṃ tiṣṭhetsaridvarā .. 2.57 ..
6.3.d:
सप्तकल्पक्षये क्षीणे न मृता तेन नर्मदा .
नर्मदैकैव राजेन्द्र परं तिष्ठेत्सरिद्वरा .. 2.57 ..
6.3.m: When the dissolution of seven aeons was spent, the Narmadā was not perished thereby; / the Narmadā alone, O king of kings, the best of rivers, would stand supreme,

6.3.s:
toyapūrṇā mahābhāga munisaṃghairabhiṣṭutā .
gaṃgādyāḥ saritaścānyāḥ kalpe kalpe kṣayaṃ gatāḥ .. 2.58 ..
6.3.d:
तोयपूर्णा महाभाग मुनिसंघैरभिष्टुता .
गंगाद्याः सरितश्चान्याः कल्पे कल्पे क्षयं गताः .. 2.58 ..
6.3.m: full of water, O highly fortunate one, praised by multitudes of sages; / whereas the other rivers, beginning with the Gaṅgā, met destruction aeon after aeon.

6.3.s:
eṣā devī purā dṛṣṭā tena vakṣyāmi te'nagha .. 2.59 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe revāmāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma dvitīyo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 3
6.3.d:
एषा देवी पुरा दृष्टा तेन वक्ष्यामि तेऽनघ .. 2.59 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे रेवामाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम द्वितीयोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 3
6.3.m:
This goddess was seen in ancient times; therefore I shall tell it to you, O sinless one.'
Thus ends the second chapter, titled 'Description of the Revāmāhātmya', in the Revākhaṇḍa of the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].
Chapter 3

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
saptakalpakṣayā ghorāstvayā dṛṣṭā mahāmune .
na cāpīhāsti bhagavandīrghāyuriha kaścana .. 3.1 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
सप्तकल्पक्षया घोरास्त्वया दृष्टा महामुने .
न चापीहास्ति भगवन्दीर्घायुरिह कश्चन .. 3.1 ..
6.3.m:
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
'The terrible destructions of seven kalpas were seen by you, O great sage,
and here, O venerable one, no one possesses such long life. 3.1

6.3.s:
tvayā hyekārṇave suptaḥ padmanābhaḥ surārihā .
dṛṣṭaḥ sahasracaraṇaḥ sahasranayanodaraḥ .. 3.2 ..
6.3.d:
त्वया ह्येकार्णवे सुप्तः पद्मनाभः सुरारिहा .
दृष्टः सहस्रचरणः सहस्रनयनोदरः .. 3.2 ..
6.3.m:
For sleeping in the single ocean, Padmanābha, the slayer of the foes of the gods,
was seen by you, having a thousand feet and a thousand eyes and bellies. 3.2

6.3.s:
tvaṃ kilānugrahāttasya dahyamāne carācare .
na kṣayaṃ samanuprāpto varadānānmahātmanaḥ .. 3.3 ..
6.3.d:
त्वं किलानुग्रहात्तस्य दह्यमाने चराचरे .
न क्षयं समनुप्राप्तो वरदानान्महात्मनः .. 3.3 ..
6.3.m:
Indeed, by his grace, when the moving and unmoving universe was burning,
you did not undergo destruction, because of the granting of a boon by the great-souled one. 3.3

6.3.s:
kiṃ tvayāścaryabhūtaṃ hi dṛṣṭaṃ ca bhramatānagha .
etadācakṣva bhagavanparaṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me .. 3.4 ..
6.3.d:
किं त्वयाश्चर्यभूतं हि दृष्टं च भ्रमतानघ .
एतदाचक्ष्व भगवन्परं कौतूहलं हि मे .. 3.4 ..
6.3.m:
What wonderful thing was seen by you, O sinless one, while wandering?
Tell this, O venerable one, for great is my curiosity. 3.4

6.3.s:
samprāpte ca mahāghore yugasyānte mahākṣaye .
anāvṛṣṭihate loke purā varṣaśatādhike .. 3.5 ..
6.3.d:
सम्प्राप्ते च महाघोरे युगस्यान्ते महाक्षये .
अनावृष्टिहते लोके पुरा वर्षशताधिके .. 3.5 ..
6.3.m:
When the exceedingly terrible destruction at the end of the yuga arrived,
the world having been struck by drought formerly for more than a hundred years...' 3.5

6.3.s:
auṣadhīnāṃ kṣaye ghore devadānavavarjite .
nirvīrye nirvaṣaṭkāre kalinā dūṣite bhṛśam .. 3.6 ..
6.3.d:
औषधीनां क्षये घोरे देवदानववर्जिते .
निर्वीर्ये निर्वषट्कारे कलिना दूषिते भृशम् .. 3.6 ..
6.3.m: When medicinal plants were terribly destroyed, when gods and Dānavas were gone, / devoid of vitality, devoid of the vaṣaṭ-call, utterly corrupted by Kali,

6.3.s:
saritsarastaḍāgeṣu palvalopavaneṣu ca .
saṃśuṣkeṣu tadā brahmannirākāre yugakṣaye .. 3.7 ..
6.3.d:
सरित्सरस्तडागेषु पल्वलोपवनेषु च .
संशुष्केषु तदा ब्रह्मन्निराकारे युगक्षये .. 3.7 ..
6.3.m: when rivers, lakes, ponds, pools, and groves / were completely dried up, O brāhmaṇa, during that formless destruction of the age,

6.3.s:
janaṃ prāpte maharloke brahmakṣatraviśādayaḥ .
ṛṣayaśca mahātmāno divyatejaḥsamanvitāḥ .. 3.8 ..
6.3.d:
जनं प्राप्ते महर्लोके ब्रह्मक्षत्रविशादयः .
ऋषयश्च महात्मानो दिव्यतेजःसमन्विताः .. 3.8 ..
6.3.m: when brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and others, / and the great-souled seers endowed with divine radiance reached Janaloka from Maharloka,

6.3.s:
sthitāni kāni bhūtāni gatānyeva mahāmune .
etatsarvaṃ mahābhāga kathayasva pṛthakpṛthak .. 3.9 ..
6.3.d:
स्थितानि कानि भूतानि गतान्येव महामुने .
एतत्सर्वं महाभाग कथयस्व पृथक्पृथक् .. 3.9 ..
6.3.m: which beings remained, and which truly perished, O great sage? / Tell all of this separately, O fortunate one!

6.3.s:
bhūtāni kāni viprendra kathaṃ siddhimavāpnuyāt .
brahmaviṣṇvindrarudrāṇāṃ kāle prāpte sudāruṇe .. 3.10 ..
6.3.d:
भूतानि कानि विप्रेन्द्र कथं सिद्धिमवाप्नुयात् .
ब्रह्मविष्ण्विन्द्ररुद्राणां काले प्राप्ते सुदारुणे .. 3.10 ..
6.3.m: Which beings, O best of vipras, and how would they attain perfection / when the dread time comes for Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Indra, and the Rudras?

6.3.s:
evamuktastataḥ so'tha dharmarājena dhīmatā .
mārkaṇḍaḥ pratyuvācedamṛṣisaṃghaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ .. 3.11 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्तस्ततः सोऽथ धर्मराजेन धीमता .
मार्कण्डः प्रत्युवाचेदमृषिसंघैः समावृतः .. 3.11 ..
6.3.m: Thus addressed by the wise Dharmarāja, / Mārkaṇḍeya, surrounded by multitudes of seers, replied then as follows:

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
śṛṇvantu ṛṣayaḥ sarve tvayā saha nareśvara .
mahatpurāṇaṃ pūrvoktaṃ śaṃbhunā vāyudaivate .. 3.12 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
शृण्वन्तु ऋषयः सर्वे त्वया सह नरेश्वर .
महत्पुराणं पूर्वोक्तं शंभुना वायुदैवते .. 3.12 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / May all the seers hear along with you, O lord of men, / the great Purāṇa formerly spoken by Śambhu to the deity Vāyu.

6.3.s:
vāyoḥ sakāśātskandena śrutametatpurātanam .
vasiṣṭhaḥ śrutavāṃstasmātparāśarastataḥ param .. 3.13 ..
6.3.d:
वायोः सकाशात्स्कन्देन श्रुतमेतत्पुरातनम् .
वसिष्ठः श्रुतवांस्तस्मात्पराशरस्ततः परम् .. 3.13 ..
6.3.m: From Vāyu, this ancient text was heard by Skanda; / Vasiṣṭha heard it from him, and Parāśara after that.

6.3.s:
tasmācca jātūkarṇyena tasmāccaiva maharṣibhiḥ .
evaṃ paramparāproktaṃ śatasaṃkhyairdvijottamaiḥ .. 3.14 ..
6.3.d:
तस्माच्च जातूकर्ण्येन तस्माच्चैव महर्षिभिः .
एवं परम्पराप्रोक्तं शतसंख्यैर्द्विजोत्तमैः .. 3.14 ..
6.3.m: And from him by Jātūkarṇya, and from him by the great seers; / thus it was spoken in unbroken succession by hundreds of best twice-born.

6.3.s:
saṃhitā śatasāhasrī puroktā śaṃbhunā kila .
āloḍya sarvaśāstrāṇi vadārthaṃ tattvataḥ purā .. 3.15 ..
6.3.d:
संहिता शतसाहस्री पुरोक्ता शंभुना किल .
आलोड्य सर्वशास्त्राणि वदार्थं तत्त्वतः पुरा .. 3.15 ..
6.3.m: A compilation of one hundred thousand verses was spoken of old by Śambhu, / having churned all scriptures to explain the truth in ancient times.

6.3.s:
yugarūpeṇa sā paścāccaturdhā viniyojitā .
madaprajñānusāreṇa narāṇāṃ tu maharṣibhiḥ .. 3.16 ..
6.3.d:
युगरूपेण सा पश्चाच्चतुर्धा विनियोजिता .
मदप्रज्ञानुसारेण नराणां तु महर्षिभिः .. 3.16 ..
6.3.m: Afterwards it was arranged fourfold according to the ages / by the great seers, according to the diminished intellect of men.

6.3.s:
ārādhya paśubhartāraṃ mayā pūrvaṃ maheśvaram .
purāṇaṃ śrutametaddhi tatte vakṣyāmyaśeṣataḥ .. 3.17 ..
6.3.d:
आराध्य पशुभर्तारं मया पूर्वं महेश्वरम् .
पुराणं श्रुतमेतद्धि तत्ते वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः .. 3.17 ..
6.3.m: Having formerly worshipped the Lord of beasts, Maheśvara, / I heard this Purāṇa; I shall relate it to you completely,

6.3.s:
yacchrutvā mucyate jantuḥ sarvapāpairnareśvara .
mānasaiḥ karmajaiścaiva saptajanmasu saṃcitaiḥ .. 3.18 ..
6.3.d:
यच्छ्रुत्वा मुच्यते जन्तुः सर्वपापैर्नरेश्वर .
मानसैः कर्मजैश्चैव सप्तजन्मसु संचितैः .. 3.18 ..
6.3.m: hearing which a living being is freed from all sins, O lord of men, / mental and born of action, accumulated over seven births.

6.3.s:
saptakalpakṣayā ghorā mayā dṛṣṭāḥ punaḥpunaḥ .
prasādāddevadevasya viṣṇośca parameṣṭhinaḥ .. 3.19 ..
6.3.d:
सप्तकल्पक्षया घोरा मया दृष्टाः पुनःपुनः .
प्रसादाद्देवदेवस्य विष्णोश्च परमेष्ठिनः .. 3.19 ..
6.3.m: Seven dreadful dissolutions of kalpas have been seen by me again and again / through the grace of the god of gods, Viṣṇu the Supreme Lord.

6.3.s:
dvādaśādityanirdagdhe jagatyekārṇavīkṛte .
śrānto'haṃ vibhramaṃstatra taranbāhubhirarṇavam .. 3.20 ..
6.3.d:
द्वादशादित्यनिर्दग्धे जगत्येकार्णवीकृते .
श्रान्तोऽहं विभ्रमंस्तत्र तरन्बाहुभिरर्णवम् .. 3.20 ..
6.3.m: When the world was burnt by the twelve suns and turned into a single vast ocean, / I wandered there, exhausted, crossing the ocean with my arms.

6.3.s:
athāhaṃ salile rājannādityasamarūpiṇam .
purā puruṣamadrākṣamanādinidhanaṃ prabhum .. 3.21 ..
6.3.d:
अथाहं सलिले राजन्नादित्यसमरूपिणम् .
पुरा पुरुषमद्राक्षमनादिनिधनं प्रभुम् .. 3.21 ..
6.3.m: Then in the water, O king, I saw of old a Man / who resembled the sun, the beginningless and endless Lord,

6.3.s:
śṛṅgaṃ caivādrirājasya bhāsayantaṃ diśo daśa .
dvitīyo'nyo manurdṛṣṭaḥ putrapautrasamanvitaḥ .. 3.22 ..
6.3.d:
शृङ्गं चैवाद्रिराजस्य भासयन्तं दिशो दश .
द्वितीयोऽन्यो मनुर्दृष्टः पुत्रपौत्रसमन्वितः .. 3.22 ..
6.3.m: and the peak of the king of mountains illuminating the ten directions. / A second one, Manu, was seen accompanied by sons and grandsons.

6.3.s:
agādhe bhramate so'pi tamobhūte mahārṇave .
aviśramanmuhūrtaṃ tu cakrārūḍha iva bhraman .. 3.23 ..
6.3.d:
अगाधे भ्रमते सोऽपि तमोभूते महार्णवे .
अविश्रमन्मुहूर्तं तु चक्रारूढ इव भ्रमन् .. 3.23 ..
6.3.m: He too wandered in that unfathomable great ocean that had become darkness, / never resting even for a moment, spinning as if mounted on a wheel.

6.3.s:
athāhaṃ bhayādudvignastaranbāhubhirarṇavam .
tatrastho'haṃ mahāmatsyamapaśyaṃ madasaṃyutam .. 3.24 ..
6.3.d:
अथाहं भयादुद्विग्नस्तरन्बाहुभिरर्णवम् .
तत्रस्थोऽहं महामत्स्यमपश्यं मदसंयुतम् .. 3.24 ..
6.3.m: Then, trembling with fear, crossing the ocean with my arms, / staying there, I saw a great fish filled with vigor.

6.3.s:
tato'bravītsa māṃ dṛṣṭvā ehyehīti ca bhārata .
paraṃ pradhānaḥ sarveṣāṃ matsyarūpo maheśvaraḥ .. 3.25 ..
6.3.d:
ततोऽब्रवीत्स मां दृष्ट्वा एह्येहीति च भारत .
परं प्रधानः सर्वेषां मत्स्यरूपो महेश्वरः .. 3.25 ..
6.3.m: Then, seeing me, he said, “Come, come!” O Bhārata; / he was Maheśvara in the form of a fish, the supreme head of all.

6.3.s:
tato'haṃ tvarayā gatvā tanmukhe manujeśvara .
suśrānto vigatajñānaḥ paraṃ nirvedamāgataḥ .. 3.26 ..
6.3.d:
ततोऽहं त्वरया गत्वा तन्मुखे मनुजेश्वर .
सुश्रान्तो विगतज्ञानः परं निर्वेदमागतः .. 3.26 ..
6.3.m: Then I went quickly into his mouth, O lord of men, / thoroughly exhausted, bereft of consciousness, fallen into utter despondency.

6.3.s:
tato'drākṣaṃ samudrānte mahadāvartasaṃkulām .
udyattaraṃgasalilāṃ phenapuñjāṭṭahāsinīm .. 3.27 ..
6.3.d:
ततोऽद्राक्षं समुद्रान्ते महदावर्तसंकुलाम् .
उद्यत्तरंगसलिलां फेनपुञ्जाट्टहासिनीम् .. 3.27 ..
6.3.m: Then at the edge of the ocean I saw a river filled with great whirlpools, / its waters surging in waves, laughing aloud with masses of foam,

6.3.s:
nadīṃ kāmagamāṃ puṇyāṃ jhaṣamīnasamākulām .
nadyāstasyāstu madhyasthā pramadā kāmarūpiṇī .. 3.28 ..
6.3.d:
नदीं कामगमां पुण्यां झषमीनसमाकुलाम् .
नद्यास्तस्यास्तु मध्यस्था प्रमदा कामरूपिणी .. 3.28 ..
6.3.m: holy, going wherever she pleased, swarming with huge fish and small fish; / and staying in the middle of that river was a woman who could take any form at will,

6.3.s:
nīlotpaladalaśyāmā mahatprakṣobhavāhinī .
divyahāṭakacitrāṅgī kanakojjvalaśobhitā .. 3.29 ..
6.3.d:
नीलोत्पलदलश्यामा महत्प्रक्षोभवाहिनी .
दिव्यहाटकचित्राङ्गी कनकोज्ज्वलशोभिता .. 3.29 ..
6.3.m: dark like a blue lotus petal, carrying a great agitation, / her limbs adorned with divine gold, radiant with bright gold.

6.3.s:
dvābhyāṃ saṃgṛhya jānubhyāṃ mahatpotaṃ vyavasthitā .
tāṃ manuḥ pratyuvācedaṃ kā tvaṃ divyavarāṅgane .. 3.30 ..
6.3.d:
द्वाभ्यां संगृह्य जानुभ्यां महत्पोतं व्यवस्थिता .
तां मनुः प्रत्युवाचेदं का त्वं दिव्यवराङ्गने .. 3.30 ..
6.3.m: Grasping a great boat between her two knees, she stood firm. / Manu addressed her with these words: “Who are you, divine and excellent woman?

6.3.s:
tiṣṭhase kena kāryeṇa tvamatra surasundari .
surāsuragaṇe naṣṭe bhramase līlayārṇave .. 3.31 ..
6.3.d:
तिष्ठसे केन कार्येण त्वमत्र सुरसुन्दरि .
सुरासुरगणे नष्टे भ्रमसे लीलयार्णवे .. 3.31 ..
6.3.m: For what purpose do you stand here, O celestial beauty? / When the host of gods and demons has perished, you wander playfully on the ocean.

6.3.s:
saritaḥ sāgarāḥ śailāḥ kṣayaṃ prāptā hyanekaśaḥ .
tvamekā tu kathaṃ sādhvi tiṣṭhase kāraṇaṃ mahat .
śrotumicchāmyahaṃ devi kathayasva hyaśeṣataḥ .. 3.32 ..
6.3.d:
सरितः सागराः शैलाः क्षयं प्राप्ता ह्यनेकशः .
त्वमेका तु कथं साध्वि तिष्ठसे कारणं महत् .
श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं देवि कथयस्व ह्यशेषतः .. 3.32 ..
6.3.m: Rivers, oceans, and mountains have perished many times over. / But how do you stand alone, O virtuous lady? There must be a great reason. / I wish to hear it, O goddess; tell it completely!”

6.3.s:
abalovāca -
īśvarāṅgasamudbhūtā hyamṛtānāma viśrutā .
saritpāpaharā puṇyā māmāśritya bhayaṃ kutaḥ .. 3.33 ..
6.3.d:
अबलोवाच -
ईश्वराङ्गसमुद्भूता ह्यमृतानाम विश्रुता .
सरित्पापहरा पुण्या मामाश्रित्य भयं कुतः .. 3.33 ..
6.3.m: The woman said: / “Born from the body of Īśvara, celebrated indeed by the name Amṛtā, / I am a holy river destroying sins; having taken refuge in me, whence fear?

6.3.s:
sāhaṃ potamimaṃ tubhyaṃ gṛhītvā hyāgatā dvija .
na hyasya potasya kṣayo yatra tiṣṭhati śaṃkaraḥ .. 3.34 ..
6.3.d:
साहं पोतमिमं तुभ्यं गृहीत्वा ह्यागता द्विज .
न ह्यस्य पोतस्य क्षयो यत्र तिष्ठति शंकरः .. 3.34 ..
6.3.m: Taking this boat, I have come for you, O twice-born. / For there is no destruction of this boat wherein Śaṃkara abides.”

6.3.s:
tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā vismayotphullalocanaḥ .
manunā saha rājendra potārūḍho hyahaṃ tadā .. 3.35 ..
6.3.d:
तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा विस्मयोत्फुल्ललोचनः .
मनुना सह राजेन्द्र पोतारूढो ह्यहं तदा .. 3.35 ..
6.3.m: Hearing her words, his eyes wide with wonder, / along with Manu I then boarded the boat, O royal sage.

6.3.s:
kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā praṇamya śirasā vibhum .
vyāpinaṃ parameśānamastauṣamabhayapradam .. 3.36 ..
6.3.d:
कृताञ्जलिपुटो भूत्वा प्रणम्य शिरसा विभुम् .
व्यापिनं परमेशानमस्तौषमभयप्रदम् .. 3.36 ..
6.3.m: Joining my palms in reverence, bowing my head to the all-pervading Lord, / the Supreme Ruler who grants fearlessness, I praised him:

6.3.s:
sadyojātāya devāya vāmadevāya vai namaḥ .
bhave bhave namastubhyaṃ bhaktigamyāya te namaḥ .. 3.37 ..
6.3.d:
सद्योजाताय देवाय वामदेवाय वै नमः .
भवे भवे नमस्तुभ्यं भक्तिगम्याय ते नमः .. 3.37 ..
6.3.m: “Homage to the god Sadyojāta, to Vāmadeva indeed homage! / Homage to you in every existence, homage to you who are attained through devotion!

6.3.s:
bhūrbhuvāya namastubhyaṃ rāmajyeṣṭhāya vai namaḥ .
namaste bhadrakālāya kalirūpāya vai namaḥ .. 3.38 ..
6.3.d:
भूर्भुवाय नमस्तुभ्यं रामज्येष्ठाय वै नमः .
नमस्ते भद्रकालाय कलिरूपाय वै नमः .. 3.38 ..
6.3.m: Homage to you, earth and atmosphere, homage to the elder brother of Rāma! / Homage to you, Bhadrakāla, homage to the embodiment of Kali!

6.3.s:
acintyāvyaktarūpāya mahādevāya dhāmane .
vidmahe devadevāya tanno rudra namonamaḥ .. 3.39 ..
6.3.d:
अचिन्त्याव्यक्तरूपाय महादेवाय धामने .
विद्महे देवदेवाय तन्नो रुद्र नमोनमः .. 3.39 ..
6.3.m: To the abode who is Mahādeva, of inconceivable and unmanifest form, / we know the god of gods; homage, homage to you, Rudra!

6.3.s:
jagatsṛṣṭivināśānāṃ kāraṇāya namonamaḥ .
evaṃ stuto mahādevaḥ pūrvaṃ sṛṣṭayā mayānagha .. 3.40 ..
6.3.d:
जगत्सृष्टिविनाशानां कारणाय नमोनमः .
एवं स्तुतो महादेवः पूर्वं सृष्टया मयानघ .. 3.40 ..
6.3.m: Homage, homage to the cause of the creation and destruction of the universe!” / When Mahādeva was thus praised of old by me, the created one, O sinless one,

6.3.s:
prasanno māvadatpaścādvaraṃ varaya suvrata .. 3.41 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe narmadāmāhātmye mārkaṇḍeyadharmarājasaṃvāde kalpakṣaye mārkaṇḍeyakṛtapotārdhārohaṇavṛttāntavarṇanaṃnāma tṛtīyo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 4
6.3.d:
प्रसन्नो मावदत्पश्चाद्वरं वरय सुव्रत .. 3.41 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे नर्मदामाहात्म्ये मार्कण्डेयधर्मराजसंवादे कल्पक्षये मार्कण्डेयकृतपोतार्धारोहणवृत्तान्तवर्णनंनाम तृतीयोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 4
6.3.m:
pleased, he then said to me: “Choose a boon, O you of noble vows!”
Thus ends the third chapter, named ‘Description of Mārkaṇḍeya's Boarding the Boat at the Dissolution of the Kalpa,’ in the conversation between Mārkaṇḍeya and Dharmarāja, in the Revākhaṇḍa of the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the Narmadāmāhātmya, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 4

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato'rṇavātsamuttīrya trikūṭaśikhare sthitam .
mahākanakavarṇābhe nānāvarṇaśilācite .. 4.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततोऽर्णवात्समुत्तीर्य त्रिकूटशिखरे स्थितम् .
महाकनकवर्णाभे नानावर्णशिलाचिते .. 4.1 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then, having emerged from the ocean, on the one stationed on the peak of Trikūṭa, / shining with the luster of great gold, piled with rocks of various colors,

6.3.s:
mahāśṛṅge samāsīnaṃ rudrakoṭisamanvitam .
mahādevaṃ mahātmānamīśānamajamavyayam .. 4.2 ..
6.3.d:
महाशृङ्गे समासीनं रुद्रकोटिसमन्वितम् .
महादेवं महात्मानमीशानमजमव्ययम् .. 4.2 ..
6.3.m: seated upon the great peak, accompanied by tens of millions of Rudras, / Mahādeva, the great-souled Lord, unborn, imperishable,

6.3.s:
sarvabhūtamayaṃ tāta manunā saha suvrata .
bhūyo vavande caraṇau sarvadevanamaskṛtau .. 4.3 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वभूतमयं तात मनुना सह सुव्रत .
भूयो ववन्दे चरणौ सर्वदेवनमस्कृतौ .. 4.3 ..
6.3.m: consisting of all beings, dear child, along with Manu, O you of noble vows, / I again reverenced his feet, which are worshipped by all the gods.

6.3.s:
tatkāle yugasāhasraṃ saha rudreṇa mānada .
tasminnekārṇave ghore sthito'haṃ kurunaṃdana .. 4.4 ..
6.3.d:
तत्काले युगसाहस्रं सह रुद्रेण मानद .
तस्मिन्नेकार्णवे घोरे स्थितोऽहं कुरुनंदन .. 4.4 ..
6.3.m: At that time, for a thousand ages with Rudra, O bestower of honor, / I remained in that dreadful single ocean, O joy of the Kurus.

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
etacchrutvā tu me tāta paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hṛdi .
jātaṃ tatkathayasveti śṛṇvataḥ saha bāndhavaiḥ .. 4.5 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु मे तात परं कौतूहलं हृदि .
जातं तत्कथयस्वेति शृण्वतः सह बान्धवैः .. 4.5 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / Having heard this, dear friend, a great curiosity in my heart / has arisen; tell that to me as I listen together with my kinsmen.

6.3.s:
kā sā padmapalāśākṣī tamobhūte mahārṇave .
yogivadbhramate nityaṃ rudrajāṃ svāṃ ca yābravīt .. 4.6 ..
6.3.d:
का सा पद्मपलाशाक्षी तमोभूते महार्णवे .
योगिवद्भ्रमते नित्यं रुद्रजां स्वां च याब्रवीत् .. 4.6 ..
6.3.m: Who was she with eyes like lotus petals in that great ocean turned to darkness, / who wandered constantly like an ascetic and who declared herself to be born of Rudra?

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
etameva mayā praśnaṃ purā pṛṣṭo manuḥ svayam .
tadeva te'dya vakṣyāmi abalāyāḥ samudbhavam .. 4.7 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
एतमेव मया प्रश्नं पुरा पृष्टो मनुः स्वयम् .
तदेव तेऽद्य वक्ष्यामि अबलायाः समुद्भवम् .. 4.7 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Long ago, this very question was asked by me to Manu himself. / That very origin of the maiden I shall tell you today. 4.7

6.3.s:
vyatītāyāṃ niśāyāṃ tu brahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ .
tataḥ prabhāte vimale sṛjyamāneṣu jantuṣu .. 4.8 ..
6.3.d:
व्यतीतायां निशायां तु ब्रह्मणः परमेष्ठिनः .
ततः प्रभाते विमले सृज्यमानेषु जन्तुषु .. 4.8 ..
6.3.m: When the night of Brahmā the supreme lord had passed, / and the pure morning dawned, as creatures were being created, 4.8

6.3.s:
manuṃ praṇamya śirasā pṛcchāmyetadyudhiṣṭhira .
keyaṃ padmapalāśākṣī śyāmā caṃdranibhānanā .. 4.9 ..
6.3.d:
मनुं प्रणम्य शिरसा पृच्छाम्येतद्युधिष्ठिर .
केयं पद्मपलाशाक्षी श्यामा चंद्रनिभानना .. 4.9 ..
6.3.m: having bowed my head to Manu, I asked him this, O Yudhiṣṭhira: / Who is this lotus-petal-eyed young woman, whose face resembles the moon, 4.9

6.3.s:
ekārṇave bhramatyekā rudrajāsmīti vādinī .
sāvitrī vedamātā ca hyathavā sā sarasvatī .. 4.10 ..
6.3.d:
एकार्णवे भ्रमत्येका रुद्रजास्मीति वादिनी .
सावित्री वेदमाता च ह्यथवा सा सरस्वती .. 4.10 ..
6.3.m: who wanders alone in the single ocean, saying, 'I was born of Rudra'? / Is she Sāvitrī the mother of the Vedas, or indeed Sarasvatī? 4.10

6.3.s:
mandākinī saricchreṣṭhā lakṣmīrvā kimatho umā .
kālarātrirbhavetsākṣātprakṛtirvā sukhocitā .. 4.11 ..
6.3.d:
मन्दाकिनी सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा लक्ष्मीर्वा किमथो उमा .
कालरात्रिर्भवेत्साक्षात्प्रकृतिर्वा सुखोचिता .. 4.11 ..
6.3.m: Is she Mandākinī, foremost of rivers, or Lakṣmī, or Umā? / Could she be Kālarātri herself, or Prakṛti suited to pleasure? 4.11

6.3.s:
etadācakṣva bhagavankā sā hyamṛtasaṃbhavā .
caratyekārṇave ghore pranaṣṭoragarākṣase .. 4.12 ..
6.3.d:
एतदाचक्ष्व भगवन्का सा ह्यमृतसंभवा .
चरत्येकार्णवे घोरे प्रनष्टोरगराक्षसे .. 4.12 ..
6.3.m: Explain this, O blessed one: Who is she, born of nectar, / who moves in the dread single ocean, where serpents and rākṣasas are destroyed? 4.12

6.3.s:
manuruvāca -
śṛṇu vatsa yathānyāyamasyā vakṣyāmi saṃbhavam .
yayā rudrasamudbhūtā yā ceyaṃ varavarṇinī .. 4.13 ..
6.3.d:
मनुरुवाच -
शृणु वत्स यथान्यायमस्या वक्ष्यामि संभवम् .
यया रुद्रसमुद्भूता या चेयं वरवर्णिनी .. 4.13 ..
6.3.m: Manu said: / Listen, dear child, I shall explain her origin in due order: / how she was born from Rudra, and who this fair-complexioned lady is. 4.13

6.3.s:
purā śivaḥ śāntatanuścacāra vipulaṃ tapaḥ .
hitārthaṃ sarvalokānāmumayā saha śaṃkaraḥ .. 4.14 ..
6.3.d:
पुरा शिवः शान्ततनुश्चचार विपुलं तपः .
हितार्थं सर्वलोकानामुमया सह शंकरः .. 4.14 ..
6.3.m: Long ago, Śiva of peaceful form practiced great austerity / together with Umā for the welfare of all worlds, he being Śaṃkara. 4.14

6.3.s:
ṛkṣaśailaṃ samāruhya tapastepe sudāruṇam .
adṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ sarvabhūtātmako vaśī .. 4.15 ..
6.3.d:
ऋक्षशैलं समारुह्य तपस्तेपे सुदारुणम् .
अदृश्यः सर्वभूतानां सर्वभूतात्मको वशी .. 4.15 ..
6.3.m: Having ascended Mount Ṛkṣa, he performed very dread austerity, / invisible to all beings, the self of all beings, self-controlled. 4.15

6.3.s:
tapatastasya devasya svedaḥ samabhavatkila .
taṃ giriṃ plāvayāmāsa sa svedo rudrasaṃbhavaḥ .. 4.16 ..
6.3.d:
तपतस्तस्य देवस्य स्वेदः समभवत्किल .
तं गिरिं प्लावयामास स स्वेदो रुद्रसंभवः .. 4.16 ..
6.3.m: As that god practiced austerity, sweat indeed arose. / That sweat born of Rudra flooded that mountain. 4.16

6.3.s:
tasmādāsītsamudbhūtā mahāpuṇyā saridvarā .
yā sā tvayārṇave dṛṣṭā padmapatrāyatekṣaṇā .. 4.17 ..
6.3.d:
तस्मादासीत्समुद्भूता महापुण्या सरिद्वरा .
या सा त्वयार्णवे दृष्टा पद्मपत्रायतेक्षणा .. 4.17 ..
6.3.m: From that arose the most meritorious, excellent river / whom you saw in the ocean, with eyes long like lotus petals. 4.17

6.3.s:
strīrūpaṃ samavasthāya rudramārādhayatpurā .
ādye kṛtayuge tasminsamānāmayutaṃ nṛpa .. 4.18 ..
6.3.d:
स्त्रीरूपं समवस्थाय रुद्रमाराधयत्पुरा .
आद्ये कृतयुगे तस्मिन्समानामयुतं नृप .. 4.18 ..
6.3.m: Assuming the form of a woman, she worshiped Rudra long ago / in that first Kṛta age for ten thousand years, O king. 4.18

6.3.s:
tatastuṣṭo mahādeva umayā saha śaṃkaraḥ .
brūhi tvaṃ tu mahābhāge yatte manasi vartate .. 4.19 ..
6.3.d:
ततस्तुष्टो महादेव उमया सह शंकरः .
ब्रूहि त्वं तु महाभागे यत्ते मनसि वर्तते .. 4.19 ..
6.3.m: Then Mahādeva Śaṃkara, pleased together with Umā, said: / 'Speak, O fortunate lady, whatever is in your mind!' 4.19

6.3.s:
sariduvāca -
pralaye samanuprāpte naṣṭe sthāvarajaṃgame .
prasādāttava deveśa akṣayāhaṃ bhave prabho .. 4.20 ..
6.3.d:
सरिदुवाच -
प्रलये समनुप्राप्ते नष्टे स्थावरजंगमे .
प्रसादात्तव देवेश अक्षयाहं भवे प्रभो .. 4.20 ..
6.3.m: The river said: / 'When universal dissolution arrives and moving and unmoving beings are destroyed, / by your grace, O lord of gods, may I be imperishable, O Lord! 4.20

6.3.s:
saritsu sāgareṣveva parvateṣu kṣayiṣvapi .
tava prasādāddeveśa puṇyā kṣayyā bhave prabho .. 4.21 ..
6.3.d:
सरित्सु सागरेष्वेव पर्वतेषु क्षयिष्वपि .
तव प्रसादाद्देवेश पुण्या क्षय्या भवे प्रभो .. 4.21 ..
6.3.m: Even when rivers, oceans, and mountains perish, / by your grace, O lord of gods, may I be holy and imperishable, O Lord! 4.21

6.3.s:
pāpopapātakairyuktā mahāpātakino'pi ye .
mucyante sarvapāpebhyo bhaktyā snātvā tu śaṃkara .. 4.22 ..
6.3.d:
पापोपपातकैर्युक्ता महापातकिनोऽपि ये .
मुच्यन्ते सर्वपापेभ्यो भक्त्या स्नात्वा तु शंकर .. 4.22 ..
6.3.m: Even those endowed with sins and minor sins, or those guilty of great sins, / are freed from all sins by bathing with devotion, O Śaṃkara. 4.22

6.3.s:
uttare jāhnavīdeśe mahāpātakanāśinī .
bhavāmi dakṣiṇe mārge yadyevaṃ surapūjitā .. 4.23 ..
6.3.d:
उत्तरे जाह्नवीदेशे महापातकनाशिनी .
भवामि दक्षिणे मार्गे यद्येवं सुरपूजिता .. 4.23 ..
6.3.m: In the northern region is the Jāhnavī, destroyer of great sins; / may I become worshiped by the gods on the southern path, if this pleases you. 4.23

6.3.s:
svargādāgamya gaṃgeti yathā khyātā kṣitau vibho .
tathā dakṣiṇagaṅgeti bhaveyaṃ tridaśeśvara .. 4.24 ..
6.3.d:
स्वर्गादागम्य गंगेति यथा ख्याता क्षितौ विभो .
तथा दक्षिणगङ्गेति भवेयं त्रिदशेश्वर .. 4.24 ..
6.3.m: Just as the Gaṅgā, having descended from heaven, is renowned on earth, O all-pervading one, / so may I become known as the Southern Gaṅgā, O lord of the thirty [gods]! 4.24

6.3.s:
pṛthivyāṃ sarvatīrtheṣu snātvā yallabhate phalam .
tatphalaṃ labhate martyo bhaktyā snātvā maheśvara .. 4.25 ..
6.3.d:
पृथिव्यां सर्वतीर्थेषु स्नात्वा यल्लभते फलम् .
तत्फलं लभते मर्त्यो भक्त्या स्नात्वा महेश्वर .. 4.25 ..
6.3.m: Whatever fruit a mortal obtains by bathing in all sacred fords on earth, / that fruit he obtains by bathing with devotion [in me], O Maheśvara. 4.25

6.3.s:
brahmahatyādikaṃ pāpaṃ yadāste saṃcitaṃ kvacit .
māsamātreṇa taddeva kṣayaṃ yātvavagāhanāt .. 4.26 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रह्महत्यादिकं पापं यदास्ते संचितं क्वचित् .
मासमात्रेण तद्देव क्षयं यात्ववगाहनात् .. 4.26 ..
6.3.m: Whatever sin, such as killing a brahmin, has been accumulated anywhere, / let it perish in just a month by plunging [in me], O god! 4.26

6.3.s:
yatphalaṃ sarvavedeṣu sarvayajñeṣu śaṃkara .
avagāhena tatsarvaṃ bhavatviti matirmama .. 4.27 ..
6.3.d:
यत्फलं सर्ववेदेषु सर्वयज्ञेषु शंकर .
अवगाहेन तत्सर्वं भवत्विति मतिर्मम .. 4.27 ..
6.3.m: Whatever fruit is found in all the Vedas and all sacrifices, O Śaṃkara, / let all that be obtained by plunging [in me]: this is my wish. 4.27

6.3.s:
sarvadānopavāseṣu sarvatīrthāvagāhane .
tatphalaṃ mama toyena jāyatāmiti śaṃkara .. 4.28 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वदानोपवासेषु सर्वतीर्थावगाहने .
तत्फलं मम तोयेन जायतामिति शंकर .. 4.28 ..
6.3.m: In all gifts and fasts, and in plunging into all sacred fords, / let that [same] fruit be produced by my water, O Śaṃkara. 4.28

6.3.s:
mama tīre narā ye tu arcayanti maheśvaram .
te gatāstava lokaṃ syuretadeva bhavecchiva .. 4.29 ..
6.3.d:
मम तीरे नरा ये तु अर्चयन्ति महेश्वरम् .
ते गतास्तव लोकं स्युरेतदेव भवेच्छिव .. 4.29 ..
6.3.m: Those men who worship Maheśvara on my bank, / let them go to your world; may this be so, O Śiva! 4.29

6.3.s:
mama kūle maheśāna umayā saha daivataiḥ .
vasa nityaṃ jagannātha eṣa eva varo mama .. 4.30 ..
6.3.d:
मम कूले महेशान उमया सह दैवतैः .
वस नित्यं जगन्नाथ एष एव वरो मम .. 4.30 ..
6.3.m: On my bank, O Maheśāna, together with Umā and the deities, / reside always, O lord of the universe! This alone is my boon. 4.30

6.3.s:
sukarmā vā vikarmā vā śānto dānto jitendriyaḥ .
mṛto janturmama jale gacchatādamarāvatīm .. 4.31 ..
6.3.d:
सुकर्मा वा विकर्मा वा शान्तो दान्तो जितेन्द्रियः .
मृतो जन्तुर्मम जले गच्छतादमरावतीम् .. 4.31 ..
6.3.m: Whether of good deeds or bad deeds, calm, restrained, with senses conquered, / let any creature who dies in my water go to Amarāvatī! 4.31

6.3.s:
triṣu lokeṣu vikhyātā mahāpātakanāśinī .
bhavāmi devadeveśa prasanno yadi manyase .. 4.32 ..
6.3.d:
त्रिषु लोकेषु विख्याता महापातकनाशिनी .
भवामि देवदेवेश प्रसन्नो यदि मन्यसे .. 4.32 ..
6.3.m: Renowned in the three worlds as the destroyer of great sins / may I become, O lord of the gods of gods, if you, being pleased, approve.' 4.32

6.3.s:
etāṃścānyānvarāndivyānprārthito nṛpasattama .
narmadayā tataḥ prāha prasanno vṛṣavāhanaḥ .. 4.33 ..
6.3.d:
एतांश्चान्यान्वरान्दिव्यान्प्रार्थितो नृपसत्तम .
नर्मदया ततः प्राह प्रसन्नो वृषवाहनः .. 4.33 ..
6.3.m: Being thus requested for these and other divine boons by the Narmadā, / O best of kings, the bull-vehicled god, pleased, said: 4.33

6.3.s:
śrīmaheśa uvāca -
evaṃ bhavatu kalyāṇi yattvayoktamanindite .
nānyā varārhā lokeṣu muktvā tvāṃ kamalekṣaṇe .. 4.34 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमहेश उवाच -
एवं भवतु कल्याणि यत्त्वयोक्तमनिन्दिते .
नान्या वरार्हा लोकेषु मुक्त्वा त्वां कमलेक्षणे .. 4.34 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Maheśa said: / 'So be it, O auspicious one, as spoken by you, O blameless lady! / No other woman in the worlds is worthy of boons except you, O lotus-eyed one. 4.34

6.3.s:
yadaiva mama dehāttvaṃ samudbhūtā varānane .
tadaiva sarvapāpānāṃ mocinī tvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .. 4.35 ..
6.3.d:
यदैव मम देहात्त्वं समुद्भूता वरानने .
तदैव सर्वपापानां मोचिनी त्वं न संशयः .. 4.35 ..
6.3.m: The very moment you were born from my body, O fair-faced one, / at that very moment you became the deliverer from all sins, there is no doubt. 4.35

6.3.s:
kalpakṣayakare kāle kāle ghore viśeṣataḥ .
uttaraṃ kūlamāśritya nivasanti ca ye narāḥ .. 4.36 ..
6.3.d:
कल्पक्षयकरे काले काले घोरे विशेषतः .
उत्तरं कूलमाश्रित्य निवसन्ति च ये नराः .. 4.36 ..
6.3.m: At the time that causes the destruction of the kalpa, especially at that dread time, / those men who dwell relying on your northern bank, 4.36

6.3.s:
api kīṭapataṅgāśca vṛkṣagulmalatādayaḥ .
ā dehapatanāddevi te'pi yāsyanti sadgatim .. 4.37 ..
6.3.d:
अपि कीटपतङ्गाश्च वृक्षगुल्मलतादयः .
आ देहपतनाद्देवि तेऽपि यास्यन्ति सद्गतिम् .. 4.37 ..
6.3.m: and even worms, winged insects, trees, shrubs, and creepers, / until the fall of their bodies, O goddess, they too shall attain the good destination. 4.37

6.3.s:
dakṣiṇaṃ kūlamāśritya ye dvijā dharmavatsalāḥ .
ā mṛtyornivasiṣyanti te gatāḥ pitṛmandire .. 4.38 ..
6.3.d:
दक्षिणं कूलमाश्रित्य ये द्विजा धर्मवत्सलाः .
आ मृत्योर्निवसिष्यन्ति ते गताः पितृमन्दिरे .. 4.38 ..
6.3.m: Those twice-born who are devoted to dharma, who rely on the southern bank / and dwell there until death, they shall go to the abode of the ancestors. 4.38

6.3.s:
ahaṃ hi tava vākyena kasmiṃścitkāraṇāntare .
tvattīre nivasiṣyāmi sadaiva hyumayā samam .. 4.39 ..
6.3.d:
अहं हि तव वाक्येन कस्मिंश्चित्कारणान्तरे .
त्वत्तीरे निवसिष्यामि सदैव ह्युमया समम् .. 4.39 ..
6.3.m: Indeed, according to your word, for a certain special purpose, / I shall always dwell on your bank together with Umā. 4.39

6.3.s:
evaṃ devi mahādevi evameva na saṃśayaḥ .
brahmendracandravaruṇaiḥ sādhyaiśca saha viṣṇunā .. 4.40 ..
6.3.d:
एवं देवि महादेवि एवमेव न संशयः .
ब्रह्मेन्द्रचन्द्रवरुणैः साध्यैश्च सह विष्णुना .. 4.40 ..
6.3.m: So it shall be, O goddess, O great goddess, precisely so, without doubt. / Together with Brahmā, Indra, Candra, Varuṇa, the Sādhyas, and Viṣṇu, 4.40

6.3.s:
uttare devi te kūle vasiṣyanti mamājñayā .
dakṣiṇe pitṛbhiḥ sārddhaṃ tathānye surasundari .. 4.41 ..
6.3.d:
उत्तरे देवि ते कूले वसिष्यन्ति ममाज्ञया .
दक्षिणे पितृभिः सार्द्धं तथान्ये सुरसुन्दरि .. 4.41 ..
6.3.m: they shall dwell on your northern bank by my command, O goddess. / On the southern [bank], together with the ancestors, other gods too, O beautiful lady of the gods, 4.41

6.3.s:
vasiṣyanti mayā sārddhameṣa te vara uttamaḥ .
gaccha gaccha mahābhāge martyānpāpādvimocaya .. 4.42 ..
6.3.d:
वसिष्यन्ति मया सार्द्धमेष ते वर उत्तमः .
गच्छ गच्छ महाभागे मर्त्यान्पापाद्विमोचय .. 4.42 ..
6.3.m: shall dwell along with me. This is your supreme boon. / Go, go, O fortunate one, deliver mortals from sin, 4.42

6.3.s:
sahitā ṛṣisaṃghaiśca tathā siddhasurāsuraiḥ .
evamuktā mahādeva umayā sahito vibhuḥ .. 4.43 ..
6.3.d:
सहिता ऋषिसंघैश्च तथा सिद्धसुरासुरैः .
एवमुक्ता महादेव उमया सहितो विभुः .. 4.43 ..
6.3.m: accompanied by hosts of seers, and likewise by siddhas, gods, and asuras.' / Having spoken thus, the all-pervading Mahādeva, accompanied by Umā, 4.43

6.3.s:
vandyamāno'tha manunā mayā cādarśanaṃ gataḥ .
tena caiṣā mahāpuṇyā mahāpātakanāśinī .. 4.44 ..
6.3.d:
वन्द्यमानोऽथ मनुना मया चादर्शनं गतः .
तेन चैषा महापुण्या महापातकनाशिनी .. 4.44 ..
6.3.m: while being praised by Manu and by me, vanished from sight. / Thus this most holy [river], destroyer of great sins, 4.44

6.3.s:
kathitā pṛcchyate yā te mā te bhavatu vismayaḥ .
eṣā gaṃgā mahāpuṇyā triṣu lokeṣu viśrutā .. 4.45 ..
6.3.d:
कथिता पृच्छ्यते या ते मा ते भवतु विस्मयः .
एषा गंगा महापुण्या त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुता .. 4.45 ..
6.3.m: about whom you ask, has been described; let there be no wonder in you. / This is the most holy Gaṅgā celebrated in the three worlds, 4.45

6.3.s:
daśābhiḥ pañcabhiḥ srotaiḥ plāvayantī diśo daśa .
śoṇo mahānadaścaiva narmadā surasā kṛtā .. 4.46 ..
6.3.d:
दशाभिः पञ्चभिः स्रोतैः प्लावयन्ती दिशो दश .
शोणो महानदश्चैव नर्मदा सुरसा कृता .. 4.46 ..
6.3.m: flooding the ten directions with fifteen streams: / the Śoṇa, the great river, and the pleasant Narmadā, 4.46

6.3.s:
mandākinī daśārṇā ca citrakūṭā tathaiva ca .
tamasā vidiśā caiva karabhā yamunā tathā .. 4.47 ..
6.3.d:
मन्दाकिनी दशार्णा च चित्रकूटा तथैव च .
तमसा विदिशा चैव करभा यमुना तथा .. 4.47 ..
6.3.m: Mandākinī, Daśārṇā, and likewise Citrakūṭā, / Tamasā, Vidiśā, Karabhā, and Yamunā, 4.47

6.3.s:
citrotpalā vipāśā ca rañjanā vāluvāhinī .
ṛkṣapādaprasūtāstāḥ sarvā vai rudrasaṃbhavāḥ .. 4.48 ..
6.3.d:
चित्रोत्पला विपाशा च रञ्जना वालुवाहिनी .
ऋक्षपादप्रसूतास्ताः सर्वा वै रुद्रसंभवाः .. 4.48 ..
6.3.m: Citrotpalā, Vipāśā, Rañjanā, and Vāluvāhinī. / All these born from the foothills of Ṛkṣa are indeed born of Rudra, 4.48

6.3.s:
sarvapāpaharāḥ puṇyāḥ sarvamaṃgaladāḥ śivāḥ .
ityetairnāmabhirdivyaiḥ stūyate vedapāragaiḥ .. 4.49 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वपापहराः पुण्याः सर्वमंगलदाः शिवाः .
इत्येतैर्नामभिर्दिव्यैः स्तूयते वेदपारगैः .. 4.49 ..
6.3.m: removers of all sins, holy, givers of all auspiciousness, benign. / With these divine names she is praised by those who have mastered the Vedas, 4.49

6.3.s:
purāṇajñairmahābhāgairājyapaiḥ somapaistathā .
ityetatsarvamākhyātaṃ mahābhāgyaṃ narottama .. 4.50 ..
6.3.d:
पुराणज्ञैर्महाभागैराज्यपैः सोमपैस्तथा .
इत्येतत्सर्वमाख्यातं महाभाग्यं नरोत्तम .. 4.50 ..
6.3.m: by fortunate knowers of the Purāṇas, by drinkers of clarified butter, and by drinkers of soma. / Thus all this greatness has been told, O best of men, 4.50

6.3.s:
manunoktaṃ purā mahyamamṛtāyāḥ samudbhavam .
puṇyaṃ pavitramatulaṃ rudrodgītamidaṃ śubham .. 4.51 ..
6.3.d:
मनुनोक्तं पुरा मह्यममृतायाः समुद्भवम् .
पुण्यं पवित्रमतुलं रुद्रोद्गीतमिदं शुभम् .. 4.51 ..
6.3.m: as the origin of the immortal lady was told to me long ago by Manu— / holy, pure, peerless, sung by Rudra, auspicious. 4.51

6.3.s:
ye narāḥ kīrtayiṣyanti bhaktyā śṛṇvanti ye'pi ca .
prātarutthāya nāmāni daśa pañca ca bhārata .. 4.52 ..
6.3.d:
ये नराः कीर्तयिष्यन्ति भक्त्या शृण्वन्ति येऽपि च .
प्रातरुत्थाय नामानि दश पञ्च च भारत .. 4.52 ..
6.3.m:
Those men who recite, or who hear with devotion,
rising in the morning, these fifteen names, O Bhārata,

6.3.s:
te narāḥ sakalaṃ puṇyaṃ labhiṣyantyavagāhajam .
vimānenārkavarṇena ghaṇṭāśataninādinā .. 4.53 ..
6.3.d:
ते नराः सकलं पुण्यं लभिष्यन्त्यवगाहजम् .
विमानेनार्कवर्णेन घण्टाशतनिनादिना .. 4.53 ..
6.3.m:
those men shall obtain all the merit born of bathing [there].
In an aerial chariot bright as the sun, resounding with a hundred bells,

6.3.s:
tyaktvā mānuṣyakaṃ bhāvaṃ yāsyanti paramāṃ gatim .. 4.54 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe narmadāpañcadaśanāmavarṇanaṃ nāma caturtho'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 5
6.3.d:
त्यक्त्वा मानुष्यकं भावं यास्यन्ति परमां गतिम् .. 4.54 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे नर्मदापञ्चदशनामवर्णनं नाम चतुर्थोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 5
6.3.m:
abandoning their human condition, they will go to the supreme destination.
Thus ends the fourth chapter, titled “Description of the Fifteen Names of the Narmadā,” in the Revākhaṇḍa of the Āvantyakhaṇḍa in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses].
Chapter 5

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
āścaryametadakhilaṃ kathitaṃ bho dvijottama .
vismayaṃ paramāpannā ṛṣisaṃghā mayā saha .. 5.1 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
आश्चर्यमेतदखिलं कथितं भो द्विजोत्तम .
विस्मयं परमापन्ना ऋषिसंघा मया सह .. 5.1 ..

6.3.s:
aho bhagavatī puṇyā narmadeyamayonijā .
rudradehādviniṣkrāntā mahāpāpakṣayaṃkarī .. 5.2 ..
6.3.d:
अहो भगवती पुण्या नर्मदेयमयोनिजा .
रुद्रदेहाद्विनिष्क्रान्ता महापापक्षयंकरी .. 5.2 ..
6.3.m:
Ah, holy is this blessed Narmadā, not born of a womb,
issued from Rudra’s body, destroying great sins!

6.3.s:
saptakalpakṣaye prāpte tvayeyaṃ saha suvrata .
na mṛtā ca mahābhāgā kimataḥ puṇyamuttamam .. 5.3 ..
6.3.d:
सप्तकल्पक्षये प्राप्ते त्वयेयं सह सुव्रत .
न मृता च महाभागा किमतः पुण्यमुत्तमम् .. 5.3 ..
6.3.m:
When the destruction of seven kalpas arrived, along with you, O observer of good vows,
she, highly fortunate, did not perish; what merit could be superior to this?

6.3.s:
ke te kalpāḥ samuddiṣṭāḥ sapta kalpakṣayaṃkarāḥ .
na mṛtā cediyaṃ devī tvaṃ caiva ṛṣipuṃgava .. 5.4 ..
6.3.d:
के ते कल्पाः समुद्दिष्टाः सप्त कल्पक्षयंकराः .
न मृता चेदियं देवी त्वं चैव ऋषिपुंगव .. 5.4 ..
6.3.m:
Which are those kalpas declared to be seven that bring about the destruction of kalpas,
if neither this goddess nor you, O bull among seers, perished?

6.3.s:
apakṣigaṇasaṃghāte jagatyekārṇavīkṛte .
kīdṛgrūpaḥ samabhavanmahādevo yugakṣaye .. 5.5 ..
6.3.d:
अपक्षिगणसंघाते जगत्येकार्णवीकृते .
कीदृग्रूपः समभवन्महादेवो युगक्षये .. 5.5 ..
6.3.m:
When the host of birds and beasts was gone, when the world had become a single cosmic ocean,
what was the form assumed by Mahādeva at the end of the yuga?

6.3.s:
kathaṃ saṃharate viśvaṃ kathaṃ cāste mahārṇave .
kathaṃ ca sṛjate viśvaṃ kathaṃ dhārayate prajāḥ .. 5.6 ..
6.3.d:
कथं संहरते विश्वं कथं चास्ते महार्णवे .
कथं च सृजते विश्वं कथं धारयते प्रजाः .. 5.6 ..
6.3.m:
How does he withdraw the universe, and how does he abide on the great ocean?
And how does he create the universe, how does he sustain creatures?

6.3.s:
kīdṛgrūpā bhaveddevī saridekārṇavīkṛte .
kimarthaṃ narmadā proktā revatī ca kathaṃ smṛtā .. 5.7 ..
6.3.d:
कीदृग्रूपा भवेद्देवी सरिदेकार्णवीकृते .
किमर्थं नर्मदा प्रोक्ता रेवती च कथं स्मृता .. 5.7 ..
6.3.m:
What was the form assumed by the goddess river when [all] was made a single cosmic ocean?
Why is she called Narmadā, and how is she remembered as Revatī?

6.3.s:
añjaneti kimarthaṃ vā kimarthaṃ suraseti ca .
mandākinī kimarthaṃ ca śoṇaśceti kathaṃ bhavet .. 5.8 ..
6.3.d:
अञ्जनेति किमर्थं वा किमर्थं सुरसेति च .
मन्दाकिनी किमर्थं च शोणश्चेति कथं भवेत् .. 5.8 ..
6.3.m:
Why is she called Añjanā, and why Surasā?
Why Mandākinī, and how does she come to be Śoṇā?

6.3.s:
trikūṭeti kimarthaṃ vā kimarthaṃ vāluvāhinī .
koṭikoṭyo hi tīrthānāṃ praviṣṭā yā mahārṇavam .. 5.9 ..
6.3.d:
त्रिकूटेति किमर्थं वा किमर्थं वालुवाहिनी .
कोटिकोट्यो हि तीर्थानां प्रविष्टा या महार्णवम् .. 5.9 ..
6.3.m:
Why is she called Trikūṭā, or why Vāluvāhinī?
For she enters the great ocean with crores and crores of sacred fords.

6.3.s:
kiyatyaḥ saritāṃ koṭyo narmadāṃ samupāsate .
yajñopavītairṛṣibhirdevatābhistathaiva ca .. 5.10 ..
6.3.d:
कियत्यः सरितां कोट्यो नर्मदां समुपासते .
यज्ञोपवीतैरृषिभिर्देवताभिस्तथैव च .. 5.10 ..
6.3.m:
How many crores of rivers attend upon the Narmadā,
along with seers bearing sacred threads, and likewise deities?

6.3.s:
vibhakteyaṃ kimarthaṃ ca śrūyate munisattama .
vaiṣṇavīti purāṇajñaiḥ kimarthamiha cocyate .. 5.11 ..
6.3.d:
