विभक्तेयं किमर्थं च श्रूयते मुनिसत्तम .
वैष्णवीति पुराणज्ञैः किमर्थमिह चोच्यते .. 5.11 ..
6.3.m:
And why is she heard to be divided, O best of sages?
Why is she called Vaiṣṇavī here by those who know the Purāṇas?

6.3.s:
keṣu sthāneṣu tīrtheṣu pūjanīyā saridvarā .
tīrthāni ca pṛthagbrūhi yatra saṃnihito haraḥ .. 5.12 ..
6.3.d:
केषु स्थानेषु तीर्थेषु पूजनीया सरिद्वरा .
तीर्थानि च पृथग्ब्रूहि यत्र संनिहितो हरः .. 5.12 ..
6.3.m:
In which places and sacred fords is the best of rivers to be worshipped?
Tell also individually of the sacred fords where Hara is present.

6.3.s:
yatpramāṇā ca sā devī yā rudreṇa vinirmitā .
kīdṛśāni ca karmāṇi rudreṇa kathitāni te .. 5.13 ..
6.3.d:
यत्प्रमाणा च सा देवी या रुद्रेण विनिर्मिता .
कीदृशानि च कर्माणि रुद्रेण कथितानि ते .. 5.13 ..
6.3.m:
And what is the extent of that goddess who was fashioned by Rudra?
And what deeds were related to you by Rudra?

6.3.s:
kathaṃ mlecchasamākīrṇo deśo'yaṃ dvijasattama .
etadācakṣva māṃ brahmanmārkaṇḍeya mahāmate .. 5.14 ..
6.3.d:
कथं म्लेच्छसमाकीर्णो देशोऽयं द्विजसत्तम .
एतदाचक्ष्व मां ब्रह्मन्मार्कण्डेय महामते .. 5.14 ..
6.3.m:
How did this region become teeming with mlecchas, O best of the twice-born?
Tell me this, O brahmin, O noble-minded Mārkaṇḍeya!

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
śṛṇvantu ṛṣayaḥ sarve tvaṃ ca tāta yudhiṣṭhira .
purāṇaṃ narmadāyāṃ tu kathitaṃ ca triśūlinā .. 5.15 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
शृण्वन्तु ऋषयः सर्वे त्वं च तात युधिष्ठिर .
पुराणं नर्मदायां तु कथितं च त्रिशूलिना .. 5.15 ..

6.3.s:
vāyoḥ sakāśācca mayā tenāpi ca maheśvarāt .
aśakyatvānmanuṣyāṇāṃ saṃkṣiptamṛṣibhiḥ purā .. 5.16 ..
6.3.d:
वायोः सकाशाच्च मया तेनापि च महेश्वरात् .
अशक्यत्वान्मनुष्याणां संक्षिप्तमृषिभिः पुरा .. 5.16 ..
6.3.m:
and [it was received] by me from Vāyu, and by him from Maheśvara.
Because of the incapacity of human beings, it was condensed by the seers of old.

6.3.s:
māyūraṃ prathamaṃ tāta kaurmyaṃ ca tadanantaram .
puraṃ tathā kauśikaṃ ca mātsyaṃ dviradameva ca .. 5.17 ..
6.3.d:
मायूरं प्रथमं तात कौर्म्यं च तदनन्तरम् .
पुरं तथा कौशिकं च मात्स्यं द्विरदमेव च .. 5.17 ..
6.3.m:
First is the Māyūra [kalpa], dear one, and next to that the Kaurmya;
and likewise the Pura, the Kauśika, the Mātsya, and the Dvirada;

6.3.s:
vārāhaṃ yanmayā dṛṣṭaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ cāṣṭamaṃ param .
nyagrodhākhyamataḥ cāsīdākāṅkṣaṃ punaruttamam .. 5.18 ..
6.3.d:
वाराहं यन्मया दृष्टं वैष्णवं चाष्टमं परम् .
न्यग्रोधाख्यमतः चासीदाकाङ्क्षं पुनरुत्तमम् .. 5.18 ..
6.3.m:
the Vārāha, which was witnessed by me, and eighth the supreme Vaiṣṇava;
after that was the one named Nyagrodha, and then the excellent Ākāṅkṣa;

6.3.s:
padmaṃ ca tāmasaṃ caiva saṃvartodvartameva ca .
mahāpralayamityāhuḥ purāṇe vedacintakāḥ .. 5.19 ..
6.3.d:
पद्मं च तामसं चैव संवर्तोद्वर्तमेव च .
महाप्रलयमित्याहुः पुराणे वेदचिन्तकाः .. 5.19 ..
6.3.m:
and the Padma, and the Tāmasa, and the Saṃvarta and Udvarta;
those who reflect upon the Vedas call these the great dissolution in the Purāṇa.

6.3.s:
etatsaṃkṣepataḥ sarvaṃ saṃkṣiptaṃ tairmahātmabhiḥ .
vibhaktaṃ ca caturbhāgairbrahmādyaiśca maharṣibhiḥ .. 5.20 ..
6.3.d:
एतत्संक्षेपतः सर्वं संक्षिप्तं तैर्महात्मभिः .
विभक्तं च चतुर्भागैर्ब्रह्माद्यैश्च महर्षिभिः .. 5.20 ..
6.3.m:
All this was summarized in brief by those great-souled ones,
and divided into four parts by Brahmā and the other great seers.

6.3.s:
tadahaṃ sampravakṣyāmi purāṇārthaviśārada .
sapta kalpā mahāghorā yairiyaṃ na mṛtā sarit .. 5.21 ..
6.3.d:
तदहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि पुराणार्थविशारद .
सप्त कल्पा महाघोरा यैरियं न मृता सरित् .. 5.21 ..
6.3.m:
That I shall declare fully, O you skilled in the meaning of the Purāṇas,
the seven most terrifying kalpas through which this river did not perish.

6.3.s:
ā jaṅgamaṃ tamobhūtamaprajñātamalakṣaṇam .
naṣṭacandrārkakiraṇamāsīdbhūtavivarjitam .. 5.22 ..
6.3.d:
आ जङ्गमं तमोभूतमप्रज्ञातमलक्षणम् .
नष्टचन्द्रार्ककिरणमासीद्भूतविवर्जितम् .. 5.22 ..
6.3.m:
Up to the animate creation, [all] had become darkness, unknowable, without distinguishing marks,
with the rays of the moon and sun lost, bereft of living beings.

6.3.s:
tamaso'to mahānāmnā puruṣaḥ sa jagadguruḥ .
cacāra tasminnekākī vyaktāvyaktaḥ sanātanaḥ .. 5.23 ..
6.3.d:
तमसोऽतो महानाम्ना पुरुषः स जगद्गुरुः .
चचार तस्मिन्नेकाकी व्यक्ताव्यक्तः सनातनः .. 5.23 ..
6.3.m:
From that darkness, that Puruṣa, the teacher of the world, called the Great One,
wandered alone therein, manifest and unmanifest, eternal.

6.3.s:
sa cauṃkāramayo'tīto gāyatrīmasṛjaddvijaḥ .
sa tayā sārddhamīśānaścikrīḍa puruṣo virāṭ .. 5.24 ..
6.3.d:
स चौंकारमयोऽतीतो गायत्रीमसृजद्द्विजः .
स तया सार्द्धमीशानश्चिक्रीड पुरुषो विराट् .. 5.24 ..
6.3.m:
He, composed of the syllable Oṃ, transcendent, the twice-born, created the Gāyatrī;
with her Īśāna, the cosmic Puruṣa, sporting, disported.

6.3.s:
svadehādasṛjadviśvaṃ pañcabhūtātmasaṃjñitam .
krīḍansamasṛjadviśvaṃ pañcabhūtātmasaṃjñitam .. 5.25 ..
6.3.d:
स्वदेहादसृजद्विश्वं पञ्चभूतात्मसंज्ञितम् .
क्रीडन्समसृजद्विश्वं पञ्चभूतात्मसंज्ञितम् .. 5.25 ..
6.3.m:
From his own body he emitted the universe designated as consisting of the five elements;
sporting, he created the universe designated as consisting of the five elements.

6.3.s:
krīḍan sṛjadvirāṭsaṃjñaḥ sabījaṃ ca hiraṇmayam .
taccāṇḍamabhavaddivyaṃ dvādaśādityasannibham .. 5.26 ..
6.3.d:
क्रीडन् सृजद्विराट्संज्ञः सबीजं च हिरण्मयम् .
तच्चाण्डमभवद्दिव्यं द्वादशादित्यसन्निभम् .. 5.26 ..
6.3.m:
Sporting, he who is named Virāṭ created the golden [egg] endowed with a seed;
and that divine egg became like twelve suns [in radiance].

6.3.s:
tadbhittvā puruṣo jajñe caturvaktraḥ pitāmahaḥ .
so'sṛjadviśvamevaṃ tu sadevāsuramānuṣam .. 5.27 ..
6.3.d:
तद्भित्त्वा पुरुषो जज्ञे चतुर्वक्त्रः पितामहः .
सोऽसृजद्विश्वमेवं तु सदेवासुरमानुषम् .. 5.27 ..
6.3.m:
Splitting it, the four-faced grandfather Puruṣa was born;
he created the universe in this manner, with gods, asuras, and mortals,

6.3.s:
satiryakpaśupakṣīkaṃ svedāṇḍajajarāyujam .
etadaṇḍaṃ purāṇeṣu prathamaṃ parikīrtitam .. 5.28 ..
6.3.d:
सतिर्यक्पशुपक्षीकं स्वेदाण्डजजरायुजम् .
एतदण्डं पुराणेषु प्रथमं परिकीर्तितम् .. 5.28 ..
6.3.m:
along with beasts, animals, and birds, sweat-born, egg-born, and womb-born;
this is celebrated in the Purāṇas as the first egg.

6.3.s:
pūrvakalpe nṛpaśreṣṭha krīḍantyā parameṣṭhinā .
umayā saha rudrasya krīḍataścārṇavīkṛtaḥ .. 5.29 ..
6.3.d:
पूर्वकल्पे नृपश्रेष्ठ क्रीडन्त्या परमेष्ठिना .
उमया सह रुद्रस्य क्रीडतश्चार्णवीकृतः .. 5.29 ..
6.3.m:
In a previous kalpa, O best of kings, as [Rudra] was sporting with the supreme goddess Umā,
and as Rudra was disporting, [the world] was made an ocean.

6.3.s:
harṣājjajñe śubhā kanyā umāyāḥ svedasaṃbhavā .
śarvasyoraḥsthalājjajñe umā kucavimardanāt .. 5.30 ..
6.3.d:
हर्षाज्जज्ञे शुभा कन्या उमायाः स्वेदसंभवा .
शर्वस्योरःस्थलाज्जज्ञे उमा कुचविमर्दनात् .. 5.30 ..
6.3.m:
Out of joy an auspicious maiden was born, originating from the sweat of Umā;
she was born from Śarva’s chest due to the crushing of Umā's breasts.

6.3.s:
svedādvijajñe mahatī kanyā rājīvalocanā .
dvitīyaḥ saṃbhavo yasyā rudradehādyudhiṣṭhira .. 5.31 ..
6.3.d:
स्वेदाद्विजज्ञे महती कन्या राजीवलोचना .
द्वितीयः संभवो यस्या रुद्रदेहाद्युधिष्ठिर .. 5.31 ..
6.3.m:
From the sweat was born a great lotus-eyed maiden,
whose second origin, O Yudhiṣṭhira, was from the body of Rudra.

6.3.s:
sā paribhramate lokān sadevāsuramānavān .
trailokyonmādajananī rūpeṇa'pratimā tadā .. 5.32 ..
6.3.d:
सा परिभ्रमते लोकान् सदेवासुरमानवान् .
त्रैलोक्योन्मादजननी रूपेणऽप्रतिमा तदा .. 5.32 ..
6.3.m:
She wandered through the worlds, which included gods, asuras, and mortals,
arousing passion in the three worlds, peerless then in beauty.

6.3.s:
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā devadaityendrā mohitā labhate katham .
mṛgayanti sma tāṃ kanyāmitaścetaśca bhārata .. 5.33 ..
6.3.d:
तां दृष्ट्वा देवदैत्येन्द्रा मोहिता लभते कथम् .
मृगयन्ति स्म तां कन्यामितश्चेतश्च भारत .. 5.33 ..
6.3.m:
Seeing her, the lords of gods and daityas were infatuated: “How can she be obtained?”
They searched for that maiden here and there, O Bhārata.

6.3.s:
hāvabhāvavilāsaiśca mohayatyakhilaṃ jagat .
bhramate divyarūpā sā vidyutsaudāminī yathā .. 5.34 ..
6.3.d:
हावभावविलासैश्च मोहयत्यखिलं जगत् .
भ्रमते दिव्यरूपा सा विद्युत्सौदामिनी यथा .. 5.34 ..
6.3.m:
And with coquetry, gestures, and playful graces she enchanted the whole world;
possessing a divine form, she wandered like a flash of lightning,

6.3.s:
meghamadhye sthitā bhābhiḥ sarvayoṣidanuttamā .
tato rudraṃ surāḥ sarve daityāśca saha dānavaiḥ .. 5.35 ..
6.3.d:
मेघमध्ये स्थिता भाभिः सर्वयोषिदनुत्तमा .
ततो रुद्रं सुराः सर्वे दैत्याश्च सह दानवैः .. 5.35 ..
6.3.m:
abiding within the cloud with radiant brilliance, unsurpassed by any woman.
Then all the gods, and the daityas along with the dānavas,

6.3.s:
varayanti sma tāṃ kanyāṃ kāmenākulitā bhṛśam .
tato'bravīnmahādevo devadānavayordvayoḥ .. 5.36 ..
6.3.d:
वरयन्ति स्म तां कन्यां कामेनाकुलिता भृशम् .
ततोऽब्रवीन्महादेवो देवदानवयोर्द्वयोः .. 5.36 ..
6.3.m:
sought that maiden in marriage from Rudra, intensely agitated by desire.
Then Mahādeva spoke to both the gods and the dānavas:

6.3.s:
balena tejasā caiva hyadhiko yo bhaviṣyati .
sa imāṃ prāpsyate kanyāṃ nānyathā vai surottamāḥ .. 5.37 ..
6.3.d:
बलेन तेजसा चैव ह्यधिको यो भविष्यति .
स इमां प्राप्स्यते कन्यां नान्यथा वै सुरोत्तमाः .. 5.37 ..
6.3.m:
“Whoever shall be superior in strength and in majesty,
he shall obtain this maiden, not otherwise indeed, O best of gods.”

6.3.s:
tato devāsurāḥ sarve kanyāṃ vai samupāgaman .
ahamenāṃ grahīṣyāmi ahamenāmiti bruvan .. 5.38 ..
6.3.d:
ततो देवासुराः सर्वे कन्यां वै समुपागमन् .
अहमेनां ग्रहीष्यामि अहमेनामिति ब्रुवन् .. 5.38 ..
6.3.m:
Then all the gods and asuras approached the maiden,
saying, “I shall seize her! I shall seize her!”

6.3.s:
paśyatāmeva sarveṣāṃ sā kanyāntaradhīyata .
punastāṃ dadṛśuḥ sarve yojanāntaradhiṣṭhitām .. 5.39 ..
6.3.d:
पश्यतामेव सर्वेषां सा कन्यान्तरधीयत .
पुनस्तां ददृशुः सर्वे योजनान्तरधिष्ठिताम् .. 5.39 ..
6.3.m:
Even as all of them were watching, that maiden vanished;
then they all saw her again standing at a distance of a yojana.

6.3.s:
jagmuste tvaritāḥ sarve yatra sā samadṛśyata .
tribhiścaturbhiśca tathā yojanairdaśabhiḥ punaḥ .. 5.40 ..
6.3.d:
जग्मुस्ते त्वरिताः सर्वे यत्र सा समदृश्यत .
त्रिभिश्चतुर्भिश्च तथा योजनैर्दशभिः पुनः .. 5.40 ..
6.3.m:
They all went swiftly to where she was seen;
then at [a distance of] three, four, and again ten yojanas [she stood].

6.3.s:
dhiṣṭhitāṃ samapaśyaṃste sarve mātaṃgagāminīm .
yojanānāṃ śatairbhūyaḥ sahasraiścāpyadhiṣṭhitām .. 5.41 ..
6.3.d:
धिष्ठितां समपश्यंस्ते सर्वे मातंगगामिनीम् .
योजनानां शतैर्भूयः सहस्रैश्चाप्यधिष्ठिताम् .. 5.41 ..
6.3.m: They all saw her walking with the gait of an elephant, stationed [far away], / and again stationed hundreds and thousands of yojanas away. 5.41

6.3.s:
tathā śatasahasreṇa laghutvātsamadṛśyata .
agrataḥ pṛṣṭhataścaiva diśāsu vidiśāsu ca .. 5.42 ..
6.3.d:
तथा शतसहस्रेण लघुत्वात्समदृश्यत .
अग्रतः पृष्ठतश्चैव दिशासु विदिशासु च .. 5.42 ..
6.3.m: Likewise, owing to her lightness, she appeared a hundred thousand [yojanas off], / in front, behind, in the cardinal directions and the intermediate directions. 5.42

6.3.s:
tāṃ paśyanti varārohāmekadhā bahudhā punaḥ .
divyavarṣasahasraṃ tu bhrāmitāste tayā purā .. 5.43 ..
6.3.d:
तां पश्यन्ति वरारोहामेकधा बहुधा पुनः .
दिव्यवर्षसहस्रं तु भ्रामितास्ते तया पुरा .. 5.43 ..
6.3.m: They saw that fair-hipped maiden, now single, now multiform; / indeed, for a thousand divine years they were led wandering about by her in ancient times. 5.43

6.3.s:
na cāvāptā tu sā kanyā mahādevāṅgasaṃbhavā .
sahomayā tato devo jahāsoccaiḥ punaḥpunaḥ .. 5.44 ..
6.3.d:
न चावाप्ता तु सा कन्या महादेवाङ्गसंभवा .
सहोमया ततो देवो जहासोच्चैः पुनःपुनः .. 5.44 ..
6.3.m: Yet that maiden, born from the limbs of Mahādeva, was not attained. / Then, together with Umā, the god laughed out loud again and again. 5.44

6.3.s:
gaṇāstālakasaṃpātairnṛtyanti ca mudānvitāḥ .
akasmāddṛśyate kanyā śaṃkarasya samīpagā .. 5.45 ..
6.3.d:
गणास्तालकसंपातैर्नृत्यन्ति च मुदान्विताः .
अकस्माद्दृश्यते कन्या शंकरस्य समीपगा .. 5.45 ..
6.3.m: The gaṇas, filled with joy, danced to the clapping of hands; / and suddenly the maiden was seen standing near Śaṃkara. 5.45

6.3.s:
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā vismayāpannā devā yānti parāṅmukhāḥ .
tasyāścakre tato nāma svayameva pinākadhṛk .. 5.46 ..
6.3.d:
तां दृष्ट्वा विस्मयापन्ना देवा यान्ति पराङ्मुखाः .
तस्याश्चक्रे ततो नाम स्वयमेव पिनाकधृक् .. 5.46 ..
6.3.m: Seeing her, the gods, filled with astonishment, turned their faces away. / Then the wielder of the Pināka himself gave her a name: 5.46

6.3.s:
narma caibhyo dade yasmāttatkṛtaiśceṣṭitaiḥ pṛthak .
bhaviṣyasi varārohe saricchreṣṭhā tu narmadā .. 5.47 ..
6.3.d:
नर्म चैभ्यो ददे यस्मात्तत्कृतैश्चेष्टितैः पृथक् .
भविष्यसि वरारोहे सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा तु नर्मदा .. 5.47 ..
6.3.m: “Since you gave amusement (narma) to these [gods] through their various antics, / you shall be Narmadā, the best of rivers, O fair-hipped one! 5.47

6.3.s:
svarūpamāsthito devaḥ prāpa hāsyaṃ yato bhuvi .
narmadā tena cokteyaṃ suśītalajalā śivā .. 5.48 ..
6.3.d:
स्वरूपमास्थितो देवः प्राप हास्यं यतो भुवि .
नर्मदा तेन चोक्तेयं सुशीतलजला शिवा .. 5.48 ..
6.3.m: Because the god, assuming his true nature, attained laughter on the earth, / she was called Narmadā, auspicious and possessing very cool waters. 5.48

6.3.s:
saptakalpakṣaye jāte yaduktaṃ śaṃbhunā purā .
na mṛtā tena rājendra narmadā khyātimāgatā .. 5.49 ..
6.3.d:
सप्तकल्पक्षये जाते यदुक्तं शंभुना पुरा .
न मृता तेन राजेन्द्र नर्मदा ख्यातिमागता .. 5.49 ..
6.3.m: Because of what was spoken by Śambhu of old, when the destruction of seven kalpas occurs, / she does not die; therefore, O best of kings, she attained renown as Narmadā. 5.49

6.3.s:
tatastāmadadātkanyāṃ śīlavatīṃ suśobhanām .
mahārṇavāya deveśaḥ sarvabhūtapatiḥ prabhuḥ .. 5.50 ..
6.3.d:
ततस्तामददात्कन्यां शीलवतीं सुशोभनाम् .
महार्णवाय देवेशः सर्वभूतपतिः प्रभुः .. 5.50 ..
6.3.m: Then the lord of gods, the lord of all beings, the sovereign ruler, / gave that well-behaved and very beautiful maiden to the great ocean. 5.50

6.3.s:
tataḥ sā ṛkṣaśailendrātphenapuñjāṭṭahāsinī .
viveśa narmadā devī samudraṃ saritāṃ patim .. 5.51 ..
6.3.d:
ततः सा ऋक्षशैलेन्द्रात्फेनपुञ्जाट्टहासिनी .
विवेश नर्मदा देवी समुद्रं सरितां पतिम् .. 5.51 ..
6.3.m: Thereupon, from the best of mountains, the Ṛkṣa, roaring with loud laughter of foam clusters, / the goddess Narmadā entered the ocean, the lord of rivers. 5.51

6.3.s:
evaṃ brāhme purā kalpe samudbhūteyamīśvarāt .
mātsye kalpe mayā dṛṣṭā samākhyātā mayā śṛṇu .. 5.52 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe pañcamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 6
6.3.d:
एवं ब्राह्मे पुरा कल्पे समुद्भूतेयमीश्वरात् .
मात्स्ये कल्पे मया दृष्टा समाख्याता मया शृणु .. 5.52 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे पञ्चमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 6
6.3.m:
Thus of old in the Brāhma-kalpa she was born from Īśvara; / in the Mātsya-kalpa she was seen by me and has been narrated by me. Listen! 5.52
Thus ends the fifth chapter in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 6

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
punaryugānte samprāpte tṛtīye nṛpasattama .
dādaśārkavapurbhūtvā bhagavānnīlalohitaḥ .. 6.1 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
पुनर्युगान्ते सम्प्राप्ते तृतीये नृपसत्तम .
दादशार्कवपुर्भूत्वा भगवान्नीललोहितः .. 6.1 ..
6.3.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Again, when the end of the yuga arrived for the third time, O best of kings, / the blessed Nīlalohita assumed the form of the twelve suns. 6.1

6.3.s:
saptadvīpasamudrāntāṃ saśailavanakānanām .
nirdagdhāṃ tu mahīṃ kṛtsnāṃ kālo bhūtvā maheśvaraḥ .. 6.2 ..
6.3.d:
सप्तद्वीपसमुद्रान्तां सशैलवनकाननाम् .
निर्दग्धां तु महीं कृत्स्नां कालो भूत्वा महेश्वरः .. 6.2 ..
6.3.m: Maheśvara, having become Time, burned up the entire earth / bounded by the seven continents and oceans, along with its mountains, forests, and woods. 6.2

6.3.s:
tato mahāghano bhūtvā plāvayāmāsa vāriṇā .
kṛṣṇaṃ kṛṣṇavapustvenāṃ vidyuccandrāyudhāṅkitām .. 6.3 ..
6.3.d:
ततो महाघनो भूत्वा प्लावयामास वारिणा .
कृष्णं कृष्णवपुस्त्वेनां विद्युच्चन्द्रायुधाङ्किताम् .. 6.3 ..
6.3.m: Then, having become a great cloud, he flooded it with water, / a black cloud with a dark body, marked with lightning and the crescent moon as weapons. 6.3

6.3.s:
plāvayitvā jagatsarvaṃ tasminnekārṇavīkṛte .
suṣvāpa vimale toye jagatsaṃkṣipya māyayā .. 6.4 ..
6.3.d:
प्लावयित्वा जगत्सर्वं तस्मिन्नेकार्णवीकृते .
सुष्वाप विमले तोये जगत्संक्षिप्य मायया .. 6.4 ..
6.3.m: Having flooded the entire world, when it had been turned into a single ocean, / he slept upon the pure water, having contracted the world by his illusory power. 6.4

6.3.s:
tato'haṃ bhramamāstu tamobhūte mahārṇave .
divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu vāyubhūte maheśvare .. 6.5 ..
6.3.d:
ततोऽहं भ्रममास्तु तमोभूते महार्णवे .
दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रं तु वायुभूते महेश्वरे .. 6.5 ..
6.3.m: Then, while Maheśvara had become the wind, I wandered about / for a thousand divine years in the great ocean enveloped in darkness. 6.5

6.3.s:
oṃkṛtvā devadeveśaṃ yenedaṃ gahanīkṛtam .
dhyāyamānastato devaṃ rājendra vimale jale .. 6.6 ..
6.3.d:
ओंकृत्वा देवदेवेशं येनेदं गहनीकृतम् .
ध्यायमानस्ततो देवं राजेन्द्र विमले जले .. 6.6 ..
6.3.m: Uttering “Om” unto the lord of the gods of gods, by whom this [world] was made impassable, / and meditating on the god, O best of kings, in that pure water, 6.6

6.3.s:
tasminmahārṇave ghore naṣṭe sthāvarajaṅgame .
mayūraṃ svarṇapatrāḍhyamapaśyaṃsahasā jale .
vicitracandrakopetaṃ nīlakaṃṭhaṃ sulocanam .. 6.7 ..
6.3.d:
तस्मिन्महार्णवे घोरे नष्टे स्थावरजङ्गमे .
मयूरं स्वर्णपत्राढ्यमपश्यंसहसा जले .
विचित्रचन्द्रकोपेतं नीलकंठं सुलोचनम् .. 6.7 ..
6.3.m: in that dreadful great ocean, when mobile and immobile beings had vanished, / I suddenly saw a peacock in the water, rich with golden feathers, / possessing wondrous eye-spots, blue-necked, and with beautiful eyes. 6.7

6.3.s:
tato mayūraḥ sa mahārṇavānte vikṣobhayitvā hi mahāsveṇa .
cacāra devastriśikhī śikhaṇḍī trailokyagoptā sa mahānubhāvaḥ .. 6.8 ..
6.3.d:
ततो मयूरः स महार्णवान्ते विक्षोभयित्वा हि महास्वेण .
चचार देवस्त्रिशिखी शिखण्डी त्रैलोक्यगोप्ता स महानुभावः .. 6.8 ..
6.3.m: Then that peacock, having agitated the expanse of the great ocean with great force, / moved about—the three-crested, plumaged god, the protector of the three worlds, of exalted majesty. 6.8

6.3.s:
śivaśca raudreṇa mayūrarūpiṇā vikṣobhyamāṇe salile'pi tasmin .
saha bhramantīṃ ca mahārṇavānte sarinmahaughāṃ sumahāndadarśa .. 6.9 ..
6.3.d:
शिवश्च रौद्रेण मयूररूपिणा विक्षोभ्यमाणे सलिलेऽपि तस्मिन् .
सह भ्रमन्तीं च महार्णवान्ते सरिन्महौघां सुमहान्ददर्श .. 6.9 ..
6.3.m: And while the water was being agitated by the fierce Śiva in the form of a peacock, / he, the very great one, saw a river of immense current wandering along within the great ocean. 6.9

6.3.s:
sa tāṃ mahādevamayūrarūpo dṛṣṭvā bhramantīṃ sahasormijālaiḥ .
kā tvaṃ śubhe śāśvatadehabhūtā kṣayaṃ na yātāsi mahākṣayānte .. 6.10 ..
6.3.d:
स तां महादेवमयूररूपो दृष्ट्वा भ्रमन्तीं सहसोर्मिजालैः .
का त्वं शुभे शाश्वतदेहभूता क्षयं न यातासि महाक्षयान्ते .. 6.10 ..
6.3.m: Mahādeva, in the form of the peacock, seeing her wandering with multitudes of violent waves, [said]: / “Who are you, O auspicious one, possessed of an eternal body, who have not met destruction at the end of the great dissolution? 6.10

6.3.s:
devāsuragaṇe naṣṭe saritsaramahārṇave .
kā tvaṃ bhramasi padmākṣi kva gatāsi ca na kṣayam .. 6.11 ..
6.3.d:
देवासुरगणे नष्टे सरित्सरमहार्णवे .
का त्वं भ्रमसि पद्माक्षि क्व गतासि च न क्षयम् .. 6.11 ..
6.3.m: When the hosts of gods and asuras, rivers, lakes, and the great ocean have perished, / who are you who wander, O lotus-eyed one, and where did you go without being destroyed?” 6.11

6.3.s:
narmadovāca -
tava prasādāddeveśa mṛtyurmama na vidyate .
sṛja deva punarviśvaṃ śarvarī kṣayamāgatā .. 6.12 ..
6.3.d:
नर्मदोवाच -
तव प्रसादाद्देवेश मृत्युर्मम न विद्यते .
सृज देव पुनर्विश्वं शर्वरी क्षयमागता .. 6.12 ..
6.3.m: Narmadā said: / “By your grace, O lord of gods, death does not exist for me. / O god, create the universe once more; the night has come to an end.” 6.12

6.3.s:
evamukto mahādevo vyadhunotpakṣapañjaram .
tāvatpañjaramadhyānte tasya pakṣādviniḥsṛtāḥ .. 6.13 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्तो महादेवो व्यधुनोत्पक्षपञ्जरम् .
तावत्पञ्जरमध्यान्ते तस्य पक्षाद्विनिःसृताः .. 6.13 ..
6.3.m: Thus addressed, Mahādeva shook the cage of his wings; / thereupon, from the midst of the cage, out of his wings they came forth. 6.13

6.3.s:
tāvanto devadaityendrāḥ pakṣābhyāṃ tasya jajñire .
teṣāṃ madhye punaḥ sā tu narmadā bhramate sarit .. 6.14 ..
6.3.d:
तावन्तो देवदैत्येन्द्राः पक्षाभ्यां तस्य जज्ञिरे .
तेषां मध्ये पुनः सा तु नर्मदा भ्रमते सरित् .. 6.14 ..
6.3.m: So many lords of gods and daityas were born from his two wings; / and in their midst, that river Narmadā wandered again. 6.14

6.3.s:
tataścānyo mahāśailo dṛśyate bharatarṣabha .
tribhiḥ kūṭaiḥ suvistīrṇaiḥ śṛṅgavāniva govṛṣaḥ .. 6.15 ..
6.3.d:
ततश्चान्यो महाशैलो दृश्यते भरतर्षभ .
त्रिभिः कूटैः सुविस्तीर्णैः शृङ्गवानिव गोवृषः .. 6.15 ..
6.3.m: Then another great mountain was seen, O bull of the Bharatas, / with three vast peaks, like a horned bull. 6.15

6.3.s:
trikūṭastu iti khyātaḥ sarvaratnairvibhūṣitaḥ .
tatastasmāttrikūṭācca plāvayantī mahīṃ yayau .. 6.16 ..
6.3.d:
त्रिकूटस्तु इति ख्यातः सर्वरत्नैर्विभूषितः .
ततस्तस्मात्त्रिकूटाच्च प्लावयन्ती महीं ययौ .. 6.16 ..
6.3.m: It was renowned as Trikūṭa, adorned with all kinds of jewels; / then, from that Trikūṭa, she went forth, flooding the earth. 6.16

6.3.s:
trikūṭī tena vikhyātā pitṝṇāṃ trāyaṇī parā .
dvitīyācca tato gaṅgā vistīrṇā dharaṇītale .. 6.17 ..
6.3.d:
त्रिकूटी तेन विख्याता पितॄणां त्रायणी परा .
द्वितीयाच्च ततो गङ्गा विस्तीर्णा धरणीतले .. 6.17 ..
6.3.m: Therefore she is celebrated as Trikūṭī, the supreme deliverer of the ancestors; / and from the second [peak] the Gaṅgā spread out across the surface of the earth. 6.17

6.3.s:
tṛtīyaṃ ca tataḥ śṛṅgaṃ saptadhā khaṇḍaśo gatam .
jambūdvīpe tu saṃjātāḥ sapta te kulaparvatāḥ .. 6.18 ..
6.3.d:
तृतीयं च ततः शृङ्गं सप्तधा खण्डशो गतम् .
जम्बूद्वीपे तु संजाताः सप्त ते कुलपर्वताः .. 6.18 ..
6.3.m: And then the third peak split into fragments in seven ways; / in Jambūdvīpa they became those seven principal mountain ranges. 6.18

6.3.s:
candranakṣatrasahitā grahagrāmanadīnadāḥ .
aṇḍajaṃ svedajaṃ jātamudbhijjaṃ ca jarāyujam .. 6.19 ..
6.3.d:
चन्द्रनक्षत्रसहिता ग्रहग्रामनदीनदाः .
अण्डजं स्वेदजं जातमुद्भिज्जं च जरायुजम् .. 6.19 ..
6.3.m: Along with the moon and constellations, planets, settlements, rivers, and streams, / what was born from eggs, sweat, sprouts, and wombs arose. 6.19

6.3.s:
evaṃ jagadidaṃ sarvaṃ mayūrādabhavatpurā .
samastaṃ naraśārdūla mahādevasamudbhavam .. 6.20 ..
6.3.d:
एवं जगदिदं सर्वं मयूरादभवत्पुरा .
समस्तं नरशार्दूल महादेवसमुद्भवम् .. 6.20 ..
6.3.m: Thus all this world originated of old from the peacock, / all of it, O tiger among men, arising from Mahādeva. 6.20

6.3.s:
tato nadīḥ samudrāṃśca saṃvibhajya pṛthakpṛthak .
narmadāmāha deveśo gaccha tvaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ diśam .. 6.21 ..
6.3.d:
ततो नदीः समुद्रांश्च संविभज्य पृथक्पृथक् .
नर्मदामाह देवेशो गच्छ त्वं दक्षिणां दिशम् .. 6.21 ..
6.3.m: Then, having divided the rivers and oceans distinctly, / the lord of gods said to Narmadā: “Go to the southern direction! 6.21

6.3.s:
evaṃ sā dakṣiṇā gaṃgā mahāpātakanāśinī .
uttare jāhnavī deśe puṇyā tvaṃ dakṣiṇe śubhā .. 6.22 ..
6.3.d:
एवं सा दक्षिणा गंगा महापातकनाशिनी .
उत्तरे जाह्नवी देशे पुण्या त्वं दक्षिणे शुभा .. 6.22 ..
6.3.m: Thus, you are the southern Gaṅgā, the destroyer of great sins; / the Jāhnavī is in the northern region, and you, auspicious and sacred, are in the south. 6.22

6.3.s:
yathā gaṃgā mahāpuṇyā mama mastakasaṃbhavā .
tadviśiṣṭā mahābhāge tvaṃ caiveti na saṃśayaḥ .. 6.23 ..
6.3.d:
यथा गंगा महापुण्या मम मस्तकसंभवा .
तद्विशिष्टा महाभागे त्वं चैवेति न संशयः .. 6.23 ..
6.3.m: Just as the Gaṅgā, born from my head, is exceedingly sacred, / even superior to her are you, O highly fortunate one, without a doubt. 6.23

6.3.s:
tvayā saha bhaviṣyāmi ekenāṃśena suvrate .
mahāpātakayuktānāmauṣadhaṃ tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi .. 6.24 ..
6.3.d:
त्वया सह भविष्यामि एकेनांशेन सुव्रते .
महापातकयुक्तानामौषधं त्वं भविष्यसि .. 6.24 ..
6.3.m: I shall remain with you by a portion of myself, O lady of good vows; / you shall be the medicine for those who are joined with great sins.” 6.24

6.3.s:
evamuktā tu devena mahāpātakanāśinī .
dakṣiṇaṃ digvibhāgaṃ tu sā jagāmāśu vikramā .. 6.25 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्ता तु देवेन महापातकनाशिनी .
दक्षिणं दिग्विभागं तु सा जगामाशु विक्रमा .. 6.25 ..
6.3.m: Thus addressed by the god, that destroyer of great sins, / striding swiftly, went to the southern quarter. 6.25

6.3.s:
ṛkṣaśailendramāsādya candramauleranugrahāt .
vāryaughaiḥ prasthitā yasmānmahādevapraṇoditā .. 6.26 ..
6.3.d:
ऋक्षशैलेन्द्रमासाद्य चन्द्रमौलेरनुग्रहात् .
वार्यौघैः प्रस्थिता यस्मान्महादेवप्रणोदिता .. 6.26 ..
6.3.m: Having reached the Ṛkṣa, the best of mountains, by the grace of the crescent-crested god, / since she set forth with floods of water impelled by Mahādeva, 6.26

6.3.s:
mahatā cāpi vegena yasmādeṣā samucchritā .
mahatī tena sā proktā mahādevānmahīpate .. 6.27 ..
6.3.d:
महता चापि वेगेन यस्मादेषा समुच्छ्रिता .
महती तेन सा प्रोक्ता महादेवान्महीपते .. 6.27 ..
6.3.m: and since she rose up with great speed, / therefore she was called Mahatī by Mahādeva, O lord of the earth. 6.27

6.3.s:
tapatastasya devasya śūlāgrādbindavo'patan .
tenaiṣā śoṇasaṃjñā tu daśa sapta ca tāḥ smṛtāḥ .. 6.28 ..
6.3.d:
तपतस्तस्य देवस्य शूलाग्राद्बिन्दवोऽपतन् .
तेनैषा शोणसंज्ञा तु दश सप्त च ताः स्मृताः .. 6.28 ..
6.3.m: As that god was performing austerities, drops fell from the tip of his trident; / by that she was named Śoṇā, and they are recorded as seventeen [streams]. 6.28

6.3.s:
sarveṣāṃ narmadā puṇyā rudradehādviniḥsṛtā .
sarvābhyaśca saridbhyaśca varadānānmahātmanaḥ .. 6.29 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वेषां नर्मदा पुण्या रुद्रदेहाद्विनिःसृता .
सर्वाभ्यश्च सरिद्भ्यश्च वरदानान्महात्मनः .. 6.29 ..
6.3.m: More sacred than all rivers is Narmadā, who came forth from the body of Rudra, / and [sacred] above all streams by the granting of a boon by the great-souled one. 6.29

6.3.s:
śaṃkarānuprahāddevī mahāpātakanāśinī .
yasmānmahārṇave ghore dṛśyate mahatī ca sā .. 6.30 ..
6.3.d:
शंकरानुप्रहाद्देवी महापातकनाशिनी .
यस्मान्महार्णवे घोरे दृश्यते महती च सा .. 6.30 ..
6.3.m: By the grace of Śaṃkara, she is the goddess who destroys great sins, / since she is seen as great even within the dreadful great ocean. 6.30

6.3.s:
suvyaktāṅgī mahākāyā mahatī tena sā smṛtā .
tasmādvikṣobhyamāṇā hi diggajairambudopamaiḥ .. 6.31 ..
6.3.d:
सुव्यक्ताङ्गी महाकाया महती तेन सा स्मृता .
तस्माद्विक्षोभ्यमाणा हि दिग्गजैरम्बुदोपमैः .. 6.31 ..
6.3.m: With well-manifest limbs and a vast form, therefore she is known as Mahatī. / Agitated by the world-elephants resembling rain-clouds,

6.3.s:
kaluṣatvaṃ nayatyeva rasena surasā tathā .
kṛpāṃ karoti sā yasmāllokānāmabhayapradā .. 6.32 ..
6.3.d:
कलुषत्वं नयत्येव रसेन सुरसा तथा .
कृपां करोति सा यस्माल्लोकानामभयप्रदा .. 6.32 ..
6.3.m: she indeed leads to turbidity with her sweet water, and thus is Surasā. / Because she grants compassion and bestows fearlessness upon creatures,

6.3.s:
saṃsārārṇavamagnānāṃ tena caiṣā kṛpā smṛtā .
purā kṛtayuge puṇye divyamandārabhūṣitā .. 6.33 ..
6.3.d:
संसारार्णवमग्नानां तेन चैषा कृपा स्मृता .
पुरा कृतयुगे पुण्ये दिव्यमन्दारभूषिता .. 6.33 ..
6.3.m: sunk in the ocean of worldly existence, she is therefore called Kṛpā. / Formerly, in the holy Kṛta age, adorned with heavenly mandāra trees,

6.3.s:
kalpavṛkṣasamākīrṇā rohītakasamākulā .
vahatyeṣā ca mandena tena mandākinī smṛtā .. 6.34 ..
6.3.d:
कल्पवृक्षसमाकीर्णा रोहीतकसमाकुला .
वहत्येषा च मन्देन तेन मन्दाकिनी स्मृता .. 6.34 ..
6.3.m: thronged with wish-granting trees and filled with rohītaka trees, / she flows gently, and therefore she is known as Mandākinī.

6.3.s:
bhittvā mahārṇavaṃ kṣipraṃ yasmāllokamihāgatā .
pūjyā suraiśca siddhaiśca tasmādeṣā mahārṇavā .. 6.35 ..
6.3.d:
भित्त्वा महार्णवं क्षिप्रं यस्माल्लोकमिहागता .
पूज्या सुरैश्च सिद्धैश्च तस्मादेषा महार्णवा .. 6.35 ..
6.3.m: Because, having quickly cleaved the great ocean, she arrived here in this world, / worthy of worship by the gods and siddhas, therefore she is Mahārṇavā.

6.3.s: vicitrotpalasaṃghātairṛkṣadvipasamākulā .. 6.36 ..
6.3.d: विचित्रोत्पलसंघातैरृक्षद्विपसमाकुला .. 6.36 ..
6.3.m: [Filled] with clusters of diverse lotuses, crowded with bears and elephants,

6.3.s:
bhittvā śailaṃ ca vipulaṃ prayātyevaṃ mahārṇavam .
bhrāmayantī diśaḥ sarvā raveṇa mahatā purā .. 6.37 ..
6.3.d:
भित्त्वा शैलं च विपुलं प्रयात्येवं महार्णवम् .
भ्रामयन्ती दिशः सर्वा रवेण महता पुरा .. 6.37 ..
6.3.m: she splits the vast mountain and thus proceeds to the great ocean. / Formerly, making all the directions echo with a great roar,

6.3.s:
plāvayantī virājantī tena revā iti smṛtā .
bhāryāputrasuduḥkhāḍhyānnarāñchāpaiḥ samāvṛtān .. 6.38 ..
6.3.d:
प्लावयन्ती विराजन्ती तेन रेवा इति स्मृता .
भार्यापुत्रसुदुःखाढ्यान्नराञ्छापैः समावृतान् .. 6.38 ..
6.3.m: flooding and shining brightly, therefore she is known as Revā. / Bringing men beset by curses and deeply afflicted by grief over wives and sons

6.3.s:
vipāpānkurute yasmādvipāpā tena sā smṛtā .
viṇmūtranicayāṃ ghorāṃ pāṃśuśoṇitakardamām .. 6.39 ..
6.3.d:
विपापान्कुरुते यस्माद्विपापा तेन सा स्मृता .
विण्मूत्रनिचयां घोरां पांशुशोणितकर्दमाम् .. 6.39 ..
6.3.m: to freedom from sin, because of that she is known as Vipāpā. / From the terrible bondage of feces and urine, mired in dust and blood,

6.3.s:
pāśairnityaṃ tu sambādhāṃ yasmānmocayate bhṛśam .
vipāśeti ca sā proktā saṃsārārṇavatāriṇī .. 6.40 ..
6.3.d:
पाशैर्नित्यं तु सम्बाधां यस्मान्मोचयते भृशम् .
विपाशेति च सा प्रोक्ता संसारार्णवतारिणी .. 6.40 ..
6.3.m: because she constantly and completely releases [men] bound by snares, / she is called Vipāśā, she who carries one across the ocean of worldly existence.

6.3.s:
narmadā vimalāmbhā ca vimalenduśubhānanā .
tamobhūte mahāghore yasmādeṣā mahāprabhā .. 6.41 ..
6.3.d:
नर्मदा विमलाम्भा च विमलेन्दुशुभानना .
तमोभूते महाघोरे यस्मादेषा महाप्रभा .. 6.41 ..
6.3.m: Narmadā has spotless waters and a fair face like the spotless moon. / Since, when all had become profound darkness, she was of great splendor,

6.3.s:
vimalā tena sā proktā vidvadbhirnṛpasattama .
karairindukaraprakhyaiḥ sūryaraśmisamaprabhā .. 6.42 ..
6.3.d:
विमला तेन सा प्रोक्ता विद्वद्भिर्नृपसत्तम .
करैरिन्दुकरप्रख्यैः सूर्यरश्मिसमप्रभा .. 6.42 ..
6.3.m: she is therefore called Vimalā by the wise, O best of kings. / With rays resembling the beams of the moon, having a brilliance equal to the sun’s rays,

6.3.s:
kṣarantī modate viśvaṃ karabhā tena cocyate .
yasmādrañjayate lokāndarśanādeva bhārata .. 6.43 ..
6.3.d:
क्षरन्ती मोदते विश्वं करभा तेन चोच्यते .
यस्माद्रञ्जयते लोकान्दर्शनादेव भारत .. 6.43 ..
6.3.m: she trickles forth and gladdens the universe; therefore she is called Karabhā. / Because she delights the worlds by her very sight, O Bhārata,

6.3.s:
rañjanādrañjanā proktā dhātvarthe rājasattama .
tṛṇavīrudhagulmādyāstiryañcaḥ pakṣiṇastathā .
tānudbhūtānnayetsvargaṃ tenoktā vāyuvāhinī .. 6.44 ..
6.3.d:
रञ्जनाद्रञ्जना प्रोक्ता धात्वर्थे राजसत्तम .
तृणवीरुधगुल्माद्यास्तिर्यञ्चः पक्षिणस्तथा .
तानुद्भूतान्नयेत्स्वर्गं तेनोक्ता वायुवाहिनी .. 6.44 ..
6.3.m: from [the root meaning] 'to delight', she is called Rañjanā according to the verbal root, O best of kings. / Grasses, creeping plants, shrubs, and so forth, as well as animals and birds— / those born [there] she leads to heaven, and therefore she is called Vāyuvāhinī.

6.3.s:
evaṃ yo vetti nāmāni nirgamaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ .
sa yāti pāpavirmukto rudralokaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .. 6.45 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe narmadāmāhātmye sahaitukarevānāmamāhātmyavarṇane mayūrakalpasamudbhavo nāma ṣaṣṭho'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 7
6.3.d:
एवं यो वेत्ति नामानि निर्गमं च विशेषतः .
स याति पापविर्मुक्तो रुद्रलोकं न संशयः .. 6.45 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे नर्मदामाहात्म्ये सहैतुकरेवानाममाहात्म्यवर्णने मयूरकल्पसमुद्भवो नाम षष्ठोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 7
6.3.m:
Whoever knows these names and her origin in this manner, / freed from sin, he goes to the world of Rudra, without doubt.
Thus ends the sixth chapter, named 'The Origin in the Mayūrakalpa', in the explanation of the greatness of the reasoned names of the Revā, in the glorification of the Narmadā, in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 7

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
punarekārṇave ghore naṣṭe sthāvarajaṃgame .
salilenāplute loke nirāloke tamodbhave .. 7.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
पुनरेकार्णवे घोरे नष्टे स्थावरजंगमे .
सलिलेनाप्लुते लोके निरालोके तमोद्भवे .. 7.1 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Once again, in the dreadful single cosmic ocean, when all mobile and immobile beings had vanished, / when the world was inundated with water, devoid of light, and enveloped in darkness,

6.3.s:
brahmaiko vicaraṃstatra tamībhūte mahārṇave .
divyavarṣasahasraṃ tu khadyota iva rūpavān .. 7.2 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रह्मैको विचरंस्तत्र तमीभूते महार्णवे .
दिव्यवर्षसहस्रं तु खद्योत इव रूपवान् .. 7.2 ..
6.3.m: Brahmā alone, wandering there in that ocean enveloped in darkness / for a thousand divine years, possessed of form like a firefly,

6.3.s:
śete yojanasāhasramaprameyamanuttamam .
dvādaśādityasaṃkāśaṃ sahasracaraṇekṣaṇam .. 7.3 ..
6.3.d:
शेते योजनसाहस्रमप्रमेयमनुत्तमम् .
द्वादशादित्यसंकाशं सहस्रचरणेक्षणम् .. 7.3 ..
6.3.m: saw [the Lord] lying over a thousand yojanas, immeasurable, unsurpassable, / resembling twelve suns, having a thousand feet and eyes,

6.3.s:
prasuptaṃ cārṇave ghore hyapaśyatkūrmarūpiṇam .
taṃ dṛṣṭvā vismayāpanno brahmā bodhayate śanaiḥ .. 7.4 ..
6.3.d:
प्रसुप्तं चार्णवे घोरे ह्यपश्यत्कूर्मरूपिणम् .
तं दृष्ट्वा विस्मयापन्नो ब्रह्मा बोधयते शनैः .. 7.4 ..
6.3.m: fast asleep in the dreadful ocean in the form of a tortoise. / Seeing him, filled with astonishment, Brahmā gently awakened him

6.3.s:
stutibhirmaṃgalaiścaiva vedavedāṃgasaṃbhavaiḥ .
vācaspate vibudhyasva mahābhūta namo'stu te .. 7.5 ..
6.3.d:
स्तुतिभिर्मंगलैश्चैव वेदवेदांगसंभवैः .
वाचस्पते विबुध्यस्व महाभूत नमोऽस्तु ते .. 7.5 ..
6.3.m: with auspicious praises arising from the Vedas and their auxiliary limbs: / 'O Lord of speech, awaken, O great being, obeisance to you!

6.3.s:
tavodare jagatsarvaṃ tiṣṭhate parameśvara .
tadvimuñca mahāsattva yatpūrvaṃ saṃhṛtaṃ tvayā .. 7.6 ..
6.3.d:
तवोदरे जगत्सर्वं तिष्ठते परमेश्वर .
तद्विमुञ्च महासत्त्व यत्पूर्वं संहृतं त्वया .. 7.6 ..
6.3.m: The entire universe resides in your belly, O supreme lord. / Release that, O being of great power, which was previously withdrawn by you.

6.3.s:
vyatītā rajanī brāhmī dinaṃ samanuvartate .
nirīkṣya sarvalokeśa yena saṃbhavate jagat .. 7.7 ..
6.3.d:
व्यतीता रजनी ब्राह्मी दिनं समनुवर्तते .
निरीक्ष्य सर्वलोकेश येन संभवते जगत् .. 7.7 ..
6.3.m: The night of Brahmā has passed; the day now follows. / Look forth, O Lord of all worlds, by whom the universe comes into being.'

6.3.s:
sa niśamya vacastasya utthitaḥ parameśvaraḥ .
samudgiran sa lokāṃstrīn grastān kalpakṣaye tadā .. 7.8 ..
6.3.d:
स निशम्य वचस्तस्य उत्थितः परमेश्वरः .
समुद्गिरन् स लोकांस्त्रीन् ग्रस्तान् कल्पक्षये तदा .. 7.8 ..
6.3.m: Hearing his words, that supreme lord arose, / vomiting forth the three worlds swallowed at the end of the kalpa.

6.3.s:
devadānavagandharvāḥ sayakṣoragarākṣasāḥ .
sacandrārkagrahāḥ sarve śarīrāttasya nirgatāḥ .. 7.9 ..
6.3.d:
देवदानवगन्धर्वाः सयक्षोरगराक्षसाः .
सचन्द्रार्कग्रहाः सर्वे शरीरात्तस्य निर्गताः .. 7.9 ..
6.3.m: The gods, Dānavas, and Gandharvas, together with Yakṣas, serpents, and Rākṣasas, / along with the moon, sun, and planets, all came forth from his body.

6.3.s:
tato hyekārṇavaṃ sarvaṃ vibhajya parameśvaraḥ .
vistīrṇopalatoyaughāṃ saritsaravivardhitām .. 7.10 ..
6.3.d:
ततो ह्येकार्णवं सर्वं विभज्य परमेश्वरः .
विस्तीर्णोपलतोयौघां सरित्सरविवर्धिताम् .. 7.10 ..
6.3.m: Then, having divided that entire single cosmic ocean, the supreme lord / saw the earth, with its expansive rock and torrents of water, magnified by rivers and lakes,

6.3.s:
paśyate medinīṃ devaḥ savṛkṣauṣadhipalvalām .
himavantaṃ giriśreṣṭhaṃ śvetaṃ parvatamuttamam .. 7.11 ..
6.3.d:
पश्यते मेदिनीं देवः सवृक्षौषधिपल्वलाम् .
हिमवन्तं गिरिश्रेष्ठं श्वेतं पर्वतमुत्तमम् .. 7.11 ..
6.3.m: the god [saw] the earth with its trees, medicinal herbs, and pools; / the Himavat, the best of mountains; Śveta, the supreme mountain;

6.3.s:
śṛṅgavantaṃ mahāśailaṃ ye cānye kulaparvatāḥ .
jaṃbudvīpaṃ kuśaṃ krauñcaṃ sagomedaṃ saśālmalam .. 7.12 ..
6.3.d:
शृङ्गवन्तं महाशैलं ये चान्ये कुलपर्वताः .
जंबुद्वीपं कुशं क्रौञ्चं सगोमेदं सशाल्मलम् .. 7.12 ..
6.3.m: the great mountain Śṛṅgavat, and whatever other principal mountain ranges [there be]; / Jambudvīpa, Kuśadvīpa, Krauñcadvīpa, along with Gomedadvīpa and Śālmaladvīpa;

6.3.s:
puṣkarāntāśca ye dvīpā ye ca saptamahārṇavāḥ .
lokālokaṃ mahāśailaṃ sarvaṃ ca purataḥ sthitam .. 7.13 ..
6.3.d:
पुष्करान्ताश्च ये द्वीपा ये च सप्तमहार्णवाः .
लोकालोकं महाशैलं सर्वं च पुरतः स्थितम् .. 7.13 ..
6.3.m: and the islands ending with Puṣkara, as well as the seven great oceans; / the great mountain Lokāloka—he saw all standing before him,

6.3.s:
catuḥprakṛtisaṃyuktaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṃgamam .
yugānte tu viniṣkrāntamapaśyatsa maheśvaraḥ .. 7.14 ..
6.3.d:
चतुःप्रकृतिसंयुक्तं जगत्स्थावरजंगमम् .
युगान्ते तु विनिष्क्रान्तमपश्यत्स महेश्वरः .. 7.14 ..
6.3.m: the universe of mobile and immobile beings, endowed with the four kinds of creation. / That Maheśvara saw it emerged at the close of the yuga.

6.3.s:
viprakīrṇaśilājālāmapaśyatsa vasuṃdharām .
kūrmapṛṣṭhopagāṃ devīṃ mahārṇavagatāṃ prabhuḥ .. 7.15 ..
6.3.d:
विप्रकीर्णशिलाजालामपश्यत्स वसुंधराम् .
कूर्मपृष्ठोपगां देवीं महार्णवगतां प्रभुः .. 7.15 ..
6.3.m: The Lord saw the earth, its masses of rocks scattered abroad, / the goddess resting upon the back of the tortoise, situated in the great ocean.

6.3.s:
tasmin viśīrṇaśailāgre saritsarovivarjite .
nānātaraṃgabhinnoda āvartodvartasaṃkule .. 7.16 ..
6.3.d:
तस्मिन् विशीर्णशैलाग्रे सरित्सरोविवर्जिते .
नानातरंगभिन्नोद आवर्तोद्वर्तसंकुले .. 7.16 ..
6.3.m: In that [ocean], where the peaks of mountains were shattered, devoid of rivers and lakes, / its waters broken by manifold waves, crowded with whirlpools and surges,

6.3.s:
nānauṣadhiprajvalite nānotpalaśilātale .
nānāvihaṃgasaṃghuṣṭāṃ matsyakūrmasamākulām .. 7.17 ..
6.3.d:
नानौषधिप्रज्वलिते नानोत्पलशिलातले .
नानाविहंगसंघुष्टां मत्स्यकूर्मसमाकुलाम् .. 7.17 ..
6.3.m: blazing with diverse medicinal plants, with rocky beds covered by manifold lotuses, / resounded by various birds, teeming with fish and tortoises,

6.3.s:
divyamāyāmayīṃ devīmutkṛṣṭāmbudasannibhām .
nadīmapaśyaddeveśo hyanaupamyajalāśayām .. 7.18 ..
6.3.d:
दिव्यमायामयीं देवीमुत्कृष्टाम्बुदसन्निभाम् .
नदीमपश्यद्देवेशो ह्यनौपम्यजलाशयाम् .. 7.18 ..
6.3.m: the Lord of the gods saw a river, the goddess fashioned of divine māyā, / resembling an excellent rain-cloud, her reservoir of water beyond compare.

6.3.s:
madhye tasyāmbudaśyāmāṃ pīnorujaghanastanīm .
vastrairanupamairdivyairnānābharaṇabhūṣitām .. 7.19 ..
6.3.d:
मध्ये तस्याम्बुदश्यामां पीनोरुजघनस्तनीम् .
वस्त्रैरनुपमैर्दिव्यैर्नानाभरणभूषिताम् .. 7.19 ..
6.3.m: In her midst [he saw her], dark as a rain-cloud, with swelling thighs, hips, and breasts, / adorned with incomparable, divine garments and diverse ornaments,

6.3.s:
sanūpuraravoddāmāṃ hārakeyūramaṇḍitām .
tādṛśīṃ narmadāṃ devīṃ svayaṃ strīrūpadhāriṇīm .. 7.20 ..
6.3.d:
सनूपुररवोद्दामां हारकेयूरमण्डिताम् .
तादृशीं नर्मदां देवीं स्वयं स्त्रीरूपधारिणीम् .. 7.20 ..
6.3.m: resounding wildly with the sound of anklets, decorated with necklaces and armlets— / he saw such a goddess Narmadā, directly assuming the form of a woman,

6.3.s:
yogamāyāmayaiścitrairbhūṣaṇaiḥ svairvibhūṣitām .
avyaktāṅgīṃ mahābhāgāmapaśyatsa tu narmadām .. 7.21 ..
6.3.d:
योगमायामयैश्चित्रैर्भूषणैः स्वैर्विभूषिताम् .
अव्यक्ताङ्गीं महाभागामपश्यत्स तु नर्मदाम् .. 7.21 ..
6.3.m: adorned with her own wondrous ornaments fashioned of yogamāyā, / with unmanifest limbs, the highly fortunate Narmadā.

6.3.s:
ardhodyatabhujāṃ bālāṃ padmapatrāyatekṣaṇām .
stuvantīṃ devadeveśamutthitāṃ tu jalāttadā .. 7.22 ..
6.3.d:
अर्धोद्यतभुजां बालां पद्मपत्रायतेक्षणाम् .
स्तुवन्तीं देवदेवेशमुत्थितां तु जलात्तदा .. 7.22 ..
6.3.m: A maiden with half-raised arms, her eyes wide as lotus petals, / praising the god of gods, having arisen from the water.

6.3.s:
vismayāviṣṭahṛdayo hyahamudvīkṣya tāṃ śubhām .
snātvā jale śubhe tasyāḥ stotumabhyudyatastataḥ .. 7.23 ..
6.3.d:
विस्मयाविष्टहृदयो ह्यहमुद्वीक्ष्य तां शुभाम् .
स्नात्वा जले शुभे तस्याः स्तोतुमभ्युद्यतस्ततः .. 7.23 ..
6.3.m: Beholding that auspicious one, my heart filled with wonder, / having bathed in her auspicious water, I then prepared to praise her.

6.3.s:
arcayāmāsa saṃhṛṣṭo mantrairvedāṃgasaṃbhavaiḥ .
sṛṣṭaṃ ca tatpurā rājanpaśyeyaṃ sacarācaram .. 7.24 ..
6.3.d:
अर्चयामास संहृष्टो मन्त्रैर्वेदांगसंभवैः .
सृष्टं च तत्पुरा राजन्पश्येयं सचराचरम् .. 7.24 ..
6.3.m: Full of joy, I worshipped her with mantras born from the Vedas and their auxiliary limbs. / 'May I see that which was created of old, O king, with all that moves and is still,

6.3.s:
sadevāsuragandharvaṃ sapannagamahoragam .
paśyāmyeṣā mahābhāgā naiva yātā kṣayaṃ purā .. 7.25 ..
6.3.d:
सदेवासुरगन्धर्वं सपन्नगमहोरगम् .
पश्याम्येषा महाभागा नैव याता क्षयं पुरा .. 7.25 ..
6.3.m: with gods, asuras, and Gandharvas, with serpents and great snakes!' / I see that this highly fortunate one never went to destruction in the past,

6.3.s:
mahādevaprasādācca taccharīrasamudbhavā .
bhūyo bhūyo mayā dṛṣṭā kathitā te nṛpottama .. 7.26 ..
6.3.d:
महादेवप्रसादाच्च तच्छरीरसमुद्भवा .
भूयो भूयो मया दृष्टा कथिता ते नृपोत्तम .. 7.26 ..
6.3.m: and by the grace of Mahādeva, she was born from his body. / Seen again and again by me, she has been described to you, O best of kings.

6.3.s:
prādurbhāvamimaṃ kaurmyaṃ ye'dhīyante dvijottamāḥ .
ye'pi śṛṇvanti vidvāṃso mucyante te'pi kilbiṣaiḥ .. 7.27 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe narmadāmāhātmye kūrmakalpasamudbhavo nāma saptamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 8
6.3.d:
प्रादुर्भावमिमं कौर्म्यं येऽधीयन्ते द्विजोत्तमाः .
येऽपि शृण्वन्ति विद्वांसो मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि किल्बिषैः .. 7.27 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे नर्मदामाहात्म्ये कूर्मकल्पसमुद्भवो नाम सप्तमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 8
6.3.m:
Those best of twice-born who study this manifestation relating to the tortoise, / and the wise who hear it, they too are freed from sins.
Thus ends the seventh chapter, named "Origin of the Tortoise Kalpa," in the Māhātmya of the Narmadā, in the Revākhaṇḍa, in the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the Mahāpurāṇa of Skanda containing eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 8

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
naṣṭe loke punaścānye salilena samāvṛte .
mahārṇavasya madhyastho bāhubhyāmataraṃ jalam .. 8.1 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
नष्टे लोके पुनश्चान्ये सलिलेन समावृते .
महार्णवस्य मध्यस्थो बाहुभ्यामतरं जलम् .. 8.1 ..
6.3.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / When the world was destroyed again and covered with water, / standing in the midst of the great ocean, I swam the water with my arms. 8.1

6.3.s:
divye varṣaśate pūrṇe śrānto'haṃ nṛpasattama .
dhyātuṃ samārabhaṃ devaṃ mahadarṇavatāraṇam .. 8.2 ..
6.3.d:
दिव्ये वर्षशते पूर्णे श्रान्तोऽहं नृपसत्तम .
ध्यातुं समारभं देवं महदर्णवतारणम् .. 8.2 ..
6.3.m: When a divine century of years was complete, I grew weary, O best of kings; / I began to meditate on the God who ferries across the great ocean. 8.2

6.3.s:
dhyāyamānastataḥ kāle apaśyaṃ pakṣiṇaṃ param .
hārakundendusaṃkāśaṃ bakaṃ gokṣīrapāṇḍuram .. 8.3 ..
6.3.d:
ध्यायमानस्ततः काले अपश्यं पक्षिणं परम् .
हारकुन्देन्दुसंकाशं बकं गोक्षीरपाण्डुरम् .. 8.3 ..
6.3.m: Then, while meditating, in due course I saw an extraordinary bird: / a crane resembling a pearl necklace, a kunda flower, or the moon, white as cow's milk. 8.3

6.3.s:
tato'haṃ vismayāviṣṭastaṃ bakaṃ samudīkṣya vai .
asminmahārṇave ghore kuto'yaṃ pakṣisaṃbhavaḥ .. 8.4 ..
6.3.d:
ततोऽहं विस्मयाविष्टस्तं बकं समुदीक्ष्य वै .
अस्मिन्महार्णवे घोरे कुतोऽयं पक्षिसंभवः .. 8.4 ..
6.3.m: Then, filled with astonishment upon looking at that crane: / "In this dreadful great ocean, from where has this bird arisen?" 8.4

6.3.s:
taranbāhubhiraśrāntastaṃ bakaṃ pratyabhāṣiṣi .
pākṣarūpaṃ samāsthāya kastvamekārṇavīkṛte .. 8.5 ..
6.3.d:
तरन्बाहुभिरश्रान्तस्तं बकं प्रत्यभाषिषि .
पाक्षरूपं समास्थाय कस्त्वमेकार्णवीकृते .. 8.5 ..
6.3.m: Swimming with unwearied arms, I addressed that crane: / "Having assumed the form of a bird, who are you in [this world] turned into a single ocean? 8.5

6.3.s:
bhramase divyayogātmanmohayanniva māṃ prabho .
etatkathaya me sarvaṃ yo'si so'si namo'stu te .. 8.6 ..
6.3.d:
भ्रमसे दिव्ययोगात्मन्मोहयन्निव मां प्रभो .
एतत्कथय मे सर्वं योऽसि सोऽसि नमोऽस्तु ते .. 8.6 ..
6.3.m: You wander, O divine inner Self of yoga, seemingly bewildering me, O Lord! / Tell me all this; whoever you may be, praise be to you!" 8.6

6.3.s:
so'bravīnmāṃ mahādevo brahmāhaṃ viṣṇureva ca .
jagatsarvaṃ mayā vatsa saṃhṛtaṃ kiṃ na budhyase .. 8.7 ..
6.3.d:
सोऽब्रवीन्मां महादेवो ब्रह्माहं विष्णुरेव च .
जगत्सर्वं मया वत्स संहृतं किं न बुध्यसे .. 8.7 ..
6.3.m: He said to me: "I am Mahādeva, I am Brahmā, and also Viṣṇu. / All the universe has been withdrawn by me, my child; do you not comprehend? 8.7

6.3.s:
tava mātā pitāhaṃ vai viśvasya ca mahāmune .
kāruṇyaṃ mama saṃjātaṃ dṛṣṭvā magnaṃ mahārṇave .. 8.8 ..
6.3.d:
तव माता पिताहं वै विश्वस्य च महामुने .
कारुण्यं मम संजातं दृष्ट्वा मग्नं महार्णवे .. 8.8 ..
6.3.m: I am indeed your mother and father, and of the universe, O great sage. / Compassion arose in me upon seeing you submerged in the great ocean. 8.8

6.3.s:
pakṣirūpaṃ samāsthāya ato'trāhaṃ samāgataḥ .
kimarthamāturo bhūtvā bhramasītthaṃ mahārṇave .. 8.9 ..
6.3.d:
पक्षिरूपं समास्थाय अतोऽत्राहं समागतः .
किमर्थमातुरो भूत्वा भ्रमसीत्थं महार्णवे .. 8.9 ..
6.3.m: Having assumed the form of a bird, therefore I have come here. / Why, having become distressed, do you wander thus in the great ocean? 8.9

6.3.s:
śīghraṃ praviśa matpakṣau yena viśramase dvija .
evamuktastatastena devenāhaṃ nareśvara .. 8.10 ..
6.3.d:
शीघ्रं प्रविश मत्पक्षौ येन विश्रमसे द्विज .
एवमुक्तस्ततस्तेन देवेनाहं नरेश्वर .. 8.10 ..
6.3.m: Quickly enter my wings, whereby you may rest, O twice-born." / Having been addressed thus by that God, O ruler of men, 8.10

6.3.s:
tato'haṃ tasya pakṣānte pralīnastu bhramañjale .
kāle yugasāhasrānte aśrānto'rṇavamadhyagaḥ .. 8.11 ..
6.3.d:
ततोऽहं तस्य पक्षान्ते प्रलीनस्तु भ्रमञ्जले .
काले युगसाहस्रान्ते अश्रान्तोऽर्णवमध्यगः .. 8.11 ..
6.3.m: then I merged into the edge of his wing, wandering in the water; / at the end of a thousand yugas, I remained unwearied in the midst of the ocean. 8.11

6.3.s:
tataḥ śṛṇomi sahasā dikṣu sarvāsu suvrata .
kiṃcinnūpurasaṃmiśramadbhutaṃ śabdamuttamam .. 8.12 ..
6.3.d:
ततः शृणोमि सहसा दिक्षु सर्वासु सुव्रत .
किंचिन्नूपुरसंमिश्रमद्भुतं शब्दमुत्तमम् .. 8.12 ..
6.3.m: Then suddenly I heard in all the directions, O one of good vows, / a certain wondrous, excellent sound mingled with the tinkle of anklets. 8.12

6.3.s:
tadārṇavajalaṃ sarvaṃ saṃkṣiptaṃ sahasābhavat .
kimetaditi saṃcintya diśaḥ samavalokayam .. 8.13 ..
6.3.d:
तदार्णवजलं सर्वं संक्षिप्तं सहसाभवत् .
किमेतदिति संचिन्त्य दिशः समवलोकयम् .. 8.13 ..
6.3.m: Then all that water of the ocean was suddenly gathered up. / Thinking, "What is this?", I looked toward the directions. 8.13

6.3.s:
daśa kanyāstato dikṣu āgatāśca mahārṇave .
vastrālaṃkārasahitā digbhyo nūpurabhūṣitāḥ .. 8.14 ..
6.3.d:
दश कन्यास्ततो दिक्षु आगताश्च महार्णवे .
वस्त्रालंकारसहिता दिग्भ्यो नूपुरभूषिताः .. 8.14 ..
6.3.m: Then ten maidens arrived in the great ocean in the directions, / adorned with clothes and ornaments, graced with anklets from the directions. 8.14

6.3.s:
kāciccandrasamābhāsā kācidādityasaprabhā .
kācidaṃjanapuñjābhā kācidraktotpalaprabhā .. 8.15 ..
6.3.d:
काचिच्चन्द्रसमाभासा काचिदादित्यसप्रभा .
काचिदंजनपुञ्जाभा काचिद्रक्तोत्पलप्रभा .. 8.15 ..
6.3.m: One had the radiance of the moon, one had the luster of the sun, / one had the splendor of a mass of collyrium, one had the brilliance of a red lotus. 8.15

6.3.s:
nānārūpadharā saumyā nānābharaṇabhūṣitā .
arghyapādyādibhirmālyairbakamabhyarcya suvratāḥ .. 8.16 ..
6.3.d:
नानारूपधरा सौम्या नानाभरणभूषिता .
अर्घ्यपाद्यादिभिर्माल्यैर्बकमभ्यर्च्य सुव्रताः .. 8.16 ..
6.3.m: Bearing various forms, gentle, adorned with various ornaments, / having worshipped the crane with offerings of arghya, pādya, and the like, and with garlands, those women of good vows, 8.16

6.3.s:
tatastaṃ parvatākāraṃ guhyaṃ pakṣiṇamavyayam .
praviveśa mahāghoraṃ parvato hyarṇavaṃ svarāṭ .. 8.17 ..
6.3.d:
ततस्तं पर्वताकारं गुह्यं पक्षिणमव्ययम् .
प्रविवेश महाघोरं पर्वतो ह्यर्णवं स्वराट् .. 8.17 ..
6.3.m: then entered that secret, imperishable bird shaped like a mountain; / the mountain, truly the sovereign of the ocean, entered the greatly dreadful [abyss]. 8.17

6.3.s:
yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi tāvantyeva śatāni ca .
triṃśadyojanasāhasraṃ yāvadbhūmaṇḍalaṃ tviti .. 8.18 ..
6.3.d:
योजनानां सहस्राणि तावन्त्येव शतानि च .
त्रिंशद्योजनसाहस्रं यावद्भूमण्डलं त्विति .. 8.18 ..
6.3.m: Thousands of yojanas and as many hundreds, / thirty thousand yojanas, extending as far as the terrestrial globe. 8.18

6.3.s:
tato bhūmaṇḍalaṃ divyaṃ pañcaratnasamākulam .
divyasphaṭikasopānaṃ rukmastaṃbhamanoramam .. 8.19 ..
6.3.d:
ततो भूमण्डलं दिव्यं पञ्चरत्नसमाकुलम् .
दिव्यस्फटिकसोपानं रुक्मस्तंभमनोरमम् .. 8.19 ..
6.3.m: Then [I saw] a divine terrestrial realm filled with the five gems, / with divine steps of crystal, charming with pillars of gold, 8.19

6.3.s:
yojanānāṃ sahasraṃ tu vistarāddviguṇāyatam .
vāpīkūpasamākīrṇaṃ prāsādāṭṭālakāvṛtam .. 8.20 ..
6.3.d:
योजनानां सहस्रं तु विस्तराद्द्विगुणायतम् .
वापीकूपसमाकीर्णं प्रासादाट्टालकावृतम् .. 8.20 ..
6.3.m: a thousand yojanas in breadth and twice that in length, / crowded with step-wells and wells, surrounded by palaces and turrets, 8.20

6.3.s:
kalpavṛkṣasamākīrṇaṃ dhvajaṣaṣṭivibhūṣitam .
tasminpuravare ramye nānāratnopaśobhitam .. 8.21 ..
6.3.d:
कल्पवृक्षसमाकीर्णं ध्वजषष्टिविभूषितम् .
तस्मिन्पुरवरे रम्ये नानारत्नोपशोभितम् .. 8.21 ..
6.3.m: crowded with wish-granting trees, adorned with sixty banners. / In that delightful, best of cities, beautified with various gems, 8.21

6.3.s:
tathānyacca puraṃ ramyaṃ patākojjvalavedikam .
śatayojanavistīrṇaṃ tāvaddviguṇamāyatam .. 8.22 ..
6.3.d:
तथान्यच्च पुरं रम्यं पताकोज्ज्वलवेदिकम् .
शतयोजनविस्तीर्णं तावद्द्विगुणमायतम् .. 8.22 ..
6.3.m: there was likewise another delightful city whose altars shone with banners, / a hundred yojanas broad and twice that in length. 8.22

6.3.s:
puramadhye tatastasminnadī paramaśobhanā .
mahatī puṇyasalilā nānāratnaśilā tathā .. 8.23 ..
6.3.d:
पुरमध्ये ततस्तस्मिन्नदी परमशोभना .
महती पुण्यसलिला नानारत्नशिला तथा .. 8.23 ..
6.3.m: Then in the midst of that city was an exceedingly beautiful river, / vast, with sacred waters, and with rocks of various gems. 8.23

6.3.s:
tasyāstīre mayā dṛṣṭaṃ taḍitsūryasamaprabham .
indranīlamahānīlaiścitaṃ ratnaiḥ samantataḥ .. 8.24 ..
6.3.d:
तस्यास्तीरे मया दृष्टं तडित्सूर्यसमप्रभम् .
इन्द्रनीलमहानीलैश्चितं रत्नैः समन्ततः .. 8.24 ..
6.3.m: On its bank I saw [a liṅga] shining like lightning and the sun, / studded on all sides with sapphires and great sapphires, with jewels, 8.24

6.3.s:
kvacidvahnisamākāraṃ kvacidindrāyudhaprabham .
kvaciddhūmraṃ kvacitpītaṃ kvacidraktaṃ kvacitsitam .. 8.25 ..
6.3.d:
क्वचिद्वह्निसमाकारं क्वचिदिन्द्रायुधप्रभम् .
क्वचिद्धूम्रं क्वचित्पीतं क्वचिद्रक्तं क्वचित्सितम् .. 8.25 ..
6.3.m: in some parts looking like fire, in some parts radiant like a rainbow, / in some parts smoky, in some parts yellow, in some parts red, in some parts white; 8.25

6.3.s:
nānāvarṇaiḥ samāyuktaṃ liṅgamadbhutadarśanam .
brahmaviṣṇvindrasādhyaiśca samantātparivāritam .. 8.26 ..
6.3.d:
नानावर्णैः समायुक्तं लिङ्गमद्भुतदर्शनम् .
ब्रह्मविष्ण्विन्द्रसाध्यैश्च समन्तात्परिवारितम् .. 8.26 ..
6.3.m: endowed with various colors, a liṅga of wonderful appearance, / surrounded on all sides by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Indra, and the Sādhyas, 8.26

6.3.s:
nandīśvaragaṇādhyakṣaiścendrādityaiśca tadvṛtam .
paśyāmi liṅgamīśānaṃ mahāliṅgaṃ tameva ca .. 8.27 ..
6.3.d:
नन्दीश्वरगणाध्यक्षैश्चेन्द्रादित्यैश्च तद्वृतम् .
पश्यामि लिङ्गमीशानं महालिङ्गं तमेव च .. 8.27 ..
6.3.m: and encompassed by Nandīśvara and the leaders of the gaṇas, and by Indra and the Ādityas. / I saw that liṅga, Īśāna, that very Great Liṅga, 8.27

6.3.s:
parivārya tatastaṃ tu prasuptāndevadānavān .
nimīlitākṣānpaśyāmi divyābharaṇabhūṣitān .. 8.28 ..
6.3.d:
परिवार्य ततस्तं तु प्रसुप्तान्देवदानवान् .
निमीलिताक्षान्पश्यामि दिव्याभरणभूषितान् .. 8.28 ..
6.3.m: and surrounding it, I saw gods and Dānavas asleep, / with closed eyes, adorned with divine ornaments. 8.28

6.3.s:
tatastāḥ padmapatrākṣyo nāryaḥ paramasaṃmatāḥ .
nadyāstasyā jale snātvā divyapuṣpairmanoramaiḥ .. 8.29 ..
6.3.d:
ततस्ताः पद्मपत्राक्ष्यो नार्यः परमसंमताः .
नद्यास्तस्या जले स्नात्वा दिव्यपुष्पैर्मनोरमैः .. 8.29 ..
6.3.m: Then those women, lotus-petal-eyed, highly esteemed, / having bathed in the water of that river, with divine, delightful flowers, 8.29

6.3.s:
dattvārghapādyaṃ vidhivalliṃgasya saha pakṣiṇā .
arcayantīrvarārohā daśa tāḥ pramadottamāḥ .. 8.30 ..
6.3.d:
दत्त्वार्घपाद्यं विधिवल्लिंगस्य सह पक्षिणा .
अर्चयन्तीर्वरारोहा दश ताः प्रमदोत्तमाः .. 8.30 ..
6.3.m: having offered arghya and pādya according to rule to the liṅga along with the bird, / those ten excellent women of fair hips worshipped [it]. 8.30

6.3.s:
tatastvabhyarcya talliṅgaṃ tasminneva purottame .
sarvā adarśanaṃ jagmurvidyuto'bhragaṇeṣviva .. 8.31 ..
6.3.d:
ततस्त्वभ्यर्च्य तल्लिङ्गं तस्मिन्नेव पुरोत्तमे .
सर्वा अदर्शनं जग्मुर्विद्युतोऽभ्रगणेष्विव .. 8.31 ..
6.3.m: Then, having worshipped that liṅga in that very best of cities, / they all vanished from sight like flashes of lightning in masses of clouds. 8.31

6.3.s:
na cāsau pakṣirāṭtasminna striyo na ca devatāḥ .
tadevaikaṃ sthitaṃ liṅgamarcayanvismayānvitaḥ .. 8.32 ..
6.3.d:
न चासौ पक्षिराट्तस्मिन्न स्त्रियो न च देवताः .
तदेवैकं स्थितं लिङ्गमर्चयन्विस्मयान्वितः .. 8.32 ..
6.3.m: And neither was that king of birds there, nor the women, nor the deities; / filled with wonder, I worshipped that single liṅga that remained. 8.32

6.3.s:
tato'haṃ duḥkhamūḍhātmā rudramāyeti cintayan .
tataḥ kanyāḥ samuttīrya divyāṃbaravibhūṣaṇāḥ .. 8.33 ..
6.3.d:
ततोऽहं दुःखमूढात्मा रुद्रमायेति चिन्तयन् .
ततः कन्याः समुत्तीर्य दिव्यांबरविभूषणाः .. 8.33 ..
6.3.m: Then, my mind bewildered with sorrow, thinking, "This is Rudra's illusion!", / maidens then emerged, adorned with divine garments and ornaments, 8.33

6.3.s:
bhāsayantyo jagatsarvaṃ vidyuto'bhragaṇāniva .
padmairhiraṇmayairdivyairarcayitvā śubhānanāḥ .. 8.34 ..
6.3.d:
भासयन्त्यो जगत्सर्वं विद्युतोऽभ्रगणानिव .
पद्मैर्हिरण्मयैर्दिव्यैरर्चयित्वा शुभाननाः .. 8.34 ..
6.3.m: illuminating the entire world like flashes of lightning in masses of clouds; / those fair-faced ones, having worshipped with divine golden lotuses, 8.34

6.3.s:
viviśustajjalaṃ kṣipraṃ samaṃtādvarabhūṣaṇāḥ .
tasminpuravare cānye tāmevāhaṃ punaḥpunaḥ .. 8.35 ..
6.3.d:
विविशुस्तज्जलं क्षिप्रं समंताद्वरभूषणाः .
तस्मिन्पुरवरे चान्ये तामेवाहं पुनःपुनः .. 8.35 ..
6.3.m: those women with excellent ornaments quickly entered that water on every side. / In that best of cities and in the other, again and again I 8.35

6.3.s:
paśyāmi hyamarāṃ kanyāmarcayantīṃ maheśvaram .
tato'haṃ tāṃ varārohāmapṛcchaṃ kamalekṣaṇām .. 8.36 ..
6.3.d:
पश्यामि ह्यमरां कन्यामर्चयन्तीं महेश्वरम् .
ततोऽहं तां वरारोहामपृच्छं कमलेक्षणाम् .. 8.36 ..
6.3.m: beheld that immortal maiden worshipping Maheśvara. / Then I asked that lotus-eyed woman of fair hips: 8.36

6.3.s:
kā tvamasminpure devi vasase śivamarcatī .
tāścāgatāḥ striyaḥ sarvāḥ kva gatāste gaṇeśvarāḥ .. 8.37 ..
6.3.d:
का त्वमस्मिन्पुरे देवि वससे शिवमर्चती .
ताश्चागताः स्त्रियः सर्वाः क्व गतास्ते गणेश्वराः .. 8.37 ..
6.3.m: "Who are you, O goddess, dwelling in this city, worshipping Śiva? / And all those women who arrived—where have they gone, and where have those lords of gaṇas gone? 8.37

6.3.s:
namo'stu te mahābhāge brūhi puṇye maheśvari .
tava prasādādvijñātumetadicchāmi suvrate .
dayāṃ kṛtvā mahādevi kathayasva mamānaghe .. 8.38 ..
6.3.d:
नमोऽस्तु ते महाभागे ब्रूहि पुण्ये महेश्वरि .
तव प्रसादाद्विज्ञातुमेतदिच्छामि सुव्रते .
दयां कृत्वा महादेवि कथयस्व ममानघे .. 8.38 ..
6.3.m: Praise be to you, O highly fortunate one! Speak, O holy one, O Maheśvarī! / By your grace I wish to know this, O one of good vows; / taking pity, O great goddess, tell me, O sinless one!" 8.38

6.3.s:
śryuvāca -
vismṛtāhaṃ kathaṃ vipra dṛṣṭvā kalpe purātane .
mā te'bhūtsmṛtivibhraṃśaḥ sā cāhaṃ kalpavāhinī .. 8.39 ..
6.3.d:
श्र्युवाच -
विस्मृताहं कथं विप्र दृष्ट्वा कल्पे पुरातने .
मा तेऽभूत्स्मृतिविभ्रंशः सा चाहं कल्पवाहिनी .. 8.39 ..
6.3.m: Śrī said: / "How is it that I am forgotten, O twice-born, having been seen in the ancient kalpa? / Let there be no loss of memory for you! I am that Kalpavāhinī, 8.39

6.3.s:
narmadā nāma vikhyātā rudradehādviniḥsṛtā .
yāstāḥ kanyāstvayā dṛṣṭā hyarcayantyo maheśvaram .. 8.40 ..
6.3.d:
नर्मदा नाम विख्याता रुद्रदेहाद्विनिःसृता .
यास्ताः कन्यास्त्वया दृष्टा ह्यर्चयन्त्यो महेश्वरम् .. 8.40 ..
6.3.m: renowned as Narmadā, issued from the body of Rudra. / Those maidens seen by you worshipping Maheśvara, 8.40

6.3.s:
yābhistviha samānītaḥ pakṣirājasamanvitāḥ .
diśastā viddhi sarveśāḥ sarvāstvaṃ munisattama .. 8.41 ..
6.3.d:
याभिस्त्विह समानीतः पक्षिराजसमन्विताः .
दिशस्ता विद्धि सर्वेशाः सर्वास्त्वं मुनिसत्तम .. 8.41 ..
6.3.m: by whom the king of birds was brought along here— / know them all to be the directions, the sovereign mistresses of all, O best of sages! 8.41

6.3.s:
tiryakpakṣisvarūpeṇa mahāyogī maheśvaraḥ .
ebhiḥ śivapurādvipra ānītaḥ sa maheśvaraḥ .. 8.42 ..
6.3.d:
तिर्यक्पक्षिस्वरूपेण महायोगी महेश्वरः .
एभिः शिवपुराद्विप्र आनीतः स महेश्वरः .. 8.42 ..
6.3.m: In the form of an animal bird is Maheśvara, the great yogin. / That Maheśvara was brought by them from the city of Śiva, O twice-born." 8.42

6.3.s:
saiṣa devo mahādevo liṅgamūrtirvyavasthitaḥ .
arcyate brahmaviṣṇvindraiḥ surāsurajagadguruḥ .. 8.43 ..
6.3.d:
सैष देवो महादेवो लिङ्गमूर्तिर्व्यवस्थितः .
अर्च्यते ब्रह्मविष्ण्विन्द्रैः सुरासुरजगद्गुरुः .. 8.43 ..
6.3.m: This very god is Mahādeva, established in the form of a liṅga; / he is worshipped by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Indra, the guru of the universe of gods and demons. 8.43

6.3.s:
layamāyāti yasmāddhi jagatsarvaṃ carācaram .
tena liṅgamiti proktaṃ purāṇajñairmaharṣibhiḥ .. 8.44 ..
6.3.d:
लयमायाति यस्माद्धि जगत्सर्वं चराचरम् .
तेन लिङ्गमिति प्रोक्तं पुराणज्ञैर्महर्षिभिः .. 8.44 ..
6.3.m: Because indeed the entire universe, moving and unmoving, attains dissolution [laya] in him, / it is therefore called liṅga by great seers who know the Purāṇas. 8.44

6.3.s:
tena devagaṇāḥ sarve saṃkṣiptā māyayā purā .
pralīnāścaiva lokeśa na dṛśyante hi sāṃpratam .. 8.45 ..
6.3.d:
तेन देवगणाः सर्वे संक्षिप्ता मायया पुरा .
प्रलीनाश्चैव लोकेश न दृश्यन्ते हि सांप्रतम् .. 8.45 ..
6.3.m: By him all the hosts of gods were formerly drawn in through his māyā; / and having dissolved, O lord of the world, they are not seen at present. 8.45

6.3.s:
punardṛśyā bhaviṣyanti sṛjamānāḥ svayaṃbhuvā .
sāhaṃ liṅgārcanaparā narmadā nāma nāmataḥ .. 8.46 ..
6.3.d:
पुनर्दृश्या भविष्यन्ति सृजमानाः स्वयंभुवा .
साहं लिङ्गार्चनपरा नर्मदा नाम नामतः .. 8.46 ..
6.3.m: They will be seen again when being created by the self-manifest one. / I am devoted to worshipping the liṅga, Narmadā by name. 8.46

6.3.s:
kālaṃ yugasahasrasya rudrasya paricārikā .
asya prasādādamarastathā tvaṃ dvijapuṃgava .. 8.47 ..
6.3.d:
कालं युगसहस्रस्य रुद्रस्य परिचारिका .
अस्य प्रसादादमरस्तथा त्वं द्विजपुंगव .. 8.47 ..
6.3.m: For the span of a thousand yugas I have been an attendant of Rudra. / By his grace, you too are immortal, O best of brahmins! 8.47

6.3.s:
satyārjavadayāyuktaḥ siddho'si tvaṃ śivārcanāt .
evamuktvā tu sā devī tatraivāntaradhīyata .. 8.48 ..
6.3.d:
सत्यार्जवदयायुक्तः सिद्धोऽसि त्वं शिवार्चनात् .
एवमुक्त्वा तु सा देवी तत्रैवान्तरधीयत .. 8.48 ..
6.3.m: Endowed with truth, honesty, and compassion, you are perfected through worshipping Śiva.' / Having spoken thus, that goddess vanished right there, 8.48

6.3.s:
tāḥ striyaḥ sa ca deveśo bakarūpo maheśvaraḥ .
tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā avatīrya mahānadīm .. 8.49 ..
6.3.d:
ताः स्त्रियः स च देवेशो बकरूपो महेश्वरः .
तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा अवतीर्य महानदीम् .. 8.49 ..
6.3.m: as did those women and that lord of gods, Maheśvara in the form of a crane. / Having heard her speech, descending into the great river, 8.49

6.3.s:
snātvā samarcaya tvaṃ hi vidhinā mantrapūrvakam .
tato'haṃ sahasā tasmātsamuttīrya jalāśayāt .. 8.50 ..
6.3.d:
स्नात्वा समर्चय त्वं हि विधिना मन्त्रपूर्वकम् .
ततोऽहं सहसा तस्मात्समुत्तीर्य जलाशयात् .. 8.50 ..
6.3.m: [she had said:] 'Having bathed, do worship him according to rule, preceded by mantras.' / Then, having quickly emerged from that body of water, 8.50

6.3.s:
na ca paśyāmi talliṅgaṃ na ca tāṃ nimnagāṃ nṛpa .
tadaiva lokāḥ saṃjātāḥ kṣitiścaiva sakānanā .. 8.51 ..
6.3.d:
न च पश्यामि तल्लिङ्गं न च तां निम्नगां नृप .
तदैव लोकाः संजाताः क्षितिश्चैव सकानना .. 8.51 ..
6.3.m: I did not see that liṅga, nor that river, O king. / Just then the worlds came into being, and the earth with its forests; 8.51

6.3.s:
ṛkṣacandrārkavitataṃ tadeva ca nabhastalam .
yathāpūrvamadṛṣṭaṃ tu tathaiva ca punaḥ kṛtam .
nato'haṃ manasā devamapūjayaṃ maheśvaram .. 8.52 ..
6.3.d:
ऋक्षचन्द्रार्कविततं तदेव च नभस्तलम् .
यथापूर्वमदृष्टं तु तथैव च पुनः कृतम् .
नतोऽहं मनसा देवमपूजयं महेश्वरम् .. 8.52 ..
6.3.m: and the vault of the sky was spread over with stars, moon, and sun. / What had been unseen was made again just as before; / bowing in my mind to the god, I worshipped Maheśvara. 8.52

6.3.s:
evaṃ bake purā kalpe mayā dṛṣṭeyamavyayā .
narmadā martyalokasya mahāpātakanāśinī .. 8.53 ..
6.3.d:
एवं बके पुरा कल्पे मया दृष्टेयमव्यया .
नर्मदा मर्त्यलोकस्य महापातकनाशिनी .. 8.53 ..
6.3.m: Thus in the ancient Baka-kalpa, this imperishable Narmadā was seen by me, / the destroyer of great sins for the world of mortals. 8.53

6.3.s:
tasmāddharmaparairvipraiḥ kṣatraśūdraviśādibhiḥ .
sadā sevyā mahābhāgā dharmavṛddhyarthakāribhiḥ .. 8.54 ..
6.3.d:
तस्माद्धर्मपरैर्विप्रैः क्षत्रशूद्रविशादिभिः .
सदा सेव्या महाभागा धर्मवृद्ध्यर्थकारिभिः .. 8.54 ..
6.3.m: Therefore, by brahmins devoted to dharma, by kṣatriyas, śūdras, vaiśyas, and others, / desiring to foster dharma, the illustrious one is always to be resorted to. 8.54

6.3.s:
ye'pi bhaktayā sakṛttoye narmadāyā maheśvaram .
snātvā te sarvaṃ pāpaṃ nāśayantyasaṃśayam .. 8.55 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe narmadāmāhātmye bakakalpasamudbhavo nāmāṣṭamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 9
6.3.d:
येऽपि भक्तया सकृत्तोये नर्मदाया महेश्वरम् .
स्नात्वा ते सर्वं पापं नाशयन्त्यसंशयम् .. 8.55 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे नर्मदामाहात्म्ये बककल्पसमुद्भवो नामाष्टमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 9
6.3.m:
Those who, with devotion, even once in the water of the Narmadā [worship] Maheśvara / after having bathed, destroy all sin without a doubt. 8.55
Thus ends the eighth chapter, named 'The Origin in the Baka-kalpa,' in the praise of the Narmadā in the Revākhaṇḍa of the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 9

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
punaryugāntaṃ te cānyaṃ sampravakṣyāmi tacchṛṇu .
sūryairādīpite loke jaṅgame sthāvare purā .. 9.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
पुनर्युगान्तं ते चान्यं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि तच्छृणु .
सूर्यैरादीपिते लोके जङ्गमे स्थावरे पुरा .. 9.1 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / 'I shall tell you of another end of a yuga; listen to it. / Formerly, when the world, moving and unmoving, was set ablaze by suns, 9.1

6.3.s:
saritsaraḥsamudreṣu kṣayaṃ yāteṣu sarvaśaḥ .
nirmānuṣavaṣaṭkāre hyamaryādagatiṃ gate .. 9.2 ..
6.3.d:
सरित्सरःसमुद्रेषु क्षयं यातेषु सर्वशः .
निर्मानुषवषट्कारे ह्यमर्यादगतिं गते .. 9.2 ..
6.3.m: when rivers, lakes, and oceans were completely destroyed, / when humanity and the vaṣaṭ-call had ceased, and bounds were transgressed, 9.2

6.3.s:
nānārūpaistato meghaiḥ śakrāyudhavirājitaiḥ .
sarvamāpūritaṃ vyoma vāryaughaiḥ pūrite tadā .. 9.3 ..
6.3.d:
नानारूपैस्ततो मेघैः शक्रायुधविराजितैः .
सर्वमापूरितं व्योम वार्यौघैः पूरिते तदा .. 9.3 ..
6.3.m: then by clouds of various forms, adorned with rainbows, / the entire sky was filled, when it was filled with floods of water. 9.3

6.3.s:
tatastvekārṇavībhūte sarvataḥ salilāvṛte .
jagatkṛtvodare sarvaṃ suṣvāpa bhagavānharaḥ .. 9.4 ..
6.3.d:
ततस्त्वेकार्णवीभूते सर्वतः सलिलावृते .
जगत्कृत्वोदरे सर्वं सुष्वाप भगवान्हरः .. 9.4 ..
6.3.m: Then, when it had become a single ocean and was covered on all sides with water, / having placed the entire universe within his belly, the blessed Hara slept. 9.4

6.3.s:
prakṛtiṃ svāmavaṣṭabhya yogātmā sa prajāpatiḥ .
śete yugasahasrāntaṃ kālamāviśya sārṇavam .. 9.5 ..
6.3.d:
प्रकृतिं स्वामवष्टभ्य योगात्मा स प्रजापतिः .
शेते युगसहस्रान्तं कालमाविश्य सार्णवम् .. 9.5 ..
6.3.m: Resting upon his own material nature, that Prajāpati, whose self is yoga, / sleeps until the end of a thousand yugas, entering the oceanic time. 9.5

6.3.s:
tatra suptaṃ mahātmānaṃ brahmalokanivāsinaḥ .
bhṛgvādiṛṣayaḥ sarve ye cānye sanakādayaḥ .. 9.6 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र सुप्तं महात्मानं ब्रह्मलोकनिवासिनः .
भृग्वादिऋषयः सर्वे ये चान्ये सनकादयः .. 9.6 ..
6.3.m: The dwellers of the world of Brahmā—all the seers such as Bhṛgu / and others such as Sanaka—[saw] the great-souled one sleeping there. 9.6

6.3.s:
paryaṅke vimale śubhre nānāstaraṇasaṃstṛte .
śayānaṃ dadṛśurdevaṃ sapatnīkaṃ vṛṣadhvajam .. 9.7 ..
6.3.d:
पर्यङ्के विमले शुभ्रे नानास्तरणसंस्तृते .
शयानं ददृशुर्देवं सपत्नीकं वृषध्वजम् .. 9.7 ..
6.3.m: Upon a spotless, bright couch spread with various coverings, / they saw the god whose banner is the bull lying with his consort. 9.7

6.3.s:
viśvarūpā tu sā nārī viśvarūpo maheśvaraḥ .
gāḍhamāliṅgya suptastāṃ dadṛśe cāhamavyayam .. 9.8 ..
6.3.d:
विश्वरूपा तु सा नारी विश्वरूपो महेश्वरः .
गाढमालिङ्ग्य सुप्तस्तां ददृशे चाहमव्ययम् .. 9.8 ..
6.3.m: That woman had the form of the universe, and Maheśvara had the form of the universe; / having embraced her closely, he slept, and I saw that imperishable one. 9.8

6.3.s:
pādamūle tatastasya śyāmāṃ tāṃ padmalakṣaṇām .
kanyāṃ paśyāmi suśroṇīṃ caraṇau tasya mṛdgatīm .. 9.9 ..
6.3.d:
पादमूले ततस्तस्य श्यामां तां पद्मलक्षणाम् .
कन्यां पश्यामि सुश्रोणीं चरणौ तस्य मृद्गतीम् .. 9.9 ..
6.3.m: Then at his feet I saw that dark maiden, marked with lotuses, / possessed of lovely hips, rubbing his feet. 9.9

6.3.s:
vimalāmbarasaṃvītāṃ vyālayajñopavītinīm .
śyāmāṃ kamalapatrākṣīṃ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitām .. 9.10 ..
6.3.d:
विमलाम्बरसंवीतां व्यालयज्ञोपवीतिनीम् .
श्यामां कमलपत्राक्षीं सर्वाभरणभूषिताम् .. 9.10 ..
6.3.m: Clad in spotless garments, wearing a serpent as a sacred thread, / dark, with eyes like lotus petals, adorned with all ornaments. 9.10

6.3.s:
sakalaṃ yugasāhasraṃ narmadeyaṃ vijānatī .
prasuptaṃ devadeveśamupāste varavarṇinī .. 9.11 ..
6.3.d:
सकलं युगसाहस्रं नर्मदेयं विजानती .
प्रसुप्तं देवदेवेशमुपास्ते वरवर्णिनी .. 9.11 ..
6.3.m: For the whole thousand yugas, this knowing Narmadā, / the fair-complexioned one, waits upon the sleeping lord of the gods. 9.11

6.3.s:
hṛtairvedaiścaturbhiśca brahmāpyevaṃ maheśvaraḥ .
bhṛgvādyairmānasaiḥ putraiḥ stauti śaṅkaramavyayam .. 9.12 ..
6.3.d:
हृतैर्वेदैश्चतुर्भिश्च ब्रह्माप्येवं महेश्वरः .
भृग्वाद्यैर्मानसैः पुत्रैः स्तौति शङ्करमव्ययम् .. 9.12 ..
6.3.m: With the four Vedas stolen away, Brahmā too, great lord, / together with his mind-born sons such as Bhṛgu, praises the imperishable Śaṅkara. 9.12

6.3.s:
bhaktyā paramayā rājaṃstatra śambhumanāmayam .
stuvantastatra deveśaṃ mantrairīśvarasambhavaiḥ .. 9.13 ..
6.3.d:
भक्त्या परमया राजंस्तत्र शम्भुमनामयम् .
स्तुवन्तस्तत्र देवेशं मन्त्रैरीश्वरसम्भवैः .. 9.13 ..
6.3.m: With supreme devotion, O king, [praising] Śambhu there, the sorrowless one, / praising the lord of gods there with mantras originating from Īśvara, 9.13

6.3.s:
prasuptaṃ devamīśānaṃ bodhayansamupasthitaḥ .
uttiṣṭha hara piṅgākṣa mahādeva maheśvara .. 9.14 ..
6.3.d:
प्रसुप्तं देवमीशानं बोधयन्समुपस्थितः .
उत्तिष्ठ हर पिङ्गाक्ष महादेव महेश्वर .. 9.14 ..
6.3.m: he stood present, awakening the sleeping god Īśāna: / 'Arise, O Hara, tawny-eyed one, Mahādeva, Maheśvara! 9.14

6.3.s:
mama vedā hṛtāḥ sarve ato'haṃ stotumudyataḥ .
vedairvyāptaṃ jagatsarvaṃ divyādivyaṃ carācaram .. 9.15 ..
6.3.d:
मम वेदा हृताः सर्वे अतोऽहं स्तोतुमुद्यतः .
वेदैर्व्याप्तं जगत्सर्वं दिव्यादिव्यं चराचरम् .. 9.15 ..
6.3.m: All my Vedas have been stolen; therefore I have undertaken to praise you. / By the Vedas the entire universe is pervaded, divine and non-divine, moving and unmoving. 9.15

6.3.s:
atītaṃ vartamānaṃ ca smarāmi ca sṛjāmyaham .
tairvinā cāhamekastu mūko'dho jaḍavatsadā .. 9.16 ..
6.3.d:
अतीतं वर्तमानं च स्मरामि च सृजाम्यहम् .
तैर्विना चाहमेकस्तु मूकोऽधो जडवत्सदा .. 9.16 ..
6.3.m: I remember the past and the present, and I create; / but without them I am alone, always mute, degraded, like an inert fool. 9.16

6.3.s:
gatirvīryaṃ balotsāhau tairvinā na prajāyate .
tairvinā devadeveśa nāhaṃ kiṃcitsmarāmi vai .. 9.17 ..
6.3.d:
गतिर्वीर्यं बलोत्साहौ तैर्विना न प्रजायते .
तैर्विना देवदेवेश नाहं किंचित्स्मरामि वै .. 9.17 ..
6.3.m: Movement, power, strength, and energy do not arise without them; / without them, O lord of the gods, I indeed do not remember anything. 9.17

6.3.s:
tānvedāndevadeveśa śīghraṃ me dātumarhasi .
jaḍāndhabadhiraṃ sarvaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam .. 9.18 ..
6.3.d:
तान्वेदान्देवदेवेश शीघ्रं मे दातुमर्हसि .
जडान्धबधिरं सर्वं जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम् .. 9.18 ..
6.3.m: You ought to give those Vedas quickly to me, O lord of the gods! / The entire universe, moving and unmoving, is inert, blind, and deaf. 9.18

6.3.s:
sthānādi daśa catvāri na śobhante sureśvara .
praṇamāmyalpavīryatvādvedahīnaḥ sureśvara .. 9.19 ..
6.3.d:
स्थानादि दश चत्वारि न शोभन्ते सुरेश्वर .
प्रणमाम्यल्पवीर्यत्वाद्वेदहीनः सुरेश्वर .. 9.19 ..
6.3.m: The fourteen realms do not shine, O lord of the gods; / deprived of the Vedas, I bow down because of my diminished power, O lord of the gods! 9.19

6.3.s:
vedebhyaḥ sakalaṃ jātaṃ yatkiṃcitsacarācaram .
tāvacchobhanti śāstrāṇi samastāni jagadguro .. 9.20 ..
6.3.d:
वेदेभ्यः सकलं जातं यत्किंचित्सचराचरम् .
तावच्छोभन्ति शास्त्राणि समस्तानि जगद्गुरो .. 9.20 ..
6.3.m: From the Vedas everything came to be, whatever there is, moving and unmoving; / all sacred treatises shine only so long, O guru of the world, 9.20

6.3.s:
yāvadvedanidhirayaṃ nopatiṣṭhetsanātanaḥ .
yathoditena sūryeṇa tamo yāti vināśatām .. 9.21 ..
6.3.d:
यावद्वेदनिधिरयं नोपतिष्ठेत्सनातनः .
यथोदितेन सूर्येण तमो याति विनाशताम् .. 9.21 ..
6.3.m: as this eternal treasure of the Vedas is not absent. / Just as darkness goes to destruction by the risen sun, 9.21

6.3.s:
evaṃ samastapāpāni yānti vedasya dhāraṇāt .
vede rahasi yatsūkṣmaṃ yattadbrahma sanātanam .. 9.22 ..
6.3.d:
एवं समस्तपापानि यान्ति वेदस्य धारणात् .
वेदे रहसि यत्सूक्ष्मं यत्तद्ब्रह्म सनातनम् .. 9.22 ..
6.3.m: so all sins vanish through holding the Veda. / That subtle, eternal Brahman which is secret in the Veda, 9.22

6.3.s:
hṛdisthaṃ deva jānāmi gataṃ tadvedagarjanāt .
vedānuccarato me'dya tava śaṅkara cāgrataḥ .. 9.23 ..
6.3.d:
हृदिस्थं देव जानामि गतं तद्वेदगर्जनात् .
वेदानुच्चरतो मेऽद्य तव शङ्कर चाग्रतः .. 9.23 ..
6.3.m: which was present in my heart, O god—I know it is gone due to the roaring of the Vedas. / As I was reciting the Vedas today in front of you, O Śaṅkara, 9.23

6.3.s:
akasmātte gatā vedā na sṛjeyaṃ vibho bhuvam .
te'pi sarve mahādeva praviṣṭāḥ sammukhārṇavam .. 9.24 ..
6.3.d:
अकस्मात्ते गता वेदा न सृजेयं विभो भुवम् .
तेऽपि सर्वे महादेव प्रविष्टाः सम्मुखार्णवम् .. 9.24 ..
6.3.m: suddenly the Vedas were gone; I cannot create the earth, O omnipresent one! / They too have all entered the ocean right before us, O Mahādeva. 9.24

6.3.s:
te yācyamānā deveśa tiṣṭhantu smaraṇe mama .
duhiteyaṃ viśālākṣī sarvaḥ sarvaṃ vijānate .. 9.25 ..
6.3.d:
ते याच्यमाना देवेश तिष्ठन्तु स्मरणे मम .
दुहितेयं विशालाक्षी सर्वः सर्वं विजानते .. 9.25 ..
6.3.m: Being asked for, O lord of the gods, let them remain in my memory! / This large-eyed daughter—everyone knows everything. 9.25

6.3.s:
jāyatī yugasāhasraṃ nānyā kācidbhavedṛśī .
ṛṣiścāyaṃ mahābhāgo mārkaṇḍo dhīmatāṃ varaḥ .. 9.26 ..
6.3.d:
जायती युगसाहस्रं नान्या काचिद्भवेदृशी .
ऋषिश्चायं महाभागो मार्कण्डो धीमतां वरः .. 9.26 ..
6.3.m: She stays awake for a thousand yugas; there can be no other like her. / And this illustrious seer Mārkaṇḍa is the best of the wise; 9.26

6.3.s:
kalpe kalpe mahādeva tvāmayaṃ paryupāsate .
jagattrayahitārthāya carate vratamuttamam .. 9.27 ..
6.3.d:
कल्पे कल्पे महादेव त्वामयं पर्युपासते .
जगत्त्रयहितार्थाय चरते व्रतमुत्तमम् .. 9.27 ..
6.3.m: kalpa after kalpa, O Mahādeva, he attends upon you, / practicing an excellent vow for the welfare of the three worlds.' 9.27

6.3.s:
evamuktastu deveśo brahmaṇā parameṣṭhinā .
uvāca ślakṣṇayā vācā narmadāṃ saritāṃ varām .. 9.28 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्तस्तु देवेशो ब्रह्मणा परमेष्ठिना .
उवाच श्लक्ष्णया वाचा नर्मदां सरितां वराम् .. 9.28 ..
6.3.m: Addressed thus by Brahmā Parameṣṭhin, the lord of the gods / spoke with gentle speech to Narmadā, the best of rivers: 9.28

6.3.s:
kathayasva mahābhāge brahmaṇastvaṃ tu pṛcchataḥ .
kena vedā hṛtāḥ sarve vedhaso jagatīguroḥ .. 9.29 ..
6.3.d:
कथयस्व महाभागे ब्रह्मणस्त्वं तु पृच्छतः .
केन वेदा हृताः सर्वे वेधसो जगतीगुरोः .. 9.29 ..
6.3.m: 'Declare, O illustrious one, to Brahmā who is questioning you: / By whom were all the Vedas stolen from Vedhas, the guru of the world?' 9.29

6.3.s:
evamuktā tu rudreṇa uvāca mṛgalocanā .
brahmaṇo japato vedāṃstvayi supte maheśvara .. 9.30 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्ता तु रुद्रेण उवाच मृगलोचना .
ब्रह्मणो जपतो वेदांस्त्वयि सुप्ते महेश्वर .. 9.30 ..
6.3.m: Thus addressed by Rudra, the deer-eyed one said: / 'While Brahmā was reciting the Vedas, and while you were asleep, O Maheśvara, 9.30

6.3.s:
bhavataśchidramāsādya ghore'sminsalilāvṛte .
pūrvakalpasamudbhūtāvasurau suradurjayau .. 9.31 ..
6.3.d:
भवतश्छिद्रमासाद्य घोरेऽस्मिन्सलिलावृते .
पूर्वकल्पसमुद्भूतावसुरौ सुरदुर्जयौ .. 9.31 ..
6.3.m: Finding an opening while you [slept], in this terrible [expanse] covered with water, / two asuras born in a previous kalpa, invincible to the gods,

6.3.s:
śriyāvṛttau mahādeva tvayā cotpāditau purā .
surāsurasudurjeyau dānavau madhukaiṭabhau .. 9.32 ..
6.3.d:
श्रियावृत्तौ महादेव त्वया चोत्पादितौ पुरा .
सुरासुरसुदुर्जेयौ दानवौ मधुकैटभौ .. 9.32 ..
6.3.m: enveloped in fortune, O Mahādeva, and produced formerly by you, / difficult for gods and asuras to overcome—the two dānavas Madhu and Kaiṭabha—

6.3.s:
tau vāyubhūtau sūkṣmau ca paṭhato'smātpitāmahāt .
tāvāśu hṛtvā vedāṃśca praviṣṭau ca mahārṇavam .. 9.33 ..
6.3.d:
तौ वायुभूतौ सूक्ष्मौ च पठतोऽस्मात्पितामहात् .
तावाशु हृत्वा वेदांश्च प्रविष्टौ च महार्णवम् .. 9.33 ..
6.3.m: having become air and subtle, as the Grandfather was reciting, / quickly snatched the Vedas from him and entered the great ocean.

6.3.s:
etacchrutvā mahātejā hyamṛtāyāstato vacaḥ .
sasmāra sa ca deveśaṃ śaṅkhacakragadādharam .. 9.34 ..
6.3.d:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा महातेजा ह्यमृतायास्ततो वचः .
सस्मार स च देवेशं शङ्खचक्रगदाधरम् .. 9.34 ..
6.3.m: Hearing this speech from Amṛtā, the god of great fiery energy / remembered the Lord of gods who bears the conch, discus, and mace.

6.3.s:
sa viveśa mahārāja bhūtalaṃ sasurottamaḥ .
dānavāntakaro devaḥ sarvadaivatapūjitaḥ .. 9.35 ..
6.3.d:
स विवेश महाराज भूतलं ससुरोत्तमः .
दानवान्तकरो देवः सर्वदैवतपूजितः .. 9.35 ..
6.3.m: He entered the surface of the earth, O great king, that best of gods, / the slayer of dānavas, the god worshipped by all deities.

6.3.s:
mīnarūpadharo devo loḍayāmāsa cārvaṇam .
vedāṃśca dadṛśe tatra pātāle nihitānprabhuḥ .. 9.36 ..
6.3.d:
मीनरूपधरो देवो लोडयामास चार्वणम् .
वेदांश्च ददृशे तत्र पाताले निहितान्प्रभुः .. 9.36 ..
6.3.m: Assuming the form of a fish, the Lord churned the ocean, / and the Lord saw the Vedas placed there in Pātāla.

6.3.s:
tau ca daityau mahāvīryau dṛṣṭavānmadhusūdanaḥ .
mahāvegau mahābāhū sūdayāmāsa tejasā .. 9.37 ..
6.3.d:
तौ च दैत्यौ महावीर्यौ दृष्टवान्मधुसूदनः .
महावेगौ महाबाहू सूदयामास तेजसा .. 9.37 ..
6.3.m: Madhusūdana saw those two daityas of great valor, / possessing great speed and mighty arms, and destroyed them by his fiery brilliance.

6.3.s:
vedāṃstatrāpi toyasthānānināya jagadguruḥ .
caturvaktrāya devāyādadāccakravibhūṣitaḥ .. 9.38 ..
6.3.d:
वेदांस्तत्रापि तोयस्थानानिनाय जगद्गुरुः .
चतुर्वक्त्राय देवायाददाच्चक्रविभूषितः .. 9.38 ..
6.3.m: The Guru of the universe brought the Vedas situated there in the waters; / adorned with the discus, he gave them to the four-faced god.

6.3.s:
tataḥ prahṛṣṭo bhagavān vedāṃllabdhvā pitāmahaḥ .
janayāmāsa nikhilaṃ jagadbhūyaścarācaram .. 9.39 ..
6.3.d:
ततः प्रहृष्टो भगवान् वेदांल्लब्ध्वा पितामहः .
जनयामास निखिलं जगद्भूयश्चराचरम् .. 9.39 ..
6.3.m: Then, delighted upon receiving the Vedas, the venerable Grandfather / created again the entire universe, both moving and unmoving.

6.3.s:
sā ca devī nadī puṇyā rudrasya paricārikā .
pāvanī sarvabhūtānāṃ provāha salilaṃ tadā .. 9.40 ..
6.3.d:
सा च देवी नदी पुण्या रुद्रस्य परिचारिका .
पावनी सर्वभूतानां प्रोवाह सलिलं तदा .. 9.40 ..
6.3.m: And that divine, holy river, the attendant of Rudra, / purifying all living beings, then flowed with water.

6.3.s:
tasyāstīre tato devā ṛṣayaśca tapodhanāḥ .
yajanti tryambakaṃ devaṃ prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā .. 9.41 ..
6.3.d:
तस्यास्तीरे ततो देवा ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः .
यजन्ति त्र्यम्बकं देवं प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना .. 9.41 ..
6.3.m: Then on her bank the gods and ṛṣis rich in austerity / worshipped Tryambaka, the god, with delighted inner self.

6.3.s:
ekā mūrtirmaheśasya kāraṇāntaramāgatā .
traiguṇyā kurute karma brahmacakrīśarūpataḥ .. 9.42 ..
6.3.d:
एका मूर्तिर्महेशस्य कारणान्तरमागता .
त्रैगुण्या कुरुते कर्म ब्रह्मचक्रीशरूपतः .. 9.42 ..
6.3.m: A single form of Maheśa, having come into existence due to other causes, / acts through the three guṇas under the forms of Brahmā, the wielder of the discus [Viṣṇu], and Īśa.

6.3.s:
eteṣāṃ tu pṛthagbhāvaṃ ye kurvanti sumohitāḥ .
teṣāṃ dharmaḥ kutaḥ siddhirjāyate pāpakarmiṇām .. 9.43 ..
6.3.d:
एतेषां तु पृथग्भावं ये कुर्वन्ति सुमोहिताः .
तेषां धर्मः कुतः सिद्धिर्जायते पापकर्मिणाम् .. 9.43 ..
6.3.m: For those greatly deluded persons who make a distinction among these, / whence can righteousness or perfection arise for such evildoers?

6.3.s:
evametā mahānadyastisro rudrasamudbhavāḥ .
ekā eva tridhā bhūtā gaṅgā revā sarasvatī .. 9.44 ..
6.3.d:
एवमेता महानद्यस्तिस्रो रुद्रसमुद्भवाः .
एका एव त्रिधा भूता गङ्गा रेवा सरस्वती .. 9.44 ..
6.3.m: Thus these three great rivers arose from Rudra; / one single [river] became threefold: Gaṅgā, Revā, and Sarasvatī.

6.3.s:
gaṅgā tu vaiṣṇavī mūrtiḥ sarvapāpapraṇāśinī .
rudradehasamudbhūtā narmadā caivameva tu .. 9.45 ..
6.3.d:
गङ्गा तु वैष्णवी मूर्तिः सर्वपापप्रणाशिनी .
रुद्रदेहसमुद्भूता नर्मदा चैवमेव तु .. 9.45 ..
6.3.m: Gaṅgā is the form of Viṣṇu, destroying all sins; / likewise Narmadā has sprung from the body of Rudra.

6.3.s:
brāhmī sarasvatī mūrtistriṣu lokeṣu viśrutā .
divyā kāmagamā devī vāgvibhūtyai tu saṃsthitā .. 9.46 ..
6.3.d:
ब्राह्मी सरस्वती मूर्तिस्त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुता .
दिव्या कामगमा देवी वाग्विभूत्यै तु संस्थिता .. 9.46 ..
6.3.m: The form of Brahmā is Sarasvatī, renowned throughout the three worlds, / a divine goddess moving at will, abiding for the abundance of speech.

6.3.s:
narmadā paramā kācinmartyamūrtikalā śivā .
divyā kāmagamā devī sarvatra surapūjitā .. 9.47 ..
6.3.d:
नर्मदा परमा काचिन्मर्त्यमूर्तिकला शिवा .
दिव्या कामगमा देवी सर्वत्र सुरपूजिता .. 9.47 ..
6.3.m: Narmadā is a supreme, auspicious fraction of the mortal form, / a divine goddess moving at will, worshipped everywhere by gods.

6.3.s:
vyāpinī sarvabhūtānāṃ sūkṣmātsūkṣmatarā smṛtā .
akṣayā hyamṛtā hyeṣā svargasopānamuttamā .. 9.48 ..
6.3.d:
