Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, named 'Description of the Destruction of the Universe in the Form of Twelve Suns' in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth Section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the Śrīskandamahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 18

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
nirdagdhe'smiṃstato loke sūryairīśvarasambhavaiḥ .
saptabhiścārṇavaiḥ śuṣkairdvīpaiḥ saptabhireva ca .. 18.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
निर्दग्धेऽस्मिंस्ततो लोके सूर्यैरीश्वरसम्भवैः .
सप्तभिश्चार्णवैः शुष्कैर्द्वीपैः सप्तभिरेव च .. 18.1 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then, when this world was burned by the suns originating from Īśvara, / and when the seven oceans were dried up along with the seven continents,

6.3.s:
tato mukhāttasya ghanā maholbaṇā niścerurindrāyudhatulyarūpāḥ .
ghorāḥ payodā jagadandhakāraṃ kurvanta īśānavaraprayuktāḥ .. 18.2 ..
6.3.d:
ततो मुखात्तस्य घना महोल्बणा निश्चेरुरिन्द्रायुधतुल्यरूपाः .
घोराः पयोदा जगदन्धकारं कुर्वन्त ईशानवरप्रयुक्ताः .. 18.2 ..
6.3.m: then from his mouth extremely terrible clouds issued forth, resembling rainbows; / dreadful clouds, making the universe dark, dispatched by the supreme command of Īśāna,

6.3.s:
nīlotpalābhāḥ kvacidaṃjanābhā gokṣīrakundendunibhāśca kecit .
mayūracandrākṛtayastathā'nye kecidvidhūmānalasaprabhāśca .. 18.3 ..
6.3.d:
नीलोत्पलाभाः क्वचिदंजनाभा गोक्षीरकुन्देन्दुनिभाश्च केचित् .
मयूरचन्द्राकृतयस्तथाऽन्ये केचिद्विधूमानलसप्रभाश्च .. 18.3 ..
6.3.m: some having the lustre of blue lotuses, some the lustre of collyrium, and some resembling cow's milk, kunda flowers, and the moon; / and others having the forms of peacock eyes, and some having the radiance of smokeless fire;

6.3.s:
kecinmahāparvatakalparūpāḥ kecinmahāmīnakulopamāśca .
kecidgajendrākṛtayaḥ surūpāḥ kecinmahākūṭanibhāḥ payodāḥ .. 18.4 ..
6.3.d:
केचिन्महापर्वतकल्परूपाः केचिन्महामीनकुलोपमाश्च .
केचिद्गजेन्द्राकृतयः सुरूपाः केचिन्महाकूटनिभाः पयोदाः .. 18.4 ..
6.3.m: some having forms like great mountains, and some resembling shoals of great fish; / some possessing the forms of lordly elephants of beautiful appearance, and some clouds resembling great peaks;

6.3.s:
calattaraṅgormisamānarūpā mahāpurodhānanibhāśca kecit .
sagopurāṭṭālakasaṃnikāśāḥ savidyudulkāśanimaṇḍitāntāḥ .. 18.5 ..
6.3.d:
चलत्तरङ्गोर्मिसमानरूपा महापुरोधाननिभाश्च केचित् .
सगोपुराट्टालकसंनिकाशाः सविद्युदुल्काशनिमण्डितान्ताः .. 18.5 ..
6.3.m: having forms like moving waves and billows, and some resembling great cities, / appearing like city-gates and watchtowers, their edges adorned with lightning, meteors, and thunderbolts.

6.3.s:
samāvṛtāṅgaḥ sa babhūva devaḥ saṃvartakonāma gaṇaḥ sa raudraḥ .
pravarṣamāṇo jagadapramāṇamekārṇavaṃ sarvamidaṃ cakāra .. 18.6 ..
6.3.d:
समावृताङ्गः स बभूव देवः संवर्तकोनाम गणः स रौद्रः .
प्रवर्षमाणो जगदप्रमाणमेकार्णवं सर्वमिदं चकार .. 18.6 ..
6.3.m: Covered over his body, that god became that dreadful host called Saṃvartaka. / Raining down, it made this entire measureless universe into a single ocean.

6.3.s:
tato mahāmeghavivardhamānamīśānamindrāśanibhirvṛtāṅgam .
dadarśa nāhaṃ bhayavihvalāṅgo gaṅgājalaughaiśca samāvṛtāṅgaḥ .. 18.7 ..
6.3.d:
ततो महामेघविवर्धमानमीशानमिन्द्राशनिभिर्वृताङ्गम् .
ददर्श नाहं भयविह्वलाङ्गो गङ्गाजलौघैश्च समावृताङ्गः .. 18.7 ..
6.3.m: Then Īśāna, increasing by means of the great clouds, his limbs covered with Indra's thunderbolts, / I did not see, my limbs agitated with fear, my body submerged in masses of Gaṅgā-waters.

6.3.s:
gajāḥ punaścaiva punaḥ pibanto jagatsamantātparidahyamānam .
āpūritaṃ caiva jagatsamantātsarvaiśca tairjagmuradarśanaṃ ca te .. 18.8 ..
6.3.d:
गजाः पुनश्चैव पुनः पिबन्तो जगत्समन्तात्परिदह्यमानम् .
आपूरितं चैव जगत्समन्तात्सर्वैश्च तैर्जग्मुरदर्शनं च ते .. 18.8 ..
6.3.m: And elephants, drinking repeatedly from the universe burning all around, / and the universe being flooded on every side by all of them, they vanished from sight.

6.3.s:
mahārṇavāḥ sapta sarāṃsi dvīpā nadyo'tha sarvā atha bhūrbhuvaśca .
āpūryamāṇāḥ salilaughajālairekārṇavaṃ sarvamidaṃ babhūva .. 18.9 ..
6.3.d:
महार्णवाः सप्त सरांसि द्वीपा नद्योऽथ सर्वा अथ भूर्भुवश्च .
आपूर्यमाणाः सलिलौघजालैरेकार्णवं सर्वमिदं बभूव .. 18.9 ..
6.3.m: The seven great oceans, the lakes, the continents, all the rivers, and the earth and the atmosphere, / being filled with masses of water, all this became a single ocean.

6.3.s:
na dṛśyate kiṃcidaho carācaraṃ niragnicandrārkamaye'pi loke .
praṇaṣṭanakṣatratamo'ndhakāre praśāntavātāstamitaikanīḍeḥ .. 18.10 ..
6.3.d:
न दृश्यते किंचिदहो चराचरं निरग्निचन्द्रार्कमयेऽपि लोके .
प्रणष्टनक्षत्रतमोऽन्धकारे प्रशान्तवातास्तमितैकनीडेः .. 18.10 ..
6.3.m: Nothing moving or stationary was seen, alas, in a world devoid of fire, moon, and sun, / in the darkness of the vanished stars, where the winds had calmed and all had merged into a single shelter.

6.3.s:
mahājalaughe'sya viśuddhasattvā stutirmayā bhūpa kṛtā tadānīm .
tato'hamityeva vicintayānaḥ śaraṇyamekaṃ kva nu yāmi śāntam .. 18.11 ..
6.3.d:
महाजलौघेऽस्य विशुद्धसत्त्वा स्तुतिर्मया भूप कृता तदानीम् .
ततोऽहमित्येव विचिन्तयानः शरण्यमेकं क्व नु यामि शान्तम् .. 18.11 ..
6.3.m: In this great flood of water, O king, a hymn of pure reality was uttered by me then. / Then, reflecting thus: 'Where indeed shall I go to that one peaceful refuge?'

6.3.s:
smarāmi devaṃ hṛdi cintayitvā prabhuṃ śaraṇyaṃ jalasaṃniviṣṭaḥ .
namāmi devaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye dhyānaṃ ca tasyeti kṛtaṃ mayā ca .. 18.12 ..
6.3.d:
स्मरामि देवं हृदि चिन्तयित्वा प्रभुं शरण्यं जलसंनिविष्टः .
नमामि देवं शरणं प्रपद्ये ध्यानं च तस्येति कृतं मया च .. 18.12 ..
6.3.m: I remember the god, having meditated on the Lord, the refuge, in my heart, settled in the water; / 'I bow to the god, I go for refuge,' and meditation upon him was performed by me.

6.3.s:
dhyātvā tato'haṃ salilaṃ tatāra tasya prasādādavimūḍhacetāḥ .
glāniḥ śramaścaiva mama praṇaṣṭau devyāḥ prasādena narendraputra .. 18.13 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe narmadāmāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmāṣṭādaśo'dhyāyaḥ ..
6.3.d:
ध्यात्वा ततोऽहं सलिलं ततार तस्य प्रसादादविमूढचेताः .
ग्लानिः श्रमश्चैव मम प्रणष्टौ देव्याः प्रसादेन नरेन्द्रपुत्र .. 18.13 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे नर्मदामाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामाष्टादशोऽध्यायः ..
6.3.m:
Having meditated, I then crossed the water by his grace, my mind unconfused; / my languor and fatigue were destroyed by the grace of the Goddess, O son of the king.
Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, named 'Description of the Greatness of the Narmadā' in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth Section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the Śrīskandamahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

6.3.s:
adhyāya 19
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tatastvekārṇave tasminmumūrṣurahamāturaḥ .
kākūcchvāsastaraṃstoyaṃ bāhubhyāṃ nṛpasattama .. 19.1 ..
6.3.d:
अध्याय 19
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततस्त्वेकार्णवे तस्मिन्मुमूर्षुरहमातुरः .
काकूच्छ्वासस्तरंस्तोयं बाहुभ्यां नृपसत्तम .. 19.1 ..
6.3.m: Chapter 19 / The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then, in that single ocean, distressed, on the verge of death, / gasping for breath, swimming the water with my arms, O best of kings,

6.3.s:
śṛṇomyarṇavamadhyastho niḥśabdastimite tadā .
ambhoravamanaupamyaṃ diśo daśa vinādinam .. 19.2 ..
6.3.d:
शृणोम्यर्णवमध्यस्थो निःशब्दस्तिमिते तदा .
अम्भोरवमनौपम्यं दिशो दश विनादिनम् .. 19.2 ..
6.3.m: standing in the middle of the ocean, in the noiseless calm then / I heard an incomparable roaring of waters that made the ten directions resound.

6.3.s:
haṃsakudendusaṃkāśāṃ hāragokṣīrapāṇḍurām .
nānāratnavicitrāṅgīṃ svarṇaśṛṅgāṃ manoramām .. 19.3 ..
6.3.d:
हंसकुदेन्दुसंकाशां हारगोक्षीरपाण्डुराम् .
नानारत्नविचित्राङ्गीं स्वर्णशृङ्गां मनोरमाम् .. 19.3 ..
6.3.m: Resembling a swan, a kunda flower, or the moon, pale as a pearl necklace or cow's milk, / her limbs variegated with diverse jewels, possessing golden horns, delightful,

6.3.s:
suraiḥ pravālakamayairlāṅguladhvajaśobhitām .
pralambaghoṇāṃ nardantīṃ khurairarṇavagāhinīm .. 19.4 ..
6.3.d:
सुरैः प्रवालकमयैर्लाङ्गुलध्वजशोभिताम् .
प्रलम्बघोणां नर्दन्तीं खुरैरर्णवगाहिनीम् .. 19.4 ..
6.3.m: adorned with a tail-banner made of coral, / with an elongated snout, lowing, wading into the ocean with her hooves,

6.3.s:
gāṃ dadarśāhamudvigno māmevābhimukhīṃ sthitām .
kiṃkiṇījālamuktābhiḥ svarṇaghaṇṭāsamāvṛtām .. 19.5 ..
6.3.d:
गां ददर्शाहमुद्विग्नो मामेवाभिमुखीं स्थिताम् .
किंकिणीजालमुक्ताभिः स्वर्णघण्टासमावृताम् .. 19.5 ..
6.3.m: distressed, I beheld a cow standing directly facing me, / covered with nets of tinkling ornaments, pearls, and golden bells.

6.3.s:
tasyāścaraṇavikṣepaiḥ sarvamekārṇavaṃ jalam .
vikṣiptaphenapuñjaughairnṛtyantīva samaṃ tataḥ .. 19.6 ..
6.3.d:
तस्याश्चरणविक्षेपैः सर्वमेकार्णवं जलम् .
विक्षिप्तफेनपुञ्जौघैर्नृत्यन्तीव समं ततः .. 19.6 ..
6.3.m: By the strides of her feet all the waters of the single ocean, / with masses of scattered foam-heaps, were as if dancing all at once.

6.3.s:
rarāsa salilotkṣepaiḥ kṣobhayantī mahārṇavam .
sā māmāha mahābhāga ślakṣṇagambhīrayā girā .. 19.7 ..
6.3.d:
ररास सलिलोत्क्षेपैः क्षोभयन्ती महार्णवम् .
सा मामाह महाभाग श्लक्ष्णगम्भीरया गिरा .. 19.7 ..
6.3.m: Agitating the great ocean with the splash of waters, she bellowed. / She said to me, O highly blessed one, in a smooth and deep voice:

6.3.s:
mā bhaiṣīrvatsa vatseti mṛtyustava na vidyate .
mahādevaprasādena na mṛtyuste mamāpi ca .. 19.8 ..
6.3.d:
मा भैषीर्वत्स वत्सेति मृत्युस्तव न विद्यते .
महादेवप्रसादेन न मृत्युस्ते ममापि च .. 19.8 ..
6.3.m: 'Do not fear, child, my child! There is no death for you. / By the grace of Mahādeva, there is no death for you, nor for me.'

6.3.s:
mamāśrayasva lāṅgūlaṃ tvāmatastārayāmyaham .
ghorādasmādbhayādvipra yāvatsaṃplavate jagat .. 19.9 ..
6.3.d:
ममाश्रयस्व लाङ्गूलं त्वामतस्तारयाम्यहम् .
घोरादस्माद्भयाद्विप्र यावत्संप्लवते जगत् .. 19.9 ..
6.3.m:
"Take hold of my tail; from this I shall convey you across,
O brahmin, from this dreadful terror, as long as the world is flooded.

6.3.s:
kṣuttṛṣāpratighātārthaṃ stanau me tvaṃ pibasva ha .
payo'mṛtāśrayaṃ divyaṃ tatpītvā nirvṛto bhava .. 19.10 ..
6.3.d:
क्षुत्तृषाप्रतिघातार्थं स्तनौ मे त्वं पिबस्व ह .
पयोऽमृताश्रयं दिव्यं तत्पीत्वा निर्वृतो भव .. 19.10 ..
6.3.m:
To overcome your hunger and thirst, drink from my two udders;
[drink] the celestial milk that holds ambrosia, and having drunk it, find peace."

6.3.s:
tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā harṣātpīto mayā stanaḥ .
na kṣuttṛṣā pītamātre stane mahyaṃ tadābhavat .. 19.11 ..
6.3.d:
तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा हर्षात्पीतो मया स्तनः .
न क्षुत्तृषा पीतमात्रे स्तने मह्यं तदाभवत् .. 19.11 ..
6.3.m:
Hearing those words of hers, in joy I drank from her udder.
As soon as the udder was sucked, neither hunger nor thirst remained in me then.

6.3.s:
divyaṃ prāṇabalaṃ jajñe samudraplavanakṣamam .
tatastāṃ pratyuvācedaṃ kā tvamekārṇavīkṛte .. 19.12 ..
6.3.d:
दिव्यं प्राणबलं जज्ञे समुद्रप्लवनक्षमम् .
ततस्तां प्रत्युवाचेदं का त्वमेकार्णवीकृते .. 19.12 ..
6.3.m:
A divine bodily strength arose [in me], capable of swimming across the sea.
Then I spoke back to her: "Who are you, wandering in the cosmic ocean?

6.3.s:
bhramase brūhi tattvena vismayo me mahānhṛdi .
bhramato'tra mamārtasya mumūrṣoḥ prahatasya .. 19.13 ..
6.3.d:
भ्रमसे ब्रूहि तत्त्वेन विस्मयो मे महान्हृदि .
भ्रमतोऽत्र ममार्तस्य मुमूर्षोः प्रहतस्य .. 19.13 ..
6.3.m:
Tell me the truth, for great wonder is in my heart!
While I was wandering here, afflicted, wishing to die, struck down,

6.3.s: tvaṃ hi me śaraṇaṃ jātā bhāgyaśeṣeṇa suvrate .. 19.14 ..
6.3.d: त्वं हि मे शरणं जाता भाग्यशेषेण सुव्रते .. 19.14 ..
6.3.m: you indeed became my refuge through the remnant of my good fortune, O virtuous one!"

6.3.s:
gauruvāca -
kimahaṃ vismṛtā tubhyaṃ viśvarūpā maheśvarī .
narmadā dharmadā nḥṇāṃ svargaśarmabalapradā .. 19.15 ..
6.3.d:
गौरुवाच -
किमहं विस्मृता तुभ्यं विश्वरूपा महेश्वरी .
नर्मदा धर्मदा न्ःणां स्वर्गशर्मबलप्रदा .. 19.15 ..
6.3.m:
The cow said:
"Have you forgotten me, the universal-formed sovereign goddess,
the Narmadā who grants righteousness to men, conferring heaven, happiness, and strength?

6.3.s:
dṛṣṭvā tvāṃ sīdamānaṃ tu rudreṇāhaṃ visarjitā .
taṃ dvijaṃ tārayasvārye mā prāṇāṃstyajatāṃ jale .. 19.16 ..
6.3.d:
दृष्ट्वा त्वां सीदमानं तु रुद्रेणाहं विसर्जिता .
तं द्विजं तारयस्वार्ये मा प्राणांस्त्यजतां जले .. 19.16 ..
6.3.m:
Seeing you sinking, however, I was dispatched by Rudra:
'Noble lady, rescue that twice-born man; let him not lose his life in the water!'

6.3.s:
gorūpeṇa vibhorvākyāttvatsakāśamihāgatā .
mā mṛṣāvacanaḥ śambhurbhavediti ca satvarā .. 19.17 ..
6.3.d:
गोरूपेण विभोर्वाक्यात्त्वत्सकाशमिहागता .
मा मृषावचनः शम्भुर्भवेदिति च सत्वरा .. 19.17 ..
6.3.m:
In the form of a cow, by the word of the Lord, I came here into your presence,
hastening so that Śambhu might not become one whose word is false."

6.3.s:
evamuktastayāhaṃ tu indrāyudhanibhaṃ śubham .
lāṅgūlamavyayaṃ jñātvā bhujābhyāmavalambitaḥ .. 19.18 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्तस्तयाहं तु इन्द्रायुधनिभं शुभम् .
लाङ्गूलमव्ययं ज्ञात्वा भुजाभ्यामवलम्बितः .. 19.18 ..
6.3.m:
Thus addressed by her, knowing her tail, splendid like Indra's bow, to be imperishable,
I clung to it with both my arms.

6.3.s:
tato'taraṃ taṃ jaladhiṃ lāṅgūladhvajamāśritaḥ .
asau devo mahādeva iti māṃ pratyabhāṣata .. 19.19 ..
6.3.d:
ततोऽतरं तं जलधिं लाङ्गूलध्वजमाश्रितः .
असौ देवो महादेव इति मां प्रत्यभाषत .. 19.19 ..
6.3.m:
Then I crossed that ocean, relying on the tail as my banner.
She spoke back to me: "This god is Mahādeva."

6.3.s:
tato yugasahasrāntamahaṃ kālaṃ tayā saha .
vyacaraṃ vai tamobhūte sarvataḥ salilāvṛte .. 19.20 ..
6.3.d:
ततो युगसहस्रान्तमहं कालं तया सह .
व्यचरं वै तमोभूते सर्वतः सलिलावृते .. 19.20 ..
6.3.m:
Then for the span of a thousand yugas I roved with her
in that world turned into darkness, covered on all sides by water.

6.3.s:
mahārṇave tatastasmin bhramangoḥ pucchamāśritaḥ .
nirvāte cāndhakāre ca nirāloke nirāmaye .. 19.21 ..
6.3.d:
महार्णवे ततस्तस्मिन् भ्रमन्गोः पुच्छमाश्रितः .
निर्वाते चान्धकारे च निरालोके निरामये .. 19.21 ..
6.3.m:
Then, wandering in that great ocean, holding on to the cow's tail,
in the windless and dark, devoid of light and free from ailment,

6.3.s:
akasmātsalile tasminnatasīpuṣpasannibham .
vibhinnāṃjanasaṅkāśamākāśamiva nirmalam .. 19.22 ..
6.3.d:
अकस्मात्सलिले तस्मिन्नतसीपुष्पसन्निभम् .
विभिन्नांजनसङ्काशमाकाशमिव निर्मलम् .. 19.22 ..
6.3.m:
suddenly in that water [I saw the Lord], resembling the flax flower,
like crushed collyrium, stainless like the sky,

6.3.s:
nīlotpaladalaśyāmaṃ pītavāsasamavyayam .
kirīṭenārkavarṇena vidyudvidyotakāriṇā .. 19.23 ..
6.3.d:
नीलोत्पलदलश्यामं पीतवाससमव्ययम् .
किरीटेनार्कवर्णेन विद्युद्विद्योतकारिणा .. 19.23 ..
6.3.m:
dark as the petal of a blue lotus, clad in yellow garments, imperishable,
with a diadem the colour of the sun, flashing like lightning,

6.3.s:
bhrājamānena śirasā khamivātyantarūpiṇam .
kuṇḍaloddhaṣṭagallaṃ tu hāroddyotitavakṣasam .. 19.24 ..
6.3.d:
भ्राजमानेन शिरसा खमिवात्यन्तरूपिणम् .
कुण्डलोद्धष्टगल्लं तु हारोद्द्योतितवक्षसम् .. 19.24 ..
6.3.m:
with a head shining like the sky, having endless forms,
his cheeks brushed by his earrings, his chest illumined by a necklace,

6.3.s:
jāmbūnadamayairdivyairbhūṣaṇairupaśobhitam .
nāgopadhānaśayanaṃ sahasrādityavarcasam .. 19.25 ..
6.3.d:
जाम्बूनदमयैर्दिव्यैर्भूषणैरुपशोभितम् .
नागोपधानशयनं सहस्रादित्यवर्चसम् .. 19.25 ..
6.3.m:
adorned with divine ornaments made of Jāmbūnada gold,
lying on the serpent as his bolster, having the splendour of a thousand suns,

6.3.s:
anekabāhūrudharaṃ naikavaktraṃ manoramam .
suptamekārṇave vīraṃ sahasrākṣaśirodharam .. 19.26 ..
6.3.d:
अनेकबाहूरुधरं नैकवक्त्रं मनोरमम् .
सुप्तमेकार्णवे वीरं सहस्राक्षशिरोधरम् .. 19.26 ..
6.3.m:
possessing many arms and thighs, having more than one face, charming,
the hero sleeping in the cosmic ocean, endowed with a thousand eyes and necks,

6.3.s:
jaṭājūṭena mahatā sphuradvidyutsamārciṣā .
ekārṇavaṃ jagatsarvaṃ vyāpya devaṃ vyavasthitam .. 19.27 ..
6.3.d:
जटाजूटेन महता स्फुरद्विद्युत्समार्चिषा .
एकार्णवं जगत्सर्वं व्याप्य देवं व्यवस्थितम् .. 19.27 ..
6.3.m:
having a great mass of matted hair with rays like flashing lightning,
the god stationed there, pervading the whole world turned into a cosmic ocean.

6.3.s:
grasitvā śaṅkaraḥ sarvaṃ sadevāsuramānavam .
prapaśyāmyahamīśānaṃ suptamekārṇave prabhum .. 19.28 ..
6.3.d:
ग्रसित्वा शङ्करः सर्वं सदेवासुरमानवम् .
प्रपश्याम्यहमीशानं सुप्तमेकार्णवे प्रभुम् .. 19.28 ..
6.3.m:
Having swallowed everything along with gods, asuras, and humans, Śaṃkara,
the sovereign Īśāna, the Lord, I behold sleeping in the single ocean,

6.3.s:
sarvavyāpinamavyaktamanantaṃ viśvatomukham .
tasya pādatalābhyāśe svarṇakeyūramaṇḍitām .. 19.29 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वव्यापिनमव्यक्तमनन्तं विश्वतोमुखम् .
तस्य पादतलाभ्याशे स्वर्णकेयूरमण्डिताम् .. 19.29 ..
6.3.m:
all-pervading, unmanifest, infinite, facing all directions.
Near the soles of his feet, [I beheld the Goddess] adorned with golden armlets,

6.3.s:
viśvarūpāṃ mahābhāgāṃ viśvamāyāvadhāriṇīm .
śrīmayīṃ hrīmayīṃ devīṃ dhīmayīṃ vāṅmayīṃ śivām .. 19.30 ..
6.3.d:
विश्वरूपां महाभागां विश्वमायावधारिणीम् .
श्रीमयीं ह्रीमयीं देवीं धीमयीं वाङ्मयीं शिवाम् .. 19.30 ..
6.3.m:
universal-formed, highly fortunate, bearing the cosmic illusion,
consisting of fortune, modesty, intellect, and speech, the auspicious Śivā,

6.3.s:
siddhiṃ kīrtiṃ ratiṃ brāhmīṃ kālarātrimayonijām .
tāmevāhaṃ tadātyantamīśvarāntikamāsthitām .. 19.31 ..
6.3.d:
सिद्धिं कीर्तिं रतिं ब्राह्मीं कालरात्रिमयोनिजाम् .
तामेवाहं तदात्यन्तमीश्वरान्तिकमास्थिताम् .. 19.31 ..
6.3.m:
perfection, fame, delight, the consort of Brahmā, the night of cosmic dissolution, not born from a womb;
her alone I then beheld, stationed very near to the Lord,

6.3.s: adrākṣaṃ candravadanāṃ dhṛtiṃ sarveśvarīmumām .. 19.32 ..
6.3.d: अद्राक्षं चन्द्रवदनां धृतिं सर्वेश्वरीमुमाम् .. 19.32 ..
6.3.m: moon-faced, constancy, Umā, the ruler of all.

6.3.s:
śāntaṃ prasuptaṃ navahemavarṇamumāsahāyaṃ bhagavantamīśam .
tamovṛtaṃ puṇyatamaṃ variṣṭhaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya namaskaromi .. 19.33 ..
6.3.d:
शान्तं प्रसुप्तं नवहेमवर्णमुमासहायं भगवन्तमीशम् .
तमोवृतं पुण्यतमं वरिष्ठं प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य नमस्करोमि .. 19.33 ..
6.3.m:
The peaceful, sleeping, fresh-gold-coloured Lord, God accompanied by Umā,
enveloped in darkness, most sacred, the highest—circumambulating him, I bow down.

6.3.s:
tataḥ prasuptaḥ sahasā vibuddho rātrikṣaye devavaraḥ svabhāvāt .
vikṣobhayan bāhubhirarṇavāmbho jagatpraṇaṣṭaṃ salile vimṛśya .. 19.34 ..
6.3.d:
ततः प्रसुप्तः सहसा विबुद्धो रात्रिक्षये देववरः स्वभावात् .
विक्षोभयन् बाहुभिरर्णवाम्भो जगत्प्रणष्टं सलिले विमृश्य .. 19.34 ..
6.3.m:
Then, having been asleep, the best of gods suddenly awoke by his own nature at the end of the night,
agitating the waters of the ocean with his arms, having reflected on the world lost in the flood.

6.3.s:
kiṃ kāryamityeva vicintayitvā vārāharūpo'bhavadadbhutāṅgaḥ .
mahāghanāmbhodharatulyavarcāḥ pralambamālāmbaraniṣkamālī .. 19.35 ..
6.3.d:
किं कार्यमित्येव विचिन्तयित्वा वाराहरूपोऽभवदद्भुताङ्गः .
महाघनाम्भोधरतुल्यवर्चाः प्रलम्बमालाम्बरनिष्कमाली .. 19.35 ..
6.3.m:
Reflecting, 'What is to be done?', he assumed the form of a boar, wondrous of limb,
with a brilliance equal to massive clouds laden with water, wearing a long garland, garments, and a gold-coin necklace,

6.3.s:
saśaṅkhacakrāsidharaḥ kirīṭī savedavedāṅgamayo mahātmā .
trailokyanirmāṇakaraḥ purāṇo devatrayīrūpadharaśca kārye .. 19.36 ..
6.3.d:
सशङ्खचक्रासिधरः किरीटी सवेदवेदाङ्गमयो महात्मा .
त्रैलोक्यनिर्माणकरः पुराणो देवत्रयीरूपधरश्च कार्ये .. 19.36 ..
6.3.m:
bearing the conch, discus, and sword, wearing a diadem, embodied with the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, the Great Soul,
the creator of the three worlds, ancient, and bearing the form of the triad of gods in action.

6.3.s:
sa eva rudraḥ sa jagajjahāra sṛṣṭyarthamīśaḥ prapitāmaho'bhūt .
saṃrakṣaṇārthaṃ jagataḥ sa eva hariḥ sucakrāsigadābjapāṇiḥ .. 19.37 ..
6.3.d:
स एव रुद्रः स जगज्जहार सृष्ट्यर्थमीशः प्रपितामहोऽभूत् .
संरक्षणार्थं जगतः स एव हरिः सुचक्रासिगदाब्जपाणिः .. 19.37 ..
6.3.m:
He alone is Rudra; he destroyed the world. For the purpose of creation, the Lord became the Grandfather [Brahmā].
For the protection of the world, he alone is Hari, bearing the auspicious discus, sword, mace, and lotus in his hands.

6.3.s:
teṣāṃ vibhāgo na hi kartumarho mahātmanāmekaśarīrabhājām .
mīmāṃsāhetvarthaviśeṣatarkairyasteṣu kuryātpravibhedamajñaḥ .. 19.38 ..
6.3.d:
तेषां विभागो न हि कर्तुमर्हो महात्मनामेकशरीरभाजाम् .
मीमांसाहेत्वर्थविशेषतर्कैर्यस्तेषु कुर्यात्प्रविभेदमज्ञः .. 19.38 ..
6.3.m:
Indeed, no division ought to be made among these great souls sharing a single body.
The ignorant person who would make a division among them with arguments based on Mīmāṃsā reasons and meanings,

6.3.s:
sa yāti ghoraṃ narakaṃ krameṇa vibhāgakṛddveṣamatirdurātmā .
yā yasya bhaktiḥ sa tayaiva nūnaṃ dehaṃ tyajan svaṃ hyamṛtatvameti .. 19.39 ..
6.3.d:
स याति घोरं नरकं क्रमेण विभागकृद्द्वेषमतिर्दुरात्मा .
या यस्य भक्तिः स तयैव नूनं देहं त्यजन् स्वं ह्यमृतत्वमेति .. 19.39 ..
6.3.m:
that evil-minded one, a maker of division whose mind is full of hatred, goes gradually to a dreadful hell.
Whichever deity one has devotion to, through that very [devotion], upon abandoning his body, one surely attains immortality.

6.3.s:
saṃmohayanmūrtibhiratra lokaṃ sraṣṭā ca goptā kṣayakṛtsa devaḥ .
tasmānna mohātmakamāviśeta dveṣaṃ na kuryātpravibhinnamūrtiḥ .. 19.40 ..
6.3.d:
संमोहयन्मूर्तिभिरत्र लोकं स्रष्टा च गोप्ता क्षयकृत्स देवः .
तस्मान्न मोहात्मकमाविशेत द्वेषं न कुर्यात्प्रविभिन्नमूर्तिः .. 19.40 ..
6.3.m:
Deluding the world here through his forms, that god is the creator, the protector, and the destroyer.
Therefore, one should not enter into delusion, nor harbor hatred, seeing the forms as divided.

6.3.s:
vārāhamīśānavaro'pyato'sau rūpaṃ samāsthāya jagadvidhātā .
naṣṭe triloke'rṇavatoyamagne vimārgitoyaughamaye'ntarātmā .. 19.41 ..
6.3.d:
वाराहमीशानवरोऽप्यतोऽसौ रूपं समास्थाय जगद्विधाता .
नष्टे त्रिलोकेऽर्णवतोयमग्ने विमार्गितोयौघमयेऽन्तरात्मा .. 19.41 ..
6.3.m:
Assuming the form of a boar, therefore, that best sovereign, the creator of the world,
when the three worlds were lost, submerged in ocean waters, the inner Self searched in the flood of waters.

6.3.s:
bhittvārṇavaṃ toyamathāntarasthaṃ viveśa pātālatalaṃ kṣaṇena .
jale nimagnāṃ dharaṇīṃ samastāṃ samaspṛśatpaṅkajapatranetrām .. 19.42 ..
6.3.d:
भित्त्वार्णवं तोयमथान्तरस्थं विवेश पातालतलं क्षणेन .
जले निमग्नां धरणीं समस्तां समस्पृशत्पङ्कजपत्रनेत्राम् .. 19.42 ..
6.3.m:
Having cleaved the ocean water, he entered the depth of Pātāla in an instant;
he touched the entire earth sunk in the water, her eyes like lotus petals,

6.3.s:
viśīrṇaśailopalaśṛṅgakūṭāṃ vasuṃdharāṃ tāṃ pralaye pralīnām .
daṃṣṭraikayā viṣṇuratulyasāhasaḥ samuddadhāra svayameva devaḥ .. 19.43 ..
6.3.d:
विशीर्णशैलोपलशृङ्गकूटां वसुंधरां तां प्रलये प्रलीनाम् .
दंष्ट्रैकया विष्णुरतुल्यसाहसः समुद्दधार स्वयमेव देवः .. 19.43 ..
6.3.m:
the earth with shattered rocks and mountain peaks, dissolved in the cosmic dissolution;
Viṣṇu, the god of incomparable valor, lifted her up himself with a single tusk.

6.3.s:
sā tasya daṃṣṭrāgravilambitāṅgī kailāsaśṛṅgāgragateva jyotsnā .
vibhrājate sāpyasamānamūrtiḥ śaśāṅkaśṛṅge ca taḍidvilagnā .. 19.44 ..
6.3.d:
सा तस्य दंष्ट्राग्रविलम्बिताङ्गी कैलासशृङ्गाग्रगतेव ज्योत्स्ना .
विभ्राजते साप्यसमानमूर्तिः शशाङ्कशृङ्गे च तडिद्विलग्ना .. 19.44 ..
6.3.m:
Her limbs hanging from the tip of his tusk, she shone like moonlight on the peak of Mount Kailāsa,
and of incomparable form, she shone like lightning clinging to the crescent of the moon.

6.3.s:
tāmujjahārārṇavatoyamagnāṃ karī nimagnāmiva hastinīṃ haṭhāt .
nāvaṃ viśīrṇāmiva toyamadhyādudīrṇasattvo'nupamaprabhāvaḥ .. 19.45 ..
6.3.d:
तामुज्जहारार्णवतोयमग्नां करी निमग्नामिव हस्तिनीं हठात् .
नावं विशीर्णामिव तोयमध्यादुदीर्णसत्त्वोऽनुपमप्रभावः .. 19.45 ..
6.3.m:
He hauled her up, sunk in the ocean water, as an elephant violently hauls up a submerged female elephant,
or like a shattered boat from the midst of the water, he of aroused vitality and matchless power.

6.3.s:
sa tāṃ samuttārya mahājalaughātsamudramāryo vyabhajatsamastam .
mahārṇaveṣveva mahārṇavāmbho nikṣepayāmāsa punarnadīṣu .. 19.46 ..
6.3.d:
स तां समुत्तार्य महाजलौघात्समुद्रमार्यो व्यभजत्समस्तम् .
महार्णवेष्वेव महार्णवाम्भो निक्षेपयामास पुनर्नदीषु .. 19.46 ..
6.3.m:
Having raised her from the great flood of water, the noble one divided the entire ocean;
he poured back the water of the great ocean into the oceans and into the rivers.

6.3.s:
śīrṇāṃśca śailānsa cakāra bhūyo dvīpānsamastāṃśca tathārṇavāṃśca .
śailopalairye vicitāḥ samantācchiloccayāṃstānsa cakāra kalpe .. 19.47 ..
6.3.d:
शीर्णांश्च शैलान्स चकार भूयो द्वीपान्समस्तांश्च तथार्णवांश्च .
शैलोपलैर्ये विचिताः समन्ताच्छिलोच्चयांस्तान्स चकार कल्पे .. 19.47 ..
6.3.m:
And he made anew the broken mountains, all the islands, and the oceans;
he made the mountain ranges that are piled up everywhere with rocks and stones in the kalpa.

6.3.s:
anekarūpaṃ pravibhajya dehaṃ cakāra devendragaṇānsamastān .
mukhācca vahnirmanasaśca candraścakṣośca sūryaḥ sahasā babhūva .. 19.48 ..
6.3.d:
अनेकरूपं प्रविभज्य देहं चकार देवेन्द्रगणान्समस्तान् .
मुखाच्च वह्निर्मनसश्च चन्द्रश्चक्षोश्च सूर्यः सहसा बभूव .. 19.48 ..
6.3.m:
Dividing his body of manifold forms, he produced all the hosts of the lords of gods.
From his mouth fire arose, from his mind the moon, and from his eye the sun suddenly came to be.

6.3.s:
jajñe'tha tasyeśvarayogamūrteḥ pradhyāyamānasya surendrasaṅghaḥ .
vedāśca yajñāśca tathaiva varṇāstathā hi sarvauṣadhayo rasāśca .. 19.49 ..
6.3.d:
जज्ञेऽथ तस्येश्वरयोगमूर्तेः प्रध्यायमानस्य सुरेन्द्रसङ्घः .
वेदाश्च यज्ञाश्च तथैव वर्णास्तथा हि सर्वौषधयो रसाश्च .. 19.49 ..
6.3.m: Then, as that [Lord] whose form is the yoga of Īśvara meditated, the host of the chiefs of the gods was born, / as well as the Vedas, sacrifices, and likewise the castes, and indeed all medicinal herbs and juices.

6.3.s:
jagatsamastaṃ manasā babhūva yatsthāvaraṃ kiṃcidihāṇḍajaṃ vā .
jarāyujaṃ svedajamudbhijjaṃ vā yatkiṃcidā kīṭapipīlakādyam .. 19.50 ..
6.3.d:
जगत्समस्तं मनसा बभूव यत्स्थावरं किंचिदिहाण्डजं वा .
जरायुजं स्वेदजमुद्भिज्जं वा यत्किंचिदा कीटपिपीलकाद्यम् .. 19.50 ..
6.3.m: The entire universe came into being from his mind: whatever is stationary here or egg-born, / or born from a womb, sweat-born, or shoot-born—whatever exists, down to insects and ants.

6.3.s:
tato vijajñe manasā kṣaṇena anekarūpāḥ sahasā maheśā .
cakāra yanmūrtibhiravyayātmā aṣṭābhirāviśya punaḥ sa tatra .. 19.51 ..
6.3.d:
ततो विजज्ञे मनसा क्षणेन अनेकरूपाः सहसा महेशा .
चकार यन्मूर्तिभिरव्ययात्मा अष्टाभिराविश्य पुनः स तत्र .. 19.51 ..
6.3.m: Then in an instant, through his mind, the great lords of various forms were suddenly born; / and the imperishable Self, having pervaded there again with his eight forms, brought it about.

6.3.s:
līlāṃ cakārātha samṛddhatejā ato'tra me paśyata eva viprāḥ .
teṣāṃ mayā darśanameva sarvaṃ yāvanmuhūrtātsamakāri bhūpa .. 19.52 ..
6.3.d:
लीलां चकाराथ समृद्धतेजा अतोऽत्र मे पश्यत एव विप्राः .
तेषां मया दर्शनमेव सर्वं यावन्मुहूर्तात्समकारि भूप .. 19.52 ..
6.3.m: Then he of abundant splendor engaged in sport; hence, right as I was watching, O brahmins, / my vision of all those [creations] took place within an instant, O king.

6.3.s:
kṛtvā tvaśeṣaṃ kila līlayaiva sa devadevo jagatāṃ vidhātā .
sarvatradṛksarvaga eva devo jagāma cādarśanamādikartā .. 19.53 ..
6.3.d:
कृत्वा त्वशेषं किल लीलयैव स देवदेवो जगतां विधाता .
सर्वत्रदृक्सर्वग एव देवो जगाम चादर्शनमादिकर्ता .. 19.53 ..
6.3.m: Having indeed accomplished everything in mere sport, that god of gods, the creator of the worlds, / the all-seeing, omnipresent god, the primeval maker, vanished from sight.

6.3.s:
yattanmuhūrtādiha nāmarūpaṃ tāvatprapaśyāmi jagattathaiva .
dvīpaiḥ samudrairabhisaṃvṛtaṃ hi nakṣatratārādivimānakīrṇam .. 19.54 ..
6.3.d:
यत्तन्मुहूर्तादिह नामरूपं तावत्प्रपश्यामि जगत्तथैव .
द्वीपैः समुद्रैरभिसंवृतं हि नक्षत्रतारादिविमानकीर्णम् .. 19.54 ..
6.3.m: Just as from that moment name and form [arose] here, so too did I behold the universe: / surrounded by continents and oceans, crowded with the aerial chariots of constellations, stars, and the like,

6.3.s:
viyatpayodagrahacakracitraṃ nānāvidhaiḥ prāṇigaṇairvṛtaṃ ca .
tāṃ vai na paśyāmi mahānubhāvāṃ gorūpiṇīṃ sarvasureśvarīṃ ca .. 19.55 ..
6.3.d:
वियत्पयोदग्रहचक्रचित्रं नानाविधैः प्राणिगणैर्वृतं च .
तां वै न पश्यामि महानुभावां गोरूपिणीं सर्वसुरेश्वरीं च .. 19.55 ..
6.3.m: variegated with the sky, clouds, and the circle of planets, and filled with various kinds of living creatures. / Yet I did not see her, the noble lady in the form of a cow, the sovereign of all the gods.

6.3.s:
kva sāṃprataṃ seti vicintya rājanvibhrāntacittastvabhavaṃ tadaiva .
diśo vibhāgānavalokayānṛte punastāṃ kathamīśvarāṅgīm .. 19.56 ..
6.3.d:
क्व सांप्रतं सेति विचिन्त्य राजन्विभ्रान्तचित्तस्त्वभवं तदैव .
दिशो विभागानवलोकयानृते पुनस्तां कथमीश्वराङ्गीम् .. 19.56 ..
6.3.m: "Where is she now?"—reflecting thus, O king, my mind became bewildered at that very moment. / Looking around at the quarters of space without seeing her whose body is of the Lord, how

6.3.s:
paśyāmi tāmatra punaśca śubhrāṃ mahābhranīlāṃ śuciśubhratoyām .
vṛkṣairanekairupaśobhitāṅgīṃ gajaisturaṅgairvihagairvṛtāṃ ca .. 19.57 ..
6.3.d:
पश्यामि तामत्र पुनश्च शुभ्रां महाभ्रनीलां शुचिशुभ्रतोयाम् .
वृक्षैरनेकैरुपशोभिताङ्गीं गजैस्तुरङ्गैर्विहगैर्वृतां च .. 19.57 ..
6.3.m: could I see her again here—the bright one, dark as a great cloud, of pure and white waters, / her body adorned with numerous trees, and surrounded by elephants, horses, and birds?

6.3.s:
yathā purātīramupetya devyāḥ samāsthitaścāpyamarakaṇṭake tu .
tathaiva paśyāmi sukhopaviṣṭa ātmānamavyagramavāptasaukhyam .. 19.58 ..
6.3.d:
यथा पुरातीरमुपेत्य देव्याः समास्थितश्चाप्यमरकण्टके तु .
तथैव पश्यामि सुखोपविष्ट आत्मानमव्यग्रमवाप्तसौख्यम् .. 19.58 ..
6.3.m: Just as previously, having approached the bank of the goddess, I remained stationed at Amarakaṇṭaka, / in that very same way, seated at ease, unperturbed, and having attained bliss, I beheld myself

6.3.s:
tathaiva puṇyā malatoyavāhāṃ dṛṣṭvā punaḥ kalpaparikṣaye'pi .
ambāmivāryāmanukampamānāmakṣīṇatoyāṃ virujāṃ viśokaḥ .. 19.59 ..
6.3.d:
तथैव पुण्या मलतोयवाहां दृष्ट्वा पुनः कल्पपरिक्षयेऽपि .
अम्बामिवार्यामनुकम्पमानामक्षीणतोयां विरुजां विशोकः .. 19.59 ..
6.3.m: having seen again—even at the end of the kalpa—the holy one, carrier of pure waters, / who is like a compassionate mother, noble, of undiminished waters, free from disease, and I was free from sorrow.

6.3.s:
evaṃ mahatpuṇyatamaṃ ca kalpaṃ paṭhanti śṛṇvanti ca ye dvijendrāḥ .
mahāvarāhasya maheśvarasya dine dine te vimalā bhavanti .. 19.60 ..
6.3.d:
एवं महत्पुण्यतमं च कल्पं पठन्ति शृण्वन्ति च ये द्विजेन्द्राः .
महावराहस्य महेश्वरस्य दिने दिने ते विमला भवन्ति .. 19.60 ..
6.3.m: The best among the twice-born who recite and listen to this most sacred kalpa / of the Great Boar and the Great Lord become pure day by day.

6.3.s:
aśubhaśatasahasraṃ te vidhūya prapannāstridivamamarajuṣṭaṃ siddhagandharvayuktam .
vimalaśaśinibhābhiḥ sarva evāpsarobhiḥ saha vividhavilāsaiḥ svargasaukhyaṃ labhante .. 19.61 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe śrīnarmadāmāhātmye vārāhakalpavṛttāntavarṇanaṃ nāmaikonaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ ..
6.3.d:
अशुभशतसहस्रं ते विधूय प्रपन्नास्त्रिदिवममरजुष्टं सिद्धगन्धर्वयुक्तम् .
विमलशशिनिभाभिः सर्व एवाप्सरोभिः सह विविधविलासैः स्वर्गसौख्यं लभन्ते .. 19.61 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे श्रीनर्मदामाहात्म्ये वाराहकल्पवृत्तान्तवर्णनं नामैकोनविंशोऽध्यायः ..
6.3.m:
Shaking off hundreds of thousands of evils, they reach the heaven frequented by the immortals and accompanied by siddhas and gandharvas; / together with all the apsarases, resplendent like the spotless moon, they attain heavenly happiness with diverse pleasures.
Thus ends the nineteenth chapter, entitled "Description of the Account of the Vārāha Kalpa," in the Narmadāmāhātmya of the Revākhaṇḍa in the fifth Āvantyakhaṇḍa of the glorious Skandamahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
śrutā me vividhā dharmāḥ saṃhārāstvatprasādataḥ .
kṛtā devena sarveṇa ye ca dṛṣṭāstvayānagha .. 20.1 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
श्रुता मे विविधा धर्माः संहारास्त्वत्प्रसादतः .
कृता देवेन सर्वेण ये च दृष्टास्त्वयानघ .. 20.1 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / By your grace I have heard of the diverse duties and the dissolutions / brought about by the god Śarva, and whatever was witnessed by you, O sinless one.

6.3.s:
sāmprataṃ śrotumicchāmi prabhāvaṃ śārṅgadhanvanaḥ .
tvayānubhūtaṃ viprendra tanme tvaṃ vaktumarhasi .. 20.2 ..
6.3.d:
साम्प्रतं श्रोतुमिच्छामि प्रभावं शार्ङ्गधन्वनः .
त्वयानुभूतं विप्रेन्द्र तन्मे त्वं वक्तुमर्हसि .. 20.2 ..
6.3.m: Now I wish to hear of the majesty of the wielder of the horn-bow (Śārṅgadhanvan) / that was experienced by you, O foremost of brahmins; you should tell me that.

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi prajāsaṃhāralakṣaṇam .
yaccihnaṃ dṛśyate tatra yathā kalpo vidhīyate .. 20.3 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि प्रजासंहारलक्षणम् .
यच्चिह्नं दृश्यते तत्र यथा कल्पो विधीयते .. 20.3 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Hereafter I shall declare the characteristics of the destruction of living beings, / whatever sign is seen there, and how the kalpa is arranged.

6.3.s:
ulkāpātāḥ sanirghātā bhūmikampastathaiva ca .
patate pāṃśuvarṣaṃ ca nirghoṣaścaiva dāruṇaḥ .. 20.4 ..
6.3.d:
उल्कापाताः सनिर्घाता भूमिकम्पस्तथैव च .
पतते पांशुवर्षं च निर्घोषश्चैव दारुणः .. 20.4 ..
6.3.m: There are falls of meteors accompanied by thunderbolts, as well as an earthquake; / a shower of dust falls, along with a dreadful roar.

6.3.s:
yakṣakinnaragandharvāḥ piśācoragarākṣasāḥ .
sarve te pralayaṃ yānti yugānte samupasthite .. 20.5 ..
6.3.d:
यक्षकिन्नरगन्धर्वाः पिशाचोरगराक्षसाः .
सर्वे ते प्रलयं यान्ति युगान्ते समुपस्थिते .. 20.5 ..
6.3.m: Yakṣas, kinnaras, gandharvas, piśācas, serpents, and rākṣasas— / all of them go to dissolution when the end of the yuga has arrived.

6.3.s:
parvatāḥ sāgarā nadyaḥ sarāṃsi vividhāni ca .
vṛkṣāḥ śeṣaṃ samāyānti vallījātaṃ tṛṇāni ca .. 20.6 ..
6.3.d:
पर्वताः सागरा नद्यः सरांसि विविधानि च .
वृक्षाः शेषं समायान्ति वल्लीजातं तृणानि च .. 20.6 ..
6.3.m: Mountains, oceans, rivers, and various lakes, / trees, species of creepers, and grasses reach their end.

6.3.s:
evaṃ hi vyākulībhūte sarvauṣadhijalojjhite .
kāṣṭhabhūte tu saṃjāte trailokye sacarācare .. 20.7 ..
6.3.d:
एवं हि व्याकुलीभूते सर्वौषधिजलोज्झिते .
काष्ठभूते तु संजाते त्रैलोक्ये सचराचरे .. 20.7 ..
6.3.m: When the three worlds, both moving and unmoving, have thus become distraught, / devoid of all medicinal herbs and water, and turned into dry timber,

6.3.s:
yāvatpaśyāmi madhyāhne snānakāla upasthite .
trailokyaṃ jvalanākāraṃ durnirīkṣaṃ durāsadam .. 20.8 ..
6.3.d:
यावत्पश्यामि मध्याह्ने स्नानकाल उपस्थिते .
त्रैलोक्यं ज्वलनाकारं दुर्निरीक्षं दुरासदम् .. 20.8 ..
6.3.m: as I looked at midday when the time for ritual ablution arrived, / the three worlds appeared like blazing fire, difficult to behold and unapproachable.

6.3.s:
dvau sūryau pūrvatastāta paścimottarayostathā .
tathaiva dakṣiṇe dvau ca sūryau dṛṣṭau pratāpinau .. 20.9 ..
6.3.d:
द्वौ सूर्यौ पूर्वतस्तात पश्चिमोत्तरयोस्तथा .
तथैव दक्षिणे द्वौ च सूर्यौ दृष्टौ प्रतापिनौ .. 20.9 ..
6.3.m: Two suns were in the east, O dear one, and two in the west and north; / likewise in the south two blazing suns were seen.

6.3.s:
dvau sūryau nāgalokasthau madhye dvau gaganasya ca .
ityete dvādaśādityāstapante sarvato diśam .. 20.10 ..
6.3.d:
द्वौ सूर्यौ नागलोकस्थौ मध्ये द्वौ गगनस्य च .
इत्येते द्वादशादित्यास्तपन्ते सर्वतो दिशम् .. 20.10 ..
6.3.m: Two suns stood in the realm of serpents, and two in the middle of the sky; / thus these twelve suns burned every direction.

6.3.s:
pṛthivīmadahansarvāṃ saśailavanakānanām .
nādagdhaṃ dṛśyate kiṃcidṛte revāṃ ca māṃ tathā .. 20.11 ..
6.3.d:
पृथिवीमदहन्सर्वां सशैलवनकाननाम् .
नादग्धं दृश्यते किंचिदृते रेवां च मां तथा .. 20.11 ..
6.3.m: They burned the whole earth, along with its mountains, forests, and groves; / nothing was seen unburnt except the Revā and myself.

6.3.s:
pṛthivyāṃ dahyamānāyāṃ havirgandhaśca jāyate .
tato me śuṣyate gātraṃ tṛṣāpyevaṃ durāsadā .. 20.12 ..
6.3.d:
पृथिव्यां दह्यमानायां हविर्गन्धश्च जायते .
ततो मे शुष्यते गात्रं तृषाप्येवं दुरासदा .. 20.12 ..
6.3.m: As the earth was being burned, an odor of sacrificial offerings arose; / then my limbs became parched, and severe thirst overcame me.

6.3.s:
na hi vindāmi pānīyaṃ śoṣitaṃ ca divākaraiḥ .
yāvatkamaṇḍaluṃ vīkṣe śuṣkaṃ tatrāpi tajjalam .. 20.13 ..
6.3.d:
न हि विन्दामि पानीयं शोषितं च दिवाकरैः .
यावत्कमण्डलुं वीक्षे शुष्कं तत्रापि तज्जलम् .. 20.13 ..
6.3.m: For I could find no drinking water, dried up as it was by the suns; / when I looked at my water-pot, even the water there was dry.

6.3.s:
tato'haṃ śokasaṃtapto viśeṣātkṣuttṛṣārditaḥ .
utpapāta kṣiterūrdhvaṃ paśyamāno divaṃ prati .. 20.14 ..
6.3.d:
ततोऽहं शोकसंतप्तो विशेषात्क्षुत्तृषार्दितः .
उत्पपात क्षितेरूर्ध्वं पश्यमानो दिवं प्रति .. 20.14 ..
6.3.m: Then, tormented by grief and especially afflicted by hunger and thirst, / I flew upward from the earth, looking toward the sky.

6.3.s:
tāvatpaśyāmi gagane gṛhaṃ śṛṅgārabhūṣitam .
tatastajjñātukāmo'haṃ prasthito rājasattama .. 20.15 ..
6.3.d:
तावत्पश्यामि गगने गृहं शृङ्गारभूषितम् .
ततस्तज्ज्ञातुकामोऽहं प्रस्थितो राजसत्तम .. 20.15 ..
6.3.m: Presently I saw in the sky a palace adorned with erotic elegance; / then, wishing to know it, I set out, O best of kings.

6.3.s:
prākāreṇa vicitreṇa kapāṭārgalabhūṣitam .
vicitraśikharopetaṃ dvāradeśamupāgataḥ .. 20.16 ..
6.3.d:
प्राकारेण विचित्रेण कपाटार्गलभूषितम् .
विचित्रशिखरोपेतं द्वारदेशमुपागतः .. 20.16 ..
6.3.m: Adorned with doors and bolts, with a wonderful enclosure wall / and possessing splendid spires, I reached the entrance area.

6.3.s:
ṣaḍaśītisahasrāṇi yojanānāṃ samucchraye .
tadardhaṃ tu pṛthaktvena kāñcanaṃ ratnabhūṣitam .. 20.17 ..
6.3.d:
षडशीतिसहस्राणि योजनानां समुच्छ्रये .
तदर्धं तु पृथक्त्वेन काञ्चनं रत्नभूषितम् .. 20.17 ..
6.3.m: Eighty-six thousand yojanas in height, / and half of that in width, it was made of gold and adorned with jewels.

6.3.s:
tatra madhye parāṃ śayyāṃ paśyāmi nṛpasattama .
śayyopari śayānaṃ tu puruṣaṃ divyamūrdhajam .. 20.18 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र मध्ये परां शय्यां पश्यामि नृपसत्तम .
शय्योपरि शयानं तु पुरुषं दिव्यमूर्धजम् .. 20.18 ..
6.3.m: There in the middle I saw an excellent couch, O best of kings; / and lying upon the couch, a Person with divine hair,

6.3.s:
vikuñcitāgrakeśāntaṃ samastaṃ yojanāyatam .
mukuṭena vicitreṇa dīptikāntena śobhitam .. 20.19 ..
6.3.d:
विकुञ्चिताग्रकेशान्तं समस्तं योजनायतम् .
मुकुटेन विचित्रेण दीप्तिकान्तेन शोभितम् .. 20.19 ..
6.3.m: the ends of his hair curled at the front, extending a whole yojana in length, / adorned with a splendid crown of brilliant radiance,

6.3.s:
śyāmaṃ kamalapatrābhaṃ suprabhaṃ ca sunāsikam .
siṃhāsyamāyatabhujaṃ gallaśmaśruvarāṅkitam .. 20.20 ..
6.3.d:
श्यामं कमलपत्राभं सुप्रभं च सुनासिकम् .
सिंहास्यमायतभुजं गल्लश्मश्रुवराङ्कितम् .. 20.20 ..
6.3.m: dark-complexioned, resplendent as a lotus petal, with radiant luster and a handsome nose, / with a lion-like face, long arms, and marked with an excellent beard upon his cheeks,

6.3.s:
trivalībhaṅgasubhagaṃ karṇakuṇḍalabhūṣitam .
viśālābhaṃ supīnāṅgaṃ pārśvasvāvartabhūṣitam .. 20.21 ..
6.3.d:
त्रिवलीभङ्गसुभगं कर्णकुण्डलभूषितम् .
विशालाभं सुपीनाङ्गं पार्श्वस्वावर्तभूषितम् .. 20.21 ..
6.3.m: charming with the fold of three lines [on his neck], adorned with earrings, / of expansive splendor, with stout limbs, adorned with auspicious curls of hair on his flanks,

6.3.s:
śobhitaṃ kaṭibhāgena vibhaktaṃ jānujaṅghayoḥ .
padmāṅkitatalaṃ devamātāmrasunakhāṅgulim .. 20.22 ..
6.3.d:
शोभितं कटिभागेन विभक्तं जानुजङ्घयोः .
पद्माङ्किततलं देवमाताम्रसुनखाङ्गुलिम् .. 20.22 ..
6.3.m: graceful in his waist, well-proportioned in his knees and shanks, / the god whose soles are marked with lotuses, with slightly red, beautiful nails and fingers,

6.3.s:
meghanādasugambhīraṃ sarvāvayavasundaram .
śayyāmadhyagataṃ devamapaśyaṃ puruṣottamam .. 20.23 ..
6.3.d:
मेघनादसुगम्भीरं सर्वावयवसुन्दरम् .
शय्यामध्यगतं देवमपश्यं पुरुषोत्तमम् .. 20.23 ..
6.3.m: deep as the roar of a cloud, handsome in every limb; / I beheld that god, the Supreme Person, reposing in the middle of the couch,

6.3.s:
śaṅkhacakragadāpāṇiṃ śayānaṃ dakṣiṇena tu .
akṣasūtrodyatakaraṃ sūryāyutasamaprabham .. 20.24 ..
6.3.d:
शङ्खचक्रगदापाणिं शयानं दक्षिणेन तु .
अक्षसूत्रोद्यतकरं सूर्यायुतसमप्रभम् .. 20.24 ..
6.3.m: holding the conch, discus, and mace in his hands, reclining upon his right side, / with a hand raised holding a rosary, equal in radiance to ten thousand suns.

6.3.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhaktimāndevaṃ stotukāmo vyavasthitaḥ .
jayeśa jaya vāgīśa jaya divyāṅgabhūṣaṇa .. 20.25 ..
6.3.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा भक्तिमान्देवं स्तोतुकामो व्यवस्थितः .
जयेश जय वागीश जय दिव्याङ्गभूषण .. 20.25 ..
6.3.m: Seeing that god, full of devotion, I stood desiring to praise him: / "Victory, O Lord! Victory, O Lord of Speech! Victory, O you whose divine limbs are adorned!

6.3.s:
jaya devapate śrīmansākṣādbrahma sanātana .
tava lokāḥ śarīrasthāstvaṃ gatiḥ parameśvara .. 20.26 ..
6.3.d:
जय देवपते श्रीमन्साक्षाद्ब्रह्म सनातन .
तव लोकाः शरीरस्थास्त्वं गतिः परमेश्वर .. 20.26 ..
6.3.m: “Victory, O Lord of the gods, glorious one, eternal Brahman manifest! / The worlds abide within your body; you are the refuge, O supreme Lord!

6.3.s:
tvadādhārā hi deveśa sarve lokā vyavasthitāḥ .
tvaṃ śreṣṭhaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ tvaṃ kartā dharaṇīdharaḥ .. 20.27 ..
6.3.d:
त्वदाधारा हि देवेश सर्वे लोका व्यवस्थिताः .
त्वं श्रेष्ठः सर्वसत्त्वानां त्वं कर्ता धरणीधरः .. 20.27 ..
6.3.m: Supported by you indeed, O Lord of the gods, all the worlds remain established. / You are the highest among all beings; you are the creator, the upholder of the earth.

6.3.s:
tvaṃ hautramagnihotrāṇāṃ sūtramantrastvameva ca .
gokarṇaṃ bhadrakarṇaṃ ca tvaṃ ca māheśvaraṃ padam .. 20.28 ..
6.3.d:
त्वं हौत्रमग्निहोत्राणां सूत्रमन्त्रस्त्वमेव च .
गोकर्णं भद्रकर्णं च त्वं च माहेश्वरं पदम् .. 20.28 ..
6.3.m: You are the hotṛ's duty of the fire-sacrifices, and you alone are the thread and the sacred mantra. / You are Gokarṇa, Bhadrakarṇa, and the supreme state of the Great Lord.

6.3.s:
tvaṃ kīrtiḥ sarvakīrtīnāṃ dainyapāpapraṇāśinī .
tvaṃ naimiṣaṃ kurukṣetraṃ tvaṃ ca viṣṇupadaṃ param .. 20.29 ..
6.3.d:
त्वं कीर्तिः सर्वकीर्तीनां दैन्यपापप्रणाशिनी .
त्वं नैमिषं कुरुक्षेत्रं त्वं च विष्णुपदं परम् .. 20.29 ..
6.3.m: You are the fame among all fames that destroys distress and sin. / You are Naimiṣa, Kurukṣetra, and the supreme abode of Viṣṇu.

6.3.s:
tvayā tu līlayā deva padākrāntā ca medinī .
tvayā baddho balirdeva tvayendrasya padaṃ kṛtam .. 20.30 ..
6.3.d:
त्वया तु लीलया देव पदाक्रान्ता च मेदिनी .
त्वया बद्धो बलिर्देव त्वयेन्द्रस्य पदं कृतम् .. 20.30 ..
6.3.m: By you indeed in mere play, O God, was the earth spanned by a step; / Bali was bound by you, O God, and Indra's station was established by you.

6.3.s:
tvaṃ kalirdvāparaṃ deva tretā kṛtayugaṃ tathā .
pralambadamanaśca tvaṃ sraṣṭā tvaṃ ca vināśakṛt .. 20.31 ..
6.3.d:
त्वं कलिर्द्वापरं देव त्रेता कृतयुगं तथा .
प्रलम्बदमनश्च त्वं स्रष्टा त्वं च विनाशकृत् .. 20.31 ..
6.3.m: You are Kali, Dvāpara, O God, as well as Tretā and Kṛtayuga. / You are the subduer of Pralamba; you are the creator and the destroyer.

6.3.s:
tvayā vai dhāryate lokāstvaṃ kālaḥ sarvasaṃkṣayaḥ .
tvayā hi deva sṛṣṭāstāḥ sarvā vai devayonayaḥ .. 20.32 ..
6.3.d:
त्वया वै धार्यते लोकास्त्वं कालः सर्वसंक्षयः .
त्वया हि देव सृष्टास्ताः सर्वा वै देवयोनयः .. 20.32 ..
6.3.m: By you indeed are the worlds upheld; you are Time, the destruction of all. / By you indeed, O God, all those divine wombs were created.

6.3.s:
tvaṃ panthāḥ sarvalokānāṃ tvaṃ ca mokṣaḥ parā gatiḥ .
brahmā tvadudbhavo devo rajorūpaḥ sanātanaḥ .
rudraḥ krodhodbhavo'pyevaṃ tvaṃ ca sattve vyavasthitaḥ .. 20.33 ..
6.3.d:
त्वं पन्थाः सर्वलोकानां त्वं च मोक्षः परा गतिः .
ब्रह्मा त्वदुद्भवो देवो रजोरूपः सनातनः .
रुद्रः क्रोधोद्भवोऽप्येवं त्वं च सत्त्वे व्यवस्थितः .. 20.33 ..
6.3.m: You are the path for all worlds, and you are liberation, the highest refuge. / The eternal god Brahmā, consisting of the quality of passion, is born from you; / Rudra too is born from anger, while you are established in pure goodness.

6.3.s:
etaccarācaraṃ deva krīḍanārthaṃ tvayā kṛtam .
evaṃ saṃtaptadehena stuto devo mayā prabhuḥ .. 20.34 ..
6.3.d:
एतच्चराचरं देव क्रीडनार्थं त्वया कृतम् .
एवं संतप्तदेहेन स्तुतो देवो मया प्रभुः .. 20.34 ..
6.3.m: All this moving and unmoving creation, O God, was made by you for your sport.” / Thus, with a body scorched [by thirst], the lordly God was praised by me,

6.3.s:
bhaktyā paramayā rājansarvabhūtapatiḥ prabhuḥ .
stuvanvai tatra paśyāmi vāripūrṇāṃstato ghaṭān .. 20.35 ..
6.3.d:
भक्त्या परमया राजन्सर्वभूतपतिः प्रभुः .
स्तुवन्वै तत्र पश्यामि वारिपूर्णांस्ततो घटान् .. 20.35 ..
6.3.m: with supreme devotion, O King, the sovereign Lord of all creatures. / As I was praising him, I saw jars full of water right there.

6.3.s:
tato mayā vismṛtā yā tṛṣā sā vardhitā punaḥ .
upāsarpaṃ tatastasya pārśvaṃ vai puruṣasya hi .. 20.36 ..
6.3.d:
ततो मया विस्मृता या तृषा सा वर्धिता पुनः .
उपासर्पं ततस्तस्य पार्श्वं वै पुरुषस्य हि .. 20.36 ..
6.3.m: Then my thirst, which had been forgotten, flared up again. / Thereupon I approached the side of that person,

6.3.s:
pānīyaṃ pātukāmena cintitaṃ ca mayā punaḥ .
nāpaśyata hi māṃ caiṣa supto'pi na ca budhyate .. 20.37 ..
6.3.d:
पानीयं पातुकामेन चिन्तितं च मया पुनः .
नापश्यत हि मां चैष सुप्तोऽपि न च बुध्यते .. 20.37 ..
6.3.m: desiring to drink the water; but again I thought: / “He does not see me, and though asleep, he does not awake.

6.3.s:
yastu pāpena saṃmūḍhaḥ sukhaṃ suptaṃ prabodhayet .
jāyate tasya pāpasya brahmahatyāphalaṃ mahat .. 20.38 ..
6.3.d:
यस्तु पापेन संमूढः सुखं सुप्तं प्रबोधयेत् .
जायते तस्य पापस्य ब्रह्महत्याफलं महत् .. 20.38 ..
6.3.m: Whoever, deluded by sin, awakens one sleeping peacefully, / to him accrues the great guilt of slaying a brahmin.”

6.3.s:
evaṃ saṃcintyamāne tu dvitīyo hyāgataḥ pumān .
nekṣate jalpate kiṃcidvāmaskandhe mṛgājinī .. 20.39 ..
6.3.d:
एवं संचिन्त्यमाने तु द्वितीयो ह्यागतः पुमान् .
नेक्षते जल्पते किंचिद्वामस्कन्धे मृगाजिनी .. 20.39 ..
6.3.m: While I was thinking thus, a second man arrived; / he looked at nothing, said nothing, and wore an antelope skin over his left shoulder.

6.3.s:
jaṭī kamaṇḍaludharo daṇḍī mekhalayā vṛtaḥ .
bhasmonmṛditasarvāṅgo mahātejāstrilocanaḥ .. 20.40 ..
6.3.d:
जटी कमण्डलुधरो दण्डी मेखलया वृतः .
भस्मोन्मृदितसर्वाङ्गो महातेजास्त्रिलोचनः .. 20.40 ..
6.3.m: He had matted locks, bore a water-pot, carried a staff, was girt with a girdle, / had his whole body smeared with sacred ashes, possessed great splendor, and had three eyes.

6.3.s:
yāvattaṃ stotukāmo'hamapaśyaṃ svacchacakṣuṣā .
tāvatsarvāṅgasambhūtyāmahatyā rūpasampadā .. 20.41 ..
6.3.d:
यावत्तं स्तोतुकामोऽहमपश्यं स्वच्छचक्षुषा .
तावत्सर्वाङ्गसम्भूत्यामहत्या रूपसम्पदा .. 20.41 ..
6.3.m: Just as, wishing to praise him, I looked with a clear gaze, / there, with great wealth of beauty springing from all her limbs,

6.3.s:
apaśyaṃ saṃvṛtāṃ nārīṃ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitām .
dṛṣṭvā tāṃ patito bhūmau jayasveti bruvaṃstataḥ .. 20.42 ..
6.3.d:
अपश्यं संवृतां नारीं सर्वाभरणभूषिताम् .
दृष्ट्वा तां पतितो भूमौ जयस्वेति ब्रुवंस्ततः .. 20.42 ..
6.3.m: I saw a woman covered [in garments] and adorned with all ornaments. / Seeing her, I fell to the ground, saying, “Hail!

6.3.s:
jaya rudrāṅgasambhūte jayavāhini sanātani .
jaya kaumāri māhendri vaiṣṇavī vāruṇī tathā .. 20.43 ..
6.3.d:
जय रुद्राङ्गसम्भूते जयवाहिनि सनातनि .
जय कौमारि माहेन्द्रि वैष्णवी वारुणी तथा .. 20.43 ..
6.3.m: Hail, O you born of Rudra’s body! O eternal one bearing victory! / Hail, O Kaumārī, Māhendrī, Vaiṣṇavī, and Vāruṇī!

6.3.s:
jaya kauberi sāvitri jaya dhātri varānane .
tṛṣṇayā taptadehasya rakṣāṃ kuru carācare .. 20.44 ..
6.3.d:
जय कौबेरि सावित्रि जय धात्रि वरानने .
तृष्णया तप्तदेहस्य रक्षां कुरु चराचरे .. 20.44 ..
6.3.m: Hail, O Kauberī, Sāvitrī! Hail, O supporter, fair-faced one! / Protect me, whose body is tormented by thirst, O mother of the moving and unmoving world!”

6.3.s:
śrīdevyuvāca -
prasannā vipraśārdūla tava vākyaiḥ suśobhanaiḥ .
vartate mānase yatte mayā jñātaṃ dvijottama .. 20.45 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीदेव्युवाच -
प्रसन्ना विप्रशार्दूल तव वाक्यैः सुशोभनैः .
वर्तते मानसे यत्ते मया ज्ञातं द्विजोत्तम .. 20.45 ..
6.3.m: The goddess said: / “I am pleased, O tiger among brahmins, with your very beautiful words. / What is in your mind is known to me, O best of the twice-born.

6.3.s:
śṛṇu vipra mamāpyasti vratametatsudāruṇam .
strīlaghutvānmayārabdhaṃ duṣkaraṃ mandamedhayā .. 20.46 ..
6.3.d:
शृणु विप्र ममाप्यस्ति व्रतमेतत्सुदारुणम् .
स्त्रीलघुत्वान्मयारब्धं दुष्करं मन्दमेधया .. 20.46 ..
6.3.m: Listen, O brahmin: I too have a very severe vow, / which, through the fickleness of a woman and with slow intellect, was undertaken by me, hard to accomplish:

6.3.s:
yadi bhāvī ca me putro dharmiṣṭho lokaviśrutaḥ .
viprasya tu stanaṃ dattvā paścāddāsyāmi bālake .. 20.47 ..
6.3.d:
यदि भावी च मे पुत्रो धर्मिष्ठो लोकविश्रुतः .
विप्रस्य तु स्तनं दत्त्वा पश्चाद्दास्यामि बालके .. 20.47 ..
6.3.m: ‘If a son shall be born to me, most righteous and renowned in the worlds, / only after giving my breast to a brahmin shall I give it to the child.’

6.3.s:
sa me putraḥ samutpanno yathokto me mahāmune .
stanaṃ piba tvaṃ viprendra yadi jīvitumicchasi .. 20.48 ..
6.3.d:
स मे पुत्रः समुत्पन्नो यथोक्तो मे महामुने .
स्तनं पिब त्वं विप्रेन्द्र यदि जीवितुमिच्छसि .. 20.48 ..
6.3.m: That son has been born to me, as was spoken, O great sage. / Drink from the breast, O leader among brahmins, if you wish to live!”

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
akāryametadviprāṇāṃ yastvimaṃ pibate stanam .
punaścaivopanayanaṃ vratasiddhiṃ na gacchati .. 20.49 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
अकार्यमेतद्विप्राणां यस्त्विमं पिबते स्तनम् .
पुनश्चैवोपनयनं व्रतसिद्धिं न गच्छति .. 20.49 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / “This is an improper act for brahmins; whoever drinks this breast / must undergo the sacred thread ceremony again and does not attain the fruition of his vow.

6.3.s:
brāhmaṇatvaṃ tribhirlokairdurlabhaṃ padmalocane .
saṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛto vipro yaiśca jāyeta tacchṛṇu .. 20.50 ..
6.3.d:
ब्राह्मणत्वं त्रिभिर्लोकैर्दुर्लभं पद्मलोचने .
संस्कारैः संस्कृतो विप्रो यैश्च जायेत तच्छृणु .. 20.50 ..
6.3.m: Brahminhood is difficult to attain in the three worlds, O lotus-eyed one. / Hear about the sacraments through which a brahmin is consecrated:

6.3.s:
prathamaṃ caiva nārīṣu saṃskārairbījavāpatam .
bījaprakṣepaṇādeva bījakṣepaḥ sa ucyate .. 20.51 ..
6.3.d:
प्रथमं चैव नारीषु संस्कारैर्बीजवापतम् .
बीजप्रक्षेपणादेव बीजक्षेपः स उच्यते .. 20.51 ..
6.3.m: First is the sowing of seed in women with sacred rites; / because the seed is cast, it is called the casting of seed.

6.3.s:
tadante ca mahābhāge garbhādhānaṃ dvitīyakam .
puṃsavanaṃ tṛtīyaṃ tu sīmantaṃ ca caturthakam .. 20.52 ..
6.3.d:
तदन्ते च महाभागे गर्भाधानं द्वितीयकम् .
पुंसवनं तृतीयं तु सीमन्तं च चतुर्थकम् .. 20.52 ..
6.3.m: After that, O fortunate lady, the rite of impregnation is the second; / the rite for procuring a male child is the third, and the parting of the hair is the fourth;

6.3.s:
pañcamaṃ jātakarma syānnāma vai ṣaṣṭhamucyate .
niṣkrāmaḥ saptamaścaiva hyannaprāśanamaṣṭamam .. 20.53 ..
6.3.d:
पञ्चमं जातकर्म स्यान्नाम वै षष्ठमुच्यते .
निष्क्रामः सप्तमश्चैव ह्यन्नप्राशनमष्टमम् .. 20.53 ..
6.3.m: the fifth is the birth-rite, the name-giving is called the sixth; / the seventh is the first outing, and the eighth is the feeding of solid food;

6.3.s:
navamaṃ vai cūḍakarma daśamaṃ mauñjibandhanam .
aiṣikaṃ dārvikaṃ caiva saumikaṃ bhaumikaṃ tathā .. 20.54 ..
6.3.d:
नवमं वै चूडकर्म दशमं मौञ्जिबन्धनम् .
ऐषिकं दार्विकं चैव सौमिकं भौमिकं तथा .. 20.54 ..
6.3.m: the ninth is the tonsure ceremony, and the tenth is the tying of the muñja-grass girdle; / then rites with reed-stalks, wooden implements, Soma rituals, and earthly rites;

6.3.s:
patnīsaṃyojanaṃ cānyaddaivakarma tataḥ param .
mānuṣyaṃ pitṛkarma syāddaśamāṣṭāsu śobhane .. 20.55 ..
6.3.d:
पत्नीसंयोजनं चान्यद्दैवकर्म ततः परम् .
मानुष्यं पितृकर्म स्याद्दशमाष्टासु शोभने .. 20.55 ..
6.3.m: and next, union with a wife, and then the rites for the gods; / the human rites, the ancestral rites, in the eighteenth, O fair one;

6.3.s: bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ tatheṣṭaṃ ca pārvaṇaṃ ca tataḥ param .. 20.56 ..
6.3.d: भूतं भव्यं तथेष्टं च पार्वणं च ततः परम् .. 20.56 ..
6.3.m: the offerings to living beings, what is yet to come, the iṣṭi rites, and after that the seasonal sacrifices;

6.3.s:
śrāddhaṃ śrāvaṇyāmāgrayaṇaṃ ca caitrāśvayujyāṃ daśapaurṇamāsyām .
nirūḍhapaśusavanasautrāmaṇyagniṣṭomātyagniṣṭomāḥ .. 20.57 ..
6.3.d:
श्राद्धं श्रावण्यामाग्रयणं च चैत्राश्वयुज्यां दशपौर्णमास्याम् .
निरूढपशुसवनसौत्रामण्यग्निष्टोमात्यग्निष्टोमाः .. 20.57 ..
6.3.m: the ancestral rite on the full-moon day of Śrāvaṇa, the first-fruits sacrifice on the full-moon of Caitra and Āśvina, the animal sacrifice, the sautrāmaṇī, the agniṣṭoma, the atyagniṣṭoma;

6.3.s:
ṣoḍaṣīvājapeyātirātrāptoryāmodaśavājapeyāḥ .
sarvabhūteṣu kṣāntiranasūyā śaucamaṅgalamakārpaṇyamaspṛheti .. 20.58 ..
6.3.d:
षोडषीवाजपेयातिरात्राप्तोर्यामोदशवाजपेयाः .
सर्वभूतेषु क्षान्तिरनसूया शौचमङ्गलमकार्पण्यमस्पृहेति .. 20.58 ..
6.3.m: the ṣoḍaśī, the vājapeya, the atirātra, the aptoryāma, and the ten-day vājapeyas; / and forbearance toward all beings, absence of envy, purity, auspicious conduct, freedom from miserliness, and lack of craving:

6.3.s: ebhiraṣṭacatvāriṃśadbhiḥ saṃskāraiḥ saṃkṛto brāhmaṇo bhavati .. 20.59 ..
6.3.d: एभिरष्टचत्वारिंशद्भिः संस्कारैः संकृतो ब्राह्मणो भवति .. 20.59 ..
6.3.m: consecrated by these forty-eight sacraments, one becomes a brahmin.

6.3.s:
evaṃ jñātvā mahābhāge na tu māṃ pātumarhasi .
śiśupeyaṃ stanaṃ bhadre kathaṃ vai madvidhaḥ pibet .. 20.60 ..
6.3.d:
एवं ज्ञात्वा महाभागे न तु मां पातुमर्हसि .
शिशुपेयं स्तनं भद्रे कथं वै मद्विधः पिबेत् .. 20.60 ..
6.3.m: Knowing this, O fortunate lady, you should not make me drink. / How could one like me drink from a breast meant for an infant, O auspicious one?”

6.3.s: mamaitadvacanaṃ śrutvā nārī vacanamabravīt .. 20.61 ..
6.3.d: ममैतद्वचनं श्रुत्वा नारी वचनमब्रवीत् .. 20.61 ..
6.3.m: Hearing these words of mine, the woman spoke these words:

6.3.s:
yadi tvaṃ na pibeḥ stanyaṃ payo bālo mariṣyati .
śrūyate triṣu lokeṣu vedeṣu ca smṛtiṣvapi .
mucyate sarvapāpebhyo bhrūṇahatyā na muñcati .. 20.62 ..
6.3.d:
यदि त्वं न पिबेः स्तन्यं पयो बालो मरिष्यति .
श्रूयते त्रिषु लोकेषु वेदेषु च स्मृतिष्वपि .
मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो भ्रूणहत्या न मुञ्चति .. 20.62 ..
6.3.m: “If you do not drink the breast-milk, the child will die. / It is heard in the three worlds, in the Vedas, and in the traditional codes: / one is freed from all sins, but the killing of an embryo does not release [one].

6.3.s:
bhavitrī tava hatyā ca mahābhāgavataḥ punaḥ .
janmāni ca śatānyaṣṭau kliśyate bhrūṇahatyayā .. 20.63 ..
6.3.d:
भवित्री तव हत्या च महाभागवतः पुनः .
जन्मानि च शतान्यष्टौ क्लिश्यते भ्रूणहत्यया .. 20.63 ..
6.3.m: The murder of a great devotee will be upon you; / and for eight hundred lifetimes one suffers for the killing of an embryo.

6.3.s:
mṛtaḥ śunatvaṃ cāpnoti varṣāṇāṃ tu śatatrayam .
tatastasya kṣaye jāte kākayoniṃ vrajetpunaḥ .. 20.64 ..
6.3.d:
मृतः शुनत्वं चाप्नोति वर्षाणां तु शतत्रयम् .
ततस्तस्य क्षये जाते काकयोनिं व्रजेत्पुनः .. 20.64 ..
6.3.m: Having died, he attains the state of a dog for three hundred years; / then, when that is exhausted, he enters the womb of a crow;

6.3.s:
tatrāpi ca śatānyaṣṭau kliśyate pāpakarmaṇi .
varāho daśa janmāni tadante jāyate kṛmiḥ .. 20.65 ..
6.3.d:
तत्रापि च शतान्यष्टौ क्लिश्यते पापकर्मणि .
वराहो दश जन्मानि तदन्ते जायते कृमिः .. 20.65 ..
6.3.m: there too he suffers for eight hundred [years] for his sinful deed; / for ten births he is a boar, and after that he is born as a worm;

6.3.s:
tataścārohiṇīṃ prāpya gogajāśvanṛjanmabhāk .
śrūyate śrutiśāstreṣu vedeṣu ca paraṃtapa .. 20.66 ..
6.3.d:
ततश्चारोहिणीं प्राप्य गोगजाश्वनृजन्मभाक् .
श्रूयते श्रुतिशास्त्रेषु वेदेषु च परंतप .. 20.66 ..
6.3.m: then, ascending the ladder of rebirths, he takes birth as a cow, an elephant, a horse, and a human. / This is heard in the revealed scriptures and in the Vedas, O scorcher of foes.

6.3.s:
sarvapāpādhikaṃ pāpaṃ bālahatyā dvijottama .
bālahatyāyuto vipraḥ pacyate narake dhruvam .. 20.67 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वपापाधिकं पापं बालहत्या द्विजोत्तम .
बालहत्यायुतो विप्रः पच्यते नरके ध्रुवम् .. 20.67 ..
6.3.m: Greater than all sins is the sin of killing a child, O best of the twice-born. / A brahmin burdened with the killing of a child is surely cooked in hell.”

6.3.s:
varṣāṇi ca śatānyaṣṭau prāpnoti yamayātanām .
tasmādalpataro doṣaḥ pibato me stanaṃ tava .. 20.68 ..
6.3.d:
वर्षाणि च शतान्यष्टौ प्राप्नोति यमयातनाम् .
तस्मादल्पतरो दोषः पिबतो मे स्तनं तव .. 20.68 ..
6.3.m: and endures the torment of Yama for eight hundred years. / Therefore, the fault is lighter for you who drink of my breast.

6.3.s:
tathaivāpibataḥ pāpaṃ jāyate bahuvarṣikam .
kṣudhātṛṣāvirāmaste puṇyaṃ ca pibataḥ stanam .. 20.69 ..
6.3.d:
तथैवापिबतः पापं जायते बहुवर्षिकम् .
क्षुधातृषाविरामस्ते पुण्यं च पिबतः स्तनम् .. 20.69 ..
6.3.m: Likewise, for one who does not drink, sin lasting for many years arises. / For you, drinking from the breast brings an end to hunger and thirst, and brings merit.

6.3.s:
ato na cetaḥ saṃdigdhaṃ kartavyamiha karhicit .
ehi vipra yathākāmaṃ bālārthe piba me stanam .. 20.70 ..
6.3.d:
अतो न चेतः संदिग्धं कर्तव्यमिह कर्हिचित् .
एहि विप्र यथाकामं बालार्थे पिब मे स्तनम् .. 20.70 ..
6.3.m: Therefore, you should never make your mind doubtful here. / Come, brahmin, drink of my breast as you please for the child’s sake.”

6.3.s:
tato'haṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā stanaṃ pātuṃ samudyataḥ .
na ca tṛptiṃ vijānāmi pibataḥ stanamuttamam .. 20.71 ..
6.3.d:
ततोऽहं वचनं श्रुत्वा स्तनं पातुं समुद्यतः .
न च तृप्तिं विजानामि पिबतः स्तनमुत्तमम् .. 20.71 ..
6.3.m: Then, having heard her words, I prepared to drink from her breast, / and drinking that supreme breast, I knew no satiety.

6.3.s:
triṃśadvarṣasahasrāṇi bhārataivaṃ śatāni ca .
tataḥ prabuddhotsaṅge'haṃ māyānidrāvimohitaḥ .. 20.72 ..
6.3.d:
त्रिंशद्वर्षसहस्राणि भारतैवं शतानि च .
ततः प्रबुद्धोत्सङ्गेऽहं मायानिद्राविमोहितः .. 20.72 ..
6.3.m: Thirty thousand and [several] hundred years [passed] thus, O Bhārata. / Then I woke upon her lap, bewildered by illusory sleep.

6.3.s:
nidrāvigatamoho'haṃ yāvatpaśyāmi pāṇḍava .
tāvatsuptaṃ na paśyāmi na ca taṃ bālakaṃ vibho .. 20.73 ..
6.3.d:
निद्राविगतमोहोऽहं यावत्पश्यामि पाण्डव .
तावत्सुप्तं न पश्यामि न च तं बालकं विभो .. 20.73 ..
6.3.m: When my delusion had departed with the sleep, as I looked, O Pāṇḍava, / I did not see the sleeping one, nor that child, O mighty one.

6.3.s:
caturastāṃśca vai kumbhān paśyāmi tatra bhārata .
na ca paśyāmi tāṃ devīṃ gatā vai kutracicca te .. 20.74 ..
6.3.d:
चतुरस्तांश्च वै कुम्भान् पश्यामि तत्र भारत .
न च पश्यामि तां देवीं गता वै कुत्रचिच्च ते .. 20.74 ..
6.3.m: And I saw there those four pitchers, O Bhārata, / but I did not see that goddess; she had gone somewhere.

6.3.s:
evaṃ vimṛśyamānasya cintayānasya tiṣṭhataḥ .
īṣaddhasitayā vācā devī vacanamabravīt .. 20.75 ..
6.3.d:
एवं विमृश्यमानस्य चिन्तयानस्य तिष्ठतः .
ईषद्धसितया वाचा देवी वचनमब्रवीत् .. 20.75 ..
6.3.m: As I stood there reflecting and pondering in this way, / the goddess spoke words in a gently smiling voice.

6.3.s:
śrīdevyuvāca -
kṛṣṇaḥ sa puruṣaḥ supto dvitīyo'pyāgato haraḥ .
ye catvāraśca te kumbhāḥ samudrāste dvijottama .. 20.76 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीदेव्युवाच -
कृष्णः स पुरुषः सुप्तो द्वितीयोऽप्यागतो हरः .
ये चत्वारश्च ते कुम्भाः समुद्रास्ते द्विजोत्तम .. 20.76 ..
6.3.m: The holy goddess said: / “That dark-complexioned person who slept was Hara, who has also departed. / Those four jars which were there are the oceans, O best of brahmins.

6.3.s:
yaśca bālastvayā dṛṣṭo brāhmā lokapitāmahaḥ .
ahaṃ ca pṛthivī jñeyā saptadvīpā sarvatā .. 20.77 ..
6.3.d:
यश्च बालस्त्वया दृष्टो ब्राह्मा लोकपितामहः .
अहं च पृथिवी ज्ञेया सप्तद्वीपा सर्वता .. 20.77 ..
6.3.m: And the child whom you saw was Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds. / And know me to be the earth, having seven continents on every side,

6.3.s:
yā gatā tvāṃ parityajya bhūtale supratiṣṭhitā .
imāṃ ca prekṣase vipra narmadāṃ saritāṃ varām .. 20.78 ..
6.3.d:
या गता त्वां परित्यज्य भूतले सुप्रतिष्ठिता .
इमां च प्रेक्षसे विप्र नर्मदां सरितां वराम् .. 20.78 ..
6.3.m: who departed leaving you, well established upon the earth's surface. / And you behold, O brahmin, this Narmadā, the best of rivers,

6.3.s:
sarvasattvopakārāya bṛhate puṇyalakṣaṇā .
revānadī tu vikhyātā na mṛtā tena narmadā .. 20.79 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वसत्त्वोपकाराय बृहते पुण्यलक्षणा .
रेवानदी तु विख्याता न मृता तेन नर्मदा .. 20.79 ..
6.3.m: endowed with holy characteristics, great, for the benefit of all living beings. / She is renowned as the river Revā; therefore Narmadā has not died.

6.3.s:
evaṃ jñātvā śamaṃ gaccha svastho bhava mahāmune .
ityuktvā māṃ tadā devī tatraivāntaradhīyata .. 20.80 ..
6.3.d:
एवं ज्ञात्वा शमं गच्छ स्वस्थो भव महामुने .
इत्युक्त्वा मां तदा देवी तत्रैवान्तरधीयत .. 20.80 ..
6.3.m: Knowing thus, attain peace; be at ease, O great sage.” / Having spoken thus to me, the goddess disappeared right there.

6.3.s:
evaṃ hi śete bhagavānsattvasthaḥ pralaye sadā .
sattvarūpo mahādevo yadādhāre jagatsthitam .. 20.81 ..
6.3.d:
एवं हि शेते भगवान्सत्त्वस्थः प्रलये सदा .
सत्त्वरूपो महादेवो यदाधारे जगत्स्थितम् .. 20.81 ..
6.3.m: Thus indeed the Lord always lies, abiding in sattva during the dissolution; / Mahādeva, the embodiment of sattva, upon whose support the universe rests.

6.3.s:
evaṃ mayānubhūtaṃ tu dṛṣṭamāścaryamuttamam .
sarvapāpaharaṃ puṇyaṃ kathitaṃ te narottama .. 20.82 ..
6.3.d:
एवं मयानुभूतं तु दृष्टमाश्चर्यमुत्तमम् .
सर्वपापहरं पुण्यं कथितं ते नरोत्तम .. 20.82 ..
6.3.m: Thus was this supreme marvel experienced and seen by me; / holy and destroying all sins, it has been recounted to you, O best of men.

6.3.s:
viṣṇoścaritamityuktaṃ yattvayā paripṛcchitam .
bhūya eva mahābāho kimanyacchrotumicchasi .. 20.83 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe vārāhakalpavṛttāntavarṇanaṃ nāma viṃśo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 21
6.3.d:
विष्णोश्चरितमित्युक्तं यत्त्वया परिपृच्छितम् .
भूय एव महाबाहो किमन्यच्छ्रोतुमिच्छसि .. 20.83 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे वाराहकल्पवृत्तान्तवर्णनं नाम विंशोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 21
6.3.m:
This deeds of Viṣṇu have been recounted, as inquired by you. / What else do you wish to hear again, O mighty-armed one?
Thus ends the twentieth chapter, named 'Description of the Account of the Vārāha Kalpa', in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth Āvantyakhaṇḍa in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses].
Chapter 21

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
śrutaṃ me vividhāścaryaṃ tvatprasādāddvijottama .
bhūyaśca śrotumicchāmi tanme kathaya suvrata .. 21.1 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
श्रुतं मे विविधाश्चर्यं त्वत्प्रसादाद्द्विजोत्तम .
भूयश्च श्रोतुमिच्छामि तन्मे कथय सुव्रत .. 21.1 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / Various wonders have been heard by me through your grace, O best of brahmins; / and I wish to hear more; tell me that, O you of noble vows.

6.3.s:
kathameṣā nadī puṇyā sarvanadīṣu cottamā .
narmadā nāma vikhyātā bhūyo me kathayānagha .. 21.2 ..
6.3.d:
कथमेषा नदी पुण्या सर्वनदीषु चोत्तमा .
नर्मदा नाम विख्याता भूयो मे कथयानघ .. 21.2 ..
6.3.m: How is this sacred river, the best among all rivers, / renowned by the name Narmadā? Tell me again, O sinless one.

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
narmadā saritāṃ śreṣṭhā sarvapāpapraṇāśinī .
tārayetsarvabhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca .. 21.3 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
नर्मदा सरितां श्रेष्ठा सर्वपापप्रणाशिनी .
तारयेत्सर्वभूतानि स्थावराणि चराणि च .. 21.3 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / The Narmadā is the best of rivers, destroying all sins; / she carries across all beings, stationary and moving.

6.3.s:
narmadāyāstu māhātmyaṃ yatpūrveṇa mayā śrutam .
tatte'haṃ sampravakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣvaikamanā nṛpa .. 21.4 ..
6.3.d:
नर्मदायास्तु माहात्म्यं यत्पूर्वेण मया श्रुतम् .
तत्तेऽहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणुष्वैकमना नृप .. 21.4 ..
6.3.m: The majesty of the Narmadā which was heard by me formerly, / that I shall relate to you; listen with a single mind, O king.

6.3.s:
gaṅgā kanakhale puṇyā kurukṣetre sarasvatī .
grāme vā yadi vāraṇye puṇyā sarvatra narmadā .. 21.5 ..
6.3.d:
गङ्गा कनखले पुण्या कुरुक्षेत्रे सरस्वती .
ग्रामे वा यदि वारण्ये पुण्या सर्वत्र नर्मदा .. 21.5 ..
6.3.m: The Gaṅgā is sacred at Kanakhala; the Sarasvatī in Kurukṣetra; / whether in a village or in a forest, the Narmadā is sacred everywhere.

6.3.s:
tribhiḥ sārasvataṃ toyaṃ saptāhena tu yāmunam .
sadyaḥ punāti gāṅgeyaṃ darśanādeva nārmadam .. 21.6 ..
6.3.d:
त्रिभिः सारस्वतं तोयं सप्ताहेन तु यामुनम् .
सद्यः पुनाति गाङ्गेयं दर्शनादेव नार्मदम् .. 21.6 ..
6.3.m: The water of the Sarasvatī purifies in three [days], but that of the Yamunā in seven days; / that of the Gaṅgā purifies immediately, but that of the Narmadā merely by seeing it.

6.3.s:
kaliṅgadeśātpaścārdhe parvate'marakaṇṭake .
puṇyā ca triṣu lokeṣu ramaṇīyā pade pade .. 21.7 ..
6.3.d:
कलिङ्गदेशात्पश्चार्धे पर्वतेऽमरकण्टके .
पुण्या च त्रिषु लोकेषु रमणीया पदे पदे .. 21.7 ..
6.3.m: In the western half from the Kaliṅga country, on Mount Amarakaṇṭaka, / she is sacred in the three worlds and delightful at every step.

6.3.s:
tatra devāśca gandharvā ṛṣayaśca tapodhanāḥ .
tapastaptvā mahārāja siddhiṃ paramikāṃ gatāḥ .. 21.8 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र देवाश्च गन्धर्वा ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः .
तपस्तप्त्वा महाराज सिद्धिं परमिकां गताः .. 21.8 ..
6.3.m: There the gods, gandharvas, and seers whose wealth is austerity, / having practiced austerity, O great king, achieved supreme perfection. // 21.8

6.3.s:
tatra snātvā naro rājanniyamastho jitendriyaḥ .
upoṣya rajanīmekāṃ kulānāṃ tārayecchatam .. 21.9 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र स्नात्वा नरो राजन्नियमस्थो जितेन्द्रियः .
उपोष्य रजनीमेकां कुलानां तारयेच्छतम् .. 21.9 ..
6.3.m: A man who bathes there, O king, firm in vows, with senses restrained, / and fasts for a single night, would deliver a hundred lineages. // 21.9

6.3.s:
siddhikṣetraṃ paraṃ tāta parvato hyamaraṃkaṭaḥ .
sarvadevāśrito yasmādṛṣibhiḥ parisevitaḥ .. 21.10 ..
6.3.d:
सिद्धिक्षेत्रं परं तात पर्वतो ह्यमरंकटः .
सर्वदेवाश्रितो यस्मादृषिभिः परिसेवितः .. 21.10 ..
6.3.m: Indeed, dear one, Mount Amarakaṇṭaka is a supreme field of perfections, / because it is resorted to by all gods and attended by seers. // 21.10

6.3.s:
siddhavidyādharā bhūtagandharvāḥ sthānamuttamam .
dṛśyādṛśyāśca rājendra sevante siddhikāṅkṣiṇaḥ .. 21.11 ..
6.3.d:
सिद्धविद्याधरा भूतगन्धर्वाः स्थानमुत्तमम् .
दृश्यादृश्याश्च राजेन्द्र सेवन्ते सिद्धिकाङ्क्षिणः .. 21.11 ..
6.3.m: Siddhas, vidyādharas, bhūtas, and gandharvas, both visible and invisible, / O lord of kings, resort to that excellent place, longing for perfection. // 21.11

6.3.s:
ahaṃ ca paramaṃ sthānaṃ tataḥ prabhṛti saṃśritaḥ .
atra praṇavarūpo vai sthāne tiṣṭhatyumāpatiḥ .. 21.12 ..
6.3.d:
अहं च परमं स्थानं ततः प्रभृति संश्रितः .
अत्र प्रणवरूपो वै स्थाने तिष्ठत्युमापतिः .. 21.12 ..
6.3.m: And I have taken refuge in that supreme abode from that time on. / Truly, in that place the lord of Umā resides in the form of the praṇava. // 21.12

6.3.s:
śrīkaṇṭhaḥ sagaṇaḥ sarvabhūtasaṅghairniṣevitaḥ .
asmādgirivarādbhūpa vakṣye tīrthasya vistaram .. 21.13 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीकण्ठः सगणः सर्वभूतसङ्घैर्निषेवितः .
अस्माद्गिरिवराद्भूप वक्ष्ये तीर्थस्य विस्तरम् .. 21.13 ..
6.3.m: Śrīkaṇṭha, attended by his retinue and worshipped by multitudes of all spirits. / From this best of mountains, O king, I will recount the extent of the sacred ford, // 21.13

6.3.s:
yāni santīha tīrthāni puṇyāni nṛpasattama .
yāni yānīha tīrthāni narmadāyāstaṭadvaye .. 21.14 ..
6.3.d:
यानि सन्तीह तीर्थानि पुण्यानि नृपसत्तम .
यानि यानीह तीर्थानि नर्मदायास्तटद्वये .. 21.14 ..
6.3.m: and whatever holy sacred fords exist here, O best of kings, / whatever sacred fords exist here on both banks of the Narmadā. // 21.14

6.3.s:
na teṣāṃ vistaraṃ vaktuṃ śakto brahmāpi bhūpate .
yojanānāṃ śataṃ sāgraṃ śrūyate sariduttamā .. 21.15 ..
6.3.d:
न तेषां विस्तरं वक्तुं शक्तो ब्रह्मापि भूपते .
योजनानां शतं साग्रं श्रूयते सरिदुत्तमा .. 21.15 ..
6.3.m: Even Brahmā is not able to recount their extent, O ruler of the earth. / That best of rivers is heard to be more than a hundred yojanas [long], // 21.15

6.3.s:
vistareṇa tu rājendra ardhayojanamāyatā .
ṣaṣṭitīrthasahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭikoṭyastathaiva ca .. 21.16 ..
6.3.d:
विस्तरेण तु राजेन्द्र अर्धयोजनमायता .
षष्टितीर्थसहस्राणि षष्टिकोट्यस्तथैव च .. 21.16 ..
6.3.m: and in breadth, O lord of kings, it extends half a yojana. / Sixty thousand sacred fords and likewise sixty crores, // 21.16

6.3.s: parvatādudadhiṃ yāvadubhe kūle na saṃśayaḥ .. 21.17 ..
6.3.d: पर्वतादुदधिं यावदुभे कूले न संशयः .. 21.17 ..
6.3.m: from the mountain as far as the ocean, on both banks without doubt. // 21.17

6.3.s:
saptaṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi saptaṣaṣṭiśatāni ca .
saptaṣaṣṭistathā koṭyo vāyustīrthāni cābravīt .. 21.18 ..
6.3.d:
सप्तषष्टिसहस्राणि सप्तषष्टिशतानि च .
सप्तषष्टिस्तथा कोट्यो वायुस्तीर्थानि चाब्रवीत् .. 21.18 ..
6.3.m: Sixty-seven thousand, sixty-seven hundred, / and sixty-seven crores of sacred fords, Vāyu has declared. // 21.18

6.3.s:
paraṃ kṛtayuge tāni yānti pratyakṣatāṃ nṛpa .
paśyanti mānavāḥ sarve satataṃ dharmabuddhayaḥ .. 21.19 ..
6.3.d:
परं कृतयुगे तानि यान्ति प्रत्यक्षतां नृप .
पश्यन्ति मानवाः सर्वे सततं धर्मबुद्धयः .. 21.19 ..
6.3.m: In the Kṛtayuga, O king, they become directly visible; / all people whose minds are fixed on dharma see them constantly. // 21.19

6.3.s:
yathāyathā kalirghoro vartate dāruṇo nṛpa .
tathātathālpatāṃ yānti hīnasattvā yato narāḥ .. 21.20 ..
6.3.d:
यथायथा कलिर्घोरो वर्तते दारुणो नृप .
तथातथाल्पतां यान्ति हीनसत्त्वा यतो नराः .. 21.20 ..
6.3.m: As the dread, terrible Kali[yuga] progresses, O king, / so they diminish, because mortals are diminished in spirit. // 21.20

6.3.s:
jāleśvarāditīrthāni parvate'sminnarādhipa .
pitṛtṛptipradānyāhuḥ svargamokṣapradāni ca .. 21.21 ..
6.3.d:
जालेश्वरादितीर्थानि पर्वतेऽस्मिन्नराधिप .
पितृतृप्तिप्रदान्याहुः स्वर्गमोक्षप्रदानि च .. 21.21 ..
6.3.m: The sacred fords on this mountain beginning with Jāleśvara, O king, / are said to bestow satisfaction upon ancestors, and to grant heaven and liberation. // 21.21

6.3.s:
śreṣṭhaṃ dāruvanaṃ tatra carukāsaṃgamaḥ śubhaḥ .
uttare narmadāyāstu carukeśvaramuttamam .. 21.22 ..
6.3.d:
श्रेष्ठं दारुवनं तत्र चरुकासंगमः शुभः .
उत्तरे नर्मदायास्तु चरुकेश्वरमुत्तमम् .. 21.22 ..
6.3.m: The excellent Dāruvana is there, [and] the auspicious confluence with the Carukā. / On the north of the Narmadā is the excellent Carukeśvara, // 21.22

6.3.s:
dārukeśvaratīrthaṃ ca vyatīpāteśvaraṃ tathā .
pātāleśvaratīrthaṃ ca koṭiyajñaṃ tathaiva ca .. 21.23 ..
6.3.d:
दारुकेश्वरतीर्थं च व्यतीपातेश्वरं तथा .
पातालेश्वरतीर्थं च कोटियज्ञं तथैव च .. 21.23 ..
6.3.m: and the Dārukeśvara sacred ford, and likewise Vyatīpāteśvara, / and the Pātāleśvara sacred ford, and likewise Koṭiyajña. // 21.23

6.3.s:
iti caivottare kūle revāyā nṛpasattama .
amareśvarapārśve ca liṅgānyaṣṭottaraṃ śatam .. 21.24 ..
6.3.d:
इति चैवोत्तरे कूले रेवाया नृपसत्तम .
अमरेश्वरपार्श्वे च लिङ्गान्यष्टोत्तरं शतम् .. 21.24 ..
6.3.m: These are on the northern bank of the Revā, O best of kings, / and near Amareśvara are one hundred and eight liṅgas, // 21.24

6.3.s: varuṇeśvaramukhyāni sarvapāpaharāṇi ca .. 21.25 ..
6.3.d: वरुणेश्वरमुख्यानि सर्वपापहराणि च .. 21.25 ..
6.3.m: chief of which is Varuṇeśvara, taking away all sins. // 21.25

6.3.s:
māndhātṛpurapārśve ca siddheśvarayameśvarau .
oṅkārātpūrvabhāge ca kedāraṃ tīrthamuttamam .. 21.26 ..
6.3.d:
मान्धातृपुरपार्श्वे च सिद्धेश्वरयमेश्वरौ .
ओङ्कारात्पूर्वभागे च केदारं तीर्थमुत्तमम् .. 21.26 ..
6.3.m: And near Māndhātṛpura are Siddheśvara and Yameśvara, / and to the east of Oṅkāra is the excellent sacred ford Kedāra. // 21.26

6.3.s:
tatsamīpe mahārāja svargadvāramaghāpaham .
nāmnā brahmeśvaraṃ puṇyaṃ saptasārasvataṃ puraḥ .. 21.27 ..
6.3.d:
तत्समीपे महाराज स्वर्गद्वारमघापहम् .
नाम्ना ब्रह्मेश्वरं पुण्यं सप्तसारस्वतं पुरः .. 21.27 ..
6.3.m: Near it, O great king, is the gate to heaven that removes sin; / in front is the holy [ford] named Brahmeśvara, and Saptasārasvata, // 21.27

6.3.s:
rudrāṣṭakaṃ ca sāvitraṃ somatīrthaṃ tathaiva ca .
etāni dakṣiṇe tīre revāyā bharatarṣabha .. 21.28 ..
6.3.d:
रुद्राष्टकं च सावित्रं सोमतीर्थं तथैव च .
एतानि दक्षिणे तीरे रेवाया भरतर्षभ .. 21.28 ..
6.3.m: and Rudrāṣṭaka, Sāvitra, and likewise the Soma sacred ford. / These are on the southern bank of the Revā, O bull of the Bharatas. // 21.28

6.3.s:
asmiṃstu parvate tāta rudrāṇāṃ koṭayaḥ sthitāḥ .
snānaistuṣṭirbhavetteṣāṃ gandhamālyānulepanaiḥ .. 21.29 ..
6.3.d:
अस्मिंस्तु पर्वते तात रुद्राणां कोटयः स्थिताः .
स्नानैस्तुष्टिर्भवेत्तेषां गन्धमाल्यानुलेपनैः .. 21.29 ..
6.3.m: Indeed, dear one, crores of Rudras abide on this mountain. / They are pleased by ablutions, and by perfumes, garlands, and ointments. // 21.29

6.3.s:
prītāste'pi bhavantyatra rudrā rājanna saṃśayaḥ .
japena pāpasaṃśuddhirdhyānenānantyamaśnute .. 21.30 ..
6.3.d:
प्रीतास्तेऽपि भवन्त्यत्र रुद्रा राजन्न संशयः .
जपेन पापसंशुद्धिर्ध्यानेनानन्त्यमश्नुते .. 21.30 ..
6.3.m: Those Rudras also become delighted here, O king, there is no doubt. / By recitation of mantras comes purification from sin; by meditation one attains eternity. // 21.30

6.3.s:
dānena bhogānāpnoti ityevaṃ śaṅkaro'bravīt .
parvatātpaścime deśe svayaṃ devo maheśvaraḥ .
sthitaḥ praṇavarūpo'sau jagadādiḥ sanātanaḥ .. 21.31 ..
6.3.d:
दानेन भोगानाप्नोति इत्येवं शङ्करोऽब्रवीत् .
पर्वतात्पश्चिमे देशे स्वयं देवो महेश्वरः .
स्थितः प्रणवरूपोऽसौ जगदादिः सनातनः .. 21.31 ..
6.3.m: By giving gifts one obtains enjoyments; thus Śaṅkara declared. / In the western region from the mountain, the god Maheśvara himself / abides in the form of the praṇava, the source of the world, eternal. // 21.31

6.3.s:
tatra snātvā śucirbhūtvā brahmacārī jitendriyaḥ .
pitṛkāryaṃ prakurvīta vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā .. 21.32 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र स्नात्वा शुचिर्भूत्वा ब्रह्मचारी जितेन्द्रियः .
पितृकार्यं प्रकुर्वीत विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा .. 21.32 ..
6.3.m: Having bathed there, purified, celibate, with senses restrained, / one should perform ancestral rites according to prescribed ritual. // 21.32

6.3.s:
tilodakena tatraiva tarpayetpitṛdevatāḥ .
ā saptamaṃ kulaṃ tasya svarge modati pāṇḍava .. 21.33 ..
6.3.d:
तिलोदकेन तत्रैव तर्पयेत्पितृदेवताः .
आ सप्तमं कुलं तस्य स्वर्गे मोदति पाण्डव .. 21.33 ..
6.3.m: Right there one should offer water with sesame to the ancestral deities. / Up to the seventh generation his family rejoices in heaven, O Pāṇḍava. // 21.33

6.3.s:
ātmanā saha bhogāṃśca vividhān labhate sukhī .
ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi krīḍate surapūjitaḥ .. 21.34 ..
6.3.d:
आत्मना सह भोगांश्च विविधान् लभते सुखी .
षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि क्रीडते सुरपूजितः .. 21.34 ..
6.3.m: Together with himself, happy, he obtains various enjoyments; / for sixty thousand years he disports, worshipped by the gods. // 21.34

6.3.s:
modate suciraṃ kālaṃ pitṛpūjāphaladhitaḥ .
tataḥ svargātparibhraṣṭo jāyate vimale kule .. 21.35 ..
6.3.d:
मोदते सुचिरं कालं पितृपूजाफलधितः .
ततः स्वर्गात्परिभ्रष्टो जायते विमले कुले .. 21.35 ..
6.3.m: He rejoices for a very long time, sustained by the fruit of ancestral worship. / Then, fallen from heaven, he is born into an untainted family, // 21.35

6.3.s:
dhanavāndānaśīlaśca nīrogo lokapūjitaḥ .
punaḥ smarati tattīrthaṃ gamanaṃ kurute punaḥ .. 21.36 ..
6.3.d:
धनवान्दानशीलश्च नीरोगो लोकपूजितः .
पुनः स्मरति तत्तीर्थं गमनं कुरुते पुनः .. 21.36 ..
6.3.m: wealthy, generous, free from sickness, and honored by the world. / He remembers that sacred ford again and travels [there] once more. // 21.36

6.3.s:
dvitīye janmani bhaveddhradasyānucarotkaṭaḥ .
tathaiva brahmacaryeṇa sopavāso jitendriyaḥ .. 21.37 ..
6.3.d:
द्वितीये जन्मनि भवेद्ध्रदस्यानुचरोत्कटः .
तथैव ब्रह्मचर्येण सोपवासो जितेन्द्रियः .. 21.37 ..
6.3.m: In a second birth, he becomes an ardent attendant of the pool; / likewise through celibacy, fasting, and restrained senses, // 21.37

6.3.s:
sarvahiṃsānivṛttastu labhate phalamuttamam .
evaṃ dharmasamācāro yastu prāṇānparityajet .. 21.38 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वहिंसानिवृत्तस्तु लभते फलमुत्तमम् .
एवं धर्मसमाचारो यस्तु प्राणान्परित्यजेत् .. 21.38 ..
6.3.m: and abstaining from all harm, he obtains the highest fruit. / One whose conduct is righteous in this way, who abandons his life, // 21.38

6.3.s:
tasya puṇyaphalaṃ yadvai tannibodha narādhipa .
śataṃ varṣasahasrāṇi svarge modati pāṇḍava .. 21.39 ..
6.3.d:
तस्य पुण्यफलं यद्वै तन्निबोध नराधिप .
शतं वर्षसहस्राणि स्वर्गे मोदति पाण्डव .. 21.39 ..
6.3.m: learn the meritorious fruit of that person, O king: / for a hundred thousand years he rejoices in heaven, O Pāṇḍava, // 21.39

6.3.s:
apsarogaṇasaṃkīrṇe divyaśabdānunādite .
divyagandhānuliptāṅgo divyālaṅkārabhūṣitaḥ .. 21.40 ..
6.3.d:
अप्सरोगणसंकीर्णे दिव्यशब्दानुनादिते .
दिव्यगन्धानुलिप्ताङ्गो दिव्यालङ्कारभूषितः .. 21.40 ..
6.3.m: thronged by groups of apsarases, echoing with celestial sounds, / his limbs anointed with divine perfume, adorned with divine ornaments. // 21.40

6.3.s:
krīḍate daivataiḥ sārddhaṃ siddhagandharvasaṃstutaḥ .
tataḥ svargātparibhraṣṭo rājā bhavati vīryavān .. 21.41 ..
6.3.d:
क्रीडते दैवतैः सार्द्धं सिद्धगन्धर्वसंस्तुतः .
ततः स्वर्गात्परिभ्रष्टो राजा भवति वीर्यवान् .. 21.41 ..
6.3.m: He disports along with the deities, praised by siddhas and gandharvas. / Then, fallen from heaven, he becomes a mighty king, // 21.41

6.3.s:
hastyaśvarathayānaiśca dharmajñaḥ śāstratatparaḥ .
gṛhe stambhaśatākīrṇe sauvarṇe rajatānvite .. 21.42 ..
6.3.d:
हस्त्यश्वरथयानैश्च धर्मज्ञः शास्त्रतत्परः .
गृहे स्तम्भशताकीर्णे सौवर्णे रजतान्विते .. 21.42 ..
6.3.m: possessing elephants, horses, and chariots, knowing dharma, devoted to scripture. / In a house filled with a hundred pillars, of gold and furnished with silver, // 21.42

6.3.s:
saptāṣṭabhūmisudvāre dāsīdāsasamākule .
mattamātaṅganiḥśvāsairvājiheṣitanāditaiḥ .. 21.43 ..
6.3.d:
सप्ताष्टभूमिसुद्वारे दासीदाससमाकुले .
मत्तमातङ्गनिःश्वासैर्वाजिहेषितनादितैः .. 21.43 ..
6.3.m: with seven or eight stories and fine doorways, crowded with female and male servants, / resounded by the sighs of rutting elephants and the neighing of horses, // 21.43

6.3.s:
kṣubhyate tasya taddvāramindrasya bhuvanaṃ yathā .
rājarājeśvaraḥ śrīmānsarvastrījanavallabhaḥ .. 21.44 ..
6.3.d:
क्षुभ्यते तस्य तद्द्वारमिन्द्रस्य भुवनं यथा .
राजराजेश्वरः श्रीमान्सर्वस्त्रीजनवल्लभः .. 21.44 ..
6.3.m: whose gate surges like the abode of Indra, / an emperor of kings, glorious, dear to all women, // 21.44

6.3.s:
tasmingṛhe vasitvā tu krīḍābhogasamanvitaḥ .
jīvedvarṣaśataṃ sāgraṃ sarvavyādhivivarjitaḥ .. 21.45 ..
6.3.d:
तस्मिन्गृहे वसित्वा तु क्रीडाभोगसमन्वितः .
जीवेद्वर्षशतं साग्रं सर्वव्याधिविवर्जितः .. 21.45 ..
6.3.m: living in that house endowed with play and enjoyment, / he would live for more than a hundred years, freed from all disease. // 21.45

6.3.s:
evaṃ teṣāṃ bhavetsarvaṃ ye mṛtā hyamareśvare .
agnipraveśaṃ yaḥ kuryādbhaktyā hyamarakaṇṭake .. 21.46 ..
6.3.d:
एवं तेषां भवेत्सर्वं ये मृता ह्यमरेश्वरे .
अग्निप्रवेशं यः कुर्याद्भक्त्या ह्यमरकण्टके .. 21.46 ..
6.3.m: All this will befall those who die at Amareśvara. / One who enters fire with devotion at Amarakaṇṭaka, // 21.46

6.3.s:
sa mṛtaḥ svargamāpnoti yāsyate paramāṃ gatim .
snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham .. 21.47 ..
6.3.d:
स मृतः स्वर्गमाप्नोति यास्यते परमां गतिम् .
स्नानं दानं जपो होमः शुभं वा यदि वाशुभम् .. 21.47 ..
6.3.m: having died, reaches heaven, [and] will attain the supreme state. / Ablution, gift-giving, mantra recitation, oblation, whether auspicious or inauspicious, // 21.47

6.3.s:
purāṇe śrūyate rājansarvaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ bhavet .
tasyāstīre tu ye vṛkṣāḥ patitāḥ kālaparyaye .. 21.48 ..
6.3.d:
पुराणे श्रूयते राजन्सर्वं कोटिगुणं भवेत् .
तस्यास्तीरे तु ये वृक्षाः पतिताः कालपर्यये .. 21.48 ..
6.3.m: it is heard in the Purāṇa, O king, all becomes multiplied ten-millionfold. / But the trees on its bank that fall in the course of time, // 21.48

6.3.s:
narmadātoyasaṃspṛṣṭāste yānti paramāṃ gatim .
anivṛttikā gatistasya pavanasyāmbare yathā .. 21.49 ..
6.3.d:
