नर्मदातोयसंस्पृष्टास्ते यान्ति परमां गतिम् .
अनिवृत्तिका गतिस्तस्य पवनस्याम्बरे यथा .. 21.49 ..
6.3.m: touched by the waters of the Narmadā, go to the supreme state. / Non-returning is the destination of one who, like wind in the sky, // 21.49

6.3.s:
patanaṃ kurute yastu tasmiṃstīrthe narādhipa .
kanyāstrīṇi sahasrāṇi pātāle bhogabhāginaḥ .. 21.50 ..
6.3.d:
पतनं कुरुते यस्तु तस्मिंस्तीर्थे नराधिप .
कन्यास्त्रीणि सहस्राणि पाताले भोगभागिनः .. 21.50 ..
6.3.m: leaps down at that sacred ford, O ruler of men. / Three thousand maidens in Pātāla, sharers of pleasure, // 21.50

6.3.s:
tiṣṭhanti bhavane tasya preṣaṇe prārthayanti ca .
divyabhogaiḥ susampannaḥ krīḍate kālam .. 21.51 ..
6.3.d:
तिष्ठन्ति भवने तस्य प्रेषणे प्रार्थयन्ति च .
दिव्यभोगैः सुसम्पन्नः क्रीडते कालम् .. 21.51 ..
6.3.m: wait in his mansion and entreat to do his bidding. / Fully endowed with divine enjoyments, he disports for an [extended] time. // 21.51

6.3.s:
pṛthivyāṃ hyāsamudrāyāṃ tādṛśo naiva jāyate .
yādṛśo'yaṃ naraśreṣṭha parvato'marakaṇṭakaḥ .. 21.52 ..
6.3.d:
पृथिव्यां ह्यासमुद्रायां तादृशो नैव जायते .
यादृशोऽयं नरश्रेष्ठ पर्वतोऽमरकण्टकः .. 21.52 ..
6.3.m: On the whole earth bounded by the oceans, there is indeed none that arises like this, / O best of men, like this Mount Amarakaṇṭaka.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthaṃ tu vijñeyaṃ parvatasyānu paścime .
hrado jāleśvaro nāma triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ .. 21.53 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थं तु विज्ञेयं पर्वतस्यानु पश्चिमे .
ह्रदो जालेश्वरो नाम त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः .. 21.53 ..
6.3.m: There a sacred ford is to be known, following the west of the mountain, / a pool named Jāleśvara, renowned in the three worlds.

6.3.s:
tatra piṇḍapradānena sandhyopāsanakena tu .
pitaro dvādaśābdāni tarpitāstu bhavanti vai .. 21.54 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र पिण्डप्रदानेन सन्ध्योपासनकेन तु .
पितरो द्वादशाब्दानि तर्पितास्तु भवन्ति वै .. 21.54 ..
6.3.m: There, indeed, by offering ancestral food-balls and by worship during twilight rituals, / the ancestors remain satisfied for twelve years.

6.3.s:
dakṣiṇe narmadātīre kapilā tu mahānadī .
saralārjunasaṃchannā khadirairupaśobhitā .. 21.55 ..
6.3.d:
दक्षिणे नर्मदातीरे कपिला तु महानदी .
सरलार्जुनसंछन्ना खदिरैरुपशोभिता .. 21.55 ..
6.3.m: On the southern bank of the Narmadā, however, is the great river Kapilā, / overgrown with sarala and arjuna trees, adorned with khadiras,

6.3.s:
mādhavīsallakībhiśca vallībhiścāpyalaṃkṛtā .
śvāpadairgarjamānaiśca gomāyuvānarādibhiḥ .. 21.56 ..
6.3.d:
माधवीसल्लकीभिश्च वल्लीभिश्चाप्यलंकृता .
श्वापदैर्गर्जमानैश्च गोमायुवानरादिभिः .. 21.56 ..
6.3.m: adorned with mādhavī and sallakī creepers, / and with roaring beasts of prey, jackals, monkeys, and others,

6.3.s:
pakṣijātiviśeṣaiśca nityaṃ pramuditā nṛpa .
sāgraṃ koṭiśataṃ tatra ṛṣīṇāmiti śuśruma .. 21.57 ..
6.3.d:
पक्षिजातिविशेषैश्च नित्यं प्रमुदिता नृप .
साग्रं कोटिशतं तत्र ऋषीणामिति शुश्रुम .. 21.57 ..
6.3.m: and ever made joyful by various kinds of birds, O king. / There, we have heard, more than a hundred million seers,

6.3.s:
tapastaptvā gataṃ mokṣaṃ yeṣāṃ janma na cāgamaḥ .
yena tatra tapastaptaṃ kapilena mahātmanā .. 21.58 ..
6.3.d:
तपस्तप्त्वा गतं मोक्षं येषां जन्म न चागमः .
येन तत्र तपस्तप्तं कपिलेन महात्मना .. 21.58 ..
6.3.m: having performed austerity, attained liberation, and having no more birth or return. / By the high-souled Kapila who performed austerity there,

6.3.s:
tatra taccābhavattīrthaṃ puṇyaṃ siddhaniṣevitam .
yena sā kāpilaistāta sevitā ṛṣibhiḥ purā .. 21.59 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तच्चाभवत्तीर्थं पुण्यं सिद्धनिषेवितम् .
येन सा कापिलैस्तात सेविता ऋषिभिः पुरा .. 21.59 ..
6.3.m: there arose that meritorious sacred ford frequented by the perfected ones. / Since in ancient times she was frequented by the seers who were followers of Kapila, O dear one,

6.3.s:
tena sā kapilā nāma gītā pāpakṣayaṃkarī .
tatra koṭiśataṃ sāgraṃ tīrthānāmamareśvare .. 21.60 ..
6.3.d:
तेन सा कपिला नाम गीता पापक्षयंकरी .
तत्र कोटिशतं साग्रं तीर्थानाममरेश्वरे .. 21.60 ..
6.3.m: therefore she is celebrated as Kapilā, destroying sins. / There, at Amareśvara, are more than a hundred million sacred fords.

6.3.s:
ahorātroṣito bhūtvā mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ .
dānaṃ ca vidhivaddattvā yathāśaktyā dvijottame .. 21.61 ..
6.3.d:
अहोरात्रोषितो भूत्वा मुच्यते सर्वकिल्बिषैः .
दानं च विधिवद्दत्त्वा यथाशक्त्या द्विजोत्तमे .. 21.61 ..
6.3.m: Having fasted for a day and night, one is freed from all evils. / And having properly given gifts according to one's capacity to the best of brahmins,

6.3.s:
īśvarānugrahātsarvaṃ tatra koṭiguṇaṃ bhavet .
yasmādanakṣaraṃ rūpaṃ praṇavasyeha bhārata .. 21.62 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वरानुग्रहात्सर्वं तत्र कोटिगुणं भवेत् .
यस्मादनक्षरं रूपं प्रणवस्येह भारत .. 21.62 ..
6.3.m: everything there becomes ten-million-fold by the grace of Īśvara. / Since the form of the praṇava here is imperishable, O Bhārata,

6.3.s:
śivasvarūpasya tataḥ kṛtamātrākṣaraṃ bhavet .
tiryañcaḥ paśavaścaiva vṛkṣā gulmalatādayaḥ .. 21.63 ..
6.3.d:
शिवस्वरूपस्य ततः कृतमात्राक्षरं भवेत् .
तिर्यञ्चः पशवश्चैव वृक्षा गुल्मलतादयः .. 21.63 ..
6.3.m: therefore, by merely reciting the syllable of Śiva's nature, it bears fruit. / Animals, beasts, trees, shrubs, and creepers,

6.3.s:
te'pi tatra kṣayaṃ yātāḥ svargaṃ yānti na saṃśayaḥ .
viśalyā tatra yā proktā tatraiva tu mahānadī .. 21.64 ..
6.3.d:
तेऽपि तत्र क्षयं याताः स्वर्गं यान्ति न संशयः .
विशल्या तत्र या प्रोक्ता तत्रैव तु महानदी .. 21.64 ..
6.3.m: even they, meeting their end there, go to heaven without doubt. / The river Viśalyā, which is spoken of there, is indeed a great river right there.

6.3.s:
snātvā dattvā yathānyāyaṃ tatrāpi sukṛtī bhavet .
tatra devagaṇāḥ sarve sakinnaramahoragāḥ .. 21.65 ..
6.3.d:
स्नात्वा दत्त्वा यथान्यायं तत्रापि सुकृती भवेत् .
तत्र देवगणाः सर्वे सकिन्नरमहोरगाः .. 21.65 ..
6.3.m: Having bathed and given gifts there according to rule, one becomes a doer of good deeds. / There all the hosts of gods, along with kinnaras and great serpents,

6.3.s:
yakṣarākṣasagandharvā ṛṣayaśca tapodhanāḥ .
sarve samāgatāstāṃ vai paśyanti hyamareśvare .. 21.66 ..
6.3.d:
यक्षराक्षसगन्धर्वा ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः .
सर्वे समागतास्तां वै पश्यन्ति ह्यमरेश्वरे .. 21.66 ..
6.3.m: yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, and seers rich in austerity, / all gather together and behold her at Amareśvara.

6.3.s:
taiśca sarvaiḥ samāgamya vanditau tau śubhau kaṭau .
purā yuge mahāghore sarvalokabhayaṃkare .. 21.67 ..
6.3.d:
तैश्च सर्वैः समागम्य वन्दितौ तौ शुभौ कटौ .
पुरा युगे महाघोरे सर्वलोकभयंकरे .. 21.67 ..
6.3.m: And all of them, having assembled, worshipped those two auspicious banks. / Long ago, in a terrifying age frightful to all the worlds,

6.3.s:
narmadāyāḥ sutastatra saśalyo viśalīkṛtaḥ .
sarvadevaiśca ṛṣibhirviśalyā tena sā smṛtā .. 21.68 ..
6.3.d:
नर्मदायाः सुतस्तत्र सशल्यो विशलीकृतः .
सर्वदेवैश्च ऋषिभिर्विशल्या तेन सा स्मृता .. 21.68 ..
6.3.m: the son of Narmadā, pierced with a dart there, was freed of the dart / by all the gods and seers; therefore she is remembered as Viśalyā.

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
utpannā tu kathaṃ tāta viśalyā kapilā katham .
kathaṃ vā narmadāputraḥ śalyayukto'bhavanmune .. 21.69 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
उत्पन्ना तु कथं तात विशल्या कपिला कथम् .
कथं वा नर्मदापुत्रः शल्ययुक्तोऽभवन्मुने .. 21.69 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / How, O dear one, was Viśalyā born, and how Kapilā? / And how did the son of Narmadā become pierced with a dart, O sage?

6.3.s: āścaryabhūtaṃ lokasya śrotumicchāmi suvrata .. 21.70 ..
6.3.d: आश्चर्यभूतं लोकस्य श्रोतुमिच्छामि सुव्रत .. 21.70 ..
6.3.m: I wish to hear this wonder of the world, O one of noble vows.

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
purā dākṣāyaṇī nāma sahitā śūlapāṇinā .
krīḍitvā narmadātoye parayā ca mudā nṛpa .. 21.71 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
पुरा दाक्षायणी नाम सहिता शूलपाणिना .
क्रीडित्वा नर्मदातोये परया च मुदा नृप .. 21.71 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Formerly, the daughter of Dakṣa, accompanied by the trident-bearing [lord], / having sported in the waters of the Narmadā with supreme delight, O king,

6.3.s:
jalāduttīrya sahasā vastramanyatsamāharat .
devyāstu snānavastraṃ tatpīḍitaṃ līlayā nṛpa .. 21.72 ..
6.3.d:
जलादुत्तीर्य सहसा वस्त्रमन्यत्समाहरत् .
देव्यास्तु स्नानवस्त्रं तत्पीडितं लीलया नृप .. 21.72 ..
6.3.m: stepped out of the water swiftly and took another garment. / The goddess's bathing garment, squeezed out playfully, O king,

6.3.s:
sahitānucarībhistu indrāyudhanibhaṃ bhṛśam .
tasminniṣpīḍyamāne tu vāri yanniḥsṛtaṃ tadā .. 21.73 ..
6.3.d:
सहितानुचरीभिस्तु इन्द्रायुधनिभं भृशम् .
तस्मिन्निष्पीड्यमाने तु वारि यन्निःसृतं तदा .. 21.73 ..
6.3.m: together with her female attendants, greatly resembled Indra's bow [a rainbow]. / As it was being wrung out, the water that flowed forth then,

6.3.s:
tasmādiyaṃ sarijjajñe kapilākhyā mahānadī .
saṃyogādaṅgarāgasya vastrodyatkapilaṃ jalam .. 21.74 ..
6.3.d:
तस्मादियं सरिज्जज्ञे कपिलाख्या महानदी .
संयोगादङ्गरागस्य वस्त्रोद्यत्कपिलं जलम् .. 21.74 ..
6.3.m: from that was born this river, the great river named Kapilā. / Through contact with body ointment, the water flowing from the cloth was tawny;

6.3.s:
galitaṃ tena kapilā varṇato nāmato'bhavat .
tathā gandharasairyuktaṃ nānāpuṣpaistu vāsitam .. 21.75 ..
6.3.d:
गलितं तेन कपिला वर्णतो नामतोऽभवत् .
तथा गन्धरसैर्युक्तं नानापुष्पैस्तु वासितम् .. 21.75 ..
6.3.m: it fell, and therefore it became Kapilā in color and in name. / Likewise filled with fragrant scents and perfumed with diverse flowers,

6.3.s:
nānāvarṇāruṇaṃ śubhraṃ vastrādyadvāri niḥsṛtam .
pīḍyamānaṃ karaiḥ śubhraistaistu pallavakomalaiḥ .. 21.76 ..
6.3.d:
नानावर्णारुणं शुभ्रं वस्त्राद्यद्वारि निःसृतम् .
पीड्यमानं करैः शुभ्रैस्तैस्तु पल्लवकोमलैः .. 21.76 ..
6.3.m: variegated in color, reddish, and bright was the water that flowed from the garment, / being wrung out by their radiant hands, soft as tender sprouts.

6.3.s:
kapilaṃ jalamiśraistu tasmādeṣā saridvarā .
kapilā cocyate tajjñaiḥ purāṇārthaviśāradaiḥ .. 21.77 ..
6.3.d:
कपिलं जलमिश्रैस्तु तस्मादेषा सरिद्वरा .
कपिला चोच्यते तज्ज्ञैः पुराणार्थविशारदैः .. 21.77 ..
6.3.m: From the water mixed with tawny coloring, therefore, this best of rivers / is called Kapilā by those who know it, skilled in the meaning of the Purāṇas.

6.3.s:
eṣā vai vastrasambhūtā narmadātoyasambhavā .
mahāpuṇyatamā jñeyā kapilā sariduttamā .. 21.78 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe narmadāmāhātmye kapilāsaritsambhavavarṇanaṃ nāmaikaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ ..
6.3.d:
एषा वै वस्त्रसम्भूता नर्मदातोयसम्भवा .
महापुण्यतमा ज्ञेया कपिला सरिदुत्तमा .. 21.78 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे नर्मदामाहात्म्ये कपिलासरित्सम्भववर्णनं नामैकविंशोऽध्यायः ..
6.3.m:
She, born from the garment and originating from the waters of Narmadā, / should be known as most highly meritorious, the excellent river Kapilā.
Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, named 'Description of the Origin of the River Kapilā,' in the Narmadāmāhātmya of the Revākhaṇḍa, in the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa containing eighty-one thousand verses.

6.3.s:
śrī mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi sā viśalyā hyabhūdyathā .
āścaryabhūtā lokasya sarvapāpakṣayaṃkarī .. 22.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्री मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि सा विशल्या ह्यभूद्यथा .
आश्चर्यभूता लोकस्य सर्वपापक्षयंकरी .. 22.1 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Hereafter I shall explain how she became Viśalyā ("dart-remover"), / a marvel to the world, destroying all sins.

6.3.s:
brahmaṇo mānasaḥ putro mukhyo hyagnirajāyata .
mukhyo vahniritiprokta ṛṣiḥ paramadhārmikaḥ .. 22.2 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रह्मणो मानसः पुत्रो मुख्यो ह्यग्निरजायत .
मुख्यो वह्निरितिप्रोक्त ऋषिः परमधार्मिकः .. 22.2 ..
6.3.m: A mind-born son of Brahmā, the foremost Agni, was born; / he is declared the chief fire, an exceedingly righteous seer.

6.3.s:
tasya svāhābhavatpatnī smṛtā dākṣāyaṇī tu sā .
tasyāṃ mukhyā mahārāja trayaḥ putrāstadā'bhavan .. 22.3 ..
6.3.d:
तस्य स्वाहाभवत्पत्नी स्मृता दाक्षायणी तु सा .
तस्यां मुख्या महाराज त्रयः पुत्रास्तदाऽभवन् .. 22.3 ..
6.3.m: His wife was Svāhā, known as Dākṣāyaṇī; / by her, O great king, three chief sons were then born:

6.3.s:
agnirāhavanīyastu dakṣiṇāgnistathaiva ca .
gārhapatyastṛtīyastu trailokyaṃ yaiśca dhāryate .. 22.4 ..
6.3.d:
अग्निराहवनीयस्तु दक्षिणाग्निस्तथैव च .
गार्हपत्यस्तृतीयस्तु त्रैलोक्यं यैश्च धार्यते .. 22.4 ..
6.3.m: the Āhavanīya fire, and likewise the Dakṣiṇāgni, / and thirdly the Gārhapatya, by whom the three worlds are upheld.

6.3.s:
tathā vai gārhapatyo'gnirjajñe putradvayaṃ śubham .
padmakaḥ śaṅkunāmā ca tāvubhāvagnisattamau .. 22.5 ..
6.3.d:
तथा वै गार्हपत्योऽग्निर्जज्ञे पुत्रद्वयं शुभम् .
पद्मकः शङ्कुनामा च तावुभावग्निसत्तमौ .. 22.5 ..
6.3.m: From that Gārhapatya fire were born two auspicious sons, / Padmaka and Śaṅku by name, both the best of fires.

6.3.s:
vasannagnirnadītīre samāśritya mahattapaḥ .
rudramārādhayāmāsa jitātmā susamāhitaḥ .. 22.6 ..
6.3.d:
वसन्नग्निर्नदीतीरे समाश्रित्य महत्तपः .
रुद्रमाराधयामास जितात्मा सुसमाहितः .. 22.6 ..
6.3.m: Living on the bank of the river, undertaking great austerity, / Agni worshiped Rudra, self-controlled and highly concentrated.

6.3.s:
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi cacāra vipulaṃ tapaḥ .
tamuvāca mahādevaḥ prasanno vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ .. 22.7 ..
6.3.d:
दशवर्षसहस्राणि चचार विपुलं तपः .
तमुवाच महादेवः प्रसन्नो वृषभध्वजः .. 22.7 ..
6.3.m: For ten thousand years he practiced vast austerity. / To him Mahādeva, whose banner bears the bull, pleased, said:

6.3.s:
bhobho brūhi mahābhāga yatte manasi vartate .
dātā hyahamasaṃdeho yadyapi syātsudurlabham .. 22.8 ..
6.3.d:
भोभो ब्रूहि महाभाग यत्ते मनसि वर्तते .
दाता ह्यहमसंदेहो यद्यपि स्यात्सुदुर्लभम् .. 22.8 ..
6.3.m: "O fortunate one, speak whatever is in your mind! / I am the giver, without doubt, even if it be very difficult to obtain."

6.3.s:
agniruvāca -
narmadeyaṃ mahābhāgā sarito yāśca ṣoḍaśa .
bhavantu mama patnyastāstvatprasādānmaheśvara .. 22.9 ..
6.3.d:
अग्निरुवाच -
नर्मदेयं महाभागा सरितो याश्च षोडश .
भवन्तु मम पत्न्यस्तास्त्वत्प्रसादान्महेश्वर .. 22.9 ..
6.3.m: Agni said: / "May this blessed Narmadā and the sixteen rivers / become my wives by your grace, O Maheśvara!

6.3.s:
tāsu vai cintitān putrānagryānutpādayāmyaham .
eṣa eva varo deva dīyatāṃ me maheśvara .. 22.10 ..
6.3.d:
तासु वै चिन्तितान् पुत्रानग्र्यानुत्पादयाम्यहम् .
एष एव वरो देव दीयतां मे महेश्वर .. 22.10 ..
6.3.m: In them may I beget the foremost sons as desired. / Let this very boon be granted to me, O god, O Maheśvara!"

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
etāstu dhiṣṇināmnyo vai bhaviṣyanti saridvarāḥ .
patnyastava viśālākṣyo vede khyātā na saṃśayaḥ .. 22.11 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
एतास्तु धिष्णिनाम्न्यो वै भविष्यन्ति सरिद्वराः .
पत्न्यस्तव विशालाक्ष्यो वेदे ख्याता न संशयः .. 22.11 ..
6.3.m: Īśvara said: / "These excellent, large-eyed rivers shall indeed be named Dhiṣṇīs; / they will be your wives, celebrated in the Veda, without doubt.

6.3.s:
tāsāṃ putrā bhaviṣyanti hyagnayo ye'dhvare smṛtāḥ .
dhiṣṇyānāma suvikhyātā yāvadābhūtasamplavam .. 22.12 ..
6.3.d:
तासां पुत्रा भविष्यन्ति ह्यग्नयो येऽध्वरे स्मृताः .
धिष्ण्यानाम सुविख्याता यावदाभूतसम्प्लवम् .. 22.12 ..
6.3.m: Their sons shall be the fires that are remembered in the sacrificial rite, / highly renowned under the name of Dhiṣṇyas until the dissolution of all beings."

6.3.s:
evamuktvā mahādevastatraivāntaradhīyata .
narmadā ca saricchreṣṭhā tasya bhāryā babhūva ha .. 22.13 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्त्वा महादेवस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत .
नर्मदा च सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा तस्य भार्या बभूव ह .. 22.13 ..
6.3.m: Having spoken thus, Mahādeva disappeared right there, / and the Narmadā, best of rivers, became his wife.

6.3.s:
kāverī kṛṣṇaveṇī ca revā ca yamunā tathā .
godāvarī vitastā ca candrabhāgā irāvatī .. 22.14 ..
6.3.d:
कावेरी कृष्णवेणी च रेवा च यमुना तथा .
गोदावरी वितस्ता च चन्द्रभागा इरावती .. 22.14 ..
6.3.m: The Kāverī, Kṛṣṇaveṇī, Revā, and Yamunā, / the Godāvarī, Vitastā, Candrabhāgā, and Irāvatī,

6.3.s:
vipāśā kauśikī caiva sarayūḥ śatarudrikā .
śiprā sarasvatī caiva hrādinī pāvanī tathā .. 22.15 ..
6.3.d:
विपाशा कौशिकी चैव सरयूः शतरुद्रिका .
शिप्रा सरस्वती चैव ह्रादिनी पावनी तथा .. 22.15 ..
6.3.m: the Vipāśā, Kauśikī, Sarayū, and Śatarudrikā, / the Śiprā, Sarasvatī, Hrādinī, and Pāvanī—

6.3.s:
etāḥ ṣoḍaśā nadyo vai bhāryārthaṃ saṃvyavasthitāḥ .
tadātmānaṃ vibhajyāśu dhiṣṇīṣu sa mahādyutiḥ .. 22.16 ..
6.3.d:
एताः षोडशा नद्यो वै भार्यार्थं संव्यवस्थिताः .
तदात्मानं विभज्याशु धिष्णीषु स महाद्युतिः .. 22.16 ..
6.3.m: these sixteen rivers were appointed to be his wives. / Then, having divided himself at once into the Dhiṣṇīs, that fire of great splendor—

6.3.s:
vyabhicārāttu bharturvai narmadādyāsu dhiṣṇiṣu .
utpannāḥ śucayaḥ putrāḥ sarve te dhiṣṇyapāḥ smṛtāḥ .. 22.17 ..
6.3.d:
व्यभिचारात्तु भर्तुर्वै नर्मदाद्यासु धिष्णिषु .
उत्पन्नाः शुचयः पुत्राः सर्वे ते धिष्ण्यपाः स्मृताः .. 22.17 ..
6.3.m: by the dispersal of the husband into the Dhiṣṇīs, beginning with Narmadā, / pure sons were born; they are all remembered as the guardians of the Dhiṣṇyas.

6.3.s:
tasyāśca narmadāyāstu dhiṣṇīndro nāma viśrutaḥ .
babhūva putro balavānrūpeṇāpratimo nṛpa .. 22.18 ..
6.3.d:
तस्याश्च नर्मदायास्तु धिष्णीन्द्रो नाम विश्रुतः .
बभूव पुत्रो बलवान्रूपेणाप्रतिमो नृप .. 22.18 ..
6.3.m: And to that Narmadā was born a son renowned by the name Dhiṣṇīndra, / mighty and peerless in beauty, O king.

6.3.s:
tato devāsuraṃ yuddhamabhavallomaharṣaṇam .
mayatārakamityevaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam .. 22.19 ..
6.3.d:
ततो देवासुरं युद्धमभवल्लोमहर्षणम् .
मयतारकमित्येवं त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम् .. 22.19 ..
6.3.m: Then there occurred a hair-raising battle between the gods and asuras, / known in the three worlds as the conflict with Maya and Tāraka.

6.3.s:
tatra daityairmahāghorairmayatārapurogamaiḥ .
tāḍitāste surāstrastā viṣṇuṃ vai śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ .. 22.20 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र दैत्यैर्महाघोरैर्मयतारपुरोगमैः .
ताडितास्ते सुरास्त्रस्ता विष्णुं वै शरणं ययुः .. 22.20 ..
6.3.m: There, battered by the most terrible daityas led by Maya and Tāra, / the frightened gods fled to Viṣṇu for refuge:

6.3.s:
trāyasva no hṛṣīkeśā ghorādasmānmahābhayāt .
daityānsarvānsaṃharasva mayatārapurogamān .. 22.21 ..
6.3.d:
त्रायस्व नो हृषीकेशा घोरादस्मान्महाभयात् .
दैत्यान्सर्वान्संहरस्व मयतारपुरोगमान् .. 22.21 ..
6.3.m: "Protect us, O Hṛṣīkeśa, from this terrible, great danger! / Destroy all the daityas led by Maya and Tāra!"

6.3.s:
evamuktaḥ sa bhagavāndiśo daśa vyalokayat .
tato bhagavatā dṛṣṭau raṇe pāvakamārutau .. 22.22 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्तः स भगवान्दिशो दश व्यलोकयत् .
ततो भगवता दृष्टौ रणे पावकमारुतौ .. 22.22 ..
6.3.m: Thus addressed, the Lord looked across the ten directions; / then the Lord saw Fire and Wind in battle.

6.3.s:
āhūtau viṣṇunā tau tu sakāśaṃ jagmatuḥ kṣaṇāt .
sthitau tau praṇatau cāgre devadevasya dhīmataḥ .. 22.23 ..
6.3.d:
आहूतौ विष्णुना तौ तु सकाशं जग्मतुः क्षणात् .
स्थितौ तौ प्रणतौ चाग्रे देवदेवस्य धीमतः .. 22.23 ..
6.3.m: Summoned by Viṣṇu, the two went to his presence in an instant, / and bowed down, standing before the wise god of gods.

6.3.s:
tato dhiṣṇiḥ pāvakendro devenokto mahātmanā .
nirdahemānmahāghorānnārmadeya mahāsurān .. 22.24 ..
6.3.d:
ततो धिष्णिः पावकेन्द्रो देवेनोक्तो महात्मना .
निर्दहेमान्महाघोरान्नार्मदेय महासुरान् .. 22.24 ..
6.3.m: Then Dhiṣṇi, the chief of fire, was addressed by the great-souled god: / "Burn down these most terrible great asuras, O son of Narmadā!"

6.3.s:
athaivamuktau tau devau raṇe pāvakamārutau .
daityān dadahatuḥ sarvānmayatārapurogamān .. 22.25 ..
6.3.d:
अथैवमुक्तौ तौ देवौ रणे पावकमारुतौ .
दैत्यान् ददहतुः सर्वान्मयतारपुरोगमान् .. 22.25 ..
6.3.m: Thus addressed, those two gods, Fire and Wind, in battle / burnt all the daityas led by Maya and Tāra.

6.3.s:
dahyamānāstu te sarve śastrairagniṃ tvaveṣṭayan .
divyairagnyarkasaṅkāśaiḥ śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ .. 22.26 ..
6.3.d:
दह्यमानास्तु ते सर्वे शस्त्रैरग्निं त्ववेष्टयन् .
दिव्यैरग्न्यर्कसङ्काशैः शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः .. 22.26 ..
6.3.m: Being scorched, all of them surrounded Fire with weapons— / with celestial weapons resembling fire and the sun, by hundreds and by thousands.

6.3.s:
tāṃścāgniḥ śastranikarairnirdadāha mahāsurān .
jvālāmālākulaṃ sarvaṃ vāyunā nirmitaṃ tadā .. 22.27 ..
6.3.d:
तांश्चाग्निः शस्त्रनिकरैर्निर्ददाह महासुरान् .
ज्वालामालाकुलं सर्वं वायुना निर्मितं तदा .. 22.27 ..
6.3.m: And Fire burned those great asuras along with their multitudes of weapons; / everything was then filled with garlands of flames created by Wind.

6.3.s:
dahyamānāstato daityā agnijvālāsamāvṛtāḥ .
praviśya pātālatalaṃ jale līnāḥ sahasraśaḥ .. 22.28 ..
6.3.d:
दह्यमानास्ततो दैत्या अग्निज्वालासमावृताः .
प्रविश्य पातालतलं जले लीनाः सहस्रशः .. 22.28 ..
6.3.m: Being scorched and enveloped by the flames of fire, the daityas / entered the realm of Pātāla and hid in the water by thousands.

6.3.s:
tataḥ kumāramagniṃ tu narmadāputramavyayam .
pūjayitvā surāḥ sarve jagmuste tridaśālayam .. 22.29 ..
6.3.d:
ततः कुमारमग्निं तु नर्मदापुत्रमव्ययम् .
पूजयित्वा सुराः सर्वे जग्मुस्ते त्रिदशालयम् .. 22.29 ..
6.3.m: Then all the gods, having worshiped the boy Fire, the imperishable son of Narmadā, / went to the abode of the thirty gods.

6.3.s:
saśalyastu mahātejā revāputro vṛto'gnibhiḥ .
narmadāmāgataḥ kṣipraṃ mātaraṃ draṣṭumutsukaḥ .. 22.30 ..
6.3.d:
सशल्यस्तु महातेजा रेवापुत्रो वृतोऽग्निभिः .
नर्मदामागतः क्षिप्रं मातरं द्रष्टुमुत्सुकः .. 22.30 ..
6.3.m: Pierced by darts, that son of Revā of great splendor, surrounded by fires, / quickly went to the Narmadā, eager to see his mother.

6.3.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā putramāyāntaṃ śastraugheṇa parikṣatam .
narmadā puṇyasalilā abhyutthāya suvismitā .. 22.31 ..
6.3.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा पुत्रमायान्तं शस्त्रौघेण परिक्षतम् .
नर्मदा पुण्यसलिला अभ्युत्थाय सुविस्मिता .. 22.31 ..
6.3.m: Seeing her son arriving, wounded by a barrage of weapons, / the Narmadā of holy water rose up in utter astonishment

6.3.s:
paryaṣvajata bāhubhyāṃ prasnavāpīḍitastanī .
saśalyaṃ putramādāya kāpilaṃ hradamāviśat .. 22.32 ..
6.3.d:
पर्यष्वजत बाहुभ्यां प्रस्नवापीडितस्तनी .
सशल्यं पुत्रमादाय कापिलं ह्रदमाविशत् .. 22.32 ..
6.3.m: and embraced him with both arms, her breasts dripping with milk; / taking her dart-pierced son, she entered the pool of the Kapilā.

6.3.s:
praviṣṭamātre tu hrade kāpile pāpanāśini .
saśalyaṃ taṃ viśalyaṃ ca kṣaṇātkṛtavatī tadā .. 22.33 ..
6.3.d:
प्रविष्टमात्रे तु ह्रदे कापिले पापनाशिनि .
सशल्यं तं विशल्यं च क्षणात्कृतवती तदा .. 22.33 ..
6.3.m: The moment he entered that sin-destroying pool of the Kapilā, / she instantly made him who was pierced by darts free of all darts.

6.3.s:
sa viśalyo'bhavadyasmātprāpya tasyāḥ śivaṃ jalam .
kapilā nāmatastena viśalyā cocyate budhaiḥ .. 22.34 ..
6.3.d:
स विशल्योऽभवद्यस्मात्प्राप्य तस्याः शिवं जलम् .
कपिला नामतस्तेन विशल्या चोच्यते बुधैः .. 22.34 ..
6.3.m: Because he became free from darts (viśalya) upon reaching her auspicious water, / therefore Kapilā is also called Viśalyā by the wise.

6.3.s:
anye'pi tatra ye snātāḥ śucayastu samāhitāḥ .
pāpaśalyaiḥ pramucyante mṛtā yānti surālayam .. 22.35 ..
6.3.d:
अन्येऽपि तत्र ये स्नाताः शुचयस्तु समाहिताः .
पापशल्यैः प्रमुच्यन्ते मृता यान्ति सुरालयम् .. 22.35 ..
6.3.m: Others too who bathe there, purified and concentrated in mind, / are freed from the darts of sin, and upon death go to the abode of the gods.

6.3.s:
etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭo'haṃ purā tvayā .
utpattikāraṇaṃ tāta viśalyāyā nareśvara .. 22.36 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe narmadāmāhātmye viśalyāsambhavo nāma dvāviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 23
6.3.d:
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं यत्पृष्टोऽहं पुरा त्वया .
उत्पत्तिकारणं तात विशल्याया नरेश्वर .. 22.36 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे नर्मदामाहात्म्ये विशल्यासम्भवो नाम द्वाविंशोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 23
6.3.m:
All this has been related to you, which I was asked about by you formerly, / the cause of the origin of Viśalyā, O dear one, O lord of men! .. 22.36 ..
.. Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, titled 'The Origin of Viśalyā', in the Narmadāmāhātmya of the Revākhaṇḍa, in the fifth [section], the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. ..
Chapter 23

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tatraiva saṅgame rājanbhaktyā paramayā nṛpa .
prāṇāṃstyajanti ye martyāste yānti paramāṃ gatim .. 23.1 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
तत्रैव सङ्गमे राजन्भक्त्या परमया नृप .
प्राणांस्त्यजन्ति ये मर्त्यास्ते यान्ति परमां गतिम् .. 23.1 ..
6.3.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Right at that confluence, O king, with supreme devotion, / mortals who abandon their life-breaths go to the supreme state.

6.3.s:
saṃnyastasarvasaṃkalpo yastu prāṇānparityajet .
amareśvaramāsādya sa svarge niyataṃ vaset .. 23.2 ..
6.3.d:
संन्यस्तसर्वसंकल्पो यस्तु प्राणान्परित्यजेत् .
अमरेश्वरमासाद्य स स्वर्गे नियतं वसेत् .. 23.2 ..
6.3.m: One who renounces all desires and abandons his life-breaths, / having reached Amareśvara, shall dwell forever in heaven.

6.3.s:
śailendraṃ yaḥ samāsādya ātmānaṃ muñcate naraḥ .
vimānenārkavarṇena sa gacchedamarāvatīm .. 23.3 ..
6.3.d:
शैलेन्द्रं यः समासाद्य आत्मानं मुञ्चते नरः .
विमानेनार्कवर्णेन स गच्छेदमरावतीम् .. 23.3 ..
6.3.m: A man who approaches the lord of mountains and releases himself / goes to Amarāvatī in an aerial chariot resembling the sun.

6.3.s:
naraṃ patantamālokya nagādamarakaṇṭakāt .
bruvantyapsarasaḥ sarvā mama bhartā bhavediti .. 23.4 ..
6.3.d:
नरं पतन्तमालोक्य नगादमरकण्टकात् .
ब्रुवन्त्यप्सरसः सर्वा मम भर्ता भवेदिति .. 23.4 ..
6.3.m: Beholding a man falling from Mount Amarakaṇṭaka, / all the apsarases say, "May he become my husband!"

6.3.s:
samaṃ jalaṃ dharmavido vadanti sārasvataṃ gāṅgamiti prabuddhāḥ .
tasyopariṣṭātpravadanti tajjñā revājalaṃ nātra vicāraṇāsti .. 23.5 ..
6.3.d:
समं जलं धर्मविदो वदन्ति सारस्वतं गाङ्गमिति प्रबुद्धाः .
तस्योपरिष्टात्प्रवदन्ति तज्ज्ञा रेवाजलं नात्र विचारणास्ति .. 23.5 ..
6.3.m: Those who know dharma say that the water belonging to Sarasvatī and the water of Gaṅgā are equal, so say the enlightened; / those who know proclaim that the water of Revā is superior to that—there is no doubt about this.

6.3.s:
anekavidyādharakinnarādyairadhyāsitaṃ puṇyatamādhivāsaiḥ .
revājalaṃ dhārayato hi mūrdhnā sthānaṃ surendrādhipateḥ samīpe .. 23.6 ..
6.3.d:
अनेकविद्याधरकिन्नराद्यैरध्यासितं पुण्यतमाधिवासैः .
रेवाजलं धारयतो हि मूर्ध्ना स्थानं सुरेन्द्राधिपतेः समीपे .. 23.6 ..
6.3.m: Inhabited by numerous vidyādharas, kinnaras, and others with most sacred abodes, / for one who carries the water of Revā on his head, his place is near the sovereign of the gods.

6.3.s:
narmadā sarvadā sevyā bahunoktena kiṃ nṛpa .
yadīcchenna punardraṣṭuṃ ghoraṃ saṃsārasāgaram .. 23.7 ..
6.3.d:
नर्मदा सर्वदा सेव्या बहुनोक्तेन किं नृप .
यदीच्छेन्न पुनर्द्रष्टुं घोरं संसारसागरम् .. 23.7 ..
6.3.m: The Narmadā is always to be resorted to; what is the use of speaking much, O king, / if one wishes not to see again the terrible ocean of cyclic existence?

6.3.s:
trayāṇāmapi lokānāṃ mahatī pāvanī smṛtā .
yatra tatra mṛtasyāpi dhruvaṃ gāṇeśvarī gatiḥ .. 23.8 ..
6.3.d:
त्रयाणामपि लोकानां महती पावनी स्मृता .
यत्र तत्र मृतस्यापि ध्रुवं गाणेश्वरी गतिः .. 23.8 ..
6.3.m: She is remembered as the great purifier of all three worlds. / Wherever one dies [on her banks], a state among the attendants of Śiva is certain.

6.3.s:
anekayajñāyatanairvṛtāṅgī na hyatra kiṃcidyadatīrthamasti .
tasyāstu tīre bhavatā yaduktaṃ tapasvino vāpyatapasvino vā .. 23.9 ..
6.3.d:
अनेकयज्ञायतनैर्वृताङ्गी न ह्यत्र किंचिद्यदतीर्थमस्ति .
तस्यास्तु तीरे भवता यदुक्तं तपस्विनो वाप्यतपस्विनो वा .. 23.9 ..
6.3.m: Her body is surrounded by numerous sacrificial sanctuaries; indeed, there is nothing here that is not a sacred ford. / As for what was said by you regarding her bank, whether ascetics or non-ascetics,

6.3.s: mriyanti ye pāpakṛto manuṣyāste svargamāyānti yathā'marendrāḥ .. 23.10 ..
6.3.d: म्रियन्ति ये पापकृतो मनुष्यास्ते स्वर्गमायान्ति यथाऽमरेन्द्राः .. 23.10 ..
6.3.m: men who die, even if they have committed sins, go to heaven like the lords of the immortals.

6.3.s:
evaṃ tu kapilā caiva viśalyā rājasattama .
īśvareṇa purā sṛṣṭā lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā .. 23.11 ..
6.3.d:
एवं तु कपिला चैव विशल्या राजसत्तम .
ईश्वरेण पुरा सृष्टा लोकानां हितकाम्यया .. 23.11 ..
6.3.m: In this way both the Kapilā and the Viśalyā, O best of kings, / were created in ancient times by Īśvara out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds.

6.3.s:
tatra snātvā naro rājansopavāso jitendriyaḥ .
aśvamedhasya mahato'saṃśayaṃ phalamāpnuyāt .. 23.12 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र स्नात्वा नरो राजन्सोपवासो जितेन्द्रियः .
अश्वमेधस्य महतोऽसंशयं फलमाप्नुयात् .. 23.12 ..
6.3.m: Having bathed there, O king, fasting and having restrained his senses, / a man without doubt obtains the fruit of the great horse sacrifice.

6.3.s:
anāśakaṃ ca yaḥ kuryāttasmiṃstīrthe narādhipa .
sarvapāpavinirmukto yāti vai śivamandiram .. 23.13 ..
6.3.d:
अनाशकं च यः कुर्यात्तस्मिंस्तीर्थे नराधिप .
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो याति वै शिवमन्दिरम् .. 23.13 ..
6.3.m: And whoever undertakes a fast unto death at that sacred ford, O ruler of men, / freed from all sins, goes indeed to Śiva's abode.

6.3.s:
pṛthivyāṃ sāgarāntāyāṃ snānadānena yatphalam .
viśalyāsaṅgame snātvā sakṛttatphalamaśnute .. 23.14 ..
6.3.d:
पृथिव्यां सागरान्तायां स्नानदानेन यत्फलम् .
विशल्यासङ्गमे स्नात्वा सकृत्तत्फलमश्नुते .. 23.14 ..
6.3.m: Whatever fruit is attained by bathing and giving gifts on the earth up to the ocean, / one obtains that fruit merely by bathing once at the confluence of the Viśalyā.

6.3.s:
evaṃ puṇyā pavitrā ca kathitā tava bhūpate .
bhūyo māṃ pṛcchasi ca yattaccaiva kathayāmyaham .. 23.15 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe viśalyāsaṅgamamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma trayoviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 24
6.3.d:
एवं पुण्या पवित्रा च कथिता तव भूपते .
भूयो मां पृच्छसि च यत्तच्चैव कथयाम्यहम् .. 23.15 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे विशल्यासङ्गममाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम त्रयोविंशोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 24
6.3.m:
Thus has this sacred and purifying [stream] been told to you, O lord of the earth. / Whatever you ask me further, that too I shall relate.
Thus ends the twenty-third chapter, entitled 'Description of the Māhātmya of the Viśalyā Confluence', in the Revākhaṇḍa of the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, the fifth [part] of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].
Chapter 24

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
saṅgamaḥ karanarmadayoḥ pure māndhātṛsaṃjñite .
gatvā snātvā tapayitvā pitḥnviṣṇupuraṃ nayet .. 24.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
सङ्गमः करनर्मदयोः पुरे मान्धातृसंज्ञिते .
गत्वा स्नात्वा तपयित्वा पित्ःन्विष्णुपुरं नयेत् .. 24.1 ..
6.3.m: Glorious Mārkaṇḍeya said: / The confluence of the Kara and the Narmadā is in the city named Māndhātṛ. / Going there, bathing, and gratifying the ancestors, one can lead them to the realm of Viṣṇu.

6.3.s:
mardayitvā karau pūrvaṃ viṣṇurdaityajighāṃsayā .
cakraṃ jagrāha tatraiva svedājjātā saridvarā .. 24.2 ..
6.3.d:
मर्दयित्वा करौ पूर्वं विष्णुर्दैत्यजिघांसया .
चक्रं जग्राह तत्रैव स्वेदाज्जाता सरिद्वरा .. 24.2 ..
6.3.m: Formerly, Viṣṇu, wishing to slay the Daityas, rubbed his hands / and took up his discus right there; from his sweat was born this best of rivers.

6.3.s:
saṃgatā revayā tatra snātvā pāpaiḥ pramucyate .. 24.3 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe narmadāmāhātmye karanarmadāsaṅgamamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma caturviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 25
6.3.d:
संगता रेवया तत्र स्नात्वा पापैः प्रमुच्यते .. 24.3 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे नर्मदामाहात्म्ये करनर्मदासङ्गममाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम चतुर्विंशोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 25
6.3.m:
Having bathed there where she joins the Revā, one is freed from sins.
Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Māhātmya of the Confluence of the Kara and Narmadā', in the Narmadāmāhātmya of the Revākhaṇḍa of the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, the fifth [part] of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].
Chapter 25

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
oṃkārātpūrvabhāge vai saṅgamo lokaviśrutaḥ .
revayā saṃgatā yatra nīlagaṅgā nṛpottama .. 25.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ओंकारात्पूर्वभागे वै सङ्गमो लोकविश्रुतः .
रेवया संगता यत्र नीलगङ्गा नृपोत्तम .. 25.1 ..
6.3.m: Glorious Mārkaṇḍeya said: / To the east of Oṃkāra is a confluence renowned throughout the world, / where the Nīlagaṅgā joins the Revā, O best of kings.

6.3.s:
tatra snātvā japitvā ca ko'rtho'labhyo bhavedbhuvi .
ṣaṣṭirvarṣasahasrāṇi nīlakaṇṭhapure vaset .. 25.2 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र स्नात्वा जपित्वा च कोऽर्थोऽलभ्यो भवेद्भुवि .
षष्टिर्वर्षसहस्राणि नीलकण्ठपुरे वसेत् .. 25.2 ..
6.3.m: Having bathed and chanted there, what goal on earth could remain unattainable? / One will dwell in the city of Nīlakaṇṭha for sixty thousand years.

6.3.s:
tarpayitvā pitṝñśrāddhe tilamiśrairjalairapi .
uddharedātmanā sārdhaṃ puruṣānekaviṃśatim .. 25.3 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe narmadāmāhātmye nīlagaṅgāyāḥ saṅgamamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma pañcaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ ..
6.3.d:
तर्पयित्वा पितॄञ्श्राद्धे तिलमिश्रैर्जलैरपि .
उद्धरेदात्मना सार्धं पुरुषानेकविंशतिम् .. 25.3 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे नर्मदामाहात्म्ये नीलगङ्गायाः सङ्गममाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम पञ्चविंशोऽध्यायः ..
6.3.m:
Having gratified the ancestors in a śrāddha with waters mixed with sesame seeds, / one elevates twenty-one generations of men along with oneself.
Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Māhātmya of the Confluence of the Nīlagaṅgā', in the Narmadāmāhātmya of the Revākhaṇḍa of the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, the fifth [part] of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
jāleśvare'pi yatproktaṃ tvayā pūrvaṃ dvijottama .
tatkathaṃ tu bhavetpuṇyamṛṣisiddhaniṣevitam .. 26.1 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
जालेश्वरेऽपि यत्प्रोक्तं त्वया पूर्वं द्विजोत्तम .
तत्कथं तु भवेत्पुण्यमृषिसिद्धनिषेवितम् .. 26.1 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / Regarding Jāleśvara as well, which was mentioned by you before, O best of twice-born, / how can it be holy and attended by seers and perfected beings? .. 26.1 ..

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
jāleśvarātparaṃ tīrthaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati .
tasyotpattiṃ kathayataḥ śṛṇu tvaṃ pāṇḍunandana .. 26.2 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
जालेश्वरात्परं तीर्थं न भूतं न भविष्यति .
तस्योत्पत्तिं कथयतः शृणु त्वं पाण्डुनन्दन .. 26.2 ..
6.3.m: The glorious Mārkaṇḍeya said: / There has never been, nor will there ever be, a sacred ford superior to Jāleśvara; / listen to me as I narrate its origin, O son of Pāṇḍu! .. 26.2 ..

6.3.s:
purā ṛṣigaṇāḥ sarve sendrāścaiva marudgaṇāḥ .
tāpitā asuraiḥ sarvaiḥ kṣayaṃ nītā hyanekaśaḥ .. 26.3 ..
6.3.d:
पुरा ऋषिगणाः सर्वे सेन्द्राश्चैव मरुद्गणाः .
तापिता असुरैः सर्वैः क्षयं नीता ह्यनेकशः .. 26.3 ..
6.3.m: In ancient times, all the hosts of seers, and the hosts of Maruts along with Indra, / being tormented by all the Asuras, were repeatedly brought to destruction .. 26.3 ..

6.3.s:
bāṇāsuraprabhṛtibhirjambhaśumbhapurogamaiḥ .
vadhyamānā hyanekaiśca brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ .. 26.4 ..
6.3.d:
बाणासुरप्रभृतिभिर्जम्भशुम्भपुरोगमैः .
वध्यमाना ह्यनेकैश्च ब्रह्माणं शरणं गताः .. 26.4 ..
6.3.m: by those headed by Bāṇāsura, led by Jambha and Śumbha. / Being slain in many ways, they went to Brahmā for refuge .. 26.4 ..

6.3.s:
vimānaiḥ parvatākārairhayaiścaiva gajopamaiḥ .
syandanairnagarākāraiḥ siṃhaśārdūlayojitaiḥ .. 26.5 ..
6.3.d:
विमानैः पर्वताकारैर्हयैश्चैव गजोपमैः .
स्यन्दनैर्नगराकारैः सिंहशार्दूलयोजितैः .. 26.5 ..
6.3.m: with aerial chariots resembling mountains, with horses resembling elephants, / with chariots resembling cities, yoked with lions and tigers; .. 26.5 ..

6.3.s:
kacchapairmakaraiścānye jagmuranye padātayaḥ .
prāpya te paramaṃ sthānamaśakyaṃ yadadhārmikaiḥ .. 26.6 ..
6.3.d:
कच्छपैर्मकरैश्चान्ये जग्मुरन्ये पदातयः .
प्राप्य ते परमं स्थानमशक्यं यदधार्मिकैः .. 26.6 ..
6.3.m: others went on turtles and crocodiles, and others on foot. / Having reached that supreme place, which cannot be attained by the unrighteous, .. 26.6 ..

6.3.s:
dṛṣṭvā padmodbhavaṃ devaṃ sarvalokasya śaṅkaram .
te sarve tatra gatvā tu stutiṃ cakruḥ samāhitāḥ .. 26.7 ..
6.3.d:
दृष्ट्वा पद्मोद्भवं देवं सर्वलोकस्य शङ्करम् .
ते सर्वे तत्र गत्वा तु स्तुतिं चक्रुः समाहिताः .. 26.7 ..
6.3.m: having seen the lotus-born god, the benefactor of all the world, / they all went there and praised [him] with concentrated minds. .. 26.7 ..

6.3.s:
devā ūcuḥ .
jayāmeya jayābheda jaya sambhūtikāraka .
padmayone suraśreṣṭha tvāṃ vayaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ .. 26.8 ..
6.3.d:
देवा ऊचुः .
जयामेय जयाभेद जय सम्भूतिकारक .
पद्मयोने सुरश्रेष्ठ त्वां वयं शरणं गताः .. 26.8 ..
6.3.m: The gods said: / 'Victory to the immeasurable! Victory to the indivisible! Victory to the cause of creation! / O lotus-born one, O best among the gods, we have come to you for refuge.' .. 26.8 ..

6.3.s:
tacchrutvā tu vaco devo devānāṃ bhāvitātmanām .
meghagambhīrayā vācā pratyuvāca pitāmahaḥ .. 26.9 ..
6.3.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचो देवो देवानां भावितात्मनाम् .
मेघगम्भीरया वाचा प्रत्युवाच पितामहः .. 26.9 ..
6.3.m: Having heard those words of the gods whose minds were purified, / the god, the Grandfather, replied in a voice deep as thunder: .. 26.9 ..

6.3.s:
kiṃ vo hyāgamanaṃ devāḥ sarveṣāṃ ca vivarṇatā .
kenāvamānitāḥ sarve śīghraṃ kathayatāmarāḥ .. 26.10 ..
6.3.d:
किं वो ह्यागमनं देवाः सर्वेषां च विवर्णता .
केनावमानिताः सर्वे शीघ्रं कथयतामराः .. 26.10 ..
6.3.m: 'What is the reason for your arrival, O gods, and the pallor of all of you? / By whom have you all been insulted? Speak quickly, O immortals!' .. 26.10 ..

6.3.s:
devā ūcuḥ .
bāṇo nāma mahāvīryo dānavo baladarpitaḥ .
tenāsmākaṃ hṛtaṃ sarvaṃ dhanaratnairviyojitāḥ .. 26.11 ..
6.3.d:
देवा ऊचुः .
बाणो नाम महावीर्यो दानवो बलदर्पितः .
तेनास्माकं हृतं सर्वं धनरत्नैर्वियोजिताः .. 26.11 ..
6.3.m: The gods said: / 'There is a Dānava named Bāṇa of great valor, arrogant with might. / By him all that is ours has been taken, and we have been deprived of wealth and jewels.' .. 26.11 ..

6.3.s:
devānāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ .
cintayāmāsa deveśastasya nāśāya yā kriyā .. 26.12 ..
6.3.d:
देवानां वचनं श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः .
चिन्तयामास देवेशस्तस्य नाशाय या क्रिया .. 26.12 ..
6.3.m: Having heard the words of the gods, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, / the lord of the gods, pondered what action [should be taken] for his destruction: .. 26.12 ..

6.3.s:
avadhyo dānavaḥ pāpaḥ sarveṣāṃ vai divaukasām .
muktvā tu śaṅkaraṃ devaṃ na mayā na ca viṣṇunā .. 26.13 ..
6.3.d:
अवध्यो दानवः पापः सर्वेषां वै दिवौकसाम् .
मुक्त्वा तु शङ्करं देवं न मया न च विष्णुना .. 26.13 ..
6.3.m: 'The wicked Dānava cannot be slain by all the denizens of heaven, / neither by me nor by Viṣṇu, except by the god Śaṅkara. .. 26.13 ..

6.3.s:
tatraiva sarve gacchāmo yatra devo maheśvaraḥ .
sa gatiścaiva sarveṣāṃ vidyate'nyo na kaścana .. 26.14 ..
6.3.d:
तत्रैव सर्वे गच्छामो यत्र देवो महेश्वरः .
स गतिश्चैव सर्वेषां विद्यतेऽन्यो न कश्चन .. 26.14 ..
6.3.m: Let us all go right there where the god Maheśvara is; / he is the refuge for all, and no other exists.' .. 26.14 ..

6.3.s:
evamuktvā suraiḥ sarvairbrahmā vedavidāṃvaraḥ .
brāhmaṇaiḥ saha vidvadbhirato yatra maheśvaraḥ .. 26.15 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्त्वा सुरैः सर्वैर्ब्रह्मा वेदविदांवरः .
ब्राह्मणैः सह विद्वद्भिरतो यत्र महेश्वरः .. 26.15 ..
6.3.m: Having spoken thus with all the gods, Brahmā, the foremost knower of the Vedas, / with the learned brahmins, went to where Maheśvara was.

6.3.s: stutibhiśca supuṣṭābhistuṣṭāva parameśvaram .. 26.16 ..
6.3.d: स्तुतिभिश्च सुपुष्टाभिस्तुष्टाव परमेश्वरम् .. 26.16 ..
6.3.m: And with lavish hymns of praise he praised Parameśvara.

6.3.s:
devā ūcuḥ .
jaya tvaṃ devadeveśa jayomārdhaśarīradhṛk .
vṛṣāsana mahābāho śaśāṅkakṛtabhūṣaṇa .. 26.17 ..
6.3.d:
देवा ऊचुः .
जय त्वं देवदेवेश जयोमार्धशरीरधृक् .
वृषासन महाबाहो शशाङ्ककृतभूषण .. 26.17 ..
6.3.m: The gods said: / 'Victory to you, O Lord of the gods of gods! Victory to you who bear Umā in half your body! / O bull-seated one, mighty-armed one, adorned with the crescent moon!

6.3.s:
namaḥ śūlāgrahastāya namaḥ khaṭvāṅgadhāriṇe .
jaya bhūtapate deva dakṣayajñavināśana .. 26.18 ..
6.3.d:
नमः शूलाग्रहस्ताय नमः खट्वाङ्गधारिणे .
जय भूतपते देव दक्षयज्ञविनाशन .. 26.18 ..
6.3.m: Homage to you who hold the tip of a spear in hand! Homage to you who bear the khaṭvāṅga! / Victory, O Lord of beings, O God, destroyer of Dakṣa's sacrifice!

6.3.s:
pañcākṣara namo deva pañcabhūtātmavigraha .
pañcavaktramayeśāna vedaistvaṃ tu pragīyase .. 26.19 ..
6.3.d:
पञ्चाक्षर नमो देव पञ्चभूतात्मविग्रह .
पञ्चवक्त्रमयेशान वेदैस्त्वं तु प्रगीयसे .. 26.19 ..
6.3.m: O Five-Syllabled One, homage, O God whose body consists of the five elements! / O Īśāna who comprises five faces, you are praised indeed by the Vedas!

6.3.s:
sṛṣṭipālanasaṃhārāṃstvaṃ sadā kuruṣe namaḥ .
aṣṭamūrte smarahara smara satyaṃ yathā stutaḥ .. 26.20 ..
6.3.d:
सृष्टिपालनसंहारांस्त्वं सदा कुरुषे नमः .
अष्टमूर्ते स्मरहर स्मर सत्यं यथा स्तुतः .. 26.20 ..
6.3.m: You always perform creation, maintenance, and destruction; homage to you! / O Eight-Formed One, destroyer of Smara, remember the truth as you are praised!

6.3.s:
pañcātmikā tanurdeva brāhmaṇaiste pragīyate .
sadyo vāme tathāghore īśo tatpuruṣe tathā .. 26.21 ..
6.3.d:
पञ्चात्मिका तनुर्देव ब्राह्मणैस्ते प्रगीयते .
सद्यो वामे तथाघोरे ईशो तत्पुरुषे तथा .. 26.21 ..
6.3.m: O God, your fivefold body is chanted by the brahmins / as Sadyojāta, Vāmadeva, likewise Aghora, Īśāna, and Tatpuruṣa.

6.3.s:
hemajāle suvistīrṇe haṃsavatkūjase hara .
evaṃ stuto munigaṇairbrahmādyaiśca surāsuraiḥ .. 26.22 ..
6.3.d:
हेमजाले सुविस्तीर्णे हंसवत्कूजसे हर .
एवं स्तुतो मुनिगणैर्ब्रह्माद्यैश्च सुरासुरैः .. 26.22 ..
6.3.m: In a vast network of gold, you sing like a swan, O Hara!' / Thus praised by the hosts of sages, and by the gods and asuras led by Brahmā,

6.3.s: prahṛṣṭaḥ sumanā bhūtvā surasaṅghānuvāca ha .. 26.23 ..
6.3.d: प्रहृष्टः सुमना भूत्वा सुरसङ्घानुवाच ह .. 26.23 ..
6.3.m: delighted and serene of mind, he spoke to the assembly of gods.

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
svāgataṃ devaviprāṇāṃ suprabhātādya śarvarī .
kiṃ kurmo vadata kṣipraṃ ko'nyaḥ sevyaḥ surāsuraiḥ .. 26.24 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
स्वागतं देवविप्राणां सुप्रभाताद्य शर्वरी .
किं कुर्मो वदत क्षिप्रं कोऽन्यः सेव्यः सुरासुरैः .. 26.24 ..
6.3.m: Īśvara said: / 'Welcome to the gods and brahmins! Today night has turned into a beautiful dawn. / Tell me quickly, what should we do? Who else is to be served by gods and asuras?

6.3.s:
kiṃ duḥkhaṃ ko nu santāpaḥ kuto vo bhayamāgatam .
kathayadhvaṃ mahābhāgāḥ kāraṇaṃ yanmanogatam .. 26.25 ..
6.3.d:
किं दुःखं को नु सन्तापः कुतो वो भयमागतम् .
कथयध्वं महाभागाः कारणं यन्मनोगतम् .. 26.25 ..
6.3.m: What sorrow, what anguish is there? From where has fear come upon you? / Tell me, fortunate ones, the purpose that is in your mind.'

6.3.s:
evamuktāstu rudreṇa pratyavocansurarṣabhāḥ .
svānsvāndehāndarśayanto lajjamānā adhomukhāḥ .. 26.26 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्तास्तु रुद्रेण प्रत्यवोचन्सुरर्षभाः .
स्वान्स्वान्देहान्दर्शयन्तो लज्जमाना अधोमुखाः .. 26.26 ..
6.3.m: Thus addressed by Rudra, the best of the gods replied, / showing their bodies, ashamed and with faces turned downward:

6.3.s:
asti ghoro mahāvīryo dānavo baladarpitaḥ .
bāṇo nāmeti vikhyāto yasya tattripuraṃ mahat .. 26.27 ..
6.3.d:
अस्ति घोरो महावीर्यो दानवो बलदर्पितः .
बाणो नामेति विख्यातो यस्य तत्त्रिपुरं महत् .. 26.27 ..
6.3.m: 'There is a terrible dānava of great valor, arrogant with strength, / renowned by the name Bāṇa, to whom belongs that great Tripura.

6.3.s:
tena vai sutapastaptaṃ daśavarṣaśatāni hi .
tasya tuṣṭo'bhavadbrahmā niyamena damena ca .. 26.28 ..
6.3.d:
तेन वै सुतपस्तप्तं दशवर्षशतानि हि .
तस्य तुष्टोऽभवद्ब्रह्मा नियमेन दमेन च .. 26.28 ..
6.3.m: Indeed, severe austerity was practiced by him for a thousand years; / Brahmā was pleased with him for his restraint and self-control,

6.3.s:
purāṇi tānyabhedyāni dadau kāmagamāni vai .
āyasaṃ rājataṃ caiva sauvarṇaṃ ca tathāparam .. 26.29 ..
6.3.d:
पुराणि तान्यभेद्यानि ददौ कामगमानि वै .
आयसं राजतं चैव सौवर्णं च तथापरम् .. 26.29 ..
6.3.m: and granted those impenetrable cities that go wherever desired: / one of iron, one of silver, and another of gold.

6.3.s:
tripuraṃ brahmaṇā sṛṣṭaṃ bhramattatkāmagāmi ca .
tasyaiva tu balotkṛṣṭāstripure dānavāḥ sthitāḥ .. 26.30 ..
6.3.d:
त्रिपुरं ब्रह्मणा सृष्टं भ्रमत्तत्कामगामि च .
तस्यैव तु बलोत्कृष्टास्त्रिपुरे दानवाः स्थिताः .. 26.30 ..
6.3.m: The triple city, created by Brahmā, wanders about moving at will, / and relying on his very strength, the dānavas dwell in Tripura.

6.3.s:
trailokyaṃ sakalaṃ deva pīḍayanti mahāsurāḥ .
daṇḍapāśāsiśastrāṇi avikāre vikurvate .
tripuraṃ dānavairjuṣṭaṃ bhramattaccakrasaṃnibham .. 26.31 ..
6.3.d:
त्रैलोक्यं सकलं देव पीडयन्ति महासुराः .
दण्डपाशासिशस्त्राणि अविकारे विकुर्वते .
त्रिपुरं दानवैर्जुष्टं भ्रमत्तच्चक्रसंनिभम् .. 26.31 ..
6.3.m: The great asuras torment the entire triple world, O God. / Without provocation they wield staffs, nooses, and swords as weapons; / Tripura, occupied by the dānavas, wanders like a wheel.

6.3.s: kvaciddṛśyamadṛśyaṃ vā mṛgatṛṣṇaiva lakṣyate .. 26.32 ..
6.3.d: क्वचिद्दृश्यमदृश्यं वा मृगतृष्णैव लक्ष्यते .. 26.32 ..
6.3.m: Somewhere visible or invisible, it appears like a mirage.

6.3.s:
yasminpatati taddivyaṃ dṛptasya tripuraṃ mahat .
na tatra brāhmaṇā devā gāvo naiva tu jantavaḥ .. 26.33 ..
6.3.d:
यस्मिन्पतति तद्दिव्यं दृप्तस्य त्रिपुरं महत् .
न तत्र ब्राह्मणा देवा गावो नैव तु जन्तवः .. 26.33 ..
6.3.m: Wherever that divine, great Tripura of that haughty one falls, / there remain no brahmins, no gods, no cows, and no living creatures.

6.3.s:
na tatra dṛśyate kiṃcitpatedyatra puratrayam .
nadyo grāmāśca deśāśca bahavo bhasmasātkṛtāḥ .. 26.34 ..
6.3.d:
न तत्र दृश्यते किंचित्पतेद्यत्र पुरत्रयम् .
नद्यो ग्रामाश्च देशाश्च बहवो भस्मसात्कृताः .. 26.34 ..
6.3.m: Nothing at all is seen where that triad of cities might fall; / rivers, villages, and many regions have been reduced to ashes.

6.3.s:
suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ caiva maṇimauktikameva ca .
strīratnaṃ śobhanaṃ yacca tatsarvaṃ karṣate balāt .. 26.35 ..
6.3.d:
सुवर्णं रजतं चैव मणिमौक्तिकमेव च .
स्त्रीरत्नं शोभनं यच्च तत्सर्वं कर्षते बलात् .. 26.35 ..
6.3.m: Gold, silver, gems, and pearls, / and whatever splendid jewel of a woman there is, all that he drags away by force.

6.3.s:
na śastreṇa na cāstreṇa na divā niśi vā hara .
śakyate devasaṅghaiśca nihantuṃ sa kathaṃcana .. 26.36 ..
6.3.d:
न शस्त्रेण न चास्त्रेण न दिवा निशि वा हर .
शक्यते देवसङ्घैश्च निहन्तुं स कथंचन .. 26.36 ..
6.3.m: Neither by weapon nor by missile, neither by day nor by night, O Hara, / can he be slain in any way by the hosts of gods.

6.3.s:
taddahasva mahādeva tvaṃ hi naḥ paramā gatiḥ .
evaṃ prasādaṃ deveśa sarveṣāṃ kartumarhasi .. 26.37 ..
6.3.d:
तद्दहस्व महादेव त्वं हि नः परमा गतिः .
एवं प्रसादं देवेश सर्वेषां कर्तुमर्हसि .. 26.37 ..
6.3.m: Therefore burn it down, O Mahādeva, for you are our ultimate refuge; / thus you should grant this favor to all, O Lord of gods,

6.3.s:
yena devāśca gandharvā ṛṣayaśca tapodhanāḥ .
parāṃ dhṛtiṃ samāyānti tatprabho kartumarhasi .. 26.38 ..
6.3.d:
येन देवाश्च गन्धर्वा ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः .
परां धृतिं समायान्ति तत्प्रभो कर्तुमर्हसि .. 26.38 ..
6.3.m: so that the gods, gandharvas, and seers rich in austerity / may attain supreme comfort; you ought to do that, O Lord.'

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
etatsarvaṃ kariṣyāmi mā viṣādaṃ gamiṣyatha .
acireṇaiva kālena kuryāṃ yuṣmatsukhāvaham .. 26.39 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
एतत्सर्वं करिष्यामि मा विषादं गमिष्यथ .
अचिरेणैव कालेन कुर्यां युष्मत्सुखावहम् .. 26.39 ..
6.3.m: Īśvara said: / 'I shall do all this; do not fall into despair. / In a very short time I shall bring about what brings you joy.'

6.3.s:
āśvāsayitvā tāndevānsarvānindrapurogamān .
cintayāmāsa deveśastripurasya vadhaṃ prati .. 26.40 ..
6.3.d:
आश्वासयित्वा तान्देवान्सर्वानिन्द्रपुरोगमान् .
चिन्तयामास देवेशस्त्रिपुरस्य वधं प्रति .. 26.40 ..
6.3.m: Having consoled those gods, all led by Indra, / the Lord of gods contemplated the destruction of Tripura:

6.3.s:
kathaṃ kena prakāreṇa hantavyaṃ tripuraṃ mayā .
tamekaṃ nāradaṃ muktvā nānyopāyo vidhīyate .. 26.41 ..
6.3.d:
कथं केन प्रकारेण हन्तव्यं त्रिपुरं मया .
तमेकं नारदं मुक्त्वा नान्योपायो विधीयते .. 26.41 ..
6.3.m: 'How, and by what means, should Tripura be slain by me? / Setting aside that sole Nārada, no other means is prescribed.'

6.3.s:
evaṃ saṃstabhya cātmānaṃ tato dhyātaḥ sa nāradaḥ .
tatkṣaṇādeva samprāpto vāyubhūto mahātapāḥ .. 26.42 ..
6.3.d:
एवं संस्तभ्य चात्मानं ततो ध्यातः स नारदः .
तत्क्षणादेव सम्प्राप्तो वायुभूतो महातपाः .. 26.42 ..
6.3.m: Having thus composed himself, he then meditated upon Nārada. / At that very instant that [sage] of great austerity arrived, moving like the wind,

6.3.s:
kamaṇḍaludharo devastridaṇḍī jñānakovidaḥ .
yogapaṭṭākṣasūtreṇa chatreṇaiva virājitaḥ .. 26.43 ..
6.3.d:
कमण्डलुधरो देवस्त्रिदण्डी ज्ञानकोविदः .
योगपट्टाक्षसूत्रेण छत्रेणैव विराजितः .. 26.43 ..
6.3.m: the divine one holding a waterpot, carrying a triple staff, skilled in knowledge, / adorned with a meditation band, a rosary, and an umbrella,

6.3.s:
jaṭājūṭābaddhaśirā jvalanārkasamaprabhaḥ .
tridhā pradakṣiṇīkṛtya daṇḍavatpatito bhuvi .. 26.44 ..
6.3.d:
जटाजूटाबद्धशिरा ज्वलनार्कसमप्रभः .
त्रिधा प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य दण्डवत्पतितो भुवि .. 26.44 ..
6.3.m: his head bound with matted hair, brilliant as the blazing sun. / Having circumambulated [him] thrice, he fell to the ground like a staff.

6.3.s:
kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhūtvā nārado bhagavānmuniḥ .
stotreṇa mahatā śarvaḥ stuto bhaktyā mahāmanāḥ .. 26.45 ..
6.3.d:
कृताञ्जलिपुटो भूत्वा नारदो भगवान्मुनिः .
स्तोत्रेण महता शर्वः स्तुतो भक्त्या महामनाः .. 26.45 ..
6.3.m: With folded hands, the divine sage Nārada, / high-minded, praised Śarva with devotion through a great hymn.

6.3.s:
nārada uvāca -
jaya śambho virūpākṣa jaya deva trilocana .
jaya śaṅkara īśāna rudreśvara namo'stu te .. 26.46 ..
6.3.d:
नारद उवाच -
जय शम्भो विरूपाक्ष जय देव त्रिलोचन .
जय शङ्कर ईशान रुद्रेश्वर नमोऽस्तु ते .. 26.46 ..
6.3.m: Nārada said: / 'Victory, O Śambhu, O Virūpākṣa! Victory, O God, three-eyed one! / Victory, O Śaṅkara, O Īśāna, O Lord of the Rudras, homage be to you!

6.3.s:
tvaṃ patistvaṃ jagatkartā tvameva layakṛdvibho .
tvameva jagatāṃ nātho duṣṭātakaniṣūdanaḥ .. 26.47 ..
6.3.d:
त्वं पतिस्त्वं जगत्कर्ता त्वमेव लयकृद्विभो .
त्वमेव जगतां नाथो दुष्टातकनिषूदनः .. 26.47 ..
6.3.m: You are the master, you are the creator of the world, you alone are the cause of dissolution, O all-pervading one! / You alone are the lord of the worlds, the slayer of the afflictions of the wicked!

6.3.s:
tvaṃ naḥ pāhi sureśāna trayīmūrte sanātana .
bhavamūrte bhavāre tvaṃ bhajatāmabhayo bhava .. 26.48 ..
6.3.d:
त्वं नः पाहि सुरेशान त्रयीमूर्ते सनातन .
भवमूर्ते भवारे त्वं भजतामभयो भव .. 26.48 ..
6.3.m: Protect us, O Lord of the gods, eternal one whose form is the three Vedas! / O you whose form is existence, enemy of mundane existence, grant fearlessness to those who worship you!

6.3.s:
bhavabhāvavināśārthaṃ bhava tvāṃ śaraṇaṃ bhaje .
kimarthaṃ cintito deva ājñā me dīyatāṃ prabho .. 26.49 ..
6.3.d:
भवभावविनाशार्थं भव त्वां शरणं भजे .
किमर्थं चिन्तितो देव आज्ञा मे दीयतां प्रभो .. 26.49 ..
6.3.m: For the destruction of mundane existence, O Bhava, I resort to you as refuge. / Why was I contemplated, O God? Let your command be given to me, O Lord!

6.3.s:
kasya saṃkṣobhaye cittaṃ ko vādya patatu kṣitau .
kamadya kalahenāhaṃ yojaye jayatāṃvara .. 26.50 ..
6.3.d:
कस्य संक्षोभये चित्तं को वाद्य पततु क्षितौ .
कमद्य कलहेनाहं योजये जयतांवर .. 26.50 ..
6.3.m: Whose mind shall I agitate? Or who should fall to the earth today? / With whom shall I engage in strife today, O foremost of victors?'

6.3.s:
nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā devadevo maheśvaraḥ .
utphullanayano bhūtvā idaṃ vacanamabravīt .. 26.51 ..
6.3.d:
नारदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा देवदेवो महेश्वरः .
उत्फुल्लनयनो भूत्वा इदं वचनमब्रवीत् .. 26.51 ..
6.3.m: Hearing Nārada's words, Maheśvara, the god of gods, / with blossoming eyes, spoke this speech:

6.3.s:
svāgataṃ te muniśreṣṭha sadaiva kalahapriya .
vīṇāvādanatattvajña brahmaputra sanātana .. 26.52 ..
6.3.d:
स्वागतं ते मुनिश्रेष्ठ सदैव कलहप्रिय .
वीणावादनतत्त्वज्ञ ब्रह्मपुत्र सनातन .. 26.52 ..
6.3.m: 'Welcome to you, best of sages, who are always fond of strife, / knower of the truth of vīṇā-playing, eternal son of Brahmā!

6.3.s:
gaccha nārada śīghraṃ tvaṃ yatra tattripuraṃ mahat .
bāṇasya dānavendrasya sarvalokabhayāvaham .. 26.53 ..
6.3.d:
गच्छ नारद शीघ्रं त्वं यत्र तत्त्रिपुरं महत् .
बाणस्य दानवेन्द्रस्य सर्वलोकभयावहम् .. 26.53 ..
6.3.m: Go quickly, Nārada, to where that great Tripura is, / belonging to Bāṇa, the lord of dānavas, which causes fear to all the worlds.

6.3.s:
bhartāro devatātulyāḥ striyastatrāpsaraḥsamāḥ .
tāsāṃ vai tejasā caiva bhramate tripuraṃ mahat .. 26.54 ..
6.3.d:
भर्तारो देवतातुल्याः स्त्रियस्तत्राप्सरःसमाः .
तासां वै तेजसा चैव भ्रमते त्रिपुरं महत् .. 26.54 ..
6.3.m: Its masters are equal to deities; the women there are equal to apsarases. / And by their brilliance that great Tripura wanders about.

6.3.s:
na śakyate kathaṃ bhettuṃ sarvopāyairdvijottama .
gatvā tvaṃ mohaya kṣipraṃ pṛthagdharmairanekadhā .. 26.55 ..
6.3.d:
न शक्यते कथं भेत्तुं सर्वोपायैर्द्विजोत्तम .
गत्वा त्वं मोहय क्षिप्रं पृथग्धर्मैरनेकधा .. 26.55 ..
6.3.m: It cannot be breached in any way by any means, O best of the twice-born. / Go and quickly delude [them] in many ways through different doctrines.'

6.3.s:
nārada uvāca -
tava vākyena deveśa bhedayāmi purottamam .
abhedyaṃ bahudhopāyairyattu devaiḥ savāsavaiḥ .. 26.56 ..
6.3.d:
नारद उवाच -
तव वाक्येन देवेश भेदयामि पुरोत्तमम् .
अभेद्यं बहुधोपायैर्यत्तु देवैः सवासवैः .. 26.56 ..
6.3.m: Nārada said: / 'At your word, O Lord of gods, I shall cause division in that foremost city, / which could not be breached by many means by the gods along with Indra.'

6.3.s:
evamuktvā gato bhūpa śatayojanamāyatam .
bāṇasya tatpuraśreṣṭhamṛddhivṛddhisamāyutam .. 26.57 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्त्वा गतो भूप शतयोजनमायतम् .
बाणस्य तत्पुरश्रेष्ठमृद्धिवृद्धिसमायुतम् .. 26.57 ..
6.3.m: Having spoken thus, O king, he went to that foremost city of Bāṇa, / extending for a hundred yojanas, endowed with prosperity and growth,

6.3.s:
kṛtakautukasambādhaṃ nānādhātuvicitritam .
anekaharmyasaṃchannamanekāyatanojjvalam .. 26.58 ..
6.3.d:
कृतकौतुकसम्बाधं नानाधातुविचित्रितम् .
अनेकहर्म्यसंछन्नमनेकायतनोज्ज्वलम् .. 26.58 ..
6.3.m: crowded with created wonders, variegated with various minerals, / covered with numerous mansions, and radiant with many temples.

6.3.s:
dvāratoraṇasaṃyuktaṃ kapāṭārgalabhūṣitam .
bahuyantrasamopetaṃ prākāraparikhojjvalam .. 26.59 ..
6.3.d:
द्वारतोरणसंयुक्तं कपाटार्गलभूषितम् .
बहुयन्त्रसमोपेतं प्राकारपरिखोज्ज्वलम् .. 26.59 ..
6.3.m: Equipped with gateways and arched portals, adorned with door leaves and bolts, / furnished with many mechanical devices, radiant with ramparts and moats,

6.3.s:
vāpīkṛpataḍāgaiśca devatāyatanairyutam .
haṃsakāraṇḍavākīrṇaṃ padminīkhaṇḍamaṇḍitam .. 26.60 ..
6.3.d:
वापीकृपतडागैश्च देवतायतनैर्युतम् .
हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णं पद्मिनीखण्डमण्डितम् .. 26.60 ..
6.3.m: Provided with step-wells, wells, and reservoirs, and temples of the gods, / thronged with geese and kāraṇḍava ducks, ornamented with clusters of lotus beds,

6.3.s:
anekavanaśobhāḍhyaṃ nānāvihagamaṇḍitam .
evaṃ guṇagaṇākīrṇaṃ bāṇasya puramuttamam .. 26.61 ..
6.3.d:
अनेकवनशोभाढ्यं नानाविहगमण्डितम् .
एवं गुणगणाकीर्णं बाणस्य पुरमुत्तमम् .. 26.61 ..
6.3.m: Rich with the beauty of numerous groves, decorated with various birds, / thus filled with a multitude of good qualities was the excellent city of Bāṇa.

6.3.s:
tasya madhye mahākāyaṃ saptakakṣaṃ suśobhitam .
bāṇasya bhavanaṃ divyaṃ sarvaṃ kāñcanabhūṣitam .. 26.62 ..
6.3.d:
तस्य मध्ये महाकायं सप्तकक्षं सुशोभितम् .
बाणस्य भवनं दिव्यं सर्वं काञ्चनभूषितम् .. 26.62 ..
6.3.m: In its center stood Bāṇa’s divine palace of immense proportions, / having seven courtyards, beautifully adorned, entirely embellished with gold,

6.3.s:
mauktikādāmaśobhāḍhyaṃ vajravaiḍūryabhūṣitam .
rukmapaṭṭatalākīrṇaṃ ratnabhūmyā suśobhitam .. 26.63 ..
6.3.d:
मौक्तिकादामशोभाढ्यं वज्रवैडूर्यभूषितम् .
रुक्मपट्टतलाकीर्णं रत्नभूम्या सुशोभितम् .. 26.63 ..
6.3.m: Rich in the luster of pearl garlands, decorated with diamonds and lapis lazuli, / covered with pavements of gold plates, splendid with jeweled floors,

6.3.s:
mattamātaṅganiḥśvāsaiḥ syandanaiḥ saṃkulīkṛtam .
hayaheṣitaśabdaiśca nārīṇāṃ nūpurasvanaiḥ .. 26.64 ..
6.3.d:
मत्तमातङ्गनिःश्वासैः स्यन्दनैः संकुलीकृतम् .
हयहेषितशब्दैश्च नारीणां नूपुरस्वनैः .. 26.64 ..
6.3.m: Thronged with chariots and the heavy breathing of intoxicated elephants, / and with the sounds of neighing horses and the tinkling of women’s anklets,

6.3.s:
khaḍgatomarahastaiśca vajrāṅkuśaśarāyudhaiḥ .
rakṣitaṃ ghorarūpaiśca dānavairbaladarpitaiḥ .. 26.65 ..
6.3.d:
खड्गतोमरहस्तैश्च वज्राङ्कुशशरायुधैः .
रक्षितं घोररूपैश्च दानवैर्बलदर्पितैः .. 26.65 ..
6.3.m: Guarded by ferocious Dānavas arrogant with power, / their hands armed with swords and lances, carrying vajras, elephant goads, and arrows.

6.3.s:
evaṃ guṇagaṇākīrṇaṃ bāṇasya bhavanottamam .
kailāsaśikharaprakhyaṃ mahendrabhavanopamam .. 26.66 ..
6.3.d:
एवं गुणगणाकीर्णं बाणस्य भवनोत्तमम् .
कैलासशिखरप्रख्यं महेन्द्रभवनोपमम् .. 26.66 ..
6.3.m: Thus filled with a host of virtues was the supreme palace of Bāṇa, / resembling the peak of Kailāsa, like the residence of Mahendra.

6.3.s:
nārado gagane śīghramagamatpurasaṃmukhaḥ .
dvāradeśaṃ samāsādya kṣattāraṃ vākyamabravīt .. 26.67 ..
6.3.d:
नारदो गगने शीघ्रमगमत्पुरसंमुखः .
द्वारदेशं समासाद्य क्षत्तारं वाक्यमब्रवीत् .. 26.67 ..
6.3.m: Nārada swiftly moved through the sky facing toward the city. / Reaching the gateway, he spoke these words to the chamberlain:

6.3.s:
bhobhoḥ kṣattarmahābuddhe rājakāryaviśārada .
śīghraṃ bāṇāya cācakṣva nārado dvāri tiṣṭhati .. 26.68 ..
6.3.d:
भोभोः क्षत्तर्महाबुद्धे राजकार्यविशारद .
शीघ्रं बाणाय चाचक्ष्व नारदो द्वारि तिष्ठति .. 26.68 ..
6.3.m: “O chamberlain of great intellect, skilled in royal affairs! / Report quickly to Bāṇa that Nārada is waiting at the door.”

6.3.s:
sa vandayitvā caraṇau nāradasya tvarānvitaḥ .
sabhāmadhyagataṃ bāṇaṃ vijñaptumupacakrame .. 26.69 ..
6.3.d:
स वन्दयित्वा चरणौ नारदस्य त्वरान्वितः .
सभामध्यगतं बाणं विज्ञप्तुमुपचक्रमे .. 26.69 ..
6.3.m: Having bowed at the feet of Nārada with haste, / he proceeded to make a representation to Bāṇa who was sitting in the assembly.

6.3.s:
vepamānāṅgayaṣṭistu kareṇāpihitānanaḥ .
śṛṇvatāṃ sarvayodhānāmidaṃ vacanamabravīt .. 26.70 ..
6.3.d:
वेपमानाङ्गयष्टिस्तु करेणापिहिताननः .
शृण्वतां सर्वयोधानामिदं वचनमब्रवीत् .. 26.70 ..
6.3.m: His slender body trembling, his face covered with his hand, / he uttered these words in the hearing of all the warriors:

6.3.s:
vandito devagandharvairyakṣakinnaradānavaiḥ .
kalipriyo durārādhyo nārado dvāri tiṣṭhati .. 26.71 ..
6.3.d:
वन्दितो देवगन्धर्वैर्यक्षकिन्नरदानवैः .
कलिप्रियो दुराराध्यो नारदो द्वारि तिष्ठति .. 26.71 ..
6.3.m: “Worshiped by gods, gandharvas, yakṣas, kinnaras, and dānavas, / fond of strife, difficult to propitiate—Nārada stands at the door!”

6.3.s:
dvārapālasya tadvākyaṃ śrutvā bāṇastvarānvitaḥ .
dvāḥsthamāha mahādaityaḥ savismayamidaṃ tadā .. 26.72 ..
6.3.d:
द्वारपालस्य तद्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा बाणस्त्वरान्वितः .
द्वाःस्थमाह महादैत्यः सविस्मयमिदं तदा .. 26.72 ..
6.3.m: Having heard those words of the doorkeeper, Bāṇa, full of haste, / the great Daitya then spoke to the doorkeeper in astonishment:

6.3.s:
bāṇa uvāca -
brahmaputraṃ satejaskaṃ duḥsahaṃ duratikramam .
praveśaya mahābhāgaṃ kimarthaṃ vārito bahiḥ .. 26.73 ..
6.3.d:
बाण उवाच -
ब्रह्मपुत्रं सतेजस्कं दुःसहं दुरतिक्रमम् .
प्रवेशय महाभागं किमर्थं वारितो बहिः .. 26.73 ..
6.3.m:
Bāṇa said:
“The glorious son of Brahmā, radiant, unbearable, unassailable— / usher him in! Why has he been made to wait outside?”

6.3.s:
śrutvā prabhorvacastasya prāveśayadudīritam .
gatvā vegena mahatā nāradaṃ gṛhamāgatam .. 26.74 ..
6.3.d:
श्रुत्वा प्रभोर्वचस्तस्य प्रावेशयदुदीरितम् .
गत्वा वेगेन महता नारदं गृहमागतम् .. 26.74 ..
6.3.m: Having heard that command uttered by his lord, going with great speed, / he brought in Nārada who had arrived at the palace.

6.3.s:
dṛṣṭvā devarṣimāyāntaṃ nāradaṃ surapūjitam .
sāhasotthāya saṃhṛṣṭo vavande caraṇau muneḥ .. 26.75 ..
6.3.d:
दृष्ट्वा देवर्षिमायान्तं नारदं सुरपूजितम् .
साहसोत्थाय संहृष्टो ववन्दे चरणौ मुनेः .. 26.75 ..
6.3.m: Seeing the celestial seer Nārada approaching, who is worshiped by the gods, / rising up boldly and filled with joy, he bowed at the feet of the sage.

6.3.s:
dadau cāsanamarghyaṃ ca pādyaṃ pūjāṃ yathāvidhi .
nyavedayacca tadrājyamātmānaṃ bāndhavaiḥ saha .. 26.76 ..
6.3.d:
ददौ चासनमर्घ्यं च पाद्यं पूजां यथाविधि .
न्यवेदयच्च तद्राज्यमात्मानं बान्धवैः सह .. 26.76 ..
6.3.m: He gave him a seat, the arghya offering, water for the feet, and ritual worship according to the rule, / and presented his kingdom and himself, along with his kinsmen.

6.3.s: papraccha kuśalaṃ cāpi muniṃ bāṇāsuraḥ svayam .. 26.77 ..
6.3.d: पप्रच्छ कुशलं चापि मुनिं बाणासुरः स्वयम् .. 26.77 ..
6.3.m: The demon Bāṇa himself also inquired after the welfare of the sage.

6.3.s:
nārada uvāca -
sādhu sādhu mahābāho danorvaṃśavivarddhana .
ko'nyastribhuvane ślāghyastvāṃ muktvā danupuṃgava .. 26.78 ..
6.3.d:
नारद उवाच -
साधु साधु महाबाहो दनोर्वंशविवर्द्धन .
कोऽन्यस्त्रिभुवने श्लाघ्यस्त्वां मुक्त्वा दनुपुंगव .. 26.78 ..
6.3.m:
Nārada said:
“Well done, well done, O mighty-armed one, enhancer of the lineage of Danu! / Who else in the three worlds is praiseworthy besides you, O best of Danu’s line?

6.3.s:
pūjito'haṃ danuśreṣṭha dhanaratnaiḥ suśobhanaiḥ .
rājyena cātmanā vāpi hyevaṃ kaḥ pūjayetparaḥ .. 26.79 ..
6.3.d:
पूजितोऽहं दनुश्रेष्ठ धनरत्नैः सुशोभनैः .
राज्येन चात्मना वापि ह्येवं कः पूजयेत्परः .. 26.79 ..
6.3.m: I have been honored by you, O foremost among Danu’s sons, with splendid wealth and gems, / and even with your kingdom and yourself! Who else would worship thus?

6.3.s:
na me kāryaṃ hi bhogena bhuṅkṣva rājyamanāmayam .
tvaddarśanotsukaḥ prāpto dṛṣṭvā devaṃ maheśvaram .. 26.80 ..
6.3.d:
न मे कार्यं हि भोगेन भुङ्क्ष्व राज्यमनामयम् .
त्वद्दर्शनोत्सुकः प्राप्तो दृष्ट्वा देवं महेश्वरम् .. 26.80 ..
6.3.m: Indeed, I have no concern with enjoyment; enjoy your trouble-free kingdom. / Eager for a darśana of you, I have arrived after seeing Lord Maheśvara.

6.3.s:
bhramate tripuraṃ loke strīsatītvānmayā śrutam .
tāndraṣṭukāmaḥ samprāptastvaddārāndānaveśvara .. 26.81 ..
6.3.d:
भ्रमते त्रिपुरं लोके स्त्रीसतीत्वान्मया श्रुतम् .
तान्द्रष्टुकामः सम्प्राप्तस्त्वद्दारान्दानवेश्वर .. 26.81 ..
6.3.m: I have heard that Tripura revolves in the world because of the chastity of women. / Desiring to see them, I have come to see your wives, O lord of the Dānavas.

6.3.s:
manyase yadi me śīghraṃ darśayasva ca māciram .
nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā kañcukiṃ samudīkṣya vai .. 26.82 ..
6.3.d:
मन्यसे यदि मे शीघ्रं दर्शयस्व च माचिरम् .
नारदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा कञ्चुकिं समुदीक्ष्य वै .. 26.82 ..
6.3.m: If you approve, show them to me quickly and without delay.” / Hearing the words of Nārada, and glancing at the chamberlain,

6.3.s:
antaḥpuracaraṃ vṛddhaṃ daṇḍapāṇiṃ guṇānvitam .
uvāca rājā hṛṣṭātmā śabdenāpūrayandiśaḥ .. 26.83 ..
6.3.d:
अन्तःपुरचरं वृद्धं दण्डपाणिं गुणान्वितम् .
उवाच राजा हृष्टात्मा शब्देनापूरयन्दिशः .. 26.83 ..
6.3.m: The elder who attends the inner apartments, staff in hand and endowed with virtues, / the king, glad at heart, spoke, filling the quarters with his voice:

6.3.s:
nāradāya mahādevīṃ darśayasveha kañcukin .
antaḥpuracaraiḥ sarvaiḥ sametāmaviśaṅkitaḥ .. 26.84 ..
6.3.d:
नारदाय महादेवीं दर्शयस्वेह कञ्चुकिन् .
अन्तःपुरचरैः सर्वैः समेतामविशङ्कितः .. 26.84 ..
6.3.m: “O chamberlain, show the queen to Nārada here, / accompanied by all the attendants of the inner apartments, without any hesitation.”

6.3.s:
nāthasyājñāṃ puraskṛtya gṛhītvā nāradaṃ kare .
praviśyākathayaddevyai nārado'yaṃ samāgataḥ .. 26.85 ..
6.3.d:
नाथस्याज्ञां पुरस्कृत्य गृहीत्वा नारदं करे .
प्रविश्याकथयद्देव्यै नारदोऽयं समागतः .. 26.85 ..
6.3.m: Placing his master’s order first, taking Nārada by the hand, / entering, he told the queen: “This is Nārada who has arrived.”

6.3.s:
dṛṣṭvā devī muniśreṣṭhaṃ kṛtvā pādābhivandanam .
āsanaṃ kāñcanaṃ śubhramarghyapādyādikaṃ dadau .. 26.86 ..
6.3.d:
दृष्ट्वा देवी मुनिश्रेष्ठं कृत्वा पादाभिवन्दनम् .
आसनं काञ्चनं शुभ्रमर्घ्यपाद्यादिकं ददौ .. 26.86 ..
6.3.m: Seeing the best of sages, the queen paid homage at his feet, / and offered a bright golden seat, arghya, water for the feet, and the rest.

6.3.s:
tasyai sa bhagavāṃstuṣṭo hyāśīrvādamadātparam .
nānyā devi triloke'pi tvatsamā dṛśyate'ṅganā .. 26.87 ..
6.3.d:
तस्यै स भगवांस्तुष्टो ह्याशीर्वादमदात्परम् .
नान्या देवि त्रिलोकेऽपि त्वत्समा दृश्यतेऽङ्गना .. 26.87 ..
6.3.m: Pleased with her, the blessed one gave her a supreme blessing: / “O queen, no other woman in the three worlds is seen equal to you,

6.3.s:
pativratā śubhācārā satyaśaucasamanvitā .
yasyāḥ prabhāvāttripuraṃ bhramate cakravatsadā .. 26.88 ..
6.3.d:
पतिव्रता शुभाचारा सत्यशौचसमन्विता .
यस्याः प्रभावात्त्रिपुरं भ्रमते चक्रवत्सदा .. 26.88 ..
6.3.m: Devoted to your husband, of virtuous conduct, endowed with truth and purity, / by whose power Tripura revolves constantly like a wheel!”

6.3.s:
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ devī nāradasya sudānvitam .
paryapṛcchadṛṣiṃ bhaktyā dharmaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃvarā .. 26.89 ..
6.3.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं देवी नारदस्य सुदान्वितम् .
पर्यपृच्छदृषिं भक्त्या धर्मं धर्मभृतांवरा .. 26.89 ..
6.3.m: Hearing those nectar-like words of Nārada, the queen, / foremost among the upholders of dharma, questioned the seer with devotion about dharma:

6.3.s:
rājñyuvāca -
bhagavanmānuṣe loke devāstuṣyanti kairvrataiḥ .
kāni dānāni dīyante yeṣāṃ ca syānmahatphalam .. 26.90 ..
6.3.d:
राज्ञ्युवाच -
भगवन्मानुषे लोके देवास्तुष्यन्ति कैर्व्रतैः .
कानि दानानि दीयन्ते येषां च स्यान्महत्फलम् .. 26.90 ..
6.3.m:
The queen said:
“O holy one, by what observances are the gods pleased in the human world? / What gifts are given that yield great fruit?

6.3.s:
upavāsāśca ye kecitstrīdharme kathitā budhaiḥ .
yaiḥ kṛtaiḥ svargamāyānti sukṛtinyaḥ striyo yathā .. 26.91 ..
6.3.d:
उपवासाश्च ये केचित्स्त्रीधर्मे कथिता बुधैः .
यैः कृतैः स्वर्गमायान्ति सुकृतिन्यः स्त्रियो यथा .. 26.91 ..
6.3.m: And what fasts have been declared by the wise regarding the dharma of women, / by performing which virtuous women go to heaven?

6.3.s:
yattatsarvaṃ mahābhāga kathayasva yathātatham .
śrotumicchāmyahaṃ sarvaṃ kathayasvāviśaṅkitaḥ .. 26.92 ..
6.3.d:
यत्तत्सर्वं महाभाग कथयस्व यथातथम् .
श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं सर्वं कथयस्वाविशङ्कितः .. 26.92 ..
6.3.m: Tell me all that accurately, O illustrious one! / I wish to hear everything; speak without hesitation.”

6.3.s:
nārada uvāca -
sādhu sādhu mahābhāge praśno'yaṃ veditastvayā .
yaṃ śrutvā sarvanārīṇāṃ dharmavṛddhistu jāyate .. 26.93 ..
6.3.d:
नारद उवाच -
साधु साधु महाभागे प्रश्नोऽयं वेदितस्त्वया .
यं श्रुत्वा सर्वनारीणां धर्मवृद्धिस्तु जायते .. 26.93 ..
6.3.m:
Nārada said:
“Well said, well said, O blessed lady! This question has been appropriately framed by you, / hearing which the increase of dharma arises for all women.

6.3.s:
upavāsaiśca dānaiśca patiputrau vaśānugau .
bāndhavaiḥ pūjyate nityaṃ yaiḥ kṛtaiḥ kathayāmi te .. 26.94 ..
6.3.d:
उपवासैश्च दानैश्च पतिपुत्रौ वशानुगौ .
बान्धवैः पूज्यते नित्यं यैः कृतैः कथयामि ते .. 26.94 ..
6.3.m: By which fasts and gifts a husband and son become obedient / and one is continually honored by relatives—those I shall tell you,

6.3.s:
durbhagā subhagā yaistu subhagā durbhagā bhavet .
putriṇī putrarahitā hyaputrā putriṇī tathā .. 26.95 ..
6.3.d:
दुर्भगा सुभगा यैस्तु सुभगा दुर्भगा भवेत् .
पुत्रिणी पुत्ररहिता ह्यपुत्रा पुत्रिणी तथा .. 26.95 ..
6.3.m: By which an unfortunate woman becomes fortunate, and a fortunate woman becomes unfortunate, / a mother of sons becomes childless, and a childless woman gains sons,

6.3.s:
bhartāraṃ labhate kanyā tathānyā bhartṛvarjitā .
kṛtākṛtaiśca jāyante tannibodhasva sundari .. 26.96 ..
6.3.d:
भर्तारं लभते कन्या तथान्या भर्तृवर्जिता .
कृताकृतैश्च जायन्ते तन्निबोधस्व सुन्दरि .. 26.96 ..
6.3.m: A maiden obtains a husband, and another is bereft of a husband. / They arise from things done and left undone; learn that, O beautiful one!

6.3.s:
tiladhenuṃ suvarṇaṃ ca rūpyaṃ gā vāsasī tathā .
pānīyaṃ bhūmidānaṃ ca gandhadhūpānulepanam .. 26.97 ..
6.3.d:
तिलधेनुं सुवर्णं च रूप्यं गा वाससी तथा .
पानीयं भूमिदानं च गन्धधूपानुलेपनम् .. 26.97 ..
6.3.m: A cow made of sesame seeds, gold, silver, cows, and two garments, / water, gift of land, fragrant scents, incense, and unguents,

6.3.s:
pādukopānahau chatraṃ puṇyāni vyañjanāni ca .
pādābhyaṅgaṃ śiro'bhyaṅgaṃ snānaṃ śayyāsanāni ca .. 26.98 ..
6.3.d:
पादुकोपानहौ छत्रं पुण्यानि व्यञ्जनानि च .
पादाभ्यङ्गं शिरोऽभ्यङ्गं स्नानं शय्यासनानि च .. 26.98 ..
6.3.m: Wooden clogs, leather shoes, an umbrella, auspicious fans, / foot-massage, head-massage, ritual ablution, beds, and seats—

6.3.s:
etāni ye prayacchanti nopasarpanti te yamam .
madhu māṣaṃ payaḥ sarpirlavaṇaṃ guḍamauṣadham .. 26.99 ..
6.3.d:
एतानि ये प्रयच्छन्ति नोपसर्पन्ति ते यमम् .
मधु माषं पयः सर्पिर्लवणं गुडमौषधम् .. 26.99 ..
6.3.m: Those who give these do not approach Yama. / Honey, black gram, milk, clarified butter, salt, jaggery, medicine,

6.3.s:
pānīyaṃ bhūmidānaṃ ca śālīnikṣurasāṃstathā .
āraktavāsasī ślakṣṇe dampatyorlalitādine .. 26.100 ..
6.3.d:
पानीयं भूमिदानं च शालीनिक्षुरसांस्तथा .
आरक्तवाससी श्लक्ष्णे दम्पत्योर्ललितादिने .. 26.100 ..
6.3.m: Water, gift of land, winter rice, and sugarcane juice, / two smooth reddish garments to a married couple on the day of Lalitā,

6.3.s:
saubhāgyaṃ jāyate caiva iha loke paratra ca .
brāhmaṇe vṛttasampanne surūpe ca guṇānvite .. 26.101 ..
6.3.d:
सौभाग्यं जायते चैव इह लोके परत्र च .
ब्राह्मणे वृत्तसम्पन्ने सुरूपे च गुणान्विते .. 26.101 ..
6.3.m: Good fortune arises both in this world and the next, / [when given] to a brahmin who is accomplished in good conduct, handsome, and endowed with virtues.

6.3.s:
tithau yasyāmidaṃ deyaṃ tatte rājñi vadāmyaham .
pratipatsu ca yā nārī pūrvāhṇe ca śucivratā .. 26.102 ..
6.3.d:
तिथौ यस्यामिदं देयं तत्ते राज्ञि वदाम्यहम् .
प्रतिपत्सु च या नारी पूर्वाह्णे च शुचिव्रता .. 26.102 ..
6.3.m: On which lunar day this should be given, that I tell you, O queen: / The woman who, pure in her observance, in the morning on the first lunar day,

6.3.s:
indhanaṃ brāhmaṇe dadyātprīyatāṃ me hutāśanaḥ .
tasyā janmāni ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgapratyaṅgasandhiṣu .. 26.103 ..
6.3.d:
इन्धनं ब्राह्मणे दद्यात्प्रीयतां मे हुताशनः .
तस्या जन्मानि षट्त्रिंशदङ्गप्रत्यङ्गसन्धिषु .. 26.103 ..
6.3.m: gives firewood to a brahmin, saying, 'May the Fire-Eater be pleased with me'— / for thirty-six births, in the joints of her major and minor limbs,

6.3.s:
na rajo naiva santāpo jāyate rājavallabhe .
dvitīyāyāṃ tu yā nārī navanītamudānvitā .. 26.104 ..
6.3.d:
न रजो नैव सन्तापो जायते राजवल्लभे .
द्वितीयायां तु या नारी नवनीतमुदान्विता .. 26.104 ..
6.3.m: neither impurity nor fever arises, O beloved of the king. / But the woman who, filled with joy, on the second lunar day

6.3.s:
dadāti dvijamukhyāya sukumāratanurbhavet .
lavaṇaṃ vipravaryāya tṛtīyāyāṃ prayacchati .. 26.105 ..
6.3.d:
ददाति द्विजमुख्याय सुकुमारतनुर्भवेत् .
लवणं विप्रवर्याय तृतीयायां प्रयच्छति .. 26.105 ..
6.3.m: gives butter to an eminent twice-born, will have a delicate body. / She who offers salt to an excellent vipra on the third lunar day,

6.3.s:
gaurī me prīyatāṃ devī tasyāḥ puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu .
kaumārikā patiṃ prāpya tena sārddhamumā yathā .. 26.106 ..
6.3.d:
गौरी मे प्रीयतां देवी तस्याः पुण्यफलं शृणु .
कौमारिका पतिं प्राप्य तेन सार्द्धमुमा यथा .. 26.106 ..
6.3.m: saying, 'May the goddess Gaurī be pleased with me'—listen to the fruit of her merit: / having obtained a husband while a virgin, she, like Umā with him,

6.3.s:
krīḍatyavidhavā cāpi labhate sā mahadyaśaḥ .
naktaṃ kṛtvā caturthyāṃ vai dadyādviprāya modakān .. 26.107 ..
6.3.d:
क्रीडत्यविधवा चापि लभते सा महद्यशः .
नक्तं कृत्वा चतुर्थ्यां वै दद्याद्विप्राय मोदकान् .. 26.107 ..
6.3.m: sports, never becoming a widow, and attains great fame. / Having undertaken a fast at night, she should indeed give modakas to a vipra on the fourth lunar day,

6.3.s:
prīyatāṃ mama deveśo gaṇanātho vināyakaḥ .
tasyāstena phalenāśu sarvakarmasu bhāmini .. 26.108 ..
6.3.d:
प्रीयतां मम देवेशो गणनाथो विनायकः .
तस्यास्तेन फलेनाशु सर्वकर्मसु भामिनि .. 26.108 ..
6.3.m: saying, 'May the lord of gods, Gaṇanātha, Vināyaka, be pleased with me.' / By that fruit, O spirited lady, in all undertakings

6.3.s:
vighnaṃ na jāyate kvāpi evamāha pitāmahaḥ .
pañcamīṃ tu tataḥ prāpya brāhmaṇe tiladā tu yā .. 26.109 ..
6.3.d:
विघ्नं न जायते क्वापि एवमाह पितामहः .
पञ्चमीं तु ततः प्राप्य ब्राह्मणे तिलदा तु या .. 26.109 ..
6.3.m: no obstacle ever arises for her; so said the Grandfather. / Then, having reached the fifth lunar day, she who gives sesame seeds to a brahmin,

6.3.s:
sā bhavedrūpasampannā yathā caiva tilottamā .
ṣaṣṭhyāṃ tu yā madhūkasya phaladā tu bhavetsadā .. 26.110 ..
6.3.d:
सा भवेद्रूपसम्पन्ना यथा चैव तिलोत्तमा .
षष्ठ्यां तु या मधूकस्य फलदा तु भवेत्सदा .. 26.110 ..
6.3.m: she will be endowed with beauty, just like Tilottamā. / On the sixth lunar day, she who always gives the fruit of the madhūka tree,

6.3.s:
uddiśya cāgnijaṃ devaṃ brāhmaṇe vedapārage .
tasyāḥ putro yathā skando devasaṅgheṣu cottamaḥ .. 26.111 ..
6.3.d:
उद्दिश्य चाग्निजं देवं ब्राह्मणे वेदपारगे .
तस्याः पुत्रो यथा स्कन्दो देवसङ्घेषु चोत्तमः .. 26.111 ..
6.3.m: dedicating it to the god born of fire, to a brahmin who has mastered the Vedas, / her son, like Skanda, the foremost among the hosts of gods,

6.3.s:
utpadyate mahārājaḥ sarvalokeṣu pūjitaḥ .
saptamyāṃ yā dvijaśreṣṭhaṃ suvarṇena prapūjayet .. 26.112 ..
6.3.d:
उत्पद्यते महाराजः सर्वलोकेषु पूजितः .
सप्तम्यां या द्विजश्रेष्ठं सुवर्णेन प्रपूजयेत् .. 26.112 ..
6.3.m: is born as a great king, worshipped in all worlds. / She who on the seventh lunar day worships an excellent twice-born with gold,

6.3.s:
uddiśya jagato nāthaṃ devadevaṃ divākaram .
tasya puṇyaphalaṃ yadvai kathitaṃ dvijasattamaiḥ .. 26.113 ..
6.3.d:
उद्दिश्य जगतो नाथं देवदेवं दिवाकरम् .
तस्य पुण्यफलं यद्वै कथितं द्विजसत्तमैः .. 26.113 ..
6.3.m: dedicating it to the lord of the universe, the god of gods, the Day-Maker— / the meritorious fruit of that which is declared by the best of the twice-born,

6.3.s:
tatte rājñi pravakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣvaikamanāḥ sati .
dadrūcitrakakuṣṭhāni maṇḍalāni vicarcikā .. 26.114 ..
6.3.d:
तत्ते राज्ञि प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणुष्वैकमनाः सति .
दद्रूचित्रककुष्ठानि मण्डलानि विचर्चिका .. 26.114 ..
6.3.m: that I will tell you, O queen; listen with an attentive mind, O virtuous woman: / ringworm, white leprosy, leprosy, skin-circles, and scabies

6.3.s:
na bhavantīha cāṅgeṣu pūrvakarmārjitānyapi .
kṛṣṇāṃ dhenuṃ tathāṣṭamyāṃ yā prayacchati bhāminī .. 26.115 ..
6.3.d:
न भवन्तीह चाङ्गेषु पूर्वकर्मार्जितान्यपि .
कृष्णां धेनुं तथाष्टम्यां या प्रयच्छति भामिनी .. 26.115 ..
6.3.m: do not occur here upon her limbs, even if acquired through past deeds. / And the spirited lady who gives a black cow on the eighth lunar day

6.3.s:
brāhmaṇe vṛttasampanne prīyatāṃ me maheśvaraḥ .
tasyā janmārjitaṃ pāpaṃ naśyate vibhavānvitā .. 26.116 ..
6.3.d:
ब्राह्मणे वृत्तसम्पन्ने प्रीयतां मे महेश्वरः .
तस्या जन्मार्जितं पापं नश्यते विभवान्विता .. 26.116 ..
6.3.m: to a brahmin endowed with good conduct, saying, 'May Maheśvara be pleased with me'— / the sin acquired across her births is destroyed, and she becomes endowed with wealth;

6.3.s:
jāyate nātra sandeho yasmāddānamanuttamam .
gandhadhūpaṃ tu yā nārī bhaktyā viprāya dāpayet .. 26.117 ..
6.3.d:
जायते नात्र सन्देहो यस्माद्दानमनुत्तमम् .
गन्धधूपं तु या नारी भक्त्या विप्राय दापयेत् .. 26.117 ..
6.3.m: there is no doubt about this, because this gift is unsurpassed. / The woman who devotedly causes fragrant incense to be given to a vipra

6.3.s:
kātyāyanīṃ samuddiśya navamyāṃ śṛṇu yatphalam .
tasyā bhrātā pitā putraḥ patirvā raṇamuttamam .. 26.118 ..
6.3.d:
कात्यायनीं समुद्दिश्य नवम्यां शृणु यत्फलम् .
तस्या भ्राता पिता पुत्रः पतिर्वा रणमुत्तमम् .. 26.118 ..
6.3.m: on the ninth lunar day, dedicating it to Kātyāyanī—hear what fruit ensues: / her brother, father, son, or husband, having entered an excellent battle,

6.3.s:
prāpyate naiva sīdanti tena dānena rakṣitāḥ .
ikṣudaṇḍarasaṃ devi daśamyāṃ yā prayacchati .. 26.119 ..
6.3.d:
प्राप्यते नैव सीदन्ति तेन दानेन रक्षिताः .
इक्षुदण्डरसं देवि दशम्यां या प्रयच्छति .. 26.119 ..
6.3.m: does not perish, protected by that gift. / O goddess, she who gives sugarcane juice on the tenth lunar day

6.3.s:
lokapālānsamuddiśya brāhmaṇe vyaṅgavarjite .
tena dānena sā nityaṃ sarvalokasya vallabhā .. 26.120 ..
6.3.d:
लोकपालान्समुद्दिश्य ब्राह्मणे व्यङ्गवर्जिते .
तेन दानेन सा नित्यं सर्वलोकस्य वल्लभा .. 26.120 ..
6.3.m: to a brahmin free from deformity, dedicating it to the World-Protectors, / through that gift she always becomes dear to all the world;

6.3.s:
jāyate nātra sandeha ityevaṃ śaṅkaro'bravīt .
ekādaśyāmupoṣyātha dvādaśyāmudakapradā .. 26.121 ..
6.3.d:
जायते नात्र सन्देह इत्येवं शङ्करोऽब्रवीत् .
एकादश्यामुपोष्याथ द्वादश्यामुदकप्रदा .. 26.121 ..
6.3.m: there is no doubt about this; thus spoke Śaṅkara. / Having fasted on the eleventh lunar day, she who gives water on the twelfth,

6.3.s:
nārāyaṇaṃ samuddiśya brāhmaṇe viṣṇutatpare .
sā sadā sparśasambhāṣairdrāvayedbhāvayejjanam .. 26.122 ..
6.3.d:
नारायणं समुद्दिश्य ब्राह्मणे विष्णुतत्परे .
सा सदा स्पर्शसम्भाषैर्द्रावयेद्भावयेज्जनम् .. 26.122 ..
6.3.m: dedicating it to Nārāyaṇa, to a brahmin devoted to Viṣṇu, / she would always delight and please people through touch and speech,

6.3.s:
yasmāddānaṃ maharloke hyanantamudake bhavet .
pādābhyaṅgaṃ śiro'bhyaṅgaṃ kāmamuddiśya vai dvije .. 26.123 ..
6.3.d:
यस्माद्दानं महर्लोके ह्यनन्तमुदके भवेत् .
पादाभ्यङ्गं शिरोऽभ्यङ्गं काममुद्दिश्य वै द्विजे .. 26.123 ..
6.3.m: because a gift of water becomes endless in Maharloka. / She who offers anointing of the feet and anointing of the head to a twice-born, dedicating it to Kāma,

6.3.s:
dadāti ca trayodaśyāṃ bhaktyā paramayāṅganā .
yasyāṃ yasyāṃ mṛtā jāyedbhūyo yonyāṃ tu janmani .. 26.124 ..
6.3.d:
ददाति च त्रयोदश्यां भक्त्या परमयाङ्गना .
यस्यां यस्यां मृता जायेद्भूयो योन्यां तु जन्मनि .. 26.124 ..
6.3.m: giving it on the thirteenth lunar day with supreme devotion, / into whatever womb she may be born again in a rebirth after dying,

6.3.s:
tasyāṃ tasyāṃ tu sā bharturna viyujyeta karhicit .
tathāpyevaṃ caturdaśyāṃ dadyātpātramupānahau .. 26.125 ..
6.3.d:
तस्यां तस्यां तु सा भर्तुर्न वियुज्येत कर्हिचित् .
तथाप्येवं चतुर्दश्यां दद्यात्पात्रमुपानहौ .. 26.125 ..
6.3.m: in that very one she will never be separated from her husband. / Likewise, on the fourteenth lunar day she should give a vessel and shoes

6.3.s:
brahmaṇe dharmamuddiśya tasyā lokā hyanāmayāḥ .
evaṃ ca pakṣapakṣānte śrāddhe tarpeddvijottamān .. 26.126 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रह्मणे धर्ममुद्दिश्य तस्या लोका ह्यनामयाः .
एवं च पक्षपक्षान्ते श्राद्धे तर्पेद्द्विजोत्तमान् .. 26.126 ..
6.3.m: to a brahmin, dedicating them to Dharma; her realms are free from affliction. / And thus at the end of each fortnight, she should satisfy excellent twice-born in a śrāddha;

6.3.s:
avyucchinnā sadā rājñi santatirjāyate bhuvi .
evaṃ te tithimāhātmyaṃ dānayogena bhāṣitam .. 26.127 ..
6.3.d:
अव्युच्छिन्ना सदा राज्ञि सन्ततिर्जायते भुवि .
एवं ते तिथिमाहात्म्यं दानयोगेन भाषितम् .. 26.127 ..
6.3.m: an unbroken lineage is always born [to her] on earth, O queen. / Thus has the majesty of lunar days been told to you in connection with gift-giving.

6.3.s:
tathā vanaspatīnāṃ tu ārādhanavidhiṃ śṛṇu .
jambūṃ nimbataruṃ caiva tindukaṃ madhukaṃ tathā .. 26.128 ..
6.3.d:
तथा वनस्पतीनां तु आराधनविधिं शृणु .
जम्बूं निम्बतरुं चैव तिन्दुकं मधुकं तथा .. 26.128 ..
6.3.m: Likewise, hear the rite of worshipping the lords of the forest: / The rose-apple, the neem tree, the tinduka, and the madhuka,

6.3.s:
āmraṃ cāmalakaṃ caiva śālmaliṃ vaṭapippalau .
śamībilvāmalīvṛkṣaṃ kadalīṃ pāṭalīṃ tathā .. 26.129 ..
6.3.d:
आम्रं चामलकं चैव शाल्मलिं वटपिप्पलौ .
शमीबिल्वामलीवृक्षं कदलीं पाटलीं तथा .. 26.129 ..
6.3.m: the mango, the āmalaka, the silk-cotton tree, the banyan and sacred fig, / the śamī, bilva, āmalī tree, the plantain, and the trumpet-flower tree—
