tathā caiva surāḥ sarve devā hyagnipurogamāḥ .. 37.12 ..
6.3.d:
एवं ज्ञात्वा ततश्चैव तपः कुरुत दुष्करम् .
तथा चैव सुराः सर्वे देवा ह्यग्निपुरोगमाः .. 37.12 ..
6.3.m: Knowing this, perform difficult austerity there!” / And so all the suras, the gods led by the fire god, [did].

6.3.s:
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tathyaṃ brahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ .
narmadāmāgatāḥ sarve devā hyagnipurogamāḥ .. 37.13 ..
6.3.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तथ्यं ब्रह्मणः परमेष्ठिनः .
नर्मदामागताः सर्वे देवा ह्यग्निपुरोगमाः .. 37.13 ..
6.3.m: Having heard that truthful speech of Brahmā, the supreme lord, / all the gods led by the fire god came to the Narmadā.

6.3.s:
cerurvai tatra vipulaṃ tapaḥ siddhimavāpnuvan .
tadāprabhṛti tattīrthaṃ devatīrthamanuttamam .. 37.14 ..
6.3.d:
चेरुर्वै तत्र विपुलं तपः सिद्धिमवाप्नुवन् .
तदाप्रभृति तत्तीर्थं देवतीर्थमनुत्तमम् .. 37.14 ..
6.3.m: They performed vast austerity there and attained perfection. / From that time on, that sacred ford is celebrated

6.3.s:
gīyate triṣu lokeṣu sarvapāpakṣayaṃkaram .
tatra gatvā ca yo martyo vidhinā saṃyatendriyaḥ .. 37.15 ..
6.3.d:
गीयते त्रिषु लोकेषु सर्वपापक्षयंकरम् .
तत्र गत्वा च यो मर्त्यो विधिना संयतेन्द्रियः .. 37.15 ..
6.3.m: in the three worlds as the supreme Devatīrtha, destroying all sins. / Whatever mortal goes there, with senses controlled according to the rule,

6.3.s:
snānaṃ samācaredbhaktyā sa labhenmauktikaṃ phalam .
yastu bhojayate viprāṃstasmiṃstīrthe narādhipa .. 37.16 ..
6.3.d:
स्नानं समाचरेद्भक्त्या स लभेन्मौक्तिकं फलम् .
यस्तु भोजयते विप्रांस्तस्मिंस्तीर्थे नराधिप .. 37.16 ..
6.3.m: and performs a ritual ablution with devotion, he will obtain the fruit of liberation. / And whoever feeds brahmins at that sacred ford, O king of kings,

6.3.s:
sa labhenmukhyaviprāṇāṃ phalaṃ sāhasrikaṃ nṛpa .
tatra devaśilā ramyā mahāpuṇyavivardhinī .. 37.17 ..
6.3.d:
स लभेन्मुख्यविप्राणां फलं साहस्रिकं नृप .
तत्र देवशिला रम्या महापुण्यविवर्धिनी .. 37.17 ..
6.3.m: he obtains the fruit of [feeding] a thousand foremost brahmins, O king. / There is the lovely Devaśilā, which greatly augments merit.

6.3.s:
saṃnyāsena mṛtā ye tu teṣāṃ syādakṣayā gatiḥ .
agnipraveśaṃ yaḥ kuryāttasmiṃstīrthe narādhipa .. 37.18 ..
6.3.d:
संन्यासेन मृता ये तु तेषां स्यादक्षया गतिः .
अग्निप्रवेशं यः कुर्यात्तस्मिंस्तीर्थे नराधिप .. 37.18 ..
6.3.m: Those who die through renunciation attain an imperishable state. / Whoever enters the fire at that sacred ford, O king,

6.3.s:
rudraloke vasettāvadyāvadābhūtasaṃplavam .
evaṃ snānaṃ japo homaḥ svādhyāyo devatārcanam .. 37.19 ..
6.3.d:
रुद्रलोके वसेत्तावद्यावदाभूतसंप्लवम् .
एवं स्नानं जपो होमः स्वाध्यायो देवतार्चनम् .. 37.19 ..
6.3.m: dwells in the world of Rudra until the dissolution of all beings. / Thus ritual ablution, muttered prayer, fire oblation, self-study, and the worship of deities—

6.3.s:
sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ vā'pi tatra tīrthe'kṣayaṃ bhavet .
eṣa te vidhiruddiṣṭa utpattiścaiva bhārata .. 37.20 ..
6.3.d:
सुकृतं दुष्कृतं वाऽपि तत्र तीर्थेऽक्षयं भवेत् .
एष ते विधिरुद्दिष्ट उत्पत्तिश्चैव भारत .. 37.20 ..
6.3.m: good deeds or bad deeds done at that sacred ford become imperishable. / This rule and the origin of Devatīrtha have been declared to you,

6.3.s:
devatīrthasya nikhilā yathā vai śaṅkarācchrutā .
paṭhanti ye pāpaharaṃ sarvaduḥkhavimocanam .. 37.21 ..
6.3.d:
देवतीर्थस्य निखिला यथा वै शङ्कराच्छ्रुता .
पठन्ति ये पापहरं सर्वदुःखविमोचनम् .. 37.21 ..
6.3.m: in full, O Bhārata, as heard from Śaṅkara. / Those who read this sin-destroying [narrative] that frees from all sorrow,

6.3.s:
devatīrthasya caritaṃ devalokaṃ vrajanti te .. 37.22 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe devatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma saptaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 38
6.3.d:
देवतीर्थस्य चरितं देवलोकं व्रजन्ति ते .. 37.22 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे देवतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम सप्तविंशोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 38
6.3.m:
this deed of Devatīrtha, go to the realm of the gods.
Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter, entitled “Description of the Māhātmya of the Devatīrtha,” in the Revākhaṇḍa of the Avantī section in the glorious Skandapurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 38

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gaccheta rājendra guhāvāsīti cottamam .
yatra siddho mahādevo guhāvāsī samārbudam .. 38.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेत राजेन्द्र गुहावासीति चोत्तमम् .
यत्र सिद्धो महादेवो गुहावासी समार्बुदम् .. 38.1 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then one should go to the supreme [sacred ford] named Guhāvāsin, O king of kings, / where Mahādeva, dwelling in the cave, attained perfection for one hundred million years.

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
kena kāryeṇa bho tāta mahādevo jagadguruḥ .
guhāyāmanayatkālaṃ sudīrghaṃ dvijasattama .. 38.2 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
केन कार्येण भो तात महादेवो जगद्गुरुः .
गुहायामनयत्कालं सुदीर्घं द्विजसत्तम .. 38.2 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / For what purpose, O dear one, O best of the twice-born, did Mahādeva, the teacher of the world, / spend so very long a time in a cave?

6.3.s:
etadvistarataḥ sarvaṃ kathayasva mamānagha .
śrotumicchāmyahaṃ sarvaparaṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me .. 38.3 ..
6.3.d:
एतद्विस्तरतः सर्वं कथयस्व ममानघ .
श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं सर्वपरं कौतूहलं हि मे .. 38.3 ..
6.3.m: Tell me all this in detail, O sinless one. / I wish to hear everything; indeed, great is my curiosity.

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
sādhu praśno mahārāja pṛṣṭo yo vai tvayottamaḥ .
purāṇe vistaro hyasya na śakyo hi mayādhunā .. 38.4 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
साधु प्रश्नो महाराज पृष्टो यो वै त्वयोत्तमः .
पुराणे विस्तरो ह्यस्य न शक्यो हि मयाधुना .. 38.4 ..
6.3.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / It is a good question, O great king, an excellent one that you have asked; / its full extent in the Purāṇa cannot indeed [be told] by me now.

6.3.s:
kathituṃ vṛddhabhāvatvādatīto bahukālikaḥ .
saṃkṣepāttena te tāta kathayāmi nibodha me .. 38.5 ..
6.3.d:
कथितुं वृद्धभावत्वादतीतो बहुकालिकः .
संक्षेपात्तेन ते तात कथयामि निबोध मे .. 38.5 ..
6.3.m:
to tell in detail, because of my old age, for a long time has passed.
Therefore, my dear, I tell it to you in brief; listen to me.

6.3.s:
purā kṛtayuge rājannāsīddāruvanaṃ mahat .
nānādrumalatākīrṇaṃ nānāvallyupaśobhitam .. 38.6 ..
6.3.d:
पुरा कृतयुगे राजन्नासीद्दारुवनं महत् .
नानाद्रुमलताकीर्णं नानावल्ल्युपशोभितम् .. 38.6 ..
6.3.m:
Long ago, in the Kṛtayuga, O king, there was a great forest named Dāruvana,
filled with various trees and creepers, and adorned with diverse vines.

6.3.s:
siṃhavyāghravarāhaiśca gajaiḥ khaḍgairniṣevitam .
bahupakṣiyutaṃ divyaṃ yathā caitrarathaṃ vanam .. 38.7 ..
6.3.d:
सिंहव्याघ्रवराहैश्च गजैः खड्गैर्निषेवितम् .
बहुपक्षियुतं दिव्यं यथा चैत्ररथं वनम् .. 38.7 ..
6.3.m:
It was frequented by lions, tigers, boars, elephants, and rhinoceroses,
filled with many birds, divine like the Caitraratha forest.

6.3.s:
tatra kecinmahāprājñā vasanti saṃśitavratāḥ .
vasanti parayā bhaktyā caturāśramabhāvitāḥ .. 38.8 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र केचिन्महाप्राज्ञा वसन्ति संशितव्रताः .
वसन्ति परया भक्त्या चतुराश्रमभाविताः .. 38.8 ..
6.3.m:
Certain men of great wisdom, resolute in their vows, dwelt there;
they lived with supreme devotion, devoted to the four stages of life:

6.3.s:
brahmacārī gṛhasthaśca vānaprastho yatistathā .
svadharmaniratāḥ sarve vāñchantaḥ paramaṃ padam .. 38.9 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रह्मचारी गृहस्थश्च वानप्रस्थो यतिस्तथा .
स्वधर्मनिरताः सर्वे वाञ्छन्तः परमं पदम् .. 38.9 ..
6.3.m:
The student, the householder, the forest hermit, and the ascetic,
all devoted to their own duties, desiring the highest state.

6.3.s:
tāvadvasantasamaye kasmiṃścitkāraṇāntare .
vimānastho mahādevo gacchanvai hyumayā saha .. 38.10 ..
6.3.d:
तावद्वसन्तसमये कस्मिंश्चित्कारणान्तरे .
विमानस्थो महादेवो गच्छन्वै ह्युमया सह .. 38.10 ..
6.3.m:
Meanwhile, in the spring season, for some particular reason,
Mahādeva, seated in an aerial chariot, travelling along with Umā,

6.3.s:
dadarśa toya āvāsamṛksāmayajurnāditam .
alakṣyāgatanirgamyaṃ sarvapāpakṣayaṃkaram .. 38.11 ..
6.3.d:
ददर्श तोय आवासमृक्सामयजुर्नादितम् .
अलक्ष्यागतनिर्गम्यं सर्वपापक्षयंकरम् .. 38.11 ..
6.3.m:
saw by the water a hermitage resounding with the Ṛg, Sāma, and Yajur Vedas,
whose entrance and exit were invisible, destroying all sins.

6.3.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā muditā devī harṣagaṅgadayā girā .
papraccha devadeveśaṃ śaśāṅkakṛtabhūṣaṇam .. 38.12 ..
6.3.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा मुदिता देवी हर्षगङ्गदया गिरा .
पप्रच्छ देवदेवेशं शशाङ्ककृतभूषणम् .. 38.12 ..
6.3.m:
Seeing it, the goddess was delighted and, with a voice choked with joy,
questioned the lord of the gods, who was adorned with the crescent moon:

6.3.s:
devyuvāca -
kasyāyamāśramo deva vedadhvaninināditaḥ .
yaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṣutpipāsādyaiḥ śramaiśca parihīyate .. 38.13 ..
6.3.d:
देव्युवाच -
कस्यायमाश्रमो देव वेदध्वनिनिनादितः .
यं दृष्ट्वा क्षुत्पिपासाद्यैः श्रमैश्च परिहीयते .. 38.13 ..
6.3.m:
The goddess said:
Whose hermitage is this, O god, resounding with the sound of the Vedas,
seeing which one is freed from exhaustion, hunger, thirst, and the like?

6.3.s:
maheśvara uvāca -
kiṃ tvayā na śrutaṃ devi mahādāruvanaṃ mahat .
bahuviprajano yatra gṛhadharmeṇa vartate .. 38.14 ..
6.3.d:
महेश्वर उवाच -
किं त्वया न श्रुतं देवि महादारुवनं महत् .
बहुविप्रजनो यत्र गृहधर्मेण वर्तते .. 38.14 ..
6.3.m:
Maheśvara said:
Have you not heard, O goddess, of the great Mahādāruvana,
where many brahmins live according to the duties of a householder?

6.3.s:
atra yaḥ strījanaḥ kaścidbhartṛśuśrūṣaṇe rataḥ .
nānyo devo na vai dharmo jñāyate śailanandini .. 38.15 ..
6.3.d:
अत्र यः स्त्रीजनः कश्चिद्भर्तृशुश्रूषणे रतः .
नान्यो देवो न वै धर्मो ज्ञायते शैलनन्दिनि .. 38.15 ..
6.3.m:
Whatever women there are here, they are devoted to the service of their husbands;
no other deity, nor any other duty, is known to them, O daughter of the mountain.

6.3.s:
etacchrutvā paraṃ vākyaṃ devadevena bhāṣitam .
kautūhalasamāviṣṭā śaṅkaraṃ punarabravīt .. 38.16 ..
6.3.d:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा परं वाक्यं देवदेवेन भाषितम् .
कौतूहलसमाविष्टा शङ्करं पुनरब्रवीत् .. 38.16 ..
6.3.m:
Having heard this supreme speech spoken by the god of gods,
filled with curiosity, she spoke again to Śaṅkara:

6.3.s:
yattvayoktaṃ mahādeva patidharmaratāḥ striyaḥ .
tāsāṃ tvaṃ madano bhūtvā cāritraṃ kṣobhaya prabho .. 38.17 ..
6.3.d:
यत्त्वयोक्तं महादेव पतिधर्मरताः स्त्रियः .
तासां त्वं मदनो भूत्वा चारित्रं क्षोभय प्रभो .. 38.17 ..
6.3.m:
Since you have said, O Mahādeva, that the women are devoted to the duty of fidelity to their husbands,
become Love incarnate, O Lord, and agitate their virtue!

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
yattvayoktaṃ ca vacanaṃ na hi me rocate priye .
brāhmaṇā hi mahadbhūtaṃ na caiṣāṃ vipriyaṃ caret .. 38.18 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
यत्त्वयोक्तं च वचनं न हि मे रोचते प्रिये .
ब्राह्मणा हि महद्भूतं न चैषां विप्रियं चरेत् .. 38.18 ..
6.3.m:
Īśvara said:
What you have said does not please me at all, O beloved.
Brahmins are great beings, and one should never do what is displeasing to them.

6.3.s:
manyupraharaṇā viprāścakrapraharaṇo hariḥ .
cakrātkrūrataro manyustasmādvipraṃ na kopayet .. 38.19 ..
6.3.d:
मन्युप्रहरणा विप्राश्चक्रप्रहरणो हरिः .
चक्रात्क्रूरतरो मन्युस्तस्माद्विप्रं न कोपयेत् .. 38.19 ..
6.3.m:
Brahmins have anger as their weapon; Hari has the discus as his weapon.
Anger is crueller than the discus; therefore one must not anger a brahmin.

6.3.s:
na te devā na te lokā na te nagā na cāsurāḥ .
dṛśyante triṣu lokeṣu ye tairdṛṣṭairna nāśitāḥ .. 38.20 ..
6.3.d:
न ते देवा न ते लोका न ते नगा न चासुराः .
दृश्यन्ते त्रिषु लोकेषु ये तैर्दृष्टैर्न नाशिताः .. 38.20 ..
6.3.m:
No gods, no worlds, no mountains, nor asuras
are seen in the three worlds who have not been destroyed by their glance.

6.3.s:
teṣāṃ mokṣastathā svargo bhūmirmartye phalāni ca .
yeṣāṃ tuṣṭā mahābhāgā brāhmaṇāḥ kṣitidevatāḥ .. 38.21 ..
6.3.d:
तेषां मोक्षस्तथा स्वर्गो भूमिर्मर्त्ये फलानि च .
येषां तुष्टा महाभागा ब्राह्मणाः क्षितिदेवताः .. 38.21 ..
6.3.m:
For them there is liberation and heaven, and the fruits on the mortal earth,
with whom the fortunate brahmins, deities of the earth, are pleased.

6.3.s:
evaṃ jñātvā mahābhāge asadgrāhaṃ parityaja .
tatra loke viruddhaṃ vai kupyante yena vai dvijāḥ .. 38.22 ..
6.3.d:
एवं ज्ञात्वा महाभागे असद्ग्राहं परित्यज .
तत्र लोके विरुद्धं वै कुप्यन्ते येन वै द्विजाः .. 38.22 ..
6.3.m:
Knowing this, O fortunate one, abandon this improper obstinacy,
which is forbidden in this world and by which the twice-born would be angered.

6.3.s:
devyuvāca -
nāhaṃ te dayitā deva nāhaṃ te vaśavartinī .
akṛtvādhaśva vai tāsāṃ mānaṃ surasupūjitam .. 38.23 ..
6.3.d:
देव्युवाच -
नाहं ते दयिता देव नाहं ते वशवर्तिनी .
अकृत्वाधश्व वै तासां मानं सुरसुपूजितम् .. 38.23 ..
6.3.m:
The goddess said:
I am not your beloved, O god, nor am I obedient to you,
if you do not bring low their pride, which is well-honoured by the gods.

6.3.s:
lokaloke mahādeva aśakyaṃ nāsti te prabho .
kriyatāṃ mama caivaikametatkāryaṃ surottama .. 38.24 ..
6.3.d:
लोकलोके महादेव अशक्यं नास्ति ते प्रभो .
क्रियतां मम चैवैकमेतत्कार्यं सुरोत्तम .. 38.24 ..
6.3.m:
In this world and beyond, O Mahādeva, there is nothing impossible for you, O Lord;
perform this one task for me, O best of gods!

6.3.s:
evamukto mahādevo devyā vākyahite rataḥ .
kṛtvā kāpālikaṃ rūpaṃ yayau dāruvanaṃ prati .. 38.25 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्तो महादेवो देव्या वाक्यहिते रतः .
कृत्वा कापालिकं रूपं ययौ दारुवनं प्रति .. 38.25 ..
6.3.m:
Thus addressed, Mahādeva, devoted to fulfilling the goddess's word,
assumed the form of a Kāpālika and went toward Dāruvana,

6.3.s:
mahāhitajaṭājūṭaṃ niyamya śaśibhūṣaṇam .
kaṇṭhatrāṇaṃ paraṃ kṛtvā dhārayan karṇakuṇḍale .. 38.26 ..
6.3.d:
महाहितजटाजूटं नियम्य शशिभूषणम् .
कण्ठत्राणं परं कृत्वा धारयन् कर्णकुण्डले .. 38.26 ..
6.3.m:
binding his mass of matted hair, wearing the moon as an ornament,
with his throat wrapped securely, wearing earrings in his ears,

6.3.s:
vyāghracarmaparīdhāno mekhalāhārabhūṣitaḥ .
nūpuradhvaninighoṣaiḥ kampayan vai vasuṃdharām .. 38.27 ..
6.3.d:
व्याघ्रचर्मपरीधानो मेखलाहारभूषितः .
नूपुरध्वनिनिघोषैः कम्पयन् वै वसुंधराम् .. 38.27 ..
6.3.m:
clad in a tiger-skin, adorned with a girdle and garlands,
shaking the earth with the jingle of his anklets,

6.3.s:
mahānūrddhvajaṭāmālī kṛttibhasmānulepanaḥ .
kṛtvā haste kapālaṃ tu brahmaṇaśca mahātmanaḥ .. 38.28 ..
6.3.d:
महानूर्द्ध्वजटामाली कृत्तिभस्मानुलेपनः .
कृत्वा हस्ते कपालं तु ब्रह्मणश्च महात्मनः .. 38.28 ..
6.3.m:
bearing high-piled matted hair, smeared with hide and ashes,
holding in his hand the skull of the great-souled Brahmā,

6.3.s:
mahāḍamarughoṣeṇa kampayan vai vasuṃdharām .
prabhātasamaye prāpto mahādāruvanaṃ prati .. 38.29 ..
6.3.d:
महाडमरुघोषेण कम्पयन् वै वसुंधराम् .
प्रभातसमये प्राप्तो महादारुवनं प्रति .. 38.29 ..
6.3.m:
making the earth tremble with the roar of his great ḍamaru drum,
he arrived at Mahādāruvana at the time of dawn.

6.3.s:
tāvatpuṇyajanaḥ sarvapuṣpapatraphalārthikaḥ .
nirgato bahubhiḥ sārddhaṃ pavamānaḥ samantataḥ .. 38.30 ..
6.3.d:
तावत्पुण्यजनः सर्वपुष्पपत्रफलार्थिकः .
निर्गतो बहुभिः सार्द्धं पवमानः समन्ततः .. 38.30 ..
6.3.m:
At that time, all those virtuous people, seeking flowers, leaves, and fruits,
had gone out everywhere with many others, purifying [the forest].

6.3.s:
taddṛṣṭvā mahadāścaryaṃ rūpaṃ devasya bhārata .
yuvatīnāṃ manastāsāṃ kāmena kaluṣīkṛtam .. 38.31 ..
6.3.d:
तद्दृष्ट्वा महदाश्चर्यं रूपं देवस्य भारत .
युवतीनां मनस्तासां कामेन कलुषीकृतम् .. 38.31 ..
6.3.m:
Seeing that greatly wondrous form of the god, O descendant of Bharata,
the minds of those young women became tainted with passion.

6.3.s:
śobhanaṃ puruṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvā api varāṅganāḥ .
kledabhāvaṃ tato jagmurmudā dāruvanastriyaḥ .. 38.32 ..
6.3.d:
शोभनं पुरुषं दृष्ट्वा सर्वा अपि वराङ्गनाः .
क्लेदभावं ततो जग्मुर्मुदा दारुवनस्त्रियः .. 38.32 ..
6.3.m:
Beholding that handsome man, all those excellent women,
the women of Dāruvana, were overcome with longing and lustful desire.

6.3.s:
vikārā bahavastāsāṃ devaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahādbhutam .
saṃjātā viprapatnīnāṃ tadā tāsu narottama .. 38.33 ..
6.3.d:
विकारा बहवस्तासां देवं दृष्ट्वा महाद्भुतम् .
संजाता विप्रपत्नीनां तदा तासु नरोत्तम .. 38.33 ..
6.3.m:
Many emotional perturbations arose in those wives of brahmins,
upon seeing that greatly wondrous god, O best of men.

6.3.s:
paridhānaṃ na jānanti kāściddṛṣṭvā varāṅganāḥ .
uttarīyaṃ tathā cānyā mahāmohasamanvitāḥ .. 38.34 ..
6.3.d:
परिधानं न जानन्ति काश्चिद्दृष्ट्वा वराङ्गनाः .
उत्तरीयं तथा चान्या महामोहसमन्विताः .. 38.34 ..
6.3.m:
Some excellent women, upon seeing him, were not aware of their lower garments;
others, seized by great infatuation, were unaware of their upper garments.

6.3.s:
keśabhāraparibhraṣṭā kācidevāsanotthitā .
dātukāmā tadā bhaikṣyaṃ ceṣṭituṃ naiva cāśakat .. 38.35 ..
6.3.d:
केशभारपरिभ्रष्टा काचिदेवासनोत्थिता .
दातुकामा तदा भैक्ष्यं चेष्टितुं नैव चाशकत् .. 38.35 ..
6.3.m:
One woman, her mass of hair dishevelled, got up from her seat,
wishing to give alms, but was unable to move.

6.3.s:
kāciddṛṣṭvā mahādevaṃ rūpayauvanagarvitā .
utsaṅge saṃsthitaṃ bālaṃ vismṛtā pāyituṃ stanam .. 38.36 ..
6.3.d:
काचिद्दृष्ट्वा महादेवं रूपयौवनगर्विता .
उत्सङ्गे संस्थितं बालं विस्मृता पायितुं स्तनम् .. 38.36 ..
6.3.m:
Another, proud of her beauty and youth, upon seeing Mahādeva,
forgot to nurse the child resting on her lap.

6.3.s:
kāmabāṇahatā cānyā bāhubhyāṃ pīḍya sustanau .
niḥśvasantī tadā coṣṇaṃ na kiṃcitpratijalpati .. 38.37 ..
6.3.d:
कामबाणहता चान्या बाहुभ्यां पीड्य सुस्तनौ .
निःश्वसन्ती तदा चोष्णं न किंचित्प्रतिजल्पति .. 38.37 ..
6.3.m:
Another, struck by the arrows of love, squeezing her shapely breasts with her arms,
sighed hot sighs and did not answer anything.

6.3.s:
evaṃ saṃkṣobhya taṃ sarvaṃ strījanaṃ parameśvaraḥ .
jagāma tatra vai tāsāṃ kṣobhaṃ kṛtvā mahādbhutam .. 38.38 ..
6.3.d:
एवं संक्षोभ्य तं सर्वं स्त्रीजनं परमेश्वरः .
जगाम तत्र वै तासां क्षोभं कृत्वा महाद्भुतम् .. 38.38 ..
6.3.m:
Having thus perturbed all those women, the supreme lord,
having caused an extraordinary agitation among them, departed thence.

6.3.s:
tāvatte brāhmaṇāḥ sarve bhramitvā kānanaṃ mahat .
āgatāḥ svagṛhe dārān dadṛśuśca hataujasaḥ .. 38.39 ..
6.3.d:
तावत्ते ब्राह्मणाः सर्वे भ्रमित्वा काननं महत् .
आगताः स्वगृहे दारान् ददृशुश्च हतौजसः .. 38.39 ..
6.3.m:
Meanwhile, all those brahmins, having wandered through the great forest,
returned to their own homes and saw their wives devoid of luster.

6.3.s:
yāsāṃ pūrvatarā bhaktiḥ pātivratye patīnprati .
calitāstā viditvāśu nirjagmurdvijasattamāḥ .. 38.40 ..
6.3.d:
यासां पूर्वतरा भक्तिः पातिव्रत्ये पतीन्प्रति .
चलितास्ता विदित्वाशु निर्जग्मुर्द्विजसत्तमाः .. 38.40 ..
6.3.m:
Those whose devotion to their husbands in marital fidelity had been supreme—
knowing that they had wavered, the best of the twice-born quickly rushed out.

6.3.s:
saṃvidaṃ paramāṃ kṛtvā jñātvā devaṃ maheśvaram .
kṣobhayitvā manastāsāṃ tataścādarśanaṃ gatam .. 38.41 ..
6.3.d:
संविदं परमां कृत्वा ज्ञात्वा देवं महेश्वरम् .
क्षोभयित्वा मनस्तासां ततश्चादर्शनं गतम् .. 38.41 ..
6.3.m:
Reaching a firm understanding, they knew that it was the god Maheśvara
who, having agitated their minds, had then disappeared from sight.

6.3.s:
krodhāviṣṭo dvijaḥ kaściddaṇḍamudyamya dhāvati .
kalmāṣayaṣṭimanye ca tathānye darbhamuṣṭikām .. 38.42 ..
6.3.d:
क्रोधाविष्टो द्विजः कश्चिद्दण्डमुद्यम्य धावति .
कल्माषयष्टिमन्ये च तथान्ये दर्भमुष्टिकाम् .. 38.42 ..
6.3.m:
One twice-born, filled with rage, ran raising a stick;
others with spotted staffs, and others with a handful of darbha grass.

6.3.s:
itaścetaśca te sarve bhramitvā kānanaṃ nṛpa .
ekībhūtvā mahātmāno vyājahruśca ruṣā giram .. 38.43 ..
6.3.d:
इतश्चेतश्च ते सर्वे भ्रमित्वा काननं नृप .
एकीभूत्वा महात्मानो व्याजह्रुश्च रुषा गिरम् .. 38.43 ..
6.3.m:
Wandering here and there through the forest, O king,
those great-souled ones gathered together and uttered words in anger:

6.3.s:
yadidaṃ ca hutaṃ kiṃcidguravastoṣitā yadi .
tena satyena devasya liṅgaṃ patatu cottamam .. 38.44 ..
6.3.d:
यदिदं च हुतं किंचिद्गुरवस्तोषिता यदि .
तेन सत्येन देवस्य लिङ्गं पततु चोत्तमम् .. 38.44 ..
6.3.m:
“If any offering has been made by us, if our teachers have been satisfied,
by that truth, let the god's excellent liṅga fall down!

6.3.s:
āśramādāśramaṃ sarve na tyajāmo vidhikramāt .
tena satyena devasya liṅgaṃ patatu bhūtale .. 38.45 ..
6.3.d:
आश्रमादाश्रमं सर्वे न त्यजामो विधिक्रमात् .
तेन सत्येन देवस्य लिङ्गं पततु भूतले .. 38.45 ..
6.3.m:
If we all do not abandon [our duties] from stage to stage according to the rules,
by that truth, let the god's liṅga fall to the ground!”

6.3.s:
evaṃ satyaprabhāvena triruktena dvijanmanām .
śivasya paśyato liṅgaṃ patitaṃ dharaṇītale .. 38.46 ..
6.3.d:
एवं सत्यप्रभावेन त्रिरुक्तेन द्विजन्मनाम् .
शिवस्य पश्यतो लिङ्गं पतितं धरणीतले .. 38.46 ..
6.3.m:
Thus, by the power of truth spoken three times by the twice-born,
as Śiva watched, his liṅga fell upon the surface of the earth.

6.3.s:
hāhākāro mahānāsīllokāloke'pi bhārata .
devasya patite liṅge jagataśca mahākṣaye .. 38.47 ..
6.3.d:
हाहाकारो महानासील्लोकालोकेऽपि भारत .
देवस्य पतिते लिङ्गे जगतश्च महाक्षये .. 38.47 ..
6.3.m:
A great cry of distress arose even in the Lokāloka mountains, O descendant of Bharata,
when the god's liṅga fell and the great destruction of the world [commenced].

6.3.s:
patamānasya liṅgasya śabdo'bhūcca sudāruṇaḥ .
ulkāpātā diśāṃ hāhā bhūmikampāśca dāruṇāḥ .. 38.48 ..
6.3.d:
पतमानस्य लिङ्गस्य शब्दोऽभूच्च सुदारुणः .
उल्कापाता दिशां हाहा भूमिकम्पाश्च दारुणाः .. 38.48 ..
6.3.m: As the liṅga fell, there arose a dreadful sound, / meteors fell, the quarters cried in lamentation, and fearful earthquakes occurred.

6.3.s:
patanti parvatāgrāṇi śoṣaṃ yānti ca sāgarāḥ .
devasya patite liṅge devā vimanaso'bhavan .. 38.49 ..
6.3.d:
पतन्ति पर्वताग्राणि शोषं यान्ति च सागराः .
देवस्य पतिते लिङ्गे देवा विमनसोऽभवन् .. 38.49 ..
6.3.m: Mountain peaks fell, and oceans dried up; / when the god's liṅga fell, the gods were dejected in mind.

6.3.s:
sametya sahitāḥ sarve brahmāṇaṃ parameṣṭhinam .
kṛtāñjalipuṭāḥ sarve stuvanti vividhaiḥ stavaiḥ .. 38.50 ..
6.3.d:
समेत्य सहिताः सर्वे ब्रह्माणं परमेष्ठिनम् .
कृताञ्जलिपुटाः सर्वे स्तुवन्ति विविधैः स्तवैः .. 38.50 ..
6.3.m: Assembling together, all approached Brahmā Parameṣṭhin, / and with folded hands, all praised him with various hymns.

6.3.s:
tatastuṣṭo jagannāthaścaturvadanapaṅkajaḥ .
ārtānprāha surānsarvānmā viṣādaṃ gamiṣyatha .. 38.51 ..
6.3.d:
ततस्तुष्टो जगन्नाथश्चतुर्वदनपङ्कजः .
आर्तान्प्राह सुरान्सर्वान्मा विषादं गमिष्यथ .. 38.51 ..
6.3.m: Then the lord of the universe, whose face is a fourfold lotus, pleased, / spoke to all the distressed gods: “Do not fall into despondency!

6.3.s:
brahmaśāpābhibhūto'sau devadevastrilocanaḥ .
tuṣṭaistaistapasā yuktaiḥ punarmokṣaṃ gamiṣyati .. 38.52 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रह्मशापाभिभूतोऽसौ देवदेवस्त्रिलोचनः .
तुष्टैस्तैस्तपसा युक्तैः पुनर्मोक्षं गमिष्यति .. 38.52 ..
6.3.m: This three-eyed god of gods has been overpowered by a brahmin's curse; / when they, endowed with austerity, are satisfied, he will attain release once more.”

6.3.s:
etacchrutvā yayurdevā yathāgatamarindama .
bhāvayitvā tataḥ sarve munayaścaiva bhārata .. 38.53 ..
6.3.d:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा ययुर्देवा यथागतमरिन्दम .
भावयित्वा ततः सर्वे मुनयश्चैव भारत .. 38.53 ..
6.3.m: Hearing this, the gods went as they had come, O conqueror of foes; / then all the sages, having deliberated, O Bhārata,

6.3.s:
viśvāmitravasiṣṭhādyā jābāliratha kaśyapaḥ .
sametya sahitāḥ sarve tamūcustripurāntakam .. 38.54 ..
6.3.d:
विश्वामित्रवसिष्ठाद्या जाबालिरथ कश्यपः .
समेत्य सहिताः सर्वे तमूचुस्त्रिपुरान्तकम् .. 38.54 ..
6.3.m: Viśvāmitra, Vasiṣṭha and others, and then Jābāli and Kaśyapa, / assembling together, all spoke to that destroyer of Tripura:

6.3.s:
brahmatejo hi balavaddvijānāṃ hi sureśvara .
kṣāntiyuktastapastaptvā bhaviṣyasi gataklamaḥ .. 38.55 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रह्मतेजो हि बलवद्द्विजानां हि सुरेश्वर .
क्षान्तियुक्तस्तपस्तप्त्वा भविष्यसि गतक्लमः .. 38.55 ..
6.3.m: “The brahmic power of the twice-born is indeed mighty, O Lord of the gods; / endowed with forbearance and having performed austerity, you will be freed from exhaustion.

6.3.s:
yataḥ kṣobhādṛṣīṇāṃ ca tadevaṃ liṅgamuttamam .
patitaṃ te mahādeva na tatpūjyaṃ bhaviṣyati .. 38.56 ..
6.3.d:
यतः क्षोभादृषीणां च तदेवं लिङ्गमुत्तमम् .
पतितं ते महादेव न तत्पूज्यं भविष्यति .. 38.56 ..
6.3.m: Since this excellent liṅga of yours has thus fallen / through the agitation of the seers, O Mahādeva, it would not be worshipped.

6.3.s:
na tacchreyo'gnihotreṇa nāgniṣṭomena labhyate .
prāpnuvanti ca yacchreyo mānavā liṅgapūjane .. 38.57 ..
6.3.d:
न तच्छ्रेयोऽग्निहोत्रेण नाग्निष्टोमेन लभ्यते .
प्राप्नुवन्ति च यच्छ्रेयो मानवा लिङ्गपूजने .. 38.57 ..
6.3.m: That good is not obtained by the agnihotra nor by the agniṣṭoma / which human beings obtain in worshipping the liṅga.

6.3.s:
devadānavayakṣāṇāṃ gandharvoragarakṣasām .
vacanena tu viprāṇāmetatpūjyaṃ bhaviṣyati .. 38.58 ..
6.3.d:
देवदानवयक्षाणां गन्धर्वोरगरक्षसाम् .
वचनेन तु विप्राणामेतत्पूज्यं भविष्यति .. 38.58 ..
6.3.m: By the word of the brahmins, it shall be worthy of worship / for gods, dānavas, yakṣas, gandharvas, serpents, and rākṣasas.

6.3.s:
brahmaviṣṇvindracandrāṇāmetatpūjyaṃ bhaviṣyati .
yatphalaṃ tava liṅgasya iha loke paratra ca .. 38.59 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रह्मविष्ण्विन्द्रचन्द्राणामेतत्पूज्यं भविष्यति .
यत्फलं तव लिङ्गस्य इह लोके परत्र च .. 38.59 ..
6.3.m: It shall be worthy of worship for Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Indra, and Candra, / [granting] whatever fruit belongs to your liṅga here in this world and in the beyond.”

6.3.s:
evamukto jagannāthaḥ praṇipatya dvijottamān .
mudā paramayā yuktaḥ kṛtāñjalirabhāṣata .. 38.60 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्तो जगन्नाथः प्रणिपत्य द्विजोत्तमान् .
मुदा परमया युक्तः कृताञ्जलिरभाषत .. 38.60 ..
6.3.m: Thus addressed, the lord of the universe bowed down to the best of the twice-born, / and, filled with supreme joy, spoke with folded hands:

6.3.s:
brāhmaṇā jaṅgamaṃ tīrthaṃ nirjalaṃ sārvakāmikam .
yeṣāṃ vākyodakenaiva śudhyanti malino janāḥ .. 38.61 ..
6.3.d:
ब्राह्मणा जङ्गमं तीर्थं निर्जलं सार्वकामिकम् .
येषां वाक्योदकेनैव शुध्यन्ति मलिनो जनाः .. 38.61 ..
6.3.m: “Brahmins are a moving tīrtha, waterless, fulfilling all desires, / by the water of whose very words impure people are cleansed.

6.3.s:
na tatkṣetraṃ na tattīrthamūṣaraṃ puṣkarāṇi ca .
brāhmaṇe manyumutpādya yatra gatvā sa śudhyati .. 38.62 ..
6.3.d:
न तत्क्षेत्रं न तत्तीर्थमूषरं पुष्कराणि च .
ब्राह्मणे मन्युमुत्पाद्य यत्र गत्वा स शुध्यति .. 38.62 ..
6.3.m: There is no kṣetra, no tīrtha, no barren ground, nor Puṣkara waters / where one may go and be purified after causing anger in a brahmin.

6.3.s:
na tacchāstraṃ yanna viprapraṇītaṃ na taddānaṃ yanna viprapradeyam .
na tatsaukhyaṃ yannavipraprasādānna tadduḥkhaṃ yanna vipraprakopāt .. 38.63 ..
6.3.d:
न तच्छास्त्रं यन्न विप्रप्रणीतं न तद्दानं यन्न विप्रप्रदेयम् .
न तत्सौख्यं यन्नविप्रप्रसादान्न तद्दुःखं यन्न विप्रप्रकोपात् .. 38.63 ..
6.3.m: There is no treatise not composed by brahmins, no gift not to be given to brahmins; / there is no happiness not from the favor of brahmins, no sorrow not from the wrath of brahmins.

6.3.s:
pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni gaṅgādyāḥ saritastathā .
ekasya vipravākyasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm .. 38.64 ..
6.3.d:
पृथिव्यां यानि तीर्थानि गङ्गाद्याः सरितस्तथा .
एकस्य विप्रवाक्यस्य कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीम् .. 38.64 ..
6.3.m: Whatever tīrthas there are on earth, and rivers such as the Gaṅgā, / are not worth a sixteenth part of a single word of a brahmin.”

6.3.s:
abhinandya dvijānsarvānanujñāto maharṣibhiḥ .
tato'gamattadā devo narmadātaṭamuttamam .. 38.65 ..
6.3.d:
अभिनन्द्य द्विजान्सर्वाननुज्ञातो महर्षिभिः .
ततोऽगमत्तदा देवो नर्मदातटमुत्तमम् .. 38.65 ..
6.3.m: Having cheered all the twice-born and permitted by the great seers, / the god then went to the excellent bank of the Narmadā.

6.3.s:
paramaṃ vratamāsthāya guhāvāsī samārbudam .
tapaścacāra bhagavāñjapasnānarataḥ sadā .. 38.66 ..
6.3.d:
परमं व्रतमास्थाय गुहावासी समार्बुदम् .
तपश्चचार भगवाञ्जपस्नानरतः सदा .. 38.66 ..
6.3.m: Undertaking a supreme vow, dwelling in a cave for a hundred million years, / the Lord performed austerity, ever devoted to recitation and ritual ablutions.

6.3.s:
samāpte niyame tāta sthāpayitvā maheśvaram .
vandyamānaḥ suraiḥ sārddhaṃ kailāsamagamatprabhuḥ .. 38.67 ..
6.3.d:
समाप्ते नियमे तात स्थापयित्वा महेश्वरम् .
वन्द्यमानः सुरैः सार्द्धं कैलासमगमत्प्रभुः .. 38.67 ..
6.3.m: When the religious observance was completed, dear one, having installed Maheśvara, / the Lord, praised by the gods, went to Kailāsa.

6.3.s:
narmadāyāstaṭe tena sthāpitaḥ parameśvaraḥ .
tenaiva kāraṇenāsau narmadeśvara ucyate .. 38.68 ..
6.3.d:
नर्मदायास्तटे तेन स्थापितः परमेश्वरः .
तेनैव कारणेनासौ नर्मदेश्वर उच्यते .. 38.68 ..
6.3.m: Parameśvara was installed by him on the bank of the Narmadā; / for that very reason he is called Narmadeśvara.

6.3.s:
yo'rcayennarmadeśānaṃ yatirvai saṃjitendriyaḥ .
snātvā caiva mahādevamaśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet .. 38.69 ..
6.3.d:
योऽर्चयेन्नर्मदेशानं यतिर्वै संजितेन्द्रियः .
स्नात्वा चैव महादेवमश्वमेधफलं लभेत् .. 38.69 ..
6.3.m: Whatever ascetic with restrained senses worships Narmadeśvara / and Mahādeva after bathing, shall obtain the fruit of an horse sacrifice.

6.3.s:
dadāti yaḥ pitṛbhyastu tilapuṣpakuśodakam .
triḥsaptapūrvajāstasya svarge modanti pāṇḍava .. 38.70 ..
6.3.d:
ददाति यः पितृभ्यस्तु तिलपुष्पकुशोदकम् .
त्रिःसप्तपूर्वजास्तस्य स्वर्गे मोदन्ति पाण्डव .. 38.70 ..
6.3.m: He who offers water with sesame, flowers, and kuśa grass to the ancestors— / his ancestors up to twenty-one generations rejoice in heaven, O Pāṇḍava.

6.3.s:
yastu bhojayate viprāṃstasmiṃstīrthe narādhipa .
pāyasaṃ ghṛtamiśraṃ tu sa labhetkoṭijaṃ phalam .. 38.71 ..
6.3.d:
यस्तु भोजयते विप्रांस्तस्मिंस्तीर्थे नराधिप .
पायसं घृतमिश्रं तु स लभेत्कोटिजं फलम् .. 38.71 ..
6.3.m: And he who feeds brahmins at that tīrtha, O king, / with milk-rice mixed with ghee, obtains a fruit multiplied ten million times.

6.3.s:
suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ vāpi brāhmaṇebhyo yudhiṣṭhira .
dadāti toyamadhyasthaḥ so'gniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet .. 38.72 ..
6.3.d:
सुवर्णं रजतं वापि ब्राह्मणेभ्यो युधिष्ठिर .
ददाति तोयमध्यस्थः सोऽग्निष्टोमफलं लभेत् .. 38.72 ..
6.3.m: Or he who, standing in the middle of the water, gives gold or silver / to brahmins, O Yudhiṣṭhira, obtains the fruit of an agniṣṭoma.

6.3.s:
aṣṭamyāṃvā caturdaśyāṃ nirāhāro vasettu yaḥ .
narmadeśvaramāsādya prāpnuyājjanmanaḥ phalam .. 38.73 ..
6.3.d:
अष्टम्यांवा चतुर्दश्यां निराहारो वसेत्तु यः .
नर्मदेश्वरमासाद्य प्राप्नुयाज्जन्मनः फलम् .. 38.73 ..
6.3.m: He who, fasting, dwells there on the eighth or fourteenth day, / having approached Narmadeśvara, shall attain the fruit of life.

6.3.s:
agnipraveśaṃ yaḥ kuryāttasmiṃstīrthe narādhipa .
tasya vyādhibhayaṃ na syātsaptajanmasu bhārata .. 38.74 ..
6.3.d:
अग्निप्रवेशं यः कुर्यात्तस्मिंस्तीर्थे नराधिप .
तस्य व्याधिभयं न स्यात्सप्तजन्मसु भारत .. 38.74 ..
6.3.m: He who performs entry into fire at that tīrtha, O king, / shall have no fear of disease for seven births, O Bhārata.

6.3.s:
anāśakaṃ tu yaḥ kuryāttasmiṃstīrthe narādhipa .
anivartikā gatistasya rudraloke bhaviṣyati .. 38.75 ..
6.3.d:
अनाशकं तु यः कुर्यात्तस्मिंस्तीर्थे नराधिप .
अनिवर्तिका गतिस्तस्य रुद्रलोके भविष्यति .. 38.75 ..
6.3.m: And he who performs fasting unto death at that tīrtha, O king, / shall attain an irreversible state in the world of Rudra.

6.3.s:
eṣa te vidhiruddiṣṭastasyotpattirnarottama .
purāṇe vihitā tāta saṃjñā tasya tu vistarāt .. 38.76 ..
6.3.d:
एष ते विधिरुद्दिष्टस्तस्योत्पत्तिर्नरोत्तम .
पुराणे विहिता तात संज्ञा तस्य तु विस्तरात् .. 38.76 ..
6.3.m: This rule has been declared to you, along with its origin, O best of men; / its designation has been laid down at length in the Purāṇa, dear one.

6.3.s:
etaṃ kīrtayate yastu narmadeśvarasambhavam .
bhaktyā śṛṇoti ca naraḥ so'pi snānaphalaṃ labhet .. 38.77 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe narmadāmāhātmye narmadeśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmāṣṭatriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 39
6.3.d:
एतं कीर्तयते यस्तु नर्मदेश्वरसम्भवम् .
भक्त्या शृणोति च नरः सोऽपि स्नानफलं लभेत् .. 38.77 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे नर्मदामाहात्म्ये नर्मदेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामाष्टत्रिंशोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 39
6.3.m:
A man who recites this origin of Narmadeśvara, / or listens to it with devotion, shall also obtain the fruit of a ritual ablution.
Thus ends the thirty-eighth chapter, entitled the Description of the Māhātmya of the Tīrtha of Narmadeśvara, in the Narmadāmāhātmya of the Revākhaṇḍa, in the fifth Avantī section, in the Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses, the glorious Skandapurāṇa.
Chapter 39

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gacchecca rājendra kapilātīrthamuttamam .
snānamātrānnaro bhaktyā mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ .. 39.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेच्च राजेन्द्र कपिलातीर्थमुत्तमम् .
स्नानमात्रान्नरो भक्त्या मुच्यते सर्वकिल्बिषैः .. 39.1 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then one should go, O best of kings, to the excellent Kapilātīrtha; / by mere bathing with devotion, a man is freed from all sins.

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
āścaryabhūtaṃ lokeṣu kathitaṃ dvijasattama .
narmadeśvaramāhātmyaṃ kāpilaṃ kathayasva me .. 39.2 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
आश्चर्यभूतं लोकेषु कथितं द्विजसत्तम .
नर्मदेश्वरमाहात्म्यं कापिलं कथयस्व मे .. 39.2 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / The māhātmya of Narmadeśvara, marvelous in the worlds, has been told, O best of the twice-born; / tell me about the māhātmya of Kapila.

6.3.s:
yasmin kāle'tha sambandhe utpannaṃ tīrthamuttamam .
sarvapāpaharaṃ puṇyaṃ tīrthaṃ jātaṃ kathaṃ prabho .. 39.3 ..
6.3.d:
यस्मिन् कालेऽथ सम्बन्धे उत्पन्नं तीर्थमुत्तमम् .
सर्वपापहरं पुण्यं तीर्थं जातं कथं प्रभो .. 39.3 ..
6.3.m: At what time and in what connection was this excellent tīrtha produced? / How did this holy tīrtha that removes all sins come to be, O lord?

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
śṛṇu vakṣye'dya te rājankapilātīrthamuttamam .
yena te vismayaḥ sarvaḥ śrutvā gacchati bhārata .. 39.4 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
शृणु वक्ष्येऽद्य ते राजन्कपिलातीर्थमुत्तमम् .
येन ते विस्मयः सर्वः श्रुत्वा गच्छति भारत .. 39.4 ..
6.3.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Listen, O king, today I shall tell you of the excellent Kapilātīrtha, / hearing which all your wonder will depart, O Bhārata.

6.3.s:
purā kṛtayugasyādau brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ .
utpādayitvā sakalaṃ bhūtagrāmaṃ caturvidham .. 39.5 ..
6.3.d:
पुरा कृतयुगस्यादौ ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः .
उत्पादयित्वा सकलं भूतग्रामं चतुर्विधम् .. 39.5 ..
6.3.m: Formerly, at the beginning of the Kṛta age, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, / having generated the entire fourfold host of beings,

6.3.s:
japahomaparo bhaktyā kṣaṇaṃ dhyātvā ca tiṣṭhati .
jvalamānāttu kapilā tāvatkuṇḍātsamutthitā .. 39.6 ..
6.3.d:
जपहोमपरो भक्त्या क्षणं ध्यात्वा च तिष्ठति .
ज्वलमानात्तु कपिला तावत्कुण्डात्समुत्थिता .. 39.6 ..
6.3.m: devoted to recitation and oblations, meditated for a moment with devotion and remained still; / just then, a tawny cow arose from the blazing fire pit,

6.3.s:
agnijvālojjvalaiḥ śṛṅgaistrinetrā supayasvinī .
agnipūrṇā hyagnimukhā agnighrāṇāgnilocanā .. 39.7 ..
6.3.d:
अग्निज्वालोज्ज्वलैः शृङ्गैस्त्रिनेत्रा सुपयस्विनी .
अग्निपूर्णा ह्यग्निमुखा अग्निघ्राणाग्निलोचना .. 39.7 ..
6.3.m: with horns radiant with tongues of fire, three-eyed, rich in milk, / full of fire, with a face of fire, with a scent of fire, with eyes of fire,

6.3.s:
agnikhurā hyagnipṛṣṭhā agnisarvāṅgasaṃsthitiḥ .
sarvalakṣaṇasampūrṇā ghaṇṭālalitaniḥsvanā .. 39.8 ..
6.3.d:
अग्निखुरा ह्यग्निपृष्ठा अग्निसर्वाङ्गसंस्थितिः .
सर्वलक्षणसम्पूर्णा घण्टाललितनिःस्वना .. 39.8 ..
6.3.m: with hooves of fire, a back of fire, and her whole body abiding in fire, / complete with all auspicious marks, with the charming sound of bells.

6.3.s:
dṛṣṭvā tu tāṃ mahābhāgāṃ kapilāṃ kuṇḍamadhyagām .
brahmā lokagurustāta praṇamyedamuvāca ha .. 39.9 ..
6.3.d:
दृष्ट्वा तु तां महाभागां कपिलां कुण्डमध्यगाम् .
ब्रह्मा लोकगुरुस्तात प्रणम्येदमुवाच ह .. 39.9 ..
6.3.m: Beholding that highly blessed tawny cow situated in the middle of the fire pit, / Brahmā, the guru of the worlds, bowed down and spoke this, dear one:

6.3.s:
namaste kapile puṇye sarvalokanamaskṛte .
maṅgalye maṅgale devi triṣu lokeṣvanupame .. 39.10 ..
6.3.d:
नमस्ते कपिले पुण्ये सर्वलोकनमस्कृते .
मङ्गल्ये मङ्गले देवि त्रिषु लोकेष्वनुपमे .. 39.10 ..
6.3.m: “Homage to you, holy Kapilā, bowed to by all the worlds, / auspicious, source of auspiciousness, O goddess incomparable in the three worlds!

6.3.s:
tvaṃ lakṣmīstvaṃ smṛtirmedhā tvaṃ dhṛtistvaṃ varānane .
umādevīti vikhyātā tvaṃ satī nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 39.11 ..
6.3.d:
त्वं लक्ष्मीस्त्वं स्मृतिर्मेधा त्वं धृतिस्त्वं वरानने .
उमादेवीति विख्याता त्वं सती नात्र संशयः .. 39.11 ..
6.3.m: You are Lakṣmī, you are Memory, Intellect, and Firmness, O fair-faced one; / you are renowned as the goddess Umā, you are Satī, there is no doubt here.”

6.3.s:
vaiṣṇavī tvaṃ mahādevī brahmāṇī tvaṃ varānane .
kumārī tvaṃ mahābhāge bhaktiḥ śraddhā tathaiva ca .. 39.12 ..
6.3.d:
वैष्णवी त्वं महादेवी ब्रह्माणी त्वं वरानने .
कुमारी त्वं महाभागे भक्तिः श्रद्धा तथैव च .. 39.12 ..
6.3.m: You are Vaiṣṇavī, you are the Great Goddess, you are Brahmāṇī, O fair-faced one; / you are Kumārī, O highly fortunate one, as well as devotion and faith. 39.12

6.3.s:
kālarātristu bhūtānāṃ kumārī parameśvarī .
tvaṃ lavastvaṃ truṭiścaiva muhūrtaṃ lakṣameva ca .. 39.13 ..
6.3.d:
कालरात्रिस्तु भूतानां कुमारी परमेश्वरी .
त्वं लवस्त्वं त्रुटिश्चैव मुहूर्तं लक्षमेव च .. 39.13 ..
6.3.m: You are indeed Kālarātri among living beings, you are Kumārī, the supreme mistress. / You are the lava, you are the truṭi, the muhūrta, and indeed a hundred thousand. 39.13

6.3.s:
saṃvatsarastvaṃ māsastvaṃ kālastvaṃ ca kṣaṇastathā .
nāsti kiṃcittvayā hīnaṃ trailokye sacarācare .. 39.14 ..
6.3.d:
संवत्सरस्त्वं मासस्त्वं कालस्त्वं च क्षणस्तथा .
नास्ति किंचित्त्वया हीनं त्रैलोक्ये सचराचरे .. 39.14 ..
6.3.m: You are the year, you are the month, you are time, and likewise the instant. / There is nothing in the three worlds, moving or unmoving, devoid of you. 39.14

6.3.s:
evaṃ stutā tu mānena kapilā parameṣṭhinā .
tamuvāca mahābhāgaṃ prahṛṣya padmasambhavam .. 39.15 ..
6.3.d:
एवं स्तुता तु मानेन कपिला परमेष्ठिना .
तमुवाच महाभागं प्रहृष्य पद्मसम्भवम् .. 39.15 ..
6.3.m: Praised thus with respect by Parameṣṭhin, / the brown cow, rejoicing, spoke to that highly fortunate lotus-born one: 39.15

6.3.s:
prasannā tava vākyena devadeva jagadguro .
kiṃ karomi priyaṃ te'dya brūhi sarvaṃ pitāmaha .. 39.16 ..
6.3.d:
प्रसन्ना तव वाक्येन देवदेव जगद्गुरो .
किं करोमि प्रियं तेऽद्य ब्रूहि सर्वं पितामह .. 39.16 ..
6.3.m: ‘I am pleased by your speech, O god of gods, teacher of the world! / What pleasing thing may I do for you today? Tell me everything, O Grandfather.’ 39.16

6.3.s:
brahmovāca -
jagaddhitāya janitā mayā tvaṃ parameśvari .
svargānmartyaṃ tato yāhi lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā .. 39.17 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच -
जगद्धिताय जनिता मया त्वं परमेश्वरि .
स्वर्गान्मर्त्यं ततो याहि लोकानां हितकाम्यया .. 39.17 ..
6.3.m: Brahmā said: / ‘You were brought forth by me for the welfare of the world, O supreme mistress; / go therefore from heaven to the mortal realm out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds. 39.17

6.3.s:
sarvadevamayī tvaṃ tu sarvalokamayī tathā .
vidhinā ye pradāsyanti teṣāṃ vāsastriviṣṭape .. 39.18 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वदेवमयी त्वं तु सर्वलोकमयी तथा .
विधिना ये प्रदास्यन्ति तेषां वासस्त्रिविष्टपे .. 39.18 ..
6.3.m: For you consist of all the gods, and likewise you consist of all the worlds. / Those who give [you] in accordance with the injunctions shall dwell in heaven.’ 39.18

6.3.s:
evamuktvā tato devī brahmāṇaṃ parameśvarī .
vandyamānā suraiḥ siddhairājagāma dharātalam .. 39.19 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्त्वा ततो देवी ब्रह्माणं परमेश्वरी .
वन्द्यमाना सुरैः सिद्धैराजगाम धरातलम् .. 39.19 ..
6.3.m: Having spoken thus to Brahmā, the goddess, the supreme mistress, / praised by gods and perfected beings, came down to the surface of the earth. 39.19

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
yadāyāteha sā tāta brāhmaṇo vacanācchubhā .
tadā devāśca lokāśca kathamaṅgeṣu saṃsthitāḥ .. 39.20 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
यदायातेह सा तात ब्राह्मणो वचनाच्छुभा .
तदा देवाश्च लोकाश्च कथमङ्गेषु संस्थिताः .. 39.20 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / ‘When that auspicious one came here at the word of the brahmin, dear father, / how were the gods and the worlds stationed in her limbs? 39.20

6.3.s:
kathaṃ vā saṃsthitāgatya kapilā sā dvijottama .
tīrthe vā hyūṣare kṣetra etanme kathaya dvija .. 39.21 ..
6.3.d:
कथं वा संस्थितागत्य कपिला सा द्विजोत्तम .
तीर्थे वा ह्यूषरे क्षेत्र एतन्मे कथय द्विज .. 39.21 ..
6.3.m: Or how, having arrived, did that brown cow take her place, O best of the twice-born, / in a sacred ford or in a barren field? Tell me this, O twice-born.’ 39.21

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
sā tadā brahmaṇā coktā dhātrā lokasya bhārata .
brahmalokādgatā puṇyāṃ narmadāṃ lokapāvanīm .. 39.22 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
सा तदा ब्रह्मणा चोक्ता धात्रा लोकस्य भारत .
ब्रह्मलोकाद्गता पुण्यां नर्मदां लोकपावनीम् .. 39.22 ..
6.3.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / ‘When spoken to then by Brahmā, the creator of the world, O Bhārata, / she went from the world of Brahmā to the sacred Narmadā that purifies the worlds. 39.22

6.3.s:
tapaḥ kṛtvā suvipulaṃ narmadātaṭamāśritā .
cacāra pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ saśailavanakānanām .. 39.23 ..
6.3.d:
तपः कृत्वा सुविपुलं नर्मदातटमाश्रिता .
चचार पृथिवीं सर्वां सशैलवनकाननाम् .. 39.23 ..
6.3.m: Having performed extensive austerity, resorting to the bank of the Narmadā, / she roamed the entire earth together with its mountains and forests. 39.23

6.3.s:
tadāprabhṛti rājendra kapilātīrthamuttamam .
sarvapāpaharaṃ khyātamṛṣisaṅghairniṣevitam .. 39.24 ..
6.3.d:
तदाप्रभृति राजेन्द्र कपिलातीर्थमुत्तमम् .
सर्वपापहरं ख्यातमृषिसङ्घैर्निषेवितम् .. 39.24 ..
6.3.m: From then on, O lord of kings, the excellent Kapilātīrtha, / celebrated as removing all sins, has been resorted to by hosts of seers. 39.24

6.3.s:
tattīrthe vidhivatsnātvā kapilāyāḥ prayacchati .
pṛthvī tena bhaveddattā saśailavanakānanā .. 39.25 ..
6.3.d:
तत्तीर्थे विधिवत्स्नात्वा कपिलायाः प्रयच्छति .
पृथ्वी तेन भवेद्दत्ता सशैलवनकानना .. 39.25 ..
6.3.m: He who, having bathed in that sacred ford according to the rule, gives a brown cow, / by him the earth, with its mountains and forests, has been given. 39.25

6.3.s:
tāṃ tu paśyati yo bhaktyā dīyamānāṃ dvijottame .
tasya varṣaśataṃ pāpaṃ naśyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 39.26 ..
6.3.d:
तां तु पश्यति यो भक्त्या दीयमानां द्विजोत्तमे .
तस्य वर्षशतं पापं नश्यते नात्र संशयः .. 39.26 ..
6.3.m: He who gazes with devotion upon her being given to the best of brahmins, / his sin of a hundred years is destroyed; of this there is no doubt. 39.26

6.3.s:
bhūrbhuvaḥ svarmahaścaiva janaḥ satyaṃ tapastathā .
te tatpṛṣṭhaṃ samāśritya sthitā lokā nṛpottama .. 39.27 ..
6.3.d:
भूर्भुवः स्वर्महश्चैव जनः सत्यं तपस्तथा .
ते तत्पृष्ठं समाश्रित्य स्थिता लोका नृपोत्तम .. 39.27 ..
6.3.m: Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ, and Mahaḥ, Janaḥ, Satya, and Tapas— / resting upon her back, those worlds reside, O best of kings. 39.27

6.3.s:
mukhe hyagniḥ sthito devo danteṣu ca bhujaṅgamāḥ .
dhātā vidhātā hyoṣṭhau ca jihvāyāṃ tu sarasvatī .. 39.28 ..
6.3.d:
मुखे ह्यग्निः स्थितो देवो दन्तेषु च भुजङ्गमाः .
धाता विधाता ह्योष्ठौ च जिह्वायां तु सरस्वती .. 39.28 ..
6.3.m: Indeed, Agni the god resides in her mouth, and the serpents in her teeth; / Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ are her lips, and Sarasvatī is on her tongue. 39.28

6.3.s:
sahasrakiraṇau devau candrādityau sulocanau .
nāsikāmadhyagaścaiva māruto nṛpasattama .. 39.29 ..
6.3.d:
सहस्रकिरणौ देवौ चन्द्रादित्यौ सुलोचनौ .
नासिकामध्यगश्चैव मारुतो नृपसत्तम .. 39.29 ..
6.3.m: The two deities of a thousand rays, the moon and the sun, are her fair eyes; / and the wind resides in the middle of her nose, O best of kings. 39.29

6.3.s:
lalāṭe tu mahādevo hyaśvinau karṇasaṃsthitau .
naranārāyaṇau śṛṅge śṛṅgamadhye pitāmahaḥ .. 39.30 ..
6.3.d:
ललाटे तु महादेवो ह्यश्विनौ कर्णसंस्थितौ .
नरनारायणौ शृङ्गे शृङ्गमध्ये पितामहः .. 39.30 ..
6.3.m: Mahādeva is on her forehead, and the two Aśvins reside in her ears; / Nara and Nārāyaṇa are in her horns, and the Grandfather is between her horns. 39.30

6.3.s:
kambalo'dhigatastāta pāśadhṛgvaruṇastathā .
yamaśca bhagavāndeva āśritya codaraṃ śritaḥ .. 39.31 ..
6.3.d:
कम्बलोऽधिगतस्तात पाशधृग्वरुणस्तथा .
यमश्च भगवान्देव आश्रित्य चोदरं श्रितः .. 39.31 ..
6.3.m: The dewlap has been reached, dear child, by Varuṇa the noose-bearer; / and the blessed god Yama, taking recourse, has settled upon her belly. 39.31

6.3.s:
khureṣu pannagāścaivaṃ pucchāgre sūryaraśmayaḥ .
evambhūtāṃ hi kapilāṃ sarvadevamayīṃ nṛpa .. 39.32 ..
6.3.d:
खुरेषु पन्नगाश्चैवं पुच्छाग्रे सूर्यरश्मयः .
एवम्भूतां हि कपिलां सर्वदेवमयीं नृप .. 39.32 ..
6.3.m: The serpents are in her hooves, and the rays of the sun are at the tip of her tail. / Truly, the brown cow who is such consists of all the gods, O king. 39.32

6.3.s:
ye dhārayanti ca gṛhe dhanyāste nātra saṃśayaḥ .
prātarutthāya yastasyāḥ kurute tu pradakṣiṇām .. 39.33 ..
6.3.d:
ये धारयन्ति च गृहे धन्यास्ते नात्र संशयः .
प्रातरुत्थाय यस्तस्याः कुरुते तु प्रदक्षिणाम् .. 39.33 ..
6.3.m: Those who keep [her] in their home are blessed; of this there is no doubt. / He who, rising at dawn, circumambulates her, 39.33

6.3.s:
pradakṣiṇā kṛtā tena saśailavanakānanā .
kapilāpañcagavyena yaḥ snāpayati śaṅkaram .. 39.34 ..
6.3.d:
प्रदक्षिणा कृता तेन सशैलवनकानना .
कपिलापञ्चगव्येन यः स्नापयति शङ्करम् .. 39.34 ..
6.3.m: by him the [entire earth] with its mountains and forests has been circumambulated. / He who bathes Śaṅkara with the five cow-products of a brown cow, 39.34

6.3.s:
upavāsaparo yastu tasmiṃstīrthe narādhipa .
snātvā hyuktavidhānena tarpayetpitṛdevatāḥ .. 39.35 ..
6.3.d:
उपवासपरो यस्तु तस्मिंस्तीर्थे नराधिप .
स्नात्वा ह्युक्तविधानेन तर्पयेत्पितृदेवताः .. 39.35 ..
6.3.m: and he who, intent on fasting at that sacred ford, O ruler of men, / having bathed according to the prescribed rite, offers libations to the ancestors and gods, 39.35

6.3.s:
tasya te vaṃśajāḥ sarve daśa pūrve daśāpare .
tṛptā rohanti vai svarge dhyāyanto'sya manorathān .. 39.36 ..
6.3.d:
तस्य ते वंशजाः सर्वे दश पूर्वे दशापरे .
तृप्ता रोहन्ति वै स्वर्गे ध्यायन्तोऽस्य मनोरथान् .. 39.36 ..
6.3.m: all his family members—ten earlier and ten later— / ascend to heaven satisfied, meditating on the fulfillment of his wishes. 39.36

6.3.s:
eṣa te vidhiruddiṣṭaḥ sambhavo nṛpasattama .
tīrthasya ca phalaṃ puṇyaṃ kimanyatparipṛcchasi .. 39.37 ..
6.3.d:
एष ते विधिरुद्दिष्टः सम्भवो नृपसत्तम .
तीर्थस्य च फलं पुण्यं किमन्यत्परिपृच्छसि .. 39.37 ..
6.3.m: This rite has been pointed out to you, along with the origin, O best of kings, / and the holy fruit of the sacred ford. What else do you ask? 39.37

6.3.s:
dhanyaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ sarvaduḥkhaghnamuttamam .
yacchrutvā sarvapāpebhyo mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 39.38 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe śrīnarmadāmāhātmye kapilātīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmaikonacatvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 40
6.3.d:
धन्यं यशस्यमायुष्यं सर्वदुःखघ्नमुत्तमम् .
यच्छ्रुत्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मुच्यते नात्र संशयः .. 39.38 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे श्रीनर्मदामाहात्म्ये कपिलातीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामैकोनचत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 40
6.3.m:
[It brings] good fortune, fame, long life, and is excellent, destroying all sorrow; / hearing it, one is released from all sins; of this there is no doubt.’ 39.38
Thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter, entitled ‘Description of the Greatness of Kapilātīrtha,’ in the Greatness of the Holy Narmadā, in the Section on Revā, in the fifth Section on Avantī, in the venerable Skanda Purāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 40

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gacchettu rājendra karañjeśvaramuttamam .
yatra siddho mahābhāgo daityo lokeṣu viśrutaḥ .. 40.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेत्तु राजेन्द्र करञ्जेश्वरमुत्तमम् .
यत्र सिद्धो महाभागो दैत्यो लोकेषु विश्रुतः .. 40.1 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / ‘Then one should go, O lord of kings, to the excellent Karañjeśvara, / where the highly fortunate Daitya, celebrated in the worlds, attained perfection.’ 40.1

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
yo'sau siddho mahābhāga tatra tīrthe mahātapāḥ .
kasya putraḥ kathaṃ siddhaḥ kasminkāle vada dvija .. 40.2 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
योऽसौ सिद्धो महाभाग तत्र तीर्थे महातपाः .
कस्य पुत्रः कथं सिद्धः कस्मिन्काले वद द्विज .. 40.2 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / ‘He who attained perfection, O highly fortunate one of great austerity, at that sacred ford— / whose son was he, how did he attain perfection, and at what time? Tell me, O twice-born.’ 40.2

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
purā kṛtayuge rājanmānaso brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ .
vedavedāṅgatattvajño marīcirnāma nāmataḥ .. 40.3 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
पुरा कृतयुगे राजन्मानसो ब्रह्मणः सुतः .
वेदवेदाङ्गतत्त्वज्ञो मरीचिर्नाम नामतः .. 40.3 ..
6.3.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / ‘Formerly, in the Kṛta age, O king, there was a mind-born son of Brahmā, / a knower of the true nature of the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas, named Marīci. 40.3

6.3.s:
tasyāpi tapaso rāśeḥ kālena mahatānagha .
putro'tha mānaso jātaḥ sākṣādbrahmeva cāparaḥ .. 40.4 ..
6.3.d:
तस्यापि तपसो राशेः कालेन महतानघ .
पुत्रोऽथ मानसो जातः साक्षाद्ब्रह्मेव चापरः .. 40.4 ..
6.3.m: To that heap of austerity as well, in the course of much time, O sinless one, / a mind-born son was born, like a second Brahmā manifest. 40.4

6.3.s:
kṣamā damo dayā dānaṃ satyaṃ śaucamathārjavam .
marīceśca guṇā hyete santi tasya ca bhārata .. 40.5 ..
6.3.d:
क्षमा दमो दया दानं सत्यं शौचमथार्जवम् .
मरीचेश्च गुणा ह्येते सन्ति तस्य च भारत .. 40.5 ..
6.3.m: Patience, self-control, compassion, generosity, truthfulness, purity, and uprightness— / these virtues of Marīci were present in him as well, O Bhārata. 40.5

6.3.s:
evaṃ guṇagaṇākīrṇaṃ kaśyapaṃ dvijasattamam .
jñātvā prajāpatirdakṣo bhāryārthe svasutāṃ dadau .. 40.6 ..
6.3.d:
एवं गुणगणाकीर्णं कश्यपं द्विजसत्तमम् .
ज्ञात्वा प्रजापतिर्दक्षो भार्यार्थे स्वसुतां ददौ .. 40.6 ..
6.3.m: Knowing Kaśyapa, the best of the twice-born, to be filled with such a host of virtues, / Dakṣa the lord of creatures gave him his daughters to wife: 40.6

6.3.s:
aditirditirdanuścaiva tathāpyevaṃ daśāparāḥ .
yāsāṃ putrāśca saṃjātāḥ pautrāśca bharatarṣabha .. 40.7 ..
6.3.d:
अदितिर्दितिर्दनुश्चैव तथाप्येवं दशापराः .
यासां पुत्राश्च संजाताः पौत्राश्च भरतर्षभ .. 40.7 ..
6.3.m: Aditi, Diti, and Danu, and likewise ten others, / from whom sons were born, as well as grandsons, O bull among the Bharatas. 40.7

6.3.s:
aditirjanayāmāsa putrānindrapurogamān .
jātāstasya mahābāho kaśyapasya prajāpateḥ .. 40.8 ..
6.3.d:
अदितिर्जनयामास पुत्रानिन्द्रपुरोगमान् .
जातास्तस्य महाबाहो कश्यपस्य प्रजापतेः .. 40.8 ..
6.3.m: Aditi gave birth to sons headed by Indra, / born to that lord of creatures, Kaśyapa, O mighty-armed one, 40.8

6.3.s:
yaistu lokatrayaṃ vyāptaṃ sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ mahat .
tathānyasya mahābhāgo danoḥ putro vyajāyata .. 40.9 ..
6.3.d:
यैस्तु लोकत्रयं व्याप्तं स्थावरं जङ्गमं महत् .
तथान्यस्य महाभागो दनोः पुत्रो व्यजायत .. 40.9 ..
6.3.m: by whom the three worlds, moving and unmoving, immense, are pervaded. / And from the other, from Danu, a highly fortunate son was born, 40.9

6.3.s:
sarvalakṣaṇasampannaḥ karañjo nāma nāmataḥ .
bāla eva mahābhāga cacāra sa mahattapaḥ .. 40.10 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वलक्षणसम्पन्नः करञ्जो नाम नामतः .
बाल एव महाभाग चचार स महत्तपः .. 40.10 ..
6.3.m: endowed with all auspicious marks, Karañja by name. / Even as a child, O highly fortunate one, he performed great austerity. 40.10

6.3.s:
narmadātaṭamāśritya cātighoramanuttamam .
divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ ca kṛcchracāndrāyaṇaṃ nṛpa .. 40.11 ..
6.3.d:
नर्मदातटमाश्रित्य चातिघोरमनुत्तमम् .
दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रं च कृच्छ्रचान्द्रायणं नृप .. 40.11 ..
6.3.m: Resorting to the bank of the Narmadā, extremely fierce and unsurpassed, / for a thousand divine years, [he performed] the kṛcchra and cāndrāyaṇa penances, O king, 40.11

6.3.s:
śākamūlaphalāhāraḥ snānahomaparāyaṇaḥ .
tatastuṣṭo mahādeva umayā sahitaḥ kila .. 40.12 ..
6.3.d:
शाकमूलफलाहारः स्नानहोमपरायणः .
ततस्तुष्टो महादेव उमया सहितः किल .. 40.12 ..
6.3.m: eating vegetables, roots, and fruits, intent on bathing and burnt offerings. / Then Mahādeva, accompanied by Umā, became pleased indeed. 40.12

6.3.s:
vareṇa chandayāmāsa tripurāntakaraḥ prabhuḥ .
bhoḥ karañja mahāsattva parituṣṭo'smi te'nagha .. 40.13 ..
6.3.d:
वरेण छन्दयामास त्रिपुरान्तकरः प्रभुः .
भोः करञ्ज महासत्त्व परितुष्टोऽस्मि तेऽनघ .. 40.13 ..
6.3.m: The Lord, the ender of Tripura, invited him to choose a boon: / “O Karañja of great fortitude, I am thoroughly pleased with you, O sinless one. 40.13

6.3.s: varaṃ vṛṇīṣva te dadmi hyamaratvamṛte mama .. 40.14 ..
6.3.d: वरं वृणीष्व ते दद्मि ह्यमरत्वमृते मम .. 40.14 ..
6.3.m: Choose a boon; I grant it to you, except for immortality like mine.”’ 40.14

6.3.s:
karañja uvāca -
yadi tuṣṭo mahādeva yadi deyo varo mama .
tarhi putrāśca pautrāśca santu me dharmavatsalāḥ .. 40.15 ..
6.3.d:
करञ्ज उवाच -
यदि तुष्टो महादेव यदि देयो वरो मम .
तर्हि पुत्राश्च पौत्राश्च सन्तु मे धर्मवत्सलाः .. 40.15 ..
6.3.m: Karañja said: / 'If you are pleased, O Mahādeva, if a boon is to be granted to me, / then let my sons and grandsons be devoted to righteousness.'

6.3.s:
tathetyuktvā mahādeva umayā sahitastadā .
vṛṣārūḍho gaṇaiḥ sārddhaṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata .. 40.16 ..
6.3.d:
तथेत्युक्त्वा महादेव उमया सहितस्तदा .
वृषारूढो गणैः सार्द्धं तत्रैवान्तरधीयत .. 40.16 ..
6.3.m: Having said, 'So be it,' Mahādeva, accompanied by Umā, / mounted upon his bull together with his gaṇas, vanished right there.

6.3.s:
gate cādarśanaṃ deve so'pi daityo mudānvitaḥ .
svanāmnātra mahādevaṃ sthāpayitvā yayau gṛham .. 40.17 ..
6.3.d:
गते चादर्शनं देवे सोऽपि दैत्यो मुदान्वितः .
स्वनाम्नात्र महादेवं स्थापयित्वा ययौ गृहम् .. 40.17 ..
6.3.m: And when the god had passed out of sight, that Daitya too, filled with joy, / having established Mahādeva here in his own name, went home.

6.3.s:
tadāprabhṛti tattīrthaṃ sarvatīrtheṣvanuttamam .
snānamātrānarastatra mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ .. 40.18 ..
6.3.d:
तदाप्रभृति तत्तीर्थं सर्वतीर्थेष्वनुत्तमम् .
स्नानमात्रानरस्तत्र मुच्यते सर्वपातकैः .. 40.18 ..
6.3.m: From that time forth, that sacred ford has been preeminent among all sacred fords; / by merely bathing there, a man is freed from all sins.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ snātvā tarpayetpitṛdevatāḥ .
so'gniṣṭomasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnotyasaṃśayam .. 40.19 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः स्नात्वा तर्पयेत्पितृदेवताः .
सोऽग्निष्टोमस्य यज्ञस्य फलं प्राप्नोत्यसंशयम् .. 40.19 ..
6.3.m: He who bathes at that sacred ford and propitiates the ancestors and deities / obtains the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, without a doubt.

6.3.s:
anāśakaṃ tu yaḥ kuryāttasmiṃstīrthe narādhipa .
anivartyā gatistasya rudralokaṃ sa gacchati .. 40.20 ..
6.3.d:
अनाशकं तु यः कुर्यात्तस्मिंस्तीर्थे नराधिप .
अनिवर्त्या गतिस्तस्य रुद्रलोकं स गच्छति .. 40.20 ..
6.3.m: And he who should undertake fasting unto death at that sacred ford, O king— / his course is non-returning; he goes to the world of Rudra.

6.3.s:
athavāgnijale prāṇānyastyajeddharmanandana .
ayutadvitayaṃ vaste varṣāṇāṃ śivamandire .. 40.21 ..
6.3.d:
अथवाग्निजले प्राणान्यस्त्यजेद्धर्मनन्दन .
अयुतद्वितयं वस्ते वर्षाणां शिवमन्दिरे .. 40.21 ..
6.3.m: Or if one should give up his life-breaths in fire or in water, O son of Dharma, / he dwells for twenty thousand years in the abode of Śiva.

6.3.s:
tataścaiva kṣaye jāte jāyate vimale kule .
vedavedāṅgatattvajñaḥ sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ .. 40.22 ..
6.3.d:
ततश्चैव क्षये जाते जायते विमले कुले .
वेदवेदाङ्गतत्त्वज्ञः सर्वशास्त्रविशारदः .. 40.22 ..
6.3.m: And after that [period] has come to an end, he is born in a spotless family, / knowing the truth of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, skilled in all scriptures,

6.3.s:
rājā vā rājatulyo vā jīvecca śaradaḥ śatam .
putrapautrasamopetaḥ sarvavyādhivivarjitaḥ .. 40.23 ..
6.3.d:
राजा वा राजतुल्यो वा जीवेच्च शरदः शतम् .
पुत्रपौत्रसमोपेतः सर्वव्याधिविवर्जितः .. 40.23 ..
6.3.m: a king or equal to a king, and he lives for a hundred autumns, / accompanied by sons and grandsons, free from all diseases.

6.3.s:
evaṃ te sarvamākhyātaṃ pṛṣṭaṃ yadyattvayānagha .
tīrthasya tu phalaṃ tasya snānadāneṣu bhārata .. 40.24 ..
6.3.d:
एवं ते सर्वमाख्यातं पृष्टं यद्यत्त्वयानघ .
तीर्थस्य तु फलं तस्य स्नानदानेषु भारत .. 40.24 ..
6.3.m: Thus all that was asked by you, O sinless one, has been related to you: / the fruit of that sacred ford regarding bath and gifts, O Bhārata.

6.3.s:
etatpuṇyaṃ pāpaharaṃ dhanyaṃ duḥsvapnanāśanam .
paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiva tīrthamāhātmyamuttamam .. 40.25 ..
6.3.d:
एतत्पुण्यं पापहरं धन्यं दुःस्वप्ननाशनम् .
पठतां शृण्वतां चैव तीर्थमाहात्म्यमुत्तमम् .. 40.25 ..
6.3.m: This supreme māhātmya of the sacred ford is meritorious, destroys sins, brings good fortune, and dispels bad dreams / for those who read it and listen to it.

6.3.s:
yastu śrāvayate śrāddhe paṭhetpitṛparāyaṇaḥ .
akṣayaṃ jāyate puṇyamityevaṃ śaṅkaro'bravīt .. 40.26 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe narmadāmāhātmye karañjeśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma catvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 41
6.3.d:
यस्तु श्रावयते श्राद्धे पठेत्पितृपरायणः .
अक्षयं जायते पुण्यमित्येवं शङ्करोऽब्रवीत् .. 40.26 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे नर्मदामाहात्म्ये करञ्जेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम चत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 41
6.3.m:
He who recites it or makes it heard at an ancestral rite, devoted to the ancestors, / his merit becomes imperishable: thus Śaṃkara declared.
Thus ends the fortieth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Māhātmya of Karañjeśvara-tīrtha', in the Narmadāmāhātmya in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth [section], the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 41

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gacchecca rājendra kuṇḍaleśvaramuttamam .
yatra siddho mahāyakṣaḥ kuṇḍadhāro nṛpottama .. 41.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेच्च राजेन्द्र कुण्डलेश्वरमुत्तमम् .
यत्र सिद्धो महायक्षः कुण्डधारो नृपोत्तम .. 41.1 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / 'Then one should go, O king of kings, to the excellent Kuṇḍaleśvara, / where the great yakṣa Kuṇḍadhāra attained perfection, O best of kings,

6.3.s:
tapaḥ kṛtvā suvipulaṃ surāsurabhayaṃkaram .
paulastyamandire caiva cikrīḍa nṛpasattama .. 41.2 ..
6.3.d:
तपः कृत्वा सुविपुलं सुरासुरभयंकरम् .
पौलस्त्यमन्दिरे चैव चिक्रीड नृपसत्तम .. 41.2 ..
6.3.m: having performed immense austerity that caused dread to gods and demons, / and sportively lived in the palace of Paulastya, O best of kings.'

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
kasminyuge samutpannaḥ kasya putro mahāmatiḥ .
tapastaptvā suvipulaṃ toṣito yena śaṅkaraḥ .. 41.3 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
कस्मिन्युगे समुत्पन्नः कस्य पुत्रो महामतिः .
तपस्तप्त्वा सुविपुलं तोषितो येन शङ्करः .. 41.3 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / 'In which yuga was he born? Whose son was that noble-minded one, / by whom, having practiced immense austerity, Śaṃkara was pleased?

6.3.s:
etadvistaratastāta kathayasva mamānagha .
śṛṇvataśca na tṛptirme kathāmṛtamanuttamam .. 41.4 ..
6.3.d:
एतद्विस्तरतस्तात कथयस्व ममानघ .
शृण्वतश्च न तृप्तिर्मे कथामृतमनुत्तमम् .. 41.4 ..
6.3.m: Tell this to me in detail, dear sir, O sinless one; / for I have no satiety in listening to the supreme nectar of your tales.'

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tretāyuge brahmasamaḥ paulastyonāma viśravāḥ .
tapaḥ kṛtvā suvipulaṃ bharadvājasutodbhavaḥ .. 41.5 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
त्रेतायुगे ब्रह्मसमः पौलस्त्योनाम विश्रवाः .
तपः कृत्वा सुविपुलं भरद्वाजसुतोद्भवः .. 41.5 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / 'In the Tretāyuga, equal to Brahmā, the descendant of Pulastya named Viśravas, / born as the son of Bharadvāja's daughter, performed immense austerity.

6.3.s:
putraṃ pautragaṇairyuktaṃ patnyā bhaktyā sutoṣitaḥ .
dhanadaṃ janayāmāsa sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitam .. 41.6 ..
6.3.d:
पुत्रं पौत्रगणैर्युक्तं पत्न्या भक्त्या सुतोषितः .
धनदं जनयामास सर्वलक्षणलक्षितम् .. 41.6 ..
6.3.m: Having thoroughly satisfied his wife with devotion, he begot a son endowed with a host of grandsons, / Dhanada, who was marked with all auspicious characteristics.

6.3.s:
jātamātraṃ tu taṃ jñātvā brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ .
cakāra nāma suprīta ṛṣidevasamanvitaḥ .. 41.7 ..
6.3.d:
जातमात्रं तु तं ज्ञात्वा ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः .
चकार नाम सुप्रीत ऋषिदेवसमन्वितः .. 41.7 ..
6.3.m: Learning that he was born, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, / surrounded by seers and gods, gave him a name with great joy:

6.3.s:
yasmādviśravaso jāto mama pautratvamāgataḥ .
tasmādvaiśravaṇo nāma tava dattaṃ mayānagha .. 41.8 ..
6.3.d:
यस्माद्विश्रवसो जातो मम पौत्रत्वमागतः .
तस्माद्वैश्रवणो नाम तव दत्तं मयानघ .. 41.8 ..
6.3.m: "Since you were born of Viśravas and have become my grandson, / therefore the name Vaiśravaṇa has been given to you by me, O sinless one.

6.3.s:
tathā tvaṃ sarvadevānāṃ dhanagoptā bhaviṣyasi .
caturtho lokapālānāmakṣayaścāvyayo bhuvi .. 41.9 ..
6.3.d:
तथा त्वं सर्वदेवानां धनगोप्ता भविष्यसि .
चतुर्थो लोकपालानामक्षयश्चाव्ययो भुवि .. 41.9 ..
6.3.m: Likewise, you shall be the guardian of wealth for all the gods, / the fourth of the world-protectors, imperishable and undecaying on earth."

6.3.s:
tasya bhāryā mahārāja īśvarīti ca viśrutā .
yakṣo yakṣādhipaḥ śreṣṭhastasya kuṇḍo'bhavatsutaḥ .. 41.10 ..
6.3.d:
तस्य भार्या महाराज ईश्वरीति च विश्रुता .
यक्षो यक्षाधिपः श्रेष्ठस्तस्य कुण्डोऽभवत्सुतः .. 41.10 ..
6.3.m: His wife, O great king, was famed as Īśvarī; / he, the yakṣa, the best ruler of yakṣas, had a son named Kuṇḍa.

6.3.s:
sa ca rūpaṃ paraṃ prāpya mātāpitroranujñayā .
tapaścacāra vipulaṃ narmadātaṭamāśritaḥ .. 41.11 ..
6.3.d:
स च रूपं परं प्राप्य मातापित्रोरनुज्ञया .
तपश्चचार विपुलं नर्मदातटमाश्रितः .. 41.11 ..
6.3.m: Attaining supreme beauty, by the permission of his parents, / he resorted to the bank of the Narmadā and performed immense austerity.

6.3.s:
grīṣme pañcāgnisaṃtapto varṣāsu sthaṇḍileśayaḥ .
hemante jalamadhyastho vāyubhakṣaḥ śataṃ samāḥ .. 41.12 ..
6.3.d:
ग्रीष्मे पञ्चाग्निसंतप्तो वर्षासु स्थण्डिलेशयः .
हेमन्ते जलमध्यस्थो वायुभक्षः शतं समाः .. 41.12 ..
6.3.m: Scorched by the five fires in summer, lying on bare ground in the rainy season, / standing in water in the winter, feeding on wind for a hundred years,

6.3.s:
evaṃ varṣaśate pūrṇe ekāṅguṣṭhe'bhavannṛpa .
asthibhūtaḥ paraṃ tāta ūrdhvabāhustataḥ param .. 41.13 ..
6.3.d:
एवं वर्षशते पूर्णे एकाङ्गुष्ठेऽभवन्नृप .
अस्थिभूतः परं तात ऊर्ध्वबाहुस्ततः परम् .. 41.13 ..
6.3.m: when a hundred years were thus complete, he stood on one big toe, O king, / reduced to mere bones, my dear, and thereafter with upraised arms.

6.3.s:
atapacca ghṛtaśvāsaḥ kuṇḍalo bharatarṣabha .
caturthe varṣaśatake tutoṣa vṛṣavāhanaḥ .. 41.14 ..
6.3.d:
अतपच्च घृतश्वासः कुण्डलो भरतर्षभ .
चतुर्थे वर्षशतके तुतोष वृषवाहनः .. 41.14 ..
6.3.m: Restraining his breath, Kuṇḍala practiced austerity, O bull of the Bharatas; / in the fourth century of years, he whose vehicle is the bull was pleased.

6.3.s:
varaṃ vṛṇīṣva bho vatsa yatte manasi rocate .
dadāmi te na sandehastapasā toṣito hyaham .. 41.15 ..
6.3.d:
वरं वृणीष्व भो वत्स यत्ते मनसि रोचते .
ददामि ते न सन्देहस्तपसा तोषितो ह्यहम् .. 41.15 ..
6.3.m: 'Choose a boon, my child, whatever pleases your mind; / I grant it to you, have no doubt, for I am pleased by your austerity.'

6.3.s:
kuṇḍala uvāca -
yakṣādhipaprasādena tasyaivānucaraḥ pure .
vicarāmi yathākāmamavadhyaḥ sarvaśatruṣu .. 41.16 ..
6.3.d:
कुण्डल उवाच -
यक्षाधिपप्रसादेन तस्यैवानुचरः पुरे .
विचरामि यथाकाममवध्यः सर्वशत्रुषु .. 41.16 ..
6.3.m: Kuṇḍala said: / 'By the grace of the lord of yakṣas, let me wander as his attendant in the city / as I desire, invulnerable to all enemies.'

6.3.s:
tathetyuktvā mahādevaḥ sarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ .
jagāmākāśamāviśya kailāsaṃ dharaṇīdharam .. 41.17 ..
6.3.d:
तथेत्युक्त्वा महादेवः सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः .
जगामाकाशमाविश्य कैलासं धरणीधरम् .. 41.17 ..
6.3.m: Having said, 'So be it,' Mahādeva, bowed to by all the worlds, / entered the sky and went to Kailāsa, the mountain.

6.3.s:
gate cādarśanaṃ deve so'pi yakṣo mudānvitaḥ .
sthāpayāmāsa deveśaṃ kuṇḍaleśvaramuttamam .. 41.18 ..
6.3.d:
गते चादर्शनं देवे सोऽपि यक्षो मुदान्वितः .
स्थापयामास देवेशं कुण्डलेश्वरमुत्तमम् .. 41.18 ..
6.3.m: And when the god had passed out of sight, that yakṣa too, filled with joy, / established the supreme Kuṇḍaleśvara, the lord of gods.

6.3.s:
alaṃkṛtvā jagannāthaṃ puṣpadhūpānulepanaiḥ .
vimānaiścāmaraiśchatraistathā vai liṅgapūraṇaiḥ .. 41.19 ..
6.3.d:
अलंकृत्वा जगन्नाथं पुष्पधूपानुलेपनैः .
विमानैश्चामरैश्छत्रैस्तथा वै लिङ्गपूरणैः .. 41.19 ..
6.3.m: Having adorned the Lord of the Universe with flowers, incenses, and ointments, / with aerial chariots, chowries, and umbrellas, and with the bathing of the liṅga,

6.3.s:
tarpayitvā dvijānsamyagannapānādibhūṣaṇaiḥ .
prīṇayitvā mahādevaṃ tataḥ svabhavanaṃ yayau .. 41.20 ..
6.3.d:
तर्पयित्वा द्विजान्सम्यगन्नपानादिभूषणैः .
प्रीणयित्वा महादेवं ततः स्वभवनं ययौ .. 41.20 ..
6.3.m: and having gratified the twice-born properly with food, drink, and ornaments, / having pleased Mahādeva, he then went to his own abode.

6.3.s:
tadāprabhṛti tattīrthaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam .
uttamaṃ paramaṃ puṇyaṃ kuṇḍaleśvaranāmataḥ .. 41.21 ..
6.3.d:
तदाप्रभृति तत्तीर्थं त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम् .
उत्तमं परमं पुण्यं कुण्डलेश्वरनामतः .. 41.21 ..
6.3.m: From that time forth, that sacred ford has been famed in the three worlds / as Kuṇḍaleśvara, supreme and most meritorious.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ kaścidupavāsaparāyaṇaḥ .
arcayeddevamīśānaṃ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate .. 41.22 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः कश्चिदुपवासपरायणः .
अर्चयेद्देवमीशानं सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते .. 41.22 ..
6.3.m: Whoever, devoted to fasting at that sacred ford, / worships the god Īśāna, is completely freed from all sins.

6.3.s:
suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ vāpi maṇiṃ mauktikameva ca .
dadyādbhojyaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ sa sukhī modate divi .. 41.23 ..
6.3.d:
सुवर्णं रजतं वापि मणिं मौक्तिकमेव च .
दद्याद्भोज्यं ब्राह्मणेभ्यः स सुखी मोदते दिवि .. 41.23 ..
6.3.m: Whether one gives gold, silver, a gem, or a pearl, / or food to brahmins, he rejoices happily in heaven.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ snātvā ṛgyajuḥsāmago'pi vā .
ṛcamekāṃ japitvā tu sakalaṃ phalamaśnute .. 41.24 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः स्नात्वा ऋग्यजुःसामगोऽपि वा .
ऋचमेकां जपित्वा तु सकलं फलमश्नुते .. 41.24 ..
6.3.m: He who bathes at that sacred ford, whether a chanter of the Ṛg, Yajur, or Sāma Veda, / and mutters even a single ṛc, enjoys the full fruit.

6.3.s:
gāṃ prayacchati viprebhyastatphalaṃ śṛṇu pāṇḍava .
yāvanti tasyā romāṇi tatprasūtikuleṣu ca .. 41.25 ..
6.3.d:
गां प्रयच्छति विप्रेभ्यस्तत्फलं शृणु पाण्डव .
यावन्ति तस्या रोमाणि तत्प्रसूतिकुलेषु च .. 41.25 ..
6.3.m: Hear the fruit of him who gives a cow to brahmins, O Pāṇḍava: / for as many hairs as are upon her and upon the line of her offspring,

6.3.s:
tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi svargaloke mahīyate .
svarge vāso bhavettasya putrapautraiḥ samanvitaḥ .. 41.26 ..
6.3.d:
तावद्वर्षसहस्राणि स्वर्गलोके महीयते .
स्वर्गे वासो भवेत्तस्य पुत्रपौत्रैः समन्वितः .. 41.26 ..
6.3.m: for so many thousands of years he is glorified in the heavenly world; / he shall have residence in heaven accompanied by sons and grandsons.

6.3.s:
tāvanti varṣāṇi mahānubhāvaḥ svarge vasetputrapautraiśca sārddham .
tatrānnado yāti maheśalokamasaṃkhyavarṣāṇi na saṃśayo'tra .. 41.27 ..
6.3.d:
तावन्ति वर्षाणि महानुभावः स्वर्गे वसेत्पुत्रपौत्रैश्च सार्द्धम् .
तत्रान्नदो याति महेशलोकमसंख्यवर्षाणि न संशयोऽत्र .. 41.27 ..
6.3.m: That noble-minded person dwells in heaven for that many years along with his sons and grandsons; / the giver of food there goes to the world of Maheśa for countless years, there is no doubt here.

6.3.s:
sa vai sukhī modate svargaloke gandharvasiddhāpsaraḥsampragīte .
evaṃ tu te dharmasuta prabhāvastīrthasya sarvaḥ kathitaśca pārtha .. 41.28 ..
6.3.d:
स वै सुखी मोदते स्वर्गलोके गन्धर्वसिद्धाप्सरःसम्प्रगीते .
एवं तु ते धर्मसुत प्रभावस्तीर्थस्य सर्वः कथितश्च पार्थ .. 41.28 ..
6.3.m: He indeed rejoices happily in the heavenly world, sung around by Gandharvas, Siddhas, and apsarases; / thus the entire power of the sacred ford has been told to you, O son of Dharma, O Pārtha.

6.3.s:
śrutvā stuvanmucyate sarvapāpaiḥ punastrilokīmiha tatprabhāvāt .. 41.29 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe narmadāmāhātmye kuṇḍaleśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmaikacatvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 42
6.3.d:
श्रुत्वा स्तुवन्मुच्यते सर्वपापैः पुनस्त्रिलोकीमिह तत्प्रभावात् .. 41.29 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे नर्मदामाहात्म्ये कुण्डलेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामैकचत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 42
6.3.m:
Having heard and praised [it], one is freed from all sins, and again [attains] the three worlds here by its power.
Thus ends the forty-first chapter, entitled “Description of the Māhātmya of the Kuṇḍaleśvara Sacred Ford,” in the Narmadā Māhātmya of the Revākhaṇḍa, in the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa comprising eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 42

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gacchettu rājendra pippaleśvaramuttamam .
yatra siddho mahāyogī pippalādo mahātapāḥ .. 42.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेत्तु राजेन्द्र पिप्पलेश्वरमुत्तमम् .
यत्र सिद्धो महायोगी पिप्पलादो महातपाः .. 42.1 ..
6.3.m: The glorious Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then one should go, O king of kings, to the supreme Pippaleśvara, / where the great yogin Pippalāda, of great austerity, attained perfection.

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
pippalādasya caritaṃ śrotumicchāmyahaṃ vibho .
māhātmyaṃ tasya tīrthasya yatra siddho mahātapāḥ .. 42.2 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
पिप्पलादस्य चरितं श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं विभो .
माहात्म्यं तस्य तीर्थस्य यत्र सिद्धो महातपाः .. 42.2 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / I wish to hear about Pippalāda's life, O lord, / and the māhātmya of that sacred ford where the [sage] of great austerity attained perfection.

6.3.s:
kasya putro mahābhāga kimarthaṃ kṛtavāṃstapaḥ .
etadvistarataḥ sarvaṃ kathayasva mamānagha .. 42.3 ..
6.3.d:
कस्य पुत्रो महाभाग किमर्थं कृतवांस्तपः .
एतद्विस्तरतः सर्वं कथयस्व ममानघ .. 42.3 ..
6.3.m: Whose son was he, O illustrious one, and for what purpose did he perform austerity? / Tell me all this in detail, O sinless one.

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
mithilāstho mahābhāgo vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ .
yājñavalkyaḥ purā tāta cacāra vipulaṃ tapaḥ .. 42.4 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
मिथिलास्थो महाभागो वेदवेदाङ्गपारगः .
याज्ञवल्क्यः पुरा तात चचार विपुलं तपः .. 42.4 ..
6.3.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / In ancient times, my dear, the illustrious Yājñavalkya, who lived in Mithilā / and was a master of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, performed vast austerity.

6.3.s:
tāpasī tasya bhaginī yājñavalkyasya dhīmataḥ .
sā saptame'pi varṣe ca vaidhavyaṃ prāpa daivataḥ .. 42.5 ..
6.3.d:
तापसी तस्य भगिनी याज्ञवल्क्यस्य धीमतः .
सा सप्तमेऽपि वर्षे च वैधव्यं प्राप दैवतः .. 42.5 ..
6.3.m: That wise Yājñavalkya had an ascetic sister. / Through destiny, she became a widow even in her seventh year.

6.3.s:
pūrvakarmavipākena hīnābhūtpitṛmātṛtaḥ .
nābhūttatpatipakṣe'pi ko'pītyekākinī sthitā .. 42.6 ..
6.3.d:
पूर्वकर्मविपाकेन हीनाभूत्पितृमातृतः .
नाभूत्तत्पतिपक्षेऽपि कोऽपीत्येकाकिनी स्थिता .. 42.6 ..
6.3.m: By the ripening of past deeds she was bereft of father and mother. / Nor was there anyone on her husband's side, so she remained alone.

6.3.s:
bhūmau bhramantī bhrātuḥ sā samīpamagamacchanaiḥ .
cacāra ca tapaḥ so'pi paralokasukhepsayā .. 42.7 ..
6.3.d:
भूमौ भ्रमन्ती भ्रातुः सा समीपमगमच्छनैः .
चचार च तपः सोऽपि परलोकसुखेप्सया .. 42.7 ..
6.3.m: Wandering upon the earth, she slowly went to her brother. / He too was practicing austerity, desiring the happiness of the other world.

6.3.s:
cacāra sāpi tatrasthā śuśrūṣantī mahattapaḥ .
kasmiṃścitsamaye sātha snātāhani rajasvalā .. 42.8 ..
6.3.d:
चचार सापि तत्रस्था शुश्रूषन्ती महत्तपः .
कस्मिंश्चित्समये साथ स्नाताहनि रजस्वला .. 42.8 ..
6.3.m: Staying there, serving him, she also practiced great austerity. / Then, at a certain time, having bathed on the day [after her period], having menstruated,

6.3.s:
antarvāso dhṛtavatī dṛṣṭvā karpaṭakaṃ rahaḥ .
yājñavalkyo'pi tadrātrau supto yatra susaṃvṛtaḥ .. 42.9 ..
6.3.d:
अन्तर्वासो धृतवती दृष्ट्वा कर्पटकं रहः .
याज्ञवल्क्योऽपि तद्रात्रौ सुप्तो यत्र सुसंवृतः .. 42.9 ..
6.3.m: she put on an undergarment, having seen a rag in secret. / Where Yājñavalkya also slept that night, well covered,

6.3.s:
svapnaṃ dṛṣṭvātyajacchukraṃ kaupīne raktabinduvat .
virājitena tapasā siddhaṃ tadanalaprabham .. 42.10 ..
6.3.d:
स्वप्नं दृष्ट्वात्यजच्छुक्रं कौपीने रक्तबिन्दुवत् .
विराजितेन तपसा सिद्धं तदनलप्रभम् .. 42.10 ..
6.3.m: he had a dream and discharged semen upon his loincloth like a drop of blood, / perfected by radiant austerity, glowing like fire.

6.3.s:
yāvatprabuddho vipro'sau vīkṣyocchiṣṭaṃ tadaṃśukam .
cikṣepa dūrato'spṛśyaṃ śaucaṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ .. 42.11 ..
6.3.d:
यावत्प्रबुद्धो विप्रोऽसौ वीक्ष्योच्छिष्टं तदंशुकम् .
चिक्षेप दूरतोऽस्पृश्यं शौचं कृत्वा विधानतः .. 42.11 ..
6.3.m: When that brahmin woke up, seeing that garment defiled, / he threw it far away as untouchable, having performed purification according to the rules.

6.3.s:
niṣiddhaṃ tu niśi snānamiti suṣvāpa sa dvijaḥ .
niśīthe sāpi tadvastraṃ bhagasyāvaraṇaṃ vyadhāt .. 42.12 ..
6.3.d:
निषिद्धं तु निशि स्नानमिति सुष्वाप स द्विजः .
निशीथे सापि तद्वस्त्रं भगस्यावरणं व्यधात् .. 42.12 ..
6.3.m: Since bathing at night is forbidden, the twice-born went back to sleep. / In the dead of night, she used that garment as a covering for her vulva.

6.3.s:
prātaranveṣayāmāsa munirvastramitastataḥ .
tataḥ sā brāhmaṇī prāha kiṃ anveṣayase prabho .
kena kāryaṃ tava tathā vadasva mama tattvataḥ .. 42.13 ..
6.3.d:
प्रातरन्वेषयामास मुनिर्वस्त्रमितस्ततः .
ततः सा ब्राह्मणी प्राह किं अन्वेषयसे प्रभो .
केन कार्यं तव तथा वदस्व मम तत्त्वतः .. 42.13 ..
6.3.m: In the morning, the sage searched here and there for the garment. / Then that brahmin woman said: “What are you looking for, my lord? / What do you need it for? Tell me the truth.”

6.3.s:
yājñavalkya uvāca -
apavitro mayā bhadre svapno dṛṣṭo'dya vai niśi .
sakledaṃ tatra me vastraṃ nikṣiptaṃ tanna dṛśyate .. 42.14 ..
6.3.d:
याज्ञवल्क्य उवाच -
अपवित्रो मया भद्रे स्वप्नो दृष्टोऽद्य वै निशि .
सक्लेदं तत्र मे वस्त्रं निक्षिप्तं तन्न दृश्यते .. 42.14 ..
6.3.m: Yājñavalkya said: / “O auspicious lady, an impure dream was seen by me tonight. / My wet garment was thrown down there, and it is not to be seen.”

6.3.s:
tacchrutvā brāhmaṇī vākyaṃ bhītabhītāvadannṛpa .
tadvastraṃ tu mayā vipra snātvā hyantaḥ kṛtaṃ mahat .. 42.15 ..
6.3.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा ब्राह्मणी वाक्यं भीतभीतावदन्नृप .
तद्वस्त्रं तु मया विप्र स्नात्वा ह्यन्तः कृतं महत् .. 42.15 ..
6.3.m: Hearing that statement, the brahmin woman, terrified, said, O king: / “O brahmin, after bathing, I used that very cloth as an inner garment.”

6.3.s:
tasyāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā hāhetyuktvā mahāmuniḥ .
nipapāta tadā bhūmau chinnamūla iva drumaḥ .. 42.16 ..
6.3.d:
तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा हाहेत्युक्त्वा महामुनिः .
निपपात तदा भूमौ छिन्नमूल इव द्रुमः .. 42.16 ..
6.3.m: Hearing her words, the great sage cried out “Alas! Alas!” / and fell to the ground like a tree cut down at its roots.

6.3.s:
kimetaditi setyuktvā hyākāśamiva nirmalā .
āśvāsayantī taṃ vipraṃ provāca vacanaṃ tadā .. 42.17 ..
6.3.d:
किमेतदिति सेत्युक्त्वा ह्याकाशमिव निर्मला .
आश्वासयन्ती तं विप्रं प्रोवाच वचनं तदा .. 42.17 ..
6.3.m: Saying “What is this?”, pure as the sky, / she comforted the brahmin and then addressed these words to him:

6.3.s:
vadasva kāraṇaṃ tāta guhyādguhyataraṃ yadi .
pratīkāro'sya yenaiva vimṛśya kriyate tvarā .. 42.18 ..
6.3.d:
वदस्व कारणं तात गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं यदि .
प्रतीकारोऽस्य येनैव विमृश्य क्रियते त्वरा .. 42.18 ..
6.3.m: “Tell me the reason, father, even if it is more secret than the secret, / so that a remedy for it may be devised and done with haste.”

6.3.s:
tataḥ sa suciraṃ dhyātvā labdhavāgvai tataḥ kṣaṇam .
provāca sādhvasamanā yattacchṛṇu nareśvara .. 42.19 ..
6.3.d:
ततः स सुचिरं ध्यात्वा लब्धवाग्वै ततः क्षणम् .
प्रोवाच साध्वसमना यत्तच्छृणु नरेश्वर .. 42.19 ..
6.3.m: Then, having meditated for a long time, regaining his speech a moment later, / his mind filled with dread, he spoke that which [I shall tell you], hear, O ruler of men:

6.3.s:
nātra doṣo'sti te kaścinmama caiva śubhavrate .
tavodare tu garbho yastatra daivaṃ parāyaṇam .. 42.20 ..
6.3.d:
नात्र दोषोऽस्ति ते कश्चिन्मम चैव शुभव्रते .
तवोदरे तु गर्भो यस्तत्र दैवं परायणम् .. 42.20 ..
6.3.m: “There is no fault here for you, nor for me, O lady of auspicious vows. / But the fetus in your womb has destiny as its cause.

6.3.s:
tasya tattvena rakṣā ca tvayā kāryā sadaiva hi .
vināśī naiva kartavyo yāvatkālasya paryayaḥ .. 42.21 ..
6.3.d:
तस्य तत्त्वेन रक्षा च त्वया कार्या सदैव हि .
विनाशी नैव कर्तव्यो यावत्कालस्य पर्ययः .. 42.21 ..
6.3.m: Its protection must truly be carried out by you at all times; / it must not be destroyed until the passage of time is complete.”

6.3.s:
tatheti vrīḍitā sādhvī dūyamānena cetasā .
apālayacca taṃ garbhaṃ yāvatputro hyajāyata .. 42.22 ..
6.3.d:
तथेति व्रीडिता साध्वी दूयमानेन चेतसा .
अपालयच्च तं गर्भं यावत्पुत्रो ह्यजायत .. 42.22 ..
6.3.m: Saying “So be it,” the virtuous woman, ashamed and with an aching heart, / protected that fetus until a son was born.

6.3.s:
jātamātraṃ ca taṃ garbhaṃ gṛhītvā brāhmaṇī ca sā .
aśvatthacchāyāmāśritya tamutsṛjya vaco'bravīt .. 42.23 ..
6.3.d:
जातमात्रं च तं गर्भं गृहीत्वा ब्राह्मणी च सा .
अश्वत्थच्छायामाश्रित्य तमुत्सृज्य वचोऽब्रवीत् .. 42.23 ..
6.3.m: As soon as he was born, that brahmin woman took the child, / sought the shade of an aśvattha tree, abandoned him, and spoke these words:

6.3.s:
yāni sattvāni lokeṣu sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca .
tāni sarvāṇi rakṣantu tyaktaṃ vai bālakaṃ mayā .. 42.24 ..
6.3.d:
यानि सत्त्वानि लोकेषु स्थावराणि चराणि च .
तानि सर्वाणि रक्षन्तु त्यक्तं वै बालकं मया .. 42.24 ..
6.3.m: “Whatever creatures there are in the worlds, both motionless and moving, / let them all protect this child abandoned by me!”

6.3.s:
evamuktvā gatā sā tu brāhmaṇī nṛpasattama .
tathāgataḥ sa tu śiśustatra sthitvā muhūrtakam .. 42.25 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्त्वा गता सा तु ब्राह्मणी नृपसत्तम .
तथागतः स तु शिशुस्तत्र स्थित्वा मुहूर्तकम् .. 42.25 ..
6.3.m: Having spoken thus, that brahmin woman departed, O best of kings. / That infant who had come into such a state, remaining there for a moment,

6.3.s:
pāṇipādau vinikṣipya nikuñcya nayane śubhe .
āsyaṃ tu vikṛtaṃ kṛtvā ruroda vikṛtaiḥ svaraiḥ .. 42.26 ..
6.3.d:
पाणिपादौ विनिक्षिप्य निकुञ्च्य नयने शुभे .
आस्यं तु विकृतं कृत्वा रुरोद विकृतैः स्वरैः .. 42.26 ..
6.3.m: flinging his hands and feet, closing his fine eyes, / and making a contorted face, wept with distorted sounds.

6.3.s:
tena śabdena vitrastāḥ sthāvarā jaṅgamāśca ye .
ākampitā mahotpātaiḥ saśailavanakānanā .. 42.27 ..
6.3.d:
तेन शब्देन वित्रस्ताः स्थावरा जङ्गमाश्च ये .
आकम्पिता महोत्पातैः सशैलवनकानना .. 42.27 ..
6.3.m: Terrified by that cry, both the motionless and the moving, / along with mountains, forests, and groves, shook with great portents.

6.3.s:
tato jñātvā mahadbhūtaṃ kṣudhāviṣṭaṃ dvijarṣabham .
na jahāti nagaśchāyāṃ pānārthāya tataḥ param .
apibacca sutaṃ tasmādabhṛtaṃ caiva bhārata .. 42.28 ..
6.3.d:
ततो ज्ञात्वा महद्भूतं क्षुधाविष्टं द्विजर्षभम् .
न जहाति नगश्छायां पानार्थाय ततः परम् .
अपिबच्च सुतं तस्मादभृतं चैव भारत .. 42.28 ..
6.3.m: Then, knowing that best of the twice-born to be a great being overwhelmed by hunger, / from then on the tree did not abandon its shade, and for his drinking / he drank the sap from it and was nourished, O descendant of Bharata.

6.3.s:
evaṃ sa vardhitastatra kumāro nijacetasi .
cintayāmāsa viśrabdhaḥ kiṃ mama grahagocaram .. 42.29 ..
6.3.d:
एवं स वर्धितस्तत्र कुमारो निजचेतसि .
चिन्तयामास विश्रब्धः किं मम ग्रहगोचरम् .. 42.29 ..
6.3.m: Thus reared there, the boy confidently thought in his own mind: / “What is within the astrological reach of my planets?”

6.3.s:
tataḥ krūrasabhācāraḥ krūraṃ dṛṣṭvā nirīkṣitaḥ .
papāta sahasā bhūmau śanaiścārī śanaiścaraḥ .. 42.30 ..
6.3.d:
ततः क्रूरसभाचारः क्रूरं दृष्ट्वा निरीक्षितः .
पपात सहसा भूमौ शनैश्चारी शनैश्चरः .. 42.30 ..
6.3.m: Then Śanaiścara, who has a cruel manner, having seen [the boy] looking cruelly, / suddenly fell to the earth, the slow-moving one.

6.3.s:
uvāca ca bhayatrastaḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭastadā .
kiṃ mayāpakṛtaṃ vipra pippalāda mahāmune .. 42.31 ..
6.3.d:
