Being burnt by the fire, he too aimed a Vāruṇa weapon.
With that great Vāruṇa weapon, the fiery [arrow] was then extinguished.

6.3.s:
tato'sau cintayāmāsa kena bāṇo visarjitaḥ .
kasyaiṣā pauruṣī śaktiḥ ko yāsyati yamālayam .. 48.5 ..
6.3.d:
ततोऽसौ चिन्तयामास केन बाणो विसर्जितः .
कस्यैषा पौरुषी शक्तिः को यास्यति यमालयम् .. 48.5 ..
6.3.m:
Then he wondered: "By whom was this arrow loosed?
Whose manly power is this? Who will go to the abode of Yama?"

6.3.s:
tato'ndhako mṛdhe kruddho bāṇamārgeṇa nirgataḥ .
sa dṛṣṭvā bāṇamārgeṇa cāpahastaṃ janārdanam .. 48.6 ..
6.3.d:
ततोऽन्धको मृधे क्रुद्धो बाणमार्गेण निर्गतः .
स दृष्ट्वा बाणमार्गेण चापहस्तं जनार्दनम् .. 48.6 ..
6.3.m:
Then, enraged in battle, Andhaka came forth along the path of the arrow.
Having seen Janārdana bow-in-hand along the path of the arrow,

6.3.s:
andhaka uvāca -
na śarma lapsyase hyadya mayā dṛṣṭyābhivīkṣitaḥ .
na śaknoṣi tathā gantuṃ nāgaḥ śārdūladarśanāt .. 48.7 ..
6.3.d:
अन्धक उवाच -
न शर्म लप्स्यसे ह्यद्य मया दृष्ट्याभिवीक्षितः .
न शक्नोषि तथा गन्तुं नागः शार्दूलदर्शनात् .. 48.7 ..
6.3.m:
Andhaka said:
"You will not find happiness today, having been beheld by my gaze!
Just as an elephant cannot escape upon seeing a tiger, so you cannot go away.

6.3.s:
āgacchati yathā bhakṣyaṃ mārjārasya ca mūṣikaḥ .
na śaknoṣi tathā yātuṃ saṃsthitastvaṃ mamāgrataḥ .. 48.8 ..
6.3.d:
आगच्छति यथा भक्ष्यं मार्जारस्य च मूषिकः .
न शक्नोषि तथा यातुं संस्थितस्त्वं ममाग्रतः .. 48.8 ..
6.3.m:
Just as a mouse comes forth to be the food of a cat,
so you, standing before me, cannot get away!

6.3.s:
ahaṃ tvāṃ preṣayiṣyāmi yamamārge sudāruṇe .
ahamanveṣayiṣyāmi kila yāsyāmi te gṛham .. 48.9 ..
6.3.d:
अहं त्वां प्रेषयिष्यामि यममार्गे सुदारुणे .
अहमन्वेषयिष्यामि किल यास्यामि ते गृहम् .. 48.9 ..
6.3.m:
I shall send you along the dreadful road of Yama;
I shall track down your house and indeed go there!

6.3.s:
upanīto'si kālena saṅgrāme mama keśava .
ye tvayā nirjitāḥ pūrvaṃ dānavā apyanekaśaḥ .. 48.10 ..
6.3.d:
उपनीतोऽसि कालेन सङ्ग्रामे मम केशव .
ये त्वया निर्जिताः पूर्वं दानवा अप्यनेकशः .. 48.10 ..
6.3.m:
You have been brought by Time to my battle, O Keśava!
Those Dānavas who were conquered by you many times before—

6.3.s:
na bhavanti pumāṃsaste striyastāścaiva keśava .
paraṃ na śastrasaṅgrāmaṃ kariṣyāmi tvayā saha .. 48.11 ..
6.3.d:
न भवन्ति पुमांसस्ते स्त्रियस्ताश्चैव केशव .
परं न शस्त्रसङ्ग्रामं करिष्यामि त्वया सह .. 48.11 ..
6.3.m:
they were not real men; they were merely women, O Keśava!
However, I shall not fight with weapons against you!"

6.3.s:
vadato dānavendrasya na cukopa sa keśavaḥ .
ayudhyamānaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā cintayāmāsa dānavaḥ .. 48.12 ..
6.3.d:
वदतो दानवेन्द्रस्य न चुकोप स केशवः .
अयुध्यमानं तं दृष्ट्वा चिन्तयामास दानवः .. 48.12 ..
6.3.m:
While the lord of Dānavas was speaking, Keśava did not become angry.
Seeing that he would not fight, the Dānava reflected:

6.3.s:
dvandvayuddhaṃ kariṣyāmi niścitya yuyudhe nṛpa .
sa kṛṣṇena padākṣiptaḥ patitaḥ pṛthivītale .. 48.13 ..
6.3.d:
द्वन्द्वयुद्धं करिष्यामि निश्चित्य युयुधे नृप .
स कृष्णेन पदाक्षिप्तः पतितः पृथिवीतले .. 48.13 ..
6.3.m:
"I will fight in single combat"; having resolved thus, O king, he fought.
He was struck down by Kṛṣṇa's foot and fell upon the surface of the earth.

6.3.s:
muhūrtātsa samāśvasya utthāyedaṃ vyacintayat .
aśakto dvandvayuddhāya tataḥ sāma prayuktavān .
pāṇibhyāṃ sampuṭaṃ kṛtvā sāṣṭāṅgaṃ praṇataḥ śuciḥ .. 48.14 ..
6.3.d:
मुहूर्तात्स समाश्वस्य उत्थायेदं व्यचिन्तयत् .
अशक्तो द्वन्द्वयुद्धाय ततः साम प्रयुक्तवान् .
पाणिभ्यां सम्पुटं कृत्वा साष्टाङ्गं प्रणतः शुचिः .. 48.14 ..
6.3.m:
Reviving after a moment, he rose up and thought:
He was incapable of hand-to-hand combat; therefore, he employed conciliation.
Folding his hands in supplication, pure, he bowed down with eight limbs prostrated.

6.3.s:
andhaka uvāca -
jaya kṛṣṇāya haraye viṣṇave jiṣṇave namaḥ .
hṛṣīkeśa jagaddhātre acyutāya mahātmane .. 48.15 ..
6.3.d:
अन्धक उवाच -
जय कृष्णाय हरये विष्णवे जिष्णवे नमः .
हृषीकेश जगद्धात्रे अच्युताय महात्मने .. 48.15 ..
6.3.m:
Andhaka said:
"Victory! Homage to Kṛṣṇa, to Hari, to Viṣṇu, the victorious one!
To Hṛṣīkeśa, the sustainer of the world, to Acyuta, the Great Soul!

6.3.s:
namaḥ paṅkajanābhāya namaḥ paṅkajamāline .
janārdanāya śrīśāya śrīpate pītavāsase .. 48.16 ..
6.3.d:
नमः पङ्कजनाभाय नमः पङ्कजमालिने .
जनार्दनाय श्रीशाय श्रीपते पीतवाससे .. 48.16 ..
6.3.m:
Homage to the lotus-navelled one, homage to the one adorned with a lotus garland,
to Janārdana, the Lord of Śrī, O consort of Śrī, clad in yellow garments!

6.3.s:
govindāya namo nityaṃ namo jaladhiśāyine .
namaḥ karālavaktrāya narasiṃhāya nādine .. 48.17 ..
6.3.d:
गोविन्दाय नमो नित्यं नमो जलधिशायिने .
नमः करालवक्त्राय नरसिंहाय नादिने .. 48.17 ..
6.3.m:
Homage always to Govinda, homage to the one lying upon the ocean;
homage to the roaring Narasiṃha of terrible face!

6.3.s:
śārṅgiṇe sitavarṇāya śaṅkhacakragadābhṛte .
namo vāmanarūpāya yajñarūpāya te namaḥ .. 48.18 ..
6.3.d:
शार्ङ्गिणे सितवर्णाय शङ्खचक्रगदाभृते .
नमो वामनरूपाय यज्ञरूपाय ते नमः .. 48.18 ..
6.3.m:
To the bow-wielder, of white complexion, bearer of the conch, discus, and mace;
homage to the one whose form is Vāmana, homage to you whose form is the sacrifice!

6.3.s:
namo varāharūpāya krāntalokatrayāya ca .
vyāptāśeṣadigantāya keśavāya namonamaḥ .. 48.19 ..
6.3.d:
नमो वराहरूपाय क्रान्तलोकत्रयाय च .
व्याप्ताशेषदिगन्ताय केशवाय नमोनमः .. 48.19 ..
6.3.m:
Homage to the one whose form is the Boar, who strode across the three worlds,
who pervades all ends of the directions; homage, homage to Keśava!

6.3.s:
vāsudeva namastubhyaṃ namaḥ kaiṭabhanāśine .
lakṣmyālaya suraśreṣṭha namaste suranāyaka .. 48.20 ..
6.3.d:
वासुदेव नमस्तुभ्यं नमः कैटभनाशिने .
लक्ष्म्यालय सुरश्रेष्ठ नमस्ते सुरनायक .. 48.20 ..
6.3.m:
O Vāsudeva, homage to you; homage to the destroyer of Kaiṭabha!
O abode of Lakṣmī, O best among gods, homage to you, O leader of the gods!

6.3.s:
viṣṇordevādhidevasya pramāṇaṃ ye'pi kurvate .
prajāpaterjagaddhātusteṣāmapi namāmyaham .. 48.21 ..
6.3.d:
विष्णोर्देवाधिदेवस्य प्रमाणं येऽपि कुर्वते .
प्रजापतेर्जगद्धातुस्तेषामपि नमाम्यहम् .. 48.21 ..
6.3.m:
Even to those who show reverence to Viṣṇu, the god over all gods,
the Lord of Creatures, the sustainer of the world—to them also I bow.

6.3.s:
samastabhūtadevasya vāsudevasya dhīmataḥ .
praṇāmaṃ ye prakurvanti teṣāmapi namāmyaham .. 48.22 ..
6.3.d:
समस्तभूतदेवस्य वासुदेवस्य धीमतः .
प्रणामं ये प्रकुर्वन्ति तेषामपि नमाम्यहम् .. 48.22 ..
6.3.m:
To those who offer salutation to wise Vāsudeva,
the god of all living beings—to them also I bow.

6.3.s:
tasya yajñavarāhasya viṣṇoramitatejasaḥ .
praṇāmaṃ ye prakurvanti teṣāmapi namāmyaham .. 48.23 ..
6.3.d:
तस्य यज्ञवराहस्य विष्णोरमिततेजसः .
प्रणामं ये प्रकुर्वन्ति तेषामपि नमाम्यहम् .. 48.23 ..
6.3.m:
To those who offer salutation to Viṣṇu of boundless splendour,
that Sacrificial Boar—to them also I bow.

6.3.s:
guṇānāṃ hi nidhānāya namaste'stu punaḥpunaḥ .
kāruṇyāmbunidhe deva sarvabhaktipriyāya ca .. 48.24 ..
6.3.d:
गुणानां हि निधानाय नमस्तेऽस्तु पुनःपुनः .
कारुण्याम्बुनिधे देव सर्वभक्तिप्रियाय च .. 48.24 ..
6.3.m:
Homage be to you again and again, the treasure-house of virtues,
O god who are an ocean of compassion and fond of all devotion!

6.3.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca -
tuṣṭaste dānavendrāhaṃ varaṃ vṛṇu yathepsitam .
dadāmi te varaṃ nūnamapi trailokyadurlabham .. 48.25 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच -
तुष्टस्ते दानवेन्द्राहं वरं वृणु यथेप्सितम् .
ददामि ते वरं नूनमपि त्रैलोक्यदुर्लभम् .. 48.25 ..
6.3.m:
The Blessed Lord said:
I am pleased with you, O lord of Dānavas; choose a boon as you desire.
I shall certainly give you a boon, even one difficult to obtain in the three worlds.

6.3.s:
andhaka uvāca -
yadi tuṣṭo'si me deva varaṃ dāsyasi cepsitam .
tadā dadasva me deva yuddhaṃ paramaśobhanam .
avaddhastapūto yenāhaṃ lokāngantāsmi śobhanān .. 48.26 ..
6.3.d:
अन्धक उवाच -
यदि तुष्टोऽसि मे देव वरं दास्यसि चेप्सितम् .
तदा ददस्व मे देव युद्धं परमशोभनम् .
अवद्धस्तपूतो येनाहं लोकान्गन्तास्मि शोभनान् .. 48.26 ..
6.3.m:
Andhaka said:
If you are pleased with me, O god, and will give a desired boon,
then grant me, O god, a supreme and splendid battle,
so that, purified by your weapon, I may go to beautiful realms.

6.3.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca -
kathaṃ dadāmi te yuddhaṃ toṣito'haṃ tvayā punaḥ .
na tvāṃ tu prabhavetkopaḥ kathaṃ yudhyāmi te'ndhaka .. 48.27 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच -
कथं ददामि ते युद्धं तोषितोऽहं त्वया पुनः .
न त्वां तु प्रभवेत्कोपः कथं युध्यामि तेऽन्धक .. 48.27 ..
6.3.m:
The Blessed Lord said:
How can I give you battle when I have been propitiated by you?
Anger cannot prevail against you; how can I fight with you, O Andhaka?

6.3.s:
yadi te vartate buddhiryuddhaṃ prati na saṃśayaḥ .
tato gacchasva yuddhāya devaṃ prati maheśvaram .. 48.28 ..
6.3.d:
यदि ते वर्तते बुद्धिर्युद्धं प्रति न संशयः .
ततो गच्छस्व युद्धाय देवं प्रति महेश्वरम् .. 48.28 ..
6.3.m:
If your mind is set on battle without a doubt,
then go to fight against the god Maheśvara.

6.3.s:
andhaka uvāca -
na tatra sidhyate kāryaṃ devaṃ prati maheśvaram .. 48.29 ..
6.3.d:
अन्धक उवाच -
न तत्र सिध्यते कार्यं देवं प्रति महेश्वरम् .. 48.29 ..
6.3.m:
Andhaka said:
My purpose will not be accomplished there, against the god Maheśvara.

6.3.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca -
putra tvaṃ śikharaṃ gatvā dhūnayasva balena ca .. 48.30 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच -
पुत्र त्वं शिखरं गत्वा धूनयस्व बलेन च .. 48.30 ..
6.3.m:
The Blessed Lord said:
Son, go to the mountain peak and shake it with your strength.

6.3.s:
vidhūte tatra deveśaḥ kopaṃ kartā sudāruṇam .
kopitaḥ śaṅkaro raudraṃ yuddhaṃ dāsyati dānava .. 48.31 ..
6.3.d:
विधूते तत्र देवेशः कोपं कर्ता सुदारुणम् .
कोपितः शङ्करो रौद्रं युद्धं दास्यति दानव .. 48.31 ..
6.3.m:
When it is shaken, the Lord of Gods will feel fierce wrath;
enraged, Śaṅkara will grant you a dreadful battle, O Dānava.

6.3.s:
viṣṇuvākyādasau pāpo gato yatra maheśvaraḥ .
kailāsaśikharaṃ prāpya dhunoti sma muhurmuhuḥ .. 48.32 ..
6.3.d:
विष्णुवाक्यादसौ पापो गतो यत्र महेश्वरः .
कैलासशिखरं प्राप्य धुनोति स्म मुहुर्मुहुः .. 48.32 ..
6.3.m:
At Viṣṇu's word, that sinful one went to where Maheśvara was;
reaching the peak of Kailāsa, he shook it repeatedly.

6.3.s:
dhūnite tatra śikhare kampitaṃ bhuvanatrayam .
nipetuḥ śikharāgrāṇi kampamānānyanekaśaḥ .. 48.33 ..
6.3.d:
धूनिते तत्र शिखरे कम्पितं भुवनत्रयम् .
निपेतुः शिखराग्राणि कम्पमानान्यनेकशः .. 48.33 ..
6.3.m:
When that peak was shaken, the three worlds trembled;
mountain summits, violently trembling, fell down in great numbers.

6.3.s:
catvāraḥ sāgarāḥ kṣipramekībhūtā mahīpate .
nipeturulkāpātāśca pādapā apyanekaśaḥ .. 48.34 ..
6.3.d:
चत्वारः सागराः क्षिप्रमेकीभूता महीपते .
निपेतुरुल्कापाताश्च पादपा अप्यनेकशः .. 48.34 ..
6.3.m:
The four oceans quickly merged into one, O king;
meteors fell, and trees tumbled in great numbers.

6.3.s:
umayā sahito devo vismayaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ .
gāḍhamāliṅgya girijā devaṃ vacanamabravīt .. 48.35 ..
6.3.d:
उमया सहितो देवो विस्मयं परमं गतः .
गाढमालिङ्ग्य गिरिजा देवं वचनमब्रवीत् .. 48.35 ..
6.3.m:
Accompanied by Umā, the god was filled with supreme astonishment.
Clasping the god tightly, the mountain-born goddess spoke [these] words:

6.3.s:
kimarthaṃ kampate śailaḥ kimarthaṃ kampate dharā .
kimarthaṃ kampate nāgo martyaḥ pātālameva ca .
kiṃ vā yugakṣayo deva tanmamākhyātumarhasi .. 48.36 ..
6.3.d:
किमर्थं कम्पते शैलः किमर्थं कम्पते धरा .
किमर्थं कम्पते नागो मर्त्यः पातालमेव च .
किं वा युगक्षयो देव तन्ममाख्यातुमर्हसि .. 48.36 ..
6.3.m: "Why does the mountain shake? Why does the earth tremble? / Why do the serpent, mortals, and even Pātāla quake? / Or is it the destruction of an age, O Lord? You should tell me that." 48.36

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
kasyaiṣā durmatirjātā kṣiptaḥ sarpamukhe karaḥ .
lalāṭe ca kṛtaṃ varma sa yāsyati yamālayam .. 48.37 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
कस्यैषा दुर्मतिर्जाता क्षिप्तः सर्पमुखे करः .
ललाटे च कृतं वर्म स यास्यति यमालयम् .. 48.37 ..
6.3.m: Īśvara said: / "Whose wicked idea was this? A hand has been thrust into the serpent's mouth; / armor has been placed on the forehead! He will go to Yama's abode. 48.37

6.3.s:
kailāsamāśrito yena supto'haṃ yena bodhitaḥ .
taṃ vadhiṣye na sandehaḥ sammukho vā bhavedyadi .. 48.38 ..
6.3.d:
कैलासमाश्रितो येन सुप्तोऽहं येन बोधितः .
तं वधिष्ये न सन्देहः सम्मुखो वा भवेद्यदि .. 48.38 ..
6.3.m: He who approached Kailāsa and woke me while I slept, / him shall I kill, there is no doubt, if he stands facing me." 48.38

6.3.s:
cintayāmāsa deveśo hyandhako'yaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .
upāyaṃ cintayāmāsa yenāsau vadhyate kṣaṇāt .. 48.39 ..
6.3.d:
चिन्तयामास देवेशो ह्यन्धकोऽयं न संशयः .
उपायं चिन्तयामास येनासौ वध्यते क्षणात् .. 48.39 ..
6.3.m: The Lord of the gods thought, "This is Andhaka, without a doubt." / He considered a means by which he might be killed in an instant. 48.39

6.3.s:
āgatāśca surāḥ sarve brahmādyā vasubhiḥ saha .
rathaṃ devamayaṃ kṛtvā sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyutam .. 48.40 ..
6.3.d:
आगताश्च सुराः सर्वे ब्रह्माद्या वसुभिः सह .
रथं देवमयं कृत्वा सर्वलक्षणसंयुतम् .. 48.40 ..
6.3.m: And all the gods, led by Brahmā along with the Vasus, arrived / having made a chariot composed of the gods, endowed with all auspicious marks. 48.40

6.3.s:
keciddevāḥ sthitāścakre kecittuṇḍāgrapārśvayoḥ .
kecinnābhyāṃ sthitā devāḥ keciddhuryeṣu saṃsthitāḥ .. 48.41 ..
6.3.d:
केचिद्देवाः स्थिताश्चक्रे केचित्तुण्डाग्रपार्श्वयोः .
केचिन्नाभ्यां स्थिता देवाः केचिद्धुर्येषु संस्थिताः .. 48.41 ..
6.3.m: Some gods stood upon the wheel, some at the sides of the chariot-front; / some gods stood at the hub, and some stood upon the yokes. 48.41

6.3.s:
dhurīṣu niścalāḥ kecitkecidyūpeṣu saṃsthitāḥ .
kecitsyandanasaṃstambhāḥ kecitsyandanaveṣṭakāḥ .. 48.42 ..
6.3.d:
धुरीषु निश्चलाः केचित्केचिद्यूपेषु संस्थिताः .
केचित्स्यन्दनसंस्तम्भाः केचित्स्यन्दनवेष्टकाः .. 48.42 ..
6.3.m: Some were motionless on the axle-poles, some stood upon the posts; / some were pillars of the chariot, some were coverings of the chariot. 48.42

6.3.s:
āmalasārake'nye'pi anye'pi kalaśe sthitāḥ .
riporbhayaṃkaraṃ divyaṃ dhvajamālādiśobhitam .. 48.43 ..
6.3.d:
आमलसारकेऽन्येऽपि अन्येऽपि कलशे स्थिताः .
रिपोर्भयंकरं दिव्यं ध्वजमालादिशोभितम् .. 48.43 ..
6.3.m: Others stood on the finial, and others on the pot, / terrifying to the enemy, divine, adorned with garlands of banners and the like. 48.43

6.3.s:
rathaṃ devamayaṃ kṛtvā tamārūḍho jagadguruḥ .
niryayau dānavo yatra kopāviṣṭo maheśvaraḥ .. 48.44 ..
6.3.d:
रथं देवमयं कृत्वा तमारूढो जगद्गुरुः .
निर्ययौ दानवो यत्र कोपाविष्टो महेश्वरः .. 48.44 ..
6.3.m: Having made the chariot composed of gods, the Guru of the universe mounted it; / filled with wrath, Maheśvara set forth where the Dānava was. 48.44

6.3.s:
tiṣṭha tiṣṭhetyuvācātha kva prayāsyasi durmate .
śarāsanaṃ kare gṛhya śarāṃścikṣepa dānave .. 48.45 ..
6.3.d:
तिष्ठ तिष्ठेत्युवाचाथ क्व प्रयास्यसि दुर्मते .
शरासनं करे गृह्य शरांश्चिक्षेप दानवे .. 48.45 ..
6.3.m: He said, "Halt, halt! Where will you go, wicked-minded one?" / Taking the bow in his hand, he shot arrows at the Dānava. 48.45

6.3.s:
dānave'dhiṣṭhite yuddhe śaraiścicheda sāyakān .
śarāsaneṇa tatraiva andhakaśchāditastadā .. 48.46 ..
6.3.d:
दानवेऽधिष्ठिते युद्धे शरैश्चिछेद सायकान् .
शरासनेण तत्रैव अन्धकश्छादितस्तदा .. 48.46 ..
6.3.m: As the Dānava stood in battle, he cut off the arrows with arrows; / then Andhaka was covered right there by [Śiva's] bow[-shot arrows]. 48.46

6.3.s:
na tatra dṛśyate sūryo nākāśaṃ na ca candramāḥ .
āgneyamastraṃ vyasṛjaddānavo'pi śivaṃ prati .. 48.47 ..
6.3.d:
न तत्र दृश्यते सूर्यो नाकाशं न च चन्द्रमाः .
आग्नेयमस्त्रं व्यसृजद्दानवोऽपि शिवं प्रति .. 48.47 ..
6.3.m: The sun could not be seen there, nor the sky, nor the moon. / The Dānava also discharged a fiery weapon against Śiva. 48.47

6.3.s:
dahyamānāḥ śarāṅgāraistatrasuḥ sarvadevatāḥ .
rakṣa rakṣa mahādeva dahyamānāṃstu dānavāt .. 48.48 ..
6.3.d:
दह्यमानाः शराङ्गारैस्तत्रसुः सर्वदेवताः .
रक्ष रक्ष महादेव दह्यमानांस्तु दानवात् .. 48.48 ..
6.3.m: Burnt by the arrow-coals, all the deities became terrified: / "Protect, protect us, O Mahādeva, who are being burnt by the Dānava!" 48.48

6.3.s:
tato devādhidevo'sau vāruṇāstramayo'jayat .
vāruṇāstreṇa nimiṣādāgneyaṃ nāśitaṃ tadā .. 48.49 ..
6.3.d:
ततो देवाधिदेवोऽसौ वारुणास्त्रमयोऽजयत् .
वारुणास्त्रेण निमिषादाग्नेयं नाशितं तदा .. 48.49 ..
6.3.m: Then that God of gods, wielding the watery weapon, conquered [it]; / by the watery weapon, the fiery [one] was destroyed in an instant. 48.49

6.3.s:
dānavena tadā muktaṃ vāyavyāstraṃ raṇājire .
vāruṇaṃ ca gataṃ tāta vāyavyāstravināśitam .. 48.50 ..
6.3.d:
दानवेन तदा मुक्तं वायव्यास्त्रं रणाजिरे .
वारुणं च गतं तात वायव्यास्त्रविनाशितम् .. 48.50 ..
6.3.m: Then the airy weapon was released by the Dānava on the field of battle, / and the watery [weapon], my dear, was destroyed by the airy weapon. 48.50

6.3.s:
devo vyasarjayatsārpaṃ krodhāviṣṭena cetasā .
mārutaṃ nāśitaṃ bāṇaiḥ sarpaistatra na saṃśayaḥ .. 48.51 ..
6.3.d:
देवो व्यसर्जयत्सार्पं क्रोधाविष्टेन चेतसा .
मारुतं नाशितं बाणैः सर्पैस्तत्र न संशयः .. 48.51 ..
6.3.m: With his mind seized with anger, the Lord released the serpent weapon; / the wind was destroyed there by the snake-arrows, of this there is no doubt. 48.51

6.3.s:
dānavena tato muktaṃ garuḍāstraṃ ca līlayā .
gāruḍāstraṃ ca taddṛṣṭvā sārpaṃ naiva vyadṛśyata .. 48.52 ..
6.3.d:
दानवेन ततो मुक्तं गरुडास्त्रं च लीलया .
गारुडास्त्रं च तद्दृष्ट्वा सार्पं नैव व्यदृश्यत .. 48.52 ..
6.3.m: Then the Garuḍa weapon was released playfully by the Dānava; / and seeing that Garuḍa weapon, the serpent [weapon] was no longer seen. 48.52

6.3.s:
tato devādhidevena nārasiṃhaṃ visarjitam .
nārasiṃhāstrabāṇena gāruḍāstraṃ praśāmitam .. 48.53 ..
6.3.d:
ततो देवाधिदेवेन नारसिंहं विसर्जितम् .
नारसिंहास्त्रबाणेन गारुडास्त्रं प्रशामितम् .. 48.53 ..
6.3.m: Then the Nārasiṃha weapon was discharged by the God of gods; / by the Nārasiṃha weapon's arrow, the Garuḍa weapon was subdued. 48.53

6.3.s:
astramastreṇa śamyeta na bādhyeta parasparam .
mahadyuddhamabhūttātasurāsurabhayaṃkaram .. 48.54 ..
6.3.d:
अस्त्रमस्त्रेण शम्येत न बाध्येत परस्परम् .
महद्युद्धमभूत्तातसुरासुरभयंकरम् .. 48.54 ..
6.3.m: Weapon was quenched by weapon, neither prevailing over the other. / A great battle took place, my dear, terrifying to gods and asuras, 48.54

6.3.s:
cakranālīkanārācaistomaraiḥ khaḍgamudgaraiḥ .
vatsadantaistathā bhallaiḥ karṇikāraiśca śobhanaiḥ .. 48.55 ..
6.3.d:
चक्रनालीकनाराचैस्तोमरैः खड्गमुद्गरैः .
वत्सदन्तैस्तथा भल्लैः कर्णिकारैश्च शोभनैः .. 48.55 ..
6.3.m: with discs, reeds, iron arrows, javelins, swords, and mallets, / with calf-tooth arrows, spears, and beautiful karṇikāra arrows. 48.55

6.3.s:
evaṃ na śakyate hantuṃ dānavo vividhāyudhaiḥ .
tadā jvālākarālāśca khaḍganārācatomarāḥ .. 48.56 ..
6.3.d:
एवं न शक्यते हन्तुं दानवो विविधायुधैः .
तदा ज्वालाकरालाश्च खड्गनाराचतोमराः .. 48.56 ..
6.3.m: Thus the Dānava could not be slain with various weapons. / Then swords, iron arrows, and javelins, formidable with flames, 48.56

6.3.s:
vṛṣāṅkena vimuktāstu samare dānavaṃ prati .
na saṃspṛśanti śastrāṇi gātraṃ gauḍavadhūriva .. 48.57 ..
6.3.d:
वृषाङ्केन विमुक्तास्तु समरे दानवं प्रति .
न संस्पृशन्ति शस्त्राणि गात्रं गौडवधूरिव .. 48.57 ..
6.3.m: were hurled in the battle against the Dānava by the bull-bannered [Śiva]; / the weapons did not touch his body, like [a bashful] Gauḍa bride. 48.57

6.3.s:
āyudhāni tatastyaktvā bāhuyuddhamupasthitau .
karaṃ kareṇa saṃgṛhya praharantau svamuṣṭibhiḥ .
raṇaprayogairyudhyantau yuyudhāte śivāndhakau .. 48.58 ..
6.3.d:
आयुधानि ततस्त्यक्त्वा बाहुयुद्धमुपस्थितौ .
करं करेण संगृह्य प्रहरन्तौ स्वमुष्टिभिः .
रणप्रयोगैर्युध्यन्तौ युयुधाते शिवान्धकौ .. 48.58 ..
6.3.m: Then, having cast aside weapons, they engaged in hand-to-hand combat; / gripping hand with hand, striking with their own fists, / fighting with combat maneuvers, Śiva and Andhaka fought. 48.58

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
andhakaṃ prati deveśaścintayāmāsa nigraham .
haniṣyāmi na sandeho duṣṭātmānaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .. 48.59 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
अन्धकं प्रति देवेशश्चिन्तयामास निग्रहम् .
हनिष्यामि न सन्देहो दुष्टात्मानं न संशयः .. 48.59 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / The Lord of the gods contemplated the suppression of Andhaka: / "I shall kill the evil-minded one, there is no doubt, without a doubt." 48.59

6.3.s:
sa śivena yadā kṣiptaḥ patitaḥ pṛthivītale .
ūrdhvabāhuradhovaktro dānavo nṛpasattama .. 48.60 ..
6.3.d:
स शिवेन यदा क्षिप्तः पतितः पृथिवीतले .
ऊर्ध्वबाहुरधोवक्त्रो दानवो नृपसत्तम .. 48.60 ..
6.3.m: When he was thrown down by Śiva, he fell onto the surface of the earth, / with his arms raised and face downward, O best of kings. 48.60

6.3.s:
krodhāviṣṭena deveśaḥ saṅgrāme devaśatruṇā .
kakṣayoḥ kuhare kṣiptvā bandhenākramya pīḍitaḥ .. 48.61 ..
6.3.d:
क्रोधाविष्टेन देवेशः सङ्ग्रामे देवशत्रुणा .
कक्षयोः कुहरे क्षिप्त्वा बन्धेनाक्रम्य पीडितः .. 48.61 ..
6.3.m: Filled with anger, the enemy of the gods in battle seized the Lord of the gods, / hurled him into the hollow of his armpits, and oppressed him, holding him bound. 48.61

6.3.s:
nispandaścābhavaddevo mūrcchāyukto maheśvaraḥ .
mūrcchāpannaṃ tu taṃ jñātvā cintayāmāsa dānavaḥ .. 48.62 ..
6.3.d:
निस्पन्दश्चाभवद्देवो मूर्च्छायुक्तो महेश्वरः .
मूर्च्छापन्नं तु तं ज्ञात्वा चिन्तयामास दानवः .. 48.62 ..
6.3.m: The Lord became motionless; Maheśvara was overtaken by a swoon. / But knowing him to be fallen into a swoon, the Dānava reflected: 48.62

6.3.s:
hāhā kaṣṭaṃ kṛtaṃ me'dya duṣkṛtaṃ pāpakarmaṇā .
kiṃ karomi kathaṃ karma kasminsthāne tu mocaye .. 48.63 ..
6.3.d:
हाहा कष्टं कृतं मेऽद्य दुष्कृतं पापकर्मणा .
किं करोमि कथं कर्म कस्मिन्स्थाने तु मोचये .. 48.63 ..
6.3.m: "Alas, a terrible misdeed has been done today by me, an evil-doer! / What shall I do? How can this act [be undone]? In what place should I release him?" 48.63

6.3.s:
gṛhītvā devamutsaṅge gataḥ kailāsaparvatam .
śayyāyāṃ śaṅkaraṃ nyasya niryayau daityarāṭtataḥ .. 48.64 ..
6.3.d:
गृहीत्वा देवमुत्सङ्गे गतः कैलासपर्वतम् .
शय्यायां शङ्करं न्यस्य निर्ययौ दैत्यराट्ततः .. 48.64 ..
6.3.m: Taking the Lord upon his lap, he went to Mount Kailāsa; / having laid Śaṅkara upon his bed, the king of Daityas then departed. 48.64

6.3.s:
śayyāyāṃ patito devaḥ prapede vedanāṃ tataḥ .
tāvaddadarśa cātmānaṃ svakīyabhavanasthitam .. 48.65 ..
6.3.d:
शय्यायां पतितो देवः प्रपेदे वेदनां ततः .
तावद्ददर्श चात्मानं स्वकीयभवनस्थितम् .. 48.65 ..
6.3.m: Fallen upon the bed, the God then felt pain; / then he saw himself situated in his own abode. 48.65

6.3.s:
parābhavaḥ kṛto madyaṃ kathaṃ tena durātmanā .
krodhavegasamāviṣṭo niryayau dānavaṃ prati .. 48.66 ..
6.3.d:
पराभवः कृतो मद्यं कथं तेन दुरात्मना .
क्रोधवेगसमाविष्टो निर्ययौ दानवं प्रति .. 48.66 ..
6.3.m: "How was defeat inflicted upon me today by that wicked soul?" / Seized by the force of anger, he went out toward the Dānava. 48.66

6.3.s:
āyasīṃ laguḍīṃ gṛhya prabhurbhārasahasrajām .
dānavaṃ ca tato dṛṣṭvā prākṣipattasya mūrdhani .. 48.67 ..
6.3.d:
आयसीं लगुडीं गृह्य प्रभुर्भारसहस्रजाम् .
दानवं च ततो दृष्ट्वा प्राक्षिपत्तस्य मूर्धनि .. 48.67 ..
6.3.m: Taking an iron club forged of a thousand bhāras, / the Lord saw the Dānava and hurled it at his head. 48.67

6.3.s:
khaḍgena tāḍayāmāsa dānavaḥ prahasanraṇe .
devenāthasmṛtaṃ cāstraṃ kauccherākhyaṃ mahāhave .. 48.68 ..
6.3.d:
खड्गेन ताडयामास दानवः प्रहसन्रणे .
देवेनाथस्मृतं चास्त्रं कौच्छेराख्यं महाहवे .. 48.68 ..
6.3.m: Laughing in battle, the Dānava struck it with his sword. / Then in that great battle, the God remembered the weapon named Kauccheira. 48.68

6.3.s:
dīpyamānaṃ samutsṛjya hṛdaye tāḍitaḥ kṣaṇāt .
tataḥ sa tāḍitastena rudhirodgāramudvaman .. 48.69 ..
6.3.d:
दीप्यमानं समुत्सृज्य हृदये ताडितः क्षणात् .
ततः स ताडितस्तेन रुधिरोद्गारमुद्वमन् .. 48.69 ..
6.3.m: Having hurled the blazing [weapon], he struck him instantly in the chest; / then, struck by that, vomiting a gush of blood, 48.69

6.3.s:
patito'dhomukho bhūtvā tataḥ śūlena bheditaḥ .
punaśca devadevena śūlena dvidalīkṛtaḥ .. 48.70 ..
6.3.d:
पतितोऽधोमुखो भूत्वा ततः शूलेन भेदितः .
पुनश्च देवदेवेन शूलेन द्विदलीकृतः .. 48.70 ..
6.3.m: he fell face downward, and then was pierced by the trident; / and again he was cleaved in two with the trident by the God of gods. 48.70

6.3.s:
śūlāgre'sau sthitaḥ pāpo bhrāntavāṃścakravattadā .
ye ye bhūmyāṃ patanti sma tatkāyādraktabindavaḥ .. 48.71 ..
6.3.d:
शूलाग्रेऽसौ स्थितः पापो भ्रान्तवांश्चक्रवत्तदा .
ये ये भूम्यां पतन्ति स्म तत्कायाद्रक्तबिन्दवः .. 48.71 ..
6.3.m: Impaled on the tip of the trident, that wicked one then spun like a wheel. / Whichever drops of blood fell to the ground from his body, 48.71

6.3.s:
te te sarve samuttasthurdānavāḥ śāstrapāṇayaḥ .
vyākulastu tato devo dānavena tarasvinā .. 48.72 ..
6.3.d:
ते ते सर्वे समुत्तस्थुर्दानवाः शास्त्रपाणयः .
व्याकुलस्तु ततो देवो दानवेन तरस्विना .. 48.72 ..
6.3.m: all those arose as Dānavas with weapons in their hands. / Then the Lord was perturbed by that mighty Dānava. 48.72

6.3.s:
devenātha smṛtā durgā cāmuṇḍā bhīṣaṇānanā .
āyātā bhīṣaṇākārā nānāyudhavirājitā .. 48.73 ..
6.3.d:
देवेनाथ स्मृता दुर्गा चामुण्डा भीषणानना .
आयाता भीषणाकारा नानायुधविराजिता .. 48.73 ..
6.3.m: Then the God remembered Durgā, Cāmuṇḍā of terrifying face; / she arrived, of formidable form, resplendent with diverse weapons, 48.73

6.3.s:
mahādaṃṣṭrā mahākāyā piṅgākṣī lambakarṇikā .
ādeśo dīyatāṃ deva ko yāsyati yamālayam .. 48.74 ..
6.3.d:
महादंष्ट्रा महाकाया पिङ्गाक्षी लम्बकर्णिका .
आदेशो दीयतां देव को यास्यति यमालयम् .. 48.74 ..
6.3.m: with huge fangs, a massive body, yellow-red eyes, and pendulous ears: / "Let the command be given, O God! Who shall go to Yama's abode?" 48.74

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
pibāsya rudhiraṃ bhadre yatheṣṭaṃ dānavasya ca .
nipatadrudhiraṃ bhūmau durge gṛhṇīṣva māciram .. 48.75 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
पिबास्य रुधिरं भद्रे यथेष्टं दानवस्य च .
निपतद्रुधिरं भूमौ दुर्गे गृह्णीष्व माचिरम् .. 48.75 ..
6.3.m: Īśvara said: / "Drink the blood of this Dānava as you please, O gentle one; / O Durgā, catch the blood falling to the ground without delay! 48.75

6.3.s:
nihanmi dānavaṃ yāvatsāhāyyaṃ kuru sundari .
evamuktā tu sā durgā papau ca rudhiraṃ tataḥ .. 48.76 ..
6.3.d:
निहन्मि दानवं यावत्साहाय्यं कुरु सुन्दरि .
एवमुक्ता तु सा दुर्गा पपौ च रुधिरं ततः .. 48.76 ..
6.3.m: Give assistance, O beautiful one, while I slay the Dānava." / Thus addressed, Durgā then drank the blood. 48.76

6.3.s:
nihatā dānavāḥ sarve deveśena sahasraśaḥ .
andhako'pi ca tān dṛṣṭvā dānavānavaniṃ gatān .
tato vāgbhiḥ pratuṣṭāva devadevaṃ maheśvaram .. 48.77 ..
6.3.d:
निहता दानवाः सर्वे देवेशेन सहस्रशः .
अन्धकोऽपि च तान् दृष्ट्वा दानवानवनिं गतान् .
ततो वाग्भिः प्रतुष्टाव देवदेवं महेश्वरम् .. 48.77 ..
6.3.m: All the Dānavas were slain by thousands by the Lord of the gods. / And Andhaka, seeing those Dānavas fallen to the earth, / then praised Maheśvara, the God of gods, with words. 48.77

6.3.s:
andhaka uvāca -
jayasva devadeveśa umārdhārdhāśarīradhṛk .
namaste devadeveśa sarvāya triguṇātmane .. 48.78 ..
6.3.d:
अन्धक उवाच -
जयस्व देवदेवेश उमार्धार्धाशरीरधृक् .
नमस्ते देवदेवेश सर्वाय त्रिगुणात्मने .. 48.78 ..
6.3.m:
Andhaka said:
Be victorious, O Lord of the gods of gods, bearing a body that is half Umā's half!
Salutations to you, O Lord of the gods of gods, to Sarva, the embodiment of the three guṇas!

6.3.s:
vṛṣabhāsanamārūḍha śaśāṅkakṛtaśekhara .
jaya khaṭvāṅgahastāya gaṅgādhara namo'stu te .. 48.79 ..
6.3.d:
वृषभासनमारूढ शशाङ्ककृतशेखर .
जय खट्वाङ्गहस्ताय गङ्गाधर नमोऽस्तु ते .. 48.79 ..
6.3.m:
Mounted on the seat of the bull, your crest formed by the moon!
Victory to him with the skull-staff in hand; O Gaṅgādhara, salutations to you!

6.3.s:
namo ḍamaruhastāya namaḥ kapālamāline .
smaradehavināśāya maheśāya namo'stu te .. 48.80 ..
6.3.d:
नमो डमरुहस्ताय नमः कपालमालिने .
स्मरदेहविनाशाय महेशाय नमोऽस्तु ते .. 48.80 ..
6.3.m:
Salutations to him with the ḍamaru drum in hand, salutations to him wearing a garland of skulls!
To the destroyer of Smara's body, to the great lord, salutations be to you!

6.3.s:
pūṣṇo dantanipātāya gaṇanāthāya te namaḥ .
jaya svarūpadehāya arūpabahurūpiṇe .. 48.81 ..
6.3.d:
पूष्णो दन्तनिपाताय गणनाथाय ते नमः .
जय स्वरूपदेहाय अरूपबहुरूपिणे .. 48.81 ..
6.3.m:
Salutations to you, the knock-downer of Pūṣan's teeth, the lord of the gaṇas!
Victory to him whose body is his own true form, who is formless and multiform!

6.3.s:
uttamāṅgavināśāya viriñcerapi śaṅkara .
śmaśānavāsine nityaṃ nityaṃ bhairavarūpiṇe .. 48.82 ..
6.3.d:
उत्तमाङ्गविनाशाय विरिञ्चेरपि शङ्कर .
श्मशानवासिने नित्यं नित्यं भैरवरूपिणे .. 48.82 ..
6.3.m:
To the destroyer of the head even of Viriñci, O Śaṅkara;
to the one who dwells constantly in the cremation ground, whose form is eternally Bhairava!

6.3.s:
tvaṃ sarvago'si tvaṃ kartā tvaṃ hartā nānya eva ca .
tvaṃ bhūmistvaṃ diśaścaiva tvaṃ gururbhārgavastathā .. 48.83 ..
6.3.d:
त्वं सर्वगोऽसि त्वं कर्ता त्वं हर्ता नान्य एव च .
त्वं भूमिस्त्वं दिशश्चैव त्वं गुरुर्भार्गवस्तथा .. 48.83 ..
6.3.m:
You are omnipresent, you are the maker, you are the destroyer, none other at all.
You are the earth, and you are the directions; you are Bṛhaspati and Bhārgava as well;

6.3.s:
sauristvaṃ devadeveśa bhūmiputrastathaiva ca .
ṛkṣagrahādikaṃ sarvaṃ yaddṛśyaṃ tattvameva ca .. 48.84 ..
6.3.d:
सौरिस्त्वं देवदेवेश भूमिपुत्रस्तथैव च .
ऋक्षग्रहादिकं सर्वं यद्दृश्यं तत्त्वमेव च .. 48.84 ..
6.3.m:
You are Śani, O Lord of the gods of gods, and likewise the son of the earth (Mars);
asterisms, planets, and all else that is visible—that is you alone!

6.3.s:
evaṃ stutiṃ tadā kṛtvā devaṃ prati sa dānavaḥ .
saṃhatābhyāṃ tu pāṇibhyāṃ praṇanāma maheśvaram .. 48.85 ..
6.3.d:
एवं स्तुतिं तदा कृत्वा देवं प्रति स दानवः .
संहताभ्यां तु पाणिभ्यां प्रणनाम महेश्वरम् .. 48.85 ..
6.3.m:
Having thus offered praise to the god, that Dānava
bowed down to Maheśvara with clasped hands.

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
sādhu sādhu mahāsattva varaṃ yācasva dānava .
dātāhaṃ yācakastvaṃ hi dadāmīha yathepsitam .. 48.86 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
साधु साधु महासत्त्व वरं याचस्व दानव .
दाताहं याचकस्त्वं हि ददामीह यथेप्सितम् .. 48.86 ..
6.3.m:
Īśvara said:
Well done, well done, O one of great fortitude! Ask a boon, O Dānava.
I am the giver and you are the petitioner; I grant here whatever you desire.

6.3.s:
andhaka uvāca -
yadi tuṣṭo'si deveśa yadi deyo varo mama .
tadātmasadṛśo'haṃ te kartavyo nāparo varaḥ .. 48.87 ..
6.3.d:
अन्धक उवाच -
यदि तुष्टोऽसि देवेश यदि देयो वरो मम .
तदात्मसदृशोऽहं ते कर्तव्यो नापरो वरः .. 48.87 ..
6.3.m:
Andhaka said:
If you are pleased, O Lord of gods, if a boon is to be given to me,
then I should be made similar to yourself; no other boon [do I ask].

6.3.s:
bhasmī jaṭī trinetrī ca triśūlī ca caturbhujaḥ .
vyāghracarmottarīyaśca nāgayajñopavītakaḥ .. 48.88 ..
6.3.d:
भस्मी जटी त्रिनेत्री च त्रिशूली च चतुर्भुजः .
व्याघ्रचर्मोत्तरीयश्च नागयज्ञोपवीतकः .. 48.88 ..
6.3.m:
Smeared with ashes, having matted hair, three-eyed, holding a trident, four-armed,
with a tiger-skin upper garment, and with a serpent sacred thread—

6.3.s: etadicchāmyahaṃ sarvaṃ yadi tuṣṭo maheśvara .. 48.89 ..
6.3.d: एतदिच्छाम्यहं सर्वं यदि तुष्टो महेश्वर .. 48.89 ..
6.3.m: all this I desire, O Maheśvara, if you are pleased.

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
dadāmi te varaṃ hyadya yastvayā yācito'nagha .
gaṇeṣu me sthitaḥ putra bhṛṅgīśastvaṃ bhaviṣyasi .. 48.90 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe'ndhakavadhatadvarapradānavarṇanaṃ nāmāṣṭacatvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 49
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
ददामि ते वरं ह्यद्य यस्त्वया याचितोऽनघ .
गणेषु मे स्थितः पुत्र भृङ्गीशस्त्वं भविष्यसि .. 48.90 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डेऽन्धकवधतद्वरप्रदानवर्णनं नामाष्टचत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 49
6.3.m:
Īśvara said:
I indeed grant you today the boon that has been asked by you, O sinless one.
Abiding among my gaṇas, O son, you shall become Bhṛṅgīśa.
Thus ends the forty-eighth chapter, named 'Description of the Slaying of Andhaka and Granting Him a Boon', in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth, Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 49

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
andhakaṃ tu nihatyātha devadevo maheśvaraḥ .
umayā sahito rudraḥ kailāsamagamannagam .. 49.1 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
अन्धकं तु निहत्याथ देवदेवो महेश्वरः .
उमया सहितो रुद्रः कैलासमगमन्नगम् .. 49.1 ..
6.3.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Then, having slain Andhaka, Maheśvara, the god of gods,
Rudra together with Umā, went to Mount Kailāsa.

6.3.s:
āgatāśca tato devā brahmādyāśca savāsavāḥ .
hṛṣṭāstuṣṭāśca te sarve praṇemuḥ pārvatīpatim .. 49.2 ..
6.3.d:
आगताश्च ततो देवा ब्रह्माद्याश्च सवासवाः .
हृष्टास्तुष्टाश्च ते सर्वे प्रणेमुः पार्वतीपतिम् .. 49.2 ..
6.3.m:
And then the gods arrived, Brahmā and others together with Indra;
delighted and pleased, they all bowed to the husband of Pārvatī.

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
upāviśantu te sarve ye kecana samāgatāḥ .
nihato dānavo hyeṣa gīrvāṇārthe pitāmaha .. 49.3 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
उपाविशन्तु ते सर्वे ये केचन समागताः .
निहतो दानवो ह्येष गीर्वाणार्थे पितामह .. 49.3 ..

6.3.s:
raktena tasya me śūlaṃ nirmalaṃ naiva jāyate .
śubhavratatapojapyarato brahmanmayā hataḥ .. 49.4 ..
6.3.d:
रक्तेन तस्य मे शूलं निर्मलं नैव जायते .
शुभव्रततपोजप्यरतो ब्रह्मन्मया हतः .. 49.4 ..
6.3.m:
by his blood my trident does not become clean at all.
Devoted to auspicious vows, austerity, and prayers, O Brahmā, he was slain by me.

6.3.s:
kartumicchāmyahaṃ samyaktīrthayānaṃ caturmukha .
āgacchantu mayā sārddhaṃ ye yūyamiha saṃgatāḥ .. 49.5 ..
6.3.d:
कर्तुमिच्छाम्यहं सम्यक्तीर्थयानं चतुर्मुख .
आगच्छन्तु मया सार्द्धं ये यूयमिह संगताः .. 49.5 ..
6.3.m:
I desire to undertake a pilgrimage to sacred fords properly, O Four-faced One;
let all of you who have assembled here come along with me.

6.3.s:
ityuktvā devadeveśaḥ prabhāsaṃ pratiniryayau .
prabhāsādyāni tīrthāni gaṅgāsāgaramadhyataḥ .. 49.6 ..
6.3.d:
इत्युक्त्वा देवदेवेशः प्रभासं प्रतिनिर्ययौ .
प्रभासाद्यानि तीर्थानि गङ्गासागरमध्यतः .. 49.6 ..
6.3.m:
Having spoken thus, the Lord of the gods of gods set forth towards Prabhāsa.
Sacred fords beginning with Prabhāsa, as far as the midst of Gaṅgāsāgara—

6.3.s:
avagāhyāpi sarvāṇi nairmalyaṃ nābhavannṛpa .
narmadāyāṃ tato gatvā devo devaiḥ samanvitaḥ .. 49.7 ..
6.3.d:
अवगाह्यापि सर्वाणि नैर्मल्यं नाभवन्नृप .
नर्मदायां ततो गत्वा देवो देवैः समन्वितः .. 49.7 ..
6.3.m:
even having bathed in all of them, O king, purity did not occur.
Then, having gone to the Narmadā, the god, accompanied by the gods,

6.3.s:
uttaraṃ dakṣiṇaṃ kūlamavāgāhatpriyavrataḥ .
gatastu dakṣiṇe kūle parvate bhṛgusaṃjñitam .. 49.8 ..
6.3.d:
उत्तरं दक्षिणं कूलमवागाहत्प्रियव्रतः .
गतस्तु दक्षिणे कूले पर्वते भृगुसंज्ञितम् .. 49.8 ..
6.3.m:
fond of vows, bathed on both the northern and the southern bank.
And having gone to the southern bank, onto the mountain named after Bhṛgu,

6.3.s:
tatra sthitvā mahādevo devaiḥ saha mahīpate .
bhrāntvā bhrāntvā ciraṃ śrānto nirviṇṇo niṣasāda ha .. 49.9 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र स्थित्वा महादेवो देवैः सह महीपते .
भ्रान्त्वा भ्रान्त्वा चिरं श्रान्तो निर्विण्णो निषसाद ह .. 49.9 ..
6.3.m:
dwelling there, O lord of earth, Mahādeva together with the gods,
having wandered long, tired and despondent, sat down.

6.3.s:
manohāri yataḥ sthānaṃ sarveṣāṃ vai divaukasām .
tīrthaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ tanmatvā sthito devo maheśvaraḥ .. 49.10 ..
6.3.d:
मनोहारि यतः स्थानं सर्वेषां वै दिवौकसाम् .
तीर्थं विशिष्टं तन्मत्वा स्थितो देवो महेश्वरः .. 49.10 ..
6.3.m:
Since the place was enchanting to all the celestials,
considering that sacred ford distinguished, the god Maheśvara stayed there.

6.3.s:
giriṃ vivyādha śūlena bhinnaṃ tena rasātalam .
nirmalaṃ cābhavacchūlaṃ na lepo dṛśyate kvacit .. 49.11 ..
6.3.d:
गिरिं विव्याध शूलेन भिन्नं तेन रसातलम् .
निर्मलं चाभवच्छूलं न लेपो दृश्यते क्वचित् .. 49.11 ..
6.3.m:
He pierced the mountain with his trident, and Rasātala was split open by it;
and the trident became clean; no stain was visible anywhere.

6.3.s:
devairāhvānitā tatra mahāpuṇyā ca bhāratī .
parvatānniḥsṛtā tatra mahāpuṇyā sarasvatī .. 49.12 ..
6.3.d:
देवैराह्वानिता तत्र महापुण्या च भारती .
पर्वतान्निःसृता तत्र महापुण्या सरस्वती .. 49.12 ..
6.3.m:
The most meritorious Bhāratī was summoned there by the gods;
and the most meritorious Sarasvatī flowed out from the mountain there.

6.3.s:
dvitīyaḥ saṅgamastatra yathā veṇyāṃ sitāsitaḥ .
tatra brahmā svayaṃ devo brahmeśaṃ liṅgamuttamam .. 49.13 ..
6.3.d:
द्वितीयः सङ्गमस्तत्र यथा वेण्यां सितासितः .
तत्र ब्रह्मा स्वयं देवो ब्रह्मेशं लिङ्गमुत्तमम् .. 49.13 ..
6.3.m:
A second confluence is there, like the dark and white [waters] at the Veṇī;
there, the god Brahmā himself [consecrated] the excellent liṅga Brahmeśa.

6.3.s:
saṃsthāpayāmāsa puṇyaṃ sarvaduḥkhaghnamuttamam .
tasya yāmye diśo bhāge svayaṃ devo janārdanaḥ .. 49.14 ..
6.3.d:
संस्थापयामास पुण्यं सर्वदुःखघ्नमुत्तमम् .
तस्य याम्ये दिशो भागे स्वयं देवो जनार्दनः .. 49.14 ..
6.3.m:
He established the meritorious, supreme [liṅga], destroyer of all sorrow.
In the southern quarter thereof, the god Janārdana himself

6.3.s:
tiṣṭhate ca sadā tatra viṣṇupādāgrasaṃsthitā .
ambhaso na bhavenmārgaḥ kuṇḍamadhyasthitasya ca .. 49.15 ..
6.3.d:
तिष्ठते च सदा तत्र विष्णुपादाग्रसंस्थिता .
अम्भसो न भवेन्मार्गः कुण्डमध्यस्थितस्य च .. 49.15 ..
6.3.m:
remains always there, standing before the foot of Viṣṇu.
There would be no path for the water resting in the middle of the pool;

6.3.s:
śūlāgreṇa kṛtā rekhā tatastoyaṃ vahennṛpa .
tattoyaṃ ca gataṃ tatra yatra revā mahānadī .. 49.16 ..
6.3.d:
शूलाग्रेण कृता रेखा ततस्तोयं वहेन्नृप .
तत्तोयं च गतं तत्र यत्र रेवा महानदी .. 49.16 ..
6.3.m:
a furrow was drawn with the tip of the trident, and from it the water flowed, O king;
and that water went to where the great river Revā is.

6.3.s:
jalaliṅgaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ cakatīrthaṃ nṛpottama .
śūlabhede ca deveśaḥ snānaṃ kuryādyathāvidhi .. 49.17 ..
6.3.d:
जललिङ्गं महापुण्यं चकतीर्थं नृपोत्तम .
शूलभेदे च देवेशः स्नानं कुर्याद्यथाविधि .. 49.17 ..
6.3.m:
The most meritorious water-liṅga, a radiant sacred ford, O best of kings—
at Śūlabheda, if the lord of gods should perform his ritual ablution according to rule,

6.3.s:
ātmānaṃ manyate śuddhaṃ na kiṃcitkalmaṣaṃ kṛtam .
tasyaivottarakāṣṭhāyāṃ devadevo jagadguruḥ .. 49.18 ..
6.3.d:
आत्मानं मन्यते शुद्धं न किंचित्कल्मषं कृतम् .
तस्यैवोत्तरकाष्ठायां देवदेवो जगद्गुरुः .. 49.18 ..
6.3.m:
he considers himself pure, with no blemish remaining.
On its northern side, the god of gods, the teacher of the world,

6.3.s:
ātmanā devadeveśaḥ śūlapāṇiḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ .
sarvatīrtheṣu tattīrthaṃ sarvadevamayaṃ param .. 49.19 ..
6.3.d:
आत्मना देवदेवेशः शूलपाणिः प्रतिष्ठितः .
सर्वतीर्थेषु तत्तीर्थं सर्वदेवमयं परम् .. 49.19 ..
6.3.m:
the trident-handed Lord of the gods of gods, established himself.
Among all sacred fords, that sacred ford is supreme, embodying all the gods,

6.3.s:
sarvapāpaharaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvaduḥkhaghnamuttamam .
tatra tīrthe pratiṣṭhāpya devadevaṃ jagadguruḥ .. 49.20 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वपापहरं पुण्यं सर्वदुःखघ्नमुत्तमम् .
तत्र तीर्थे प्रतिष्ठाप्य देवदेवं जगद्गुरुः .. 49.20 ..
6.3.m:
destroying all sins, meritorious, the best destroyer of all sorrows.
Having installed the god of gods at that sacred ford, the teacher of the world,

6.3.s:
rakṣāpālāṃstato muktvā śataṃ sāṣṭavināyakān .
kṣetrapālāḥ śataṃ sāṣṭaṃ tadrakṣanti prayatnataḥ .. 49.21 ..
6.3.d:
रक्षापालांस्ततो मुक्त्वा शतं साष्टविनायकान् .
क्षेत्रपालाः शतं साष्टं तद्रक्षन्ति प्रयत्नतः .. 49.21 ..
6.3.m:
having stationed guardian deities there, one hundred and eight Vināyakas,
one hundred and eight guardians of the field protect it with effort.

6.3.s:
vighnāstasyopajāyante yastatra sthātumicchati .
kecitkuṭumbāttatāsu vyāgrāḥ kecitkṛṣīṣu ca .. 49.22 ..
6.3.d:
विघ्नास्तस्योपजायन्ते यस्तत्र स्थातुमिच्छति .
केचित्कुटुम्बात्ततासु व्याग्राः केचित्कृषीषु च .. 49.22 ..
6.3.m:
Obstacles arise for anyone who wishes to stay there:
some are preoccupied with family and children, some in agricultural works;

6.3.s:
kecitsabhāṃ prakurvanti keciddravyārjane ratāḥ .
parokṣavādaṃ kurvanti ke'pi hiṃsāratāḥ sadā .. 49.23 ..
6.3.d:
केचित्सभां प्रकुर्वन्ति केचिद्द्रव्यार्जने रताः .
परोक्षवादं कुर्वन्ति केऽपि हिंसारताः सदा .. 49.23 ..
6.3.m:
some hold assemblies, some are devoted to accumulating wealth;
some speak ill behind backs, and some are always intent on harm;

6.3.s:
paradāraratāḥ kecitkecidvṛttivihiṃsakāḥ .
anye kecidvadantyevaṃ kathaṃ tīrtheṣu gamyate .. 49.24 ..
6.3.d:
परदाररताः केचित्केचिद्वृत्तिविहिंसकाः .
अन्ये केचिद्वदन्त्येवं कथं तीर्थेषु गम्यते .. 49.24 ..
6.3.m:
some are attached to others' wives, some destroy livelihoods;
others say thus: 'How can one go to sacred fords?

6.3.s:
kṣudhayā pīḍyate bhāryā putrabhṛtyādayastadā .
mohajāleṣu yojyante evaṃ devagaṇairnarāḥ .. 49.25 ..
6.3.d:
क्षुधया पीड्यते भार्या पुत्रभृत्यादयस्तदा .
मोहजालेषु योज्यन्ते एवं देवगणैर्नराः .. 49.25 ..
6.3.m:
A wife, sons, servants, and others are afflicted by hunger then.'
Thus men are entangled in webs of delusion by the hosts of the gods.

6.3.s:
pāpācārāśca ye martyāḥ snānaṃ teṣāṃ na jāyate .
saṃrakṣanti ca tattīrthaṃ devabhṛtyagaṇāḥ sadā .. 49.26 ..
6.3.d:
पापाचाराश्च ये मर्त्याः स्नानं तेषां न जायते .
संरक्षन्ति च तत्तीर्थं देवभृत्यगणाः सदा .. 49.26 ..
6.3.m:
And mortals of sinful conduct—their ritual ablution does not take place;
and the attendant hosts of the gods guard that sacred ford always.

6.3.s:
dhanyāḥ puṇyāśca ye martyāsteṣāṃ snānaṃ prajāyate .
sarasvatyā bhogavatyā devanadyā viśeṣataḥ .. 49.27 ..
6.3.d:
धन्याः पुण्याश्च ये मर्त्यास्तेषां स्नानं प्रजायते .
सरस्वत्या भोगवत्या देवनद्या विशेषतः .. 49.27 ..
6.3.m:
Mortals who are fortunate and meritorious—their ritual ablution takes place,
especially in the celestial river Sarasvatī, the Bhogavatī.

6.3.s:
ayaṃ tu saṅgamaḥ puṇyo yathā veṇyāṃ sitāsitaḥ .
dṛṣṭvā tīrthaṃ tu te sarve gīrvāṇā hṛṣṭacetasaḥ .. 49.28 ..
6.3.d:
अयं तु सङ्गमः पुण्यो यथा वेण्यां सितासितः .
दृष्ट्वा तीर्थं तु ते सर्वे गीर्वाणा हृष्टचेतसः .. 49.28 ..
6.3.m:
This is a meritorious confluence, like the dark and white [waters] at the Veṇī.
Having seen that sacred ford, all those gods, glad at heart,

6.3.s:
devasya sannidhau bhūtvā varṇayāmāsuruttamam .
idaṃ tīrthaṃ tu deveśa gayātīrthena te samam .. 49.29 ..
6.3.d:
देवस्य सन्निधौ भूत्वा वर्णयामासुरुत्तमम् .
इदं तीर्थं तु देवेश गयातीर्थेन ते समम् .. 49.29 ..
6.3.m:
came into the presence of the god and described it as supreme:
'This sacred ford, O Lord of gods, is equal to the sacred ford of Gayā for you.'

6.3.s:
guhyādguhyatamaṃ tīrthaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati .
śūlapāṇiḥ samabhyarcya indrādyairapsarogaṇaiḥ .. 49.30 ..
6.3.d:
गुह्याद्गुह्यतमं तीर्थं न भूतं न भविष्यति .
शूलपाणिः समभ्यर्च्य इन्द्राद्यैरप्सरोगणैः .. 49.30 ..
6.3.m: A sacred ford more secret than the secret, there never was nor will there be. / Having worshipped the Trident-bearer, along with Indra and the other hosts of apsarases,

6.3.s:
yakṣakinnaragandharvairdikpālairlokapairapi .
nṛtyagītaistathā stotraiḥ sarvaiścāpi surāsuraiḥ .. 49.31 ..
6.3.d:
यक्षकिन्नरगन्धर्वैर्दिक्पालैर्लोकपैरपि .
नृत्यगीतैस्तथा स्तोत्रैः सर्वैश्चापि सुरासुरैः .. 49.31 ..
6.3.m: along with yakṣas, kinnaras, gandharvas, guardians of the directions, and world-protectors, / with dances, songs, and praises, by all the gods and asuras,

6.3.s:
pūjyamāno gaṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ siddhairnāgairmaheśvaraḥ .
devena bheditaṃ tatra śūlāgreṇa narādhipa .. 49.32 ..
6.3.d:
पूज्यमानो गणैः सर्वैः सिद्धैर्नागैर्महेश्वरः .
देवेन भेदितं तत्र शूलाग्रेण नराधिप .. 49.32 ..
6.3.m: Maheśvara was worshipped by all the hosts, siddhas, and serpents. / O king, [the ground] was pierced there by the god with the tip of his trident,

6.3.s:
tridhā yatrekṣyate'dyāpi hyāvartaḥ surapūritaḥ .
kuṇḍatrayaṃ naravyāghra mahatkalakalānvitam .. 49.33 ..
6.3.d:
त्रिधा यत्रेक्ष्यतेऽद्यापि ह्यावर्तः सुरपूरितः .
कुण्डत्रयं नरव्याघ्र महत्कलकलान्वितम् .. 49.33 ..
6.3.m: where even today a whirlpool filled by the gods is seen divided threefold, / a triad of pools, O tiger among men, accompanied by a great murmuring sound,

6.3.s:
sarvapāpakṣayakaraṃ sarvaduḥkhaghnamuttamam .
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ snāti upavāsaparāyaṇaḥ .. 49.34 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वपापक्षयकरं सर्वदुःखघ्नमुत्तमम् .
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः स्नाति उपवासपरायणः .. 49.34 ..
6.3.m: destroying all sins, supreme, dispelling all sorrow. / Whoever bathes in that sacred ford, dedicated to fasting,

6.3.s:
dīkṣāmantravihīno'pi mucyate cābdikādaghāt .
ye punarvidhivatsnānti mantraiḥ pañcabhireva ca .. 49.35 ..
6.3.d:
दीक्षामन्त्रविहीनोऽपि मुच्यते चाब्दिकादघात् .
ये पुनर्विधिवत्स्नान्ति मन्त्रैः पञ्चभिरेव च .. 49.35 ..
6.3.m: even if devoid of initiation and mantra, is freed from the sin of a whole year. / Those, however, who bathe according to rule with the five mantras,

6.3.s:
vedoktaiḥ pañcabhirmantraiḥ sahiraṇyaghaṭaiḥ śubhaiḥ .
akṣarairdaśabhiścaiva ṣaḍbhirvā tribhireva vā .. 49.36 ..
6.3.d:
वेदोक्तैः पञ्चभिर्मन्त्रैः सहिरण्यघटैः शुभैः .
अक्षरैर्दशभिश्चैव षड्भिर्वा त्रिभिरेव वा .. 49.36 ..
6.3.m: with the five mantras proclaimed in the Veda, with auspicious jars containing gold, / or with ten syllables, or six, or three,

6.3.s:
pṛthagbhūtairdvijātīnāṃ tīrthe kāryaṃ narādhipa .
brahmakṣatraviśāṃ vāpi strīśūdrāṇāṃ tathaiva ca .. 49.37 ..
6.3.d:
पृथग्भूतैर्द्विजातीनां तीर्थे कार्यं नराधिप .
ब्रह्मक्षत्रविशां वापि स्त्रीशूद्राणां तथैव च .. 49.37 ..
6.3.m: distinctly for the twice-born, it must be performed at the sacred ford, O king; / or for brahmins, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas, and likewise for women and śūdras.

6.3.s:
puruṣāṇāṃ trayīṃ dhyātvā snānaṃ kuryādyathāvidhi .
daśākṣareṇa mantreṇa ye pibanti jalaṃ narāḥ .. 49.38 ..
6.3.d:
पुरुषाणां त्रयीं ध्यात्वा स्नानं कुर्याद्यथाविधि .
दशाक्षरेण मन्त्रेण ये पिबन्ति जलं नराः .. 49.38 ..
6.3.m: Having meditated upon the triad of persons, one should perform the ritual ablution according to rule. / The men who drink the water with the ten-syllabled mantra,

6.3.s:
te gacchanti paraṃ lokaṃ yatra devo maheśvaraḥ .
kedāre ca yathā pītaṃ rudrakuṇḍe tathaiva ca .. 49.39 ..
6.3.d:
ते गच्छन्ति परं लोकं यत्र देवो महेश्वरः .
केदारे च यथा पीतं रुद्रकुण्डे तथैव च .. 49.39 ..
6.3.m: they go to the supreme realm where the god Maheśvara is, / just as if drunk at Kedāra, and likewise at the Rudrakuṇḍa.

6.3.s:
pañcarephasamāyuktaṃ kṣakāraṃ surapūjitam .
oṅkāreṇa samāyuktametadvedyaṃ prakīrtitam .. 49.40 ..
6.3.d:
पञ्चरेफसमायुक्तं क्षकारं सुरपूजितम् .
ओङ्कारेण समायुक्तमेतद्वेद्यं प्रकीर्तितम् .. 49.40 ..
6.3.m: Equipped with five rephas, the letter kṣa is worshipped by the gods; / joined with the oṃkāra, this is proclaimed to be the object of knowledge.

6.3.s:
yastatra kurute snānaṃ vidhiyukto jitendriyaḥ .
tilamiśreṇa toyena tarpayetpitṛdevatāḥ .. 49.41 ..
6.3.d:
यस्तत्र कुरुते स्नानं विधियुक्तो जितेन्द्रियः .
तिलमिश्रेण तोयेन तर्पयेत्पितृदेवताः .. 49.41 ..
6.3.m: He who performs ritual ablution there, endowed with the rites, with senses controlled, / should offer libations to the ancestral gods with water mixed with sesame.

6.3.s:
kulānāṃ tārayedviṃśaṃ daśapūrvāndaśāparān .
gayādipañcasthāneṣu yaḥ śrāddhaṃ kurute naraḥ .. 49.42 ..
6.3.d:
कुलानां तारयेद्विंशं दशपूर्वान्दशापरान् .
गयादिपञ्चस्थानेषु यः श्राद्धं कुरुते नरः .. 49.42 ..
6.3.m: He delivers twenty generations: ten preceding and ten succeeding. / The person who performs a śrāddha in the five places beginning with Gayā,

6.3.s:
sa tatra phalamāpnoti śūlabhede na saṃśayaḥ .
yastatra vidhinā yukto dadyāddānāni bhaktitaḥ .. 49.43 ..
6.3.d:
स तत्र फलमाप्नोति शूलभेदे न संशयः .
यस्तत्र विधिना युक्तो दद्याद्दानानि भक्तितः .. 49.43 ..
6.3.m: he obtains that same fruit at Śūlabheda, without a doubt. / He who, observing proper rites, bestows gifts there with devotion,

6.3.s:
tudakṣayaṃ phalaṃ tatra sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ tathā .
gayāśiro yathā puṇyaṃ pitṛkāryeṣu sarvadā .. 49.44 ..
6.3.d:
तुदक्षयं फलं तत्र सुकृतं दुष्कृतं तथा .
गयाशिरो यथा पुण्यं पितृकार्येषु सर्वदा .. 49.44 ..
6.3.m: imperishable is the fruit thereof, whether good deeds or bad deeds. / Just as Gayāśiras is ever meritorious in ancestral rites,

6.3.s:
śūlabhedaṃ tathā puṇyaṃ snānadānāditarpaṇaiḥ .
bhaktyā dadāti yastatra kāñcanaṃ gāṃ mahīṃ tilān .. 49.45 ..
6.3.d:
शूलभेदं तथा पुण्यं स्नानदानादितर्पणैः .
भक्त्या ददाति यस्तत्र काञ्चनं गां महीं तिलान् .. 49.45 ..
6.3.m: so Śūlabheda is meritorious through ritual ablutions, gifts, and libations. / Whoever gives there with devotion gold, a cow, land, sesame seeds,

6.3.s:
āsanopānahau śayyāṃ varāśvān kṣatriyastathā .
vastrayugmaṃ ca dhānyaṃ ca gṛhaṃ pūrṇaṃ prayatnataḥ .. 49.46 ..
6.3.d:
आसनोपानहौ शय्यां वराश्वान् क्षत्रियस्तथा .
वस्त्रयुग्मं च धान्यं च गृहं पूर्णं प्रयत्नतः .. 49.46 ..
6.3.m: a seat, sandals, a bed, and likewise a kṣatriya [who gives] excellent horses, / a pair of garments, grain, and carefully [gives] a fully furnished house,

6.3.s:
sayoktraṃ lāṅgalaṃ dadyātkṛṣṭāṃ caiva vasuṃdharām .
dānānyetāni yo dadyādbrāhmaṇe vedapārage .. 49.47 ..
6.3.d:
सयोक्त्रं लाङ्गलं दद्यात्कृष्टां चैव वसुंधराम् .
दानान्येतानि यो दद्याद्ब्राह्मणे वेदपारगे .. 49.47 ..
6.3.m: and gives a plow with its yoke and cultivated earth— / who gives these gifts to a brahmin who has mastered the Vedas,

6.3.s:
śrotriye kulasampanne śuciṣmati jitendriye .
śrutādhyayanasampanne dambhahīne kriyānvite .
trayodaśāhaḥsvekaikaṃ trayodaśaguṇaṃ bhavet .. 49.48 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe śūlabhedotpattimāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmaikonapañcāśattamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 50
6.3.d:
श्रोत्रिये कुलसम्पन्ने शुचिष्मति जितेन्द्रिये .
श्रुताध्ययनसम्पन्ने दम्भहीने क्रियान्विते .
त्रयोदशाहःस्वेकैकं त्रयोदशगुणं भवेत् .. 49.48 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे शूलभेदोत्पत्तिमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामैकोनपञ्चाशत्तमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 50
6.3.m:
a Vedic scholar of noble family, pure, with senses subdued, / endowed with learning and study of scripture, devoid of hypocrisy, engaged in rituals— / each gift shall become thirteenfold on the thirteenth day.
Thus ends the forty-ninth chapter, entitled "Description of the Glorification of the Origin of Śūlabheda," in the Revākhaṇḍa of the Āvantyakhaṇḍa in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 50

6.3.s:
uttānapāda uvāca -
dvijāśca kīdṛśāḥ pūjyā apūjyāḥ kīdṛśāḥ smṛtāḥ .
śrāddhe vaivāhike kārye dāne caiva viśeṣataḥ .. 50.1 ..
6.3.d:
उत्तानपाद उवाच -
द्विजाश्च कीदृशाः पूज्या अपूज्याः कीदृशाः स्मृताः .
श्राद्धे वैवाहिके कार्ये दाने चैव विशेषतः .. 50.1 ..
6.3.m: Uttānapāda said: / What kind of twice-born are worthy of worship, and what kind are remembered as unworthy of worship, / in ancestral rites, in marital rites, and especially in giving?

6.3.s:
yadi śraddhā bhaveddaivayogācchrāddhādike vidhau .
etadākhyāhi me deva kasya dānaṃ na dīyate .. 50.2 ..
6.3.d:
यदि श्रद्धा भवेद्दैवयोगाच्छ्राद्धादिके विधौ .
एतदाख्याहि मे देव कस्य दानं न दीयते .. 50.2 ..
6.3.m: If faith should arise through destiny in the rites of śrāddha and the like, / tell me this, O God: to whom should a gift not be given?

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
yathā kāṣṭhamayo hastī yathā carmamayo mṛgaḥ .
brāhmaṇaścānadhīyānastrayaste nāmadhārakāḥ .. 50.3 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
यथा काष्ठमयो हस्ती यथा चर्ममयो मृगः .
ब्राह्मणश्चानधीयानस्त्रयस्ते नामधारकाः .. 50.3 ..
6.3.m: Īśvara said: / Just as a wooden elephant, just as a leather deer, / so is an unlearned brahmin: these three are bearers of the name only.

6.3.s:
yathā ṣaṇḍho'phalaḥ strīṣu yathā gaurgavi cāphalā .
yathā cājñe'phalaṃ dānaṃ tathā vipro'nṛco'phalaḥ .. 50.4 ..
6.3.d:
यथा षण्ढोऽफलः स्त्रीषु यथा गौर्गवि चाफला .
यथा चाज्ञेऽफलं दानं तथा विप्रोऽनृचोऽफलः .. 50.4 ..
6.3.m: Just as a eunuch is fruitless among women, just as a cow with a cow is fruitless, / and just as a gift given to an ignorant man is fruitless, so a brahmin devoid of the Ṛgveda is fruitless.

6.3.s:
yathā'nṛṇe bījamuptvā vaptā na labhate phalam .
tathānṛce havirdattvā na dātā labhate phalam .. 50.5 ..
6.3.d:
यथाऽनृणे बीजमुप्त्वा वप्ता न लभते फलम् .
तथानृचे हविर्दत्त्वा न दाता लभते फलम् .. 50.5 ..
6.3.m: Just as a sower who sows seed in barren ground obtains no fruit, / so the giver who offers an oblation to one ignorant of the Ṛgveda obtains no fruit.

6.3.s:
rogī hīnātiriktāṅgaḥ kāṇaḥ paunarbhavastathā .
avakīrṇī śyāvadantaḥ sarvāśī vṛṣalīpatiḥ .. 50.6 ..
6.3.d:
रोगी हीनातिरिक्ताङ्गः काणः पौनर्भवस्तथा .
अवकीर्णी श्यावदन्तः सर्वाशी वृषलीपतिः .. 50.6 ..
6.3.m: One who is diseased, missing or having redundant limbs, one-eyed, born of a remarried woman, / a vow-breaker, one with dark teeth, an indiscriminate eater, the husband of a śūdra woman,

6.3.s:
mitradhrukpiśunaḥ somavikrayī paranindakaḥ .
pitṛmātṛgurutyāgī nityaṃ brāhmaṇanindakaḥ .. 50.7 ..
6.3.d:
मित्रध्रुक्पिशुनः सोमविक्रयी परनिन्दकः .
पितृमातृगुरुत्यागी नित्यं ब्राह्मणनिन्दकः .. 50.7 ..
6.3.m: a betrayer of friends, a slanderer, a seller of soma, a vilifier of others, / an abandoner of mother, father, and teacher, one who constantly reviles brahmins,

6.3.s:
śūdrānnaṃ mantrasaṃyuktaṃ yo vipro bhakṣayennṛpa .
so'spṛśyaḥ karmacāṇḍālaḥ spṛṣṭvā snānaṃ samācaret .. 50.8 ..
6.3.d:
शूद्रान्नं मन्त्रसंयुक्तं यो विप्रो भक्षयेन्नृप .
सोऽस्पृश्यः कर्मचाण्डालः स्पृष्ट्वा स्नानं समाचरेत् .. 50.8 ..
6.3.m: the brahmin who eats food from a śūdra accompanied by mantras, O king, / is untouchable, an outcaste by deed; having touched him, one must bathe.

6.3.s:
kunakhī vṛṣalī steyī vārddhuṣyaḥ kuṇḍagolakau .
mahādānarato yaśca yaścātmahanane rataḥ .. 50.9 ..
6.3.d:
कुनखी वृषली स्तेयी वार्द्धुष्यः कुण्डगोलकौ .
महादानरतो यश्च यश्चात्महनने रतः .. 50.9 ..
6.3.m: One with diseased nails, a śūdra woman’s husband, a thief, a usurer, sons born of adultery or widowhood, / one intent on receiving great gifts, and one intent on suicide,

6.3.s:
bhṛtakādhyāpakaḥ klībaḥ kanyādūṣyabhiśastakaḥ .
ete viprāḥ sadā tyājyāḥ paribhāvya prayatnataḥ .. 50.10 ..
6.3.d:
भृतकाध्यापकः क्लीबः कन्यादूष्यभिशस्तकः .
एते विप्राः सदा त्याज्याः परिभाव्य प्रयत्नतः .. 50.10 ..
6.3.m: a hired teacher, an impotent man, a defiler of maidens, one falsely or truly accused— / these brahmins should always be avoided with careful consideration.

6.3.s:
pratigrahaṃ gṛhītvā tu vāṇijyaṃ yastu kārayet .
tasya dānaṃ na dātavyaṃ vṛthā bhavati tasya tat .. 50.11 ..
6.3.d:
प्रतिग्रहं गृहीत्वा तु वाणिज्यं यस्तु कारयेत् .
तस्य दानं न दातव्यं वृथा भवति तस्य तत् .. 50.11 ..
6.3.m: He who takes gifts and engages in trade, / to him no gift must be given; that [gift] becomes useless to him.

6.3.s:
śrutādhyayanasampannā ye dvijā vṛttatatparāḥ .
teṣāṃ yaddīyate dānaṃ sarvamakṣayatāṃ vrajet .. 50.12 ..
6.3.d:
श्रुताध्ययनसम्पन्ना ये द्विजा वृत्ततत्पराः .
तेषां यद्दीयते दानं सर्वमक्षयतां व्रजेत् .. 50.12 ..
6.3.m: The twice-born who are endowed with learning and study of scripture, devoted to right conduct, / whatever gift is given to them, all becomes imperishable.

6.3.s:
daridrānbhara bhūpāla mā samṛddhān kadācana .
vyādhitasyauṣadhaṃ pathyaṃ nīrujasya kimauṣadhaiḥ .. 50.13 ..
6.3.d:
दरिद्रान्भर भूपाल मा समृद्धान् कदाचन .
व्याधितस्यौषधं पथ्यं नीरुजस्य किमौषधैः .. 50.13 ..
6.3.m: Support the poor, O ruler of the earth, never the affluent; / medicine is beneficial to the diseased: what use is medicine to the healthy?

6.3.s:
uttānapāda uvāca -
kīdṛśo'tha vidhistatra tīrthaśrāddhasya kā kriyā .
dānaṃ ca dīyate yadvattanmamākhyāhi śaṅkara .. 50.14 ..
6.3.d:
उत्तानपाद उवाच -
कीदृशोऽथ विधिस्तत्र तीर्थश्राद्धस्य का क्रिया .
दानं च दीयते यद्वत्तन्ममाख्याहि शङ्कर .. 50.14 ..
6.3.m: Uttānapāda said: / What is the proper rule there, and what is the rite for a śrāddha at a sacred ford? / And how is a gift given? Tell me that, O Śaṅkara.

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
śrāddhaṃ kṛtvā gṛhe bhaktyā śuciścāpi jitendriyaḥ .
guruṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhojya sīmāntake tataḥ .. 50.15 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
श्राद्धं कृत्वा गृहे भक्त्या शुचिश्चापि जितेन्द्रियः .
गुरुं प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य भोज्य सीमान्तके ततः .. 50.15 ..
6.3.m: Īśvara said: / Having performed a śrāddha at home with devotion, pure and with subdued senses, / having circumambulated the teacher, and then having fed [him] at the boundary,

6.3.s:
vāgyataḥ pravrajettāvadyāvatsīmāṃ na laṅghayet .
śūlabhedaṃ tato gatvā snānaṃ kuryādyathāvidhi .. 50.16 ..
6.3.d:
वाग्यतः प्रव्रजेत्तावद्यावत्सीमां न लङ्घयेत् .
शूलभेदं ततो गत्वा स्नानं कुर्याद्यथाविधि .. 50.16 ..
6.3.m: one should proceed restrained in speech as long as one does not cross the boundary. / Then, having gone to Śūlabheda, one should perform the ritual ablution according to rule,

6.3.s:
pañcasthāneṣu ca śrāddhaṃ havyakavyādibhiḥ kramāt .
piṇḍadānaṃ ca yaḥ kuryātpāyasairmadhusarpiṣā .. 50.17 ..
6.3.d:
पञ्चस्थानेषु च श्राद्धं हव्यकव्यादिभिः क्रमात् .
पिण्डदानं च यः कुर्यात्पायसैर्मधुसर्पिषा .. 50.17 ..
6.3.m: and perform a śrāddha in the five places with offerings to gods and ancestors in order. / And whoever performs the offering of rice-balls with milk-rice, honey, and clarified butter,

6.3.s:
pitarastasya tṛpyanti dvādaśābdāni pañca ca .
akṣatairbadarairbilvairgudamadhusarpiṣā .. 50.18 ..
6.3.d:
पितरस्तस्य तृप्यन्ति द्वादशाब्दानि पञ्च च .
अक्षतैर्बदरैर्बिल्वैर्गुदमधुसर्पिषा .. 50.18 ..
6.3.m: his ancestors are satisfied for five and twelve years. / With unbroken grains, jujubes, bilva leaves, jaggery, honey, and clarified butter,

6.3.s:
sāpi tatphalamāpnoti tīrthe'sminnātra saṃśayaḥ .
upānahau ca yo dadyādbrāhmaṇebhyaḥ prayatnataḥ .. 50.19 ..
6.3.d:
सापि तत्फलमाप्नोति तीर्थेऽस्मिन्नात्र संशयः .
उपानहौ च यो दद्याद्ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रयत्नतः .. 50.19 ..
6.3.m: he too attains that fruit at this sacred ford, there is no doubt here. / And whoever gives shoes to brahmins with care,

6.3.s:
so'pi svargamavāpnoti hayārūḍho na saṃśayaḥ .
śayyāmaśvaṃ ca yo dadyācchattrikāṃ vā viśeṣataḥ .. 50.20 ..
6.3.d:
सोऽपि स्वर्गमवाप्नोति हयारूढो न संशयः .
शय्यामश्वं च यो दद्याच्छत्त्रिकां वा विशेषतः .. 50.20 ..
6.3.m: he too reaches heaven mounted upon a horse, without a doubt. / Whoever gives a bed and a horse, or especially a parasol,

6.3.s:
gacchedvimānamārūḍhaḥ so'psarovṛndaveṣṭitaḥ .
uttamaṃ yo gṛhaṃ dadyātsaptadhānyasamanvitam .. 50.21 ..
6.3.d:
गच्छेद्विमानमारूढः सोऽप्सरोवृन्दवेष्टितः .
उत्तमं यो गृहं दद्यात्सप्तधान्यसमन्वितम् .. 50.21 ..
6.3.m: mounted upon an aerial chariot, he goes surrounded by a multitude of apsarases. / Whoever gives an excellent house stocked with the seven grains,

6.3.s:
svecchayā me vaselloke kāñcane bhavane hi saḥ .
tiladhenuṃ ca yo dadyātsavatsāṃ vastrasaṃplutām .. 50.22 ..
6.3.d:
स्वेच्छया मे वसेल्लोके काञ्चने भवने हि सः .
तिलधेनुं च यो दद्यात्सवत्सां वस्त्रसंप्लुताम् .. 50.22 ..
6.3.m: he will indeed dwell at his pleasure in my realm, in a palace of gold. / And whoever gives a sesame-cow, along with its calf, wrapped in cloth,

6.3.s:
nākapṛṣṭhe vasettāvadyāvadābhūtasamplavam .
gṛhe vā yadi vāraṇye tīrthavartmani vā nṛpa .. 50.23 ..
6.3.d:
नाकपृष्ठे वसेत्तावद्यावदाभूतसम्प्लवम् .
गृहे वा यदि वारण्ये तीर्थवर्त्मनि वा नृप .. 50.23 ..
6.3.m: shall dwell on the vault of heaven until the dissolution of all beings. / Whether at home, in the forest, or on the road to a sacred ford, O king,

6.3.s:
toyamannaṃ ca yo dadyādyamalokaṃ sa nekṣate .
sarvadānāni dīyante teṣāṃ phalamavāpyate .. 50.24 ..
6.3.d:
तोयमन्नं च यो दद्याद्यमलोकं स नेक्षते .
सर्वदानानि दीयन्ते तेषां फलमवाप्यते .. 50.24 ..
6.3.m: whoever gives water and food does not see the realm of Yama. / All gifts are given, [and] their fruit is attained;

6.3.s:
udakaṃ cātra dānaṃ ca dadyādabhayameva ca .
annadānātparaṃ dānaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati .. 50.25 ..
6.3.d:
उदकं चात्र दानं च दद्यादभयमेव च .
अन्नदानात्परं दानं न भूतं न भविष्यति .. 50.25 ..
6.3.m: and here one should give water, a gift, and fearlessness indeed. / There has been no gift greater than the gift of food, nor will there be.

6.3.s:
kanyādānaṃ tu yaḥ kuryādvṛṣaṃ vā yaḥ samutsṛjet .
tasya vāso bhavettatra yatrāhamiti nānyathā .. 50.26 ..
6.3.d:
कन्यादानं तु यः कुर्याद्वृषं वा यः समुत्सृजेत् .
तस्य वासो भवेत्तत्र यत्राहमिति नान्यथा .. 50.26 ..
6.3.m: Moreover, he who gives away a maiden in marriage, or who releases a bull, / his dwelling shall be there where I am; it is not otherwise.

6.3.s:
uttānapāda uvāca -
kanyādānaṃ kathaṃ svāmin kartavyaṃ dhārmikaiḥ sadā .
parigraho yathā poṣyaḥ kanyodvāhastathaiva ca .. 50.27 ..
6.3.d:
उत्तानपाद उवाच -
कन्यादानं कथं स्वामिन् कर्तव्यं धार्मिकैः सदा .
परिग्रहो यथा पोष्यः कन्योद्वाहस्तथैव च .. 50.27 ..
6.3.m: Uttānapāda said: / How should the gift of a maiden always be performed by the righteous, O Lord? / Just as a wife is to be supported, so too is a daughter's wedding [to be conducted].

6.3.s:
anyatpṛcchāmi deveśa kasya kanyā na dīyate .
dātavyaṃ kutra taddeva kasmai dattamathākṣayam .. 50.28 ..
6.3.d:
अन्यत्पृच्छामि देवेश कस्य कन्या न दीयते .
दातव्यं कुत्र तद्देव कस्मै दत्तमथाक्षयम् .. 50.28 ..
6.3.m: I ask another thing, O Lord of the gods: To whom should a daughter not be given? / Where should that be given, O God? Given to whom does it become imperishable?

6.3.s:
uttamaṃ madhyamaṃ vāpi kanīyaḥ syātkathaṃ vibho .
rājasaṃ tāmasaṃ vāpi niḥśreyasamathāpi vā .. 50.29 ..
6.3.d:
उत्तमं मध्यमं वापि कनीयः स्यात्कथं विभो .
राजसं तामसं वापि निःश्रेयसमथापि वा .. 50.29 ..
6.3.m: How, O omnipresent Lord, would it be highest, middling, or lowest? / Or how [would it be] passionate, dark, or leading to the highest good?

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
sarveṣāmeva dānānāṃ kanyādānaṃ viśiṣyate .
yo dadyātparayā bhaktyābhigamya tanayāṃ nijām .. 50.30 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
सर्वेषामेव दानानां कन्यादानं विशिष्यते .
यो दद्यात्परया भक्त्याभिगम्य तनयां निजाम् .. 50.30 ..
6.3.m: Īśvara said: / The gift of a maiden is indeed superior to all gifts. / He who gives his own daughter with supreme devotion, having approached [the groom]—

6.3.s:
kulīnāya surūpāya guṇajñāya manīṣiṇe .
sulagne sumuhūrte ca dadyātkanyāmalaṃkṛtām .. 50.31 ..
6.3.d:
कुलीनाय सुरूपाय गुणज्ञाय मनीषिणे .
सुलग्ने सुमुहूर्ते च दद्यात्कन्यामलंकृताम् .. 50.31 ..
6.3.m: to one of good family, handsome, discerning of virtues, and wise, / at an auspicious lagna and an auspicious muhūrta, should give the adorned maiden.

6.3.s:
aśvānnā gāṃśca vāsāṃsi yo'tra dadyātsvaśaktitaḥ .
tasya vāso bhavettatra padaṃ yatra nirāmayam .. 50.32 ..
6.3.d:
अश्वान्ना गांश्च वासांसि योऽत्र दद्यात्स्वशक्तितः .
तस्य वासो भवेत्तत्र पदं यत्र निरामयम् .. 50.32 ..
6.3.m: He who gives horses, elephants, cows, and garments here according to his capacity, / his dwelling will be there where the station is free from disease.

6.3.s:
yenātra duhitā dattā prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī .
tena sarvamidaṃ dattaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram .. 50.33 ..
6.3.d:
येनात्र दुहिता दत्ता प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसी .
तेन सर्वमिदं दत्तं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् .. 50.33 ..
6.3.m: By him by whom a daughter, dearer even than life-breaths, has been given here, / by him all this threefold world, with the moving and the unmoving, has been given.

6.3.s:
yaḥ kanyārthaṃ tato labdhvā bhikṣate caiva taddhanam .
sa bhavetkarmacaṇḍālaḥ kāṣṭhakīlo bhavenmṛtaḥ .. 50.34 ..
6.3.d:
यः कन्यार्थं ततो लब्ध्वा भिक्षते चैव तद्धनम् .
स भवेत्कर्मचण्डालः काष्ठकीलो भवेन्मृतः .. 50.34 ..
6.3.m: He who, having received [a gift] for the sake of the maiden, then begs for that wealth [as a price], / he becomes an outcast by his deeds, and when dead, becomes a wooden stake.

6.3.s:
gṛhe'pi tasya yo'śnīyājjihvālaulyātkathaṃcana .
cāndrāyaṇena śudhyeta taptakṛcchreṇa vā punaḥ .. 50.35 ..
6.3.d:
गृहेऽपि तस्य योऽश्नीयाज्जिह्वालौल्यात्कथंचन .
चान्द्रायणेन शुध्येत तप्तकृच्छ्रेण वा पुनः .. 50.35 ..
6.3.m: Whoever, out of greed of the tongue, eats even in his house by any means, / would be purified by a cāndrāyaṇa penance or by a taptakṛcchra.

6.3.s:
uttānapāda uvāca -
vittaṃ na vidyate yasya kanyaivāsti ca yadgṛhe .
kathaṃ codvāhanaṃ tasya na yāñcāṃ kurute yadi .. 50.36 ..
6.3.d:
उत्तानपाद उवाच -
वित्तं न विद्यते यस्य कन्यैवास्ति च यद्गृहे .
कथं चोद्वाहनं तस्य न याञ्चां कुरुते यदि .. 50.36 ..
6.3.m: Uttānapāda said: / He who has no wealth, and in whose house there is only a daughter, / how can her marriage take place if he does not beg?

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
avitenaiva kartavyaṃ kanyodvahanakaṃ nṛpa .
kanyānāma samuccārya na doṣāya kadācana .. 50.37 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
अवितेनैव कर्तव्यं कन्योद्वहनकं नृप .
कन्यानाम समुच्चार्य न दोषाय कदाचन .. 50.37 ..
6.3.m: Īśvara said: / The marriage of a maiden must indeed be performed without wealth, O king. / Uttering the maiden's name [to request aid] is never a fault.

6.3.s:
abhigamyottamaṃ dānaṃ yacca dānamayācitam .
bhaviṣyati yugasyāntastasyānto naiva vidyate .. 50.38 ..
6.3.d:
अभिगम्योत्तमं दानं यच्च दानमयाचितम् .
भविष्यति युगस्यान्तस्तस्यान्तो नैव विद्यते .. 50.38 ..
6.3.m: The gift given after approaching [the recipient] is highest, and that gift which is unasked. / There will be an end of the cosmic age, but of that [gift's fruit] no end is found.

6.3.s:
abhigamyottamaṃ dānaṃ smṛtamāhūya madhyamam .
yācyamānaṃ kanīyaḥ syāddehi dehīti cādhamam .. 50.39 ..
6.3.d:
अभिगम्योत्तमं दानं स्मृतमाहूय मध्यमम् .
याच्यमानं कनीयः स्याद्देहि देहीति चाधमम् .. 50.39 ..
6.3.m: A gift given after approaching is taught to be highest; one given having summoned [the recipient] is middling; / one given when being asked would be inferior; and one given upon [repeated pleading], 'Give, give!' is lowest.

6.3.s:
yathaivāśmāśmanābaddho nikṣipto vārimadhyataḥ .
dvāvetau nidhanaṃ yātastadvadannamapātrake .. 50.40 ..
6.3.d:
यथैवाश्माश्मनाबद्धो निक्षिप्तो वारिमध्यतः .
द्वावेतौ निधनं यातस्तद्वदन्नमपात्रके .. 50.40 ..
6.3.m: Just as a stone bound to a stone and thrown into the middle of the water— / both of these go to destruction; likewise food [given] to an unworthy recipient.

6.3.s:
asamarthe tato dānaṃ na pradeyaṃ kadācana .
dātāraṃ nayate'dhastādātmānaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ .. 50.41 ..
6.3.d:
असमर्थे ततो दानं न प्रदेयं कदाचन .
दातारं नयतेऽधस्तादात्मानं च विशेषतः .. 50.41 ..
6.3.m: Therefore, a gift should never be given to one who is incapable [of digesting it]. / It drags the giver downward, and especially himself.

6.3.s:
samarthastārayeddvau tu kāṣṭhaṃ śuṣkaṃ yathā jale .
yathā nauśca tathā vidvānprāpayedaparaṃ taṭam .. 50.42 ..
6.3.d:
समर्थस्तारयेद्द्वौ तु काष्ठं शुष्कं यथा जले .
यथा नौश्च तथा विद्वान्प्रापयेदपरं तटम् .. 50.42 ..
6.3.m: A capable person, however, can ferry both across, just as dry wood does in water. / And just as a boat [does], so a wise man can make [one] reach the other shore.

6.3.s:
āhitāgniśca gṛhṇāti yaḥ śūdrāṇāṃ pratigraham .
iha janmani śūdro'sau mṛtaḥ śvā copajāyate .. 50.43 ..
6.3.d:
आहिताग्निश्च गृह्णाति यः शूद्राणां प्रतिग्रहम् .
इह जन्मनि शूद्रोऽसौ मृतः श्वा चोपजायते .. 50.43 ..
6.3.m: And the agnihotrin who accepts a gift from śūdras / becomes a śūdra in this life, and when dead, is born as a dog.

6.3.s:
vṛthā kleśaśca jāyeta brāhmaṇe hyagnihotriṇi .
asatpratigrahaṃ kurvanguptaṃ nīcasya garhitam .. 50.44 ..
6.3.d:
वृथा क्लेशश्च जायेत ब्राह्मणे ह्यग्निहोत्रिणि .
असत्प्रतिग्रहं कुर्वन्गुप्तं नीचस्य गर्हितम् .. 50.44 ..
6.3.m: And useless affliction arises for the brahmin, the agnihotrin, / who accepts an unworthy gift secretly from a low person, [a gift] that is censured.

6.3.s:
abhojyaḥ sa bhavenmartyo dahyate kāriṣāgninā .
kaṭakāro bhavetpaścātsapta janma na saṃśayaḥ .. 50.45 ..
6.3.d:
अभोज्यः स भवेन्मर्त्यो दह्यते कारिषाग्निना .
कटकारो भवेत्पश्चात्सप्त जन्म न संशयः .. 50.45 ..
6.3.m: That mortal becomes one whose food cannot be eaten; he is burned with fire made of dried cow dung. / Afterward, he becomes a mat-maker for seven births, without doubt.

6.3.s:
lajjādākṣiṇyalobhācca yaddānaṃ coparodhajam .
bhṛtyebhyaśca tu yaddānaṃ tadvṛthā niṣphalaṃ bhavet .. 50.46 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe śūlabhedamāhātmye pātrāpātraparīkṣādānādiniyamavarṇanaṃ nāma pañcāśattamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 51
6.3.d:
लज्जादाक्षिण्यलोभाच्च यद्दानं चोपरोधजम् .
भृत्येभ्यश्च तु यद्दानं तद्वृथा निष्फलं भवेत् .. 50.46 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे शूलभेदमाहात्म्ये पात्रापात्रपरीक्षादानादिनियमवर्णनं नाम पञ्चाशत्तमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 51
6.3.m:
A gift given out of shame, courtesy, greed, or arising from coercion, / and a gift [given only] to servants—that becomes useless and devoid of fruit.
Thus ends the fiftieth chapter, named 'Description of the Rules of Giving, Examination of Worthy and Unworthy Recipients, and So Forth,' in the Śūlabhedamāhātmya of the Revākhaṇḍa in the fifth Āvantyakhaṇḍa of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, containing eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 51

6.3.s:
uttānapāda uvāca -
kāle tatkriyate kasmiñchrāddhaṃ dānaṃ tatheśvara .
yātrā tatra prakartavyā tithau yasyāṃ vadāśu tat .. 51.1 ..
6.3.d:
उत्तानपाद उवाच -
काले तत्क्रियते कस्मिञ्छ्राद्धं दानं तथेश्वर .
यात्रा तत्र प्रकर्तव्या तिथौ यस्यां वदाशु तत् .. 51.1 ..
6.3.m: Uttānapāda said: / At what time should śrāddha and gift-giving be performed there, O Lord? / On which lunar day should the pilgrimage be undertaken there? Tell that quickly!

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
pitṛtīrthaṃ yathā puṇyaṃ sarvakāmikamuttamam .
idaṃ tīrthaṃ tathā puṇyaṃ snānadānāditarpaṇaiḥ .. 51.2 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
पितृतीर्थं यथा पुण्यं सर्वकामिकमुत्तमम् .
इदं तीर्थं तथा पुण्यं स्नानदानादितर्पणैः .. 51.2 ..
6.3.m: Īśvara said: / Just as the tīrtha of the ancestors is holy, granting all desires, and excellent, / so is this holy tīrtha through ritual ablutions, gifts, libations, and the like.

6.3.s:
viśeṣeṇa tu kurvīta śrāddhaṃ sarvayugādiṣu .
manvantarādayo vatsa śrūyantāṃ ca caturdaśa .. 51.3 ..
6.3.d:
विशेषेण तु कुर्वीत श्राद्धं सर्वयुगादिषु .
मन्वन्तरादयो वत्स श्रूयन्तां च चतुर्दश .. 51.3 ..
6.3.m: One should especially perform śrāddha on all the beginnings of the yugas. / And listen, my child, to the fourteen beginnings of the manvantaras:

6.3.s:
aśvayukchuklanavamī dvādaśī kārttikasya ca .
tṛtīyā caitramāsasya tathā bhādrapadasya ca .. 51.4 ..
6.3.d:
अश्वयुक्छुक्लनवमी द्वादशी कार्त्तिकस्य च .
तृतीया चैत्रमासस्य तथा भाद्रपदस्य च .. 51.4 ..
6.3.m: The bright ninth of Aśvina, and the twelfth of Kārttika, / the third of the month of Caitra, and likewise of Bhādrapada;

6.3.s:
āṣāḍhasyaiva daśamī māghasyaiva tu saptamī .
śrāvaṇasyāṣṭamī kṛṣṇā tathāṣāḍhasya pūrṇimā .. 51.5 ..
6.3.d:
आषाढस्यैव दशमी माघस्यैव तु सप्तमी .
श्रावणस्याष्टमी कृष्णा तथाषाढस्य पूर्णिमा .. 51.5 ..
6.3.m: the tenth of Āṣāḍha, and the seventh of Māgha; / the dark eighth of Śrāvaṇa, and the full moon of Āṣāḍha;

6.3.s:
phālgunasya tvamāvāsyā pauṣasyaikādaśī sitā .
kārttikī phālgunī caitrī jyaiṣṭhī pañcadaśī tathā .. 51.6 ..
6.3.d:
फाल्गुनस्य त्वमावास्या पौषस्यैकादशी सिता .
कार्त्तिकी फाल्गुनी चैत्री ज्यैष्ठी पञ्चदशी तथा .. 51.6 ..
6.3.m: the new moon of Phālguna, and the bright eleventh of Pauṣa; / the fifteenth of Kārttika, Phālguna, Caitra, and Jyeṣṭha.

6.3.s:
manvantarādayaścaite anantaphaladāḥ smṛtāḥ .
ayane cottare rājandakṣiṇe śrāddhamācaret .. 51.7 ..
6.3.d:
मन्वन्तरादयश्चैते अनन्तफलदाः स्मृताः .
अयने चोत्तरे राजन्दक्षिणे श्राद्धमाचरेत् .. 51.7 ..
6.3.m: These beginnings of the manvantaras are remembered as yielding endless fruit. / And at the northern solstice, O king, and at the southern, one should perform a śrāddha;

6.3.s:
kārttikī ca tathā māghī vaiśākhasya tṛtīyikā .
paurṇamāsī ca caitrasya jyeṣṭhasya ca viśeṣataḥ .. 51.8 ..
6.3.d:
कार्त्तिकी च तथा माघी वैशाखस्य तृतीयिका .
पौर्णमासी च चैत्रस्य ज्येष्ठस्य च विशेषतः .. 51.8 ..
6.3.m: likewise the [full moons] of Kārttika and Māgha, and the third of Vaiśākha, / and especially the full moon of Caitra and of Jyeṣṭha;

6.3.s:
aṣṭakāsu ca saṃkrāntau vyatīpāte tathaiva ca .
śrāddhakālā ime sarve dattameṣvakṣayaṃ smṛtam .. 51.9 ..
6.3.d:
अष्टकासु च संक्रान्तौ व्यतीपाते तथैव च .
श्राद्धकाला इमे सर्वे दत्तमेष्वक्षयं स्मृतम् .. 51.9 ..
6.3.m: and on the aṣṭakā days, at a saṃkrānti, and likewise on a vyatīpāta. / All these are times for śrāddha; what is given on these is remembered as imperishable.

6.3.s:
madhumāse site pakṣa ekādaśyāmupoṣitaḥ .
niśi jāgaraṇaṃ kuryādviṣṇupādasamīpataḥ .. 51.10 ..
6.3.d:
मधुमासे सिते पक्ष एकादश्यामुपोषितः .
निशि जागरणं कुर्याद्विष्णुपादसमीपतः .. 51.10 ..
6.3.m: In the spring month, in the bright fortnight, having fasted on the eleventh day, / one should keep a vigil at night near the footprint of Viṣṇu.

6.3.s:
dhūpadīpādinaivedyaiḥ sraṅmālāgurucandanaiḥ .
arcāṃ kurvanti ye viṣṇoḥ paṭheyuḥ prāktanīṃ kathām .. 51.11 ..
6.3.d:
धूपदीपादिनैवेद्यैः स्रङ्मालागुरुचन्दनैः .
अर्चां कुर्वन्ति ये विष्णोः पठेयुः प्राक्तनीं कथाम् .. 51.11 ..
6.3.m: Those who perform worship of Viṣṇu with incense, lamps, food offerings, and the like, with garlands and agallochum sandalwood, / and read an ancient narrative,

6.3.s:
ṛgyajuḥsāmamantroktaṃ sūktaṃ japati yo dvijaḥ .
sarvapāpavinirmukto viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati .. 51.12 ..
6.3.d:
ऋग्यजुःसाममन्त्रोक्तं सूक्तं जपति यो द्विजः .
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो विष्णुलोकं स गच्छति .. 51.12 ..
6.3.m: and the twice-born who recites a sūkta stated in the mantras of the Ṛg, Yajur, or Sāma [Veda], / being completely freed from all sins, he goes to the realm of Viṣṇu.

6.3.s:
prātaḥ śrāddhaṃ prakurvīta dvijān sampūjya yatnataḥ .
dānaṃ dadyādyathāśakti gohiraṇyāmbarādikam .. 51.13 ..
6.3.d:
प्रातः श्राद्धं प्रकुर्वीत द्विजान् सम्पूज्य यत्नतः .
दानं दद्याद्यथाशक्ति गोहिरण्याम्बरादिकम् .. 51.13 ..
6.3.m: In the morning he should perform a śrāddha, having carefully worshipped the twice-born. / He should give a gift according to his capacity: a cow, gold, garments, and the like.

6.3.s:
pitarastasya tṛpyanti yāvadābhūtasamplavam .
śrāddhadastu vrajettatra yatra devo janārdanaḥ .. 51.14 ..
6.3.d:
पितरस्तस्य तृप्यन्ति यावदाभूतसम्प्लवम् .
श्राद्धदस्तु व्रजेत्तत्र यत्र देवो जनार्दनः .. 51.14 ..
6.3.m: His ancestors are satisfied until the dissolution of all beings, / and the giver of the śrāddha goes there where Lord Janārdana is.

6.3.s:
trayodaśyāṃ tato gacchedguhāvāsini liṅgake .
dṛṣṭvā mārkaṇḍamīśānaṃ mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ .. 51.15 ..
6.3.d:
त्रयोदश्यां ततो गच्छेद्गुहावासिनि लिङ्गके .
दृष्ट्वा मार्कण्डमीशानं मुच्यते सर्वपातकैः .. 51.15 ..
6.3.m: Then, on the thirteenth day, he should go to the liṅga residing in the cave. / Having seen Mārkaṇḍeśa, he is freed from all sins.

6.3.s:
uttānapāda uvāca -
guhāmadhye mahādeva liṅgaṃ paramaśobhitam .
yena pratiṣṭhitaṃ deva tanmamākhyātumarhasi .. 51.16 ..
6.3.d:
उत्तानपाद उवाच -
गुहामध्ये महादेव लिङ्गं परमशोभितम् .
येन प्रतिष्ठितं देव तन्ममाख्यातुमर्हसि .. 51.16 ..
6.3.m:
Uttānapāda said:
O Mahādeva, inside the cave is a most radiant liṅga.
O god, you ought to tell me by whom it was installed.

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
triṣu lokeṣu vikhyāto mārkaṇḍeyo munīśvaraḥ .
divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ sa tapastepe sudāruṇam .. 51.17 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
त्रिषु लोकेषु विख्यातो मार्कण्डेयो मुनीश्वरः .
दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रं स तपस्तेपे सुदारुणम् .. 51.17 ..
6.3.m:
Īśvara said:
Renowned in the three worlds is the lord of sages, Mārkaṇḍeya.
For a divine thousand years he practiced very severe austerity.

6.3.s:
guhāmadhyaṃ praviṣṭo'sau yogābhyāsamupāśritaḥ .
liṅgaṃ tu sthāpitaṃ tena mārkaṇḍeśvarasaṃjñitam .. 51.18 ..
6.3.d:
गुहामध्यं प्रविष्टोऽसौ योगाभ्यासमुपाश्रितः .
लिङ्गं तु स्थापितं तेन मार्कण्डेश्वरसंज्ञितम् .. 51.18 ..
6.3.m:
Having entered inside the cave and resorted to the practice of yoga,
a liṅga named Mārkaṇḍeśvara was established by him.

6.3.s:
tatra snātvā ca yo bhaktyā sopavāso jitendriyaḥ .
tatra jāgaraṇaṃ kurvan dadyāddīpaṃ prayatnataḥ .. 51.19 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र स्नात्वा च यो भक्त्या सोपवासो जितेन्द्रियः .
तत्र जागरणं कुर्वन् दद्याद्दीपं प्रयत्नतः .. 51.19 ..
6.3.m:
Having bathed there with devotion, fasting, with senses conquered,
keeping a night vigil there, one should diligently offer a lamp.

6.3.s:
devasya snapanaṃ kuryānmṛtaiḥ pañcabhistathā .
yathā śaktyā samālabhya pūjāṃ kuryādyathāvidhi .. 51.20 ..
6.3.d:
देवस्य स्नपनं कुर्यान्मृतैः पञ्चभिस्तथा .
यथा शक्त्या समालभ्य पूजां कुर्याद्यथाविधि .. 51.20 ..
6.3.m:
One should perform the ceremonial bath of the god with the five amṛtas;
anointing it according to one's ability, one should perform worship according to rule.

6.3.s:
svaśākhotpannamantraiśca japaṃ kuryurdvijātayaḥ .
sāvitryaṣṭasahasraṃ tu śatāṣṭakamathāpi vā .. 51.21 ..
6.3.d:
स्वशाखोत्पन्नमन्त्रैश्च जपं कुर्युर्द्विजातयः .
सावित्र्यष्टसहस्रं तु शताष्टकमथापि वा .. 51.21 ..
6.3.m:
Twice-born ones should perform recitation with mantras originating in their own Vedic branch,
either eight thousand or one hundred and eight times the Sāvitrī.

6.3.s:
etatkṛtvā nṛpaśreṣṭha janmanaḥ phalamāpnuyāt .
caturdaśyāṃ tu vai snātvā pūjāṃ kṛtvā yathāvidhi .. 51.22 ..
6.3.d:
एतत्कृत्वा नृपश्रेष्ठ जन्मनः फलमाप्नुयात् .
चतुर्दश्यां तु वै स्नात्वा पूजां कृत्वा यथाविधि .. 51.22 ..
6.3.m:
Having done this, O best of kings, one obtains the fruit of one's birth.
Indeed, having bathed on the fourteenth day and performed worship according to rule,

6.3.s:
pātraṃ parīkṣya dātavyamātmanaḥ śreya icchatā .
pitarastasya tṛpyanti dvādaśābdānyasaṃśayam .. 51.23 ..
6.3.d:
पात्रं परीक्ष्य दातव्यमात्मनः श्रेय इच्छता .
पितरस्तस्य तृप्यन्ति द्वादशाब्दान्यसंशयम् .. 51.23 ..
6.3.m:
one who desires his own welfare should give gifts after examining the recipient.
His ancestors are satisfied for twelve years, without doubt.

6.3.s:
dātā sa gacchate tatra yatra bhogāḥ sanātanāḥ .
guhāmadhye praviṣṭastu loṭayeccaiva śaktitaḥ .. 51.24 ..
6.3.d:
दाता स गच्छते तत्र यत्र भोगाः सनातनाः .
गुहामध्ये प्रविष्टस्तु लोटयेच्चैव शक्तितः .. 51.24 ..
6.3.m:
That donor goes to that place where eternal enjoyments are.
Having entered inside the cave, one should roll [on the ground] according to one's ability.

6.3.s:
nīle girau hi yatpuṇyaṃ tatsamastaṃ labhanti te .
śūlabhede tu yaḥ kuryācchrāddhaṃ parvaṇi parvaṇi .. 51.25 ..
6.3.d:
नीले गिरौ हि यत्पुण्यं तत्समस्तं लभन्ति ते .
शूलभेदे तु यः कुर्याच्छ्राद्धं पर्वणि पर्वणि .. 51.25 ..
6.3.m:
They obtain all that merit which is gained on the Blue Mountain.
He who performs a śrāddha at Śūlabheda on every auspicious festival day,

6.3.s:
viśeṣāccaitramāsānte tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu .
kedāre caiva yatpuṇyaṃ gaṅgāsāgarasaṅgame .. 51.26 ..
6.3.d:
विशेषाच्चैत्रमासान्ते तस्य पुण्यफलं शृणु .
केदारे चैव यत्पुण्यं गङ्गासागरसङ्गमे .. 51.26 ..
6.3.m:
especially at the end of the month of Caitra—hear the meritorious fruit of that:
Whatever merit is gained at Kedāra and at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean,

6.3.s:
sitāsite tu yatpuṇyamanyatīrthe viśeṣataḥ .
arbude vidyate puṇyaṃ puṇyaṃ cāmaraparvate .. 51.27 ..
6.3.d:
सितासिते तु यत्पुण्यमन्यतीर्थे विशेषतः .
अर्बुदे विद्यते पुण्यं पुण्यं चामरपर्वते .. 51.27 ..
6.3.m:
and whatever merit is at the Sitāsita [confluence of Gaṅgā and Yamunā], especially at other sacred fords,
what merit is found at Arbuda, and the merit at the Mountain of the Immortals,

6.3.s:
gayādisarvatīrthānāṃ phalamāpnoti mānavaḥ .
vidhimantrasamāyuktastarpayetpitṛdevatāḥ .. 51.28 ..
6.3.d:
गयादिसर्वतीर्थानां फलमाप्नोति मानवः .
विधिमन्त्रसमायुक्तस्तर्पयेत्पितृदेवताः .. 51.28 ..
6.3.m:
a person obtains the fruit of all sacred fords, such as Gayā.
Endowed with the prescribed mantras, he should offer libations to the ancestral gods.

6.3.s:
kulānāṃ tārayedviṃśaṃ daśa pūrvān daśāparān .
dakṣiṇasyāṃ tato mūrtau śucirbhūtvā samāhitaḥ .. 51.29 ..
6.3.d:
कुलानां तारयेद्विंशं दश पूर्वान् दशापरान् .
दक्षिणस्यां ततो मूर्तौ शुचिर्भूत्वा समाहितः .. 51.29 ..
6.3.m:
He delivers twenty [generations] of his families—ten preceding and ten succeeding.
Then, becoming pure and concentrated, facing the southern icon,

6.3.s:
nyāsaṃ kṛtvā tu pūrvoktaṃ pradadyādaṣṭapuṣpikām .
śāstroktairaṣṭabhiḥ puṣpairmānasaiḥ śṛṇu tadyathā .. 51.30 ..
6.3.d:
न्यासं कृत्वा तु पूर्वोक्तं प्रदद्यादष्टपुष्पिकाम् .
शास्त्रोक्तैरष्टभिः पुष्पैर्मानसैः शृणु तद्यथा .. 51.30 ..
6.3.m:
having performed the previously mentioned nyāsa, he should offer the eight-flower offering.
Hear how it is done, with the eight mental flowers declared in the scriptures:

6.3.s:
vārijaṃ saumyamāgneyaṃ vāyavyaṃ pārthivaṃ punaḥ .
vānaspatyaṃ bhavetṣaṣṭhaṃ prājāpatyaṃ tu saptamam .. 51.31 ..
6.3.d:
वारिजं सौम्यमाग्नेयं वायव्यं पार्थिवं पुनः .
वानस्पत्यं भवेत्षष्ठं प्राजापत्यं तु सप्तमम् .. 51.31 ..
6.3.m:
The water-born, the gentle, the fiery, the airy, and again the earthy;
the arboreal is the sixth, and the Prajāpati-related is the seventh;

6.3.s:
aṣṭamaṃ śivapuṣpaṃ syādeṣāṃ śṛṇu vinirṇayam .
vārijaṃ salilaṃ jñeyaṃ saumyaṃ madhughṛtaṃ payaḥ .. 51.32 ..
6.3.d:
अष्टमं शिवपुष्पं स्यादेषां शृणु विनिर्णयम् .
वारिजं सलिलं ज्ञेयं सौम्यं मधुघृतं पयः .. 51.32 ..
6.3.m:
the flower of Śiva is the eighth. Hear the precise determination of these:
