The water-born is known to be water; the gentle is honey, ghee, and milk;

6.3.s:
āgneyaṃ dhūpadīpādyaṃ vāyavyaṃ candanādikam .
pārthivaṃ kandamūlādyaṃ vānaspatyaṃ phalātmakam .. 51.33 ..
6.3.d:
आग्नेयं धूपदीपाद्यं वायव्यं चन्दनादिकम् .
पार्थिवं कन्दमूलाद्यं वानस्पत्यं फलात्मकम् .. 51.33 ..
6.3.m:
the fiery consists of incense, lamps, and the like; the airy is sandalwood paste and the like;
the earthy consists of bulbs, roots, and the like; the arboreal consists of fruit;

6.3.s:
prājāpatyaṃ tu pāṭhādyaṃ śivapuṣpaṃ tu vāsanā .
ahiṃsā prathamaṃ puṣpaṃ puṣpamindriyanigrahaḥ .. 51.34 ..
6.3.d:
प्राजापत्यं तु पाठाद्यं शिवपुष्पं तु वासना .
अहिंसा प्रथमं पुष्पं पुष्पमिन्द्रियनिग्रहः .. 51.34 ..
6.3.m:
the Prajāpati-related consists of recitation and the like; and the flower of Śiva is residual impression.
Non-violence is the first flower; the restraint of the senses is a flower;

6.3.s:
tṛtīyaṃ tu dayā puṣpaṃ kṣamā puṣpaṃ caturthakam .
dhyānapuṣpaṃ tapaḥ puṣpaṃ jñānapuṣpaṃ tu saptamam .. 51.35 ..
6.3.d:
तृतीयं तु दया पुष्पं क्षमा पुष्पं चतुर्थकम् .
ध्यानपुष्पं तपः पुष्पं ज्ञानपुष्पं तु सप्तमम् .. 51.35 ..
6.3.m:
compassion is the third flower, and forbearance is the fourth flower;
meditation is a flower, austerity is a flower, and knowledge is the seventh flower;

6.3.s:
satyaṃ caivāṣṭamaṃ puṣpamebhistuṣyanti devatāḥ .
bhaktyā tapasvinaḥ pūjyā jñāninaśca narādhipa .. 51.36 ..
6.3.d:
सत्यं चैवाष्टमं पुष्पमेभिस्तुष्यन्ति देवताः .
भक्त्या तपस्विनः पूज्या ज्ञानिनश्च नराधिप .. 51.36 ..
6.3.m:
and truth is the eighth flower: the deities are pleased by these.
Ascetics and men of knowledge should be worshipped with devotion, O king.

6.3.s:
chatramāvaraṇaṃ dadyādupānadyugalaṃ tathā .
tena pūjitamātreṇa pūjitāḥ puruṣāstrayaḥ .. 51.37 ..
6.3.d:
छत्रमावरणं दद्यादुपानद्युगलं तथा .
तेन पूजितमात्रेण पूजिताः पुरुषास्त्रयः .. 51.37 ..
6.3.m:
One should give an umbrella, an outer garment, and a pair of sandals;
by merely worshipping him, the three Puruṣas are worshipped.

6.3.s:
svargaloke vasettāvadyāvadābhūtasamplavam .
śūlapāṇestu bhaktyā vai jāpyaṃ kurvanti ye narāḥ .. 51.38 ..
6.3.d:
स्वर्गलोके वसेत्तावद्यावदाभूतसम्प्लवम् .
शूलपाणेस्तु भक्त्या वै जाप्यं कुर्वन्ति ये नराः .. 51.38 ..
6.3.m:
He shall dwell in the heavenly world until the dissolution of all beings.
Those men who with devotion perform the recitation of the Trident-bearer,

6.3.s:
pañcāmṛtaiḥ pañcagavyairyakṣakardamakuṅkumaiḥ .
samālabheta deveśaṃ śrīkhaṇḍāgurucandanaiḥ .. 51.39 ..
6.3.d:
पञ्चामृतैः पञ्चगव्यैर्यक्षकर्दमकुङ्कुमैः .
समालभेत देवेशं श्रीखण्डागुरुचन्दनैः .. 51.39 ..
6.3.m:
and anoint the Lord of Gods with the five nectars, the five cow products,
yakṣakardama paste, saffron, white sandalwood, and aloe,

6.3.s:
nānāvidhaiśca ye puṣpairarcāṃ kurvanti śūlinaḥ .
niśi jāgaraṇaṃ kuryurdīpadānaṃ prayatnataḥ .. 51.40 ..
6.3.d:
नानाविधैश्च ये पुष्पैरर्चां कुर्वन्ति शूलिनः .
निशि जागरणं कुर्युर्दीपदानं प्रयत्नतः .. 51.40 ..
6.3.m:
and who worship the Trident-bearer with various kinds of flowers,
should keep a vigil at night and diligently make an offering of lamps.

6.3.s:
dhūpanaivedyakaṃ dadyātpaṭhetpaurāṇikīṃ kathām .
tatra sthāne sthitā bhaktyā japaṃ kurvanti ye narāḥ .. 51.41 ..
6.3.d:
धूपनैवेद्यकं दद्यात्पठेत्पौराणिकीं कथाम् .
तत्र स्थाने स्थिता भक्त्या जपं कुर्वन्ति ये नराः .. 51.41 ..
6.3.m:
One should offer incense and food offerings, and read a Purāṇic narrative.
Those men who, remaining in that place, perform recitation with devotion—

6.3.s:
śrīsūktaṃ pauruṣaṃ sūktaṃ pāvamānaṃ vṛṣākapim .
vedoktaiścaiva mantraiśca raudrīṃ vā bahurūpiṇīm .. 51.42 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीसूक्तं पौरुषं सूक्तं पावमानं वृषाकपिम् .
वेदोक्तैश्चैव मन्त्रैश्च रौद्रीं वा बहुरूपिणीम् .. 51.42 ..
6.3.m:
the Śrīsūkta, the Pauruṣasūkta, the Pāvamāna, the Vṛṣākapi,
and the Raudrī or the Bahurūpiṇī with mantras taught in the Vedas—

6.3.s:
brāhmaṇān pūjayedbhaktyā pūjayitvā praṇamya ca .
nānāvidhairmahābhogaiḥ śivaloke mahīyate .. 51.43 ..
6.3.d:
ब्राह्मणान् पूजयेद्भक्त्या पूजयित्वा प्रणम्य च .
नानाविधैर्महाभोगैः शिवलोके महीयते .. 51.43 ..
6.3.m:
should worship brahmins with devotion; having worshipped and bowed down to them,
he is magnified in the world of Śiva with various great enjoyments.

6.3.s:
agnimityādi jāpyāni ṛgvedī japate tu yaḥ .
rudrān puruṣasūktaṃ ca ślokādhyāyaṃ ca śukriyam .. 51.44 ..
6.3.d:
अग्निमित्यादि जाप्यानि ऋग्वेदी जपते तु यः .
रुद्रान् पुरुषसूक्तं च श्लोकाध्यायं च शुक्रियम् .. 51.44 ..
6.3.m:
He who, being a knower of the Ṛgveda, recites texts to be recited such as "Agni...",
the Rudras, the Puruṣasūkta, the Ślokādhyāya, and the Śukriya,

6.3.s:
iṣetvā dikamantraughaṃ jyotirbrāhmaṇameva ca .
gāyatryaṃ vai madhu caiva maṇḍalabrāhmaṇāni ca .. 51.45 ..
6.3.d:
इषेत्वा दिकमन्त्रौघं ज्योतिर्ब्राह्मणमेव च .
गायत्र्यं वै मधु चैव मण्डलब्राह्मणानि च .. 51.45 ..
6.3.m:
or, if he is a knower of the Yajurveda, recites with devotion these texts to be recited:
the collection of mantras beginning with "Iṣe tvā...", the Jyotirbrāhmaṇa,
the Gāyatra, the Madhu, and the Maṇḍalabrāhmaṇas,

6.3.s:
etāñjapyāṃstu yo bhaktyā yajurvedī japedyadi .
devavrataṃ vāmadevyaṃ puruṣarṣabhameva ca .. 51.46 ..
6.3.d:
एताञ्जप्यांस्तु यो भक्त्या यजुर्वेदी जपेद्यदि .
देवव्रतं वामदेव्यं पुरुषर्षभमेव च .. 51.46 ..
6.3.m: or the Devavrata, the Vāmadevya, the Puruṣarṣabha,

6.3.s:
bṛhadrathāntaraṃ caiva yo japedbhaktitatparaḥ .
sa prayāti naraḥ sthānaṃ yatra devo maheśvaraḥ .. 51.47 ..
6.3.d:
बृहद्रथान्तरं चैव यो जपेद्भक्तितत्परः .
स प्रयाति नरः स्थानं यत्र देवो महेश्वरः .. 51.47 ..
6.3.m:
and the Bṛhat and the Rathāntara, being intent on devotion—
that man goes to the place where God Maheśvara resides.

6.3.s:
pādaśaucaṃ tathābhyaṅgaṃ kurute yo'tra bhaktitaḥ .
godāne caiva yatpuṇyaṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 51.48 ..
6.3.d:
पादशौचं तथाभ्यङ्गं कुरुते योऽत्र भक्तितः .
गोदाने चैव यत्पुण्यं लभते नात्र संशयः .. 51.48 ..
6.3.m:
He who here performs the washing of feet and the application of unguents with devotion
obtains the merit of gifting a cow; there is no doubt about this.

6.3.s:
brāhmaṇān bhojayettatra madhunā pāyasena ca .
ekasmin bhojite vipre koṭirbhavati bhojitā .. 51.49 ..
6.3.d:
ब्राह्मणान् भोजयेत्तत्र मधुना पायसेन च .
एकस्मिन् भोजिते विप्रे कोटिर्भवति भोजिता .. 51.49 ..
6.3.m:
One should feed brahmins there with honey and milk rice.
When one brahmin is fed, ten million are fed.

6.3.s:
suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ vastraṃ dadyādbhaktyā dvijottame .
tarpitāstena devāḥ syurmanuṣyāḥ pitarastathā .. 51.50 ..
6.3.d:
सुवर्णं रजतं वस्त्रं दद्याद्भक्त्या द्विजोत्तमे .
तर्पितास्तेन देवाः स्युर्मनुष्याः पितरस्तथा .. 51.50 ..
6.3.m:
One should give gold, silver, and cloth with devotion to an excellent twice-born;
by that, gods, humans, and ancestors are satisfied.

6.3.s:
candrasūryagrahe bhaktyā snānaṃ kurvanti ye narāḥ .
devārcanaṃ ye ca kuryurjapaṃ homaṃ viśeṣataḥ .
dadyāddānaṃ yathāśakti brāhmaṇe vedapārage .. 51.51 ..
6.3.d:
चन्द्रसूर्यग्रहे भक्त्या स्नानं कुर्वन्ति ये नराः .
देवार्चनं ये च कुर्युर्जपं होमं विशेषतः .
दद्याद्दानं यथाशक्ति ब्राह्मणे वेदपारगे .. 51.51 ..
6.3.m:
Those men who take a bath with devotion during an eclipse of the moon or the sun,
and who perform the worship of the deity, especially recitation and fire offerings,
should give gifts according to their ability to a brahmin who has mastered the Vedas:

6.3.s:
aśvaṃ rathaṃ gajaṃ yānaṃ tulāpuruṣameva ca .
śakaṭaṃ yaḥ pradadyādvā saptadhānyaprapūritam .. 51.52 ..
6.3.d:
अश्वं रथं गजं यानं तुलापुरुषमेव च .
शकटं यः प्रदद्याद्वा सप्तधान्यप्रपूरितम् .. 51.52 ..
6.3.m:
a horse, a chariot, an elephant, a vehicle, or the gift of a man-weighed balance,
or a cart filled with seven kinds of grains.

6.3.s:
sayoktraṃ lāṅgalaṃ dadyādyuvānau tu dhuraṃdharau .
gobhūtilahiraṇyādi pātre dātavyamarcitam .. 51.53 ..
6.3.d:
सयोक्त्रं लाङ्गलं दद्याद्युवानौ तु धुरंधरौ .
गोभूतिलहिरण्यादि पात्रे दातव्यमर्चितम् .. 51.53 ..
6.3.m:
One should give a plough with yoke-ropes and two young draught-bulls.
Cows, land, sesame seeds, gold, and other gifts should be given with reverence to a worthy recipient.

6.3.s:
apātre viduṣā kiṃcinna deyaṃ bhūtimicchatā .
yato'sau sarvabhūtāni dadhāti dharaṇī kila .. 51.54 ..
6.3.d:
अपात्रे विदुषा किंचिन्न देयं भूतिमिच्छता .
यतोऽसौ सर्वभूतानि दधाति धरणी किल .. 51.54 ..
6.3.m:
Nothing should be given to an unworthy recipient by a wise person desiring prosperity.
Because the earth indeed sustains all beings,

6.3.s:
tato viprāya sā deyā sarvasasyaughamālinī .
athānyacchṛṇu rājendra godānasya tu yatphalam .. 51.55 ..
6.3.d:
ततो विप्राय सा देया सर्वसस्यौघमालिनी .
अथान्यच्छृणु राजेन्द्र गोदानस्य तु यत्फलम् .. 51.55 ..
6.3.m:
it should be given to a brahmin, garlanded with masses of all crops.
Now hear another matter, O lord of kings: the fruit of gifting a cow.

6.3.s:
yāvadvatsasya pādau dvau mukhaṃ yonyāṃ pradṛśyate .
tāvadgauḥ pṛthivī jñeyā yāvadgarbhaṃ na muñcati .. 51.56 ..
6.3.d:
यावद्वत्सस्य पादौ द्वौ मुखं योन्यां प्रदृश्यते .
तावद्गौः पृथिवी ज्ञेया यावद्गर्भं न मुञ्चति .. 51.56 ..
6.3.m:
As long as the calf's two feet and face are visible in the birth canal,
for that long the cow is considered the earth, until she releases the embryo.

6.3.s:
yena kenāpyupāyena brāhmaṇe tāṃ samarpayet .
pṛthvī dattā bhavettena saśailavanakānanā .. 51.57 ..
6.3.d:
येन केनाप्युपायेन ब्राह्मणे तां समर्पयेत् .
पृथ्वी दत्ता भवेत्तेन सशैलवनकानना .. 51.57 ..
6.3.m:
By whatever means possible, one should offer her to a brahmin;
by him the earth, with its mountains and forests, has been given.

6.3.s:
tārayenniyataṃ dattā kulānāmekaviṃśatim .
raupyakhurīṃ kāṃsyadohāṃ savastrāṃ ca payasvinīm .. 51.58 ..
6.3.d:
तारयेन्नियतं दत्ता कुलानामेकविंशतिम् .
रौप्यखुरीं कांस्यदोहां सवस्त्रां च पयस्विनीम् .. 51.58 ..
6.3.m: Given [in this state], it surely delivers twenty-one generations: / [a cow] with silver hooves, a bronze milking pail, adorned with cloth, and rich in milk.

6.3.s:
ye prayacchanti kṛtino graste sūrye niśākare .
teṣāṃ saṃkhyāṃ na jānāmi puṇyasyābdaśatairapi .. 51.59 ..
6.3.d:
ये प्रयच्छन्ति कृतिनो ग्रस्ते सूर्ये निशाकरे .
तेषां संख्यां न जानामि पुण्यस्याब्दशतैरपि .. 51.59 ..
6.3.m: Those fortunate ones who bestow [her] when the sun or the moon is seized [by eclipse]— / even in hundreds of years, I do not know the measure of their merit.

6.3.s:
sarvasyāpi hi dānasya saṃkhyāstīha narādhipa .
candrasūryoparāge ca dānasaṃkhyā na vidyate .. 51.60 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वस्यापि हि दानस्य संख्यास्तीह नराधिप .
चन्द्रसूर्योपरागे च दानसंख्या न विद्यते .. 51.60 ..
6.3.m: For in this world there is a count for every gift, O lord of men; / but during an eclipse of the moon or the sun, the gift cannot be counted.

6.3.s:
yatra gaurdṛśyate rājan sarvatīrthāni tatra hi .
tatra parva vijānīyānnātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 51.61 ..
6.3.d:
यत्र गौर्दृश्यते राजन् सर्वतीर्थानि तत्र हि .
तत्र पर्व विजानीयान्नात्र कार्या विचारणा .. 51.61 ..
6.3.m: Where a cow is seen, O king, there indeed are all the sacred fords; / there one should recognize an auspicious occasion; no doubt should be entertained here.

6.3.s:
punaḥ smṛtvā tu tattīrthaṃ yaḥ kuryādgamanaṃ naraḥ .
athavā mriyate yo'tra rudrasyānucaro bhavet .. 51.62 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe śūlabhede dānadharmapraśaṃsāvarṇanaṃ nāmaikapañcāśattamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 52
6.3.d:
पुनः स्मृत्वा तु तत्तीर्थं यः कुर्याद्गमनं नरः .
अथवा म्रियते योऽत्र रुद्रस्यानुचरो भवेत् .. 51.62 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे शूलभेदे दानधर्मप्रशंसावर्णनं नामैकपञ्चाशत्तमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 52
6.3.m:
Moreover, a man who, remembering that sacred ford, goes there, / or who dies there, becomes an attendant of Rudra.
Thus ends the fifty-first chapter, entitled “Praise of the Duty of Giving at Śūlabheda,” in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth Avantī section in the glorious Skanda Purāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 52

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
anyadākhyānakaṃ vakṣye purā vṛttaṃ narādhipa .
sakuṭumbo gataḥ svargaṃ muniryatra mahātapāḥ .. 52.1 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
अन्यदाख्यानकं वक्ष्ये पुरा वृत्तं नराधिप .
सकुटुम्बो गतः स्वर्गं मुनिर्यत्र महातपाः .. 52.1 ..
6.3.m: Īśvara said: / I shall tell another narrative that occurred long ago, O lord of men, / in which a sage of great austerity went to heaven together with his family.

6.3.s:
uttānapāda uvāca -
kathaṃ nākaṃ gato vipraḥ sakuṭumbo mahānṛṣiḥ .
kautukaṃ paramaṃ deva kathayasva mama prabho .. 52.2 ..
6.3.d:
उत्तानपाद उवाच -
कथं नाकं गतो विप्रः सकुटुम्बो महानृषिः .
कौतुकं परमं देव कथयस्व मम प्रभो .. 52.2 ..
6.3.m: Uttānapāda said: / How did the brahmin, the great seer, go to heaven with his family? / Tell me, O Lord, O God; it is a matter of supreme curiosity to me.

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
citrasena iti khyātaḥ kāśīrājaḥ purābhavat .
śūro dātā sudharmātmā sarvakāmasamṛddhimān .. 52.3 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
चित्रसेन इति ख्यातः काशीराजः पुराभवत् .
शूरो दाता सुधर्मात्मा सर्वकामसमृद्धिमान् .. 52.3 ..
6.3.m: Īśvara said: / Long ago there was a king of Kāśī known as Citrasena, / heroic, generous, very righteous, and abundant in every desire.

6.3.s:
sā purī janasaṃkīrṇā nānāratnopaśobhitā .
vārāṇasīti vikhyātā gaṅgātīramupāśritā .. 52.4 ..
6.3.d:
सा पुरी जनसंकीर्णा नानारत्नोपशोभिता .
वाराणसीति विख्याता गङ्गातीरमुपाश्रिता .. 52.4 ..
6.3.m: That city, crowded with people and adorned with various gems, / was renowned as Vārāṇasī, resting upon the bank of the Gaṅgā.

6.3.s:
śaraccandrapratīkāśā vidvajjanavibhūṣitā .
indrayaṣṭisamākīrṇā gopagokulasaṃvṛtā .. 52.5 ..
6.3.d:
शरच्चन्द्रप्रतीकाशा विद्वज्जनविभूषिता .
इन्द्रयष्टिसमाकीर्णा गोपगोकुलसंवृता .. 52.5 ..
6.3.m: Resplendent like the autumn moon, adorned with learned men, / crowded with Indra’s poles, and surrounded by herds of cattle and cowherds,

6.3.s:
bahudhvajasamākīrṇā vedadhvaninināditā .
vaṇigjanairbahuvidhaiḥ krayavikrayaśālinī .. 52.6 ..
6.3.d:
बहुध्वजसमाकीर्णा वेदध्वनिनिनादिता .
वणिग्जनैर्बहुविधैः क्रयविक्रयशालिनी .. 52.6 ..
6.3.m: it was crowded with many banners and made resonant with the sound of the Vedas, / flourishing with buying and selling conducted by various merchants.

6.3.s:
yantrādānaiḥ pratolībhiruccaiścānyaiḥ suśobhitā .
devatāyatanairdivyairāśramairgahanairyutā .. 52.7 ..
6.3.d:
यन्त्रादानैः प्रतोलीभिरुच्चैश्चान्यैः सुशोभिता .
देवतायतनैर्दिव्यैराश्रमैर्गहनैर्युता .. 52.7 ..
6.3.m: It was beautifully adorned with mechanical defenses, streets, and other lofty structures, / and endowed with divine temples of deities and dense hermitages.

6.3.s:
nānāpuṣpaphalairramyā kadalīkhaṇḍamaṇḍitā .
panasairbakulaistālairaśokairāmrakaistathā .. 52.8 ..
6.3.d:
नानापुष्पफलैर्रम्या कदलीखण्डमण्डिता .
पनसैर्बकुलैस्तालैरशोकैराम्रकैस्तथा .. 52.8 ..
6.3.m: Delightful with various flowers and fruits, adorned with groves of plantains, / with jackfruits, bakulas, palmyras, aśokas, and mangos,

6.3.s:
rājavṛkṣakapitthaiśca dāḍimairupaśobhitā .
vedādhyayananirghoṣaiḥ pavitrīkṛtamaṅgalā .. 52.9 ..
6.3.d:
राजवृक्षकपित्थैश्च दाडिमैरुपशोभिता .
वेदाध्ययननिर्घोषैः पवित्रीकृतमङ्गला .. 52.9 ..
6.3.m: and adorned with rājavṛkṣas, kapitthas, and pomegranates, / its auspiciousness was made pure by the loud chanting of Vedic study.

6.3.s:
tasyā uttaradigbhāge āśramo'bhūtsuśobhanaḥ .
tanmandāravanaṃ nāma triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam .. 52.10 ..
6.3.d:
तस्या उत्तरदिग्भागे आश्रमोऽभूत्सुशोभनः .
तन्मन्दारवनं नाम त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम् .. 52.10 ..
6.3.m: In the northern part of it, there was a very beautiful hermitage, / known throughout the three worlds as Mandāravana.

6.3.s:
bahumandārasaṃyuktaṃ tena mandārakaṃ viduḥ .
vipro dīrghatapā nāma sarvadā tatra tiṣṭhati .. 52.11 ..
6.3.d:
बहुमन्दारसंयुक्तं तेन मन्दारकं विदुः .
विप्रो दीर्घतपा नाम सर्वदा तत्र तिष्ठति .. 52.11 ..
6.3.m: Because it was filled with many coral trees, they called it Mandāraka. / A brahmin named Dīrghatapas always resided there.

6.3.s:
tapastapati so'tyarthaṃ tena dīrghatapāḥ smṛtaḥ .
sa tiṣṭhati sapatnīkaḥ sasutaḥ sasnuṣastathā .. 52.12 ..
6.3.d:
तपस्तपति सोऽत्यर्थं तेन दीर्घतपाः स्मृतः .
स तिष्ठति सपत्नीकः ससुतः सस्नुषस्तथा .. 52.12 ..
6.3.m: He performed intense austerity, and was thus remembered as Dīrghatapas. / He resided there with his wife, with his sons, and with his daughters-in-law.

6.3.s:
śuśrūṣanti sadā tasya putrāḥ pañca prayatnataḥ .
tasya putraḥ kanīyāṃstu ṛkṣaśṛṅgo mahātapāḥ .. 52.13 ..
6.3.d:
शुश्रूषन्ति सदा तस्य पुत्राः पञ्च प्रयत्नतः .
तस्य पुत्रः कनीयांस्तु ऋक्षशृङ्गो महातपाः .. 52.13 ..
6.3.m: His five sons always served him diligently. / His youngest son was Ṛkṣaśṛṅga, a man of great austerity,

6.3.s:
vedādhyayanasampanno brahmacārī guṇānvitaḥ .
yogābhyāsarato nityaṃ kandamūlaphalāśanaḥ .. 52.14 ..
6.3.d:
वेदाध्ययनसम्पन्नो ब्रह्मचारी गुणान्वितः .
योगाभ्यासरतो नित्यं कन्दमूलफलाशनः .. 52.14 ..
6.3.m: endowed with Vedic study, a celibate student possessed of virtues, / constantly devoted to the practice of yoga, subsisting on roots and fruits.

6.3.s:
tiṣṭhate mṛgarūpeṇa mṛgayūthacarastadā .
dinānte ca dinānte ca mātāpitroḥ samīpagaḥ .. 52.15 ..
6.3.d:
तिष्ठते मृगरूपेण मृगयूथचरस्तदा .
दिनान्ते च दिनान्ते च मातापित्रोः समीपगः .. 52.15 ..
6.3.m: At that time, roaming among a herd of deer in the form of a deer, he remained there. / And at the end of every day, going near his parents,

6.3.s:
abhivādayate nityaṃ bhaktimānmuniputrakaḥ .
punargacchati tatraiva kānane girigahvare .. 52.16 ..
6.3.d:
अभिवादयते नित्यं भक्तिमान्मुनिपुत्रकः .
पुनर्गच्छति तत्रैव कानने गिरिगह्वरे .. 52.16 ..
6.3.m: the devoted son of the sage always paid homage to them. / Then he would go back to that very forest, into a mountain cave.

6.3.s:
krīḍanbālamṛgaiḥ sārddhaṃ pratyahaṃ sa muneḥ sutaḥ .
kadāciddaivayogena ṛkṣaśṛṅgo mamāra saḥ .. 52.17 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe śūlabhedamāhātmye ṛkṣaśṛṅgacaritre dīrghatapomunyākhyānavarṇanaṃ nāma dvipañcāśattamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 53
6.3.d:
क्रीडन्बालमृगैः सार्द्धं प्रत्यहं स मुनेः सुतः .
कदाचिद्दैवयोगेन ऋक्षशृङ्गो ममार सः .. 52.17 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे शूलभेदमाहात्म्ये ऋक्षशृङ्गचरित्रे दीर्घतपोमुन्याख्यानवर्णनं नाम द्विपञ्चाशत्तमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 53
6.3.m:
Playing daily with the young deer, that son of the sage / once died, through the workings of destiny—that Ṛkṣaśṛṅga.
Thus ends the fifty-second chapter, entitled “The Narration of the Story of the Sage Dīrghatapas, in the Account of Ṛkṣaśṛṅga,” in the greatness of Śūlabheda in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth Avantī section in the glorious Skanda Purāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 53

6.3.s:
uttānapāda uvāca -
āśrame vasatastasya sa dīrghatapaso muneḥ .
kanīyāṃstanayo deva kathaṃ mṛtyumupāgataḥ .. 53.1 ..
6.3.d:
उत्तानपाद उवाच -
आश्रमे वसतस्तस्य स दीर्घतपसो मुनेः .
कनीयांस्तनयो देव कथं मृत्युमुपागतः .. 53.1 ..
6.3.m: Uttānapāda said: / While he dwelt in the hermitage, O God, how did that younger son / of the sage Dīrghatapas meet his death?

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
śṛṇuṣvaikamanā bhūtvā kathāṃ divyāṃ mahīpate .
śravaṇādeva yasyāstu mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ .. 53.2 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
शृणुष्वैकमना भूत्वा कथां दिव्यां महीपते .
श्रवणादेव यस्यास्तु मुच्यते सर्वकिल्बिषैः .. 53.2 ..
6.3.m: Īśvara said: / Listen with single-minded attention, O king, to the divine tale, / by the mere hearing of which one is freed from all sins.

6.3.s:
kāśīrājo mahāvīryo mahābalaparākramaḥ .
citrasena iti khyātāṃ dharaṇyāṃ sa narādhipa .. 53.3 ..
6.3.d:
काशीराजो महावीर्यो महाबलपराक्रमः .
चित्रसेन इति ख्यातां धरण्यां स नराधिप .. 53.3 ..
6.3.m: There was a king of Kāśī of great valor and of mighty strength and prowess, / renowned on earth, O lord of men, as Citrasena.

6.3.s:
tasya rājye sadā dharmo nādharmo vidyate kvacit .
vedadharmarato nityaṃ prajā dharmeṇa pālayan .. 53.4 ..
6.3.d:
तस्य राज्ये सदा धर्मो नाधर्मो विद्यते क्वचित् .
वेदधर्मरतो नित्यं प्रजा धर्मेण पालयन् .. 53.4 ..
6.3.m: In his realm there was always righteousness; unrighteousness was nowhere to be found. / He was constantly devoted to Vedic dharma, protecting the subjects righteously.

6.3.s:
svadharmanirataścaiva yuddhātithyapriyaḥ sadā .
kṣatradharmaṃ samāśritya bhogānbhuṅkte sa kāmataḥ .. 53.5 ..
6.3.d:
स्वधर्मनिरतश्चैव युद्धातिथ्यप्रियः सदा .
क्षत्रधर्मं समाश्रित्य भोगान्भुङ्क्ते स कामतः .. 53.5 ..
6.3.m: Devoted to his own duty, always fond of war and hospitality, / adhering to the duty of a kṣatriya, he enjoyed pleasures at will.

6.3.s:
kośasyānto na vidyeta hastyaśvarathapattimān .
itihāsapurāṇajñaiḥ paṇḍitaiḥ saha saṃkathām .. 53.6 ..
6.3.d:
कोशस्यान्तो न विद्येत हस्त्यश्वरथपत्तिमान् .
इतिहासपुराणज्ञैः पण्डितैः सह संकथाम् .. 53.6 ..
6.3.m: There was no end to his treasury; he possessed elephants, horses, chariots, and foot-soldiers. / Conversing with learned men conversant with the Itihāsas and Purāṇas,

6.3.s:
kathayanrājate rājā kailāsa iva śaṅkaraḥ .
evaṃ sa pālayanrājyaṃ rājā mantriṇamabravīt .. 53.7 ..
6.3.d:
कथयन्राजते राजा कैलास इव शङ्करः .
एवं स पालयन्राज्यं राजा मन्त्रिणमब्रवीत् .. 53.7 ..
6.3.m: the king shone like Śaṅkara on Mount Kailāsa. / Protecting the kingdom in this manner, the king said to his minister:

6.3.s:
mṛgayāyāṃ gamiṣyāmi tiṣṭhadhvaṃ rājyapālane .
gamyatāṃ sacivaiḥ prokte gato'sau vasudhādhipaḥ .. 53.8 ..
6.3.d:
मृगयायां गमिष्यामि तिष्ठध्वं राज्यपालने .
गम्यतां सचिवैः प्रोक्ते गतोऽसौ वसुधाधिपः .. 53.8 ..
6.3.m: “I shall go on a hunt; remain here protecting the kingdom.” / When the ministers said, “Go,” that lord of the earth set out.

6.3.s:
aśvārūḍhāśca dhāvanto rājāno maṇḍalādhipāḥ .
chatraiśchatrāṇi ghṛṣyanto'nujagmuḥ kānanaṃ prati .. 53.9 ..
6.3.d:
अश्वारूढाश्च धावन्तो राजानो मण्डलाधिपाः .
छत्रैश्छत्राणि घृष्यन्तोऽनुजग्मुः काननं प्रति .. 53.9 ..
6.3.m: Riding on horses and galloping along, kings and rulers of provinces, / their parasols rubbing against one another, followed toward the forest.

6.3.s:
rajastatrotthitaṃ bhaumaṃ gajavājipadāhatam .
tenaitacchāditaṃ sarvaṃ sadiṅmārtaṇḍamaṃlam .. 53.10 ..
6.3.d:
रजस्तत्रोत्थितं भौमं गजवाजिपदाहतम् .
तेनैतच्छादितं सर्वं सदिङ्मार्तण्डमंलम् .. 53.10 ..
6.3.m: The earthly dust raised there, struck by the feet of elephants and horses, / covered everything, together with the quarters of space and the disc of the sun.

6.3.s:
na tatra dṛśyate sūryo na kāṣṭhā na ca candramāḥ .
pādapāśca na dṛśyante giriśṛṅgāṇi sarvataḥ .. 53.11 ..
6.3.d:
न तत्र दृश्यते सूर्यो न काष्ठा न च चन्द्रमाः .
पादपाश्च न दृश्यन्ते गिरिशृङ्गाणि सर्वतः .. 53.11 ..
6.3.m: Neither the sun, nor the cardinal directions, nor the moon could be seen there; / nor could the trees and mountain peaks be seen anywhere.

6.3.s:
parasparaṃ na paśyanti niśārddhe vārṣike yathā .
tatrāsau sumahadyūthaṃ mṛgāṇāṃ samalakṣyata .. 53.12 ..
6.3.d:
परस्परं न पश्यन्ति निशार्द्धे वार्षिके यथा .
तत्रासौ सुमहद्यूथं मृगाणां समलक्ष्यत .. 53.12 ..
6.3.m: They could not see one another, just as in the middle of a night in the rainy season. / Then he sighted an immense herd of deer there.

6.3.s:
adhāvatsahitaḥ sarvaiḥ sa rājā rājaputrakaiḥ .
vṛndāsphoṭo'bhavatteṣāṃ śīghraṃ jagmurdiśo daśa .. 53.13 ..
6.3.d:
अधावत्सहितः सर्वैः स राजा राजपुत्रकैः .
वृन्दास्फोटोऽभवत्तेषां शीघ्रं जग्मुर्दिशो दश .. 53.13 ..
6.3.m: The king ran accompanied by all the princes; / their gathering broke apart, and they quickly scattered in the ten directions.

6.3.s:
ekamārgagato rājā citraseno mahīpatiḥ .
ekākī sa gatastatra yatra yatra ca te mṛgāḥ .. 53.14 ..
6.3.d:
एकमार्गगतो राजा चित्रसेनो महीपतिः .
एकाकी स गतस्तत्र यत्र यत्र च ते मृगाः .. 53.14 ..
6.3.m: King Citrasena, the lord of the earth, took a single path; / he went alone wherever those deer went.

6.3.s:
praviṣṭo'sau tato durgaṃ kānanaṃ girigahvaram .
vallīgulmasamākīrṇaṃ sthito yatra na lakṣyate .. 53.15 ..
6.3.d:
प्रविष्टोऽसौ ततो दुर्गं काननं गिरिगह्वरम् .
वल्लीगुल्मसमाकीर्णं स्थितो यत्र न लक्ष्यते .. 53.15 ..
6.3.m: Then he entered an impassable forest and mountain cavern, / thick with creepers and bushes, where one could not be seen standing.

6.3.s:
adṛśyāṃstu mṛgānmatvā diśo rājā vyalokayat .
kāṃ diśaṃ nu gamiṣyāmi kva me sainyasamāgamaḥ .. 53.16 ..
6.3.d:
अदृश्यांस्तु मृगान्मत्वा दिशो राजा व्यलोकयत् .
कां दिशं नु गमिष्यामि क्व मे सैन्यसमागमः .. 53.16 ..
6.3.m: Considering the deer to have become invisible, the king looked around at the quarters of space: / “To which direction shall I go? Where is the reunion with my army?”

6.3.s:
evaṃ kaṣṭaṃ gato rājā citraseno narādhipaḥ .
vṛkṣacchāyāṃ samāśritya viśrāmamakaronnṛpaḥ .. 53.17 ..
6.3.d:
एवं कष्टं गतो राजा चित्रसेनो नराधिपः .
वृक्षच्छायां समाश्रित्य विश्राममकरोन्नृपः .. 53.17 ..
6.3.m: Having thus fallen into distress, King Citrasena, the lord of men, / took shelter under the shade of a tree and rested.

6.3.s:
kṣuttṛṣārto bhramandurge kānane girigahvare .
tato'paśyatsaro divyaṃ padminīkhaṇḍamaṇḍitam .. 53.18 ..
6.3.d:
क्षुत्तृषार्तो भ्रमन्दुर्गे कानने गिरिगह्वरे .
ततोऽपश्यत्सरो दिव्यं पद्मिनीखण्डमण्डितम् .. 53.18 ..
6.3.m: Afflicted with hunger and thirst, wandering in the impassable forest and mountain cave, / he then saw a divine lake adorned with clusters of lotuses.

6.3.s:
haṃsakāraṇḍavākīrṇaṃ cakravākopaśobhitam .
tato dṛṣṭvā sa rājendraḥ samprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ .. 53.19 ..
6.3.d:
हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णं चक्रवाकोपशोभितम् .
ततो दृष्ट्वा स राजेन्द्रः सम्प्रहृष्टतनूरुहः .. 53.19 ..
6.3.m: Filled with swans and kāraṇḍava ducks, adorned with cakravāka birds, / upon seeing it, that king of kings had the hair of his body stand on end with joy.

6.3.s:
kamalāni gṛhītvā tu tataḥ snānaṃ samācarat .
tarpayitvā pitṛdevānmanuṣyāṃśca yathāvidhi .. 53.20 ..
6.3.d:
कमलानि गृहीत्वा तु ततः स्नानं समाचरत् .
तर्पयित्वा पितृदेवान्मनुष्यांश्च यथाविधि .. 53.20 ..
6.3.m: Taking lotuses, he then performed ritual ablution, / having offered libations to the ancestors, gods, and men according to the injunctions.

6.3.s:
ācchādya śatapatraiśca pūjayāmāsa śaṅkaram .
yayau pānīyamamalaṃ yathāvatsa samāhitaḥ .. 53.21 ..
6.3.d:
आच्छाद्य शतपत्रैश्च पूजयामास शङ्करम् .
ययौ पानीयममलं यथावत्स समाहितः .. 53.21 ..
6.3.m: Covering [it] with lotuses, he worshipped Śaṃkara; / attentive, he drank pure water in the prescribed manner.

6.3.s:
uttīrya salilāttīre dṛṣṭvā vṛkṣaṃ samīpagam .
uttarīyamadhaḥ kṛtvopaviṣṭo dharaṇītale .. 53.22 ..
6.3.d:
उत्तीर्य सलिलात्तीरे दृष्ट्वा वृक्षं समीपगम् .
उत्तरीयमधः कृत्वोपविष्टो धरणीतले .. 53.22 ..
6.3.m: Coming out of the water onto the bank, seeing a tree nearby, / placing his upper garment below, he sat down on the surface of the ground.

6.3.s:
cintayannupaviṣṭo'sau kimadya prakaromyaham .
tatrāsīno dadarśātha vanoddeśe mṛgānbahūn .. 53.23 ..
6.3.d:
चिन्तयन्नुपविष्टोऽसौ किमद्य प्रकरोम्यहम् .
तत्रासीनो ददर्शाथ वनोद्देशे मृगान्बहून् .. 53.23 ..
6.3.m: Sitting there, he reflected: 'What shall I do today?' / Seated there, he then saw many deer in that part of the forest.

6.3.s:
kecitpūrvamukhāstatra cāpare dakṣiṇāmukhāḥ .
vāruṇyamimukhāḥ kecitkecitkauberadiṅmukhāḥ .. 53.24 ..
6.3.d:
केचित्पूर्वमुखास्तत्र चापरे दक्षिणामुखाः .
वारुण्यमिमुखाः केचित्केचित्कौबेरदिङ्मुखाः .. 53.24 ..
6.3.m: Some were facing east, others facing south, / some facing west, and some facing the quarter of Kubera [north].

6.3.s:
kecinnidrāparāḥ kecidūrdhvakarṇāḥ sthitāḥ pare .
mṛgamadhye sthito yogī ṛkṣaśṛṅgo mahātapāḥ .. 53.25 ..
6.3.d:
केचिन्निद्रापराः केचिदूर्ध्वकर्णाः स्थिताः परे .
मृगमध्ये स्थितो योगी ऋक्षशृङ्गो महातपाः .. 53.25 ..
6.3.m: Some were devoted to sleep; others stood with their ears pricked up. / In the midst of the deer was the yogin Ṛkṣaśṛṅga of great austerity.

6.3.s:
mṛgāndṛṣṭvā tato rājā āhārārthamacintayat .
hatvaiteṣu mṛgaṃ kaṃcidbhakṣayāmi yadṛcchayā .. 53.26 ..
6.3.d:
मृगान्दृष्ट्वा ततो राजा आहारार्थमचिन्तयत् .
हत्वैतेषु मृगं कंचिद्भक्षयामि यदृच्छया .. 53.26 ..
6.3.m: Seeing the deer, the king then thought of food: / 'Having killed one of these deer, I shall eat at will;

6.3.s:
svasthāvastho bhaviṣyāmi mṛgamāṃsasya bhakṣaṇāt .
kāśīṃ prati gamiṣyāmi mārgamanviṣya yatnataḥ .. 53.27 ..
6.3.d:
स्वस्थावस्थो भविष्यामि मृगमांसस्य भक्षणात् .
काशीं प्रति गमिष्यामि मार्गमन्विष्य यत्नतः .. 53.27 ..
6.3.m: I will regain my strength from eating deer meat, / [and then] I shall go toward Kāśī, searching for the way with effort.'

6.3.s:
vicintyaivaṃ tato rājā vṛkṣamūlamupāśritaḥ .
cāpaṃ gṛhya karāgreṇa sa śaraṃ saṃdadhe tataḥ .. 53.28 ..
6.3.d:
विचिन्त्यैवं ततो राजा वृक्षमूलमुपाश्रितः .
चापं गृह्य कराग्रेण स शरं संदधे ततः .. 53.28 ..
6.3.m: Having thought thus, the king, leaning against the foot of the tree, / took his bow in hand and then fitted an arrow.

6.3.s:
vicikṣepa śaraṃ tatra yatra te bahavo mṛgāḥ .
teṣāṃ madhye sa vai viddha ṛkṣaśṛṅgo mahātapāḥ .. 53.29 ..
6.3.d:
विचिक्षेप शरं तत्र यत्र ते बहवो मृगाः .
तेषां मध्ये स वै विद्ध ऋक्षशृङ्गो महातपाः .. 53.29 ..
6.3.m: He shot an arrow there, where those many deer were; / in their midst, that Ṛkṣaśṛṅga of great austerity was struck.

6.3.s:
jagmustrastāstu te sarve śabdaṃ kṛtvā vanaukasaḥ .
sa ṛṣiḥ patitastatra kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇeti cābravīt .. 53.30 ..
6.3.d:
जग्मुस्त्रस्तास्तु ते सर्वे शब्दं कृत्वा वनौकसः .
स ऋषिः पतितस्तत्र कृष्ण कृष्णेति चाब्रवीत् .. 53.30 ..
6.3.m: Frightened, all those forest-dwellers ran away, crying out; / that seer fell there and cried, 'Kṛṣṇa! Kṛṣṇa!'

6.3.s:
hāhā kaṣṭaṃ kṛtaṃ tena yenāhaṃ ghātito'dhunā .
kasyaiṣā durmatirjātā pāpabuddhermamopari .. 53.31 ..
6.3.d:
हाहा कष्टं कृतं तेन येनाहं घातितोऽधुना .
कस्यैषा दुर्मतिर्जाता पापबुद्धेर्ममोपरि .. 53.31 ..
6.3.m: 'Alas, a terrible deed has been done by the one who has now struck me down! / Whose evil intent, wicked of mind, has arisen against me?

6.3.s:
mṛgamadhye sthitaścāhaṃ na kaṃciduparodhaye .
tāṃ vācaṃ mānuṣīṃ śrutvā sa rājā vismayānvitaḥ .. 53.32 ..
6.3.d:
मृगमध्ये स्थितश्चाहं न कंचिदुपरोधये .
तां वाचं मानुषीं श्रुत्वा स राजा विस्मयान्वितः .. 53.32 ..
6.3.m: I stood among the deer, harming no one.' / Hearing that human voice, the king was filled with astonishment.

6.3.s:
śīghraṃ gatvā tato'paśyadbrāhmaṇaṃ brahmatejasā .
hāhā kaṣṭaṃ kṛtaṃ me'dya yenāsau ghātito dvijaḥ .. 53.33 ..
6.3.d:
शीघ्रं गत्वा ततोऽपश्यद्ब्राह्मणं ब्रह्मतेजसा .
हाहा कष्टं कृतं मेऽद्य येनासौ घातितो द्विजः .. 53.33 ..
6.3.m: Going quickly, he then saw a brahmin blazing with brahmanic splendor: / 'Alas, a terrible thing I have done today, by which this twice-born has been struck down!'

6.3.s:
citrasena uvāca -
akāmādghātitastvaṃ tu mṛgabhrāntyā mayānagha .
gṛhītvā bahudārūṇi svatanuṃ dāhayāmyaham .. 53.34 ..
6.3.d:
चित्रसेन उवाच -
अकामाद्घातितस्त्वं तु मृगभ्रान्त्या मयानघ .
गृहीत्वा बहुदारूणि स्वतनुं दाहयाम्यहम् .. 53.34 ..
6.3.m: Citrasena said: / 'Unintentionally, mistaking you for a deer, you have been struck down by me, O sinless one! / Gathering much wood, I will burn my own body.

6.3.s:
dṛṣṭādṛṣṭaṃ tu yatkiṃcinna samaṃ brahmahatyayā .
anyathā brahmahatyāyāḥ śuddhirme na bhaviṣyati .. 53.35 ..
6.3.d:
दृष्टादृष्टं तु यत्किंचिन्न समं ब्रह्महत्यया .
अन्यथा ब्रह्महत्यायाः शुद्धिर्मे न भविष्यति .. 53.35 ..
6.3.m: Whatever [sin] exists, seen or unseen, none equals the murder of a brahmin. / Otherwise, my purification from the murder of a brahmin will not come to pass.'

6.3.s:
ṛkṣaśṛṅga uvāca -
na te siddhirbhavetkācinmayi pañcatvamāgate .
bahvyo hatyā bhaviṣyanti vināśe mama sāmpratam .. 53.36 ..
6.3.d:
ऋक्षशृङ्ग उवाच -
न ते सिद्धिर्भवेत्काचिन्मयि पञ्चत्वमागते .
बह्व्यो हत्या भविष्यन्ति विनाशे मम साम्प्रतम् .. 53.36 ..
6.3.m: Ṛkṣaśṛṅga said: / 'No attainment whatsoever will be yours if I meet my death. / Many deaths will follow upon my destruction now.

6.3.s:
jananī me pitā vṛddho bhrātaraśca tapasvinaḥ .
bhrātṛjāyā mariṣyanti mayi pañcatvamāgate .. 53.37 ..
6.3.d:
जननी मे पिता वृद्धो भ्रातरश्च तपस्विनः .
भ्रातृजाया मरिष्यन्ति मयि पञ्चत्वमागते .. 53.37 ..
6.3.m: My mother, my aged father, my ascetic brothers, / and my brothers' wives will die if I meet my death.

6.3.s:
etā hatyā bhaviṣyanti kathaṃ śuddhirbhavettava .
upāyaṃ kathayiṣyāmi taṃ kartuṃ yadi manyase .. 53.38 ..
6.3.d:
एता हत्या भविष्यन्ति कथं शुद्धिर्भवेत्तव .
उपायं कथयिष्यामि तं कर्तुं यदि मन्यसे .. 53.38 ..
6.3.m: These killings will happen; how will your purification come to pass? / I will tell you a remedy, if you think to do it.'

6.3.s:
citrasena uvāca -
upāyaḥ kathyatāṃ me'dya yaste manasi vartate .
kariṣye tamahaṃ sarvaṃ yatnenāpi mahāmune .. 53.39 ..
6.3.d:
चित्रसेन उवाच -
उपायः कथ्यतां मेऽद्य यस्ते मनसि वर्तते .
करिष्ये तमहं सर्वं यत्नेनापि महामुने .. 53.39 ..
6.3.m: Citrasena said: / 'Tell me today the remedy that is in your mind; / I will do all of it with every effort, O great sage.'

6.3.s:
ṛkṣaśṛṅga uvāca -
pṛcchāmi tvāṃ kathaṃ ko vā kutastvamiha cāgataḥ .
brahmakṣatraviśāṃ madhye ko bhavānuta śūdrajaḥ .. 53.40 ..
6.3.d:
ऋक्षशृङ्ग उवाच -
पृच्छामि त्वां कथं को वा कुतस्त्वमिह चागतः .
ब्रह्मक्षत्रविशां मध्ये को भवानुत शूद्रजः .. 53.40 ..
6.3.m: Ṛkṣaśṛṅga said: / 'I ask you: who are you, and whence have you come here? / Among brahmins, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas, which are you—or born of a śūdra?'

6.3.s:
citrasena uvāca -
nāhaṃ śūdro'smi bhostāta na vaiśyo brāhmaṇo na vā .
na cāntyajo'smi viprendra kṣatriyo'smi mahāmune .. 53.41 ..
6.3.d:
चित्रसेन उवाच -
नाहं शूद्रोऽस्मि भोस्तात न वैश्यो ब्राह्मणो न वा .
न चान्त्यजोऽस्मि विप्रेन्द्र क्षत्रियोऽस्मि महामुने .. 53.41 ..
6.3.m: Citrasena said: / 'I am not a śūdra, sir, nor a vaiśya, nor a brahmin; / nor am I an outcaste, O foremost of the twice-born: I am a kṣatriya, O great sage,

6.3.s:
dharmajñaśca kṛtajñaśca sarvasattvahite rataḥ .
akāmātpātakaṃ jātaṃ kathaṃ śuddhirbhaviṣyati .. 53.42 ..
6.3.d:
धर्मज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च सर्वसत्त्वहिते रतः .
अकामात्पातकं जातं कथं शुद्धिर्भविष्यति .. 53.42 ..
6.3.m: knowing righteousness, grateful, and devoted to the welfare of all beings. / The sin has occurred unintentionally; how will purification come to pass?'

6.3.s:
ṛkṣaśṛṅga uvāca -
māṃ gṛhītvā āśramaṃ gaccha yatra tau pitarau mama .
āvedayasva cātmānaṃ putraghātinamāturam .. 53.43 ..
6.3.d:
ऋक्षशृङ्ग उवाच -
मां गृहीत्वा आश्रमं गच्छ यत्र तौ पितरौ मम .
आवेदयस्व चात्मानं पुत्रघातिनमातुरम् .. 53.43 ..
6.3.m: Ṛkṣaśṛṅga said: / 'Take me and go to the hermitage where my parents are, / and announce yourself as the afflicted killer of their son.

6.3.s:
te dṛṣṭvā māṃ kariṣyanti kāruṇyaṃ ca tavopari .
upāyaṃ kathayiṣyanti yena śāntirbhaviṣyati .. 53.44 ..
6.3.d:
ते दृष्ट्वा मां करिष्यन्ति कारुण्यं च तवोपरि .
उपायं कथयिष्यन्ति येन शान्तिर्भविष्यति .. 53.44 ..
6.3.m: Seeing me, they will have compassion on you; / they will tell you the remedy by which peace will be attained.'

6.3.s:
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā citraseno nṛpottama .
skandhe kṛtvā tu taṃ vipraṃ jagāmāśramasannidhau .. 53.45 ..
6.3.d:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा चित्रसेनो नृपोत्तम .
स्कन्धे कृत्वा तु तं विप्रं जगामाश्रमसन्निधौ .. 53.45 ..
6.3.m: Hearing his words, Citrasena, best of kings, / took the twice-born on his shoulder and went toward the hermitage.

6.3.s:
na śaknoti yadā voḍhuṃ viśrāmyati punaḥpunaḥ .
tāvatpaśyati taṃ vipraṃ mūrchitaṃ vikalendriyam .. 53.46 ..
6.3.d:
न शक्नोति यदा वोढुं विश्राम्यति पुनःपुनः .
तावत्पश्यति तं विप्रं मूर्छितं विकलेन्द्रियम् .. 53.46 ..
6.3.m: When he was unable to carry him, resting again and again, / he then saw that twice-born fainted, his faculties failing.

6.3.s:
mumoca citrasenastaṃ chāyāyāṃ vaṭabhūruhaḥ .
vastraṃ caturguṇaṃ kṛtvā cakre vātaṃ muhurmuhuḥ .. 53.47 ..
6.3.d:
मुमोच चित्रसेनस्तं छायायां वटभूरुहः .
वस्त्रं चतुर्गुणं कृत्वा चक्रे वातं मुहुर्मुहुः .. 53.47 ..
6.3.m: Citrasena set him down in the shade of a banyan tree; / folding a cloth fourfold, he fanned him repeatedly.

6.3.s:
paśyatastasya rājendra ṛkṣaśṛṅgo mahātapāḥ .
pañcatvamagamacchīghraṃ dhyānayogena yogavit .. 53.48 ..
6.3.d:
पश्यतस्तस्य राजेन्द्र ऋक्षशृङ्गो महातपाः .
पञ्चत्वमगमच्छीघ्रं ध्यानयोगेन योगवित् .. 53.48 ..
6.3.m: As he watched, O king of kings, Ṛkṣaśṛṅga of great austerity, / skilled in yoga, swiftly met his death through the yoga of meditation.

6.3.s:
dāhayāmāsa taṃ vipraṃ vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā .
snānaṃ kṛtvā sa śokārto vilalāpa muhurmuhuḥ .. 53.49 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe śūlabhedamāhātmye ṛkṣaśṛṅgasvargagamanavarṇanaṃ nāma tripañcāśattamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 54
6.3.d:
दाहयामास तं विप्रं विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा .
स्नानं कृत्वा स शोकार्तो विललाप मुहुर्मुहुः .. 53.49 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे शूलभेदमाहात्म्ये ऋक्षशृङ्गस्वर्गगमनवर्णनं नाम त्रिपञ्चाशत्तमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 54
6.3.m:
He cremated that twice-born according to the prescribed rite; / having performed ritual ablution, stricken with grief, he lamented repeatedly.
Thus ends the fifty-third chapter, entitled 'Description of Ṛkṣaśṛṅga's Departure to Heaven' in the Śūlabhedamāhātmya of the Revākhaṇḍa in the fifth Āvantyakhaṇḍa of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 54

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
tataścānantaraṃ rājā jagāmodvegamuttamam .
kathaṃ yāmi gṛhaṃ tvadya vārāṇasyāmahaṃ punaḥ .. 54.1 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
ततश्चानन्तरं राजा जगामोद्वेगमुत्तमम् .
कथं यामि गृहं त्वद्य वाराणस्यामहं पुनः .. 54.1 ..
6.3.m: Īśvara said: / Thereupon, the king was seized with great agitation: / 'How can I go home to Vārāṇasī now?

6.3.s:
brahmahatyāsamāviṣṭo juhomyagnau kalevaram .
athavā tasya vākyena taṃ gacchāmyāśramaṃ prati .. 54.2 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रह्महत्यासमाविष्टो जुहोम्यग्नौ कलेवरम् .
अथवा तस्य वाक्येन तं गच्छाम्याश्रमं प्रति .. 54.2 ..
6.3.m: Overcome by the murder of a brahmin, I shall offer my body into the fire; / or, according to his word, I shall go to that hermitage.

6.3.s:
kathayāmi yathāvṛttaṃ gatvā tasya mahāmuneḥ .
evaṃ saṃcintya rājāsau jagāmāśramasannidhau .. 54.3 ..
6.3.d:
कथयामि यथावृत्तं गत्वा तस्य महामुनेः .
एवं संचिन्त्य राजासौ जगामाश्रमसन्निधौ .. 54.3 ..
6.3.m: Going to that great sage, I shall report what has happened.' / Reflecting thus, the king went near the hermitage.

6.3.s:
ṛkṣaśṛṅgasya cāsthīni gṛhītvā sa nṛpottamaḥ .
dṛṣṭimārge sthitastasya maharṣerbhāvitātmanaḥ .. 54.4 ..
6.3.d:
ऋक्षशृङ्गस्य चास्थीनि गृहीत्वा स नृपोत्तमः .
दृष्टिमार्गे स्थितस्तस्य महर्षेर्भावितात्मनः .. 54.4 ..
6.3.m: Taking the bones of Ṛkṣaśṛṅga, that best of kings / stood within the line of sight of that great seer of cultivated soul.

6.3.s:
dīrghatapā uvāca -
āgaccha svāgataṃ te'stu āsane'tropaviśyatām .
arghaṃ dadāmyahaṃ yena madhuparkaṃ saviṣṭaram .. 54.5 ..
6.3.d:
दीर्घतपा उवाच -
आगच्छ स्वागतं तेऽस्तु आसनेऽत्रोपविश्यताम् .
अर्घं ददाम्यहं येन मधुपर्कं सविष्टरम् .. 54.5 ..
6.3.m: Dīrghatapas said: / 'Come, welcome to you! Sit down on this seat, / so that I may offer argha-water, madhuparka, and a woven seat.'

6.3.s:
citrasena uvāca -
arghasyāsya na yogyo'haṃ maharṣe nāsmi bhāṣaṇe .
mṛgamadhyasthito viprastava putro mayā hataḥ .. 54.6 ..
6.3.d:
चित्रसेन उवाच -
अर्घस्यास्य न योग्योऽहं महर्षे नास्मि भाषणे .
मृगमध्यस्थितो विप्रस्तव पुत्रो मया हतः .. 54.6 ..
6.3.m: Citrasena said: / 'I am not worthy of this argha-water, O great seer, nor to speak [with you]; / standing amidst deer, your son, a twice-born, has been killed by me.

6.3.s:
putraghnaṃ viddhi māṃ vipra tīvradaṇḍena daṇḍaya .
mṛgabhrāntyā hato vipra ṛkṣaśṛṅgo mahātapāḥ .. 54.7 ..
6.3.d:
पुत्रघ्नं विद्धि मां विप्र तीव्रदण्डेन दण्डय .
मृगभ्रान्त्या हतो विप्र ऋक्षशृङ्गो महातपाः .. 54.7 ..
6.3.m: Know me as the killer of your son, O twice-born, and punish me with severe punishment; / mistaking him for a deer, the twice-born Ṛkṣaśṛṅga of great austerity was killed.

6.3.s:
iti matvā muniśreṣṭha kuru me tvaṃ yathocitam .
mātā tadvacanaṃ śrutvā gṛhānniṣkramya vihvalā .. 54.8 ..
6.3.d:
इति मत्वा मुनिश्रेष्ठ कुरु मे त्वं यथोचितम् .
माता तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा गृहान्निष्क्रम्य विह्वला .. 54.8 ..
6.3.m: Considering this, O best of sages, do to me what is proper.' / Hearing his words, the mother, emerging from the house, distraught,

6.3.s:
hā hatāsmītyuvācedaṃ papāta dharaṇītale .
vilalāpa suduḥkhārtā putraśokena pīḍitā .. 54.9 ..
6.3.d:
हा हतास्मीत्युवाचेदं पपात धरणीतले .
विललाप सुदुःखार्ता पुत्रशोकेन पीडिता .. 54.9 ..
6.3.m: cried out, 'Alas, I am undone!' and fell to the ground; / she wailed, intensely grief-stricken, tormented by sorrow for her son.

6.3.s:
hā hatā putra putreti karuṇaṃ kurarī yathā .
vilalāpāturā mātā kva gato māṃ vihāya vai .
mukhaṃ darśaya cātmīyaṃ mātaraṃ māṃ hi mānaya .. 54.10 ..
6.3.d:
हा हता पुत्र पुत्रेति करुणं कुररी यथा .
विललापातुरा माता क्व गतो मां विहाय वै .
मुखं दर्शय चात्मीयं मातरं मां हि मानय .. 54.10 ..
6.3.m: "Alas, I am undone! My son, my son!" Thus like an osprey plaintively / cried the distressed mother: "Where have you gone, abandoning me? / Show me your face, and show respect to me, your mother! 54.10

6.3.s:
śrutādhyayanasampannaṃ japahomaparāyaṇam .
āgataṃ tvāṃ gṛhadvāre kadā drakṣyāmi putraka .. 54.11 ..
6.3.d:
श्रुताध्ययनसम्पन्नं जपहोमपरायणम् .
आगतं त्वां गृहद्वारे कदा द्रक्ष्यामि पुत्रक .. 54.11 ..
6.3.m: Endowed with sacred learning and study, devoted to silent recitation and oblations— / when shall I see you, dear son, arriving at the door of our house? 54.11

6.3.s:
lokoktyā śrūyate caitaccandanaṃ kila śītalam .
putragātrapariṣvaṅgaścandanādapi śītalaḥ .. 54.12 ..
6.3.d:
लोकोक्त्या श्रूयते चैतच्चन्दनं किल शीतलम् .
पुत्रगात्रपरिष्वङ्गश्चन्दनादपि शीतलः .. 54.12 ..
6.3.m: It is heard in worldly proverbs that sandalwood is indeed cool; / but the embrace of a son's limbs is cooler even than sandalwood. 54.12

6.3.s: kiṃ candanena pīyūpabindunā kiṃ kimindunā .. 54.13 ..
6.3.d: किं चन्दनेन पीयूपबिन्दुना किं किमिन्दुना .. 54.13 ..
6.3.m: What need of sandalwood, what need of a drop of nectar, what need of the moon, 54.13

6.3.s: putragātrapariṣvaṅgapātraṃ gātraṃ bhavedyadi .. 54.14 ..
6.3.d: पुत्रगात्रपरिष्वङ्गपात्रं गात्रं भवेद्यदि .. 54.14 ..
6.3.m: if the body should be the recipient of the embrace of a son's body? 54.14

6.3.s:
pariṣvajitumicchāmi tvāmahaṃ putra supriya .
pañcatvamanuyāsyāmi tvadvihīnādya duḥkhitā .. 54.15 ..
6.3.d:
परिष्वजितुमिच्छामि त्वामहं पुत्र सुप्रिय .
पञ्चत्वमनुयास्यामि त्वद्विहीनाद्य दुःखिता .. 54.15 ..
6.3.m: I desire to embrace you, dearest son. / Bereft of you today, sorrowful, I shall go to dissolution [in death]." 54.15

6.3.s:
evaṃ vilapatī dīnā putraśokena pīḍitā .
mūrchitā vihvalā dīnā nipapāta mahītale .. 54.16 ..
6.3.d:
एवं विलपती दीना पुत्रशोकेन पीडिता .
मूर्छिता विह्वला दीना निपपात महीतले .. 54.16 ..
6.3.m: Lamenting thus, wretched, afflicted by grief for her son, / fainting, distraught, and pitiful, she fell down upon the ground. 54.16

6.3.s:
bhāryāṃ ca patitāṃ dṛṣṭvā putraśokena pīḍitām .
cukopa sa munistatra citrasenāya bhūbhṛte .. 54.17 ..
6.3.d:
भार्यां च पतितां दृष्ट्वा पुत्रशोकेन पीडिताम् .
चुकोप स मुनिस्तत्र चित्रसेनाय भूभृते .. 54.17 ..
6.3.m: And seeing his wife fallen, afflicted by grief for her son, / the sage then grew enraged at King Citrasena. 54.17

6.3.s:
dīrghatapā uvāca -
yāhi yāhi mahāpāpa mā mukhaṃ darśayasva me .
kiṃ tvayā ghātito vipro hyakāmācca suto mama .. 54.18 ..
6.3.d:
दीर्घतपा उवाच -
याहि याहि महापाप मा मुखं दर्शयस्व मे .
किं त्वया घातितो विप्रो ह्यकामाच्च सुतो मम .. 54.18 ..
6.3.m: Dīrghatapas said: / "Begone, begone, great sinner! Do not show me your face! / Why did you unwittingly kill a brahmin, my son? 54.18

6.3.s:
brahmahatyā bhaviṣyanti bahvyaste vasudhādhipa .
sakuṭumbasya me tvaṃ hi mṛtyureṣa upasthitaḥ .. 54.19 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रह्महत्या भविष्यन्ति बह्व्यस्ते वसुधाधिप .
सकुटुम्बस्य मे त्वं हि मृत्युरेष उपस्थितः .. 54.19 ..
6.3.m: Many murders of brahmins will fall upon you, O ruler of the earth! / For you have arrived as death itself to me and my family." 54.19

6.3.s:
evamuktvā tato vipro vicintya ca punaḥpunaḥ .
parityajya tadā krodhaṃ munibhāvājjagāda ha .. 54.20 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्त्वा ततो विप्रो विचिन्त्य च पुनःपुनः .
परित्यज्य तदा क्रोधं मुनिभावाज्जगाद ह .. 54.20 ..
6.3.m: Having spoken thus, the brahmin then reflected again and again; / relinquishing his anger then, out of his nature as a sage, he spoke: 54.20

6.3.s:
dīrghatapā uvāca -
udvegaṃ tyaja bho vatsa duruktaṃ gadito mayā .
putraśokābhibhūtena duḥkhataptena mānada .. 54.21 ..
6.3.d:
दीर्घतपा उवाच -
उद्वेगं त्यज भो वत्स दुरुक्तं गदितो मया .
पुत्रशोकाभिभूतेन दुःखतप्तेन मानद .. 54.21 ..
6.3.m: Dīrghatapas said: / "Cast away anxiety, dear boy! Harsh words were uttered by me, / overwhelmed by grief for my son and tormented by sorrow, O honour-giver. 54.21

6.3.s:
kiṃ karoti naraḥ prājñaḥ preryamāṇaḥ svakarmabhiḥ .
prāgeva hi manuṣyāṇāṃ buddhiḥ karmānusāriṇī .. 54.22 ..
6.3.d:
किं करोति नरः प्राज्ञः प्रेर्यमाणः स्वकर्मभिः .
प्रागेव हि मनुष्याणां बुद्धिः कर्मानुसारिणी .. 54.22 ..
6.3.m: What can a wise man do, driven by his own past deeds? / For a person's intellect follows their past actions from the very start. 54.22

6.3.s:
anenaiva vidhānena pañcatvaṃ vihitaṃ mama .
hatyāstava bhaviṣyanti pūrvamuktā na saṃśayaḥ .. 54.23 ..
6.3.d:
अनेनैव विधानेन पञ्चत्वं विहितं मम .
हत्यास्तव भविष्यन्ति पूर्वमुक्ता न संशयः .. 54.23 ..
6.3.m: By this very destiny, my own dissolution has been ordained. / The murders previously mentioned will indeed fall upon you, of this there is no doubt. 54.23

6.3.s:
brahmakṣatraviśāṃ madhye śūdracaṇḍālajātiṣu .
kastvaṃ kathaya satyaṃ me kasmācca nihato dvijaḥ .. 54.24 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रह्मक्षत्रविशां मध्ये शूद्रचण्डालजातिषु .
कस्त्वं कथय सत्यं मे कस्माच्च निहतो द्विजः .. 54.24 ..
6.3.m: Among brahmins, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas, or among the castes of śūdras and caṇḍālas, / who are you? Tell me the truth, and why was the twice-born killed?" 54.24

6.3.s:
citrasena uvāca -
vijñāpayāmi viprarṣe kṣantavyaṃ te mamopari .
nāhaṃ vipro'smi vai tāta na vaiśyo na ca śūdrajaḥ .. 54.25 ..
6.3.d:
चित्रसेन उवाच -
विज्ञापयामि विप्रर्षे क्षन्तव्यं ते ममोपरि .
नाहं विप्रोऽस्मि वै तात न वैश्यो न च शूद्रजः .. 54.25 ..
6.3.m: Citrasena said: / "I submit this to you, O brahmin seer: you should forgive me. / I am not a brahmin, dear sir, nor a vaiśya, nor born of a śūdra. 54.25

6.3.s:
na vyādhaścāntyajāto vā kṣatriyo'haṃ mahāmune .
kāśīrājo mṛgān hantumāgato vanamuttamam .. 54.26 ..
6.3.d:
न व्याधश्चान्त्यजातो वा क्षत्रियोऽहं महामुने .
काशीराजो मृगान् हन्तुमागतो वनमुत्तमम् .. 54.26 ..
6.3.m: Nor am I a hunter, nor lowest-born; I am a kṣatriya, O great sage, / the king of Kāśī, who came to this excellent forest to hunt deer. 54.26

6.3.s:
bhrāntyā nipātito hyeṣa mṛgarūpadharo muniḥ .
idānīṃ tava pādānte saṃśritaḥ pātakānvitaḥ .. 54.27 ..
6.3.d:
भ्रान्त्या निपातितो ह्येष मृगरूपधरो मुनिः .
इदानीं तव पादान्ते संश्रितः पातकान्वितः .. 54.27 ..
6.3.m: Through delusion this sage, bearing the form of a deer, was struck down. / Now, laden with sin, I have taken refuge at your feet. 54.27

6.3.s: kiṃ kartavyaṃ mayā vipra upāyaṃ kathayasva me .. 54.28 ..
6.3.d: किं कर्तव्यं मया विप्र उपायं कथयस्व मे .. 54.28 ..
6.3.m: What should be done by me, O brahmin? Tell me a means." 54.28

6.3.s:
dīrghatapā uvāca -
brahmahatyā na śakyetāpyekā nistarituṃ prabho .
daśaikā ca kathaṃ śakyāstāḥ śṛṇuṣva nareśvara .. 54.29 ..
6.3.d:
दीर्घतपा उवाच -
ब्रह्महत्या न शक्येताप्येका निस्तरितुं प्रभो .
दशैका च कथं शक्यास्ताः शृणुष्व नरेश्वर .. 54.29 ..
6.3.m: Dīrghatapas said: / "Even a single murder of a brahmin cannot be crossed over, O lord; / how can eleven be overcome? Listen to them, O ruler of men: 54.29

6.3.s:
catvāro me sutā rājan sabhāryā mātṛpūrvakāḥ .
mayā saha na jīvanti ṛkṣaśṛṅgasya kāraṇe .. 54.30 ..
6.3.d:
चत्वारो मे सुता राजन् सभार्या मातृपूर्वकाः .
मया सह न जीवन्ति ऋक्षशृङ्गस्य कारणे .. 54.30 ..
6.3.m: My four sons, O king, along with their wives and their mother, / will not live along with me, on account of Ṛkṣaśṛṅga. 54.30

6.3.s:
upāyaṃ śobhanaṃ tāta kathayiṣye śṛṇuṣva tam .
śakro'pi yadi taṃ kartuṃ sukhopāyaṃ nareśvara .. 54.31 ..
6.3.d:
उपायं शोभनं तात कथयिष्ये शृणुष्व तम् .
शक्रोऽपि यदि तं कर्तुं सुखोपायं नरेश्वर .. 54.31 ..
6.3.m: I shall tell you an excellent means, dear sir; listen to it, / if you are able to perform it, an easy means, O ruler of men. 54.31

6.3.s:
sakuṭumbaṃ samastaṃ māṃ dāhayitvānale nṛpa .
asthīni narmadātoye śūlabhede vinikṣipa .. 54.32 ..
6.3.d:
सकुटुम्बं समस्तं मां दाहयित्वानले नृप .
अस्थीनि नर्मदातोये शूलभेदे विनिक्षिप .. 54.32 ..
6.3.m: Having burned me together with my entire family in fire, O king, / cast our bones into the waters of the Narmadā at Śūlabheda. 54.32

6.3.s:
narmadādakṣiṇe kūle śūlabhedaṃ hi viśrutam .
sarvapāpaharaṃ tīrthaṃ sarvaduḥkhaghnamuttamam .. 54.33 ..
6.3.d:
नर्मदादक्षिणे कूले शूलभेदं हि विश्रुतम् .
सर्वपापहरं तीर्थं सर्वदुःखघ्नमुत्तमम् .. 54.33 ..
6.3.m: On the southern bank of the Narmadā, Śūlabheda is renowned / as an excellent sacred ford that removes all sins and destroys all sorrows. 54.33

6.3.s:
śucirbhūtvā mamāsthīni tatra tīrthe vinikṣipa .
mokṣyase sarvapāpaistvaṃ mama vākyānna saṃśayaḥ .. 54.34 ..
6.3.d:
शुचिर्भूत्वा ममास्थीनि तत्र तीर्थे विनिक्षिप .
मोक्ष्यसे सर्वपापैस्त्वं मम वाक्यान्न संशयः .. 54.34 ..
6.3.m: Having become pure, deposit my bones in that sacred ford. / You will be freed from all sins by my word, of this there is no doubt." 54.34

6.3.s:
rājovāca -
ādeśo dīyatāṃ tāta kariṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ .
samastaṃ me'sti yatkiṃcidrājyaṃ kośaḥ suhṛtsutāḥ .. 54.35 ..
6.3.d:
राजोवाच -
आदेशो दीयतां तात करिष्यामि न संशयः .
समस्तं मेऽस्ति यत्किंचिद्राज्यं कोशः सुहृत्सुताः .. 54.35 ..
6.3.m: The king said: / "Let the command be given, dear sir; I will do it, without a doubt. / Whatever I possess—kingdom, treasury, friends, and sons— 54.35

6.3.s:
tavādhīnaṃ mahāvipra prayacchāmi prasīda me .
parasparaṃ vivadatorvipra rājñostadā nṛpa .. 54.36 ..
6.3.d:
तवाधीनं महाविप्र प्रयच्छामि प्रसीद मे .
परस्परं विवदतोर्विप्र राज्ञोस्तदा नृप .. 54.36 ..
6.3.m: is at your command, O great brahmin; I offer it, be gracious to me." / While the brahmin and the king were thus speaking to one another, O king, 54.36

6.3.s:
sphuṭitvā hṛdayaṃ śīghraṃ munibhāryā mṛtā tadā .
putraśokasamāviṣṭā nirjīvā patitā kṣitau .. 54.37 ..
6.3.d:
स्फुटित्वा हृदयं शीघ्रं मुनिभार्या मृता तदा .
पुत्रशोकसमाविष्टा निर्जीवा पतिता क्षितौ .. 54.37 ..
6.3.m: her heart suddenly bursting, the sage's wife then died; / overwhelmed by grief for her son, she fell lifeless to the ground. 54.37

6.3.s:
putrāśca mātṛśokena sarve pañcatvamāgatāḥ .
snuṣāścaiva tadā sarvā mṛtāśca saha bhartṛbhiḥ .. 54.38 ..
6.3.d:
पुत्राश्च मातृशोकेन सर्वे पञ्चत्वमागताः .
स्नुषाश्चैव तदा सर्वा मृताश्च सह भर्तृभिः .. 54.38 ..
6.3.m: And all the sons met dissolution through grief for their mother, / and all the daughters-in-law died along with their husbands. 54.38

6.3.s:
pañcatvaṃ ca gatāḥ sarve munimukhyā nṛpottama .
viprānāhvāpayāmāsa ye tatrāśramavāsinaḥ .. 54.39 ..
6.3.d:
पञ्चत्वं च गताः सर्वे मुनिमुख्या नृपोत्तम .
विप्रानाह्वापयामास ये तत्राश्रमवासिनः .. 54.39 ..
6.3.m: And when they all met dissolution, O best of kings, the foremost of sages / summoned the brahmins who dwelt in that hermitage. 54.39

6.3.s:
tebhyo nivedayāmāsa yathāvṛttaṃ nṛpottamaḥ .
sa taistadābhyanujñātaḥ kāṣṭhānyādāya yatnataḥ .. 54.40 ..
6.3.d:
तेभ्यो निवेदयामास यथावृत्तं नृपोत्तमः .
स तैस्तदाभ्यनुज्ञातः काष्ठान्यादाय यत्नतः .. 54.40 ..
6.3.m: The best of kings reported to them what had happened. / Permitted then by them, collecting firewood with care, 54.40

6.3.s:
dāhaṃ saṃcayanaṃ cakre citraseno mahīpatiḥ .
ṛkṣaśṛṅgādisarveṣāṃ gṛhītvāsthīni yatnataḥ .. 54.41 ..
6.3.d:
दाहं संचयनं चक्रे चित्रसेनो महीपतिः .
ऋक्षशृङ्गादिसर्वेषां गृहीत्वास्थीनि यत्नतः .. 54.41 ..
6.3.m: King Citrasena performed the cremation and the gathering [of ashes], / carefully collecting the bones of all of them, beginning with Ṛkṣaśṛṅga. 54.41

6.3.s:
yāmyāśāṃ prasthito rājā pādacārī mahīpate .
na śaknoti yadā gantuṃ chāyāmāśritya tiṣṭhati .. 54.42 ..
6.3.d:
याम्याशां प्रस्थितो राजा पादचारी महीपते .
न शक्नोति यदा गन्तुं छायामाश्रित्य तिष्ठति .. 54.42 ..
6.3.m: The king set forth toward the southern quarter on foot, O ruler of the earth. / When he was unable to walk, he would stop, seeking shade. 54.42

6.3.s:
viśramya ca punargacchedbhārākrānto mahīpatiḥ .
sacailaṃ kurute snānaṃ muktvāsthīni pade pade .. 54.43 ..
6.3.d:
विश्रम्य च पुनर्गच्छेद्भाराक्रान्तो महीपतिः .
सचैलं कुरुते स्नानं मुक्त्वास्थीनि पदे पदे .. 54.43 ..
6.3.m: Resting, the king would proceed again, weighed down by the burden. / Having set down the bones at every step, he performed a bath with his clothes on. 54.43

6.3.s:
pibejjalaṃ nirāhāraḥ sa gacchan dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ .
acireṇaiva kālena saṃgato narmadātaṭam .. 54.44 ..
6.3.d:
पिबेज्जलं निराहारः स गच्छन् दक्षिणामुखः .
अचिरेणैव कालेन संगतो नर्मदातटम् .. 54.44 ..
6.3.m: Fasting, he would only drink water, journeying facing the south. / In a short time he arrived at the bank of the Narmadā. 54.44

6.3.s: āśramasthān dvijān dṛṣṭvā papraccha pṛthivīpatiḥ .. 54.45 ..
6.3.d: आश्रमस्थान् द्विजान् दृष्ट्वा पप्रच्छ पृथिवीपतिः .. 54.45 ..
6.3.m: Seeing the twice-born dwelling in the hermitage, the lord of the earth asked: 54.45

6.3.s:
citrasena uvāca -
kathyatāṃ śūlabhedasya mārgaṃ me dvijasattamāḥ .
yena yāmi mahābhāgāḥ svakāryārthasya siddhaye .. 54.46 ..
6.3.d:
चित्रसेन उवाच -
कथ्यतां शूलभेदस्य मार्गं मे द्विजसत्तमाः .
येन यामि महाभागाः स्वकार्यार्थस्य सिद्धये .. 54.46 ..
6.3.m: Citrasena said: / "Tell me the way to Śūlabheda, O best of the twice-born, / so that I may go, O fortunate ones, to accomplish my purpose." 54.46

6.3.s:
munaya ūcuḥ .
itaḥ krośāntarādarvāktīrthaṃ paramaśobhanam .
narmadādakṣiṇe kūle tato drakṣyasi nānyathā .. 54.47 ..
6.3.d:
मुनय ऊचुः .
इतः क्रोशान्तरादर्वाक्तीर्थं परमशोभनम् .
नर्मदादक्षिणे कूले ततो द्रक्ष्यसि नान्यथा .. 54.47 ..
6.3.m: The sages said: / "Within a distance of one krośa from here is an exceedingly beautiful sacred ford / on the southern bank of the Narmadā; there you will see it, not elsewhere." 54.47

6.3.s:
ṛṣivākyena rājāsau śīghraṃ gatvā nareśvaraḥ .
sa dadarśa tataḥ śīghraṃ bahudvijasamākulam .. 54.48 ..
6.3.d:
ऋषिवाक्येन राजासौ शीघ्रं गत्वा नरेश्वरः .
स ददर्श ततः शीघ्रं बहुद्विजसमाकुलम् .. 54.48 ..
6.3.m: Following the word of the seers, that king, the ruler of men, went swiftly; / then he quickly beheld [the sacred ford], filled with many twice-born, 54.48

6.3.s:
bahudrumalatākīrṇaṃ bahupuṣpopaśobhitam .
ṛkṣasiṃhasamākīrṇaṃ nānāvratadharaiḥ śubhaiḥ .. 54.49 ..
6.3.d:
बहुद्रुमलताकीर्णं बहुपुष्पोपशोभितम् .
ऋक्षसिंहसमाकीर्णं नानाव्रतधरैः शुभैः .. 54.49 ..
6.3.m: thronged with many trees and creepers, adorned with many flowers, / frequented by bears and lions, and by auspicious [ascetics] observing diverse vows: 54.49

6.3.s:
ekapādāsthitāḥ kecidapare sūryadṛṣṭayaḥ .
ekāṅguṣṭha sthitāḥ kecidūrdhvabāhusthitāḥ pare .. 54.50 ..
6.3.d:
एकपादास्थिताः केचिदपरे सूर्यदृष्टयः .
एकाङ्गुष्ठ स्थिताः केचिदूर्ध्वबाहुस्थिताः परे .. 54.50 ..
6.3.m: some standing on one foot, others with their gaze fixed on the sun, / some standing on a single big toe, others with their arms raised; 54.50

6.3.s:
dinaikabhojanāḥ kecitkecitkandaphalāśanāḥ .
trirātrabhojanāḥ kecitparākavratino'pare .. 54.51 ..
6.3.d:
दिनैकभोजनाः केचित्केचित्कन्दफलाशनाः .
त्रिरात्रभोजनाः केचित्पराकव्रतिनोऽपरे .. 54.51 ..
6.3.m: some eating once a day, some eating roots and fruits, / some eating every three nights, others observing the Parāka vow; 54.51

6.3.s:
cāndrāyaṇaratāḥ kecitkecitpakṣopavāsinaḥ .
māsopavāsinaḥ kecitkecidṛtvantapāraṇāḥ .. 54.52 ..
6.3.d:
चान्द्रायणरताः केचित्केचित्पक्षोपवासिनः .
मासोपवासिनः केचित्केचिदृत्वन्तपारणाः .. 54.52 ..
6.3.m: some devoted to the Cāndrāyaṇa vow, some fasting for a fortnight, / some fasting for a month, some breaking fast only at the end of a season; 54.52

6.3.s:
yogābhyāsaratāḥ kecitkeciddhyāyanti tatpadam .
śīrṇaparṇāśinaḥ kecitkecicca kaṭukāśanāḥ .. 54.53 ..
6.3.d:
योगाभ्यासरताः केचित्केचिद्ध्यायन्ति तत्पदम् .
शीर्णपर्णाशिनः केचित्केचिच्च कटुकाशनाः .. 54.53 ..
6.3.m: some devoted to the practice of yoga, some meditating on that supreme state, / some eating withered leaves, and others eating bitter food. 54.53

6.3.s:
śaivālabhojanāḥ kecitkecinmārutabhojanāḥ .
gārhasthye ca sthitāḥ kecitkeciccaivāgnihotriṇaḥ .. 54.54 ..
6.3.d:
शैवालभोजनाः केचित्केचिन्मारुतभोजनाः .
गार्हस्थ्ये च स्थिताः केचित्केचिच्चैवाग्निहोत्रिणः .. 54.54 ..
6.3.m: Some fed on moss, some fed on wind; / some remained in the householder's life, and some were performers of the agnihotra.

6.3.s:
evaṃvidhān dvijān dṛṣṭvā jānubhyāmavaniṃ gataḥ .
praṇamya śirasā rājanrājā vacanamabravīt .. 54.55 ..
6.3.d:
एवंविधान् द्विजान् दृष्ट्वा जानुभ्यामवनिं गतः .
प्रणम्य शिरसा राजन्राजा वचनमब्रवीत् .. 54.55 ..
6.3.m: Having seen such twice-born [ascetics], the king fell to the ground on his knees, / and having bowed his head, O king, he spoke these words:

6.3.s:
citrasena uvāca -
kasmindeśe ca tattīrthaṃ satyaṃ kathayata dvijāḥ .
yenābhivāñchitā siddhiḥ saphalā me bhaviṣyati .. 54.56 ..
6.3.d:
चित्रसेन उवाच -
कस्मिन्देशे च तत्तीर्थं सत्यं कथयत द्विजाः .
येनाभिवाञ्छिता सिद्धिः सफला मे भविष्यति .. 54.56 ..
6.3.m: Citrasena said: / 'In which region is that sacred ford? Tell me truly, O twice-born ones, / by which my desired accomplishment will bear fruit.'

6.3.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .
dhanvantaraśataṃ gaccha bhṛgutuṅgasya mūrdhani .
kuṇḍaṃ drakṣyasi tatpūrṇaṃ vistīrṇaṃ payasā śivam .. 54.57 ..
6.3.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः .
धन्वन्तरशतं गच्छ भृगुतुङ्गस्य मूर्धनि .
कुण्डं द्रक्ष्यसि तत्पूर्णं विस्तीर्णं पयसा शिवम् .. 54.57 ..
6.3.m: The seers said: / 'Go a hundred bow-lengths to the summit of Bhṛgutuṅga; / there you will see an auspicious, extensive pool filled with water.'

6.3.s:
teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā gataḥ kuṇḍasya sannidhau .
dṛṣṭvā caiva tu tattīrthaṃ bhrāntirjātā nṛpasya vai .. 54.58 ..
6.3.d:
तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा गतः कुण्डस्य सन्निधौ .
दृष्ट्वा चैव तु तत्तीर्थं भ्रान्तिर्जाता नृपस्य वै .. 54.58 ..
6.3.m: Having heard their words, he went near the pool; / but seeing that sacred ford, doubt arose in the king.

6.3.s:
tato vismayamāpannaścintayanvai muhurmuhuḥ .
ākāśasthaṃ dadarśāsau sāmiṣaṃ kuraraṃ nṛpaḥ .. 54.59 ..
6.3.d:
ततो विस्मयमापन्नश्चिन्तयन्वै मुहुर्मुहुः .
आकाशस्थं ददर्शासौ सामिषं कुररं नृपः .. 54.59 ..
6.3.m: Then, seized with wonder and pondering again and again, / the king saw an osprey in the sky holding a piece of meat,

6.3.s:
bhramamāṇaṃ gṛhītāhiṃ vadhyamānaṃ nirāmiṣaiḥ .
parasparaṃ ca yuyudhuḥ sarve'pyāmiṣakāṅkṣayā .. 54.60 ..
6.3.d:
भ्रममाणं गृहीताहिं वध्यमानं निरामिषैः .
परस्परं च युयुधुः सर्वेऽप्यामिषकाङ्क्षया .. 54.60 ..
6.3.m: wheeling about with a snake it had seized, being struck by [other birds] without meat; / and they all fought with one another, craving the meat.

6.3.s:
hataścañcuprahāreṇa sa tataḥ patito'ṃbhasi .
śūlena śūlinā yatra bhūbhāgo bheditaḥ purā .. 54.61 ..
6.3.d:
हतश्चञ्चुप्रहारेण स ततः पतितोऽंभसि .
शूलेन शूलिना यत्र भूभागो भेदितः पुरा .. 54.61 ..
6.3.m: Struck by a blow from a beak, it then fell into the water, / where long ago the portion of earth had been split by the Trident-bearer with his trident.

6.3.s:
tattīrthasya prabhāveṇa sa sadyaḥ puruṣo'bhavat .
vimānasthaṃ dadarśāsau pumāṃsaṃ divyarūpiṇam .. 54.62 ..
6.3.d:
तत्तीर्थस्य प्रभावेण स सद्यः पुरुषोऽभवत् .
विमानस्थं ददर्शासौ पुमांसं दिव्यरूपिणम् .. 54.62 ..
6.3.m: By the power of that sacred ford, it instantly became a human; / he saw a man of divine form standing in an aerial chariot.

6.3.s:
gandharvāpsaraso yakṣāstaṃ yāntaṃ tuṣṭuvurdivi .
apsarogīyamāne tu gate sūryasya mūrdhani .
citrasenastatastasminnāścaryaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ .. 54.63 ..
6.3.d:
गन्धर्वाप्सरसो यक्षास्तं यान्तं तुष्टुवुर्दिवि .
अप्सरोगीयमाने तु गते सूर्यस्य मूर्धनि .
चित्रसेनस्ततस्तस्मिन्नाश्चर्यं परमं गतः .. 54.63 ..
6.3.m: Gandharvas, apsarases, and yakṣas praised him as he went in the sky. / When he had reached the summit of the sun while being sung to by apsarases, / Citrasena was filled with supreme wonder at that.

6.3.s:
ṛṣiṇā kathitaṃ yadvattadvattīrthaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .
hṛṣṭaromābhavaddṛṣṭvā prabhāvaṃ tīrthasambhavam .. 54.64 ..
6.3.d:
ऋषिणा कथितं यद्वत्तद्वत्तीर्थं न संशयः .
हृष्टरोमाभवद्दृष्ट्वा प्रभावं तीर्थसम्भवम् .. 54.64 ..
6.3.m: 'Just as the seer spoke, so indeed is the sacred ford; there is no doubt.' / His hair stood on end upon seeing the power arising from the sacred ford.

6.3.s:
mamādya divaso dhanyo yasmādatra samāgataḥ .
asthīni bhūmau nikṣipya snānaṃ kṛtvā yathāvidhi .. 54.65 ..
6.3.d:
ममाद्य दिवसो धन्यो यस्मादत्र समागतः .
अस्थीनि भूमौ निक्षिप्य स्नानं कृत्वा यथाविधि .. 54.65 ..
6.3.m: 'Blessed is this day of mine, since I have arrived here.' / Laying down the bones on the ground and having performed his ritual ablution according to the rule,

6.3.s:
tilamiśreṇa toyenātarpayatpitṛdevatāḥ .
gṛhyāsthīni tato rājā cikṣepāntarjale tadā .. 54.66 ..
6.3.d:
तिलमिश्रेण तोयेनातर्पयत्पितृदेवताः .
गृह्यास्थीनि ततो राजा चिक्षेपान्तर्जले तदा .. 54.66 ..
6.3.m: he gratified the ancestors and the gods with water mixed with sesame seeds. / Then taking the bones, the king cast them into the midst of the water.

6.3.s:
kṣaṇamekaṃ tato vīkṣya rājorddhvavadanaḥ sthitaḥ .
tān dadarśa punaḥ sarvān divyarūpadharāñchubhān .. 54.67 ..
6.3.d:
क्षणमेकं ततो वीक्ष्य राजोर्द्ध्ववदनः स्थितः .
तान् ददर्श पुनः सर्वान् दिव्यरूपधराञ्छुभान् .. 54.67 ..
6.3.m: Then, having looked for a moment, the king stood with his face turned upward; / he saw them all again, auspicious and wearing divine forms,

6.3.s:
divyavastraiśca saṃvītān divyābharaṇabhūṣitān .
vimānairvividhairdivyairapsarogaṇasevitaiḥ .. 54.68 ..
6.3.d:
दिव्यवस्त्रैश्च संवीतान् दिव्याभरणभूषितान् .
विमानैर्विविधैर्दिव्यैरप्सरोगणसेवितैः .. 54.68 ..
6.3.m: clothed in divine garments and adorned with divine ornaments, / in various celestial aerial chariots attended by hosts of apsarases.

6.3.s:
pṛthagbhūtāṃśca tān sarvān vimāneṣu vyavasthitān .
utpattivatsamālokya rājā saṃharṣī so'bhavat .. 54.69 ..
6.3.d:
पृथग्भूतांश्च तान् सर्वान् विमानेषु व्यवस्थितान् .
उत्पत्तिवत्समालोक्य राजा संहर्षी सोऽभवत् .. 54.69 ..
6.3.m: Seeing them all separated and stationed in aerial chariots / as though freshly born, the king was filled with joy.

6.3.s:
ṛṣirvimānamārūḍhaścitrasenamathābravīt .
bhobhoḥ sādho mahārāja citrasena mahīpate .. 54.70 ..
6.3.d:
ऋषिर्विमानमारूढश्चित्रसेनमथाब्रवीत् .
भोभोः साधो महाराज चित्रसेन महीपते .. 54.70 ..
6.3.m: The sage, having mounted an aerial chariot, then said to Citrasena: / 'O noble one! O great king, Citrasena, lord of the earth!

6.3.s:
tvatprasādānnṛpaśreṣṭha gatirdivyā mamedṛṣī .
jāteyaṃ yattvayā kāryaṃ kṛtaṃ paramaśobhanam .. 54.71 ..
6.3.d:
त्वत्प्रसादान्नृपश्रेष्ठ गतिर्दिव्या ममेदृषी .
जातेयं यत्त्वया कार्यं कृतं परमशोभनम् .. 54.71 ..
6.3.m: By your grace, O best of kings, such a divine state / has been attained by me, because you have performed a most splendid deed.

6.3.s:
svasuto'pi na śaknoti pitḥṇāṃ kartumīdṛśam .
madīyavacanāttāta niṣpāpastvaṃ bhaviṣyasi .. 54.72 ..
6.3.d:
स्वसुतोऽपि न शक्नोति पित्ःणां कर्तुमीदृशम् .
मदीयवचनात्तात निष्पापस्त्वं भविष्यसि .. 54.72 ..
6.3.m: Even one's own son cannot do such a thing for his ancestors. / By my word, dear child, you shall be free of sin.

6.3.s:
phalaṃ prāpsyasi rājendra kāmikaṃ manasepsitam .
āśīrvādāṃstato dattvā citrasenāya dhīmate .
svargaṃ jagāma sasutastato dīrghatapā muniḥ .. 54.73 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcamāvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe dīrghatapasaḥ svargārohaṇavarṇanaṃ nāma catuḥpañcāśattamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 55
6.3.d:
फलं प्राप्स्यसि राजेन्द्र कामिकं मनसेप्सितम् .
आशीर्वादांस्ततो दत्त्वा चित्रसेनाय धीमते .
स्वर्गं जगाम ससुतस्ततो दीर्घतपा मुनिः .. 54.73 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चमावन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे दीर्घतपसः स्वर्गारोहणवर्णनं नाम चतुःपञ्चाशत्तमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 55
6.3.m:
You will obtain a desirable fruit, wished for in your heart, O king of kings.' / Then, having given blessings to the wise Citrasena, / the sage Dīrghatapas went to heaven together with his sons.
Thus ends the fifty-fourth chapter, called 'The Description of the Ascent to Heaven of Dīrghatapas,' in the Revākhaṇḍa of the Avantyakhaṇḍa, the fifth [book], in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 55

6.3.s:
uttānapāda uvāca -
māhātmyaṃ tīrthajaṃ dṛṣṭvā citraseno nareśvaraḥ .
kiṃ cakāra kva vā vāsaṃ kimāhāro babhūva ha .. 55.1 ..
6.3.d:
उत्तानपाद उवाच -
माहात्म्यं तीर्थजं दृष्ट्वा चित्रसेनो नरेश्वरः .
किं चकार क्व वा वासं किमाहारो बभूव ह .. 55.1 ..
6.3.m: Uttānapāda said: / 'Having seen the māhātmya born of the sacred ford, what did the lord of men Citrasena / do? Where did he dwell, and what did he take as food?'

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
bhṛgutuṅgaṃ samāruhya aiśānīṃ diśamāśritaḥ .
tapaścacāra vipulaṃ kuṇḍe tatra nṛpottamaḥ .. 55.2 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
भृगुतुङ्गं समारुह्य ऐशानीं दिशमाश्रितः .
तपश्चचार विपुलं कुण्डे तत्र नृपोत्तमः .. 55.2 ..
6.3.m: Īśvara said: / 'Having climbed Bhṛgutuṅga and resorted to the north-eastern direction, / that best of kings performed immense austerity at that pool.

6.3.s:
sarvān devān hṛdi dhyātvā brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarān .
vicikṣepa yadātmānaṃ pratyakṣau rudrakeśavau .
kare gṛhītvā rājānaṃ rudro vacanamabravīt .. 55.3 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वान् देवान् हृदि ध्यात्वा ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वरान् .
विचिक्षेप यदात्मानं प्रत्यक्षौ रुद्रकेशवौ .
करे गृहीत्वा राजानं रुद्रो वचनमब्रवीत् .. 55.3 ..
6.3.m: Having meditated in his heart on all the gods—Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara— / when he threw himself [into the pool], Rudra and Keśava appeared in visible form. / Taking the king by the hand, Rudra spoke these words:

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
prāṇatyāgaṃ mahārāja mā kāle tvaṃ kṛthā vṛthā .
adyāpyasi yuvā tvaṃ vai na yuktaṃ maraṇaṃ tava .. 55.4 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
प्राणत्यागं महाराज मा काले त्वं कृथा वृथा .
अद्याप्यसि युवा त्वं वै न युक्तं मरणं तव .. 55.4 ..
6.3.m: Īśvara said: / 'Do not cast away your life in vain, O great king, when it is not your time. / Even now you are indeed young; death is not fitting for you.

6.3.s:
svasthānaṃ gaccha śīghraṃ tvaṃ bhuktvā bhogānyathepsitān .
kuru niṣkaṇṭakaṃ rājyaṃ nāke śakra ivāparaḥ .. 55.5 ..
6.3.d:
स्वस्थानं गच्छ शीघ्रं त्वं भुक्त्वा भोगान्यथेप्सितान् .
कुरु निष्कण्टकं राज्यं नाके शक्र इवापरः .. 55.5 ..
6.3.m: Go quickly to your own place, and having enjoyed the pleasures you desire, / rule a realm free of thorns, like a second Śakra in heaven.'

6.3.s:
citrasena uvāca -
na rājyaṃ kāmaye deva na putrānna ca bāndhavān .
na bhāryāṃ na ca kośaṃ ca na gajānna turaṃgamān .. 55.6 ..
6.3.d:
चित्रसेन उवाच -
न राज्यं कामये देव न पुत्रान्न च बान्धवान् .
न भार्यां न च कोशं च न गजान्न तुरंगमान् .. 55.6 ..
6.3.m: Citrasena said: / 'I do not desire kingship, O God, nor sons, nor relatives; / not a wife, nor a treasury, nor elephants, nor horses.

6.3.s:
muñca muñca mahādeva mā vighnaḥ kriyatāṃ mama .
svargaprāptirmamādyaiva tvatprasādānmaheśvara .. 55.7 ..
6.3.d:
मुञ्च मुञ्च महादेव मा विघ्नः क्रियतां मम .
स्वर्गप्राप्तिर्ममाद्यैव त्वत्प्रसादान्महेश्वर .. 55.7 ..
6.3.m: Release me, release me, O Mahādeva! Let no obstacle be made for me; / let me attain heaven this very day by your grace, O Maheśvara.'

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
yasyāgrato bhavedbrahmā viṣṇuḥ śambhustathaiva ca .
svargeṇa tasya kiṃ kāryaṃ sa gataḥ kiṃ kariṣyati .. 55.8 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
यस्याग्रतो भवेद्ब्रह्मा विष्णुः शम्भुस्तथैव च .
स्वर्गेण तस्य किं कार्यं स गतः किं करिष्यति .. 55.8 ..
6.3.m: Īśvara said: / 'For one before whom Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śambhu stand, / what need has he of heaven? What will he do once gone there?

6.3.s:
tuṣṭā vayaṃ trayo devā vṛṇīṣva varamuttamam .
yathepsitaṃ mahārāja satyametadasaṃśayam .. 55.9 ..
6.3.d:
तुष्टा वयं त्रयो देवा वृणीष्व वरमुत्तमम् .
यथेप्सितं महाराज सत्यमेतदसंशयम् .. 55.9 ..
6.3.m: We three gods are pleased. Choose an excellent boon / as you desire, O great king. This is true, without doubt.'

6.3.s:
citrasena uvāca -
yadi tuṣṭāstrayo devā brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ .
adyaprabhṛti yuṣmābhiḥ sthātavyamiha sarvadā .. 55.10 ..
6.3.d:
चित्रसेन उवाच -
यदि तुष्टास्त्रयो देवा ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वराः .
अद्यप्रभृति युष्माभिः स्थातव्यमिह सर्वदा .. 55.10 ..
6.3.m: Citrasena said: / 'If the three gods—Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara—are pleased, / from this day onward you must always remain here.

6.3.s:
gayāśiro yathā puṇyaṃ kṛtaṃ yuṣmābhireva ca .
tathaivedaṃ prakartavyaṃ śūlabhedaṃ ca pāvanam .. 55.11 ..
6.3.d:
गयाशिरो यथा पुण्यं कृतं युष्माभिरेव च .
तथैवेदं प्रकर्तव्यं शूलभेदं च पावनम् .. 55.11 ..
6.3.m: Just as Gayāśiras was made holy by you alone, / so too should this Śūlabheda be made purifying.

6.3.s:
yatrayatra sthitā yūyaṃ tatratatra vasāmyaham .
gaṇānāṃ caiva sarveṣāmādhipatyamathāstu me .. 55.12 ..
6.3.d:
यत्रयत्र स्थिता यूयं तत्रतत्र वसाम्यहम् .
गणानां चैव सर्वेषामाधिपत्यमथास्तु मे .. 55.12 ..
6.3.m: Wherever you remain, there I shall dwell; / and may I have lordship over all the gaṇas.'

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
adyaprabhṛti tiṣṭhāmaḥ śūlabhede nareśvara .
trikālāṃ hi trayo devāḥ kalāṃśena vasāmahe .. 55.13 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
अद्यप्रभृति तिष्ठामः शूलभेदे नरेश्वर .
त्रिकालां हि त्रयो देवाः कलांशेन वसामहे .. 55.13 ..
6.3.m: Īśvara said: / 'From this day onward we will remain at Śūlabheda, O lord of men; / through all three times indeed, we three gods dwell here by a fraction of our potency.

6.3.s:
nandisaṃjño gaṇādhīśo bhaviṣyati bhavāndhruvam .
matsamīpe tu bhavata ādau pūjā bhaviṣyati .. 55.14 ..
6.3.d:
नन्दिसंज्ञो गणाधीशो भविष्यति भवान्ध्रुवम् .
मत्समीपे तु भवत आदौ पूजा भविष्यति .. 55.14 ..
6.3.m: You shall certainly become the leader of the gaṇas named Nandi; / and in my presence, worship will first be offered to you.

6.3.s:
prakṣipya tāni cāsthīni yatra dīrghatapā yayau .
sakuṭumbo vimānasthaḥ svargatastvaṃ tathā kuru .. 55.15 ..
6.3.d:
प्रक्षिप्य तानि चास्थीनि यत्र दीर्घतपा ययौ .
सकुटुम्बो विमानस्थः स्वर्गतस्त्वं तथा कुरु .. 55.15 ..
6.3.m: Cast those bones [into the water] where Dīrghatapas went / to heaven seated in an aerial chariot with his family; do you likewise.'

6.3.s:
evaṃ devā varaṃ dattvā citrasenāya pārthiva .
kuṇḍamūrdhani yāmyāyāṃ trayo devāstadā sthitāḥ .. 55.16 ..
6.3.d:
एवं देवा वरं दत्त्वा चित्रसेनाय पार्थिव .
कुण्डमूर्धनि याम्यायां त्रयो देवास्तदा स्थिताः .. 55.16 ..
6.3.m: Having thus granted the boon to Citrasena, O king, / the three gods then stationed themselves on the southern side at the head of the pool.

6.3.s:
parasparaṃ vadantyevaṃ puṇyatīrthamidaṃ param .
yathā hi gayāśiraḥ puṇyaṃ pūrvameva paṭhyate .
tathā revātaṭe puṇyaṃ śūlabhedaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .. 55.17 ..
6.3.d:
परस्परं वदन्त्येवं पुण्यतीर्थमिदं परम् .
यथा हि गयाशिरः पुण्यं पूर्वमेव पठ्यते .
तथा रेवातटे पुण्यं शूलभेदं न संशयः .. 55.17 ..
6.3.m: They said this to one another: "This supreme sacred ford is meritorious. / Just as Gayāśiras is celebrated as meritorious of old, / so is Śūlabheda on the bank of the Revā meritorious, without doubt."

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
idaṃ tīrthaṃ tathā puṇyaṃ yathā puṇyaṃ gayāśiraḥ .
sakṛtpiṇḍodakenaiva naro nirmalatāṃ vrajet .. 55.18 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
इदं तीर्थं तथा पुण्यं यथा पुण्यं गयाशिरः .
सकृत्पिण्डोदकेनैव नरो निर्मलतां व्रजेत् .. 55.18 ..
6.3.m: Īśvara said: / 'This sacred ford is as meritorious as Gayāśiras is meritorious; / by a single offering of rice balls and water, a person reaches purity.'

6.3.s:
ekaṃ gayāśiro muktvā sarvatīrthāni bhūpate .
śūlabhedasya tīrthasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm .. 55.19 ..
6.3.d:
एकं गयाशिरो मुक्त्वा सर्वतीर्थानि भूपते .
शूलभेदस्य तीर्थस्य कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीम् .. 55.19 ..
6.3.m: Except for Gayāśiras alone, O king, / all sacred fords are not worth a sixteenth part of the sacred ford of Śūlabheda.

6.3.s:
kuṇḍamudīcyāṃ yāmyāyāṃ daśahastapramāṇataḥ .
raudravāruṇakāṣṭhāyāṃ pramāṇaṃ caikaviṃśati .. 55.20 ..
6.3.d:
कुण्डमुदीच्यां याम्यायां दशहस्तप्रमाणतः .
रौद्रवारुणकाष्ठायां प्रमाणं चैकविंशति .. 55.20 ..
6.3.m: The pool measures ten cubits in the north and south, / and the measurement in the north-east and western directions is twenty-one.

6.3.s:
etatpramāṇaṃ tattīrthaṃ piṇḍadānādikarmasu .
nādharmaniratā dātuṃ labhante dānamatra hi .. 55.21 ..
6.3.d:
एतत्प्रमाणं तत्तीर्थं पिण्डदानादिकर्मसु .
नाधर्मनिरता दातुं लभन्ते दानमत्र हि .. 55.21 ..
6.3.m: Such is the measure of that sacred ford for rites such as offering rice-balls; / those intent on unrighteousness indeed do not obtain [the right] to give gifts here.

6.3.s:
viṣṇustu pitṛrūpeṇa brahmarūpī pitāmahaḥ .
prapitāmaho rudro'bhūdevaṃ tripuruṣāḥ sthitāḥ .. 55.22 ..
6.3.d:
विष्णुस्तु पितृरूपेण ब्रह्मरूपी पितामहः .
प्रपितामहो रुद्रोऽभूदेवं त्रिपुरुषाः स्थिताः .. 55.22 ..
6.3.m: Viṣṇu stands in the form of the father, the grandfather has the form of Brahmā, / and the great-grandfather has become Rudra; thus the three generations of ancestors abide.

6.3.s:
kadā paśyati tīrthaṃ vai kadā nastārayiṣyati .
iti pratīkṣāṃ kurvanti putrāṇāṃ satataṃ nṛpa .
śūlabhede naraḥ snātvā dṛṣṭvā śūladharaṃ sakṛt .. 55.23 ..
6.3.d:
कदा पश्यति तीर्थं वै कदा नस्तारयिष्यति .
इति प्रतीक्षां कुर्वन्ति पुत्राणां सततं नृप .
शूलभेदे नरः स्नात्वा दृष्ट्वा शूलधरं सकृत् .. 55.23 ..
6.3.m: "When will he see the sacred ford? When will he deliver us?" / Thus they constantly wait for sons, O king. / If a man bathes at Śūlabheda and beholds the Bearer of the Trident once,

6.3.s:
nāputro nādhano rogī saptajanmasu jāyate .
ekaviṃśatiṃ pituḥ pakṣe mātuśvaivekaviṃśatim .. 55.24 ..
6.3.d:
नापुत्रो नाधनो रोगी सप्तजन्मसु जायते .
एकविंशतिं पितुः पक्षे मातुश्वैवेकविंशतिम् .. 55.24 ..
6.3.m: he is not born sonless, poor, or diseased for seven lifetimes. / Twenty-one [ancestors] on his father's side, and twenty-one on his mother's side,

6.3.s:
bhāryāpakṣe daśaiveha kulānyetāni tārayet .
śūlabhedavane rājañchākamūlaphalairapi .. 55.25 ..
6.3.d:
भार्यापक्षे दशैवेह कुलान्येतानि तारयेत् .
शूलभेदवने राजञ्छाकमूलफलैरपि .. 55.25 ..
6.3.m: and ten families on his wife's side he delivers here. / In the forest of Śūlabheda, O king, even with vegetables, roots, and fruits,

6.3.s:
ekasminbhojite vipre koṭīrbhavati bhojitā .
pañcasthāneṣu yaḥ śrāddhaṃ kurute bhaktimānnaraḥ .. 55.26 ..
6.3.d:
एकस्मिन्भोजिते विप्रे कोटीर्भवति भोजिता .
पञ्चस्थानेषु यः श्राद्धं कुरुते भक्तिमान्नरः .. 55.26 ..
6.3.m: when one wise brahmin is fed, ten million are fed. / A devoted man who performs a funeral rite in the five places,

6.3.s:
kulāni pretabhūtāni sarvāṇyapi hi tārayet .
dvijadevaprasādena pitṝṇāṃ ca prasādataḥ .. 55.27 ..
6.3.d:
कुलानि प्रेतभूतानि सर्वाण्यपि हि तारयेत् .
द्विजदेवप्रसादेन पितॄणां च प्रसादतः .. 55.27 ..
6.3.m: delivers all families, even those that have become ghosts, / through the grace of the brahmins and the gods, and through the grace of the ancestors.

6.3.s:
śrāddhado nivasettatra yatra devo maheśvaraḥ .
syurātmaghātino ye ca gobrāhmaṇahanāśca ye .. 55.28 ..
6.3.d:
श्राद्धदो निवसेत्तत्र यत्र देवो महेश्वरः .
स्युरात्मघातिनो ये च गोब्राह्मणहनाश्च ये .. 55.28 ..
6.3.m: The giver of the funeral rite dwells there where the god Maheśvara is. / And those who have committed suicide, and those who have slain cows or brahmins,

6.3.s:
daṃṣṭribhirjalapāte ca vidyutpāteṣu ye mṛtāḥ .
na yeṣāmagnisaṃskāro nāśaucaṃ nodakakriyā .. 55.29 ..
6.3.d:
दंष्ट्रिभिर्जलपाते च विद्युत्पातेषु ये मृताः .
न येषामग्निसंस्कारो नाशौचं नोदकक्रिया .. 55.29 ..
6.3.m: those who have died by fanged beasts, by falling into water, or by lightning strikes, / those who have had no cremation, no impurity period, and no water rite—

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yasteṣāṃ śrāddhaṃ kurvīta bhaktitaḥ .
mokṣāvāptirbhavetteṣāṃ yugamekaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .. 55.30 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यस्तेषां श्राद्धं कुर्वीत भक्तितः .
मोक्षावाप्तिर्भवेत्तेषां युगमेकं न संशयः .. 55.30 ..
6.3.m: for them, whoever performs a funeral rite with devotion at that sacred ford, / they attain liberation for one yuga; there is no doubt.

6.3.s:
ajñānādyatkṛtaṃ pāpaṃ bālabhāvācca yatkṛtam .
tatsarvaṃ nāśayetpāpaṃ snānamātreṇa bhūpate .. 55.31 ..
6.3.d:
अज्ञानाद्यत्कृतं पापं बालभावाच्च यत्कृतम् .
तत्सर्वं नाशयेत्पापं स्नानमात्रेण भूपते .. 55.31 ..
6.3.m: Whatever sin was committed through ignorance, and whatever was committed in childhood, / all that sin is destroyed merely by bathing, O king.

6.3.s:
rajakena yathā dhautaṃ vastraṃ bhavati nirmalam .
tathā pāpo'pi tattīrthe snāto bhavati nirmalaḥ .. 55.32 ..
6.3.d:
रजकेन यथा धौतं वस्त्रं भवति निर्मलम् .
तथा पापोऽपि तत्तीर्थे स्नातो भवति निर्मलः .. 55.32 ..
6.3.m: Just as a cloth washed by a washerman becomes spotless, / so even a sinner, having bathed at that sacred ford, becomes spotless.

6.3.s:
saṃnyāsaṃ kurute yo'tra tīrthe vidhisamanvitam .
dhyāyannityaṃ mahādevaṃ sa gacchetparamaṃ padam .. 55.33 ..
6.3.d:
संन्यासं कुरुते योऽत्र तीर्थे विधिसमन्वितम् .
ध्यायन्नित्यं महादेवं स गच्छेत्परमं पदम् .. 55.33 ..
6.3.m: Whoever takes renunciation according to the rules at this sacred ford, / meditating constantly on Mahādeva, goes to the supreme state.

6.3.s:
krīḍitvā sa yathākāmaṃ svecchayā śivamandire .
vedavedāṅgatattvajño jāyate'sau śubhe kule .. 55.34 ..
6.3.d:
क्रीडित्वा स यथाकामं स्वेच्छया शिवमन्दिरे .
वेदवेदाङ्गतत्त्वज्ञो जायतेऽसौ शुभे कुले .. 55.34 ..
6.3.m: Having sported according to his desire at will in the abode of Śiva, / he is born into an auspicious family, knowing the reality of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas,

6.3.s:
rūpavānsubhagaścaiva sarvavyādhivivarjitaḥ .
rājā vā rājaputro vācārasamanvitaḥ .. 55.35 ..
6.3.d:
रूपवान्सुभगश्चैव सर्वव्याधिविवर्जितः .
राजा वा राजपुत्रो वाचारसमन्वितः .. 55.35 ..
6.3.m: handsome, fortunate, free from all diseases, / a king or a prince endowed with good conduct.

6.3.s:
etatte kathitaṃ rājaṃstīrthasya phalamuttamam .
yacchrutvā mānavo nityaṃ mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ .. 55.36 ..
6.3.d:
एतत्ते कथितं राजंस्तीर्थस्य फलमुत्तमम् .
यच्छ्रुत्वा मानवो नित्यं मुच्यते सर्वकिल्बिषैः .. 55.36 ..
6.3.m: This excellent fruit of the sacred ford has been told to you, O king, / hearing which a mortal is constantly freed from all sins.

6.3.s:
ya idaṃ śrāvayennityamākhyānaṃ dvijapuṃgavān .
śrāddhe devakule vāpi paṭhetparvaṇi parvaṇi .. 55.37 ..
6.3.d:
य इदं श्रावयेन्नित्यमाख्यानं द्विजपुंगवान् .
श्राद्धे देवकुले वापि पठेत्पर्वणि पर्वणि .. 55.37 ..
6.3.m: Whoever constantly recites this narrative to the best of brahmins, / or reads it during a funeral rite, or in a temple on every auspicious festival day,

6.3.s:
gīrvāṇāstasya tuṣyanti manuṣyāḥ pitṛbhiḥ saha .
paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiva naśyate sarvapātakam .. 55.38 ..
6.3.d:
गीर्वाणास्तस्य तुष्यन्ति मनुष्याः पितृभिः सह .
पठतां शृण्वतां चैव नश्यते सर्वपातकम् .. 55.38 ..
6.3.m: the gods are pleased with him, and mortals along with their ancestors. / For those who read and hear it, all sin is destroyed.

6.3.s:
likhitvā tīrthamāhātmyaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo dadāti yaḥ .
jātismaratvaṃ labhate prāpnotyabhimataṃ phalam .. 55.39 ..
6.3.d:
लिखित्वा तीर्थमाहात्म्यं ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददाति यः .
जातिस्मरत्वं लभते प्राप्नोत्यभिमतं फलम् .. 55.39 ..
6.3.m: Whoever writes down the māhātmya of the sacred ford and gives it to brahmins, / obtains recollection of past births and achieves the desired fruit.

6.3.s:
rudraloke vasettāvadyāvadakṣaramanvitam .. 55.40 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe śūlabhedamāhātmye kāśīrājamokṣagamanaṃ nāma pañcapañcāśattamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 56
6.3.d:
रुद्रलोके वसेत्तावद्यावदक्षरमन्वितम् .. 55.40 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे शूलभेदमाहात्म्ये काशीराजमोक्षगमनं नाम पञ्चपञ्चाशत्तमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 56
6.3.m:
He dwells in the world of Rudra for as many [years] as there are syllables.
Thus ends the fifty-fifth chapter, named "The King of Kāśī's Attainment of Liberation," in the māhātmya of Śūlabheda, in the Revākhaṇḍa, in the fifth Avantyakhaṇḍa, in the Skandapurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 56

6.3.s:
uttānapāda uvāca -
anyacca śrotumicchāmi kena gaṅgāvatāritā .
rudraśīrṣe sthitā devī puṇyā kathamihāgatā .. 56.1 ..
6.3.d:
उत्तानपाद उवाच -
अन्यच्च श्रोतुमिच्छामि केन गङ्गावतारिता .
रुद्रशीर्षे स्थिता देवी पुण्या कथमिहागता .. 56.1 ..
6.3.m: Uttānapāda said: / I wish to hear something else: by whom was Gaṅgā brought down? / How did the holy goddess, dwelling on the head of Rudra, come here?

6.3.s:
puṇyā devāśilā nāma tasyā māhātmyamuttamam .
etadākhyāhi me sarvaṃ prasanno yadi śaṅkara .. 56.2 ..
6.3.d:
पुण्या देवाशिला नाम तस्या माहात्म्यमुत्तमम् .
एतदाख्याहि मे सर्वं प्रसन्नो यदि शङ्कर .. 56.2 ..
6.3.m: The sacred stone named Devaśilā, and its excellent māhātmya— / tell me all this, if you are pleased, O Śaṅkara.

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
śṛṇuṣvaikamanā bhūtvā yathā gaṅgāvatāritā .
devaiḥ sarvairmahābhāgā sarvalokahitāya vai .. 56.3 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
शृणुष्वैकमना भूत्वा यथा गङ्गावतारिता .
