चित्रन्यस्ता इव गताः प्रकामालोकनीयताम् .. 90.17 ..
6.3.m: And how is it that these Ādityas, cooled by the loss of their scorching heat, / have become fully visible to the gaze, as if painted in a picture?

6.3.s:
tadbrūta vatsāḥ kimitaḥ prārthayadhvaṃ samāgatāḥ .
kimāgamanakṛtyaṃ vo brūta niḥsaṃśayaṃ surāḥ .. 90.18 ..
6.3.d:
तद्ब्रूत वत्साः किमितः प्रार्थयध्वं समागताः .
किमागमनकृत्यं वो ब्रूत निःसंशयं सुराः .. 90.18 ..
6.3.m: Therefore speak, children: what do you seek, having gathered here? / What is the purpose of your coming? Tell without hesitation, O gods!

6.3.s:
mayi sṛṣṭirhi lokānāṃ rakṣā yuṣmāsvavasthitā .
tato mandānilodbhūtakamalākaraśobhinā .. 90.19 ..
6.3.d:
मयि सृष्टिर्हि लोकानां रक्षा युष्मास्ववस्थिता .
ततो मन्दानिलोद्भूतकमलाकरशोभिना .. 90.19 ..
6.3.m: For the creation of the worlds rests in me, and their protection in you. / Then, with [a glance] resembling a bed of lotuses stirred by a gentle breeze,

6.3.s:
guruṃ netrasahasreṇa prerayāmāsa vṛtrahā .
sa dvinetraṃ hareścakṣuḥ sahasranayanādhikam .. 90.20 ..
6.3.d:
गुरुं नेत्रसहस्रेण प्रेरयामास वृत्रहा .
स द्विनेत्रं हरेश्चक्षुः सहस्रनयनाधिकम् .. 90.20 ..
6.3.m: the slayer of Vṛtra urged his teacher with his thousand eyes. / Having two eyes, he [looked at] Hari's eye which was greater than a thousand eyes.

6.3.s:
vācaspatiruvācedaṃ prāñjalirjalajāsanam .
yuṣmadvaṃśodbhavastāta tālamegho mahābalaḥ .. 90.21 ..
6.3.d:
वाचस्पतिरुवाचेदं प्राञ्जलिर्जलजासनम् .
युष्मद्वंशोद्भवस्तात तालमेघो महाबलः .. 90.21 ..
6.3.m: With folded hands, Vācaspati spoke thus to the lotus-seated one: / 'Father, born of your lineage is the mighty Tālamegha.'

6.3.s:
upatāpayate devāndhūmaketurivocchritaḥ .
tena devagaṇāḥ sarve duḥkhitā dānavena ca .. 90.22 ..
6.3.d:
उपतापयते देवान्धूमकेतुरिवोच्छ्रितः .
तेन देवगणाः सर्वे दुःखिता दानवेन च .. 90.22 ..
6.3.m: Rising like a comet, he torments the gods; / and because of that Dānava all the hosts of gods are afflicted.

6.3.s:
tālamegho daityapatiḥ sarvānno bādhate balī .
tasmāttvāṃ śaraṇaṃ prāptāḥ śaraṇaṃ no vidhe bhava .. 90.23 ..
6.3.d:
तालमेघो दैत्यपतिः सर्वान्नो बाधते बली .
तस्मात्त्वां शरणं प्राप्ताः शरणं नो विधे भव .. 90.23 ..
6.3.m: Tālamegha, the mighty lord of the Daityas, harasses us all. / Therefore we have sought refuge with you; O Creator, be our refuge!

6.3.s: tataḥ prasanno bhagavān vedhāstānabravīdvacaḥ .. 90.24 ..
6.3.d: ततः प्रसन्नो भगवान् वेधास्तानब्रवीद्वचः .. 90.24 ..
6.3.m: Then the blessed Creator, pleased, spoke these words to them:

6.3.s:
brahmovāca -
tālameghena vo madhye balī tena samaḥ surāḥ .
vinā mādhavadevena sādhyo me naiva dānavaḥ .. 90.25 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच -
तालमेघेन वो मध्ये बली तेन समः सुराः .
विना माधवदेवेन साध्यो मे नैव दानवः .. 90.25 ..
6.3.m: Brahmā said: / 'O gods, among you he is powerful, and equal [to the greatest]; / without Lord Mādhava, that Dānava cannot be subdued by me.'

6.3.s:
tataḥ suragaṇāḥ sarve viriñcipramukhā nṛpa .
kṣīrodaṃ prasthitāḥ sarve duḥkhitāstena vairiṇā .. 90.26 ..
6.3.d:
ततः सुरगणाः सर्वे विरिञ्चिप्रमुखा नृप .
क्षीरोदं प्रस्थिताः सर्वे दुःखितास्तेन वैरिणा .. 90.26 ..
6.3.m: Then all the hosts of gods, headed by Brahmā, O king, / departed for the Milk Ocean, all distressed by that enemy.

6.3.s:
tvaritāḥ prasthitā devāḥ keśavaṃ draṣṭukāmyayā .
kṣīrodaṃ sāgaraṃ gatvāstuvaṃste jalaśāyinam .. 90.27 ..
6.3.d:
त्वरिताः प्रस्थिता देवाः केशवं द्रष्टुकाम्यया .
क्षीरोदं सागरं गत्वास्तुवंस्ते जलशायिनम् .. 90.27 ..
6.3.m: The gods set out swiftly, desiring to see Keśava. / Having gone to the Milk Ocean, they praised the one who lies upon the waters:

6.3.s:
devā ūcuḥ .
jagadādiranādistvaṃ jagadanto'pyanantakaḥ .
jaganmūrtiramūrtistvaṃ jaya gīrvāṇapūjita .. 90.28 ..
6.3.d:
देवा ऊचुः .
जगदादिरनादिस्त्वं जगदन्तोऽप्यनन्तकः .
जगन्मूर्तिरमूर्तिस्त्वं जय गीर्वाणपूजित .. 90.28 ..
6.3.m: The gods said: / 'You are the origin of the universe, yet without origin; the end of the universe, yet endless. / You possess the cosmic form, yet are formless. Victory to you, worshipped by the gods!

6.3.s:
jaya kṣīrodaśayana jaya lakṣmyā sadā vṛta .
jaya dānavanāśāya jaya devakinandana .. 90.29 ..
6.3.d:
जय क्षीरोदशयन जय लक्ष्म्या सदा वृत .
जय दानवनाशाय जय देवकिनन्दन .. 90.29 ..
6.3.m: Victory to you who recline upon the Milk Ocean! Victory to you who are ever attended by Lakṣmī! / Victory to you for the destruction of the Dānavas! Victory, O son of Devakī!

6.3.s:
jaya śaṅkhagadāpāṇe jaya cakradhara prabho .
iti devastutiṃ śrutvā prabuddho jalaśāyyatha .. 90.30 ..
6.3.d:
जय शङ्खगदापाणे जय चक्रधर प्रभो .
इति देवस्तुतिं श्रुत्वा प्रबुद्धो जलशाय्यथ .. 90.30 ..
6.3.m: Victory, O Lord who hold the conch and mace in hand, bearer of the discus!' / Hearing this hymn of the gods, the one who lies upon the waters awakened.

6.3.s:
uvāca madhurāṃ vāṇīṃ meghagambhīranisvanām .
kimarthaṃ bodhito brahman samarthairvaḥ surāsuraiḥ .. 90.31 ..
6.3.d:
उवाच मधुरां वाणीं मेघगम्भीरनिस्वनाम् .
किमर्थं बोधितो ब्रह्मन् समर्थैर्वः सुरासुरैः .. 90.31 ..
6.3.m: He spoke in sweet words resonant like the deep rumbling of clouds: / 'For what purpose have I been awakened, O Brahmā, by you capable gods and asuras?'

6.3.s:
brahmovāca -
tālameghabhayātkṛṣṇa samprāptāstava mandiram .
na vadhyaḥ kasyacitpāpastālamegho janārdana .. 90.32 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच -
तालमेघभयात्कृष्ण सम्प्राप्तास्तव मन्दिरम् .
न वध्यः कस्यचित्पापस्तालमेघो जनार्दन .. 90.32 ..
6.3.m: Brahmā said: / 'Out of fear of Tālamegha, O Kṛṣṇa, we have come to your abode. / That sinful Tālamegha cannot be slain by anyone else, O Janārdana.

6.3.s: tvameva jahi taṃ duṣṭaṃ mṛtyuṃ yāsyati nānyathā .. 90.33 ..
6.3.d: त्वमेव जहि तं दुष्टं मृत्युं यास्यति नान्यथा .. 90.33 ..
6.3.m: You alone must slay that wicked one; in no other way will he meet death.'

6.3.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca -
svasthānaṃ gamyatāṃ devāḥ svakīyāṃ labhata prajām .
duṣṭātmānaṃ haniṣyāmi tālameghaṃ mahābalam .. 90.34 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच -
स्वस्थानं गम्यतां देवाः स्वकीयां लभत प्रजाम् .
दुष्टात्मानं हनिष्यामि तालमेघं महाबलम् .. 90.34 ..
6.3.m: The blessed Kṛṣṇa said: / 'Go to your own abodes, O gods; take charge of your own subjects. / I shall slay the wicked-minded, mighty Tālamegha.

6.3.s: sthānaṃ bruvantu me devā vasedyatra sa dānavaḥ .. 90.35 ..
6.3.d: स्थानं ब्रुवन्तु मे देवा वसेद्यत्र स दानवः .. 90.35 ..
6.3.m: Let the gods tell me the place where that Dānava dwells.'

6.3.s:
devā ūcuḥ .
himācalaguhāyāṃ sa vasate dānaveśvaraḥ .
caturviṃśatisāhasraiḥ kanyābhiḥ parivāritaḥ .. 90.36 ..
6.3.d:
देवा ऊचुः .
हिमाचलगुहायां स वसते दानवेश्वरः .
चतुर्विंशतिसाहस्रैः कन्याभिः परिवारितः .. 90.36 ..
6.3.m: The gods said: / 'That lord of the Dānavas dwells in a cave of the Himālaya, / surrounded by twenty-four thousand maidens.

6.3.s:
turaṅgaiḥ syandanaiḥ kṛṣṇa saṃkhyā tasya na vidyate .
naṭā nānāvidhāstatra asaṃkhyātaguṇā hare .. 90.37 ..
6.3.d:
तुरङ्गैः स्यन्दनैः कृष्ण संख्या तस्य न विद्यते .
नटा नानाविधास्तत्र असंख्यातगुणा हरे .. 90.37 ..
6.3.m: His horses and chariots, O Kṛṣṇa, are beyond count. / Dancers of various kinds are there, countless in number, O Hari.

6.3.s:
dviradāḥ parvatākārā hayāśca dviradopamāḥ .
mahābalo vasettatra gīrvāṇabhayadāyakaḥ .. 90.38 ..
6.3.d:
द्विरदाः पर्वताकारा हयाश्च द्विरदोपमाः .
महाबलो वसेत्तत्र गीर्वाणभयदायकः .. 90.38 ..
6.3.m: Elephants like mountains and horses resembling elephants are his. / There dwells that mighty one, who strikes terror into the gods.'

6.3.s:
śrutvā devo vacasteṣāṃ devānāmāturātmanām .
acintayadgarutmantaṃ śatrusaṅghavināśanam .. 90.39 ..
6.3.d:
श्रुत्वा देवो वचस्तेषां देवानामातुरात्मनाम् .
अचिन्तयद्गरुत्मन्तं शत्रुसङ्घविनाशनम् .. 90.39 ..
6.3.m: Hearing the words of those afflicted gods, the Lord / thought of Garuḍa, the destroyer of hosts of foes.

6.3.s:
cakraṃ kareṇa saṃgṛhya gadācakradharaḥ prabhuḥ .
śārṅgaṃ ca muśalaṃ sīraṃ karairgṛhya janārdanaḥ .. 90.40 ..
6.3.d:
चक्रं करेण संगृह्य गदाचक्रधरः प्रभुः .
शार्ङ्गं च मुशलं सीरं करैर्गृह्य जनार्दनः .. 90.40 ..
6.3.m: Taking the discus in his hand, the Lord, bearer of the mace and discus, / taking up with his hands the Śārṅga bow, the pestle, and the plough, Janārdana

6.3.s:
ārūḍhaḥ pakṣirājendraṃ vadhārthaṃ dānavasya ca .
dānavasya pure peturutpātā ghorarūpiṇaḥ .. 90.41 ..
6.3.d:
आरूढः पक्षिराजेन्द्रं वधार्थं दानवस्य च .
दानवस्य पुरे पेतुरुत्पाता घोररूपिणः .. 90.41 ..
6.3.m: mounted the king of birds to slay the Dānava. / And in the city of the Dānava, portents of dreadful form descended:

6.3.s:
gomāyurgṛdhramadhye tu kapotaiḥ samamāviśat .
vinā vātena tasyaiva dhvajadaṇḍaḥ papāta ha .. 90.42 ..
6.3.d:
गोमायुर्गृध्रमध्ये तु कपोतैः सममाविशत् .
विना वातेन तस्यैव ध्वजदण्डः पपात ह .. 90.42 ..
6.3.m: A jackal entered among vultures together with pigeons; / and without any wind, his flagstaff fell down.

6.3.s:
sarpasūṣakayoryuddhaṃ tathā kesarināgayoḥ .
unmārgāḥ saritastatrāvahanraktavimiśritāḥ .
akālatarupuṣpāṇi dṛśyante sma samantataḥ .. 90.43 ..
6.3.d:
सर्पसूषकयोर्युद्धं तथा केसरिनागयोः .
उन्मार्गाः सरितस्तत्रावहन्रक्तविमिश्रिताः .
अकालतरुपुष्पाणि दृश्यन्ते स्म समन्ततः .. 90.43 ..
6.3.m: There was fighting between a snake and a mouse, and likewise between a lion and an elephant; / rivers there flowed backward, mingled with blood; / and unseasonal tree flowers were seen everywhere.

6.3.s:
tataḥ prāpto jagannātho himavantaṃ nageśvaram .
pāñcajanyaśvasahasā pūritaḥ purasannidhau .. 90.44 ..
6.3.d:
ततः प्राप्तो जगन्नाथो हिमवन्तं नगेश्वरम् .
पाञ्चजन्यश्वसहसा पूरितः पुरसन्निधौ .. 90.44 ..
6.3.m: Then the Lord of the Universe arrived at the Himālaya, the king of mountains; / near the city, he suddenly blew the Pāñcajanya.

6.3.s:
tena śabdena mahatā hyārūḍho dānaveśvaraḥ .
uvāca ca tadā vākyaṃ tālamegho mahābalaḥ .. 90.45 ..
6.3.d:
तेन शब्देन महता ह्यारूढो दानवेश्वरः .
उवाच च तदा वाक्यं तालमेघो महाबलः .. 90.45 ..
6.3.m: At that tremendous sound, the lord of the Dānavas mounted [his chariot]; / and then the mighty Tālamegha spoke these words:

6.3.s:
tālamegha uvāca -
ko'yaṃ mṛtyuvaśaṃ prāpto hyajñātvā mama vikramam .
dhundhumārājñayā hyāśu svasainyaparivāritaḥ .. 90.46 ..
6.3.d:
तालमेघ उवाच -
कोऽयं मृत्युवशं प्राप्तो ह्यज्ञात्वा मम विक्रमम् .
धुन्धुमाराज्ञया ह्याशु स्वसैन्यपरिवारितः .. 90.46 ..
6.3.m: Tālamegha said: / 'Who is this that has fallen into the grasp of death, unaware of my prowess? / Dhundhumāra, by my command, swiftly surrounded by your army,

6.3.s: balādānaya taṃ baddhvā mamāgre bahuśālinam .. 90.47 ..
6.3.d: बलादानय तं बद्ध्वा ममाग्रे बहुशालिनम् .. 90.47 ..
6.3.m: bind by force and bring before me that one who boasts of great strength!'

6.3.s:
dhundhumāra uvāca -
ānayāmi na sandehaḥ suro yakṣo'tha kinnaraḥ .
syandanaughaiḥ samāyukto gajavājibhaṭaiḥ saha .. 90.48 ..
6.3.d:
धुन्धुमार उवाच -
आनयामि न सन्देहः सुरो यक्षोऽथ किन्नरः .
स्यन्दनौघैः समायुक्तो गजवाजिभटैः सह .. 90.48 ..
6.3.m: Dhundhumāra said: / 'I shall bring him, no doubt, whether he be a god, a yakṣa, or a kinnara!' / Accompanied by hosts of chariots, along with elephants, horses, and warriors,

6.3.s:
hṛṣṭastato jagadyoniḥ suparṇastho mahābalaḥ .
gṛhyatāṃ gṛhyatāmeṣa ityuktāstena kiṃkarāḥ .. 90.49 ..
6.3.d:
हृष्टस्ततो जगद्योनिः सुपर्णस्थो महाबलः .
गृह्यतां गृह्यतामेष इत्युक्तास्तेन किंकराः .. 90.49 ..
6.3.m: the mighty source of the universe, seated upon Garuḍa, rejoiced. / 'Seize him! Seize him!' thus his servants were ordered by him.

6.3.s:
caturdikṣu pradhāvanta itaścetaśca sarvataḥ .
suparṇenāgnirūpeṇa dagdhāste śalabhā yathā .. 90.50 ..
6.3.d:
चतुर्दिक्षु प्रधावन्त इतश्चेतश्च सर्वतः .
सुपर्णेनाग्निरूपेण दग्धास्ते शलभा यथा .. 90.50 ..
6.3.m: They ran in the four directions, hither and thither on all sides. / But by Garuḍa, who had assumed the form of fire, they were burned like moths.

6.3.s:
dhundhumāro'pi kṛṣṇena śaraghātena tāḍitaḥ .
hato vakṣaḥsthale pāpo mṛtāvastho rathopari .. 90.51 ..
6.3.d:
धुन्धुमारोऽपि कृष्णेन शरघातेन ताडितः .
हतो वक्षःस्थले पापो मृतावस्थो रथोपरि .. 90.51 ..
6.3.m: Dhundhumāra too was struck down by Kṛṣṇa with a volley of arrows; / struck in the chest, the sinner lay dying upon his chariot.

6.3.s:
hāhākāraṃ tataḥ sarve dānavāścakrurāturāḥ .
tālameghastataḥ kruddho rathārūḍho vinirgataḥ .
dadṛśe keśavaṃ pārtha śaṅkhacakragadādharam .. 90.52 ..
6.3.d:
हाहाकारं ततः सर्वे दानवाश्चक्रुरातुराः .
तालमेघस्ततः क्रुद्धो रथारूढो विनिर्गतः .
ददृशे केशवं पार्थ शङ्खचक्रगदाधरम् .. 90.52 ..
6.3.m: Then all the Dānavas raised a lamentation in distress. / Thereupon Tālamegha, enraged, set forth mounted upon his chariot. / He saw Keśava, O Pārtha, bearing the conch, discus, and mace.

6.3.s:
tālamegha uvāca -
anye te dānavāḥ kṛṣṇa ye hatāḥ samare tvayā .
hiraṇyakaśipuprakhyānapumāṃso hi te'cyuta .. 90.53 ..
6.3.d:
तालमेघ उवाच -
अन्ये ते दानवाः कृष्ण ये हताः समरे त्वया .
हिरण्यकशिपुप्रख्यानपुमांसो हि तेऽच्युत .. 90.53 ..
6.3.m: Tālamegha said: / 'Other were those Dānavas, O Kṛṣṇa, who were slain by you in battle! / Those men like Hiraṇyakaśipu were unmanly, O Acyuta!'

6.3.s:
ityuktvā dānavaḥ pārtha varṣayāmāsa sāyakaiḥ .
dānavasya śarānmuktān chedayāmāsa keśavaḥ .. 90.54 ..
6.3.d:
इत्युक्त्वा दानवः पार्थ वर्षयामास सायकैः .
दानवस्य शरान्मुक्तान् छेदयामास केशवः .. 90.54 ..
6.3.m: Having spoken thus, O Pārtha, the Dānava showered him with arrows; / but Keśava cut down the arrows discharged by the Dānava.

6.3.s:
garutmānavadhītsainyamavadhyaṃ yatsurāsuraiḥ .
kṛṣṇena dviguṇāstasya preṣitāḥ svaśilīmukhāḥ .. 90.55 ..
6.3.d:
गरुत्मानवधीत्सैन्यमवध्यं यत्सुरासुरैः .
कृष्णेन द्विगुणास्तस्य प्रेषिताः स्वशिलीमुखाः .. 90.55 ..
6.3.m: Garuḍa slew the army that could not be slain by gods and asuras. / By Kṛṣṇa, twice as many arrows of his own were shot against him.

6.3.s:
dviguṇaṃ dviguṇīkṛtya preṣayāmāsa dānavaḥ .
tānapyaṣṭaguṇaiḥ kṛṣṇaśchādayāmāsa sāyakaiḥ .. 90.56 ..
6.3.d:
द्विगुणं द्विगुणीकृत्य प्रेषयामास दानवः .
तानप्यष्टगुणैः कृष्णश्छादयामास सायकैः .. 90.56 ..
6.3.m: Doubling that double number, the Dānava shot back; / and Kṛṣṇa covered even those with eightfold arrows.

6.3.s: tataḥ kruddhena daityena hyāgneyaṃ bāṇamuttamam .. 90.57 ..
6.3.d: ततः क्रुद्धेन दैत्येन ह्याग्नेयं बाणमुत्तमम् .. 90.57 ..
6.3.m: Then by the enraged Daitya, an excellent fiery missile [was discharged].

6.3.s:
vāruṇaṃ preṣayāmāsa tvāgneyaṃ śamitaṃ tataḥ .
vāruṇenaiva vāyavyaṃ tālamegho vyasarjayat .. 90.58 ..
6.3.d:
वारुणं प्रेषयामास त्वाग्नेयं शमितं ततः .
वारुणेनैव वायव्यं तालमेघो व्यसर्जयत् .. 90.58 ..
6.3.m: He [Kṛṣṇa] sent a watery missile, and then the fiery one was extinguished. / Countering the watery missile, Tālamegha launched a windy missile.

6.3.s:
sārpaṃ caiva hṛṣīkeśo vāyavyasya praśāntaye .
nārasiṃhaṃ nṛsiṃho'pi preṣayāmāsa pāṇḍava .. 90.59 ..
6.3.d:
सार्पं चैव हृषीकेशो वायव्यस्य प्रशान्तये .
नारसिंहं नृसिंहोऽपि प्रेषयामास पाण्डव .. 90.59 ..
6.3.m: Hṛṣīkeśa [sent] a serpentine missile to quell the windy one. / The man-lion also sent forth the Nārasiṃha missile, O Pāṇḍava.

6.3.s:
nārasiṃhaṃ tato dṛṣṭvā tālamegho mahābalaḥ .
uttīrya syandanācchīghraṃ gṛhītvā khaḍgacarmaṇī .. 90.60 ..
6.3.d:
नारसिंहं ततो दृष्ट्वा तालमेघो महाबलः .
उत्तीर्य स्यन्दनाच्छीघ्रं गृहीत्वा खड्गचर्मणी .. 90.60 ..
6.3.m: Then seeing the Nārasiṃha missile, the mighty Tālamegha, / descending swiftly from his chariot and grasping sword and shield, [shouted:]

6.3.s:
kṛṣṇa tvāṃ preṣayiṣyāmi yamamārgaṃ sudāruṇam .
ityuktvā dānavaḥ pārtha āgataḥ keśavaṃ prati .. 90.61 ..
6.3.d:
कृष्ण त्वां प्रेषयिष्यामि यममार्गं सुदारुणम् .
इत्युक्त्वा दानवः पार्थ आगतः केशवं प्रति .. 90.61 ..
6.3.m: 'Kṛṣṇa, I will send you onto the dreadful path of Yama!' / Having spoken thus, O Pārtha, the Dānava charged toward Keśava.

6.3.s:
khaḍgenātāḍayaddaityo gadāpāṇiṃ janārdanam .
maṇḍalāgraṃ tato gṛhya keśavo hṛṣṭamānasaḥ .. 90.62 ..
6.3.d:
खड्गेनाताडयद्दैत्यो गदापाणिं जनार्दनम् .
मण्डलाग्रं ततो गृह्य केशवो हृष्टमानसः .. 90.62 ..
6.3.m: The Daitya struck with his sword Janārdana, who held the mace in his hand. / Then seizing a curved sword, Keśava, delighted in mind,

6.3.s:
jaghanoraḥsthale pārtha tālameghaṃ mahāhave .
janārdanastadā daityaṃ daityo harimahanmṛdhe .. 90.63 ..
6.3.d:
जघनोरःस्थले पार्थ तालमेघं महाहवे .
जनार्दनस्तदा दैत्यं दैत्यो हरिमहन्मृधे .. 90.63 ..
6.3.m: struck Tālamegha in the chest in that great battle, O Pārtha. / Then Janārdana struck the Daitya, and the Daitya struck Hari in the fray.

6.3.s:
janārdanastataḥ kruddhastālameghāya bhārata .
amoghaṃ cakramādāya muktaṃ tasya ca mūrdhani .. 90.64 ..
6.3.d:
जनार्दनस्ततः क्रुद्धस्तालमेघाय भारत .
अमोघं चक्रमादाय मुक्तं तस्य च मूर्धनि .. 90.64 ..
6.3.m: Then Janārdana, enraged, took up the infallible discus against Tālamegha, O Bhārata, / and hurled it at his head.

6.3.s:
nipapāta śirastasya parvatāśca cakampire .
samudrāḥ kṣubhitāḥ pārtha nadya unmārgagāminīḥ .. 90.65 ..
6.3.d:
निपपात शिरस्तस्य पर्वताश्च चकम्पिरे .
समुद्राः क्षुभिताः पार्थ नद्य उन्मार्गगामिनीः .. 90.65 ..
6.3.m: His head fell down, and the mountains trembled; / the oceans were agitated, O Pārtha, and rivers ran off their courses.

6.3.s:
puṣpavṛṣṭiṃ tato devā mumucuḥ keśavopari .
avadhyaḥ surasaṅghānāṃ sūditaḥ keśava tvayā .. 90.66 ..
6.3.d:
पुष्पवृष्टिं ततो देवा मुमुचुः केशवोपरि .
अवध्यः सुरसङ्घानां सूदितः केशव त्वया .. 90.66 ..
6.3.m: Then the gods showered blossoms upon Keśava: / "He who was unslayable by the hosts of gods has been slain, O Keśava, by you!"

6.3.s:
svasthāścaiva tato devāstālameghe nipātite .
janārdano'pi kaunteya narmadātaṭamāśritaḥ .. 90.67 ..
6.3.d:
स्वस्थाश्चैव ततो देवास्तालमेघे निपातिते .
जनार्दनोऽपि कौन्तेय नर्मदातटमाश्रितः .. 90.67 ..
6.3.m: The gods were relieved once Tālamegha was brought down; / and Janārdana, too, O son of Kuntī, took resort on the bank of the Narmadā.

6.3.s:
kṣīrodāṃ narmadāṃ matvā anantabhujagopari .
lakṣmyā samanvitaḥ kṛṣṇo nilīnaścottare taṭe .. 90.68 ..
6.3.d:
क्षीरोदां नर्मदां मत्वा अनन्तभुजगोपरि .
लक्ष्म्या समन्वितः कृष्णो निलीनश्चोत्तरे तटे .. 90.68 ..
6.3.m: Considering the Narmadā as the Milk Ocean, Kṛṣṇa, accompanied by Lakṣmī, / reclined upon the serpent Ananta on the northern bank.

6.3.s:
cakraṃ vibhīṣaṇaṃ martye jvālāmālāsamanvitam .
patitaṃ narmadātoye jalaśāyisamīpataḥ .. 90.69 ..
6.3.d:
चक्रं विभीषणं मर्त्ये ज्वालामालासमन्वितम् .
पतितं नर्मदातोये जलशायिसमीपतः .. 90.69 ..
6.3.m: His terrifying discus, blazing with wreaths of flames, / fell into the waters of the Narmadā near the Lord sleeping on the water.

6.3.s:
nirdhūtakalmaṣaṃ jātaṃ narmadātoyayogataḥ .
tālameghavadhotpannaṃ yatpāpaṃ nṛpanandana .. 90.70 ..
6.3.d:
निर्धूतकल्मषं जातं नर्मदातोययोगतः .
तालमेघवधोत्पन्नं यत्पापं नृपनन्दन .. 90.70 ..
6.3.m: Through contact with the waters of the Narmadā, it became cleansed of stain; / whatever sin had arisen from the slaying of Tālamegha, O son of the king,

6.3.s:
tatsravaṃ kṣālitaṃ sadyo narmadāṃbhasi bhārata .
tadāprabhṛti loke'smiñjalaśāyī mahīpate .. 90.71 ..
6.3.d:
तत्स्रवं क्षालितं सद्यो नर्मदांभसि भारत .
तदाप्रभृति लोकेऽस्मिञ्जलशायी महीपते .. 90.71 ..
6.3.m: that effusion was instantly washed away in the water of the Narmadā, O descendant of Bharata. / Since that time, O king, in this world [He has been known as] Jalaśāyin.

6.3.s:
cakratīrthaṃ vadantyanye kecitkālāghanāśanam .
vikhyātaṃ bhārate varṣe narmadāyāṃ mahīpate .. 90.72 ..
6.3.d:
चक्रतीर्थं वदन्त्यन्ये केचित्कालाघनाशनम् .
विख्यातं भारते वर्षे नर्मदायां महीपते .. 90.72 ..
6.3.m: Others call it Cakratīrtha, and some [call it] Kālāghanāśana, / famous in the realm of Bhārata on the Narmadā, O king.

6.3.s:
tattīrthasya prabhāvo'yaṃ śrūyatāmavanīpate .
yathā'nanto hi nāgānāṃ devānāṃ ca janārdanaḥ .. 90.73 ..
6.3.d:
तत्तीर्थस्य प्रभावोऽयं श्रूयतामवनीपते .
यथाऽनन्तो हि नागानां देवानां च जनार्दनः .. 90.73 ..
6.3.m: Hear now the power of that sacred ford, O lord of the earth: / Just as Ananta is supreme among the serpents, and Janārdana among the gods,

6.3.s:
māsānāṃ mārgaśīrṣo'sti nadīnāṃ narmadā yathā .
māsi mārgaśire pārtha hyekādaśyāṃ site'hani .. 90.74 ..
6.3.d:
मासानां मार्गशीर्षोऽस्ति नदीनां नर्मदा यथा .
मासि मार्गशिरे पार्थ ह्येकादश्यां सितेऽहनि .. 90.74 ..
6.3.m: just as Mārgaśīrṣa is among the months, and the Narmadā among the rivers, / [so it is with this tīrtha]. In the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, O son of Pṛthā, on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight,

6.3.s:
gatvā yo manujo bhaktyā kāmakrodhavivarjitaḥ .
vaiṣṇavīṃ bhāvanāṃ kṛtvā jaleśaṃ tu vrajeta vai .. 90.75 ..
6.3.d:
गत्वा यो मनुजो भक्त्या कामक्रोधविवर्जितः .
वैष्णवीं भावनां कृत्वा जलेशं तु व्रजेत वै .. 90.75 ..
6.3.m: whichever human goes there with devotion, free from desire and anger, / adopting a Vaiṣṇava disposition, and approaches the Lord of the Waters,

6.3.s:
ekabhuktaṃ ca naktaṃ ca tathaivāyācitaṃ nṛpa .
upavāsaṃ tathā dānaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ ca bhojanam .. 90.76 ..
6.3.d:
एकभुक्तं च नक्तं च तथैवायाचितं नृप .
उपवासं तथा दानं ब्राह्मणानां च भोजनम् .. 90.76 ..
6.3.m: and observes eating only once a day, or eating only at night, or living on unbegged food, O king, / or fasting, and makes gifts and feeds brahmins,

6.3.s:
karoti ca kuruśreṣṭha na sa yāti yamālayam .
yamalokabhayādbhītā ye lokāḥ pāṇḍunandana .. 90.77 ..
6.3.d:
करोति च कुरुश्रेष्ठ न स याति यमालयम् .
यमलोकभयाद्भीता ये लोकाः पाण्डुनन्दन .. 90.77 ..
6.3.m: he does so, O best of the Kurus, and does not go to the abode of Yama. / Those people who are terrified of the realm of Yama, O joy of the Pāṇḍus,

6.3.s:
te paśyantu śriyaḥ kāntaṃ nāgaparyaṅkaśāyinam .
gopījanasamāvṛttaṃ yoganidrāṃ samāśritam .
viśvarūpaṃ jagannāthaṃ saṃsārabhayanāśanam .. 90.78 ..
6.3.d:
ते पश्यन्तु श्रियः कान्तं नागपर्यङ्कशायिनम् .
गोपीजनसमावृत्तं योगनिद्रां समाश्रितम् .
विश्वरूपं जगन्नाथं संसारभयनाशनम् .. 90.78 ..
6.3.m: let them behold the beloved of Śrī lying on the serpent-couch, / surrounded by the cowherd women, resting in yogic sleep, / the Lord of the Universe, universal in form, the destroyer of the fear of worldly existence.

6.3.s:
snāpayetparayā bhaktyā kṣaudrakṣīreṇa sarpiṣā .
khaṇḍena toyamiśreṇa jagadyoniṃ janārdanam .. 90.79 ..
6.3.d:
स्नापयेत्परया भक्त्या क्षौद्रक्षीरेण सर्पिषा .
खण्डेन तोयमिश्रेण जगद्योनिं जनार्दनम् .. 90.79 ..
6.3.m: With supreme devotion one should bathe Janārdana, the source of the universe, / with honey, milk, and clarified butter, and with candy mixed with water.

6.3.s:
snāpyamānaṃ ca paśyanti ye lokā gatamatsarāḥ .
te yānti paramaṃ lokaṃ surāsuranamaskṛtam .. 90.80 ..
6.3.d:
स्नाप्यमानं च पश्यन्ति ये लोका गतमत्सराः .
ते यान्ति परमं लोकं सुरासुरनमस्कृतम् .. 90.80 ..
6.3.m: And those people, free from malice, who behold him being bathed, / go to the supreme realm, venerated by gods and asuras.

6.3.s:
ghṛtena bodhayeddīpamathavā tailapūritam .
rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kṛtvā daivasyāgre vimatsarāḥ .. 90.81 ..
6.3.d:
घृतेन बोधयेद्दीपमथवा तैलपूरितम् .
रात्रौ जागरणं कृत्वा दैवस्याग्रे विमत्सराः .. 90.81 ..
6.3.m: One should kindle a lamp with clarified butter, or filled with oil, / and having kept a night vigil before the deity, free from envy,

6.3.s:
ye kathāṃ vaiṣṇavīṃ bhaktyā śṛṇvanti ca nṛpottama .
brahmahatyādipāpāni naśyante nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 90.82 ..
6.3.d:
ये कथां वैष्णवीं भक्त्या शृण्वन्ति च नृपोत्तम .
ब्रह्महत्यादिपापानि नश्यन्ते नात्र संशयः .. 90.82 ..
6.3.m: those who listen with devotion to the Vaiṣṇava narrative, O best of kings, / their sins such as the murder of a brahmin are destroyed; of this there is no doubt.

6.3.s:
pradakṣiṇanti ye martyā jalaśāyijagadgurum .
pradakṣiṇīkṛtā taistu saptadvīpā vasuṃdharā .. 90.83 ..
6.3.d:
प्रदक्षिणन्ति ये मर्त्या जलशायिजगद्गुरुम् .
प्रदक्षिणीकृता तैस्तु सप्तद्वीपा वसुंधरा .. 90.83 ..
6.3.m: Those mortals who circumambulate Jalaśāyin, the teacher of the universe, / have indeed circumambulated the earth with its seven continents.

6.3.s:
tataḥ prabhāte vimale pitḥn saṃtarpayejjalaiḥ .
śrāddhaṃ ca brāhmaṇaistatra yogyaiḥ pāṇḍava mānavāḥ .. 90.84 ..
6.3.d:
ततः प्रभाते विमले पित्ःन् संतर्पयेज्जलैः .
श्राद्धं च ब्राह्मणैस्तत्र योग्यैः पाण्डव मानवाः .. 90.84 ..
6.3.m: Then, at clear dawn, one should offer libations of water to the ancestors; / and there, O descendant of Pāṇḍu, men [should perform] a śrāddha through worthy brahmins:

6.3.s:
svadāranirataiḥ śāntaiḥ paradāravivarjakaiḥ .
vedābhyasanaśīlaiśca svakarmanirataiḥ śubhaiḥ .. 90.85 ..
6.3.d:
स्वदारनिरतैः शान्तैः परदारविवर्जकैः .
वेदाभ्यसनशीलैश्च स्वकर्मनिरतैः शुभैः .. 90.85 ..
6.3.m: those devoted to their own wives, tranquil, avoiding other men's wives, / habituated to the recitation of the Veda, devoted to their own duties, auspicious,

6.3.s:
nityaṃ yajanaśīlaiśca trisandhyāparipālakaiḥ .
śraddhayā kārayecchrāddhaṃ yadīcchecchreya ātmanaḥ .. 90.86 ..
6.3.d:
नित्यं यजनशीलैश्च त्रिसन्ध्यापरिपालकैः .
श्रद्धया कारयेच्छ्राद्धं यदीच्छेच्छ्रेय आत्मनः .. 90.86 ..
6.3.m: always prone to sacrifice, observing the three twilight prayers— / with faith one should have a śrāddha performed [by them] if one desires one's own welfare.

6.3.s:
te dhanyā mānuṣe loke vandyā hi bhuvi mānavāḥ .
ye vasanti sadākālaṃ pādapadmāśrayā hareḥ .. 90.87 ..
6.3.d:
ते धन्या मानुषे लोके वन्द्या हि भुवि मानवाः .
ये वसन्ति सदाकालं पादपद्माश्रया हरेः .. 90.87 ..
6.3.m: Blessed are those in the world of men, praiseworthy indeed are mortals on earth, / who dwell at all times taking refuge at the lotus feet of Hari,

6.3.s:
jalaśāyaṃ prapaśyanti pratyakṣaṃ suranāyakam .
pakṣopavāsaṃ pārākaṃ vrataṃ cāndrāyaṇaṃ śubham .. 90.88 ..
6.3.d:
जलशायं प्रपश्यन्ति प्रत्यक्षं सुरनायकम् .
पक्षोपवासं पाराकं व्रतं चान्द्रायणं शुभम् .. 90.88 ..
6.3.m: and behold Jalaśāya, the leader of the gods, visibly manifest. / A fast for a fortnight, the Parāka penance, the auspicious Cāndrāyaṇa vow,

6.3.s:
māsopavāsamugraṃ ca ṣaṣṭhānnaṃ pañcamaṃ vratam .
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ kuryātso'kṣayāṃ gatimāpnuyāt .. 90.89 ..
6.3.d:
मासोपवासमुग्रं च षष्ठान्नं पञ्चमं व्रतम् .
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः कुर्यात्सोऽक्षयां गतिमाप्नुयात् .. 90.89 ..
6.3.m: a severe fast for a month, or the vow of eating only at the sixth mealtime— / whoever performs these at that sacred ford attains an imperishable destiny.

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi tiladhenośca yatphalam .
yathā yasminyadā deyā dāne tasyāḥ śubhaṃ phalam .. 90.90 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि तिलधेनोश्च यत्फलम् .
यथा यस्मिन्यदा देया दाने तस्याः शुभं फलम् .. 90.90 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Hereafter I shall declare the fruit of the sesamum-cow: / how, to whom, and when it should be given, and the auspicious fruit of gifting it.

6.3.s:
etatkathāntaraṃ puṇyamṛṣerdvaipāyanātpurā .
śrutaṃ hi naimiṣe puṇye nāradādyairanekadhā .. 90.91 ..
6.3.d:
एतत्कथान्तरं पुण्यमृषेर्द्वैपायनात्पुरा .
श्रुतं हि नैमिषे पुण्ये नारदाद्यैरनेकधा .. 90.91 ..
6.3.m: This holy narrative was formerly heard in various ways / from the seer Dvaipāyana by Nārada and others in the holy Naimiṣa [forest].

6.3.s:
idaṃ paramamāyuṣyaṃ maṅgalyaṃ kīrtivardhanam .
viprāṇāṃ śrāvayanvidvānphalānantyaṃsamaśnute .. 90.92 ..
6.3.d:
इदं परममायुष्यं मङ्गल्यं कीर्तिवर्धनम् .
विप्राणां श्रावयन्विद्वान्फलानन्त्यंसमश्नुते .. 90.92 ..
6.3.m: This [narrative] yields supreme longevity, is auspicious, and enhances fame; / a wise man who recites it to brahmins obtains endless fruit.

6.3.s:
bahubhyo na pradeyāni gaurgṛhaṃ śayanaṃ striyaḥ .
vibhaktadakṣiṇā hyetā dātāraṃ nāpnuvanti ca .. 90.93 ..
6.3.d:
बहुभ्यो न प्रदेयानि गौर्गृहं शयनं स्त्रियः .
विभक्तदक्षिणा ह्येता दातारं नाप्नुवन्ति च .. 90.93 ..
6.3.m: A cow, a house, a bed, and women must not be given to many [recipients]; / for when divided, these sacrificial gifts do not benefit the giver.

6.3.s:
ekametatpradātavyaṃ na bahūnāṃ yudhiṣṭhira .
sā ca vikrayamāpannā dahatyāsaptamaṃ kulam .. 90.94 ..
6.3.d:
एकमेतत्प्रदातव्यं न बहूनां युधिष्ठिर .
सा च विक्रयमापन्ना दहत्यासप्तमं कुलम् .. 90.94 ..
6.3.m: This [gift] should be given to one, not to many, O Yudhiṣṭhira; / if she is sold, she burns the family up to the seventh generation.

6.3.s:
yathālābhā tu sarveṣāṃ caturdroṇā tu gauḥ smṛtā .
droṇasya vatsakaḥ kāryo bahūnāṃ vāpi kāmataḥ .. 90.95 ..
6.3.d:
यथालाभा तु सर्वेषां चतुर्द्रोणा तु गौः स्मृता .
द्रोणस्य वत्सकः कार्यो बहूनां वापि कामतः .. 90.95 ..
6.3.m: According to one's means, a cow is traditionally made of four droṇas [of sesamum]; / the calf should be made of one droṇa, or [of more] according to desire.

6.3.s:
yasmindeśe tu yanmānaṃ viṣaye vā vicāritam .
tena mānena tāṃ kurvannakṣayaṃ phalamaśnute .. 90.96 ..
6.3.d:
यस्मिन्देशे तु यन्मानं विषये वा विचारितम् .
तेन मानेन तां कुर्वन्नक्षयं फलमश्नुते .. 90.96 ..
6.3.m: Whatever measure is considered authoritative in a particular land or region, / by fashioning her according to that measure, one enjoys an imperishable fruit.

6.3.s:
sukhapūrvaṃ śucau bhūmau puṣpadhūpākṣataistathā .
karṇābhyāṃ ratne dātavye dīpau netradvaye tathā .. 90.97 ..
6.3.d:
सुखपूर्वं शुचौ भूमौ पुष्पधूपाक्षतैस्तथा .
कर्णाभ्यां रत्ने दातव्ये दीपौ नेत्रद्वये तथा .. 90.97 ..
6.3.m: Comfortably on clean ground, with flowers, incense, and unhusked rice grains, / two jewels are to be placed for the ears, and two lamps for the pair of eyes;

6.3.s:
śrīkhaṇḍamurasi sthāpyaṃ tābhyāṃ caiva tu kāñcanam .
ūrdhve madhu ghṛtaṃ deyaṃ kuryātsarṣaparomakam .. 90.98 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीखण्डमुरसि स्थाप्यं ताभ्यां चैव तु काञ्चनम् .
ऊर्ध्वे मधु घृतं देयं कुर्यात्सर्षपरोमकम् .. 90.98 ..
6.3.m: sandalwood paste is to be placed on the chest, and gold for the two [horns]; / honey and clarified butter should be placed above; one should make the body hairs out of mustard seeds.

6.3.s:
kambale kambalaṃ dadyācchroṇyāṃ madhu ghṛtaṃ tathā .
yavasaṃ pāyasaṃ dadyādghṛtaṃ kṣaudrasamanvitam .. 90.99 ..
6.3.d:
कम्बले कम्बलं दद्याच्छ्रोण्यां मधु घृतं तथा .
यवसं पायसं दद्याद्घृतं क्षौद्रसमन्वितम् .. 90.99 ..
6.3.m: One should place a woollen blanket upon the blanket; similarly, honey and clarified butter on the hips; / one should offer fodder, milk-rice, and clarified butter combined with honey.

6.3.s:
svarṇaśṛṅgī rūpyaśiphārukmalāṅgūlasaṃyutā .
ratnapṛṣṭhī tu dātavyā kāṃsyapātrāvadohinī .. 90.100 ..
6.3.d:
स्वर्णशृङ्गी रूप्यशिफारुक्मलाङ्गूलसंयुता .
रत्नपृष्ठी तु दातव्या कांस्यपात्रावदोहिनी .. 90.100 ..
6.3.m: With gold horns, silver hooves, furnished with a gold tail, / having a jewelled back, and a bronze vessel for milking, she should be given.

6.3.s:
yatsyādbālyakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ yadvā kṛtamajānatā .
vācā kṛtaṃ karmakṛtaṃ manasā yadvicintitam .. 90.101 ..
6.3.d:
यत्स्याद्बाल्यकृतं पापं यद्वा कृतमजानता .
वाचा कृतं कर्मकृतं मनसा यद्विचिन्तितम् .. 90.101 ..
6.3.m: Whatever sin was committed in childhood, or committed through ignorance, / committed by speech, committed by deed, or conceived in the mind;

6.3.s:
jale niṣṭhīvitaṃ caiva muśalaṃ vāpi laṅghitam .
vṛṣalīgamanaṃ caiva gurudāraniṣevaṇam .. 90.102 ..
6.3.d:
जले निष्ठीवितं चैव मुशलं वापि लङ्घितम् .
वृषलीगमनं चैव गुरुदारनिषेवणम् .. 90.102 ..
6.3.m: spitting into water, or stepping across a pestle, / having relations with an outcaste woman, intercourse with the teacher's wife,

6.3.s:
kanyāyā gamanaṃ caiva suvarṇasteyameva ca .
surāpānaṃ tathā cānyattiladhenuḥ punāti hi .. 90.103 ..
6.3.d:
कन्याया गमनं चैव सुवर्णस्तेयमेव च .
सुरापानं तथा चान्यत्तिलधेनुः पुनाति हि .. 90.103 ..
6.3.m: intercourse with an unmarried maiden, the theft of gold, / and the drinking of liquor, as well as other [sins]—the sesamum-cow purifies indeed.

6.3.s:
ahorātropavāsena vidhivattāṃ visarjayet .
yā sā yamapure ghore nadī vaitaraṇī smṛtā .. 90.104 ..
6.3.d:
अहोरात्रोपवासेन विधिवत्तां विसर्जयेत् .
या सा यमपुरे घोरे नदी वैतरणी स्मृता .. 90.104 ..
6.3.m: Fasting for a day and night, one should ritualistically dedicate her. / That which is known as the dreadful river Vaitaraṇī in the city of Yama,

6.3.s:
vālukāyo'śmasthalā ca pacyate yatra duṣkṛtī .
avīcirnarako yatra yatra yāmalaparvatau .. 90.105 ..
6.3.d:
वालुकायोऽश्मस्थला च पच्यते यत्र दुष्कृती .
अवीचिर्नरको यत्र यत्र यामलपर्वतौ .. 90.105 ..
6.3.m: where the evil-doer is boiled on fiery sands and rocks, / where is the hell Avīci, and where are the Twin Mountains,

6.3.s:
yatra lohamukhāḥ kākā yatra śvāno bhayaṃkarāḥ .
asipattravanaṃ caiva yatra sā kūṭaśālmalī .. 90.106 ..
6.3.d:
यत्र लोहमुखाः काका यत्र श्वानो भयंकराः .
असिपत्त्रवनं चैव यत्र सा कूटशाल्मली .. 90.106 ..
6.3.m: where there are iron-beaked crows, where there are terrifying dogs, / and the forest of sword-like leaves, and where the Kūṭaśālmalī tree stands—

6.3.s:
tānsukhena vyatikramya dharmarājālayaṃ vrajet .
dharmarājastu taṃ dṛṣṭvā sūnṛtaṃ vakti bhārata .. 90.107 ..
6.3.d:
तान्सुखेन व्यतिक्रम्य धर्मराजालयं व्रजेत् .
धर्मराजस्तु तं दृष्ट्वा सूनृतं वक्ति भारत .. 90.107 ..
6.3.m: having crossed beyond those with ease, he goes to the abode of the King of Dharma; / and the King of Dharma, seeing him, speaks gentle and truthful words, O descendant of Bharata:

6.3.s:
vimānamuttamaṃ yogyaṃ maṇiratnavibhūṣitam .
atrāruhya naraśreṣṭha prayāhi paramāṃ gatim .. 90.108 ..
6.3.d:
विमानमुत्तमं योग्यं मणिरत्नविभूषितम् .
अत्रारुह्य नरश्रेष्ठ प्रयाहि परमां गतिम् .. 90.108 ..
6.3.m: "An excellent, worthy aerial chariot adorned with gems and jewels [awaits]; / mount this, O best of men, and go to the supreme state!"

6.3.s:
mā ca cāṭu bhaṭe dehi maiva dehi purohite .
mā ca kāṇe virūpe ca nyūnāṅge na ca devale .. 90.109 ..
6.3.d:
मा च चाटु भटे देहि मैव देहि पुरोहिते .
मा च काणे विरूपे च न्यूनाङ्गे न च देवले .. 90.109 ..
6.3.m: Do not give it to a flatterer or a soldier, nor give it to a domestic priest; / nor to a one-eyed man, an ugly man, one with deficient limbs, or a temple priest.

6.3.s:
avedaviduṣe naiva brāhmaṇe sarvavikraye .
mitraghne ca kṛtaghne ca mantrahīne tathaiva ca .. 90.110 ..
6.3.d:
अवेदविदुषे नैव ब्राह्मणे सर्वविक्रये .
मित्रघ्ने च कृतघ्ने च मन्त्रहीने तथैव च .. 90.110 ..
6.3.m: Never to a brahmin ignorant of the Veda, nor to one who sells everything, / nor to a betrayer of friends, an ungrateful person, or one devoid of mantras.

6.3.s:
vedāntagāya dātavyā śrotriyāya kuṭumbine .
vedāntagasute deyā śrotriye gṛhapālake .. 90.111 ..
6.3.d:
वेदान्तगाय दातव्या श्रोत्रियाय कुटुम्बिने .
वेदान्तगसुते देया श्रोत्रिये गृहपालके .. 90.111 ..
6.3.m: It should be given to one versed in Vedānta, a learned Vedic scholar with a family; / it should be given to the son of one versed in Vedānta, a learned Vedic scholar who maintains a household;

6.3.s:
sarvāṅgarucire vipre sadvṛtte ca priyaṃvade .
pūrṇimāyāṃ tu māghasya kārttikyāmatha bhārata .. 90.112 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वाङ्गरुचिरे विप्रे सद्वृत्ते च प्रियंवदे .
पूर्णिमायां तु माघस्य कार्त्तिक्यामथ भारत .. 90.112 ..
6.3.m: to a brahmin handsome in all limbs, of good conduct, and speaking pleasant words, / on the full moon of Māgha or on Kārttikī, O Bhārata,

6.3.s:
vaiśākhyāṃ mārgaśīrṣyāṃ vāṣāḍhyāṃ caitryāmathāpi vā .
ayane viṣuve caiva vyatīpāte ca sarvadā .. 90.113 ..
6.3.d:
वैशाख्यां मार्गशीर्ष्यां वाषाढ्यां चैत्र्यामथापि वा .
अयने विषुवे चैव व्यतीपाते च सर्वदा .. 90.113 ..
6.3.m: or on Vaiśākhī, Mārgaśīrṣī, Āṣāḍhī, or Caitrī, / or on a solstice, an equinox, and always at a vyatīpāta;

6.3.s:
ṣaḍaśītimukhe puṇye chāyāyāṃ kuṃjarasya vā .
eṣa te kathitaḥ kalpastiladhenormayānagha .. 90.114 ..
6.3.d:
षडशीतिमुखे पुण्ये छायायां कुंजरस्य वा .
एष ते कथितः कल्पस्तिलधेनोर्मयानघ .. 90.114 ..
6.3.m: at the auspicious saḍaśītimukha, or during the shadow of an elephant. / This ritual procedure for the sesamum-cow has been told to you by me, O sinless one.

6.3.s:
vrajanti vaiṣṇavaṃ lokaṃ dattvā pādaṃ yamopari .
prāṇatyāgātparaṃ lokaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ .
bhittvāśu bhāskaraṃ yānti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 90.115 ..
6.3.d:
व्रजन्ति वैष्णवं लोकं दत्त्वा पादं यमोपरि .
प्राणत्यागात्परं लोकं वैष्णवं नात्र संशयः .
भित्त्वाशु भास्करं यान्ति नात्र कार्या विचारणा .. 90.115 ..
6.3.m: Setting their foot upon Yama, they go to the world of Viṣṇu; / after casting off their life-breaths they attain the supreme world of Viṣṇu, without doubt; / piercing through the sun, they go straightaway; no doubt should be entertained here.

6.3.s:
etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ cakratīrthaphalaṃ nṛpa .
yacchrutvā mānavo bhaktyā sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate .. 90.116 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe jalaśāyitīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma navatitamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 91
6.3.d:
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं चक्रतीर्थफलं नृप .
यच्छ्रुत्वा मानवो भक्त्या सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते .. 90.116 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे जलशायितीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम नवतितमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 91
6.3.m:
This whole fruit of Cakratīrtha has been related to you, O king, / hearing which with devotion, a mortal is freed from all sins.
Thus ends the ninetieth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Māhātmya of Jalaśāyitīrtha', in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 91

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gacchenmahīpāla tīrthaparamapāvanam .
caṇḍādityaṃ nṛpaśreṣṭha sthāpitaṃ caṇḍamuṇḍayoḥ .. 91.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेन्महीपाल तीर्थपरमपावनम् .
चण्डादित्यं नृपश्रेष्ठ स्थापितं चण्डमुण्डयोः .. 91.1 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then one should go, O ruler of the earth, to the supremely purifying sacred ford / Caṇḍāditya, O best of kings, established by Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa.

6.3.s:
āstāṃ purā mahādaityau caṇḍamuṇḍau sudāruṇau .
narmadātīramāśritya ceraturvipulaṃ tapaḥ .. 91.2 ..
6.3.d:
आस्तां पुरा महादैत्यौ चण्डमुण्डौ सुदारुणौ .
नर्मदातीरमाश्रित्य चेरतुर्विपुलं तपः .. 91.2 ..
6.3.m: Formerly there were two very terrible great Daityas, Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa. / Resorting to the bank of the Narmadā, they performed extensive austerity,

6.3.s:
dhyāyantau bhāskaraṃ devaṃ tamonāśaṃ jagattraye .
tuṣṭastattapasā devaḥ sahasrāṃśuruvāca ha .. 91.3 ..
6.3.d:
ध्यायन्तौ भास्करं देवं तमोनाशं जगत्त्रये .
तुष्टस्तत्तपसा देवः सहस्रांशुरुवाच ह .. 91.3 ..
6.3.m: meditating upon the Sun god, who destroys darkness in the three worlds. / Pleased by their austerity, the thousand-rayed god spoke:

6.3.s:
sādhu sādhviti tau pārtha narmadāyāḥ śubhe taṭe .
varaṃ prārthayataṃ vīrau yatheṣṭaṃ cetasecchitam .. 91.4 ..
6.3.d:
साधु साध्विति तौ पार्थ नर्मदायाः शुभे तटे .
वरं प्रार्थयतं वीरौ यथेष्टं चेतसेच्छितम् .. 91.4 ..
6.3.m: "Well done, well done!" to the two, O Pārtha, on the auspicious bank of the Narmadā. / "Choose a boon, O heroes, according to your desire, whatever your mind wishes."

6.3.s:
caṇḍamuṇḍāvūcatuḥ .
ajeyau sarvadevānāṃ bhūyāsvāvāṃ samāhitau .
sarvarogaiḥ parityaktau sarvakālaṃ divākara .. 91.5 ..
6.3.d:
चण्डमुण्डावूचतुः .
अजेयौ सर्वदेवानां भूयास्वावां समाहितौ .
सर्वरोगैः परित्यक्तौ सर्वकालं दिवाकर .. 91.5 ..
6.3.m: Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa said: / "May we two be unconquerable by all the gods, focused in mind, / and free from all diseases at all times, O Sun!"

6.3.s:
evamastviti tau prāha bhāskaro vāritaskaraḥ .
ityuktvāntardadhe bhānurdaityābhyāṃ tatra bhāskaraḥ .. 91.6 ..
6.3.d:
एवमस्त्विति तौ प्राह भास्करो वारितस्करः .
इत्युक्त्वान्तर्दधे भानुर्दैत्याभ्यां तत्र भास्करः .. 91.6 ..
6.3.m: "So be it!" the Sun, the stealer of water, said to them. / Having spoken thus, the Sun vanished there before the two Daityas.

6.3.s:
sthāpitaḥ parayā bhaktyā taṃ gacchedātmasiddhaye .
gīrvāṇāṃśca manuṣyāṃśca pitḥṃstatrāpi tarpayet .. 91.7 ..
6.3.d:
स्थापितः परया भक्त्या तं गच्छेदात्मसिद्धये .
गीर्वाणांश्च मनुष्यांश्च पित्ःंस्तत्रापि तर्पयेत् .. 91.7 ..
6.3.m: Established by them with supreme devotion, one should go to it for one's own perfection. / One should satisfy gods, humans, and ancestors there as well.

6.3.s:
sa vasedbhāskare loke viriñcidivasaṃ nṛpa .
ghṛtena bodhayeddīpaṃ ṣaṣṭhyāṃ sa ca nareśvara .
mucyate sarvapāpaistu pratiyāti puraṃ raveḥ .. 91.8 ..
6.3.d:
स वसेद्भास्करे लोके विरिञ्चिदिवसं नृप .
घृतेन बोधयेद्दीपं षष्ठ्यां स च नरेश्वर .
मुच्यते सर्वपापैस्तु प्रतियाति पुरं रवेः .. 91.8 ..
6.3.m: He dwells in the world of the Sun for a day of Brahmā, O king. / And whoever lights a lamp with ghee on the sixth day, O lord of men, / is freed from all sins and goes to the city of the Sun.

6.3.s:
utpattiṃ caṇḍabhānoryaḥ śṛṇoti bharatarṣabha .
vijayī sa sadā nūnamādhivyādhivivarjitaḥ .. 91.9 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe caṇḍādityatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmaikanavatitamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
6.3.d:
उत्पत्तिं चण्डभानोर्यः शृणोति भरतर्षभ .
विजयी स सदा नूनमाधिव्याधिविवर्जितः .. 91.9 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे चण्डादित्यतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामैकनवतितमोऽध्यायः ..
6.3.m:
Whoever hears the origin of Caṇḍabhānu, O bull of the Bharatas, / is surely always victorious and free from mental agony and physical disease.
Thus ends the ninety-first chapter, entitled 'Description of the Māhātmya of Caṇḍādityatīrtha', in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gacchettu rājendra yamahāsyamanuttamam .
sarvapāpaharaṃ tīrthaṃ narmadātaṭamāśritam .. 92.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेत्तु राजेन्द्र यमहास्यमनुत्तमम् .
सर्वपापहरं तीर्थं नर्मदातटमाश्रितम् .. 92.1 ..
6.3.m: Glorious Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then, king of kings, one should go to the unsurpassed Yamahāsya, / A sacred ford that removes all sins, situated on the bank of the Narmadā.

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
yamahāsyaṃ kathaṃ jātaṃ pṛthivyāṃ dvijapuṃgava .
etatsarvaṃ mamākhyāhi paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me .. 92.2 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
यमहास्यं कथं जातं पृथिव्यां द्विजपुंगव .
एतत्सर्वं ममाख्याहि परं कौतूहलं हि मे .. 92.2 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / How did Yamahāsya come to be on earth, O best of twice-born? / Tell me all this, for great indeed is my curiosity.

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
sādhu sādhu mahāprājña pṛṣṭo'haṃ nṛpanandana .
snānārthaṃ narmadāṃ puṇyāmāgataste pitā purā .. 92.3 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
साधु साधु महाप्राज्ञ पृष्टोऽहं नृपनन्दन .
स्नानार्थं नर्मदां पुण्यामागतस्ते पिता पुरा .. 92.3 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Well asked, well asked, O highly wise son of a king! / Formerly, your father came to the holy Narmadā for the sake of ritual ablution.

6.3.s:
rajakena yathā dhautaṃ vastraṃ bhavati nirmalam .
tathāsau nirmalo jāto dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhira .. 92.4 ..
6.3.d:
रजकेन यथा धौतं वस्त्रं भवति निर्मलम् .
तथासौ निर्मलो जातो धर्मराजो युधिष्ठिर .. 92.4 ..
6.3.m: Just as a cloth washed by a washerman becomes stainless, / so that Dharmarāja became stainless, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

6.3.s: sa paśyannirmalaṃ dehaṃ hasanprovāca vismitaḥ .. 92.5 ..
6.3.d: स पश्यन्निर्मलं देहं हसन्प्रोवाच विस्मितः .. 92.5 ..
6.3.m: Seeing his stainless body, he said, laughing in astonishment:

6.3.s:
yama uvāca -
matpuraṃ kathamāyānti manujāḥ pāpabṛṃhitāḥ .
snānenaikena revāyāḥ prāpyate vaiṣṇavaṃ padam .. 92.6 ..
6.3.d:
यम उवाच -
मत्पुरं कथमायान्ति मनुजाः पापबृंहिताः .
स्नानेनैकेन रेवायाः प्राप्यते वैष्णवं पदम् .. 92.6 ..
6.3.m: Yama said: / How can men burdened with sins come to my city? / By a single ritual ablution in the Revā, the state of Viṣṇu is attained.

6.3.s:
samarthā ye na paśyanti revāṃ puṇyajalāṃ śubhām .
jātyandhaiste samā jñeyā mṛtaiḥ paṅgubhireva vā .. 92.7 ..
6.3.d:
समर्था ये न पश्यन्ति रेवां पुण्यजलां शुभाम् .
जात्यन्धैस्ते समा ज्ञेया मृतैः पङ्गुभिरेव वा .. 92.7 ..
6.3.m: Those who, being capable, do not behold the auspicious Revā of holy waters, / are to be considered equal to those blind from birth, or to the dead and the crippled.

6.3.s:
samarthā ye na paśyanti revāṃ puṇyajalāṃ nadīm .
etasmātkāraṇādrājanhasito lokaśāsanaḥ .. 92.8 ..
6.3.d:
समर्था ये न पश्यन्ति रेवां पुण्यजलां नदीम् .
एतस्मात्कारणाद्राजन्हसितो लोकशासनः .. 92.8 ..
6.3.m: Those who, being capable, do not behold the river Revā of holy waters— / for this reason, O King, the punisher of the world laughed.

6.3.s:
sthāpayitvā yamastatra devaṃ svargaṃ jagāma ha .
yamahāseśvare rājañjitakrodho jitendriyaḥ .. 92.9 ..
6.3.d:
स्थापयित्वा यमस्तत्र देवं स्वर्गं जगाम ह .
यमहासेश्वरे राजञ्जितक्रोधो जितेन्द्रियः .. 92.9 ..
6.3.m: Having installed the deity Yamahāseśvara there, O King, / Yama, with anger conquered and senses controlled, went to heaven.

6.3.s:
viśeṣāccāśvine māsi kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśīm .
upoṣya parayā bhaktyā sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate .. 92.10 ..
6.3.d:
विशेषाच्चाश्विने मासि कृष्णपक्षे चतुर्दशीम् .
उपोष्य परया भक्त्या सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते .. 92.10 ..
6.3.m: Especially on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight in the month of Āśvina, / fasting with supreme devotion, one is freed from all sins.

6.3.s:
rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kuryāddīpaṃ devasya bodhayet .
ghṛtena caiva rājendra śṛṇu tatrāsti yatphalam .. 92.11 ..
6.3.d:
रात्रौ जागरणं कुर्याद्दीपं देवस्य बोधयेत् .
घृतेन चैव राजेन्द्र शृणु तत्रास्ति यत्फलम् .. 92.11 ..
6.3.m: One should keep vigil at night and kindle a lamp for the deity / with ghee, O lord of kings. Hear the fruit that lies therein:

6.3.s:
mucyate pātakaiḥ sarvairagamyāgamanodbhavaiḥ .
abhakṣyabhakṣaṇodbhūtairapeyāpeyajairapi .. 92.12 ..
6.3.d:
मुच्यते पातकैः सर्वैरगम्यागमनोद्भवैः .
अभक्ष्यभक्षणोद्भूतैरपेयापेयजैरपि .. 92.12 ..
6.3.m: He is freed from all sins born of approaching women who should not be approached, / born of eating food that should not be eaten, and arising from drinking what should not be drunk.

6.3.s:
avāhyavāhite yatsyādadohyādohane yathā .
snānamātreṇa tasyaivaṃ yānti pāpānyanekadhā .. 92.13 ..
6.3.d:
अवाह्यवाहिते यत्स्याददोह्यादोहने यथा .
स्नानमात्रेण तस्यैवं यान्ति पापान्यनेकधा .. 92.13 ..
6.3.m: Whatever [sin] arises from riding an animal that should not be ridden, or from milking an animal that should not be milked, / by the mere ritual ablution of that person, thus do the sins depart in manifold ways.

6.3.s:
yamalokaṃ na vīkṣeta manujaḥ sa kadācana .
pitḥṇāṃ paramaṃ guhyamidaṃ bhūmau nareśvara .. 92.14 ..
6.3.d:
यमलोकं न वीक्षेत मनुजः स कदाचन .
पित्ःणां परमं गुह्यमिदं भूमौ नरेश्वर .. 92.14 ..
6.3.m: That man shall never behold the world of Yama. / This is the supreme secret of the ancestors on earth, O ruler of men.

6.3.s:
dadatāmakṣayaṃ sarvaṃ yamahāsye na saṃśayaḥ .
amāvāsyāṃ jitakrodho yastu pūjayate dvijān .. 92.15 ..
6.3.d:
ददतामक्षयं सर्वं यमहास्ये न संशयः .
अमावास्यां जितक्रोधो यस्तु पूजयते द्विजान् .. 92.15 ..
6.3.m: For those who give at Yamahāsya, everything is imperishable, there is no doubt. / The one who, with anger conquered, worships twice-born men on the new moon day,

6.3.s:
hiraṇyabhūmidānena tiladānena bhūyasā .
kṛṣṇājinapradānena tiladhenupradānataḥ .. 92.16 ..
6.3.d:
हिरण्यभूमिदानेन तिलदानेन भूयसा .
कृष्णाजिनप्रदानेन तिलधेनुप्रदानतः .. 92.16 ..
6.3.m: by giving gold and land, by giving an abundance of sesame seeds, / by bestowing a black antelope skin, and by giving a cow made of sesame seeds,

6.3.s:
vidhānoktadvijāgryāya ye pradāsyanti bhaktitaḥ .
hayaṃ vā kuṃjaraṃ vātha dhūrvahau sīrasaṃyutau .. 92.17 ..
6.3.d:
विधानोक्तद्विजाग्र्याय ये प्रदास्यन्ति भक्तितः .
हयं वा कुंजरं वाथ धूर्वहौ सीरसंयुतौ .. 92.17 ..
6.3.m: and who with devotion give to an eminent twice-born described in the ordinances / a horse, or an elephant, or two [oxen] bearing a yoke together with a plough,

6.3.s:
kanyāṃ vasumatīṃ gāṃ ca mahiṣīṃ vā payasvinīm .
dadate ye nṛpaśreṣṭha nopasarpanti te yamam .. 92.18 ..
6.3.d:
कन्यां वसुमतीं गां च महिषीं वा पयस्विनीम् .
ददते ये नृपश्रेष्ठ नोपसर्पन्ति ते यमम् .. 92.18 ..
6.3.m: a maiden, land, a cow, or a buffalo cow yielding milk— / those who give [these], O best of kings, do not approach Yama.

6.3.s:
yamo'pi bhavati prītaḥ pratijanma yudhiṣṭhira .
yamasya vāho mahiṣo mahiṣyastasya mātaraḥ .. 92.19 ..
6.3.d:
यमोऽपि भवति प्रीतः प्रतिजन्म युधिष्ठिर .
यमस्य वाहो महिषो महिष्यस्तस्य मातरः .. 92.19 ..
6.3.m: Yama too becomes pleased in every birth, O Yudhiṣṭhira. / The mount of Yama is the buffalo, and female buffaloes are his mothers.

6.3.s:
tāsāṃ dānaprabhāveṇa yamaḥ prīto bhaveddhruvam .
nāsau yamamavāpnoti yadi pāpaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ .. 92.20 ..
6.3.d:
तासां दानप्रभावेण यमः प्रीतो भवेद्ध्रुवम् .
नासौ यममवाप्नोति यदि पापैः समावृतः .. 92.20 ..
6.3.m: By the power of giving them, Yama will surely be pleased. / He does not reach Yama even if covered with sins.

6.3.s:
etasmātkāraṇādatra mahiṣīdānamuttamam .
tasyāḥ śṛṅge jalaṃ kāryaṃ dhūmravastrānuveṣṭitā .. 92.21 ..
6.3.d:
एतस्मात्कारणादत्र महिषीदानमुत्तमम् .
तस्याः शृङ्गे जलं कार्यं धूम्रवस्त्रानुवेष्टिता .. 92.21 ..
6.3.m: For this reason, the gift of a female buffalo is supreme here. / Water should be placed on her horns, and she should be covered with a dark grey cloth.

6.3.s:
āyasasya khurāḥ kāryāstāmrapṛṣṭhāḥ subhūṣitāḥ .
lavaṇācalaṃ pūrvasyāmāgneyyāṃ guḍaparvatam .. 92.22 ..
6.3.d:
आयसस्य खुराः कार्यास्ताम्रपृष्ठाः सुभूषिताः .
लवणाचलं पूर्वस्यामाग्नेय्यां गुडपर्वतम् .. 92.22 ..
6.3.m: Her hooves should be made of iron, her back covered with copper, handsomely adorned. / [One should place] a heap of salt in the east, a heap of molasses in the south-east,

6.3.s:
kārpāsaṃ yāmyabhāgaṃ tu navanītaṃ tu nairṛte .
paścime saptadhānyāni vāyavye taṃdulāḥ smṛtāḥ .. 92.23 ..
6.3.d:
कार्पासं याम्यभागं तु नवनीतं तु नैरृते .
पश्चिमे सप्तधान्यानि वायव्ये तंदुलाः स्मृताः .. 92.23 ..
6.3.m: cotton in the southern direction, and butter in the south-west; / the seven grains in the west, and husked rice is prescribed in the north-west.

6.3.s:
saumye tu kāñcanaṃ dadyādīśāne ghṛtameva ca .
pradadyādyamarājo me prīyatāmityudīrayan .. 92.24 ..
6.3.d:
सौम्ये तु काञ्चनं दद्यादीशाने घृतमेव च .
प्रदद्याद्यमराजो मे प्रीयतामित्युदीरयन् .. 92.24 ..
6.3.m: In the north he should give gold, and in the north-east, ghee; / saying, ‘May the king of death, Yama, be pleased with me,’ he should give [it].

6.3.s:
ityuccārya dvijasyāgre yamalokaṃ mahābhayam .
asipattravanaṃ ghoraṃ yamacullī sudāruṇā .. 92.25 ..
6.3.d:
इत्युच्चार्य द्विजस्याग्रे यमलोकं महाभयम् .
असिपत्त्रवनं घोरं यमचुल्ली सुदारुणा .. 92.25 ..
6.3.m: Having spoken thus before the twice-born: ‘The realm of Yama is full of great terror, / the forest of sword-leaved trees is terrible, Yama’s furnace is most dreadful,

6.3.s:
raudrā vaitaraṇī caiva kumbhīpāko bhayāvahaḥ .
kālasūtro mahābhīmastathā yamalaparvatau .. 92.26 ..
6.3.d:
रौद्रा वैतरणी चैव कुम्भीपाको भयावहः .
कालसूत्रो महाभीमस्तथा यमलपर्वतौ .. 92.26 ..
6.3.m: the fierce Vaitaraṇī, the fear-inspiring Kumbhīpāka, / the terrible Kālasūtra, and the twin mountains of Yama,

6.3.s:
krakacaṃ tailayantraṃ ca śvāno gṛdhrāḥ sudāruṇāḥ .
nirucchvāsā mahānādā bhairavo rauravastathā .. 92.27 ..
6.3.d:
क्रकचं तैलयन्त्रं च श्वानो गृध्राः सुदारुणाः .
निरुच्छ्वासा महानादा भैरवो रौरवस्तथा .. 92.27 ..
6.3.m: the saw, the oil-press, the dogs, and the dreadful vultures, / the Nirucchvāsa, the Mahānāda, the Bhairava, and the Raurava—

6.3.s:
ete ghorā yāmyaloke śrūyante dvijasattama .
tvatprasādena te somyāstīrthasyāsya prabhāvataḥ .. 92.28 ..
6.3.d:
एते घोरा याम्यलोके श्रूयन्ते द्विजसत्तम .
त्वत्प्रसादेन ते सोम्यास्तीर्थस्यास्य प्रभावतः .. 92.28 ..
6.3.m: these dreadful things are heard of in the realm of Yama, O best of twice-born. / By your grace may they become gentle through the power of this sacred ford.

6.3.s:
dānasyāsya prabhāveṇa yamarājaprasādataḥ .
narake'haṃ na yāsyāmi dvija janmani janmani .. 92.29 ..
6.3.d:
दानस्यास्य प्रभावेण यमराजप्रसादतः .
नरकेऽहं न यास्यामि द्विज जन्मनि जन्मनि .. 92.29 ..
6.3.m: By the power of this gift, by the grace of King Yama, / may I not go to hell, O twice-born, birth after birth.’

6.3.s:
yamahāsyasya cākhyānamidaṃ śṛṇvanti ye narāḥ .
te'pi pāpavinirmuktā na paśyanti yamālayam .. 92.30 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe yamahāsyatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma dvinavatitamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 93
6.3.d:
यमहास्यस्य चाख्यानमिदं शृण्वन्ति ये नराः .
तेऽपि पापविनिर्मुक्ता न पश्यन्ति यमालयम् .. 92.30 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे यमहास्यतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम द्विनवतितमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 93
6.3.m:
Those men who listen to this narrative of Yamahāsya / are also freed from sin and do not behold the abode of Yama.
Thus ends the ninety-second chapter, titled ‘Description of the Greatness of Yamahāsyatīrtha’, in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses, the glorious Skandapurāṇa.
Chapter 93

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gacchettu rājendra kalhoḍītīrthamuttamam .
vikhyātaṃ bhārate loke gaṅgāyāḥ pāpanāśanam .. 93.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेत्तु राजेन्द्र कल्होडीतीर्थमुत्तमम् .
विख्यातं भारते लोके गङ्गायाः पापनाशनम् .. 93.1 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then, O best of kings, one should go to the excellent Kalhoḍītīrtha, / famed in the world of Bhārata, which destroys the sin of Gaṅgā,

6.3.s:
durlabhaṃ manujaiḥ pārtha revātaṭasamāśritam .
prāṇināṃ pāpanāśāya ūṣaraṃ puṣkaraṃ tathā .. 93.2 ..
6.3.d:
दुर्लभं मनुजैः पार्थ रेवातटसमाश्रितम् .
प्राणिनां पापनाशाय ऊषरं पुष्करं तथा .. 93.2 ..
6.3.m: difficult to be reached by men, O Pārtha, situated on the bank of the Revā, / for the destruction of the sins of living beings, just like the saline soil or Puṣkara.

6.3.s:
tattu tīrthamidaṃ puṇyamityevaṃ śūlino vacaḥ .
jāhnavī paśurūpeṇa tatra snānārthamāgatā .. 93.3 ..
6.3.d:
तत्तु तीर्थमिदं पुण्यमित्येवं शूलिनो वचः .
जाह्नवी पशुरूपेण तत्र स्नानार्थमागता .. 93.3 ..
6.3.m: "That is this sacred ford," such was the word of Śiva. / The river Gaṅgā came there in the form of an animal for the sake of bathing;

6.3.s:
atastadviśrutaṃ loke kalhoḍītīrthamuttamam .
trirātraṃ kārayettatra pūrṇimāyāṃ yudhiṣṭhira .. 93.4 ..
6.3.d:
अतस्तद्विश्रुतं लोके कल्होडीतीर्थमुत्तमम् .
त्रिरात्रं कारयेत्तत्र पूर्णिमायां युधिष्ठिर .. 93.4 ..
6.3.m: therefore, it is renowned in the world as the excellent Kalhoḍītīrtha. / One should observe a fast of three nights there on the full moon, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

6.3.s:
rajastamastathā krodhaṃ dambhaṃ mātsaryameva ca .
etāṃstyajati yaḥ pārtha tenāptaṃ mokṣajaṃ phalam .. 93.5 ..
6.3.d:
रजस्तमस्तथा क्रोधं दम्भं मात्सर्यमेव च .
एतांस्त्यजति यः पार्थ तेनाप्तं मोक्षजं फलम् .. 93.5 ..
6.3.m: Passion, darkness, anger, hypocrisy, and malice— / whoever abandons these, O Pārtha, by him the fruit born of liberation is attained.

6.3.s:
payasā snāpayeddevaṃ trisandhyaṃ ca tryahaṃ tathā .
payo gosambhavaṃ sadyaḥ savatsā jīvaputriṇī .. 93.6 ..
6.3.d:
पयसा स्नापयेद्देवं त्रिसन्ध्यं च त्र्यहं तथा .
पयो गोसम्भवं सद्यः सवत्सा जीवपुत्रिणी .. 93.6 ..
6.3.m: One should bathe the god with milk at the three junctures of the day, and thus for three days— / fresh milk obtained from a cow that has her calf and whose offspring is alive.

6.3.s:
kṛtvā tattāmraje pātre kṣaudreṇa caiva yojite .
oṃ namaḥ śrīśivāyeti snānaṃ devasya kārayet .. 93.7 ..
6.3.d:
कृत्वा तत्ताम्रजे पात्रे क्षौद्रेण चैव योजिते .
ओं नमः श्रीशिवायेति स्नानं देवस्य कारयेत् .. 93.7 ..
6.3.m: Placing it in a copper vessel mixed with honey, / one should bathe the god with the mantra: 'Om, salutations to Śrī Śiva!'

6.3.s:
sa yāti tridaśasthānaṃ nākastrībhiḥ samāvṛtaḥ .
yastatra vidhivatsnātvā dānaṃ preteṣu yacchati .. 93.8 ..
6.3.d:
स याति त्रिदशस्थानं नाकस्त्रीभिः समावृतः .
यस्तत्र विधिवत्स्नात्वा दानं प्रेतेषु यच्छति .. 93.8 ..
6.3.m: He goes to the abode of the gods, surrounded by celestial women, / who, having bathed there according to rule, gives gifts on behalf of the deceased.

6.3.s:
śuklāṃ gāṃ dāpayettatra prīyatāṃ me pitāmahāḥ .
brāhmaṇe śaucasampanne svadāranirate sadā .. 93.9 ..
6.3.d:
शुक्लां गां दापयेत्तत्र प्रीयतां मे पितामहाः .
ब्राह्मणे शौचसम्पन्ने स्वदारनिरते सदा .. 93.9 ..
6.3.m: One should give a white cow there, saying, 'May my ancestors be pleased,' / to a brahmin endowed with purity and always devoted to his own wife,

6.3.s:
savatsāṃ vastrasaṃyuktāṃ hiraṇyopari saṃsthitām .
sattvayukto dadadrājañchāmbhavaṃ lokamāpnuyāt .. 93.10 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe kalhoḍītīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma trinavatitamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 94
6.3.d:
सवत्सां वस्त्रसंयुक्तां हिरण्योपरि संस्थिताम् .
सत्त्वयुक्तो ददद्राजञ्छाम्भवं लोकमाप्नुयात् .. 93.10 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे कल्होडीतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम त्रिनवतितमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 94
6.3.m:
a cow with her calf, adorned with cloth, standing upon gold. / Giving it with pure intent, O king, he attains the world of Śambhu.
Thus ends the ninety-third chapter, entitled 'Description of the Māhātmya of Kalhoḍītīrtha', in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 94

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tasyaivānantaraṃ rājannanditīrthaṃ vrajecchubham .
sarvapāpaharaṃ puṃsāṃ nandinā nirmitaṃ purā .. 94.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
तस्यैवानन्तरं राजन्नन्दितीर्थं व्रजेच्छुभम् .
सर्वपापहरं पुंसां नन्दिना निर्मितं पुरा .. 94.1 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Immediately after that, O king, one should go to the auspicious Nanditīrtha, / which removes all sins of men and was created by Nandin of old,

6.3.s:
pāpaughahatajantūnāṃ mokṣadaṃ narmadātaṭe .
ahorātroṣito bhūtvā nandināthe yudhiṣṭhira .. 94.2 ..
6.3.d:
पापौघहतजन्तूनां मोक्षदं नर्मदातटे .
अहोरात्रोषितो भूत्वा नन्दिनाथे युधिष्ठिर .. 94.2 ..
6.3.m: bestowing liberation on the bank of the Narmadā to creatures stricken by a flood of sins. / Having fasted for a day and night at Nandinātha, O Yudhiṣṭhira,

6.3.s:
pañcopacārapūjāyāmarcayennandikeśvaram .
ratnāni caiva viprebhyo yo dadyāddharmanandana .. 94.3 ..
6.3.d:
पञ्चोपचारपूजायामर्चयेन्नन्दिकेश्वरम् .
रत्नानि चैव विप्रेभ्यो यो दद्याद्धर्मनन्दन .. 94.3 ..
6.3.m: one should worship Nandikeśvara with a fivefold offering of worship. / And whoever gives jewels to brahmins, O son of Dharma,

6.3.s:
sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ yatra vāsaḥ pinākinaḥ .
sarvasaukhyasamāyukto'psarobhiḥ saha modate .. 94.4 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe nandikeśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma caturnavatitamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 95
6.3.d:
स याति परमं स्थानं यत्र वासः पिनाकिनः .
सर्वसौख्यसमायुक्तोऽप्सरोभिः सह मोदते .. 94.4 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे नन्दिकेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम चतुर्नवतितमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 95
6.3.m:
goes to the supreme abode where the wielder of the Pināka dwells; / endowed with all comforts, he rejoices together with the apsarases.
Thus ends the ninety-fourth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Māhātmya of Nandikeśvaratīrtha', in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 95

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gacchettu rājendra badaryāśramamuttamam .
sarvatīrthavaraṃ puṇyaṃ kathitaṃ śaṃbhunā purā .. 95.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेत्तु राजेन्द्र बदर्याश्रममुत्तमम् .
सर्वतीर्थवरं पुण्यं कथितं शंभुना पुरा .. 95.1 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then one should go, O best of kings, to the excellent hermitage of Badarī, / the best of all sacred fords, auspicious, spoken of formerly by Śambhu,

6.3.s:
yaścaiṣa bhāratasyārthe tatra siddhaḥ kirīṭabhṛt .
bhrātā te phālguno nāma viddhyenaṃ naradaivatam .. 95.2 ..
6.3.d:
यश्चैष भारतस्यार्थे तत्र सिद्धः किरीटभृत् .
भ्राता ते फाल्गुनो नाम विद्ध्येनं नरदैवतम् .. 95.2 ..
6.3.m: and where that crowned one achieved perfection for the sake of the Bhārata war— / know your brother named Phālguna to be the deity Nara.

6.3.s:
naranārāyaṇau dvau tāvāgatau narmadātaṭe .
jñānaṃ tasyaiva yo rājanbhaktimānvai janārdane .. 95.3 ..
6.3.d:
नरनारायणौ द्वौ तावागतौ नर्मदातटे .
ज्ञानं तस्यैव यो राजन्भक्तिमान्वै जनार्दने .. 95.3 ..
6.3.m: Those two, Nara and Nārāyaṇa, came to the bank of the Narmadā. / Knowledge belongs to him alone, O king, who is devoted to Janārdana,

6.3.s:
samaṃ paśyati sarveṣu sthāvareṣu careṣu ca .
brāhmaṇaṃ śvapacaṃ caiva tatra prīto janārdanaḥ .. 95.4 ..
6.3.d:
समं पश्यति सर्वेषु स्थावरेषु चरेषु च .
ब्राह्मणं श्वपचं चैव तत्र प्रीतो जनार्दनः .. 95.4 ..
6.3.m: who looks with equality upon all stationary and moving beings, / upon a brahmin and an outcaste; with him Janārdana is pleased.

6.3.s:
aikātmyaṃ paśya kaunteya mayi cātmani nāntaram .
naranārāyaṇābhyāṃ hi kṛtaṃ badarikāśramam .. 95.5 ..
6.3.d:
ऐकात्म्यं पश्य कौन्तेय मयि चात्मनि नान्तरम् .
नरनारायणाभ्यां हि कृतं बदरिकाश्रमम् .. 95.5 ..
6.3.m: “Behold oneness of self, O son of Kuntī; there is no difference between me and the soul. / Indeed, Badarikāśrama was founded by Nara and Nārāyaṇa. 95.5

6.3.s:
sthāpitaḥ śaṅkarastatra lokānugrahakāraṇāt .
trimūrtisthāpitaṃ liṅgaṃ svargamārgānumuktidam .. 95.6 ..
6.3.d:
स्थापितः शङ्करस्तत्र लोकानुग्रहकारणात् .
त्रिमूर्तिस्थापितं लिङ्गं स्वर्गमार्गानुमुक्तिदम् .. 95.6 ..
6.3.m: Śaṃkara was established there for the sake of bestowing grace upon the world. / The liṅga established by the three deities grants passage to heaven followed by liberation. 95.6

6.3.s:
tatra gatvā śucirbhūtvā hyekarātropavāsakṛt .
rajastamastathā tyaktvā sāttvikaṃ bhāvamāśrayet .. 95.7 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र गत्वा शुचिर्भूत्वा ह्येकरात्रोपवासकृत् .
रजस्तमस्तथा त्यक्त्वा सात्त्विकं भावमाश्रयेत् .. 95.7 ..
6.3.m: Having gone there and become pure, having observed a fast for one night, / having cast aside passion and darkness, one should resort to a state of purity. 95.7

6.3.s:
rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kṛtvā madhumāsāṣṭamīdine .
athavā ca caturdaśyāmubhau pakṣau ca kārayet .. 95.8 ..
6.3.d:
रात्रौ जागरणं कृत्वा मधुमासाष्टमीदिने .
अथवा च चतुर्दश्यामुभौ पक्षौ च कारयेत् .. 95.8 ..
6.3.m: Having kept a night-vigil on the eighth day of the spring month, / or on the fourteenth, one should perform [the rites] during both fortnights. 95.8

6.3.s:
āśvinasya viśeṣeṇa kathitaṃ tava pāṇḍava .
snāpayetparayā bhaktyā kṣīreṇa madhunā saha .. 95.9 ..
6.3.d:
आश्विनस्य विशेषेण कथितं तव पाण्डव .
स्नापयेत्परया भक्त्या क्षीरेण मधुना सह .. 95.9 ..
6.3.m: Especially during [the month of] Āśvina, O son of Pāṇḍu, [this] has been told to you. / With supreme devotion, one should bathe [the liṅga] with milk together with honey, 95.9

6.3.s:
dadhnā śarkarayā yuktaṃ ghṛtena samalaṃkṛtam .
pañcāmṛtamidaṃ puṇyaṃ snāpayedvṛṣabhadhvajam .. 95.10 ..
6.3.d:
दध्ना शर्करया युक्तं घृतेन समलंकृतम् .
पञ्चामृतमिदं पुण्यं स्नापयेद्वृषभध्वजम् .. 95.10 ..
6.3.m: combined with curd and sugar, adorned with clarified butter: / with this sacred five-nectar mixture one should bathe the bull-bannered [god]. 95.10

6.3.s:
snāpyamānaṃ śivaṃ bhaktyā vīkṣate yo vimatsaraḥ .
tasya vāsaḥ śivopānte śakraloke na saṃśayaḥ .. 95.11 ..
6.3.d:
स्नाप्यमानं शिवं भक्त्या वीक्षते यो विमत्सरः .
तस्य वासः शिवोपान्ते शक्रलोके न संशयः .. 95.11 ..
6.3.m: He who, free from jealousy, gazes with devotion upon Śiva being bathed, / his dwelling is near Śiva in Indra's world—there is no doubt. 95.11

6.3.s:
śāṭhyenāpi namaskāraḥ prayuktaḥ śūlapāṇine .
saṃsāramūlabaddhānāmudveṣṭanakaro hi yaḥ .. 95.12 ..
6.3.d:
शाठ्येनापि नमस्कारः प्रयुक्तः शूलपाणिने .
संसारमूलबद्धानामुद्वेष्टनकरो हि यः .. 95.12 ..
6.3.m: Even when offered deceitfully, a salutation to the trident-handed [god] / indeed unties the knots of those bound by the root of cyclic existence. 95.12

6.3.s:
tenādhītaṃ śrutaṃ tena tena sarvamanuṣṭhitam .
yenauṃ namaḥ śivāyeti mantrābhyāsaḥ sthirīkṛtaḥ .. 95.13 ..
6.3.d:
तेनाधीतं श्रुतं तेन तेन सर्वमनुष्ठितम् .
येनौं नमः शिवायेति मन्त्राभ्यासः स्थिरीकृतः .. 95.13 ..
6.3.m: By him has been studied, by him heard, by him all has been practiced, / by whom the repetition of the mantra ‘Om, obeisance to Śiva’ has been made steadfast. 95.13

6.3.s:
yaḥ punaḥ snāpayedbhaktyā ekabhakto jitendriyaḥ .
tasyāpi yatphalaṃ pārtha vakṣye talleśatastava .. 95.14 ..
6.3.d:
यः पुनः स्नापयेद्भक्त्या एकभक्तो जितेन्द्रियः .
तस्यापि यत्फलं पार्थ वक्ष्ये तल्लेशतस्तव .. 95.14 ..
6.3.m: Moreover, he who bathes [the liṅga] with devotion, single-minded and with senses subdued— / the fruit of his act too, O son of Pṛthā, I shall describe to you in brief. 95.14

6.3.s:
pīḍito vṛddhabhāvena tava bhaktyā vadāmyaham .
te yānti paramaṃ sthānaṃ bhittvā bhāskaramaṇḍalam .. 95.15 ..
6.3.d:
पीडितो वृद्धभावेन तव भक्त्या वदाम्यहम् .
ते यान्ति परमं स्थानं भित्त्वा भास्करमण्डलम् .. 95.15 ..
6.3.m: Though afflicted by old age, out of devotion to you I speak: / They pierce the solar orb and go to the supreme abode. 95.15

6.3.s:
saṃsāre sarvasaukhyānāṃ nilayāste bhavanti ca .
āścaryaṃ jñātivargāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ nilayāstu te .. 95.16 ..
6.3.d:
संसारे सर्वसौख्यानां निलयास्ते भवन्ति च .
आश्चर्यं ज्ञातिवर्गाणां धर्माणां निलयास्तु ते .. 95.16 ..
6.3.m: And in cyclic existence they become the abode of all pleasures; / a marvel to their circle of kinsmen, they are indeed the dwellings of virtues. 95.16

6.3.s:
sampannāḥ sarvakāmaiste pṛthivyāṃ pṛthivīpate .
śrāddhaṃ tatraiva yaḥ kuryānnarmadodakamiśritam .. 95.17 ..
6.3.d:
सम्पन्नाः सर्वकामैस्ते पृथिव्यां पृथिवीपते .
श्राद्धं तत्रैव यः कुर्यान्नर्मदोदकमिश्रितम् .. 95.17 ..
6.3.m: Furnished with all desires, they [prosper] on the earth, O lord of the earth. / Whoever performs a śrāddha right there with water mingled from the Narmadā, 95.17

6.3.s:
yogyaiśca brāhmaṇairrājankulīnairvedapāragaiḥ .
surūpaiśca suśīlaiśca svadāranirataiḥ śubhaiḥ .. 95.18 ..
6.3.d:
योग्यैश्च ब्राह्मणैर्राजन्कुलीनैर्वेदपारगैः .
सुरूपैश्च सुशीलैश्च स्वदारनिरतैः शुभैः .. 95.18 ..
6.3.m: with suitable brahmins, O king, well-born, masters of the Vedas, / handsome, of good character, devoted to their own wives, auspicious, 95.18

6.3.s:
āryadeśaprasūtaiśca ślakṣṇaiścaiva surūpibhiḥ .
kārayetpiṇḍadānaṃ vai bhāskare kutapasthite .. 95.19 ..
6.3.d:
आर्यदेशप्रसूतैश्च श्लक्ष्णैश्चैव सुरूपिभिः .
कारयेत्पिण्डदानं वै भास्करे कुतपस्थिते .. 95.19 ..
6.3.m: born in the Āryan land, refined, and shapely, / should have the offering of rice-balls made when the sun reaches the kutapa period. 95.19

6.3.s:
pitḥṇāṃ paramaṃ lokaṃ yadīccheddharmanandana .
varjayettānprayatnena kāṇānduṣṭāṃśca dāmbhikān .. 95.20 ..
6.3.d:
पित्ःणां परमं लोकं यदीच्छेद्धर्मनन्दन .
वर्जयेत्तान्प्रयत्नेन काणान्दुष्टांश्च दाम्भिकान् .. 95.20 ..
6.3.m: If he desires the supreme world of the ancestors, O joy of Dharma, / he must carefully avoid those who are one-eyed, wicked, and hypocritical. 95.20

6.3.s:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena yogyaṃ vipraṃ samāśrayet .
narakānmocayetpretānkumbhīpākapurogamān .. 95.21 ..
6.3.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन योग्यं विप्रं समाश्रयेत् .
नरकान्मोचयेत्प्रेतान्कुम्भीपाकपुरोगमान् .. 95.21 ..
6.3.m: Therefore, by every effort, one should resort to a worthy brahmin. / One delivers departed spirits from hell, beginning with Kumbhīpāka; 95.21

6.3.s:
mokṣo bhavati sarveṣāṃ pitḥṇāṃ nṛpanandana .
viprebhyaḥ kāñcanaṃ dadyātprīyatāṃ me pitāmahaḥ .. 95.22 ..
6.3.d:
मोक्षो भवति सर्वेषां पित्ःणां नृपनन्दन .
विप्रेभ्यः काञ्चनं दद्यात्प्रीयतां मे पितामहः .. 95.22 ..
6.3.m: liberation comes to all ancestors, O prince. / One should give gold to the brahmins, [praying:] ‘May my grandfather be pleased!’ 95.22

6.3.s:
annaṃ ca dāpayettatra bhaktyā vastraṃ ca bhārata .
gāṃ vṛṣaṃ medinīṃ dadyācchatraṃ śastaṃ nṛpottama .. 95.23 ..
6.3.d:
अन्नं च दापयेत्तत्र भक्त्या वस्त्रं च भारत .
गां वृषं मेदिनीं दद्याच्छत्रं शस्तं नृपोत्तम .. 95.23 ..
6.3.m: And there one should devoutly give food, O Bhārata, and clothing; / one should give a cow, a bull, land, an umbrella, [and] a sword, O best of kings. 95.23

6.3.s:
sa pumānsvargamāpnoti ityevaṃ śaṅkaro'bravīt .
prāṇatyāgaṃ tu yaḥ kuryācchikhinā salilena vā .. 95.24 ..
6.3.d:
स पुमान्स्वर्गमाप्नोति इत्येवं शङ्करोऽब्रवीत् .
प्राणत्यागं तु यः कुर्याच्छिखिना सलिलेन वा .. 95.24 ..
6.3.m: That man attains heaven—thus indeed Śaṅkara declared. / But he who abandons his life by fire or by water, 95.24

6.3.s:
anāśakena vā bhūyaḥ sa gacchecchivamandiram .
naranārāyaṇītīre devadroṇyāṃ ca yo nṛpa .. 95.25 ..
6.3.d:
अनाशकेन वा भूयः स गच्छेच्छिवमन्दिरम् .
नरनारायणीतीरे देवद्रोण्यां च यो नृप .. 95.25 ..
6.3.m: or furthermore by fasting, goes to Śiva's temple. / O king, he who [perishes] on the bank of the Naranārāyaṇī or in the Devadroṇī, 95.25

6.3.s:
sa vasedīśvarasyāgre yāvadindrāścaturdaśa .
punaḥ svargāccyutaḥ so'pi rājā bhavati vīryavān .. 95.26 ..
6.3.d:
स वसेदीश्वरस्याग्रे यावदिन्द्राश्चतुर्दश .
पुनः स्वर्गाच्च्युतः सोऽपि राजा भवति वीर्यवान् .. 95.26 ..
6.3.m: shall reside before Īśvara for as long as fourteen Indras [endure]. / Fallen again from heaven, he becomes a valiant king, 95.26

6.3.s:
sarvaiśvaryaguṇairyuktaḥ prajāpālanatatparaḥ .
tataḥ smarati tattīrthaṃ punarevāgamiṣyati .. 95.27 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe nārāyaṇītīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma pañcanavatitamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 96
6.3.d:
सर्वैश्वर्यगुणैर्युक्तः प्रजापालनतत्परः .
ततः स्मरति तत्तीर्थं पुनरेवागमिष्यति .. 95.27 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे नारायणीतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम पञ्चनवतितमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 96
6.3.m:
endowed with all royal virtues and powers, intent on protecting the subjects. / Then he remembers that sacred ford and will come there once again.” 95.27
Thus ends the ninety-fifth chapter, titled ‘Description of the Māhātmya of the Nārāyaṇī Tīrtha,’ in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth Avantī section in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 96

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gacchettu rājendra tīrthaṃ koṭīśvaraṃ param .
ṛṣikoṭiḥ samāyātā yatra vai kurunandana .. 96.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेत्तु राजेन्द्र तीर्थं कोटीश्वरं परम् .
ऋषिकोटिः समायाता यत्र वै कुरुनन्दन .. 96.1 ..
6.3.m: Glorious Mārkaṇḍeya said: / “Then one should proceed, O king of kings, to the supreme sacred ford Koṭīśvara, / where, O joy of the Kurus, a crore of seers arrived, 96.1

6.3.s:
kṛṣṇadvaipāyanasyaiva kṣemārthaṃ munipuṃgavāḥ .
mantrayitvā dvijaiḥ sarvairvedamaṅgalapāṭhakaiḥ .. 96.2 ..
6.3.d:
कृष्णद्वैपायनस्यैव क्षेमार्थं मुनिपुंगवाः .
मन्त्रयित्वा द्विजैः सर्वैर्वेदमङ्गलपाठकैः .. 96.2 ..
6.3.m: for the welfare of Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana himself, O best of sages. / Having conferred with all the twice-born who recite the auspicious Vedic hymns, 96.2

6.3.s:
sthāpitaḥ śaṅkarastatra kāraṇaṃ bandhanāśanam .
saṃsāracchedakaraṇaṃ prāṇināmārtināśanam .. 96.3 ..
6.3.d:
स्थापितः शङ्करस्तत्र कारणं बन्धनाशनम् .
संसारच्छेदकरणं प्राणिनामार्तिनाशनम् .. 96.3 ..
6.3.m: Śaṅkara was established there as the primal cause, destroyer of bondage, / the severer of cyclic existence, destroyer of the afflictions of living beings. 96.3

6.3.s:
koṭīśvaramiti proktaṃ pṛthivyāṃ nṛpanandana .
snāpayettaṃ tu yo bhaktyā pūrṇimāyāṃ nṛpottama .. 96.4 ..
6.3.d:
कोटीश्वरमिति प्रोक्तं पृथिव्यां नृपनन्दन .
स्नापयेत्तं तु यो भक्त्या पूर्णिमायां नृपोत्तम .. 96.4 ..
6.3.m: It is called ‘Koṭīśvara’ on earth, O prince. / Whoever bathes him with devotion on a full-moon day, O best of kings, 96.4

6.3.s:
pitḥṇāṃ tarpaṇaṃ kṛtvā piṇḍadānaṃ yathāvidhi .
śrāvaṇasya viśeṣeṇa pūrṇimāyāṃ yudhiṣṭhira .. 96.5 ..
6.3.d:
पित्ःणां तर्पणं कृत्वा पिण्डदानं यथाविधि .
श्रावणस्य विशेषेण पूर्णिमायां युधिष्ठिर .. 96.5 ..
6.3.m: having offered libations to the ancestors and the offering of rice-balls according to rule, / especially on the full-moon day of Śrāvaṇa, O Yudhiṣṭhira, 96.5

6.3.s:
pitḥṇāmakṣayā tṛptiryāvadābhūtasamplavam .
pitḥṇāṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ revātaṭasamāśritam .
mokṣadaṃ sarvajantūnāṃ nirmitaṃ munisattamaiḥ .. 96.6 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe koṭīśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma ṣaṇṇavatitamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 97
6.3.d:
पित्ःणामक्षया तृप्तिर्यावदाभूतसम्प्लवम् .
पित्ःणां परमं गुह्यं रेवातटसमाश्रितम् .
मोक्षदं सर्वजन्तूनां निर्मितं मुनिसत्तमैः .. 96.6 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे कोटीश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम षण्णवतितमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 97
6.3.m:
the satisfaction of his ancestors is inexhaustible until the dissolution of all beings. / Established on the bank of the Revā, supreme secret of the ancestors, / it grants liberation to all living beings, constructed by the best of sages.” 96.6
Thus ends the ninety-sixth chapter, titled ‘Description of the Māhātmya of the Koṭīśvara Tīrtha,’ in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth Avantī section in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 97

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gacchenmahīpāla vyāsatīrthamanuttamam .
durlabhaṃ manujaiḥ puṇyamantarikṣe vyavasthitam .. 97.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेन्महीपाल व्यासतीर्थमनुत्तमम् .
दुर्लभं मनुजैः पुण्यमन्तरिक्षे व्यवस्थितम् .. 97.1 ..
6.3.m: Glorious Mārkaṇḍeya said: / “Then, O protector of the earth, one should proceed to the peerless Vyāsatīrtha, / sacred, hard to attain for human beings, situated in the intermediate space.” 97.1

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
kasmādvai vyāsatīrthaṃ tadantarikṣe vyavasthitam .
etadākhyāhi saṃkṣepāttyaja granthasya vistaram .. 97.2 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
कस्माद्वै व्यासतीर्थं तदन्तरिक्षे व्यवस्थितम् .
एतदाख्याहि संक्षेपात्त्यज ग्रन्थस्य विस्तरम् .. 97.2 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / “Why indeed is that Vyāsatīrtha situated in the intermediate space? / Tell me this concisely; avoid an expansive treatise.” 97.2

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
sādhu sādhu mahābāho dharmavānsādhuvatsala .
svakarmanirataḥ pārtha tīrthayātrākṛtādaraḥ .. 97.3 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
साधु साधु महाबाहो धर्मवान्साधुवत्सल .
स्वकर्मनिरतः पार्थ तीर्थयात्राकृतादरः .. 97.3 ..
6.3.m: Glorious Mārkaṇḍeya said: / “Well said, well said, O mighty-armed one, virtuous, affectionate to the righteous, / devoted to your own duty, O son of Pṛthā, full of reverence for pilgrimages to sacred fords! 97.3

6.3.s:
durlabhaṃ sarvajantūnāṃ vyāsatīrthaṃ nareśvara .
pīḍito vṛddhabhāvena akalpo'haṃ nṛpātmaja .. 97.4 ..
6.3.d:
दुर्लभं सर्वजन्तूनां व्यासतीर्थं नरेश्वर .
पीडितो वृद्धभावेन अकल्पोऽहं नृपात्मज .. 97.4 ..
6.3.m: Hard to attain for all creatures is Vyāsatīrtha, O lord of men. / Afflicted by old age, I am incapable, O prince; 97.4

6.3.s:
visaṃjño gatavittastu saṃjātaḥ smṛtivarjitaḥ .
guhyādguhyataraṃ tīrthaṃ nākhyātaṃ kasyacinmayā .. 97.5 ..
6.3.d:
विसंज्ञो गतवित्तस्तु संजातः स्मृतिवर्जितः .
गुह्याद्गुह्यतरं तीर्थं नाख्यातं कस्यचिन्मया .. 97.5 ..
6.3.m: confused in senses, deprived of faculties, and bereft of memory. / This sacred ford, more secret than the secret, has not been related to anyone by me. 97.5

6.3.s:
kalistatraiva rājendra na viśedvyāsasaṃśrayāt .
antarikṣe tu saṃjātaṃ revāyāśceṣṭitena tu .. 97.6 ..
6.3.d:
कलिस्तत्रैव राजेन्द्र न विशेद्व्याससंश्रयात् .
अन्तरिक्षे तु संजातं रेवायाश्चेष्टितेन तु .. 97.6 ..
6.3.m: The Kali age does not enter there, O king of kings, because it is the refuge of Vyāsa. / And it was brought forth in the intermediate space by the movement of the Revā. 97.6

6.3.s:
viriñcirnaiva śaknoti revāyā guṇakīrtanam .
kathaṃ jñāsyāmyahaṃ tāta revāmāhātmyamuttamam .. 97.7 ..
6.3.d:
विरिञ्चिर्नैव शक्नोति रेवाया गुणकीर्तनम् .
कथं ज्ञास्याम्यहं तात रेवामाहात्म्यमुत्तमम् .. 97.7 ..
6.3.m: Even Brahmā cannot proclaim the virtues of the Revā; / how shall I know, my dear one, the supreme māhātmya of the Revā? 97.7

6.3.s:
vyāsatīrthaṃ viśeṣeṇa lavamātraṃ bravīmyataḥ .
pratyakṣaḥ pratyayo yatra dṛśyate'dya kalau yuge .. 97.8 ..
6.3.d:
व्यासतीर्थं विशेषेण लवमात्रं ब्रवीम्यतः .
प्रत्यक्षः प्रत्ययो यत्र दृश्यतेऽद्य कलौ युगे .. 97.8 ..
6.3.m: Therefore, I shall tell only a mere particle of Vyāsatīrtha, / where a visible proof is seen even today in the Kali age: 97.8

6.3.s:
vihaṅgo gacchate naiva bhittvā śūlaṃ sudāruṇam .
tasyotpattiṃ samāsena kathayāmi nṛpātmaja .. 97.9 ..
6.3.d:
विहङ्गो गच्छते नैव भित्त्वा शूलं सुदारुणम् .
तस्योत्पत्तिं समासेन कथयामि नृपात्मज .. 97.9 ..
6.3.m: a bird never passes [across], piercing the frightful lance. / I will relate its origin in brief, O prince. 97.9

6.3.s:
āsītpūrvaṃ mahīpāla munirmānyaḥ parāśaraḥ .
tenātyugraṃ tapaścīrṇaṃ gaṅgāmbhasi mahāphalam .. 97.10 ..
6.3.d:
आसीत्पूर्वं महीपाल मुनिर्मान्यः पराशरः .
तेनात्युग्रं तपश्चीर्णं गङ्गाम्भसि महाफलम् .. 97.10 ..
6.3.m: Formerly, O king, there was the venerable sage Parāśara; / exceedingly fierce austerity bearing great fruit was performed by him in the waters of the Gaṅgā. 97.10

6.3.s:
prāṇāyāmena saṃtasthau praviṣṭo jāhnavījale .
pūrṇe dvādaśame varṣe niṣkrānto jalamadhyataḥ .. 97.11 ..
6.3.d:
प्राणायामेन संतस्थौ प्रविष्टो जाह्नवीजले .
पूर्णे द्वादशमे वर्षे निष्क्रान्तो जलमध्यतः .. 97.11 ..
6.3.m: Having entered the water of the Jāhnavī, he remained there practicing prāṇāyāma. / When the twelfth year was complete, he emerged from the midst of the water.

6.3.s:
bhikṣārthī saṃcaredgrāmaṃ nāvā yatraiva tiṣṭhati .
tatra tena parā dṛṣṭā bālā caiva manoharā .. 97.12 ..
6.3.d:
भिक्षार्थी संचरेद्ग्रामं नावा यत्रैव तिष्ठति .
तत्र तेन परा दृष्टा बाला चैव मनोहरा .. 97.12 ..
6.3.m: Seeking alms, he wandered to a village where a boat was stationed. / There he saw an exquisite and charming maiden.

6.3.s:
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā sa ca kāmārta uvāca madhuraṃ tadā .
māṃ nayasva paraṃ pāraṃ kāsi tvaṃ mṛgalocane .. 97.13 ..
6.3.d:
तां दृष्ट्वा स च कामार्त उवाच मधुरं तदा .
मां नयस्व परं पारं कासि त्वं मृगलोचने .. 97.13 ..
6.3.m: Seeing her, stricken with desire, he spoke sweetly then: / 'Take me to the opposite bank. Who are you, fawn-eyed one,

6.3.s:
nāvārūḍhe nadītīre mama cittapramāthini .
evamuktā tu sā tena praṇamya ṛṣipuṃgavam .. 97.14 ..
6.3.d:
नावारूढे नदीतीरे मम चित्तप्रमाथिनि .
एवमुक्ता तु सा तेन प्रणम्य ऋषिपुंगवम् .. 97.14 ..
6.3.m: standing on the riverbank aboard a boat, agitating my heart?' / Thus addressed by him, she bowed down to the eminent seer

6.3.s:
kathayāmāsa cātmānaṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ kāmamohitam .
kaivartānāṃ gṛhe dāsī kanyāhaṃ dvijasattama .. 97.15 ..
6.3.d:
कथयामास चात्मानं दृष्ट्वा तं काममोहितम् .
कैवर्तानां गृहे दासी कन्याहं द्विजसत्तम .. 97.15 ..
6.3.m: and, seeing him infatuated with desire, spoke about herself: / 'I am a maidservant, a maiden in the house of fishermen, O best of brahmins.

6.3.s:
nāvāsaṃrakṣaṇārthāya ādiṣṭā svāminā vibho .
mayā vijñāpitaṃ vṛttamaśeṣaṃ jñātumarhasi .. 97.16 ..
6.3.d:
नावासंरक्षणार्थाय आदिष्टा स्वामिना विभो .
मया विज्ञापितं वृत्तमशेषं ज्ञातुमर्हसि .. 97.16 ..
6.3.m: I was instructed by my master to watch over the boat, O lord. / I have related everything; please understand my full circumstances.'

6.3.s: evamuktastayā so'tha kṣaṇaṃ dhyātvābravīdidam .. 97.17 ..
6.3.d: एवमुक्तस्तया सोऽथ क्षणं ध्यात्वाब्रवीदिदम् .. 97.17 ..
6.3.m: Thus addressed by her, he meditated for a moment and then said this:

6.3.s:
parāśara uvāca -
ahaṃ jñānabalādbhadre tava jānāmi sambhavam .
kaivartaputrikā na tvaṃ rājakanyāsi sundari .. 97.18 ..
6.3.d:
पराशर उवाच -
अहं ज्ञानबलाद्भद्रे तव जानामि सम्भवम् .
कैवर्तपुत्रिका न त्वं राजकन्यासि सुन्दरि .. 97.18 ..
6.3.m: Parāśara said: / 'By the power of knowledge, auspicious one, I know your origin. / You are not the daughter of a fisherman; you are a king’s daughter, beautiful lady.'

6.3.s:
kanyovāca -
kaḥ pitā kathyatāṃ brahmankasyā vā hyudarodbhavā .
kasminvaṃśe prasūtāhaṃ kaivartatanayā katham .. 97.19 ..
6.3.d:
कन्योवाच -
कः पिता कथ्यतां ब्रह्मन्कस्या वा ह्युदरोद्भवा .
कस्मिन्वंशे प्रसूताहं कैवर्ततनया कथम् .. 97.19 ..
6.3.m: The maiden said: / 'Tell me, O holy one, who is my father, or from whose womb was I born? / In what lineage was I born, and how am I the daughter of a fisherman?'

6.3.s:
parāśara uvāca -
kathayāmi samastaṃ yattvayā pṛṣṭamaśeṣataḥ .
vasurnāmeti bhūpālaḥ somavaṃśavibhūṣaṇaḥ .. 97.20 ..
6.3.d:
पराशर उवाच -
कथयामि समस्तं यत्त्वया पृष्टमशेषतः .
वसुर्नामेति भूपालः सोमवंशविभूषणः .. 97.20 ..
6.3.m: Parāśara said: / 'I shall tell you everything in full, exactly as you have asked. / There was a king named Vasu, an ornament of the lunar dynasty,

6.3.s:
jambūdvīpādhipo bhadre śatrūṇāṃ bhayavardhanaḥ .
śatāni sapta bhāryāṇāṃ putrāṇāṃ ca daśaiva tu .. 97.21 ..
6.3.d:
जम्बूद्वीपाधिपो भद्रे शत्रूणां भयवर्धनः .
शतानि सप्त भार्याणां पुत्राणां च दशैव तु .. 97.21 ..
6.3.m: the ruler of Jambūdvīpa, auspicious one, who struck terror into enemies. / He had seven hundred wives and ten sons.

6.3.s:
dharmeṇa pālayellokānīśavatpūjyate sadā .
mlecchāstasyāvidheyāśca kṣīradvīpanivāsinaḥ .. 97.22 ..
6.3.d:
धर्मेण पालयेल्लोकानीशवत्पूज्यते सदा .
म्लेच्छास्तस्याविधेयाश्च क्षीरद्वीपनिवासिनः .. 97.22 ..
6.3.m: He protected the worlds according to dharma and was ever honored like the Lord. / The Mlecchas who dwelt on Kṣīradvīpa were insubordinate to him.

6.3.s:
teṣāmutsādanārthāya yayāvullaṅghya sāgaram .
saṃyuktaḥ putrabhṛtyaiśca pauruṣe mahati sthitaiḥ .. 97.23 ..
6.3.d:
तेषामुत्सादनार्थाय ययावुल्लङ्घ्य सागरम् .
