ततो गच्छेन्महीपाल तापेश्वरमनुत्तमम् .
यत्र सा हरिणी सिद्धा व्याधभीता नरेश्वर .. 141.1 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then one should go, O protector of the earth, to the unsurpassed Tāpeśvara, / where that doe, frightened by a hunter, attained perfection, O lord of men.

6.3.s:
jale prakṣipya gātrāṇi hyantarikṣaṃ gatā tu sā .
vyādho vismitacittastu tāṃ mṛgīmavalokya ca .. 141.2 ..
6.3.d:
जले प्रक्षिप्य गात्राणि ह्यन्तरिक्षं गता तु सा .
व्याधो विस्मितचित्तस्तु तां मृगीमवलोक्य च .. 141.2 ..
6.3.m: Having cast her limbs into the water, she went to the sky; / and the hunter, his mind filled with wonder having seen that female deer,

6.3.s:
vimucya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ prārebhe tapa uttamam .
divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu vyādhenācaritaṃ tapaḥ .. 141.3 ..
6.3.d:
विमुच्य सशरं चापं प्रारेभे तप उत्तमम् .
दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रं तु व्याधेनाचरितं तपः .. 141.3 ..
6.3.m: abandoned his bow along with the arrow and undertook supreme austerity. / Austerity was performed by the hunter for a thousand divine years.

6.3.s:
atīte tu tataḥ kāle parituṣṭo maheśvaraḥ .
varaṃ brūhi mahāvyādha yatte manasi rocate .. 141.4 ..
6.3.d:
अतीते तु ततः काले परितुष्टो महेश्वरः .
वरं ब्रूहि महाव्याध यत्ते मनसि रोचते .. 141.4 ..
6.3.m: Then, after time had passed, Maheśvara was pleased: / "Choose a boon, O great hunter, whatever pleases your mind."

6.3.s:
vyādha uvāca -
yadi tuṣṭo'si deveśa yadi deyo varo mama .
tava pārśve mahādeva vāso me pratidīyatām .. 141.5 ..
6.3.d:
व्याध उवाच -
यदि तुष्टोऽसि देवेश यदि देयो वरो मम .
तव पार्श्वे महादेव वासो मे प्रतिदीयताम् .. 141.5 ..
6.3.m: The hunter said: / "If you are pleased, O Lord of Gods, if a boon is to be given to me, / grant me residence by your side, O Mahādeva."

6.3.s:
īśvara uvāca -
evaṃ bhavatu te vyādha yastvayā kāṅkṣito varaḥ .
daivadevo mahādeva ityuktvāntaradhīyata .
gate cādarśanaṃ deve sthāpayitvā maheśvaram .. 141.6 ..
6.3.d:
ईश्वर उवाच -
एवं भवतु ते व्याध यस्त्वया काङ्क्षितो वरः .
दैवदेवो महादेव इत्युक्त्वान्तरधीयत .
गते चादर्शनं देवे स्थापयित्वा महेश्वरम् .. 141.6 ..
6.3.m: Īśvara said: / "Let it be so for you, O hunter, as the boon was desired by you." / Having spoken thus, Mahādeva, the God of gods, vanished. / When the god had disappeared, having established Maheśvara,

6.3.s:
pūjayitvā vidhānena gato vyādhastato divam .
tadāprabhṛti tattīrthaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam .. 141.7 ..
6.3.d:
पूजयित्वा विधानेन गतो व्याधस्ततो दिवम् .
तदाप्रभृति तत्तीर्थं त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम् .. 141.7 ..
6.3.m: and having worshipped according to the rule, the hunter went from there to heaven. / From that time on, that sacred ford has been renowned in the three worlds.

6.3.s:
vyādhānutāpasaṃjātaṃ tāpeśvaramiti śrutam .
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ snātvā sampūjayati śaṅkaram .. 141.8 ..
6.3.d:
व्याधानुतापसंजातं तापेश्वरमिति श्रुतम् .
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः स्नात्वा सम्पूजयति शङ्करम् .. 141.8 ..
6.3.m: Born from the hunter's repentance (anutāpa), it is heard of as Tāpeśvara. / Whoever bathes in that sacred ford and thoroughly worships Śaṅkara

6.3.s:
śivalokamavāpnoti māmuvāca maheśvaraḥ .
ye snātā narmadātoye tīrthe tāpeśvare narāḥ .. 141.9 ..
6.3.d:
शिवलोकमवाप्नोति मामुवाच महेश्वरः .
ये स्नाता नर्मदातोये तीर्थे तापेश्वरे नराः .. 141.9 ..
6.3.m: attains the world of Śiva; so Maheśvara said to me. / Those men who have bathed in the waters of the Narmadā at the sacred ford Tāpeśvara

6.3.s:
tāpatrayavimuktāste nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .
aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ tṛtīyāyāṃ viśeṣataḥ .. 141.10 ..
6.3.d:
तापत्रयविमुक्तास्ते नात्र कार्या विचारणा .
अष्टम्यां च चतुर्दश्यां तृतीयायां विशेषतः .. 141.10 ..
6.3.m: are freed from the threefold miseries; no doubt should be entertained here, / especially on the eighth, fourteenth, and third [tithis].

6.3.s:
snānaṃ samācarennityaṃ sarvapātakaśāntaye .. 141.11 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe tāpeśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmaikacatvāriṃśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 142
6.3.d:
स्नानं समाचरेन्नित्यं सर्वपातकशान्तये .. 141.11 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे तापेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामैकचत्वारिंशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 142
6.3.m:
one should regularly perform ritual ablution for the pacification of all sins. // 141.11
Thus ends the one hundred and forty-first chapter, entitled 'Description of the Māhātmya of Tāpeśvaratīrtha,' in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 142

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gacchenmahārāja rukmiṇītīrthamuttamam .
yatraiva snānamātreṇa rūpavānsubhago bhavet .. 142.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेन्महाराज रुक्मिणीतीर्थमुत्तमम् .
यत्रैव स्नानमात्रेण रूपवान्सुभगो भवेत् .. 142.1 ..
6.3.m:
The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Then, O great king, one should go to the excellent Rukmiṇītīrtha,
where by merely performing ritual ablution one becomes handsome and fortunate. // 142.1

6.3.s:
aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ tṛtīyāyāṃ viśeṣataḥ .
snānaṃ samācarettatra na ceha jāyate punaḥ .. 142.2 ..
6.3.d:
अष्टम्यां च चतुर्दश्यां तृतीयायां विशेषतः .
स्नानं समाचरेत्तत्र न चेह जायते पुनः .. 142.2 ..
6.3.m:
Especially on the eighth, fourteenth, and third days,
one should perform ritual ablution there and will not be born in this world again. // 142.2

6.3.s:
yaḥ snātvā rukmiṇītīrthe dānaṃ dadyāttu kāṃcanam .
tattīrthasya prabhāvena śokaṃ nāpnoti mānavaḥ .. 142.3 ..
6.3.d:
यः स्नात्वा रुक्मिणीतीर्थे दानं दद्यात्तु कांचनम् .
तत्तीर्थस्य प्रभावेन शोकं नाप्नोति मानवः .. 142.3 ..
6.3.m:
A person who, having bathed in the Rukmiṇītīrtha, gives a gift of gold,
does not encounter sorrow through the power of that sacred ford. // 142.3

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
tīrthasyāsya kathaṃ jāto mahimedṛṅmunīśvara .
rūpasaubhāgyadaṃ yena tīrthametadbravīhi me .. 142.4 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
तीर्थस्यास्य कथं जातो महिमेदृङ्मुनीश्वर .
रूपसौभाग्यदं येन तीर्थमेतद्ब्रवीहि मे .. 142.4 ..
6.3.m:
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
How did such greatness come to this sacred ford, O lord of sages,
by which this sacred ford grants beauty and good fortune? Tell me. // 142.4

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
kathayāmi yathāvṛttamitihāsaṃ purātanam .
kathitaṃ pūrvato vṛddhaiḥ pāramparyeṇa bhārata .. 142.5 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
कथयामि यथावृत्तमितिहासं पुरातनम् .
कथितं पूर्वतो वृद्धैः पारम्पर्येण भारत .. 142.5 ..
6.3.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
I shall narrate an ancient legend just as it happened,
which was told of old by the elders through succession, O Bhārata. // 142.5

6.3.s:
taṃ te'haṃ sampravakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣvaikāgramānasaḥ .
nagaraṃ kuṇḍinaṃ nāma bhīṣmakaḥ paripāti hi .. 142.6 ..
6.3.d:
तं तेऽहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणुष्वैकाग्रमानसः .
नगरं कुण्डिनं नाम भीष्मकः परिपाति हि .. 142.6 ..
6.3.m:
I shall relate that to you; listen with a single-minded heart.
There was a city named Kuṇḍina which Bhīṣmaka protected. // 142.6

6.3.s:
hastyaśvarathasampanno dhanāḍhyo'ti pratāpavān .
strīsahasrasya madhyasthaḥ kurute rājyamuttamam .. 142.7 ..
6.3.d:
हस्त्यश्वरथसम्पन्नो धनाढ्योऽति प्रतापवान् .
स्त्रीसहस्रस्य मध्यस्थः कुरुते राज्यमुत्तमम् .. 142.7 ..
6.3.m:
Supplied with elephants, horses, and chariots, wealthy, exceedingly glorious,
surrounded by a thousand women, he ruled an excellent kingdom. // 142.7

6.3.s:
tasya bhāryā mahādevī prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī .
tasyāmutpādayāmāsa putramekaṃ ca rukmakam .. 142.8 ..
6.3.d:
तस्य भार्या महादेवी प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसी .
तस्यामुत्पादयामास पुत्रमेकं च रुक्मकम् .. 142.8 ..
6.3.m:
His wife, the queen, was dearer [to him] than life itself.
Upon her he begot a single son, Rukma. // 142.8

6.3.s:
dvitīyā tanayā jajñe rukmiṇī nāma nāmataḥ .
tadāśarīriṇī vācā rājānaṃ tamuvāca ha .. 142.9 ..
6.3.d:
द्वितीया तनया जज्ञे रुक्मिणी नाम नामतः .
तदाशरीरिणी वाचा राजानं तमुवाच ह .. 142.9 ..
6.3.m:
A second child, a daughter named Rukmiṇī, was born.
Then a bodiless voice spoke indeed to that king: // 142.9

6.3.s:
caturbhujāya dātavyā kanyeyaṃ bhuvi bhīṣmaka .
evaṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā jaharṣa priyayā saha .. 142.10 ..
6.3.d:
चतुर्भुजाय दातव्या कन्येयं भुवि भीष्मक .
एवं तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा जहर्ष प्रियया सह .. 142.10 ..
6.3.m:
'This maiden must be given to a four-armed one on earth, O Bhīṣmaka!'
Hearing that speech, he rejoiced along with his beloved [wife]. // 142.10

6.3.s:
brāhmaṇaiḥ saha vidvadbhiḥ praviṣṭaḥ sūtikāgṛham .
svastikaṃ vācayitvāsyāścakre nāmeti rukmiṇī .. 142.11 ..
6.3.d:
ब्राह्मणैः सह विद्वद्भिः प्रविष्टः सूतिकागृहम् .
स्वस्तिकं वाचयित्वास्याश्चक्रे नामेति रुक्मिणी .. 142.11 ..
6.3.m:
Accompanied by learned brahmins, he entered the maternity room.
Having caused benedictions to be recited, he gave her the name Rukmiṇī. // 142.11

6.3.s:
yataḥ suvarṇatilako janmanā saha bhārata .
tataḥ sā rukmiṇīnāma brāhmaṇaiḥ kīrtitā tadā .. 142.12 ..
6.3.d:
यतः सुवर्णतिलको जन्मना सह भारत .
ततः सा रुक्मिणीनाम ब्राह्मणैः कीर्तिता तदा .. 142.12 ..
6.3.m:
Because she had a golden mark from her birth, O Bhārata,
she was then called Rukmiṇī by the brahmins. // 142.12

6.3.s:
tataḥ sā kālaparyāyādaṣṭavarṣā vyajāyata .
pūrvoktaṃ caiva tadvākyamaśarīriṇyudīritam .. 142.13 ..
6.3.d:
ततः सा कालपर्यायादष्टवर्षा व्यजायत .
पूर्वोक्तं चैव तद्वाक्यमशरीरिण्युदीरितम् .. 142.13 ..
6.3.m:
Then, in the course of time, she became eight years old.
And remembering repeatedly that speech previously uttered // 142.13

6.3.s:
smṛtvā smṛtvātha nṛpatiścintayāmāsa bhūpatiḥ .
kasmai deyā mayā bālā bhavitā kaścaturbhujaḥ .. 142.14 ..
6.3.d:
स्मृत्वा स्मृत्वाथ नृपतिश्चिन्तयामास भूपतिः .
कस्मै देया मया बाला भविता कश्चतुर्भुजः .. 142.14 ..
6.3.m:
by the bodiless voice, the king, the lord of the earth, reflected:
'To whom should this girl be given by me? Who will be the four-armed one?' // 142.14

6.3.s:
etasminnantare tāvadraivatātparvatottamāt .
mukhyaścedipatistatra damaghoṣaḥ samāgataḥ .. 142.15 ..
6.3.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तावद्रैवतात्पर्वतोत्तमात् .
मुख्यश्चेदिपतिस्तत्र दमघोषः समागतः .. 142.15 ..
6.3.m:
Meanwhile, Damaghoṣa, the prominent lord of Cedi,
arrived there from the excellent Raivata mountain. // 142.15

6.3.s:
praviṣṭo rājasadanaṃ yatra rājā sa bhīṣmakaḥ .
taṃ dṛṣṭvā cāgataṃ gehe pūjayāmāsa bhūpatiḥ .. 142.16 ..
6.3.d:
प्रविष्टो राजसदनं यत्र राजा स भीष्मकः .
तं दृष्ट्वा चागतं गेहे पूजयामास भूपतिः .. 142.16 ..
6.3.m:
He entered the royal palace where King Bhīṣmaka was.
Seeing him arrived at his home, the king honored him. // 142.16

6.3.s:
āsanaṃ vipulaṃ dattvā sabhāṃ gatvā niveśitaḥ .
kuśalaṃ tava rājendra damaghoṣa śriyāyuta .. 142.17 ..
6.3.d:
आसनं विपुलं दत्त्वा सभां गत्वा निवेशितः .
कुशलं तव राजेन्द्र दमघोष श्रियायुत .. 142.17 ..
6.3.m:
Having offered a spacious seat, he led him to the assembly and seated him:
'Is all well with you, O king of kings, O Damaghoṣa endowed with prosperity? // 142.17

6.3.s:
puṇyāhamadya saṃjātamahaṃ tvaddarśanotsukaḥ .
kanyā madīyā rājendra hyaṣṭavarṣā vyajāyata .. 142.18 ..
6.3.d:
पुण्याहमद्य संजातमहं त्वद्दर्शनोत्सुकः .
कन्या मदीया राजेन्द्र ह्यष्टवर्षा व्यजायत .. 142.18 ..
6.3.m:
Today has become an auspicious day; I was eager for the sight of you.
My daughter, O king of kings, has indeed reached eight years of age. // 142.18

6.3.s:
caturbhujāya dātavyā vāguvācāśarīriṇī .
bhīṣmakasya vacaḥ śrutvā damaghoṣo'bravīdidam .. 142.19 ..
6.3.d:
चतुर्भुजाय दातव्या वागुवाचाशरीरिणी .
भीष्मकस्य वचः श्रुत्वा दमघोषोऽब्रवीदिदम् .. 142.19 ..
6.3.m:
She is to be given to a four-armed one, said a bodiless voice.'
Hearing Bhīṣmaka's words, Damaghoṣa spoke this: // 142.19

6.3.s:
caturbhujo mama sutastriṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ .
tasyeyaṃ dīyatāṃ kanyā śiśupālasya bhīṣmaka .. 142.20 ..
6.3.d:
चतुर्भुजो मम सुतस्त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः .
तस्येयं दीयतां कन्या शिशुपालस्य भीष्मक .. 142.20 ..
6.3.m:
'My son is four-armed, renowned throughout the three worlds.
Let this maiden be given to him, to Śiśupāla, O Bhīṣmaka!' // 142.20

6.3.s:
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā damaghoṣasya bhūmipa .
bhīṣmakena tato dattā śiśupālāya rukmiṇī .. 142.21 ..
6.3.d:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा दमघोषस्य भूमिप .
भीष्मकेन ततो दत्ता शिशुपालाय रुक्मिणी .. 142.21 ..
6.3.m:
Hearing that speech of Damaghoṣa, O ruler of the earth,
Rukmiṇī was then promised by Bhīṣmaka to Śiśupāla. // 142.21

6.3.s:
prārabdhaṃ maṅgalaṃ tatra bhīṣmakeṇa yudhiṣṭhira .
dikṣu deśāntareṣveva ye vasanti svagotrajāḥ .. 142.22 ..
6.3.d:
प्रारब्धं मङ्गलं तत्र भीष्मकेण युधिष्ठिर .
दिक्षु देशान्तरेष्वेव ये वसन्ति स्वगोत्रजाः .. 142.22 ..
6.3.m:
The auspicious ceremonies were commenced there by Bhīṣmaka, O Yudhiṣṭhira.
Those kinsmen who lived in the various directions and other lands // 142.22

6.3.s:
nimantritāstu te sarve samājagmuryathākramam .
tato yādavavaṃśasya tilakau balakeśavau .. 142.23 ..
6.3.d:
निमन्त्रितास्तु ते सर्वे समाजग्मुर्यथाक्रमम् .
ततो यादववंशस्य तिलकौ बलकेशवौ .. 142.23 ..
6.3.m:
were all invited and arrived in due order.
Then Balarāma and Keśava, ornaments of the Yādava lineage, // 142.23

6.3.s:
nimantritau samāyātau kuṇḍinaṃ bhīṣmakasya tu .
bhīṣmakeṇa yathānyāyaṃ pūjitau tau yadūttamau .. 142.24 ..
6.3.d:
निमन्त्रितौ समायातौ कुण्डिनं भीष्मकस्य तु .
भीष्मकेण यथान्यायं पूजितौ तौ यदूत्तमौ .. 142.24 ..
6.3.m:
invited, came to Kuṇḍina, to Bhīṣmaka's [palace].
Those two best of Yadus were honored properly by Bhīṣmaka. // 142.24

6.3.s:
tataḥ pradoṣasamaye rukmiṇī kāmamohinī .
sakhībhiḥ sahitā yātā pūrbahiścāmbikārcane .. 142.25 ..
6.3.d:
ततः प्रदोषसमये रुक्मिणी काममोहिनी .
सखीभिः सहिता याता पूर्बहिश्चाम्बिकार्चने .. 142.25 ..
6.3.m:
Then, at the time of dusk, Rukmiṇī, infatuated with desire,
went outside the city with her female companions to worship Ambikā. // 142.25

6.3.s:
sāpaśyattatra deveśaṃ gopaveṣadharaṃ harim .
taṃ dṛṣṭvā mohamāpannā kāmena kaluṣīkṛtā .. 142.26 ..
6.3.d:
सापश्यत्तत्र देवेशं गोपवेषधरं हरिम् .
तं दृष्ट्वा मोहमापन्ना कामेन कलुषीकृता .. 142.26 ..
6.3.m:
There she saw Hari, the lord of gods, wearing the attire of a cowherd.
Seeing him, she fell into bewilderment, agitation brought on by love. // 142.26

6.3.s:
keśavo'pi ca tāṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃkarṣaṇamuvāca ha .
strīratnapravaraṃ tāta hartavyamiti me matiḥ .. 142.27 ..
6.3.d:
केशवोऽपि च तां दृष्ट्वा संकर्षणमुवाच ह .
स्त्रीरत्नप्रवरं तात हर्तव्यमिति मे मतिः .. 142.27 ..
6.3.m:
Keśava, too, seeing her, said to Saṃkarṣaṇa:
'This jewel among women, dear brother, should be abducted—this is my mind.' // 142.27

6.3.s:
keśavasya vacaḥ śrutvā saṃkarṣaṇa uvāca ha .
gaccha kṛṣṇa mahābāho strīratnaṃ cāśu gṛhyatām .. 142.28 ..
6.3.d:
केशवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा संकर्षण उवाच ह .
गच्छ कृष्ण महाबाहो स्त्रीरत्नं चाशु गृह्यताम् .. 142.28 ..
6.3.m:
Hearing Keśava's words, Saṃkarṣaṇa said:
'Go, O mighty-armed Kṛṣṇa, and seize this jewel among women swiftly! // 142.28

6.3.s:
ahaṃ ca tava mārgeṇa hyāgamiṣyāmi pṛṣṭhataḥ .
dānavānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ kurvaṃśca kadanaṃ mahat .. 142.29 ..
6.3.d:
अहं च तव मार्गेण ह्यागमिष्यामि पृष्ठतः .
दानवानां च सर्वेषां कुर्वंश्च कदनं महत् .. 142.29 ..
6.3.m:
And I will follow along behind your path,
causing great slaughter among all the Dānavas.' // 142.29

6.3.s:
saṃkarṣaṇamataṃ prāpya keśavaḥ keśisūdanaḥ .
yayau kanyāṃ gṛhītvā tu rathamāropya satvaram .. 142.30 ..
6.3.d:
संकर्षणमतं प्राप्य केशवः केशिसूदनः .
ययौ कन्यां गृहीत्वा तु रथमारोप्य सत्वरम् .. 142.30 ..
6.3.m:
Having obtained Saṃkarṣaṇa's assent, Keśava, the slayer of Keśin,
took the maiden, placed her on his chariot, and departed swiftly. // 142.30

6.3.s:
nirgataḥ sahasā rājanvegenaivānilo yathā .
hāhākārastadā jāto bhīṣmakasya pure mahān .. 142.31 ..
6.3.d:
निर्गतः सहसा राजन्वेगेनैवानिलो यथा .
हाहाकारस्तदा जातो भीष्मकस्य पुरे महान् .. 142.31 ..
6.3.m:
He departed suddenly, O king, with the speed of the wind itself.
Then a great cry of despair arose in Bhīṣmaka's city. // 142.31

6.3.s:
nirgatā dānavāḥ kruddhā velā iva mahodadheḥ .
garjantaḥ sāyudhāḥ sarve dhāvanto rathavartmani .. 142.32 ..
6.3.d:
निर्गता दानवाः क्रुद्धा वेला इव महोदधेः .
गर्जन्तः सायुधाः सर्वे धावन्तो रथवर्त्मनि .. 142.32 ..
6.3.m:
The enraged Dānavas rushed out like the tide of the great ocean,
all roaring, armed with weapons, running upon the path of the chariot. // 142.32

6.3.s:
baladevaṃ tataḥ prāptā rathamārgānugāminam .
teṣāṃ yuddhaṃ balasyāsītsarvalokakṣayaṃkaram .. 142.33 ..
6.3.d:
बलदेवं ततः प्राप्ता रथमार्गानुगामिनम् .
तेषां युद्धं बलस्यासीत्सर्वलोकक्षयंकरम् .. 142.33 ..
6.3.m:
Then they reached Baladeva, who followed the path of the chariot.
A battle took place between them and Bala, bringing destruction to all beings, // 142.33

6.3.s:
yathā tārāmaye pūrvaṃ saṅgrāme lokaviśrute .
gadāhasto mahābāhustrailokye'pratimo balaḥ .. 142.34 ..
6.3.d:
यथा तारामये पूर्वं सङ्ग्रामे लोकविश्रुते .
गदाहस्तो महाबाहुस्त्रैलोक्येऽप्रतिमो बलः .. 142.34 ..
6.3.m:
just like formerly in the Tārakā battle renowned in the worlds.
Mace in hand, mighty-armed, Bala had no equal in the three worlds. // 142.34

6.3.s:
halenākṛṣya sahasā gadāpātairapātayat .
aśakyo dānavairhantuṃ balabhadro mahābalaḥ .. 142.35 ..
6.3.d:
हलेनाकृष्य सहसा गदापातैरपातयत् .
अशक्यो दानवैर्हन्तुं बलभद्रो महाबलः .. 142.35 ..
6.3.m:
Dragging them violently with his plowshare, he felled them with blows of his mace.
Balabhadra of mighty strength could not be slain by the Dānavas. // 142.35

6.3.s:
babhañja dānavānsarvāṃstasthau giririvācalaḥ .
taṃ dṛṣṭvā ca balaṃ kruddhaṃ durdharṣaṃ tridaśairapi .. 142.36 ..
6.3.d:
बभञ्ज दानवान्सर्वांस्तस्थौ गिरिरिवाचलः .
तं दृष्ट्वा च बलं क्रुद्धं दुर्धर्षं त्रिदशैरपि .. 142.36 ..
6.3.m:
He crushed all the Dānavas and stood firm like an unshakeable mountain.
And seeing Bala enraged, hard to overcome even for the gods, // 142.36

6.3.s:
bhīṣmaputro mahātejā rukmīnāṃ mahayaśāḥ .
narāṇāmatiśūrāṇāmakṣauhiṇyā samanvitaḥ .. 142.37 ..
6.3.d:
भीष्मपुत्रो महातेजा रुक्मीनां महयशाः .
नराणामतिशूराणामक्षौहिण्या समन्वितः .. 142.37 ..
6.3.m:
Bhīṣmaka's son, possessed of great fiery energy, celebrated as Rukmin,
accompanied by an akṣauhiṇī of exceedingly heroic men, // 142.37

6.3.s:
balabhadramatikramya tato yuddhe nirākarot .
tadyuddhaṃ vañcayitvā tu rathamārgeṇa satvaram .. 142.38 ..
6.3.d:
बलभद्रमतिक्रम्य ततो युद्धे निराकरोत् .
तद्युद्धं वञ्चयित्वा तु रथमार्गेण सत्वरम् .. 142.38 ..
6.3.m:
bypassing Balabhadra, then challenged [him] in battle.
Having bypassed that battle swiftly along the chariot-path, // 142.38

6.3.s:
keśavo'pi tadā devo rukmiṇyā sahito yayau .
vindhyaṃ tu laṅghayitvāgre trailokyagururavyayaḥ .. 142.39 ..
6.3.d:
केशवोऽपि तदा देवो रुक्मिण्या सहितो ययौ .
विन्ध्यं तु लङ्घयित्वाग्रे त्रैलोक्यगुरुरव्ययः .. 142.39 ..
6.3.m:
Lord Keśava then departed along with Rukmiṇī.
Crossing the Vindhya ahead, the imperishable teacher of the three worlds // 142.39

6.3.s:
narmadātaṭamāpede yatra siddhaḥ purā punaḥ .
ajeyo yena saṃjātastīrthasyāsya prabhāvataḥ .. 142.40 ..
6.3.d:
नर्मदातटमापेदे यत्र सिद्धः पुरा पुनः .
अजेयो येन संजातस्तीर्थस्यास्य प्रभावतः .. 142.40 ..
6.3.m:
reached the bank of the Narmadā, where he had formerly attained perfection;
whereby he became invincible by the power of this sacred ford. // 142.40

6.3.s:
etasmātkāraṇāttāta yodhanīpuramucyate .
rukmo'pi dānavendro'sau prāptaḥ .. 142.41 ..
6.3.d:
एतस्मात्कारणात्तात योधनीपुरमुच्यते .
रुक्मोऽपि दानवेन्द्रोऽसौ प्राप्तः .. 142.41 ..
6.3.m:
For this reason, dear child, it is called Yodhanīpura.
Rukma too, that lord of Dānavas, arrived... // 142.41

6.3.s:
pratyuvācācyutaṃ kruddhastiṣṭha tiṣṭheti mā vraja .
adya tvāṃ niśitairbāṇairneṣyāmi yamasādanam .. 142.42 ..
6.3.d:
प्रत्युवाचाच्युतं क्रुद्धस्तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति मा व्रज .
अद्य त्वां निशितैर्बाणैर्नेष्यामि यमसादनम् .. 142.42 ..
6.3.m: Enraged, he answered Acyuta: “Halt! Halt! Do not flee! / Today I will send you to Yama's abode with sharpened arrows!”

6.3.s:
evaṃ parasparaṃ vīrau jagarjaturubhāvapi .
tayoryuddhamabhūdghoraṃ tārakāgnijasannibham .. 142.43 ..
6.3.d:
एवं परस्परं वीरौ जगर्जतुरुभावपि .
तयोर्युद्धमभूद्घोरं तारकाग्निजसन्निभम् .. 142.43 ..
6.3.m: Thus the two heroes roared at each other. / A terrible battle ensued between them, like the one between the fire-born [Skanda] and Tāraka.

6.3.s:
cikṣepa śarajālāni keśavaṃ prati dānavaḥ .
nānucintya śarāṃstasya keśavaḥ keśisūdanaḥ .. 142.44 ..
6.3.d:
चिक्षेप शरजालानि केशवं प्रति दानवः .
नानुचिन्त्य शरांस्तस्य केशवः केशिसूदनः .. 142.44 ..
6.3.m: The dānava discharged volleys of arrows against Keśava. / Disregarding his arrows, Keśava, the slayer of Keśin,

6.3.s:
tato viṣṇuḥ svayaṃ kruddhaścakraṃ gṛhya sudarśanam .
sampraharatyamuṃ yāvadrukmiṇyātra nivāritaḥ .. 142.45 ..
6.3.d:
ततो विष्णुः स्वयं क्रुद्धश्चक्रं गृह्य सुदर्शनम् .
सम्प्रहरत्यमुं यावद्रुक्मिण्यात्र निवारितः .. 142.45 ..
6.3.m: Viṣṇu himself, then grew enraged and took up the Sudarśana discus. / Just as he was about to strike him, he was checked there by Rukmiṇī:

6.3.s:
tvāṃ na jānāti deveśaṃ caturbāhuṃ janārdanam .
darśayasva svakaṃ rūpaṃ dayāṃ kṛtvā mamopari .. 142.46 ..
6.3.d:
त्वां न जानाति देवेशं चतुर्बाहुं जनार्दनम् .
दर्शयस्व स्वकं रूपं दयां कृत्वा ममोपरि .. 142.46 ..
6.3.m: “He does not recognize you as the lord of the gods, the four-armed Janārdana. / Taking pity on me, show your own form.”

6.3.s:
evamuktastu rukmiṇyā darśayāmāsa bhārata .
devā dṛṣṭvāpi tadrūpaṃ stuvantyākāśasaṃsthitāḥ .
divyaṃ cakṣustadā devo dadau rukmasya bhārata .. 142.47 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्तस्तु रुक्मिण्या दर्शयामास भारत .
देवा दृष्ट्वापि तद्रूपं स्तुवन्त्याकाशसंस्थिताः .
दिव्यं चक्षुस्तदा देवो ददौ रुक्मस्य भारत .. 142.47 ..
6.3.m: Addressed thus by Rukmiṇī, he showed [it], O Bhārata. / Seeing that form, the gods standing in the sky praised him. / Then the god gave divine vision to Rukma, O Bhārata.

6.3.s:
rukma uvāca -
yanmayā pāpaniṣṭhena mandabhāgyena keśava .
sāyakairāhataṃ vakṣastatsarvaṃ kṣantumarhasi .. 142.48 ..
6.3.d:
रुक्म उवाच -
यन्मया पापनिष्ठेन मन्दभाग्येन केशव .
सायकैराहतं वक्षस्तत्सर्वं क्षन्तुमर्हसि .. 142.48 ..
6.3.m: Rukma said: / “O Keśava, that your chest was struck with arrows by me, / devoted to sin and wretched of fortune, you ought to forgive all that.

6.3.s:
pūrvaṃ dattā svayaṃ deva jānakī janakena vai .
mayā pradattā deveśa rukmiṇī tava keśava .. 142.49 ..
6.3.d:
पूर्वं दत्ता स्वयं देव जानकी जनकेन वै .
मया प्रदत्ता देवेश रुक्मिणी तव केशव .. 142.49 ..
6.3.m: Formerly, O Lord, Jānakī was given by Janaka himself; / by me is Rukmiṇī given to you, O Keśava, lord of the gods.

6.3.s:
udvāhaya yathānyāyaṃ vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā .
rukmasya vacanaṃ śrutvā tatastuṣṭo jagadguruḥ .. 142.50 ..
6.3.d:
उद्वाहय यथान्यायं विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा .
रुक्मस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा ततस्तुष्टो जगद्गुरुः .. 142.50 ..
6.3.m: Marry [her] according to rule, with the rite prescribed by the sacred ordinances.” / Having heard Rukma's words, the teacher of the world was then pleased.

6.3.s:
babhāṣe devadeveśo rukmiṇaṃ bhīṣmakātmajam .
gaccha svakaṃ puraṃ mā bhaiḥ kuru rājyamakaṇṭakam .. 142.51 ..
6.3.d:
बभाषे देवदेवेशो रुक्मिणं भीष्मकात्मजम् .
गच्छ स्वकं पुरं मा भैः कुरु राज्यमकण्टकम् .. 142.51 ..
6.3.m: The lord of the god of gods said to Rukma, the son of Bhīṣmaka: / “Go to your own city, do not fear, and rule the kingdom free from thorns.”

6.3.s:
keśavasya vacaḥ śrutvā rukmo dānavapuṃgavaḥ .
taṃ praṇamya jagannāthaṃ jagāma bhavanaṃ pituḥ .. 142.52 ..
6.3.d:
केशवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा रुक्मो दानवपुंगवः .
तं प्रणम्य जगन्नाथं जगाम भवनं पितुः .. 142.52 ..
6.3.m: Hearing Keśava's words, Rukma, best among dānavas, / bowed to that lord of the world and went to his father's house.

6.3.s:
gate rukme tadā kṛṣṇaḥ samāmantrya dvijottamān .
marīcimatryaṅgirasaṃ pulastyaṃ pulahaṃ kratum .. 142.53 ..
6.3.d:
गते रुक्मे तदा कृष्णः समामन्त्र्य द्विजोत्तमान् .
मरीचिमत्र्यङ्गिरसं पुलस्त्यं पुलहं क्रतुम् .. 142.53 ..
6.3.m: When Rukma had gone, Kṛṣṇa then invited the best among the twice-born: / Marīci, Atri, Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu,

6.3.s:
vasiṣṭhaṃ ca mahābhāgamityete sapta mānasāḥ .
ityete brāhmaṇāḥ sapta purāṇe niścayaṃ gatāḥ .. 142.54 ..
6.3.d:
वसिष्ठं च महाभागमित्येते सप्त मानसाः .
इत्येते ब्राह्मणाः सप्त पुराणे निश्चयं गताः .. 142.54 ..
6.3.m: and the illustrious Vasiṣṭha—these are the seven mind-born [sons]. / These are the seven brahmins established with certainty in the Purāṇa,

6.3.s:
kṣamāvantaḥ prajāvanto maharṣibhiralaṃkṛtāḥ .
ityevaṃ brahmaputrāśca satyavanto mahāmate .. 142.55 ..
6.3.d:
क्षमावन्तः प्रजावन्तो महर्षिभिरलंकृताः .
इत्येवं ब्रह्मपुत्राश्च सत्यवन्तो महामते .. 142.55 ..
6.3.m: forbearing, blessed with offspring, adorned by great seers; / thus these truthful sons of Brahmā, O wise one,

6.3.s:
narmadātaṭamāśritya nivasanti jitendriyāḥ .
tapaḥsvādhyāyaniratā japahomaparāyaṇāḥ .. 142.56 ..
6.3.d:
नर्मदातटमाश्रित्य निवसन्ति जितेन्द्रियाः .
तपःस्वाध्यायनिरता जपहोमपरायणाः .. 142.56 ..
6.3.m: dwell taking refuge on the bank of the Narmadā, with their senses mastered, / dedicated to austerity and self-study, devoted to silent recitation and oblations.

6.3.s:
nimantritāstu rājendra keśavena mahātmanā .
śrāddhaṃ kṛtvā yathānyāyaṃ brahmoktavidhinā tataḥ .. 142.57 ..
6.3.d:
निमन्त्रितास्तु राजेन्द्र केशवेन महात्मना .
श्राद्धं कृत्वा यथान्यायं ब्रह्मोक्तविधिना ततः .. 142.57 ..
6.3.m: Invited by the high-souled Keśava, O king of kings, / he then performed a śrāddha according to rule, following the rite spoken by Brahmā.

6.3.s:
haristānpūjayāmāsa saptabrahmarṣipuṃgavān .
pradadau dvādaśa grāmāṃstebhyastatra janārdanaḥ .. 142.58 ..
6.3.d:
हरिस्तान्पूजयामास सप्तब्रह्मर्षिपुंगवान् .
प्रददौ द्वादश ग्रामांस्तेभ्यस्तत्र जनार्दनः .. 142.58 ..
6.3.m: Hari worshipped those seven foremost brahmanical seers. / Janārdana gave twelve villages to them there:

6.3.s:
yāvaccandraśca sūryaśca yāvattiṣṭhati medinī .
tāvaddānaṃ mayā dattaṃ paripanthī na kaścana .. 142.59 ..
6.3.d:
यावच्चन्द्रश्च सूर्यश्च यावत्तिष्ठति मेदिनी .
तावद्दानं मया दत्तं परिपन्थी न कश्चन .. 142.59 ..
6.3.m: “As long as the moon and the sun [shine], as long as the earth stands, / for so long is this gift given by me; let no one be an adversary [to it].

6.3.s:
maddattaṃ pālayiṣyante ye nṛpā gatakalmaṣāḥ .
tebhyaḥ svasti kariṣyāmi dāsyāmi paramāṃ gatim .. 142.60 ..
6.3.d:
मद्दत्तं पालयिष्यन्ते ये नृपा गतकल्मषाः .
तेभ्यः स्वस्ति करिष्यामि दास्यामि परमां गतिम् .. 142.60 ..
6.3.m: Whichever sinless kings preserve what has been given by me, / to them I shall bring welfare; I will grant the supreme goal.

6.3.s:
yāvaddhi yānti lokeṣu mahābhūtāni pañca ca .
tāvatte divi modante maddattaparipālakāḥ .. 142.61 ..
6.3.d:
यावद्धि यान्ति लोकेषु महाभूतानि पञ्च च .
तावत्ते दिवि मोदन्ते मद्दत्तपरिपालकाः .. 142.61 ..
6.3.m: As long as the five great elements remain in the worlds, / for that long those who protect what has been given by me shall rejoice in heaven.

6.3.s:
yastu lopayate mūḍho dattaṃ vaḥ pṛthivītale .
narake tasya vāsaḥ syādyāvadābhūtasamplavam .. 142.62 ..
6.3.d:
यस्तु लोपयते मूढो दत्तं वः पृथिवीतले .
नरके तस्य वासः स्याद्यावदाभूतसम्प्लवम् .. 142.62 ..
6.3.m: But the fool who revokes what is given to you on the surface of the earth, / his residence shall be in hell until the destruction of all beings.

6.3.s:
svadattā paradattā vā pālanīyā vasuṃdharā .
yasya yasya yadā bhūmistasya tasya tadā phalam .. 142.63 ..
6.3.d:
स्वदत्ता परदत्ता वा पालनीया वसुंधरा .
यस्य यस्य यदा भूमिस्तस्य तस्य तदा फलम् .. 142.63 ..
6.3.m: Whether given by oneself or given by another, land must be protected; / whoever holds the earth at any time, his is the fruit at that time.

6.3.s:
svadattāṃ paradattāṃ vā yo hareta vasuṃdharām .
sa viṣṭhāyāṃ kṛmirbhūtvā pitṛbhiḥ saha majjati .. 142.64 ..
6.3.d:
स्वदत्तां परदत्तां वा यो हरेत वसुंधराम् .
स विष्ठायां कृमिर्भूत्वा पितृभिः सह मज्जति .. 142.64 ..
6.3.m: He who seizes land, whether given by himself or given by another, / becomes a worm in excrement and sinks along with his ancestors.

6.3.s:
anyāyena hṛtā bhūmiranyāyena ca hāritā .
hartā hārayitā caiva viṣṭhāyāṃ jāyate kṛmiḥ .. 142.65 ..
6.3.d:
अन्यायेन हृता भूमिरन्यायेन च हारिता .
हर्ता हारयिता चैव विष्ठायां जायते कृमिः .. 142.65 ..
6.3.m: Land stolen unjustly or caused to be taken away unjustly: / the taker and the one who causes the taking is born a worm in excrement.

6.3.s:
ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi svarge tiṣṭhati bhūmidaḥ .
ācchettā cānumantā ca tānyeva narake vaset .. 142.66 ..
6.3.d:
षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि स्वर्गे तिष्ठति भूमिदः .
आच्छेत्ता चानुमन्ता च तान्येव नरके वसेत् .. 142.66 ..
6.3.m: The giver of land remains in heaven for sixty thousand years; / he who revokes it and he who assents [to the seizure] shall dwell in hell for as many [years].

6.3.s:
yānīha dattāni purā narendrairdānāni dharmārthayaśaskarāṇi .
nirmālyarūpapratimāni tāni ko nāma sādhuḥ punarādadāti .. 142.67 ..
6.3.d:
यानीह दत्तानि पुरा नरेन्द्रैर्दानानि धर्मार्थयशस्कराणि .
निर्माल्यरूपप्रतिमानि तानि को नाम साधुः पुनराददाति .. 142.67 ..
6.3.m: Those gifts given here formerly by rulers of men, which bring righteousness, wealth, and renown, / are like remnant offerings: what virtuous person would take them back?

6.3.s:
evaṃ tānpūjayitvā tu samyaṅnyāyena pāṇḍava .
rukmiṇyā vidhivatpāṇiṃ jagrāha madhusūdanaḥ .. 142.68 ..
6.3.d:
एवं तान्पूजयित्वा तु सम्यङ्न्यायेन पाण्डव .
रुक्मिण्या विधिवत्पाणिं जग्राह मधुसूदनः .. 142.68 ..
6.3.m: Having thus worshipped them according to proper rule, O Pāṇḍava, / the slayer of Madhu took Rukmiṇī's hand in marriage as ordained.

6.3.s:
muśalī ca tataḥ sarvāñjitvā dānavapuṃgavān .
svasthānamagamattatra kṛtvā kāryaṃ suśobhanam .. 142.69 ..
6.3.d:
मुशली च ततः सर्वाञ्जित्वा दानवपुंगवान् .
स्वस्थानमगमत्तत्र कृत्वा कार्यं सुशोभनम् .. 142.69 ..
6.3.m: Then the mace-bearer, having defeated all the foremost dānavas / and having accomplished that very splendid deed, went to his own place.

6.3.s:
prayātau dvāravatyāṃ tau kṛṣṇasaṃkarṣaṇāvubhau .
gacchamānaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā keśavaṃ kleśanāśanam .. 142.70 ..
6.3.d:
प्रयातौ द्वारवत्यां तौ कृष्णसंकर्षणावुभौ .
गच्छमानं तु तं दृष्ट्वा केशवं क्लेशनाशनम् .. 142.70 ..
6.3.m: Both Kṛṣṇa and Saṃkarṣaṇa set out for Dvāravatī. / Seeing that Keśava, the destroyer of distress, was departing,

6.3.s:
brāhmaṇāḥ satyavantaśca nirgatāḥ śaṃsitavratāḥ .
āgacchamānāṃstau vīkṣya rathamārgeṇa brāhmaṇān .. 142.71 ..
6.3.d:
ब्राह्मणाः सत्यवन्तश्च निर्गताः शंसितव्रताः .
आगच्छमानांस्तौ वीक्ष्य रथमार्गेण ब्राह्मणान् .. 142.71 ..
6.3.m: the brahmins, truthful and strict in their vows, set forth. / Seeing those brahmins coming along the road of his chariot,

6.3.s:
muhūrtaṃ tatra viśramya keśavo vākyamabravīt .
kimāgamanakāryaṃ vo brūta sarvaṃ dvijottamāḥ .. 142.72 ..
6.3.d:
मुहूर्तं तत्र विश्रम्य केशवो वाक्यमब्रवीत् .
किमागमनकार्यं वो ब्रूत सर्वं द्विजोत्तमाः .. 142.72 ..
6.3.m: resting there for a moment, Keśava spoke these words: / “What is the purpose of your coming? Tell me everything, O best of the twice-born.

6.3.s:
kurvāṇāḥ svīyakarmāṇi mama kṛtyaṃ tu tiṣṭhate .
devasya vacanaṃ śrutvā munayo vākyamabruvan .. 142.73 ..
6.3.d:
कुर्वाणाः स्वीयकर्माणि मम कृत्यं तु तिष्ठते .
देवस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा मुनयो वाक्यमब्रुवन् .. 142.73 ..
6.3.m: Performing your own duties, what remains to be done for me?” / Hearing the god's words, the sages spoke:

6.3.s:
kalpakoṭisahasreṇa satyabhāvāttu vanditaḥ .
duṣprāpyo'si manuṣyāṇāṃ prāptaḥ kiṃ tyajase hi naḥ .. 142.74 ..
6.3.d:
कल्पकोटिसहस्रेण सत्यभावात्तु वन्दितः .
दुष्प्राप्योऽसि मनुष्याणां प्राप्तः किं त्यजसे हि नः .. 142.74 ..
6.3.m: “Praised with true disposition for thousands of crores of kalpas, / you are difficult for mortals to attain; having attained [you], why do you abandon us?”

6.3.s:
brāhmaṇānāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā bhagavānidamabravīt .
mathurāyāṃ dvāravatyāṃ yodhanīpura eva ca .. 142.75 ..
6.3.d:
ब्राह्मणानां वचः श्रुत्वा भगवानिदमब्रवीत् .
मथुरायां द्वारवत्यां योधनीपुर एव च .. 142.75 ..
6.3.m: Hearing the words of the brahmins, the Lord said this: / “In Mathurā, in Dvāravatī, and at Yodhanīpura,

6.3.s:
trikālamāgamiṣyāmi satyaṃ satyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ .
evaṃ te brāhmaṇāḥ śrutvā yodhanīpuramāgatāḥ .. 142.76 ..
6.3.d:
त्रिकालमागमिष्यामि सत्यं सत्यं पुनः पुनः .
एवं ते ब्राह्मणाः श्रुत्वा योधनीपुरमागताः .. 142.76 ..
6.3.m: I shall come at the three times [of day]; truly, truly, again and again.” / Having heard this, those brahmins returned to Yodhanīpura.

6.3.s:
avatīrṇastribhāgena prādurbhāve tu māthure .
etatte kathitaṃ sarvaṃ tīrthasyotpattikāraṇam .. 142.77 ..
6.3.d:
अवतीर्णस्त्रिभागेन प्रादुर्भावे तु माथुरे .
एतत्ते कथितं सर्वं तीर्थस्योत्पत्तिकारणम् .. 142.77 ..
6.3.m: He descended by a third part in the manifestation at Mathurā. / This whole reason for the origin of the sacred ford has been told to you,

6.3.s:
bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyacca vartamānaṃ tathāparam .
yaṃ śrutvā sarvapāpebhyo mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 142.78 ..
6.3.d:
भूतं भव्यं भविष्यच्च वर्तमानं तथापरम् .
यं श्रुत्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मुच्यते नात्र संशयः .. 142.78 ..
6.3.m: past, present, and future, as well as the other [truths], / hearing which one is freed from all sins; of this there is no doubt.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ snātvā pūjayedbalakeśavau .
tena devo jagaddhātā pūjitastriguṇātmavān .. 142.79 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः स्नात्वा पूजयेद्बलकेशवौ .
तेन देवो जगद्धाता पूजितस्त्रिगुणात्मवान् .. 142.79 ..
6.3.m: Whoever bathes in that sacred ford and worships Bala and Keśava, / by him the god who upholds the world, possessing the three guṇas, is worshipped.

6.3.s:
upavāsī naro bhūtvā yastu kuryātpradakṣiṇam .
mucyate sarvapāpebhyo nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 142.80 ..
6.3.d:
उपवासी नरो भूत्वा यस्तु कुर्यात्प्रदक्षिणम् .
मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो नात्र कार्या विचारणा .. 142.80 ..
6.3.m: A person who fasts and performs circumambulation / is freed from all sins; no doubt should be held on this.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu ye vṛkṣāstānpaśyantyapi ye narāḥ .
te'pi pāpaiḥ pramucyante bhrūṇahatyāsamairapi .. 142.81 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु ये वृक्षास्तान्पश्यन्त्यपि ये नराः .
तेऽपि पापैः प्रमुच्यन्ते भ्रूणहत्यासमैरपि .. 142.81 ..
6.3.m: Whatever trees are in that sacred ford, even the men who only look upon them, / they too are freed from sins, even those equal to the slaying of an embryo.

6.3.s:
prātarutthāya ye kecitpaśyanti balakeśavau .
tena te sadṛśāḥ syurvai devadevena cakriṇā .. 142.82 ..
6.3.d:
प्रातरुत्थाय ये केचित्पश्यन्ति बलकेशवौ .
तेन ते सदृशाः स्युर्वै देवदेवेन चक्रिणा .. 142.82 ..
6.3.m: Those who, having risen in the morning, behold Bala and Keśava, / become equal to that discus-bearing god of gods.

6.3.s:
te pūjyāste namaskāryāsteṣāṃ janma sujīvitam .
ye namanti jagannāthaṃ devaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ harim .. 142.83 ..
6.3.d:
ते पूज्यास्ते नमस्कार्यास्तेषां जन्म सुजीवितम् .
ये नमन्ति जगन्नाथं देवं नारायणं हरिम् .. 142.83 ..
6.3.m: They are worshipful, they are to be bowed to, their life is well-lived, / who bow down to the lord of the world, God Nārāyaṇa, Hari.”

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaddānaṃ snānaṃ devārcanaṃ nṛpa .
tatsarvamakṣayaṃ tasya ityevaṃ śaṅkaro'bravīt .. 142.84 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यद्दानं स्नानं देवार्चनं नृप .
तत्सर्वमक्षयं तस्य इत्येवं शङ्करोऽब्रवीत् .. 142.84 ..
6.3.m: Whatever gift, ritual ablution, or worship of the gods is performed at that sacred ford, O king, / all that becomes imperishable for him—thus Śaṅkara declared.

6.3.s:
praviśyāgnau mṛtānāṃ ca yatphalaṃ samudāhṛtam .
tacchṛṇuṣva nṛpaśreṣṭha procyamānamaśeṣataḥ .. 142.85 ..
6.3.d:
प्रविश्याग्नौ मृतानां च यत्फलं समुदाहृतम् .
तच्छृणुष्व नृपश्रेष्ठ प्रोच्यमानमशेषतः .. 142.85 ..
6.3.m: And whatever fruit is declared for those who die after entering fire, / listen to that in its entirety as it is being told, O best of kings.

6.3.s:
vimānenārkavarṇena kiṃkiṇījālamālinā .
āgneye bhavate tatra modate kālamīpsitam .. 142.86 ..
6.3.d:
विमानेनार्कवर्णेन किंकिणीजालमालिना .
आग्नेये भवते तत्र मोदते कालमीप्सितम् .. 142.86 ..
6.3.m: By means of an aerial chariot bright as the sun, garlanded with nets of tinkling bells, / he goes to the fiery world of Agni and rejoices there for his desired span of time.

6.3.s:
jale caivā mṛtānāṃ tu yodhanīpuramadhyataḥ .
vasanti vāruṇe loke yāvadābhūtasamplavam .. 142.87 ..
6.3.d:
जले चैवा मृतानां तु योधनीपुरमध्यतः .
वसन्ति वारुणे लोके यावदाभूतसम्प्लवम् .. 142.87 ..
6.3.m: And those who die in the water, within the midst of Yodhanīpura, / dwell in the world of Varuṇa until the dissolution of all beings.

6.3.s:
anāśake mṛtānāṃ tu tatra tīrthe narādhipa .
anivartikā gatirnṛṇāṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 142.88 ..
6.3.d:
अनाशके मृतानां तु तत्र तीर्थे नराधिप .
अनिवर्तिका गतिर्नृणां नात्र कार्या विचारणा .. 142.88 ..
6.3.m: For those who die by fasting at that sacred ford, O ruler of men, / their destination is one from which there is no return; no doubt should be entertained on this point.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yo dadyātkapilādānamuttamam .
vidhānena tu saṃyuktaṃ śṛṇu tasyāpi yatphalam .. 142.89 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यो दद्यात्कपिलादानमुत्तमम् .
विधानेन तु संयुक्तं शृणु तस्यापि यत्फलम् .. 142.89 ..
6.3.m: Now listen to the fruit of him who gives the supreme gift of a brown cow / at that sacred ford in accordance with the prescribed rites.

6.3.s:
yāvanti tasyā romāṇi tatprasūteśca bhārata .
tāvanti divi modante sarvakāmaiḥ supūjitāḥ .. 142.90 ..
6.3.d:
यावन्ति तस्या रोमाणि तत्प्रसूतेश्च भारत .
तावन्ति दिवि मोदन्ते सर्वकामैः सुपूजिताः .. 142.90 ..
6.3.m: As many hairs as she has, and as many as her offspring has, O descendant of Bharata, / for that many [years] they rejoice in heaven, honored with all desires.

6.3.s:
yāvanti romāṇi bhavanti dhenvāstāvanti varṣāṇi mahīyate saḥ .
svargāccyutaścāpi tatastrilokyāṃ kule samutpatsyati gomatāṃ saḥ .. 142.91 ..
6.3.d:
यावन्ति रोमाणि भवन्ति धेन्वास्तावन्ति वर्षाणि महीयते सः .
स्वर्गाच्च्युतश्चापि ततस्त्रिलोक्यां कुले समुत्पत्स्यति गोमतां सः .. 142.91 ..
6.3.m: For as many hairs as there are on the cow, for so many years he is glorified; / and when he falls from heaven, he will then be born in the three worlds into a family possessing many cows.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yo dadyādrūpyaṃ kāñcanameva vā .
kāñcanena vimānena viṣṇuloke mahīyate .. 142.92 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यो दद्याद्रूप्यं काञ्चनमेव वा .
काञ्चनेन विमानेन विष्णुलोके महीयते .. 142.92 ..
6.3.m: Whoever gives silver or gold at that sacred ford / is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu in a golden aerial chariot.

6.3.s:
tasmiṃstīrthe tu yo dadyātpāduke vastrameva ca .
dānasyāsya prabhāvena labhate svargamīpsitam .. 142.93 ..
6.3.d:
तस्मिंस्तीर्थे तु यो दद्यात्पादुके वस्त्रमेव च .
दानस्यास्य प्रभावेन लभते स्वर्गमीप्सितम् .. 142.93 ..
6.3.m: Whoever gives sandals and clothing at that sacred ford / attains the heaven he desires by the power of this gift.

6.3.s:
ṛgyajuḥsāmavedānāṃ paṭhanādyatphalaṃ bhavet .
tatra tīrthe tu rājendra gāyatryā tatphalaṃ labhet .. 142.94 ..
6.3.d:
ऋग्यजुःसामवेदानां पठनाद्यत्फलं भवेत् .
तत्र तीर्थे तु राजेन्द्र गायत्र्या तत्फलं लभेत् .. 142.94 ..
6.3.m: Whatever fruit comes from the recitation of the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāmavedas, / at that sacred ford, O king of kings, he attains that fruit through the Gāyatrī alone.

6.3.s:
prayāge yadbhavetpuṇyaṃ gayāyāṃ ca tripuṣkare .
kurukṣetre tu rājendra rāhugraste divākare .. 142.95 ..
6.3.d:
प्रयागे यद्भवेत्पुण्यं गयायां च त्रिपुष्करे .
कुरुक्षेत्रे तु राजेन्द्र राहुग्रस्ते दिवाकरे .. 142.95 ..
6.3.m: Whatever merit there is at Prayāga, at Gayā, and at Tripuṣkara, / and at Kurukṣetra, O king of kings, when the sun is seized by Rāhu,

6.3.s:
someśvare ca yatpuṇyaṃ somasya grahaṇe tathā .
tatphalaṃ labhate tatra snānamātrānna saṃśayaḥ .. 142.96 ..
6.3.d:
सोमेश्वरे च यत्पुण्यं सोमस्य ग्रहणे तथा .
तत्फलं लभते तत्र स्नानमात्रान्न संशयः .. 142.96 ..
6.3.m: and whatever merit is at Someśvara during an eclipse of the moon, / he obtains that fruit there merely by a ritual ablution; of this there is no doubt.

6.3.s:
dvādaśyāṃ tu naraḥ snātvā namaskṛtya janārdanam .
uddhṛtāḥ pitarastena avāptaṃ janmanaḥ phalam .. 142.97 ..
6.3.d:
द्वादश्यां तु नरः स्नात्वा नमस्कृत्य जनार्दनम् .
उद्धृताः पितरस्तेन अवाप्तं जन्मनः फलम् .. 142.97 ..
6.3.m: A man who performs a ritual ablution on the twelfth day and bows to Janārdana / has delivered his ancestors and attained the fruit of his birth.

6.3.s:
saṃkrāntau ca vyatīpāte dvādaśyāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ .
brāhmaṇaṃ bhojayedekaṃ koṭirbhavati bhojitā .. 142.98 ..
6.3.d:
संक्रान्तौ च व्यतीपाते द्वादश्यां च विशेषतः .
ब्राह्मणं भोजयेदेकं कोटिर्भवति भोजिता .. 142.98 ..
6.3.m: If he feeds a single brahmin at a solstice, during Vyatīpāta, / and especially on the twelfth day, ten million have been fed.

6.3.s:
pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni hyāsamudrāṇi pāṇḍava .
tāni sarvāṇi tatraiva dvādaśyāṃ pāṇḍunandana .. 142.99 ..
6.3.d:
पृथिव्यां यानि तीर्थानि ह्यासमुद्राणि पाण्डव .
तानि सर्वाणि तत्रैव द्वादश्यां पाण्डुनन्दन .. 142.99 ..
6.3.m: All the sacred fords on the earth extending as far as the ocean, O Pāṇḍava, / are present right there on the twelfth day, O son of Pāṇḍu.

6.3.s:
kṣayaṃ yānti ca dānāni yajñahomabalikriyāḥ .
na kṣīyate mahārāja tatra tīrthe tu yatkṛtam .. 142.100 ..
6.3.d:
क्षयं यान्ति च दानानि यज्ञहोमबलिक्रियाः .
न क्षीयते महाराज तत्र तीर्थे तु यत्कृतम् .. 142.100 ..
6.3.m: Gifts, sacrifices, oblations, and offerings of food come to an end, / but what is done at that sacred ford never perishes, O great king.

6.3.s:
yadbhūtaṃ yadbhaviṣyacca tīrthamāhātmyamuttamam .
kathitaṃ te mayā sarvaṃ pṛthagbhāvena bhārata .. 142.101 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe rukmiṇītīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma dvicatvāriṃśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 143
6.3.d:
यद्भूतं यद्भविष्यच्च तीर्थमाहात्म्यमुत्तमम् .
कथितं ते मया सर्वं पृथग्भावेन भारत .. 142.101 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे रुक्मिणीतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम द्विचत्वारिंशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 143
6.3.m:
The past and the future of this excellent sacred ford's māhātmya / has all been told to you in detail by me, O descendant of Bharata.
Thus ends the one hundred and forty-second chapter, named the Description of the Māhātmya of Rukmiṇītīrtha, in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the Skandamahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 143

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gacchenmahārāja yojaneśvaramuttamam .
yatra siddhau purā kalpe naranārāyaṇāvṛṣī .. 143.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेन्महाराज योजनेश्वरमुत्तमम् .
यत्र सिद्धौ पुरा कल्पे नरनारायणावृषी .. 143.1 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then one should go, O great king, to the excellent Yojaneśvara, / where the two seers Nara and Nārāyaṇa attained perfection in a former aeon.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tapastaptvā saṅgrāme devadānavaiḥ .
jayaṃ prāptau mahātmānau naranārāyaṇāvubhau .. 143.2 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तपस्तप्त्वा सङ्ग्रामे देवदानवैः .
जयं प्राप्तौ महात्मानौ नरनारायणावुभौ .. 143.2 ..
6.3.m: Having performed austerities at that sacred ford, both the great-souled Nara and Nārāyaṇa / obtained victory in battle over the gods and Dānavas.

6.3.s:
punastretāyuge prāpte tau devau rāmalakṣmaṇau .
tatra tīrthe punaḥ snātvā rāvaṇo durjayo hataḥ .. 143.3 ..
6.3.d:
पुनस्त्रेतायुगे प्राप्ते तौ देवौ रामलक्ष्मणौ .
तत्र तीर्थे पुनः स्नात्वा रावणो दुर्जयो हतः .. 143.3 ..
6.3.m: Then, when the Tretāyuga arrived, those two gods, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, / bathed again at that sacred ford, and the invincible Rāvaṇa was slain.

6.3.s:
punaḥ pārtha kalau prāpte tau devau balakeśavau .
vasudevakule jātau duṣkaraṃ karma cakratuḥ .. 143.4 ..
6.3.d:
पुनः पार्थ कलौ प्राप्ते तौ देवौ बलकेशवौ .
वसुदेवकुले जातौ दुष्करं कर्म चक्रतुः .. 143.4 ..
6.3.m: Again, O son of Pṛthā, when the Kali age arrived, those two gods, Balarāma and Keśava, / were born in the lineage of Vasudeva and accomplished arduous deeds.

6.3.s:
narakaṃ kālanemiṃ ca kaṃsaṃ cāṇūramuṣṭikau .
śiśupālaṃ jarāsaṃdhaṃ jaghnaturbalakeśavau .. 143.5 ..
6.3.d:
नरकं कालनेमिं च कंसं चाणूरमुष्टिकौ .
शिशुपालं जरासंधं जघ्नतुर्बलकेशवौ .. 143.5 ..
6.3.m: Balarāma and Keśava slew Naraka, Kālanemi, Kaṃsa, Cāṇūra, and Muṣṭika, / as well as Śiśupāla and Jarāsandha.

6.3.s:
tatastatra ripūnsaṃkhye bhīṣmadroṇapuraḥsarān .
karṇaduryodhanādīṃśca nihaniṣyati sa prabhuḥ .. 143.6 ..
6.3.d:
ततस्तत्र रिपून्संख्ये भीष्मद्रोणपुरःसरान् .
कर्णदुर्योधनादींश्च निहनिष्यति स प्रभुः .. 143.6 ..
6.3.m: Then, in the battle there, that lord will strike down enemies / headed by Bhīṣma and Droṇa, as well as Karṇa, Duryodhana, and others.

6.3.s:
dharmakṣetre kurukṣetre tatra yudhyanti te kṣaṇam .
bhīmārjunanimittena śiṣyau kṛtvā parasparam .. 143.7 ..
6.3.d:
धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे तत्र युध्यन्ति ते क्षणम् .
भीमार्जुननिमित्तेन शिष्यौ कृत्वा परस्परम् .. 143.7 ..
6.3.m: In the sacred field of Dharma, Kurukṣetra, they will fight for a moment, / having made pupils on account of Bhīma and Arjuna against each other.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe punargatvā tapaḥ kṛtvā suduṣkaram .
pūjayitvā dvijānbhaktyā yāsyete dvārakāṃ punaḥ .. 143.8 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे पुनर्गत्वा तपः कृत्वा सुदुष्करम् .
पूजयित्वा द्विजान्भक्त्या यास्येते द्वारकां पुनः .. 143.8 ..
6.3.m: Having gone again to that sacred ford and performed exceedingly arduous austerities, / and having honored the twice-born with devotion, they will return to Dvārakā.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ snātvā pūjayedbalakeśavau .
tena devo jagaddhātā pūjitastriguṇātmavān .. 143.9 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः स्नात्वा पूजयेद्बलकेशवौ .
तेन देवो जगद्धाता पूजितस्त्रिगुणात्मवान् .. 143.9 ..
6.3.m: He who bathes at that sacred ford and worships Balarāma and Keśava, / has thereby worshipped the god who sustains the world and embodies the three qualities.

6.3.s:
upavāsī naro bhūtvā yastu kuryātprajāgaram .
mucyate sarvapāpebhyo gāyaṃstasya śubhāṃ kathām .. 143.10 ..
6.3.d:
उपवासी नरो भूत्वा यस्तु कुर्यात्प्रजागरम् .
मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो गायंस्तस्य शुभां कथाम् .. 143.10 ..
6.3.m: A man who fasts, keeps a night vigil, / and sings his auspicious narrative is freed from all sins.

6.3.s:
yāvatastatra tīrthe tu vṛkṣān paśyanti mānavāḥ .
brahmahatyādikaṃ pāpaṃ tāvadeṣāṃ praṇaśyati .. 143.11 ..
6.3.d:
यावतस्तत्र तीर्थे तु वृक्षान् पश्यन्ति मानवाः .
ब्रह्महत्यादिकं पापं तावदेषां प्रणश्यति .. 143.11 ..
6.3.m: As many trees as men look upon at that sacred ford, / so much sin, beginning with the killing of a brahmin, is destroyed for them.

6.3.s:
prātarutthāya ye kecitpaśyanti balakeśavau .
tenaiva sadṛśāḥ sarve devadevena cakriṇā .. 143.12 ..
6.3.d:
प्रातरुत्थाय ये केचित्पश्यन्ति बलकेशवौ .
तेनैव सदृशाः सर्वे देवदेवेन चक्रिणा .. 143.12 ..
6.3.m: Whoever rises early in the morning and beholds Balarāma and Keśava / becomes equal to that god of gods who bears the discus.

6.3.s:
te pūjyāste namaskāryāsteṣāṃ janma sujīvitam .
ye namanti jagatpūjyaṃ devaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ harim .. 143.13 ..
6.3.d:
ते पूज्यास्ते नमस्कार्यास्तेषां जन्म सुजीवितम् .
ये नमन्ति जगत्पूज्यं देवं नारायणं हरिम् .. 143.13 ..
6.3.m: They are worthy of worship, they are worthy of salutation, and fruitful is their life / who bow to the god Nārāyaṇa, Hari, who is worshipped by the universe.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaddānaṃ snānaṃ devārcanaṃ nṛpa .
kriyate tatphalaṃ sarvamakṣayāyopakalpate .. 143.14 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यद्दानं स्नानं देवार्चनं नृप .
क्रियते तत्फलं सर्वमक्षयायोपकल्पते .. 143.14 ..
6.3.m: Whatever gift, ritual ablution, and worship of the gods is performed at that sacred ford, O king, / all of that fruit serves to be imperishable.

6.3.s:
agnerapatyaṃ prathamaṃ suvarṇaṃ bhūrvaiṣṇavī sūryasutāśca gāvaḥ .
lokāstrayastena bhavanti dattā yaḥ kāñcanaṃ gāṃ ca bhuvaṃ ca dadyāt .. 143.15 ..
6.3.d:
अग्नेरपत्यं प्रथमं सुवर्णं भूर्वैष्णवी सूर्यसुताश्च गावः .
लोकास्त्रयस्तेन भवन्ति दत्ता यः काञ्चनं गां च भुवं च दद्यात् .. 143.15 ..
6.3.m: Gold was the first offspring of Agni, the earth belongs to Viṣṇu, and cows are daughters of the sun; / he who gives gold, a cow, and land has given the three worlds.

6.3.s:
etatte kathitaṃ sarvaṃ tīrthamāhātmyamuttamam .
atītaṃ ca bhaviṣyacca vartamānaṃ mahābalam .. 143.16 ..
6.3.d:
एतत्ते कथितं सर्वं तीर्थमाहात्म्यमुत्तमम् .
अतीतं च भविष्यच्च वर्तमानं महाबलम् .. 143.16 ..
6.3.m: All this excellent sacred ford's māhātmya has been told to you— / past, future, and present, possessing great power.

6.3.s:
śrutvā vāpi paṭhitvedaṃ śrāvayipatvātha dhārmikān .
mucyate sarvapāpebhyo nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 143.17 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe yojaneśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma tricatvāriṃśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 144
6.3.d:
श्रुत्वा वापि पठित्वेदं श्रावयिपत्वाथ धार्मिकान् .
मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो नात्र कार्या विचारणा .. 143.17 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे योजनेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम त्रिचत्वारिंशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 144
6.3.m:
Having heard this, or having read it, or having caused the righteous to hear it, / one is freed from all sins; no doubt should be entertained on this point.
Thus ends the one hundred and forty-third chapter, named the Description of the Māhātmya of Yojaneśvaratīrtha, in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the Skandamahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 144

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gacchenmahārāja dvādaśītīrthamuttamam .
kṣaranti sarvadānāni japahomabalikriyāḥ .. 144.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेन्महाराज द्वादशीतीर्थमुत्तमम् .
क्षरन्ति सर्वदानानि जपहोमबलिक्रियाः .. 144.1 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then one should go, O great king, to the excellent Dvādaśītīrtha. / All gifts, recitations, oblations, and offerings of food diminish,

6.3.s:
na kṣīyate tu rājendra cakratīrthe tu yatkṛtam .
yadbhūtaṃ yadbhaviṣyacca tīrthamāhātmyamuttamam .. 144.2 ..
6.3.d:
न क्षीयते तु राजेन्द्र चक्रतीर्थे तु यत्कृतम् .
यद्भूतं यद्भविष्यच्च तीर्थमाहात्म्यमुत्तमम् .. 144.2 ..
6.3.m: but what is performed at Cakratīrtha never perishes, O king of kings. / Whatever past and future māhātmya of this excellent sacred ford there is,

6.3.s:
kathitaṃ tanmayā sarvaṃ pṛthagbhāvena bhārata .. 144.3 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe dvādaśītīrthamahātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma catuścatvāriṃśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
6.3.d:
कथितं तन्मया सर्वं पृथग्भावेन भारत .. 144.3 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे द्वादशीतीर्थमहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम चतुश्चत्वारिंशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः ..
6.3.m:
all that has been told to you in detail by me, O descendant of Bharata.
Thus ends the one hundred and forty-fourth chapter, entitled "Description of the Greatness of Dvādaśī-tīrtha," in the Revākhaṇḍa of the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses].

6.3.s:
adhyāya 145
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gaccheddharāpāla śīvatīrthamanuttamam .
darśanādyasya devasya mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ .. 145.1 ..
6.3.d:
अध्याय 145
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेद्धरापाल शीवतीर्थमनुत्तमम् .
दर्शनाद्यस्य देवस्य मुच्यते सर्वकिल्बिषैः .. 145.1 ..
6.3.m: Chapter 145 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then one should go, O protector of the earth, to the unexcelled Śivatīrtha, / by beholding whose deity one is freed from all sins.

6.3.s:
śivatīrthe tu yaḥ snātvā jitakrodho jitendriyaḥ .
pūjayeta mahādevaṃ so'gniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet .. 145.2 ..
6.3.d:
शिवतीर्थे तु यः स्नात्वा जितक्रोधो जितेन्द्रियः .
पूजयेत महादेवं सोऽग्निष्टोमफलं लभेत् .. 145.2 ..
6.3.m: Whoever, having bathed at Śivatīrtha with anger conquered and senses subdued, / worships Mahādeva, attains the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yo bhaktyā sopavāso'rcayecchivam .
anivartikā gatistasya rudralokādasaṃśayam .. 145.3 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe śivatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma pañcacatvāriṃśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 146
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यो भक्त्या सोपवासोऽर्चयेच्छिवम् .
अनिवर्तिका गतिस्तस्य रुद्रलोकादसंशयम् .. 145.3 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे शिवतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम पञ्चचत्वारिंशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 146
6.3.m:
Whoever worships Śiva with devotion at that sacred ford while fasting, / his state of existence from Rudraloka is non-returning, beyond doubt.
Thus ends the one hundred and forty-fifth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Māhātmya of the Śivatīrtha,' in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 146

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
asmāhakaṃ tato gacchetpitṛtīrthamanuttamam .
pretatvādyatra mucyante piṇḍenaikena pūrvajāḥ .. 146.1 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
अस्माहकं ततो गच्छेत्पितृतीर्थमनुत्तमम् .
प्रेतत्वाद्यत्र मुच्यन्ते पिण्डेनैकेन पूर्वजाः .. 146.1 ..
6.3.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then one should go to Asmāhaka, the unsurpassed sacred ford for the ancestors, / where forefathers are freed from the state of ghosts by a single rice-ball offering.

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
asmāhakasya māhātmyaṃ kathayasva mamānagha .
snānadānena yatpuṇyaṃ tathā piṇḍodakena ca .. 146.2 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
अस्माहकस्य माहात्म्यं कथयस्व ममानघ .
स्नानदानेन यत्पुण्यं तथा पिण्डोदकेन च .. 146.2 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / Tell me, faultless one, the māhātmya of Asmāhaka, / and the merit obtained through bathing and gift-giving, as well as through offerings of rice-balls and water.

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
purā kalpe nṛpaśreṣṭha ṛṣidevasamāgame .
praśnaḥ pṛṣṭo mayā tāta yathā tvamanupṛcchasi .. 146.3 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
पुरा कल्पे नृपश्रेष्ठ ऋषिदेवसमागमे .
प्रश्नः पृष्टो मया तात यथा त्वमनुपृच्छसि .. 146.3 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Long ago in a former kalpa, best of kings, at a gathering of seers and gods, / I asked this question, dear one, just as you are asking now.

6.3.s:
ekatra sāgarāḥ sapta saprayāgāḥ sapuṣkarāḥ .
nāsya sāmyaṃ labhante te nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 146.4 ..
6.3.d:
एकत्र सागराः सप्त सप्रयागाः सपुष्कराः .
नास्य साम्यं लभन्ते ते नात्र कार्या विचारणा .. 146.4 ..
6.3.m: The seven oceans brought together in one place, along with Prayāga and Puṣkara, / do not equal it; about this there should be no doubt.

6.3.s:
somanāthaṃ tu vikhyātaṃ yatsomena pratiṣṭhitam .
tatra somagrahe puṇyaṃ tatpuṇyaṃ labhate naraḥ .. 146.5 ..
6.3.d:
सोमनाथं तु विख्यातं यत्सोमेन प्रतिष्ठितम् .
तत्र सोमग्रहे पुण्यं तत्पुण्यं लभते नरः .. 146.5 ..
6.3.m: The renowned Somanātha was established by Soma; / whatever merit is gained there during a lunar eclipse, a man obtains that very merit [here].

6.3.s:
māsānte pitaro nṛṇāṃ vīkṣante santatiṃ svakām .
kaścidasmatkule'smākaṃ piṇḍamatra pradāsyati .. 146.6 ..
6.3.d:
मासान्ते पितरो नृणां वीक्षन्ते सन्ततिं स्वकाम् .
कश्चिदस्मत्कुलेऽस्माकं पिण्डमत्र प्रदास्यति .. 146.6 ..
6.3.m: At the end of each month, the ancestors look upon their descendants, [hoping:] / "Someone in our lineage will offer a rice-ball for us here."

6.3.s:
prapitāmahāstathādityāḥ śrutireṣā sanātanī .
evaṃ bruvanti devāśca ṛṣayaḥ satapodhanāḥ .. 146.7 ..
6.3.d:
प्रपितामहास्तथादित्याः श्रुतिरेषा सनातनी .
एवं ब्रुवन्ति देवाश्च ऋषयः सतपोधनाः .. 146.7 ..
6.3.m: The great-grandfathers are likewise the Ādityas; this is the eternal Vedic revelation. / Thus say the gods and the seers rich in austerity.

6.3.s:
sakṛtpiṇḍodakenaiva śṛṇu pārthiva yatphalam .
dvādaśābdāni rājendra yogaṃ bhuktvā suśobhanam .. 146.8 ..
6.3.d:
सकृत्पिण्डोदकेनैव शृणु पार्थिव यत्फलम् .
द्वादशाब्दानि राजेन्द्र योगं भुक्त्वा सुशोभनम् .. 146.8 ..
6.3.m: Hear, O king, the fruit produced by offering a rice-ball and water even once: / after enjoying a most splendid association for twelve years, O best of kings,

6.3.s:
yuge yuge mahārāja asmāhake pitāmahāḥ .
sarvadā hyavalokanta āgacchantaṃ svagotrajam .. 146.9 ..
6.3.d:
युगे युगे महाराज अस्माहके पितामहाः .
सर्वदा ह्यवलोकन्त आगच्छन्तं स्वगोत्रजम् .. 146.9 ..
6.3.m: in age after age, great king, the grandfathers at Asmāhaka / always look out for one born in their lineage who is arriving.

6.3.s:
bhaviṣyati kimasmākamamāvāsyāpyamāhake .
snānaṃ dānaṃ ca ye kuryuḥ pitṝṇāṃ tilatarpaṇam .. 146.10 ..
6.3.d:
भविष्यति किमस्माकममावास्याप्यमाहके .
स्नानं दानं च ये कुर्युः पितॄणां तिलतर्पणम् .. 146.10 ..
6.3.m: [They wonder:] "Will there be a new-moon day for us at Amāhaka?" / Those who perform ritual ablution, give gifts, and offer sesame-water to the ancestors,

6.3.s:
te sarvapāpanirmuktāḥ sarvānkāmāṃllabhati vai .
jalamadhye'tra bhūpāla agnitīrthaṃ ca tiṣṭhati .. 146.11 ..
6.3.d:
ते सर्वपापनिर्मुक्ताः सर्वान्कामांल्लभति वै .
जलमध्येऽत्र भूपाल अग्नितीर्थं च तिष्ठति .. 146.11 ..
6.3.m: are freed from all sins and certainly obtain all desires. / In the midst of the water here, protector of the earth, stands Agnitīrtha.

6.3.s:
darśanāttasya tīrthasya pāparāśirvilīyate .
snānamātreṇa rājendra brahmahatyāṃ vyapohati .. 146.12 ..
6.3.d:
दर्शनात्तस्य तीर्थस्य पापराशिर्विलीयते .
स्नानमात्रेण राजेन्द्र ब्रह्महत्यां व्यपोहति .. 146.12 ..
6.3.m: By the sight of that sacred ford, a heap of sins melts away; / by mere bathing [in it], O best of kings, it wipes away the killing of a brahmin.

6.3.s:
śuklāmbaradharo nityaṃ niyataḥ sa jitendriyaḥ .
ekakālaṃ tu bhuñjāno māsaṃ tīrthasya sannidhau .. 146.13 ..
6.3.d:
शुक्लाम्बरधरो नित्यं नियतः स जितेन्द्रियः .
एककालं तु भुञ्जानो मासं तीर्थस्य सन्निधौ .. 146.13 ..
6.3.m: Dressed always in white garments, restrained, with senses mastered, / eating only once a day for a month in the presence of the sacred ford,

6.3.s:
suvarṇālaṃkṛtānāṃ tu kanyānāṃ śatadānajam .
phalamāpnoti sampūrṇaṃ pitṛloke mahīyate .. 146.14 ..
6.3.d:
सुवर्णालंकृतानां तु कन्यानां शतदानजम् .
फलमाप्नोति सम्पूर्णं पितृलोके महीयते .. 146.14 ..
6.3.m: he obtains the full fruit of giving a hundred maidens adorned with gold, / and is glorified in the world of the ancestors.

6.3.s:
pṛthivyāmāsamudrāyāṃ mahābhogapatirbhavet .
dhanadhānyasamāyukto dātā bhavati dhārmikaḥ .. 146.15 ..
6.3.d:
पृथिव्यामासमुद्रायां महाभोगपतिर्भवेत् .
धनधान्यसमायुक्तो दाता भवति धार्मिकः .. 146.15 ..
6.3.m: He becomes the master of great enjoyments over the earth as far as the ocean; / endowed with wealth and grain, he becomes a generous and righteous man.

6.3.s:
upavāsī śucirbhūtvā brahmalokamavāpnuyāt .
asmāhakaṃ samāsādya yastu prāṇān parityajet .. 146.16 ..
6.3.d:
उपवासी शुचिर्भूत्वा ब्रह्मलोकमवाप्नुयात् .
अस्माहकं समासाद्य यस्तु प्राणान् परित्यजेत् .. 146.16 ..
6.3.m: Fasting and becoming pure, he reaches the world of Brahmā. / And whoever casts off his life-breaths after reaching Asmāhaka

6.3.s:
koṭivarṣasahasrāṇi rudraloke mahīyate .
tataḥ svargātparibhraṣṭaḥ kṣīṇakarmā divaścyutaḥ .. 146.17 ..
6.3.d:
कोटिवर्षसहस्राणि रुद्रलोके महीयते .
ततः स्वर्गात्परिभ्रष्टः क्षीणकर्मा दिवश्च्युतः .. 146.17 ..
6.3.m: is glorified in the world of Rudra for thousands of ten millions of years. / Falling from that heaven when his karmic merit is exhausted, cast down from the sky,

6.3.s:
suvarṇamaṇimuktāḍhye kule jāyeta rūpavān .
kṛtvābhiṣekavidhinā hayamedhaphalaṃ labhet .. 146.18 ..
6.3.d:
सुवर्णमणिमुक्ताढ्ये कुले जायेत रूपवान् .
कृत्वाभिषेकविधिना हयमेधफलं लभेत् .. 146.18 ..
6.3.m: he is born handsome in a family rich in gold, gems, and pearls. / Performing the bath according to the prescribed rule, he attains the fruit of a horse-sacrifice.

6.3.s:
dhanāḍhyo rūpavāndakṣo dātā bhavati dhārmikaḥ .
caturvedeṣu yatpuṇyaṃ satyavādiṣu yatphalam .. 146.19 ..
6.3.d:
धनाढ्यो रूपवान्दक्षो दाता भवति धार्मिकः .
चतुर्वेदेषु यत्पुण्यं सत्यवादिषु यत्फलम् .. 146.19 ..
6.3.m: He becomes rich in wealth, handsome, capable, generous, and righteous. / Whatever merit is in the four Vedas, whatever fruit is among the speakers of truth,

6.3.s:
tatphalaṃ labhate nūnaṃ tatra tīrthe'bhiṣecanāt .
tīrthānāṃ paramaṃ tīrthaṃ nirmitaṃ śambhunā purā .. 146.20 ..
6.3.d:
तत्फलं लभते नूनं तत्र तीर्थेऽभिषेचनात् .
तीर्थानां परमं तीर्थं निर्मितं शम्भुना पुरा .. 146.20 ..
6.3.m: surely he attains that fruit from bathing in that sacred ford. / Long ago, this supreme sacred ford among sacred fords was fashioned by Śambhu.

6.3.s:
hṛdayeśaḥ svayaṃ viṣṇurjapeddevaṃ maheśvaram .
gandharvāpsarasaścaiva maruto mārutāstathā .. 146.21 ..
6.3.d:
हृदयेशः स्वयं विष्णुर्जपेद्देवं महेश्वरम् .
गन्धर्वाप्सरसश्चैव मरुतो मारुतास्तथा .. 146.21 ..
6.3.m: Viṣṇu himself, lord of the heart, mutters prayers to the god Maheśvara [there]; / gandharvas and apsarases, the Maruts and the wind-deities,

6.3.s:
viśvedevāśca pitaraḥ sacandrāḥ sadivākarāḥ .
marīciratryaṅgirasau pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ .. 146.22 ..
6.3.d:
विश्वेदेवाश्च पितरः सचन्द्राः सदिवाकराः .
मरीचिरत्र्यङ्गिरसौ पुलस्त्यः पुलहः क्रतुः .. 146.22 ..
6.3.m: the Viśvedevas and the ancestors, together with the moon and the sun, / Marīci, Atri, Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu,

6.3.s:
pracetāśca vasiṣṭhaśca bhṛgurnārada eva ca .
cyavano gālavaścaiva vāmadevo mahāmuniḥ .. 146.23 ..
6.3.d:
प्रचेताश्च वसिष्ठश्च भृगुर्नारद एव च .
च्यवनो गालवश्चैव वामदेवो महामुनिः .. 146.23 ..
6.3.m: Pracetas, Vasiṣṭha, Bhṛgu, and Nārada, / Cyavana, Gālava, and the great sage Vāmadeva,

6.3.s:
vālakhilyāśca gandhārāstṛṇabinduśca jājaliḥ .
uddālakaścarṣyaśṛṅgo vasiṣṭhaśca sanandanaḥ .. 146.24 ..
6.3.d:
वालखिल्याश्च गन्धारास्तृणबिन्दुश्च जाजलिः .
उद्दालकश्चर्ष्यशृङ्गो वसिष्ठश्च सनन्दनः .. 146.24 ..
6.3.m: the Vālakhilyas, Gandhāras, Tṛṇabindu, Jājali, / Uddālaka, Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, Vasiṣṭha, Sanandana,

6.3.s:
śukraścaiva bharadvājo vātsyo vātsyāyanastathā .
agastirmitrāvaruṇau viśvāmitro munīśvaraḥ .. 146.25 ..
6.3.d:
शुक्रश्चैव भरद्वाजो वात्स्यो वात्स्यायनस्तथा .
अगस्तिर्मित्रावरुणौ विश्वामित्रो मुनीश्वरः .. 146.25 ..
6.3.m: Śukra, Bharadvāja, Vātsya, Vātsyāyana, / Agasti, Mitra and Varuṇa, the lord of sages Viśvāmitra,

6.3.s:
gautamaśca pulastyaśca paulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ .
sanātanastu kapilo vāhniḥ pañcaśikhastathā .. 146.26 ..
6.3.d:
गौतमश्च पुलस्त्यश्च पौलस्त्यः पुलहः क्रतुः .
सनातनस्तु कपिलो वाह्निः पञ्चशिखस्तथा .. 146.26 ..
6.3.m: Gautama, Pulastya, the son of Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, / Sanātana, Kapila, Vahni, and Pañcaśikha,

6.3.s:
anye'pi bahavastatra munayaḥ śaṃsitavratāḥ .
krīḍanti devatāḥ sarva ṛṣayaḥ satapodhanāḥ .. 146.27 ..
6.3.d:
अन्येऽपि बहवस्तत्र मुनयः शंसितव्रताः .
क्रीडन्ति देवताः सर्व ऋषयः सतपोधनाः .. 146.27 ..
6.3.m: and many other sages of celebrated vows [dwell there]. / All the deities sport there, along with the seers rich in austerity.

6.3.s:
manuṣyāścaiva yogīndrāḥ pitaraḥ sapitāmahāḥ .
asmāhake'tra tiṣṭhanti sarva eva na saṃśayaḥ .. 146.28 ..
6.3.d:
मनुष्याश्चैव योगीन्द्राः पितरः सपितामहाः .
अस्माहकेऽत्र तिष्ठन्ति सर्व एव न संशयः .. 146.28 ..
6.3.m: Mortals, foremost yogins, and ancestors with grandfathers— / all of them dwell here at Asmāhaka, without a doubt.

6.3.s:
pitaraḥ pitāmahāścaiva tathaiva prapitāmahāḥ .
yeṣāṃ dattamupasthāyi sukṛtaṃ vāpi duṣkṛtam .. 146.29 ..
6.3.d:
पितरः पितामहाश्चैव तथैव प्रपितामहाः .
येषां दत्तमुपस्थायि सुकृतं वापि दुष्कृतम् .. 146.29 ..
6.3.m: To the fathers, the grandfathers, and likewise the great-grandfathers / what is offered stands ready, whether good deeds or bad deeds.

6.3.s:
akṣayaṃ tatra tatsarvaṃ yatkṛtaṃ yodhanīpure .
mātaraṃ pitaraṃ tyaktvā sarvabandhusuhṛjjanān .. 146.30 ..
6.3.d:
अक्षयं तत्र तत्सर्वं यत्कृतं योधनीपुरे .
मातरं पितरं त्यक्त्वा सर्वबन्धुसुहृज्जनान् .. 146.30 ..
6.3.m: Whatever is done in Yodhanīpura remains imperishable there. / Leaving behind mother, father, and all relatives and dear friends,

6.3.s:
dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ priyānputrāṃstathā dehaṃ nṛpottama .
gacchate vāyubhūtastu śubhāśubhasamanvitaḥ .. 146.31 ..
6.3.d:
धनं धान्यं प्रियान्पुत्रांस्तथा देहं नृपोत्तम .
गच्छते वायुभूतस्तु शुभाशुभसमन्वितः .. 146.31 ..
6.3.m: wealth, grain, beloved sons, and even the body, O best of kings, / becoming of the nature of wind, he departs, accompanied by his good and evil deeds.

6.3.s:
adṛśyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ paramātmā mahattaraḥ .
śubhāśubhagatiṃ prāptaḥ karmaṇā svena pārthiva .. 146.32 ..
6.3.d:
अदृश्यः सर्वभूतानां परमात्मा महत्तरः .
शुभाशुभगतिं प्राप्तः कर्मणा स्वेन पार्थिव .. 146.32 ..
6.3.m: Invisible to all beings, the greater supreme self / reaches a good or evil destiny according to his own action, O king.

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
śubhāśubhaṃ na bandhūnāṃ jāyate kena hetunā .
ekaḥ prasūyate jantureka eva pralīyate .. 146.33 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
शुभाशुभं न बन्धूनां जायते केन हेतुना .
एकः प्रसूयते जन्तुरेक एव प्रलीयते .. 146.33 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / For what reason do the good and evil deeds of relatives not accrue [to one]? / A living being is born alone, and alone it dissolves.

6.3.s: eko hi bhuṅkte sukṛtameka eva hi duṣkṛtam .. 146.34 ..
6.3.d: एको हि भुङ्क्ते सुकृतमेक एव हि दुष्कृतम् .. 146.34 ..
6.3.m: Alone one enjoys good deeds, and alone indeed bad deeds.

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
eṣa tvayokto nṛpate mahāpraśnaḥ smṛto mayā .. 146.35 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
एष त्वयोक्तो नृपते महाप्रश्नः स्मृतो मया .. 146.35 ..
6.3.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / This great question stated by you, O king, has been remembered by me.

6.3.s:
pitāmahamukhodgītaṃ śrutaṃ te kathayāmyaham .
yanme pitāmahātpūrvaṃ vijñātamṛṣisaṃsadi .. 146.36 ..
6.3.d:
पितामहमुखोद्गीतं श्रुतं ते कथयाम्यहम् .
यन्मे पितामहात्पूर्वं विज्ञातमृषिसंसदि .. 146.36 ..
6.3.m: I shall tell you what was sung from the mouth of the Grandfather and heard [by me], / which was previously learned by me from the Grandfather in an assembly of seers.

6.3.s:
na mātā na pitā bandhuḥ kasyacinna suhṛtkvacit .
kasya na jñāyate rūpaṃ vāyubhūtasya dehinaḥ .. 146.37 ..
6.3.d:
न माता न पिता बन्धुः कस्यचिन्न सुहृत्क्वचित् .
कस्य न ज्ञायते रूपं वायुभूतस्य देहिनः .. 146.37 ..
6.3.m: Neither mother, nor father, nor kin, nor friend belongs to anyone anywhere; / whose form cannot be recognized when the embodied being becomes of the nature of wind?

6.3.s:
yadyevaṃ na bhavettāta lokasya tu nareśvara .
amaryādaṃ bhavennūnaṃ vinaśyati carācaram .. 146.38 ..
6.3.d:
यद्येवं न भवेत्तात लोकस्य तु नरेश्वर .
अमर्यादं भवेन्नूनं विनश्यति चराचरम् .. 146.38 ..
6.3.m: If it were not so for the world, dear lord of men, / the world of mobile and immobile beings would surely become lawless and perish.

6.3.s:
evaṃ jñātvā pūrā rājansamastairlokakartṛbhiḥ .
maryādā sthāpitā loke yathā dharmo na naśyati .. 146.39 ..
6.3.d:
एवं ज्ञात्वा पूरा राजन्समस्तैर्लोककर्तृभिः .
मर्यादा स्थापिता लोके यथा धर्मो न नश्यति .. 146.39 ..
6.3.m: Knowing this long ago, O king, an orderly boundary was established in the world / by all the creators of the world, so that dharma would not perish.

6.3.s:
dharme naṣṭe manuṣyāṇāmadharmo'bhibhavetpunaḥ .
tataḥ svadharmacalanānnarake gamanaṃ dhruvam .. 146.40 ..
6.3.d:
धर्मे नष्टे मनुष्याणामधर्मोऽभिभवेत्पुनः .
ततः स्वधर्मचलनान्नरके गमनं ध्रुवम् .. 146.40 ..
6.3.m: When dharma is destroyed among mortals, adharma overcomes them again; / then, by deviating from one's own duty, going to hell is certain.

6.3.s:
loko niraṅkuśaḥ sarvo maryādālaṅghane rataḥ .
maryādā sthāpitā tena śāstraṃ vīkṣya maharṣibhiḥ .. 146.41 ..
6.3.d:
लोको निरङ्कुशः सर्वो मर्यादालङ्घने रतः .
मर्यादा स्थापिता तेन शास्त्रं वीक्ष्य महर्षिभिः .. 146.41 ..
6.3.m: The entire world is unbridled, intent on transgressing the boundary; / therefore, having examined the scriptures, an orderly boundary was established by the great seers:

6.3.s:
snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ svādhyāyo devatārcanam .
piṇḍodakapradānaṃ ca tathaivātithipūjanam .. 146.42 ..
6.3.d:
स्नानं दानं जपो होमः स्वाध्यायो देवतार्चनम् .
पिण्डोदकप्रदानं च तथैवातिथिपूजनम् .. 146.42 ..
6.3.m: ritual ablution, gift-giving, silent recitation, fire-offering, recitation of scripture, worship of the deity, / offering of rice-balls and water, and likewise honoring guests.

6.3.s:
pitaraḥ pitāmahāścaiva tathaiva prapitāmahāḥ .
trayo devāḥ smṛtāstāta brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ .. 146.43 ..
6.3.d:
पितरः पितामहाश्चैव तथैव प्रपितामहाः .
त्रयो देवाः स्मृतास्तात ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वराः .. 146.43 ..
6.3.m:
Fathers, grandfathers, and likewise great-grandfathers
are traditionally regarded as the three deities, dear one: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara.

6.3.s:
pūjitaiḥ pūjitāḥ sarve tathā mātāmahāstrayaḥ .
tasmātsarvaprayatnena śrutismṛtyarthanoditān .. 146.44 ..
6.3.d:
पूजितैः पूजिताः सर्वे तथा मातामहास्त्रयः .
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन श्रुतिस्मृत्यर्थनोदितान् .. 146.44 ..
6.3.m:
When they are worshiped, all are worshiped, as well as the three maternal grandfathers.
Therefore, with every effort, [performing] the duties taught in the sense of the Śruti and Smṛti,

6.3.s:
dharmaṃ samācarannityaṃ pāpāṃśena na lipyate .
śrutismṛtyuditaṃ dharmaṃ manasāpi na laṅghayet .. 146.45 ..
6.3.d:
धर्मं समाचरन्नित्यं पापांशेन न लिप्यते .
श्रुतिस्मृत्युदितं धर्मं मनसापि न लङ्घयेत् .. 146.45 ..
6.3.m:
always practicing righteousness, one is not tainted by a fraction of sin.
One should not transgress, even in thought, the righteousness taught in the Śruti and Smṛti,

6.3.s:
iha loke pare caiva yadīcchecchreya ātmanaḥ .
pitāputrau sadāpyekau bimbādbimbamivoddhṛtau .. 146.46 ..
6.3.d:
इह लोके परे चैव यदीच्छेच्छ्रेय आत्मनः .
पितापुत्रौ सदाप्येकौ बिम्बाद्बिम्बमिवोद्धृतौ .. 146.46 ..
6.3.m:
if one desires one's own welfare in this world and the next.
Father and son are always one, like an image drawn out from an image,

6.3.s:
vibhaktau vāvibhaktau vā śrutismṛtyarthatastathā .
uddharedātmanātmānamātmānamavasādayet .. 146.47 ..
6.3.d:
विभक्तौ वाविभक्तौ वा श्रुतिस्मृत्यर्थतस्तथा .
उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानमात्मानमवसादयेत् .. 146.47 ..
6.3.m:
whether divided or undivided according to the purport of the Śruti and Smṛti.
One should uplift oneself by oneself; one [can also] ruin oneself,

6.3.s:
piṇḍodakapradānābhyāmṛte pārtha na saṃśayaḥ .
evaṃ jñātvā prayatnena piṇḍodakaprado bhavet .. 146.48 ..
6.3.d:
पिण्डोदकप्रदानाभ्यामृते पार्थ न संशयः .
एवं ज्ञात्वा प्रयत्नेन पिण्डोदकप्रदो भवेत् .. 146.48 ..
6.3.m:
by lacking the offerings of rice-balls and water, O son of Pṛthā, there is no doubt.
Knowing this, one should diligently offer rice-balls and water.

6.3.s:
āyurdharmo yaśastejaḥ santatiścaiva vardhate .
pṛthivyāṃ sāgarāntāyāṃ pitṛkṣetrāṇi yāni ca .. 146.49 ..
6.3.d:
आयुर्धर्मो यशस्तेजः सन्ततिश्चैव वर्धते .
पृथिव्यां सागरान्तायां पितृक्षेत्राणि यानि च .. 146.49 ..
6.3.m:
Lifespan, righteousness, fame, splendor, and offspring increase.
And whatever sacred fields for the ancestors exist on the earth bounded by oceans,

6.3.s:
tāni te sampravakṣyāmi yeṣu dattaṃ mahāphalam .
gayāyāṃ puṣkare jyeṣṭhe prayāge naimiṣe tathā .. 146.50 ..
6.3.d:
तानि ते सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि येषु दत्तं महाफलम् .
गयायां पुष्करे ज्येष्ठे प्रयागे नैमिषे तथा .. 146.50 ..
6.3.m:
I shall declare them to you, where what is given bears great fruit:
at Gayā, at the foremost Puṣkara, at Prayāga, and at Naimiṣa,

6.3.s:
saṃnihatyāṃ kurukṣetre prabhāse kurunandana .
piṇḍodakapradānena yatphalaṃ kathitaṃ budhaiḥ .. 146.51 ..
6.3.d:
संनिहत्यां कुरुक्षेत्रे प्रभासे कुरुनन्दन .
पिण्डोदकप्रदानेन यत्फलं कथितं बुधैः .. 146.51 ..
6.3.m:
at Saṃnihiti, in Kurukṣetra, and in Prabhāsa, O delight of the Kurus—
whatever reward the wise speak of from giving rice-balls and water,

6.3.s:
asmāhake tadāpnoti narmadāyāṃ na saṃśayaḥ .
tatra brahmā murāriśca rudraśca umayā saha .. 146.52 ..
6.3.d:
अस्माहके तदाप्नोति नर्मदायां न संशयः .
तत्र ब्रह्मा मुरारिश्च रुद्रश्च उमया सह .. 146.52 ..
6.3.m:
one obtains that at Asmāhaka on the Narmadā, without a doubt.
There Brahmā and Murāri, and Rudra along with Umā,

6.3.s:
indrādyā devatāḥ sarve pitaro munayastathā .
sāgarāḥ saritaścaiva parvatāśca balāhakāḥ .. 146.53 ..
6.3.d:
इन्द्राद्या देवताः सर्वे पितरो मुनयस्तथा .
सागराः सरितश्चैव पर्वताश्च बलाहकाः .. 146.53 ..
6.3.m:
all the deities headed by Indra, the ancestors, and the sages,
the oceans, the rivers, the mountains, and the clouds,

6.3.s:
tiṣṭhanti pitaraḥ sarve sarvatīrthādhikaṃ tataḥ .
sthitā brahmaśilā tatra gajakumbhanibhā nṛpa .. 146.54 ..
6.3.d:
तिष्ठन्ति पितरः सर्वे सर्वतीर्थाधिकं ततः .
स्थिता ब्रह्मशिला तत्र गजकुम्भनिभा नृप .. 146.54 ..
6.3.m:
all the ancestors dwell there; therefore, it is superior to all sacred fords.
There stands the Brahma-rock, resembling an elephant's forehead-bump, O king.

6.3.s:
kalau na dṛśyā bhavati pradhānaṃ yadgayāśiraḥ .
vaiśākhe māsi samprāpte'māvāsyāṃ nṛpottama .. 146.55 ..
6.3.d:
कलौ न दृश्या भवति प्रधानं यद्गयाशिरः .
वैशाखे मासि सम्प्राप्तेऽमावास्यां नृपोत्तम .. 146.55 ..
6.3.m:
In the Kali age it cannot be seen—that which is the foremost Gayā-śiras.
When the new moon of the month of Vaiśākha arrives, O best of kings,

6.3.s:
vyāpya sā tiṣṭhate tīrthaṃ gajakumbhanibhā śilā .
tacca gavyūtimātraṃ hi tīrthaṃ tataḥ pravakṣate .. 146.56 ..
6.3.d:
व्याप्य सा तिष्ठते तीर्थं गजकुम्भनिभा शिला .
तच्च गव्यूतिमात्रं हि तीर्थं ततः प्रवक्षते .. 146.56 ..
6.3.m:
that rock, resembling an elephant's forehead-bump, stands pervading the sacred ford.
That sacred ford is said to measure just one gavyūti.

6.3.s:
tasmindine tatra gatvā yastu śrāddhaprado bhavet .
pitṝṇāmakṣayā tṛptirjāyate śatavārṣikī .. 146.57 ..
6.3.d:
तस्मिन्दिने तत्र गत्वा यस्तु श्राद्धप्रदो भवेत् .
पितॄणामक्षया तृप्तिर्जायते शतवार्षिकी .. 146.57 ..
6.3.m:
He who goes there on that day and offers a śrāddha,
for his ancestors an imperishable satisfaction of a hundred years is produced.

6.3.s:
anyasyāmapyamāvāsyāṃ yaḥ snātvā vijitendriyaḥ .
karoti manujaḥ śrāddhaṃ vidhivanmantrasaṃyutam .. 146.58 ..
6.3.d:
अन्यस्यामप्यमावास्यां यः स्नात्वा विजितेन्द्रियः .
करोति मनुजः श्राद्धं विधिवन्मन्त्रसंयुतम् .. 146.58 ..
6.3.m:
Even on any other new moon day, a self-controlled man who bathes
and performs a śrāddha according to rule, accompanied by mantras,

6.3.s:
tasya puṇyaphalaṃ yatsyāttacchṛṇuṣva narādhipa .
agniṣṭomāśvamedhābhyāṃ vājapeyasya yatphalam .. 146.59 ..
6.3.d:
तस्य पुण्यफलं यत्स्यात्तच्छृणुष्व नराधिप .
अग्निष्टोमाश्वमेधाभ्यां वाजपेयस्य यत्फलम् .. 146.59 ..
6.3.m:
listen to what merit and reward belong to him, O ruler of men:
Whatever is the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma and the horse sacrifice, and of the Vājapeya,

6.3.s:
tatphalaṃ samavāpnoti yathā me śaṅkaro'bravīt .
rauravādiṣu sarveṣu narakeṣu vyavasthitāḥ .. 146.60 ..
6.3.d:
तत्फलं समवाप्नोति यथा मे शङ्करोऽब्रवीत् .
रौरवादिषु सर्वेषु नरकेषु व्यवस्थिताः .. 146.60 ..
6.3.m:
that fruit he fully attains, just as Śaṅkara told me.
Those who reside in all the hells such as Raurava—

6.3.s:
pitā pitāmahādyāśca pitṛke mātṛke tathā .
piṇḍodakena caikena tarpaṇena viśeṣataḥ .. 146.61 ..
6.3.d:
पिता पितामहाद्याश्च पितृके मातृके तथा .
पिण्डोदकेन चैकेन तर्पणेन विशेषतः .. 146.61 ..
6.3.m:
the father, grandfathers, and others on the paternal as well as on the maternal side—
by a single offering of rice-balls and water, especially by libation,

6.3.s:
krīḍanti pitṛlokasthā yāvadābhūtasamplavam .
ye karmasthā vikarmasthā ye jātāḥ pretakalmaṣāḥ .. 146.62 ..
6.3.d:
क्रीडन्ति पितृलोकस्था यावदाभूतसम्प्लवम् .
ये कर्मस्था विकर्मस्था ये जाताः प्रेतकल्मषाः .. 146.62 ..
6.3.m:
dwell in the world of the ancestors, rejoicing until the dissolution of all beings.
Those who are performing rituals, those performing forbidden deeds, and those who have become impure ghosts,

6.3.s:
piṇḍenaikena mucyante te'pi tatra na saṃśayaḥ .
asmāhake śilā divyā tiṣṭhate gajasannibhā .. 146.63 ..
6.3.d:
पिण्डेनैकेन मुच्यन्ते तेऽपि तत्र न संशयः .
अस्माहके शिला दिव्या तिष्ठते गजसन्निभा .. 146.63 ..
6.3.m:
even they are liberated by a single rice-ball there; there is no doubt.
At Asmāhaka stands a divine rock resembling an elephant,

6.3.s:
brahmaṇā nirmitā pūrvaṃ sarvapāpakṣayaṃkarī .
uparyasyā yathānyāyaṃ pitṝnuddiśya bhārata .. 146.64 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रह्मणा निर्मिता पूर्वं सर्वपापक्षयंकरी .
उपर्यस्या यथान्यायं पितॄनुद्दिश्य भारत .. 146.64 ..
6.3.m:
fashioned anciently by Brahmā, destroying all sins.
Upon it, duly dedicated to the ancestors, O descendant of Bharata,

6.3.s:
dakṣiṇāgreṣu darbheṣu dadyātpiṇḍānvicakṣaṇaḥ .
bhūmau cānnena siddhena śrāddhaṃ kṛtvā yathāvidhi .. 146.65 ..
6.3.d:
दक्षिणाग्रेषु दर्भेषु दद्यात्पिण्डान्विचक्षणः .
भूमौ चान्नेन सिद्धेन श्राद्धं कृत्वा यथाविधि .. 146.65 ..
6.3.m:
the wise man should place rice-balls upon darbha grasses with tips pointing southward;
and having performed a śrāddha on the ground with prepared food according to rule,

6.3.s:
śrāddhibhyo vastrayugmāni chatropānatkamaṇḍalu .
dakṣiṇā vividhā deyā pitṝnuddiśya bhārata .. 146.66 ..
6.3.d:
श्राद्धिभ्यो वस्त्रयुग्मानि छत्रोपानत्कमण्डलु .
दक्षिणा विविधा देया पितॄनुद्दिश्य भारत .. 146.66 ..
6.3.m:
pairs of garments, parasols, sandals, and water pots should be given to the śrāddha participants,
and diverse priestly fees dedicated to the ancestors, O descendant of Bharata.

6.3.s:
yo dadāti dvijaśreṣṭha tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu .
tasya te dvādaśābdāni tṛptiṃ yānti na saṃśayaḥ .. 146.67 ..
6.3.d:
यो ददाति द्विजश्रेष्ठ तस्य पुण्यफलं शृणु .
तस्य ते द्वादशाब्दानि तृप्तिं यान्ति न संशयः .. 146.67 ..
6.3.m:
He who gives them, O best of the twice-born—hear the fruit of his merit:
They attain satisfaction for twelve years; of this there is no doubt.

6.3.s:
asmāhake mahārāja pitaraśca pitāmahāḥ .
vāyubhūtā nirīkṣante āgacchantaṃ svagotrajam .. 146.68 ..
6.3.d:
अस्माहके महाराज पितरश्च पितामहाः .
वायुभूता निरीक्षन्ते आगच्छन्तं स्वगोत्रजम् .. 146.68 ..
6.3.m:
At Asmāhaka, O great king, the fathers and grandfathers,
having become air, watch for a man born in their clan who is arriving:

6.3.s:
atra tīrthe suto'bhyetya snātvā toyaṃ pradāsyati .
śrāddhaṃ vā piṇḍadānaṃ vā tena yāsyāma sadgatim .. 146.69 ..
6.3.d:
अत्र तीर्थे सुतोऽभ्येत्य स्नात्वा तोयं प्रदास्यति .
श्राद्धं वा पिण्डदानं वा तेन यास्याम सद्गतिम् .. 146.69 ..
6.3.m:
‘Our son will come to this sacred ford, bathe, and offer water,
or a śrāddha, or an offering of rice-balls; through that we shall reach a good destination.’

6.3.s:
snāne kṛte tu ye kecijjāyante vastravipluṣaḥ .
prīṇayennarakasthāṃstu taiḥ pitṝnnātra saṃśayaḥ .. 146.70 ..
6.3.d:
स्नाने कृते तु ये केचिज्जायन्ते वस्त्रविप्लुषः .
प्रीणयेन्नरकस्थांस्तु तैः पितॄन्नात्र संशयः .. 146.70 ..
6.3.m:
When the bath is performed, whatever drops of water come from the clothes—
with them he pleases those ancestors who reside in hell; there is no doubt of this.

6.3.s:
keśodabindavastasya ye cānye lepabhājinaḥ .
tṛpyantyanagninasaṃskārā yaṃ mṛtāḥ syuḥ svagotrajāḥ .. 146.71 ..
6.3.d:
केशोदबिन्दवस्तस्य ये चान्ये लेपभाजिनः .
तृप्यन्त्यनग्निनसंस्कारा यं मृताः स्युः स्वगोत्रजाः .. 146.71 ..
6.3.m:
By the drops of water from his hair, and whatever other [offerings] belong to the scrapings of the hand,
those who died without fire-rites and those born in his own clan are satisfied.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu ye kecicchrāddhaṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ .
narakāduddharantyāśu japantaḥ pitṛsaṃhitām .. 146.72 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु ये केचिच्छ्राद्धं कृत्वा विधानतः .
नरकादुद्धरन्त्याशु जपन्तः पितृसंहिताम् .. 146.72 ..
6.3.m:
Indeed, whoever performs a śrāddha according to rule at that sacred ford,
reciting the Pitṛsaṃhitā, swiftly delivers [them] from hell.

6.3.s:
vanaspatigate some yadā somadinaṃ bhavet .
akṣayāllabhate lokānpiṇḍenaikena mānavaḥ .. 146.73 ..
6.3.d:
वनस्पतिगते सोमे यदा सोमदिनं भवेत् .
अक्षयाल्लभते लोकान्पिण्डेनैकेन मानवः .. 146.73 ..
6.3.m:
When Soma is in the lunar mansion of plants and it is Monday,
a man attains imperishable worlds by means of a single rice-ball.

6.3.s:
akṣayaṃ tatra vai sarvaṃ jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .
narakāduddharantyāśu japante pitṛsaṃhitām .. 146.74 ..
6.3.d:
अक्षयं तत्र वै सर्वं जायते नात्र संशयः .
नरकादुद्धरन्त्याशु जपन्ते पितृसंहिताम् .. 146.74 ..
6.3.m:
Everything there becomes imperishable; of this there is no doubt.
Reciting the Pitṛsaṃhitā, they swiftly deliver [them] from hell.

6.3.s:
tasmiṃstīrthe tvamāvāsyāṃ pitṝnuddiśya bhārata .
nīlaṃ sarvāṅgasampūrṇaṃ yo'bhiṣicya samutsṛjet .. 146.75 ..
6.3.d:
तस्मिंस्तीर्थे त्वमावास्यां पितॄनुद्दिश्य भारत .
नीलं सर्वाङ्गसम्पूर्णं योऽभिषिच्य समुत्सृजेत् .. 146.75 ..
6.3.m:
At that sacred ford, on the new moon day, dedicated to the ancestors, O descendant of Bharata,
whoever consecrates and releases a dark bull possessing all auspicious marks,

6.3.s:
tasya puṇyaphalaṃ vaktuṃ na tu vācaspatiḥ kṣamaḥ .
asmāhake vṛṣotsargādyatpuṇyaṃ samavāpyate .. 146.76 ..
6.3.d:
तस्य पुण्यफलं वक्तुं न तु वाचस्पतिः क्षमः .
अस्माहके वृषोत्सर्गाद्यत्पुण्यं समवाप्यते .. 146.76 ..
6.3.m:
even the Lord of Speech is not capable of describing his meritorious fruit.
Whatever merit is attained by the release of a bull at Asmāhaka,

6.3.s:
tava śuśrūṣaṇātsarvaṃ tatpravakṣyāmi bhārata .
rauravādiṣu ye kiṃcitpacyante tasya pūrvajāḥ .. 146.77 ..
6.3.d:
तव शुश्रूषणात्सर्वं तत्प्रवक्ष्यामि भारत .
रौरवादिषु ये किंचित्पच्यन्ते तस्य पूर्वजाः .. 146.77 ..
6.3.m:
I shall tell it all to you because of your desire to hear, O descendant of Bharata.
Whatever ancestors of his are roasted in the Raurava and other hells,

6.3.s:
vṛṣotsargeṇa tānsarvāṃstārayedekaviṃśatim .
lohito yastu varṇena mukhe pucche ca pāṇḍuraḥ .. 146.78 ..
6.3.d:
वृषोत्सर्गेण तान्सर्वांस्तारयेदेकविंशतिम् .
