लोहितो यस्तु वर्णेन मुखे पुच्छे च पाण्डुरः .. 146.78 ..
6.3.m:
by the release of a bull he delivers all twenty-one of them.
One that is reddish in color, but pale at the face and tail,

6.3.s:
piṅgaḥ khuraviṣāṇābhyāṃ sa nīlo vṛṣa ucyate .
yastu sarvāṅgapiṅgaśca śvetaḥ pucchakhureṣu ca .. 146.79 ..
6.3.d:
पिङ्गः खुरविषाणाभ्यां स नीलो वृष उच्यते .
यस्तु सर्वाङ्गपिङ्गश्च श्वेतः पुच्छखुरेषु च .. 146.79 ..
6.3.m:
and tawny at the hooves and horns, is called a ‘dark’ (nīla) bull.
One that is tawny throughout all limbs and white at the tail and hooves,

6.3.s:
sa piṅgo vṛṣa ityāhuḥ pitṝṇāṃ prītivardhanaḥ .
pārāvatasavarṇaśca lalāṭe tilako bhavet .. 146.80 ..
6.3.d:
स पिङ्गो वृष इत्याहुः पितॄणां प्रीतिवर्धनः .
पारावतसवर्णश्च ललाटे तिलको भवेत् .. 146.80 ..
6.3.m:
they call a tawny bull; it increases the pleasure of the ancestors.
One having the color of a pigeon and a mark on the forehead,

6.3.s:
taṃ vṛṣaṃ babhrumityāhuḥ pūrṇaṃ sarvāṅgaśobhanam .
sarvāṅgeṣvekavarṇo yaḥ piṅgaḥ pucchakhureṣu ca .. 146.81 ..
6.3.d:
तं वृषं बभ्रुमित्याहुः पूर्णं सर्वाङ्गशोभनम् .
सर्वाङ्गेष्वेकवर्णो यः पिङ्गः पुच्छखुरेषु च .. 146.81 ..
6.3.m:
they call that bull ‘brown’ (babhru), complete and beautiful in all limbs.
One that is of a single color in all limbs, but tawny at the tail and hooves,

6.3.s:
khurapiṅgaṃ tamityāhuḥ pitṝṇāṃ sadgatipradam .
nīlaṃ sarvaśarīreṇa svāraktanayanaṃ dṛḍham .. 146.82 ..
6.3.d:
खुरपिङ्गं तमित्याहुः पितॄणां सद्गतिप्रदम् .
नीलं सर्वशरीरेण स्वारक्तनयनं दृढम् .. 146.82 ..
6.3.m:
they call ‘tawny-hoofed’ (khurapiṅga); it grants a good destination to the ancestors.
One that is dark across the whole body, with reddish eyes, and strong,

6.3.s:
tameva nīlamityāhurnīlaḥ pañcavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ .
yastu vaiśyagṛhe jātaḥ sa vai nīlo viśiṣyate .. 146.83 ..
6.3.d:
तमेव नीलमित्याहुर्नीलः पञ्चविधः स्मृतः .
यस्तु वैश्यगृहे जातः स वै नीलो विशिष्यते .. 146.83 ..
6.3.m:
that indeed they call the dark [bull]; the dark one is recorded as fivefold.
However, one born in the house of a vaiśya is especially distinguished as a dark bull.

6.3.s:
na vāhayedgṛhe jātaṃ vatsakaṃ tu kadācana .
tenaiva ca vṛṣotsarge pitṝṇāmanṛṇo bhavet .. 146.84 ..
6.3.d:
न वाहयेद्गृहे जातं वत्सकं तु कदाचन .
तेनैव च वृषोत्सर्गे पितॄणामनृणो भवेत् .. 146.84 ..
6.3.m:
One should never yoke a calf born in one's house;
by using that very [calf] for the release of a bull, one becomes free of debt to the ancestors.

6.3.s:
jātaṃ tu svagṛhe vatsaṃ dvijanmā yastu vāhayet .
patanti pitarastasya brahmakokagatā api .. 146.85 ..
6.3.d:
जातं तु स्वगृहे वत्सं द्विजन्मा यस्तु वाहयेत् .
पतन्ति पितरस्तस्य ब्रह्मकोकगता अपि .. 146.85 ..
6.3.m:
If a twice-born person yokes a calf born in his own home,
his ancestors fall, even if they have reached the world of Brahmā.

6.3.s:
yathāyathā hi pibati pītvā dhūnāti mastakam .
pibanpitṝn prīṇayati narakāduddhareddhunan .. 146.86 ..
6.3.d:
यथायथा हि पिबति पीत्वा धूनाति मस्तकम् .
पिबन्पितॄन् प्रीणयति नरकादुद्धरेद्धुनन् .. 146.86 ..
6.3.m: For as he drinks, and having drunk shakes his head, / in drinking he satisfies the ancestors, and in shaking [his head] he delivers them from hell.

6.3.s:
yathā pucchābhighātena skandhaṃ gacchanti bindavaḥ .
narakāduddharantyāśu patitān gotriṇastathā .. 146.87 ..
6.3.d:
यथा पुच्छाभिघातेन स्कन्धं गच्छन्ति बिन्दवः .
नरकादुद्धरन्त्याशु पतितान् गोत्रिणस्तथा .. 146.87 ..
6.3.m: Just as the drops reach his shoulder by the lashing of his tail, / so they quickly deliver from hell those kinsmen who have fallen [there].

6.3.s:
garjanprāvṛṣi kāle tu viṣāṇābhyāṃ bhuvaṃ likhan .
khurebhyo yā mṛdudbhūtā tayā saṃprīṇayedṛṣīn .. 146.88 ..
6.3.d:
गर्जन्प्रावृषि काले तु विषाणाभ्यां भुवं लिखन् .
खुरेभ्यो या मृदुद्भूता तया संप्रीणयेदृषीन् .. 146.88 ..
6.3.m: Bellowing in the rainy season while scratching the earth with both horns, / by the dust that rises from his hooves he completely pleases the seers.

6.3.s:
pibanpitṝn prīṇayate khādanollekhane surān .
garjannṛṣimanuṣyāṃśca dharmarūpo hi dharmaja .. 146.89 ..
6.3.d:
पिबन्पितॄन् प्रीणयते खादनोल्लेखने सुरान् .
गर्जन्नृषिमनुष्यांश्च धर्मरूपो हि धर्मज .. 146.89 ..
6.3.m: In drinking he satisfies the ancestors; in eating and digging up [the earth] he satisfies the gods; / in bellowing he pleases the seers and mortals, for he is the embodiment of dharma, O son of Dharma.

6.3.s:
bhūtairvāpi piśācairvā cāturthikajvareṇa vā .
gṛhīto'smāhakaṃ gacchetsarveṣāmādhināśanam .. 146.90 ..
6.3.d:
भूतैर्वापि पिशाचैर्वा चातुर्थिकज्वरेण वा .
गृहीतोऽस्माहकं गच्छेत्सर्वेषामाधिनाशनम् .. 146.90 ..
6.3.m: One who is seized by bhūtas, piśācas, or a quartan fever / should go to Asmāhaka, which destroys all afflictions.

6.3.s:
snātvā tu vimale toye darbhagranthiṃ nibandhayet .
mastake bāhumūle vā nābhyāṃ vā galake'pi vā .. 146.91 ..
6.3.d:
स्नात्वा तु विमले तोये दर्भग्रन्थिं निबन्धयेत् .
मस्तके बाहुमूले वा नाभ्यां वा गलकेऽपि वा .. 146.91 ..
6.3.m: Having bathed in the pure water, he should tie a knot of darbha grass / on the head, or at the base of the arm, or on the navel, or around the throat.

6.3.s:
gatvā devasamīpaṃ ca prādakṣiṇyena keśavam .
tataḥ samuccaranmantraṃ gāyatryā vātha vaiṣṇavam .. 146.92 ..
6.3.d:
गत्वा देवसमीपं च प्रादक्षिण्येन केशवम् .
ततः समुच्चरन्मन्त्रं गायत्र्या वाथ वैष्णवम् .. 146.92 ..
6.3.m: Having approached the god Keśava, [circumambulating] him clockwise, / he should then recite the mantra, either with the Gāyatrī or a Vaiṣṇava [formula]:

6.3.s:
nārāyaṇaṃ śaraṇyeśaṃ sarvadevanamaskṛtam .
namo yajñāṅgasambhūta sarvavyāpinnamo'stu te .. 146.93 ..
6.3.d:
नारायणं शरण्येशं सर्वदेवनमस्कृतम् .
नमो यज्ञाङ्गसम्भूत सर्वव्यापिन्नमोऽस्तु ते .. 146.93 ..
6.3.m: ‘O Nārāyaṇa, Lord of refuge, bowed to by all the gods! / Homage to you who arose from the limbs of sacrifice, O all-pervading one, homage to you!

6.3.s:
namo namaste deveśa padmagarbha sanātana .
dāmodara jayānanta rakṣa māṃ śaraṇāgatam .. 146.94 ..
6.3.d:
नमो नमस्ते देवेश पद्मगर्भ सनातन .
दामोदर जयानन्त रक्ष मां शरणागतम् .. 146.94 ..
6.3.m: Homage, homage to you, Lord of the gods, lotus-wombed eternal one! / O Dāmodara, victorious infinite one, protect me who have come for refuge!

6.3.s:
tvaṃ kartā tvaṃ ca hartā ca jagatyasmiṃścarācare .
tvaṃ pālayasi bhūtāni bhuvanaṃ tvaṃ bibharṣi ca .. 146.95 ..
6.3.d:
त्वं कर्ता त्वं च हर्ता च जगत्यस्मिंश्चराचरे .
त्वं पालयसि भूतानि भुवनं त्वं बिभर्षि च .. 146.95 ..
6.3.m: You are the creator and you are the destroyer in this world of moving and unmoving beings. / You protect all beings and you sustain the universe.

6.3.s:
prasīda devadeveśa suptamaṅgaṃ prabodhaya .
tvaddhyānanirato nityaṃ tvadbhaktiparamo hare .. 146.96 ..
6.3.d:
प्रसीद देवदेवेश सुप्तमङ्गं प्रबोधय .
त्वद्ध्याननिरतो नित्यं त्वद्भक्तिपरमो हरे .. 146.96 ..
6.3.m: Be gracious, O Lord of the gods! Awaken this sleeping body! / Always devoted to meditation on you, wholly dedicated to devotion to you, O Hari!

6.3.s:
iti stuto mayā deva prasādaṃ kuru me'cyuta .
māṃ rakṣa rakṣa pāpebhyastrāyasva śaraṇāgatam .. 146.97 ..
6.3.d:
इति स्तुतो मया देव प्रसादं कुरु मेऽच्युत .
मां रक्ष रक्ष पापेभ्यस्त्रायस्व शरणागतम् .. 146.97 ..
6.3.m: Thus praised by me, O god, grant me your grace, O Acyuta! / Protect me, protect me from sins; save me who have come for refuge!’

6.3.s:
evaṃ stutvā ca deveśaṃ dānavāntakaraṃ harim .
punaruktena vai snātvā tato viprāṃstu bhojayet .. 146.98 ..
6.3.d:
एवं स्तुत्वा च देवेशं दानवान्तकरं हरिम् .
पुनरुक्तेन वै स्नात्वा ततो विप्रांस्तु भोजयेत् .. 146.98 ..
6.3.m: Having thus praised the Lord of the gods, Hari who destroys the Dānavas, / and having bathed once more, he should then feed the brahmins.

6.3.s:
vedoktena vidhānena snānaṃ kṛtvā yathāvidhi .
piṇḍanirvapaṇaṃ kṛtvā vācayetsvastikaṃ tataḥ .. 146.99 ..
6.3.d:
वेदोक्तेन विधानेन स्नानं कृत्वा यथाविधि .
पिण्डनिर्वपणं कृत्वा वाचयेत्स्वस्तिकं ततः .. 146.99 ..
6.3.m: Having performed the ritual ablution according to the rule declared in the Veda as prescribed, / and having offered the funeral cakes, he should then have benedictions recited.

6.3.s:
evaṃ stutvā ca deveśaṃ dānavāntakaraṃ harim .
punaruktena vai snātvā tato viprāṃstu bhojayet .. 146.100 ..
6.3.d:
एवं स्तुत्वा च देवेशं दानवान्तकरं हरिम् .
पुनरुक्तेन वै स्नात्वा ततो विप्रांस्तु भोजयेत् .. 146.100 ..
6.3.m: Having thus praised the Lord of the gods, Hari who destroys the Dānavas, / and having bathed once more, he should then feed the brahmins.

6.3.s:
vedoktena vidhānena snānaṃ kṛtvā yathāvidhi .
evaṃ tānvācayitvā tu tato viprānvisarjayet .. 146.101 ..
6.3.d:
वेदोक्तेन विधानेन स्नानं कृत्वा यथाविधि .
एवं तान्वाचयित्वा तु ततो विप्रान्विसर्जयेत् .. 146.101 ..
6.3.m: Having performed the ritual ablution according to the rule declared in the Veda as prescribed, / and having thus had them recite blessings, he should then dismiss the brahmins.

6.3.s:
yattatroccaritaṃ kiṃcittadviprebhyo nivedayet .
tatra tīrthe naraḥ snātvā nārī vā bhaktitatparā .
śaktito dakṣiṇāṃ dadyātkṛtvā śrāddhaṃ yathāvidhi .. 146.102 ..
6.3.d:
यत्तत्रोच्चरितं किंचित्तद्विप्रेभ्यो निवेदयेत् .
तत्र तीर्थे नरः स्नात्वा नारी वा भक्तितत्परा .
शक्तितो दक्षिणां दद्यात्कृत्वा श्राद्धं यथाविधि .. 146.102 ..
6.3.m: Whatever has been uttered there, he should offer that to the brahmins. / A man or a devoted woman, having bathed at that sacred ford, / should give a priestly gift according to their means, having performed the śrāddha as prescribed.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe naro yāvatsnāpayedvidhipūrvakam .
kṣīreṇa madhunā vāpi dadhnā vā śītavāriṇā .. 146.103 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे नरो यावत्स्नापयेद्विधिपूर्वकम् .
क्षीरेण मधुना वापि दध्ना वा शीतवारिणा .. 146.103 ..
6.3.m: As long as a man bathes [the deity] at that sacred ford according to the rite, / with milk, or honey, or curd, or cold water,

6.3.s:
tāvatpuṣkarapātreṣu pibanti pitaro jalam .
ayane viṣuve caiva yugādau sūryasaṃkrame .. 146.104 ..
6.3.d:
तावत्पुष्करपात्रेषु पिबन्ति पितरो जलम् .
अयने विषुवे चैव युगादौ सूर्यसंक्रमे .. 146.104 ..
6.3.m: for so long do the ancestors drink water from lotus-leaf vessels. / At the solstices, at the equinoxes, at the beginning of a yuga, and at the sun's transit,

6.3.s:
puṣpaiḥ sampūjya deveśaṃ naivedyaṃ yaḥ pradāpayet .
so'śvamedhasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoti puṣkalam .. 146.105 ..
6.3.d:
पुष्पैः सम्पूज्य देवेशं नैवेद्यं यः प्रदापयेत् .
सोऽश्वमेधस्य यज्ञस्य फलं प्राप्नोति पुष्कलम् .. 146.105 ..
6.3.m: whoever, having worshipped the Lord of the gods with flowers, presents an offering of food, / obtains the abundant fruit of a horse sacrifice.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yo rājan sūryagrahaṇamācaret .
sūryatejonibhairyānairviṣṇuloke mahīyate .. 146.106 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यो राजन् सूर्यग्रहणमाचरेत् .
सूर्यतेजोनिभैर्यानैर्विष्णुलोके महीयते .. 146.106 ..
6.3.m: He who observes a solar eclipse at that sacred ford, O king, / is honoured in the world of Viṣṇu on aerial chariots resembling the radiance of the sun.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ śrāddhaṃ pitṛbhyaḥ samprayacchati .
satputreṇa ca tenaiva samprāptaṃ janmanaḥ phalam .. 146.107 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः श्राद्धं पितृभ्यः सम्प्रयच्छति .
सत्पुत्रेण च तेनैव सम्प्राप्तं जन्मनः फलम् .. 146.107 ..
6.3.m: He who offers a śrāddha to the ancestors at that sacred ford, / through him as a good son the purpose of birth has indeed been attained.

6.3.s:
iti śrutvā tato devāḥ sarve śakrapurogamāḥ .
brahmaviṣṇumaheśāśca sthāpayāṃcakrurīśvaram .. 146.108 ..
6.3.d:
इति श्रुत्वा ततो देवाः सर्वे शक्रपुरोगमाः .
ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेशाश्च स्थापयांचक्रुरीश्वरम् .. 146.108 ..
6.3.m: Hearing this, all the gods headed by Śakra, / together with Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa, established the Lord.

6.3.s:
sarvarogopaśamanaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam .
yastu saṃvatsaraṃ pūrṇamamāvāsyāṃ tu bhāvitaḥ .. 146.109 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वरोगोपशमनं सर्वपातकनाशनम् .
यस्तु संवत्सरं पूर्णममावास्यां तु भावितः .. 146.109 ..
6.3.m: It soothes all diseases and destroys all grave sins. / He who, purified in mind, for a full year on the new moon day

6.3.s:
pitṛbhyaḥ piṇḍadānaṃ ca kuryādasmāhake nṛpa .
tripuṣkare gayāyāṃ ca prabhāse naimiṣe tathā .. 146.110 ..
6.3.d:
पितृभ्यः पिण्डदानं च कुर्यादस्माहके नृप .
त्रिपुष्करे गयायां च प्रभासे नैमिषे तथा .. 146.110 ..
6.3.m: offers funeral cakes to the ancestors at Asmāhaka, O king, / [secures] the merit of performing a śrāddha at Tripuṣkara, Gayā, Prabhāsa, and Naimiṣa;

6.3.s:
yatpuṇyaṃ śrāddhakartṝṇāṃ tadihaiva bhaveddhruvam .
tilodakaṃ kuśairmiśraṃ yo dadyāddakṣiṇāmukhaḥ .. 146.111 ..
6.3.d:
यत्पुण्यं श्राद्धकर्तॄणां तदिहैव भवेद्ध्रुवम् .
तिलोदकं कुशैर्मिश्रं यो दद्याद्दक्षिणामुखः .. 146.111 ..
6.3.m: that merit certainly accrues right here. / Facing south, whoever offers water with sesame seeds mixed with kuśa grass

6.3.s:
manvādau ca yugādau ca vyatīpāte dinakṣaye .
yo dadyātpitṛmātṛbhyaḥ so'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet .. 146.112 ..
6.3.d:
मन्वादौ च युगादौ च व्यतीपाते दिनक्षये .
यो दद्यात्पितृमातृभ्यः सोऽश्वमेधफलं लभेत् .. 146.112 ..
6.3.m: at the start of a Manvantara, at the start of a yuga, on a vyatīpāta, and on a dinakṣaya, / to his fathers and mothers, obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.

6.3.s:
asmāhake naro yastu snātvā sampūjayeddharim .
brahmāṇaṃ śaṅkaraṃ bhaktyā kuryājjāgaraṇakriyām .. 146.113 ..
6.3.d:
अस्माहके नरो यस्तु स्नात्वा सम्पूजयेद्धरिम् .
ब्रह्माणं शङ्करं भक्त्या कुर्याज्जागरणक्रियाम् .. 146.113 ..
6.3.m: A man who, having bathed at Asmāhaka, worships Hari, / Brahmā, and Śaṃkara with devotion, and keeps a night vigil,

6.3.s:
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ śakrātithyamavāpnuyāt .
tatra tīrthe naraḥ snātvā yaḥ paśyati janārdanam .. 146.114 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तः शक्रातिथ्यमवाप्नुयात् .
तत्र तीर्थे नरः स्नात्वा यः पश्यति जनार्दनम् .. 146.114 ..
6.3.m: is freed from all sins and receives the hospitality of Śakra. / A man who, having bathed at that sacred ford, beholds Janārdana,

6.3.s:
viśeṣavidhinābhyarcya praṇamya ca punaḥpunaḥ .
saputreṇa ca tenaiva pitṝṇāṃ vihitā gatiḥ .. 146.115 ..
6.3.d:
विशेषविधिनाभ्यर्च्य प्रणम्य च पुनःपुनः .
सपुत्रेण च तेनैव पितॄणां विहिता गतिः .. 146.115 ..
6.3.m: and worships him with the special rites, bowing again and again, / through him as a son, the [highest] destination is secured for his ancestors.

6.3.s:
ekamūrtistrayo devā brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ .
satkāryakāraṇopetāḥ susūkṣmāḥ sumahāphalāḥ .. 146.116 ..
6.3.d:
एकमूर्तिस्त्रयो देवा ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वराः .
सत्कार्यकारणोपेताः सुसूक्ष्माः सुमहाफलाः .. 146.116 ..
6.3.m: The three gods Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara have one form; / endowed with noble cause and effect, they are extremely subtle and yield exceedingly great fruit.

6.3.s:
etatte kathitaṃ rājanmahāpātakanāśanam .
asmāhakasya māhātmyaṃ kimanyatparipṛcchasi .. 146.117 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe asmāhakatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma ṣaṭcatvāriṃśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 147
6.3.d:
एतत्ते कथितं राजन्महापातकनाशनम् .
अस्माहकस्य माहात्म्यं किमन्यत्परिपृच्छसि .. 146.117 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे अस्माहकतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम षट्चत्वारिंशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 147
6.3.m:
This has been told to you, O king, which destroys grave sins: / the māhātmya of Asmāhaka. What else do you ask?
Thus ends the one hundred and forty-sixth chapter, called 'The Description of the Māhātmya of the Sacred Ford of Asmāhaka', in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth [part], Āvantyakhaṇḍa, of the Skandapurāṇa containing eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 147

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gacchenmahīpāla siddheśvaramanuttamam .
narmadādakṣiṇe kūle tīrthaṃ paramaśobhanam .. 147.1 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेन्महीपाल सिद्धेश्वरमनुत्तमम् .
नर्मदादक्षिणे कूले तीर्थं परमशोभनम् .. 147.1 ..
6.3.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then, O protector of the earth, one should go to the unsurpassed Siddheśvara, / an exceedingly beautiful sacred ford on the southern bank of the Narmadā.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ snātvā pūjayedvṛṣabhadhvajam .
sarvapāpavinirmukto gatiṃ yātyaśvamedhinām .. 147.2 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः स्नात्वा पूजयेद्वृषभध्वजम् .
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो गतिं यात्यश्वमेधिनाम् .. 147.2 ..
6.3.m: Whoever bathes at that sacred ford and worships the bull-bannered [god], / freed from all sins, attains the destination of performers of the horse sacrifice.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ snātvā śrāddhaṃ kuryātprayatnataḥ .
pitṝṇāṃ prīṇanārthāya sarvaṃ tena kṛtaṃ bhavet .. 147.3 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः स्नात्वा श्राद्धं कुर्यात्प्रयत्नतः .
पितॄणां प्रीणनार्थाय सर्वं तेन कृतं भवेत् .. 147.3 ..
6.3.m: Whoever, having bathed at that sacred ford, performs a śrāddha with diligence / for the sake of pleasing the ancestors, everything has been accomplished by him.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe mṛtānāṃ tu jantūnāṃ nṛpasattama .
garbhavāse matisteṣāṃ na jāyeta kadācana .. 147.4 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे मृतानां तु जन्तूनां नृपसत्तम .
गर्भवासे मतिस्तेषां न जायेत कदाचन .. 147.4 ..
6.3.m: Of living creatures who die at that sacred ford, O best of kings, / the thought of dwelling in a womb never arises for them again.

6.3.s:
garbhavāso hi duḥkhāya na sukhāya kadācana .
tattīrthavāriṇā snāturna punarbhavasambhavaḥ .. 147.5 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe siddheśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma saptacatvāriṃśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 148
6.3.d:
गर्भवासो हि दुःखाय न सुखाय कदाचन .
तत्तीर्थवारिणा स्नातुर्न पुनर्भवसम्भवः .. 147.5 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे सिद्धेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम सप्तचत्वारिंशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 148
6.3.m:
Dwelling in a womb leads indeed to sorrow, never to happiness. / For one who bathes with the water of that sacred ford, there is no recurrence of rebirth.
Thus ends the one hundred and forty-seventh chapter, called 'The Description of the Māhātmya of the Sacred Ford of Siddheśvara', in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth [part], Āvantyakhaṇḍa, of the Skandapurāṇa containing eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 148

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gacchenmahīpāla tīrthamaṅgārakaṃ śivam .
uttare narmadākūle sarvapāpakṣayaṃkaram .. 148.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेन्महीपाल तीर्थमङ्गारकं शिवम् .
उत्तरे नर्मदाकूले सर्वपापक्षयंकरम् .. 148.1 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then, O protector of the earth, one should go to the auspicious Aṅgāraka sacred ford / on the northern bank of the Narmadā, which brings about the destruction of all sins.

6.3.s:
caturthyaṅgārakadine saṃkalpya kṛtaniścayaḥ .
snāyādastaṃ gate sūrye sandhyopāsanatatparaḥ .. 148.2 ..
6.3.d:
चतुर्थ्यङ्गारकदिने संकल्प्य कृतनिश्चयः .
स्नायादस्तं गते सूर्ये सन्ध्योपासनतत्परः .. 148.2 ..
6.3.m: Having made a resolution with firm resolve on the fourth lunar day falling on a Tuesday, / one should bathe when the sun has set, intent upon the twilight worship.

6.3.s:
pūjayellohitaṃ bhaktyā gandhamālyavibhūṣaṇaiḥ .
saṃsthāpyasthaṇḍile devaṃ raktacandanacarcitam .. 148.3 ..
6.3.d:
पूजयेल्लोहितं भक्त्या गन्धमाल्यविभूषणैः .
संस्थाप्यस्थण्डिले देवं रक्तचन्दनचर्चितम् .. 148.3 ..
6.3.m: One should worship the Red One with devotion, using perfumes, garlands, and ornaments, / having installed the god, anointed with red sandalwood paste, upon a sacrificial platform.

6.3.s:
aṅgārakāyeti namaḥ karṇikāyāṃ prapūjayet .
kujāya bhūmiputrāya raktāṅgāya suvāsase .. 148.4 ..
6.3.d:
अङ्गारकायेति नमः कर्णिकायां प्रपूजयेत् .
कुजाय भूमिपुत्राय रक्ताङ्गाय सुवाससे .. 148.4 ..
6.3.m: One should worship him on the pericarp with: 'Obeisance to Aṅgāraka,' / to Kuja, to the son of the Earth, to the red-limbed one, to the well-attired one;

6.3.s:
harakopodbhavāyeti svedajāyātibāhave .
sarvakāmapradāyeti pūrvādiṣu daleṣu ca .. 148.5 ..
6.3.d:
हरकोपोद्भवायेति स्वेदजायातिबाहवे .
सर्वकामप्रदायेति पूर्वादिषु दलेषु च .. 148.5 ..
6.3.m: to the one born from Hara's wrath, to the one produced from sweat, to the mighty-armed one, / to the granter of all desires, [worshipping him] on the petals beginning with the east.

6.3.s:
evaṃ sampūjya vidhivaddadyādarghyaṃ vidhānataḥ .
bhūmiputra mahāvīrya svedodbhava pinākinaḥ .. 148.6 ..
6.3.d:
एवं सम्पूज्य विधिवद्दद्यादर्घ्यं विधानतः .
भूमिपुत्र महावीर्य स्वेदोद्भव पिनाकिनः .. 148.6 ..
6.3.m: Having thus worshipped properly according to the rules, one should offer an arghya: / 'O son of the Earth, of mighty valor, born from the sweat of the Wielder of the Pināka,

6.3.s:
aṅgāraka mahātejā lohitāṅga namo'stu te .
karakaṃ vārisaṃyuktaṃ śālitaṃdulapūritam .. 148.7 ..
6.3.d:
अङ्गारक महातेजा लोहिताङ्ग नमोऽस्तु ते .
करकं वारिसंयुक्तं शालितंदुलपूरितम् .. 148.7 ..
6.3.m: O Aṅgāraka, O one of great splendor, O red-limbed one, obeisance to you!' / A water-pot filled with water, packed with śāli rice grains,

6.3.s:
sahiraṇyaṃ savastraṃ ca modakopari saṃsthitam .
brāhmaṇāya nivedyaṃ tatkujo me prīyatāmiti .. 148.8 ..
6.3.d:
सहिरण्यं सवस्त्रं च मोदकोपरि संस्थितम् .
ब्राह्मणाय निवेद्यं तत्कुजो मे प्रीयतामिति .. 148.8 ..
6.3.m: with gold and cloth, and placed upon sweetmeats, / should be offered to a brahmin, saying: 'May Kuja be pleased with me.'

6.3.s:
arghaṃ dattvā vidhānena raktacandanavāriṇā .
raktapuṣpasamākīrṇaṃ tilataṃdulamiśritam .. 148.9 ..
6.3.d:
अर्घं दत्त्वा विधानेन रक्तचन्दनवारिणा .
रक्तपुष्पसमाकीर्णं तिलतंदुलमिश्रितम् .. 148.9 ..
6.3.m: Having duly offered arghya with red sandalwood water, / scattered over with red flowers and mixed with sesamum and rice grains,

6.3.s:
kṛtvā tāmramaye pātre maṇḍale vartule śubhe .
kṛtvā śirasi tatpātraṃ jānubhyāṃ dharaṇīṃ gataḥ .. 148.10 ..
6.3.d:
कृत्वा ताम्रमये पात्रे मण्डले वर्तुले शुभे .
कृत्वा शिरसि तत्पात्रं जानुभ्यां धरणीं गतः .. 148.10 ..
6.3.m: prepared in a copper vessel within an auspicious circular diagram, / placing that vessel upon one's head and going down on one's knees upon the earth,

6.3.s:
mantrapūtaṃ mahābhāga dadyādarghyaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ .
tato bhuñjīta maunena kṣāratilāmlavarjitam .. 148.11 ..
6.3.d:
मन्त्रपूतं महाभाग दद्यादर्घ्यं विचक्षणः .
ततो भुञ्जीत मौनेन क्षारतिलाम्लवर्जितम् .. 148.11 ..
6.3.m: the wise one, O fortunate one, should offer the arghya consecrated by mantras. / Then he should eat in silence, avoiding alkaline food, sesamum, and sour things,

6.3.s:
snigdhaṃ mṛdusamadhuramātmanaḥ śreya icchatā .
evaṃ caturthe samprāpte caturthyaṅgārake nṛpa .. 148.12 ..
6.3.d:
स्निग्धं मृदुसमधुरमात्मनः श्रेय इच्छता .
एवं चतुर्थे सम्प्राप्ते चतुर्थ्यङ्गारके नृप .. 148.12 ..
6.3.m: eating unctuous, soft, and sweet food, if desiring his own welfare. / Thus, when the fourth [month] arrives on an Aṅgārakacaturthī, O king,

6.3.s:
sauvarṇaṃ kārayeddevaṃ yathāśakti surūpiṇam .
sthāpayettāmrake pātre guḍapīṭhasamanvite .. 148.13 ..
6.3.d:
सौवर्णं कारयेद्देवं यथाशक्ति सुरूपिणम् .
स्थापयेत्ताम्रके पात्रे गुडपीठसमन्विते .. 148.13 ..
6.3.m: one should have a well-formed image of the god made of gold according to one's capacity, / and place it in a copper vessel provided with a pedestal of jaggery.

6.3.s:
gandhapuṣpādibhirdevaṃ pūjayedguḍasaṃsthitam .
īśānyāṃ sthāpayeddevaṃ guḍatoyasamanvitam .. 148.14 ..
6.3.d:
गन्धपुष्पादिभिर्देवं पूजयेद्गुडसंस्थितम् .
ईशान्यां स्थापयेद्देवं गुडतोयसमन्वितम् .. 148.14 ..
6.3.m: One should worship the god placed on jaggery with perfumes, flowers, and the like; / one should place the god in the northeast together with jaggery-water.

6.3.s:
kāsāreṇa tathāgneyyāṃ sthāpayetkarakaṃ param .
raktatandulasaṃmiśraṃ nairṛtyāṃ vāyugocare .. 148.15 ..
6.3.d:
कासारेण तथाग्नेय्यां स्थापयेत्करकं परम् .
रक्ततन्दुलसंमिश्रं नैरृत्यां वायुगोचरे .. 148.15 ..
6.3.m: In the southeast, one should likewise place an excellent water-pot with wheat flour pastry; / in the southwest, mixed with red rice grains; in the region of Vāyu (the northwest),

6.3.s:
sthāpayenmodakaiḥ sārdhaṃ caturthaṃ karakaṃ budhaḥ .
sūtreṇa veṣṭitagrīvaṃ gandhamālyairalaṃkṛtam .. 148.16 ..
6.3.d:
स्थापयेन्मोदकैः सार्धं चतुर्थं करकं बुधः .
सूत्रेण वेष्टितग्रीवं गन्धमाल्यैरलंकृतम् .. 148.16 ..
6.3.m: the wise one should place a fourth water-pot along with sweetmeats, / its neck encircled with a cord, adorned with perfumes and garlands.

6.3.s:
śaṅkhatūryaninādena jayaśabdādimaṅgalaiḥ .
raktāmbaradharaṃ vipraṃ raktamālyānulepanam .. 148.17 ..
6.3.d:
शङ्खतूर्यनिनादेन जयशब्दादिमङ्गलैः .
रक्ताम्बरधरं विप्रं रक्तमाल्यानुलेपनम् .. 148.17 ..
6.3.m: With the sounding of conches and musical instruments, and auspicious cries of victory and the like, / a brahmin clad in red garments, with red garlands and red paste,

6.3.s:
vedimadhyagataṃ vāpi mahadāsanasaṃsthitam .
surūpaṃ subhagaṃ śāntaṃ sarvabhūtahite ratam .. 148.18 ..
6.3.d:
वेदिमध्यगतं वापि महदासनसंस्थितम् .
सुरूपं सुभगं शान्तं सर्वभूतहिते रतम् .. 148.18 ..
6.3.m: seated in the middle of the sacrificial altar or upon an elevated seat, / handsome, fortunate, peaceful, delighting in the welfare of all beings,

6.3.s:
vedavidyāvratasnātaṃ sarvaśāstraviśāradam .
pūjayitvā yathānyāyaṃ vācayetpāṇḍunandana .. 148.19 ..
6.3.d:
वेदविद्याव्रतस्नातं सर्वशास्त्रविशारदम् .
पूजयित्वा यथान्यायं वाचयेत्पाण्डुनन्दन .. 148.19 ..
6.3.m: bathed in the vows of Vedic lore, proficient in all the scriptures— / having worshipped him according to rule, O son of Pāṇḍu, one should have him recite the blessings.

6.3.s:
raktāṃ gāṃ ca tato dadyādraktenānaḍuhā saha .
prīyatāṃ bhūmijo devaḥ sarvadaivatapūjitaḥ .. 148.20 ..
6.3.d:
रक्तां गां च ततो दद्याद्रक्तेनानडुहा सह .
प्रीयतां भूमिजो देवः सर्वदैवतपूजितः .. 148.20 ..
6.3.m: Then one should give a red cow along with a red bull, saying: / 'May the god born of the Earth, worshipped by all deities, be pleased.'

6.3.s:
vipraṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya patnīputrasamanvitaḥ .
pitṛmātṛsuhṛtsārddhaṃ kṣamāpya ca visarjayet .. 148.21 ..
6.3.d:
विप्रं प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य पत्नीपुत्रसमन्वितः .
पितृमातृसुहृत्सार्द्धं क्षमाप्य च विसर्जयेत् .. 148.21 ..
6.3.m: Having circumambulated the brahmin, accompanied by wife and son, / and along with father, mother, and friends, one should beg his forgiveness and dismiss him.

6.3.s:
evaṃ kṛtasya tasyātha tasmiṃstīrthe viśeṣataḥ .
yatpuṇyaṃ phalamuddiṣṭaṃ tatte sarvaṃ vadāmyaham .. 148.22 ..
6.3.d:
एवं कृतस्य तस्याथ तस्मिंस्तीर्थे विशेषतः .
यत्पुण्यं फलमुद्दिष्टं तत्ते सर्वं वदाम्यहम् .. 148.22 ..
6.3.m: Now, whatever meritorious fruit is prescribed for one who has done this, / especially at that sacred ford, I shall tell you all of that:

6.3.s:
sapta janmāni rājendra surūpaḥ subhago bhavet .
tīrthasyāsya prabhāvena nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 148.23 ..
6.3.d:
सप्त जन्मानि राजेन्द्र सुरूपः सुभगो भवेत् .
तीर्थस्यास्य प्रभावेन नात्र कार्या विचारणा .. 148.23 ..
6.3.m: For seven births, O best of kings, he becomes handsome and fortunate / through the power of this sacred ford; no doubt should be entertained here.

6.3.s:
akāmo vā sakāmo vā tatra tīrthe mṛto naraḥ .
aṅgārakapuraṃ yāti devagandharvapūjitaḥ .. 148.24 ..
6.3.d:
अकामो वा सकामो वा तत्र तीर्थे मृतो नरः .
अङ्गारकपुरं याति देवगन्धर्वपूजितः .. 148.24 ..
6.3.m: Whether free of desire or full of desire, a man who dies at that sacred ford / goes to the city of Aṅgāraka, worshipped by gods and gandharvas.

6.3.s:
upabhujya yathānyāyaṃ divyānbhogānanuttamān .
iha mānuṣyaloke vai rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ .. 148.25 ..
6.3.d:
उपभुज्य यथान्यायं दिव्यान्भोगाननुत्तमान् .
इह मानुष्यलोके वै राजा भवति धार्मिकः .. 148.25 ..
6.3.m: Having duly enjoyed supreme divine pleasures, / he indeed becomes a righteous king here in the world of mortals,

6.3.s:
surūpaḥ subhagaścaiva sarvavyādhivivarjitaḥ .
jīvedvarṣaśataṃ sāgraṃ sarvalokanamaskṛtaḥ .. 148.26 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇe ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe maṅgaleśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmāṣṭācatvāriṃśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 149
6.3.d:
सुरूपः सुभगश्चैव सर्वव्याधिविवर्जितः .
जीवेद्वर्षशतं साग्रं सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः .. 148.26 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराणे एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे मङ्गलेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामाष्टाचत्वारिंशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 149
6.3.m:
handsome, fortunate, free from all diseases; / he lives for a full hundred years, bowed to by all the world.
Thus ends the one hundred and forty-eighth chapter, named 'Description of the Glory of Maṅgaleśvara Tīrtha', in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth Avantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].
Chapter 149

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tasyaivānantaraṃ tīrthaṃ liṅgeśvaramiti śrutam .
darśanāddevadevasya yatra pāpaṃ praṇaśyati .. 149.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
तस्यैवानन्तरं तीर्थं लिङ्गेश्वरमिति श्रुतम् .
दर्शनाद्देवदेवस्य यत्र पापं प्रणश्यति .. 149.1 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Immediately after that is the sacred ford known as Liṅgeśvara, / where sin is destroyed through the darśana of the God of gods.

6.3.s:
kṛtvā tu kadanaṃ ghoraṃ dānavānāṃ yudhiṣṭhira .
vārāhaṃ rūpamāsthāya narmadāyāṃ vyavasthitaḥ .. 149.2 ..
6.3.d:
कृत्वा तु कदनं घोरं दानवानां युधिष्ठिर .
वाराहं रूपमास्थाय नर्मदायां व्यवस्थितः .. 149.2 ..
6.3.m: Having wrought a terrible slaughter of the Dānavas, O Yudhiṣṭhira, / [Viṣṇu], assuming the form of the Boar, took up his abode on the Narmadā.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ snānaṃ kṛtvā devaṃ namasyati .
sa mucyate nṛpaśreṣṭha mahāpāpaiḥ purākṛtaiḥ .. 149.3 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः स्नानं कृत्वा देवं नमस्यति .
स मुच्यते नृपश्रेष्ठ महापापैः पुराकृतैः .. 149.3 ..
6.3.m: One who takes a ritual ablution at that sacred ford and bows down to the god, / O best of kings, is freed from great sins committed in the past.

6.3.s:
dvādaśyāṃ kṛṣṇapakṣasya śukle ca samupoṣitaḥ .
gandhamālyairjagannāthaṃ pūjayetpāṇḍunandana .. 149.4 ..
6.3.d:
द्वादश्यां कृष्णपक्षस्य शुक्ले च समुपोषितः .
गन्धमाल्यैर्जगन्नाथं पूजयेत्पाण्डुनन्दन .. 149.4 ..
6.3.m: Having fasted completely on the twelfth day of the dark fortnight and of the bright [fortnight], / one should worship the Lord of the Universe with perfumes and garlands, O son of Pāṇḍu.

6.3.s:
brāhmaṇāṃśca mahābhāga dānasaṃmānabhojanaiḥ .
pūjayetparayā bhaktyā tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu .. 149.5 ..
6.3.d:
ब्राह्मणांश्च महाभाग दानसंमानभोजनैः .
पूजयेत्परया भक्त्या तस्य पुण्यफलं शृणु .. 149.5 ..
6.3.m: And one should worship brahmins, O fortunate one, with gifts, honor, and meals, / with supreme devotion; hear the meritorious fruit thereof:

6.3.s:
satrayājiphalaṃ janturlabhate dvādaśābdakaiḥ .
brāhmaṇānbhojayaṃstatra tadeva labhate phalam .. 149.6 ..
6.3.d:
सत्रयाजिफलं जन्तुर्लभते द्वादशाब्दकैः .
ब्राह्मणान्भोजयंस्तत्र तदेव लभते फलम् .. 149.6 ..
6.3.m: A living being obtains the fruit of performing a sacrificial session for twelve years; / feeding brahmins there, he obtains that very fruit.

6.3.s:
tarpayitvā pitṝn devān snātvā tadgatamānasaḥ .
japeddvādaśanāmāni devasya purataḥ sthitaḥ .. 149.7 ..
6.3.d:
तर्पयित्वा पितॄन् देवान् स्नात्वा तद्गतमानसः .
जपेद्द्वादशनामानि देवस्य पुरतः स्थितः .. 149.7 ..
6.3.m: Having offered libations to the ancestors and gods, having bathed, with mind fixed on Him, / standing before the god, one should chant the twelve names.

6.3.s:
māsi māsi nirāhāro dvādaśyāṃ kurunandana .
keśavaṃ pūjayennityaṃ māsi mārgaśire budhaḥ .. 149.8 ..
6.3.d:
मासि मासि निराहारो द्वादश्यां कुरुनन्दन .
केशवं पूजयेन्नित्यं मासि मार्गशिरे बुधः .. 149.8 ..
6.3.m: Fasting month after month on the twelfth day, O delight of the Kurus, / the wise one should always worship Keśava in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa,

6.3.s:
pauṣe nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ māghamāse tu mādhavam .
govindaṃ phālgune māsi viṣṇuṃ caitre samarcayet .. 149.9 ..
6.3.d:
पौषे नारायणं देवं माघमासे तु माधवम् .
गोविन्दं फाल्गुने मासि विष्णुं चैत्रे समर्चयेत् .. 149.9 ..
6.3.m: the god Nārāyaṇa in Pauṣa, Mādhava in the month of Māgha, / Govinda in the month of Phālguna, and Viṣṇu in Caitra.

6.3.s:
vaiśākhe madhuhantāraṃ jyeṣṭhe devaṃ trivikramam .
vāmanaṃ tu tathāṣāḍhe śrāvaṇe śrīdharaṃ smaret .. 149.10 ..
6.3.d:
वैशाखे मधुहन्तारं ज्येष्ठे देवं त्रिविक्रमम् .
वामनं तु तथाषाढे श्रावणे श्रीधरं स्मरेत् .. 149.10 ..
6.3.m: In Vaiśākha one should remember the Slayer of Madhu, in Jyeṣṭha the god Trivikrama, / Vāmana in Āṣāḍha, and Śrīdhara in Śrāvaṇa.

6.3.s:
hṛṣīkeśaṃ bhādrapade padmanābhaṃ tathāśvine .
dāmodaraṃ kārttike tu kīrtayannāvasīdati .. 149.11 ..
6.3.d:
हृषीकेशं भाद्रपदे पद्मनाभं तथाश्विने .
दामोदरं कार्त्तिके तु कीर्तयन्नावसीदति .. 149.11 ..
6.3.m: Chanting Hṛṣīkeśa in Bhādrapada, Padmanābha in Āśvina, / and Dāmodara in Kārttika, one does not perish.

6.3.s:
vācikaṃ mānasaṃ pāpaṃ karmajaṃ yatpurā kṛtam .
tannaśyati na sandeho māsanāmānukīrtanāt .. 149.12 ..
6.3.d:
वाचिकं मानसं पापं कर्मजं यत्पुरा कृतम् .
तन्नश्यति न सन्देहो मासनामानुकीर्तनात् .. 149.12 ..
6.3.m: Whatever sin was committed in the past through speech, mind, or action / is destroyed, beyond doubt, through the recitation of the names of the months.

6.3.s:
svayaṃ vinuddhaḥ satatamunmiṣannimiṣaṃstathā .
śīghraṃ prapaśya bhuñjāno mantrahīnaṃ samudgiret .. 149.13 ..
6.3.d:
स्वयं विनुद्धः सततमुन्मिषन्निमिषंस्तथा .
शीघ्रं प्रपश्य भुञ्जानो मन्त्रहीनं समुद्गिरेत् .. 149.13 ..
6.3.m: Continually driven on oneself, opening and closing the eyes, / looking about swiftly, eating, [even if] uttering [names] devoid of mantras,

6.3.s:
paramāpadgatasyāpi jantoreṣā pratikriyā .
yanmāsādhipaterviṣṇormāsanāmānukīrtanam .. 149.14 ..
6.3.d:
परमापद्गतस्यापि जन्तोरेषा प्रतिक्रिया .
यन्मासाधिपतेर्विष्णोर्मासनामानुकीर्तनम् .. 149.14 ..
6.3.m: this is the remedy even for a living being fallen into the direst calamity: / reciting the monthly name of Viṣṇu, the presiding deity of the months.

6.3.s:
tā niśāste ca divasāste māsāste ca vatsarāḥ .
narāṇāṃ saphalā yeṣu cintito bhagavānhariḥ .. 149.15 ..
6.3.d:
ता निशास्ते च दिवसास्ते मासास्ते च वत्सराः .
नराणां सफला येषु चिन्तितो भगवान्हरिः .. 149.15 ..
6.3.m: Those nights, those days, those months, and those years / are fruitful for men in which Lord Hari has been meditated upon.

6.3.s:
paramāpadgatasyāpi yasya devo janārdanaḥ .
nāvasarpati hṛtpadmātsa yogī nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 149.16 ..
6.3.d:
परमापद्गतस्यापि यस्य देवो जनार्दनः .
नावसर्पति हृत्पद्मात्स योगी नात्र संशयः .. 149.16 ..
6.3.m: Even when he has fallen into the direst calamity, he from whose heart-lotus / the god Janārdana does not slip away is a yogin; of this there is no doubt.

6.3.s:
te bhāgyahīnā manujāḥ suśocyāste bhūmibhārāya kṛtāvatārāḥ .
acetanāste paśubhiḥ samānā ye bhaktihīnā bhagavatyanante .. 149.17 ..
6.3.d:
ते भाग्यहीना मनुजाः सुशोच्यास्ते भूमिभाराय कृतावताराः .
अचेतनास्ते पशुभिः समाना ये भक्तिहीना भगवत्यनन्ते .. 149.17 ..
6.3.m: Devoid of good fortune are those men, greatly to be pitied; they have descended as an incarnation only to be a burden to the earth; / they are senseless, equal to beasts—those who are devoid of devotion to the infinite Lord.

6.3.s:
te pūrṇakāryāḥ puruṣāḥ pṛthivyāṃ te svāṅgapātādbhuvanaṃ punanti .
vicakṣaṇā viśvavibhūṣaṇāste ye bhaktiyuktā bhagavatyanante .. 149.18 ..
6.3.d:
ते पूर्णकार्याः पुरुषाः पृथिव्यां ते स्वाङ्गपाताद्भुवनं पुनन्ति .
विचक्षणा विश्वविभूषणास्ते ये भक्तियुक्ता भगवत्यनन्ते .. 149.18 ..
6.3.m: Those men have accomplished their purpose on earth; they purify the world by the fall of their own limbs [in prostration]; / they are discerning, an ornament to the universe—those who are filled with devotion to the infinite Lord. 149.18

6.3.s:
sa eva sukṛtī tena labdhaṃ janmataroḥ phalam .
citte vacasi kāye ca yasya devo janārdanaḥ .. 149.19 ..
6.3.d:
स एव सुकृती तेन लब्धं जन्मतरोः फलम् .
चित्ते वचसि काये च यस्य देवो जनार्दनः .. 149.19 ..
6.3.m: He alone is virtuous; by him the fruit of the tree of birth has been attained, / in whose heart, speech, and body the god Janārdana resides. 149.19

6.3.s:
etattīrthavaraṃ puṇyaṃ liṅgo yatra janārdanaḥ .
vañcayitvā ripūnsaṃkhye krodho bhūtvā sanātanaḥ .. 149.20 ..
6.3.d:
एतत्तीर्थवरं पुण्यं लिङ्गो यत्र जनार्दनः .
वञ्चयित्वा रिपून्संख्ये क्रोधो भूत्वा सनातनः .. 149.20 ..
6.3.m: This is an excellent, holy sacred ford, where the eternal Janārdana became a liṅga, / having deceived his enemies in battle, [assumed the form of] the Boar. 149.20

6.3.s:
upaplave candramaso raveśca yo hyaṣṭakānāmayanadvaye ca .
pānīyamapyatra tilairvimiśraṃ dadyātpitṛbhyaḥ prayato manuṣyaḥ .. 149.21 ..
6.3.d:
उपप्लवे चन्द्रमसो रवेश्च यो ह्यष्टकानामयनद्वये च .
पानीयमप्यत्र तिलैर्विमिश्रं दद्यात्पितृभ्यः प्रयतो मनुष्यः .. 149.21 ..
6.3.m: During an eclipse of the moon and sun, on the aṣṭakās, and during both solstices, / a restrained man should indeed offer even water mixed with sesame seeds to the ancestors here. 149.21

6.3.s:
ghoṇonmīlitamerurandhranivaho duḥkhābdhimajjatplavaḥ prādurbhūtarasātalodarabṛhatpaṅkārdhamagnakṣuraḥ .
phūtkārotkaranunnavātavidaladdigdantinādaśrutinyastastabdhavapuḥ śrutirbhavatu vaḥ kroḍo hariḥ śāntaye .. 149.22 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe liṅgavārāhatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmaikonapañcāśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 150
6.3.d:
घोणोन्मीलितमेरुरन्ध्रनिवहो दुःखाब्धिमज्जत्प्लवः प्रादुर्भूतरसातलोदरबृहत्पङ्कार्धमग्नक्षुरः .
फूत्कारोत्करनुन्नवातविदलद्दिग्दन्तिनादश्रुतिन्यस्तस्तब्धवपुः श्रुतिर्भवतु वः क्रोडो हरिः शान्तये .. 149.22 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे लिङ्गवाराहतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामैकोनपञ्चाशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 150
6.3.m:
May the Boar Hari bring you peace!—by whose snout the network of hollows of Mount Meru was unclosed; who was a raft for those sinking into the ocean of sorrow; / whose hooves were half-submerged in the deep mire that arose from the belly of Rasātala; whose ears were frozen, rigid in listening to the roar of the elephants of the quarters shattered by the wind blast driven by his exhalations. 149.22
Thus ends the one hundred and forty-ninth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Glory of the Sacred Ford of the Liṅga-Boar,' in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth book, Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 150

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gacchenmahārāja kusumeśvaramuttamam .
dakṣiṇe narmadākūle upapātakanāśanam .. 150.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेन्महाराज कुसुमेश्वरमुत्तमम् .
दक्षिणे नर्मदाकूले उपपातकनाशनम् .. 150.1 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then one should go, O great king, to the excellent Kusumeśvara / on the southern bank of the Narmadā, which destroys minor sins. 150.1

6.3.s:
kāmena sthāpito devaḥ kusumeśvarasaṃjñitaḥ .
khyātaḥ sarveṣu lokeṣu devadevaḥ sanātanaḥ .. 150.2 ..
6.3.d:
कामेन स्थापितो देवः कुसुमेश्वरसंज्ञितः .
ख्यातः सर्वेषु लोकेषु देवदेवः सनातनः .. 150.2 ..
6.3.m: The god named Kusumeśvara was established by Kāma; / he is renowned throughout all worlds, the eternal god of gods. 150.2

6.3.s:
kāmo manobhavo viśvaḥ kusumāyudhacāpabhṛt .
sa kāmān dadāti sarvān pūjito mīnaketanaḥ .. 150.3 ..
6.3.d:
कामो मनोभवो विश्वः कुसुमायुधचापभृत् .
स कामान् ददाति सर्वान् पूजितो मीनकेतनः .. 150.3 ..
6.3.m: Kāma, mind-born, universal, bearer of the bow and weapons of flowers, / he of the fish-banner, when worshipped, bestows all desires. 150.3

6.3.s:
tena nirdagdhakāyena cārādhya parameśvaram .
anaṅgena tathā prāptamaṅgitvaṃ narmadātaṭe .. 150.4 ..
6.3.d:
तेन निर्दग्धकायेन चाराध्य परमेश्वरम् .
अनङ्गेन तथा प्राप्तमङ्गित्वं नर्मदातटे .. 150.4 ..
6.3.m: Having worshipped the Supreme Lord when his body had been consumed by fire, / the bodiless one (Anaṅga) thus regained embodiment on the bank of the Narmadā. 150.4

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
aṅgibhṛtasya nāśatvamanaṅgasya tu me vada .
na śrutaṃ na ca me dṛṣṭaṃ bhūtapūrvaṃ kadācana .. 150.5 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
अङ्गिभृतस्य नाशत्वमनङ्गस्य तु मे वद .
न श्रुतं न च मे दृष्टं भूतपूर्वं कदाचन .. 150.5 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / Tell me how the embodied one was destroyed and then became the bodiless one; / I have neither heard nor ever seen such a thing happening before. 150.5

6.3.s:
etatsarvaṃ yathā vṛttamācakṣva dvijasattama .
śrotumicchāmi viprendra bhīmārjunayamaiḥ saha .. 150.6 ..
6.3.d:
एतत्सर्वं यथा वृत्तमाचक्ष्व द्विजसत्तम .
श्रोतुमिच्छामि विप्रेन्द्र भीमार्जुनयमैः सह .. 150.6 ..
6.3.m: Tell me everything just as it happened, O best of the twice-born; / I wish to hear it, O leader of brahmins, along with Bhīma, Arjuna, and the twins. 150.6

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
ādau kṛtayuge tāta devadevo maheśvaraḥ .
tapaścacāra vipulaṃ gaṅgāsāgarasaṃsthitaḥ .. 150.7 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
आदौ कृतयुगे तात देवदेवो महेश्वरः .
तपश्चचार विपुलं गङ्गासागरसंस्थितः .. 150.7 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / In the beginning, in the Kṛta age, O dear one, Maheśvara, the god of gods, / practiced extensive austerity while residing at Gaṅgāsāgara. 150.7

6.3.s:
tena sampāditā lokāstapasā sasurāsurāḥ .
jagmuste śaraṇaṃ sarve devadevaṃ śacīpatim .. 150.8 ..
6.3.d:
तेन सम्पादिता लोकास्तपसा ससुरासुराः .
जग्मुस्ते शरणं सर्वे देवदेवं शचीपतिम् .. 150.8 ..
6.3.m: By his austerity, the worlds along with the gods and asuras were afflicted; / they all went for refuge to the husband of Śacī, the god of gods. 150.8

6.3.s:
vyāpakaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ devadevo maheśvaraḥ .
saṃtāpayati lokāṃstrīṃstannivāraya gopate .. 150.9 ..
6.3.d:
व्यापकः सर्वभूतानां देवदेवो महेश्वरः .
संतापयति लोकांस्त्रींस्तन्निवारय गोपते .. 150.9 ..
6.3.m: 'Maheśvara, the god of gods, who pervades all beings, / torments the three worlds; avert him, O protector of the earth!' 150.9

6.3.s:
śrutvā tadvacanaṃ teṣāṃ devānāṃ balavṛtrahā .
cintayāmāsa manasā tapovighnāyacādiśat .. 150.10 ..
6.3.d:
श्रुत्वा तद्वचनं तेषां देवानां बलवृत्रहा .
चिन्तयामास मनसा तपोविघ्नायचादिशत् .. 150.10 ..
6.3.m: Hearing those words of the gods, the slayer of Bala and Vṛtra / reflected in his mind and commanded [them] to obstruct his austerity. 150.10

6.3.s:
apsarāṃ menakāṃ rambhāṃ ghṛtācīṃ ca tilottamām .
vasantaṃ kokilaṃ kāmaṃ dakṣiṇānilamuttamam .. 150.11 ..
6.3.d:
अप्सरां मेनकां रम्भां घृताचीं च तिलोत्तमाम् .
वसन्तं कोकिलं कामं दक्षिणानिलमुत्तमम् .. 150.11 ..
6.3.m: The apsarases Menakā, Rambhā, Ghṛtācī, and Tilottamā, / Spring, the cuckoo, Kāma, and the excellent southern breeze— 150.11

6.3.s:
gatvā tatra mahādevaṃ tapaścaraṇatatparam .
kṣobhayadhvaṃ yathānyāyaṃ gaṅgāsāgaravāsinam .. 150.12 ..
6.3.d:
गत्वा तत्र महादेवं तपश्चरणतत्परम् .
क्षोभयध्वं यथान्यायं गङ्गासागरवासिनम् .. 150.12 ..
6.3.m: 'Go there and disturb Mahādeva, who is intent on the practice of austerity, / dwelling at Gaṅgāsāgara, as is fitting!' 150.12

6.3.s:
evamuktāstu te sarve devarājena bhārata .
devāpsaraḥsamopetā jagmuste harasannidhau .. 150.13 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्तास्तु ते सर्वे देवराजेन भारत .
देवाप्सरःसमोपेता जग्मुस्ते हरसन्निधौ .. 150.13 ..
6.3.m: Having been spoken to thus by the king of the gods, O descendant of Bharata, / all of them, accompanied by the divine apsarases, went into the presence of Hara. 150.13

6.3.s:
vasantamāse kusumākarākule mayūradātyūhasukokilākule .
pranṛtya devāpsaragītasaṃkule pravāti vāte yamanairṛtākule .. 150.14 ..
6.3.d:
वसन्तमासे कुसुमाकराकुले मयूरदात्यूहसुकोकिलाकुले .
प्रनृत्य देवाप्सरगीतसंकुले प्रवाति वाते यमनैरृताकुले .. 150.14 ..
6.3.m: In the spring month filled with abundant flowers, filled with peacocks, water-hens, and fine cuckoos, / resplendent with dancing and songs of the divine apsarases, as the wind blew, agitated from the south and southwest, 150.14

6.3.s:
tena saṃmūrchitāḥ sarve saṃsargācca khagottamāḥ .
madhumādhavagandhena sakinnaramahoragāḥ .. 150.15 ..
6.3.d:
तेन संमूर्छिताः सर्वे संसर्गाच्च खगोत्तमाः .
मधुमाधवगन्धेन सकिन्नरमहोरगाः .. 150.15 ..
6.3.m: all the best of birds, along with the kinnaras and great serpents, / became swooned by that contact and by the fragrance of spring and Madhu. 150.15

6.3.s:
yāvadālokate tāvattadvanaṃ vyākulīkṛtam .
vīkṣate madanāviṣṭaṃ daśāvasthāgataṃ janam .. 150.16 ..
6.3.d:
यावदालोकते तावत्तद्वनं व्याकुलीकृतम् .
वीक्षते मदनाविष्टं दशावस्थागतं जनम् .. 150.16 ..
6.3.m: As far as one looked, so far was that forest agitated; / one saw people overcome with passion, having entered the ten states of love. 150.16

6.3.s:
devadevo'pi devānāmavasthātritayaṃ gataḥ .
sāttvikīṃ rājasīṃ rājaṃstāmasīṃ tāṃ śṛṇuṣva me .. 150.17 ..
6.3.d:
देवदेवोऽपि देवानामवस्थात्रितयं गतः .
सात्त्विकीं राजसीं राजंस्तामसीं तां शृणुष्व मे .. 150.17 ..
6.3.m: Even the god of gods attained the three states, / the sāttvika, the rājasa, and the tāmasa; hear that from me, O king! 150.17

6.3.s:
ekaṃ yogasamādhinā mukulitaṃ cakṣurdvitīyaṃ punaḥ pārvatyā jaghanasthalastanataṭe śṛṅgārabhārālasam .
anyaddūranirastacāpamadanakrodhānaloddīpitaṃ śambhorbhinnarasaṃ samādhisamaye netratrayaṃ pātu vaḥ .. 150.18 ..
6.3.d:
एकं योगसमाधिना मुकुलितं चक्षुर्द्वितीयं पुनः पार्वत्या जघनस्थलस्तनतटे शृङ्गारभारालसम् .
अन्यद्दूरनिरस्तचापमदनक्रोधानलोद्दीपितं शम्भोर्भिन्नरसं समाधिसमये नेत्रत्रयं पातु वः .. 150.18 ..
6.3.m: One eye closed in yogic absorption; the second languid with the weight of erotic passion upon the slope of Pārvatī's hips and breasts; / the other blazing with the fire of wrath at Madana whose bow was cast far away: may Śambhu's three eyes, bearing diverse sentiments at the time of meditation, protect you! 150.18

6.3.s:
evaṃ dṛṣṭaḥ sa devena saśaraḥ saśarāsanaḥ .
bhasmībhūto gataḥ kāmo vināśaḥ sarvadehinām .. 150.19 ..
6.3.d:
एवं दृष्टः स देवेन सशरः सशरासनः .
भस्मीभूतो गतः कामो विनाशः सर्वदेहिनाम् .. 150.19 ..
6.3.m: Seen thus by the god, with arrow and bow, / Kāma was reduced to ashes, destroyed—he who destroys all embodied beings. 150.19

6.3.s:
kāmaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṣayaṃ yātaṃ tatra devāpsarogaṇāḥ .
bhītā yathāgataṃ sarve jagmuścaiva diśo daśa .. 150.20 ..
6.3.d:
कामं दृष्ट्वा क्षयं यातं तत्र देवाप्सरोगणाः .
भीता यथागतं सर्वे जग्मुश्चैव दिशो दश .. 150.20 ..
6.3.m: Seeing Kāma destroyed, the hosts of gods and apsarases there, / terrified, fled in the ten directions just as they had come. 150.20

6.3.s:
kāmena rahitā lokāḥ sasurāsuramānavāḥ .
brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ jagmurdevā indrapurogamāḥ .. 150.21 ..
6.3.d:
कामेन रहिता लोकाः ससुरासुरमानवाः .
ब्रह्माणं शरणं जग्मुर्देवा इन्द्रपुरोगमाः .. 150.21 ..
6.3.m: The worlds, devoid of Kāma, along with gods, asuras, and mortals, / went for refuge to Brahmā, the gods led by Indra. 150.21

6.3.s:
sīdamānaṃ jagaddṛṣṭvā tamūcuḥ parameṣṭhinam .
jānāsi tvaṃ jagaccheṣaṃ prabho maithunasambhavāt .. 150.22 ..
6.3.d:
सीदमानं जगद्दृष्ट्वा तमूचुः परमेष्ठिनम् .
जानासि त्वं जगच्छेषं प्रभो मैथुनसम्भवात् .. 150.22 ..
6.3.m: Seeing the universe languishing, they said to the Supreme Lord: / 'You know, O Lord, that the continuance of the universe is due to sexual union. 150.22

6.3.s: prajāḥ sarvā viśuṣyanti kāmena rahitā vibho .. 150.23 ..
6.3.d: प्रजाः सर्वा विशुष्यन्ति कामेन रहिता विभो .. 150.23 ..
6.3.m: All creatures are wasting away, devoid of desire, O all-pervading Lord!' 150.23

6.3.s:
etacchrutvā vacasteṣāṃ devānāṃ prapitāmahaḥ .
jagāma sahitastatra yatra devo maheśvaraḥ .. 150.24 ..
6.3.d:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तेषां देवानां प्रपितामहः .
जगाम सहितस्तत्र यत्र देवो महेश्वरः .. 150.24 ..
6.3.m: Hearing this speech of those gods, the Great Grandfather / went together with them to where the god Maheśvara was. 150.24

6.3.s:
atoṣayajjagannāthaṃ sarvabhūtamaheśvaram .
stutibhistaṇḍakaiḥ stotrairvedavedāṅgasambhavaiḥ .. 150.25 ..
6.3.d:
अतोषयज्जगन्नाथं सर्वभूतमहेश्वरम् .
स्तुतिभिस्तण्डकैः स्तोत्रैर्वेदवेदाङ्गसम्भवैः .. 150.25 ..
6.3.m: He propitiated the Lord of the universe, the Maheśvara of all beings, / with hymns of praise, rhythmic verses, and hymns arising from the Vedas and Vedāṅgas. 150.25

6.3.s:
tatastuṣṭo mahādevo devānāṃ parameśvaraḥ .
uvāca madhurāṃ vāṇīṃ devānbrahmapurogamān .. 150.26 ..
6.3.d:
ततस्तुष्टो महादेवो देवानां परमेश्वरः .
उवाच मधुरां वाणीं देवान्ब्रह्मपुरोगमान् .. 150.26 ..
6.3.m: Then Mahādeva, the Supreme Lord of the gods, pleased, / spoke sweet words to the gods led by Brahmā: 150.26

6.3.s:
kiṃ kāryaṃ kaśca santāpaḥ kiṃ vāgamanakāraṇam .
devatānāmṛṣīṇāṃ ca kathyatāṃ mama māciram .. 150.27 ..
6.3.d:
किं कार्यं कश्च सन्तापः किं वागमनकारणम् .
देवतानामृषीणां च कथ्यतां मम माचिरम् .. 150.27 ..
6.3.m: 'What is the task, and what is the distress, or what is the cause of your coming, / of the deities and seers? Tell me without delay!' 150.27

6.3.s:
devā ūcuḥ .
kāmanāśājjagannāśo bhavitāyaṃ carācare .
trailokyaṃ tvaṃ punaḥ śambho utpādayitumarhasi .. 150.28 ..
6.3.d:
देवा ऊचुः .
कामनाशाज्जगन्नाशो भवितायं चराचरे .
त्रैलोक्यं त्वं पुनः शम्भो उत्पादयितुमर्हसि .. 150.28 ..
6.3.m: The gods said: / 'Because of the destruction of Kāma, this destruction of the universe will occur among moving and unmoving beings. / You ought to generate the three worlds once again, O Śambhu!' 150.28

6.3.s:
etacchrutvā vacasteṣāṃ vimṛśya parameśvaraḥ .
cintayāmāsa kāmasya vigrahaṃ bhuvi durlabham .. 150.29 ..
6.3.d:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तेषां विमृश्य परमेश्वरः .
चिन्तयामास कामस्य विग्रहं भुवि दुर्लभम् .. 150.29 ..
6.3.m: Hearing their words and reflecting, the Supreme Lord / considered the bodily form of Kāma, which is difficult to attain on earth. 150.29

6.3.s:
ājagāma tataḥ śīghramanaṅgo hyaṅgatāṃ gataḥ .
prāṇadaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ paśyatāṃ nṛpasattama .. 150.30 ..
6.3.d:
आजगाम ततः शीघ्रमनङ्गो ह्यङ्गतां गतः .
प्राणदः सर्वभूतानां पश्यतां नृपसत्तम .. 150.30 ..
6.3.m: Then the bodiless one (Anaṅga), having indeed attained embodiment, swiftly arrived, / the giver of life to all beings, as they looked on, O best of kings. 150.30

6.3.s:
tataḥ śaṅkhaninādena bherīṇāṃ niḥsvanena ca .
abhyanandaṃstato devaṃ surāsuramahoragāḥ .. 150.31 ..
6.3.d:
ततः शङ्खनिनादेन भेरीणां निःस्वनेन च .
अभ्यनन्दंस्ततो देवं सुरासुरमहोरगाः .. 150.31 ..
6.3.m: Then, with the blare of conches and the roll of kettle-drums, / the gods, asuras, and great serpents applauded the god. 150.31

6.3.s:
namaste devadeveśa kṛtārthāḥ surasattamāḥ .
visarjitāḥ punarjagmuryathāgatamarindama .. 150.32 ..
6.3.d:
नमस्ते देवदेवेश कृतार्थाः सुरसत्तमाः .
विसर्जिताः पुनर्जग्मुर्यथागतमरिन्दम .. 150.32 ..
6.3.m: 'Homage to you, O Lord of the gods of gods!' The best of gods, having achieved their purpose / and being dismissed, departed once again as they had come, O subduer of enemies. 150.32

6.3.s:
gateṣu sarvadeveṣu kāmadevo'pi bhārata .
tapaścacāra vipulaṃ narmadātaṭamāśritaḥ .. 150.33 ..
6.3.d:
गतेषु सर्वदेवेषु कामदेवोऽपि भारत .
तपश्चचार विपुलं नर्मदातटमाश्रितः .. 150.33 ..
6.3.m: When all the gods had departed, Kāmadeva also, O descendant of Bharata, / took refuge on the bank of the Narmadā and performed severe austerity. 150.33

6.3.s:
tapojapakṛśībhūto divyaṃ varṣaśataṃ kila .
mahābhūtairvighnakaraiḥ pīḍyamānaḥ samantataḥ .. 150.34 ..
6.3.d:
तपोजपकृशीभूतो दिव्यं वर्षशतं किल .
महाभूतैर्विघ्नकरैः पीड्यमानः समन्ततः .. 150.34 ..
6.3.m: He became emaciated by austerity and silent recitation for a hundred divine years, it is said, / being afflicted on all sides by great spirits who create obstacles. 150.34

6.3.s:
ātmavighnavināśārthaṃ saṃsmṛtaḥ kuṇḍaleśvaraḥ .
cakāra rakṣāṃ sarvatra śarapāte nṛpottama .. 150.35 ..
6.3.d:
आत्मविघ्नविनाशार्थं संस्मृतः कुण्डलेश्वरः .
चकार रक्षां सर्वत्र शरपाते नृपोत्तम .. 150.35 ..
6.3.m: To destroy his own obstacles, he remembered Kuṇḍaleśvara. / O best of kings, he provided protection everywhere within the range of an arrow-shot.

6.3.s:
tatastuṣṭo mahādevo dṛḍhabhaktyā varapradaḥ .
vareṇa chandayāmāsa kāmaṃ kāmavināśanaḥ .. 150.36 ..
6.3.d:
ततस्तुष्टो महादेवो दृढभक्त्या वरप्रदः .
वरेण छन्दयामास कामं कामविनाशनः .. 150.36 ..
6.3.m: Then Mahādeva, the granter of boons, pleased by his firm devotion, / the destroyer of Kāma, invited Kāma to choose a boon.

6.3.s:
jñātvā tuṣṭaṃ mahādevamuvāca jhaṣaketanaḥ .
praṇataḥ prāñjalirbhūtvā devadevaṃ trilocanam .. 150.37 ..
6.3.d:
ज्ञात्वा तुष्टं महादेवमुवाच झषकेतनः .
प्रणतः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा देवदेवं त्रिलोचनम् .. 150.37 ..
6.3.m: Knowing that Mahādeva was pleased, the fish-bannered [Kāma], / bowed low with joined palms, spoke to the god of gods, the three-eyed one:

6.3.s:
yadi tuṣṭo'si deveśa yadi deyo varo mama .
atra tīrthe jagannātha sadā saṃnihito bhava .. 150.38 ..
6.3.d:
यदि तुष्टोऽसि देवेश यदि देयो वरो मम .
अत्र तीर्थे जगन्नाथ सदा संनिहितो भव .. 150.38 ..
6.3.m: "If you are pleased, O lord of gods, if a boon is to be granted to me, / be perpetually present at this sacred ford, O Lord of the Universe."

6.3.s:
tatheti coktvā vacanaṃ devadevo maheśvaraḥ .
jagāmākāśamāviśya stūyamāno'psarogaṇaiḥ .. 150.39 ..
6.3.d:
तथेति चोक्त्वा वचनं देवदेवो महेश्वरः .
जगामाकाशमाविश्य स्तूयमानोऽप्सरोगणैः .. 150.39 ..
6.3.m: Saying "So be it," the god of gods, Maheśvara, / entered the sky and departed, praised by hosts of apsarases.

6.3.s:
gate cādarśanaṃ deve kāmadevo jagadgurum .
sthāpayāmāsa rājendra kusumeśvarasaṃjñitam .. 150.40 ..
6.3.d:
गते चादर्शनं देवे कामदेवो जगद्गुरुम् .
स्थापयामास राजेन्द्र कुसुमेश्वरसंज्ञितम् .. 150.40 ..
6.3.m: When the god had vanished from sight, Kāmadeva established / the guru of the universe, named Kusumeśvara, O king of kings.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ snātvā hyupavāsaparāyaṇaḥ .
caitramāse caturdaśyāṃ madanasya dine'thavā .. 150.41 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः स्नात्वा ह्युपवासपरायणः .
चैत्रमासे चतुर्दश्यां मदनस्य दिनेऽथवा .. 150.41 ..
6.3.m: Whoever bathes at that sacred ford, devoted to fasting, / on the fourteenth day in the month of Caitra, or on the day of Madana,

6.3.s:
prabhāte vimale prāpte snātvā pūjya divākaram .
tilamiśreṇa toyena tarpayetpitṛdevatāḥ .. 150.42 ..
6.3.d:
प्रभाते विमले प्राप्ते स्नात्वा पूज्य दिवाकरम् .
तिलमिश्रेण तोयेन तर्पयेत्पितृदेवताः .. 150.42 ..
6.3.m: having bathed when the clear dawn arrives and having worshipped the sun, / should satisfy the pitṛs and deities with water mixed with sesame seeds.

6.3.s:
kṛtvā snānaṃ vidhānena pūjayitvā ca taṃ nṛpa .
piṇḍanirvapaṇaṃ kuryāttasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu .. 150.43 ..
6.3.d:
कृत्वा स्नानं विधानेन पूजयित्वा च तं नृप .
पिण्डनिर्वपणं कुर्यात्तस्य पुण्यफलं शृणु .. 150.43 ..
6.3.m: Having performed the ritual ablution according to rule and having worshipped him, O king, / one should offer piṇḍas; hear the sacred fruit of that!

6.3.s:
sattrayājiphalaṃ yacca labhate dvādaśābdikam .
piṇḍadānātphalaṃ tacca labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 150.44 ..
6.3.d:
सत्त्रयाजिफलं यच्च लभते द्वादशाब्दिकम् .
पिण्डदानात्फलं तच्च लभते नात्र संशयः .. 150.44 ..
6.3.m: The fruit which one obtains from a twelve-year sacrificial session— / one obtains that fruit from the offering of a piṇḍa; there is no doubt about this.

6.3.s:
aṅkullamūle yaḥ piṇḍaṃ pitḥnuddiśya dāpayet .
tasya te dvādaśābdāni tṛptiṃ yānti pitāmahāḥ .. 150.45 ..
6.3.d:
अङ्कुल्लमूले यः पिण्डं पित्ःनुद्दिश्य दापयेत् .
तस्य ते द्वादशाब्दानि तृप्तिं यान्ति पितामहाः .. 150.45 ..
6.3.m: Whoever has a piṇḍa offered for his ancestors at the root of an aṅkulla tree, / his forefathers attain satisfaction for twelve years.

6.3.s:
kṛmikīṭapataṅgā ye tatra tīrthe yudhiṣṭhira .
prāpnuvanti mṛtāḥ svargaṃ kiṃ punarye narā mṛtāḥ .. 150.46 ..
6.3.d:
कृमिकीटपतङ्गा ये तत्र तीर्थे युधिष्ठिर .
प्राप्नुवन्ति मृताः स्वर्गं किं पुनर्ये नरा मृताः .. 150.46 ..
6.3.m: Even the worms, insects, and moths that die at that sacred ford, O Yudhiṣṭhira, / attain heaven; how much more so men who have died [there]!

6.3.s:
saṃnyāsaṃ kurute yo'tra jitakrodho jitendriyaḥ .
kusumeśe naro bhaktyā sa gacchecchivamandiram .. 150.47 ..
6.3.d:
संन्यासं कुरुते योऽत्र जितक्रोधो जितेन्द्रियः .
कुसुमेशे नरो भक्त्या स गच्छेच्छिवमन्दिरम् .. 150.47 ..
6.3.m: Whoever renounces the world here at Kusumeśa, having conquered anger and subdued the senses, / that man goes with devotion to the abode of Śiva.

6.3.s:
tatra divyāpsarobhiśca devagandharvagāyanaiḥ .
krīḍate sevyamānastu kalpakoṭiśataṃ nṛpa .. 150.48 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र दिव्याप्सरोभिश्च देवगन्धर्वगायनैः .
क्रीडते सेव्यमानस्तु कल्पकोटिशतं नृप .. 150.48 ..
6.3.m: Served there by celestial apsarases and divine Gandharva singers, / he sports for a hundred times ten million kalpas, O king.

6.3.s:
pūrṇe caiva tataḥ kāla iha mānuṣyatāṃ gataḥ .
jāyate rājarājendraiḥ pūjyamāno nṛpo mahān .. 150.49 ..
6.3.d:
पूर्णे चैव ततः काल इह मानुष्यतां गतः .
जायते राजराजेन्द्रैः पूज्यमानो नृपो महान् .. 150.49 ..
6.3.m: And then, when that time is completed, having returned to human state here, / he is born as a great king worshipped by supreme emperors,

6.3.s:
surūpaḥ subhago vāgmī vikrānto matimāñchuciḥ .
jīvedvarṣaśataṃ sāgraṃ sarvavyādhivivarjitaḥ .. 150.50 ..
6.3.d:
सुरूपः सुभगो वाग्मी विक्रान्तो मतिमाञ्छुचिः .
जीवेद्वर्षशतं साग्रं सर्वव्याधिविवर्जितः .. 150.50 ..
6.3.m: handsome, fortunate, eloquent, valorous, wise, and pure; / he would live a full hundred years, free from all diseases.

6.3.s:
etatpuṇyaṃ pāpaharaṃ tīrthakoṭiśatādhikam .
kusumeśeti vikhyātaṃ sarvadevanamaskṛtam .. 150.51 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe kusumeśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma pañcāśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
6.3.d:
एतत्पुण्यं पापहरं तीर्थकोटिशताधिकम् .
कुसुमेशेति विख्यातं सर्वदेवनमस्कृतम् .. 150.51 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे कुसुमेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम पञ्चाशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः ..
6.3.m:
This sacred [ford], destroying sins, is superior to a hundred million sacred fords, / renowned as Kusumeśa, bowed to by all the gods.
Thus ends the one hundred and fiftieth chapter, named "Description of the Greatness of Kusumeśvara Sacred Ford", in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth [khaṇḍa], the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the Skandapurāṇa comprising eighty-one thousand verses.

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
uttare narmadākūle tīrthaṃ paramaśobhanam .
jayavārāhamāhātmyaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam .. 151.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
उत्तरे नर्मदाकूले तीर्थं परमशोभनम् .
जयवाराहमाहात्म्यं सर्वपापप्रणाशनम् .. 151.1 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / On the northern bank of the Narmadā there is a supremely splendid sacred ford / possessing the greatness of Jayavārāha, destroying all sins.

6.3.s:
uddhṛtā jagatī yena sarvadevanamaskṛtā .
lokānugrahabuddhyā ca saṃsthito narmadātaṭe .. 151.2 ..
6.3.d:
उद्धृता जगती येन सर्वदेवनमस्कृता .
लोकानुग्रहबुद्ध्या च संस्थितो नर्मदातटे .. 151.2 ..
6.3.m: He by whom the earth, reverenced by all the gods, was raised up / resides on the bank of the Narmadā out of a desire to show grace to the worlds.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ snātvā vīkṣate madhusūdanam .
mucyate sarvapāpebhyo daśajanmānukīrtanāt .. 151.3 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः स्नात्वा वीक्षते मधुसूदनम् .
मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो दशजन्मानुकीर्तनात् .. 151.3 ..
6.3.m: He who bathes in that sacred ford and beholds Madhusūdana / is freed from all sins by reciting the ten incarnations.

6.3.s:
matsyaḥ kūrmo varāhaśca narasiṃho'tha vāmanaḥ .
rāmo rāmaśca kṛṣṇaśca buddhaḥ kalkiśca te daśa .. 151.4 ..
6.3.d:
मत्स्यः कूर्मो वराहश्च नरसिंहोऽथ वामनः .
रामो रामश्च कृष्णश्च बुद्धः कल्किश्च ते दश .. 151.4 ..
6.3.m: The Fish, the Tortoise, and the Boar, the Man-Lion, then the Dwarf, / Rāma, Rāma, Kṛṣṇa, Buddha, and Kalki—these are the ten.

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
matsyena kiṃ kṛtaṃ tāta kūrmeṇa munisattama .
varāheṇa ca kiṃ karma narasiṃhena kiṃ kṛtam .. 151.5 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
मत्स्येन किं कृतं तात कूर्मेण मुनिसत्तम .
वराहेण च किं कर्म नरसिंहेन किं कृतम् .. 151.5 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / What was done by the Fish, O father? What by the Tortoise, O best of sages? / And what deed was done by the Boar? What was done by the Man-Lion?

6.3.s:
vāmanena ca rāmeṇa rāghaveṇa ca kiṃ kṛtam .
buddharūpeṇa kiṃ vāpi kalkinā kiṃ kṛtaṃ vada .. 151.6 ..
6.3.d:
वामनेन च रामेण राघवेण च किं कृतम् .
बुद्धरूपेण किं वापि कल्किना किं कृतं वद .. 151.6 ..
6.3.m: And what was done by the Dwarf, by Rāma, and by the descendant of Raghu? / Or what by him in the form of Buddha? What was done by Kalki? Tell [me].

6.3.s:
evamuktastu viprendro dharmaputreṇa dhīmatā .
uvāca madhurāṃ vāṇīṃ tadā dharmasutaṃ prati .. 151.7 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्तस्तु विप्रेन्द्रो धर्मपुत्रेण धीमता .
उवाच मधुरां वाणीं तदा धर्मसुतं प्रति .. 151.7 ..
6.3.m: Thus addressed by the wise son of Dharma, the best of brahmins / then spoke sweet words to the son of Dharma:

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
mīno bhūtvā purā kalpe prītyarthaṃ brahmaṇo vibhuḥ .
samarpayatsamuddhṛtya vandānmagnānmahārṇave .. 151.8 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
मीनो भूत्वा पुरा कल्पे प्रीत्यर्थं ब्रह्मणो विभुः .
समर्पयत्समुद्धृत्य वन्दान्मग्नान्महार्णवे .. 151.8 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having become a fish formerly in the kalpa for the pleasure of Brahmā, the Lord, / lifting up the Vedas sunken in the great ocean, delivered them.

6.3.s:
amṛtotpādane rājankūrmo bhūtvā jagadguruḥ .
mandaraṃ dhārayāmāsa tathā devīṃ vasuṃdharām .. 151.9 ..
6.3.d:
अमृतोत्पादने राजन्कूर्मो भूत्वा जगद्गुरुः .
मन्दरं धारयामास तथा देवीं वसुंधराम् .. 151.9 ..
6.3.m: At the churning of the nectar, O king, the guru of the universe, having become a tortoise, / supported Mandara, and likewise the goddess earth.

6.3.s:
ujjahāra dharāṃ magnāṃ pātālatalavāsinīm .
vārāhaṃ rūpamāsthāya devadevo janārdanaḥ .. 151.10 ..
6.3.d:
उज्जहार धरां मग्नां पातालतलवासिनीम् .
वाराहं रूपमास्थाय देवदेवो जनार्दनः .. 151.10 ..
6.3.m: Assuming the form of a boar, the god of gods, Janārdana, / lifted up the earth that had sunk down to dwell on the floor of Pātāla.

6.3.s:
narasyārddhatanuṃ kṛtvā siṃhasyārddhatanuṃ tathā .
hiraṇyakaśiporvakṣo vidadāra nakhāṅkuśaiḥ .. 151.11 ..
6.3.d:
नरस्यार्द्धतनुं कृत्वा सिंहस्यार्द्धतनुं तथा .
हिरण्यकशिपोर्वक्षो विददार नखाङ्कुशैः .. 151.11 ..
6.3.m: Having made half his body that of a man and half the body that of a lion, / he tore open the chest of Hiraṇyakaśipu with the hooks of his claws.

6.3.s:
jaṭī vāmanarūpeṇa stūyamāno dvijottamaiḥ .
taddivyaṃ rūpamāsthāya kramitvā medinīṃ kramaiḥ .. 151.12 ..
6.3.d:
जटी वामनरूपेण स्तूयमानो द्विजोत्तमैः .
तद्दिव्यं रूपमास्थाय क्रमित्वा मेदिनीं क्रमैः .. 151.12 ..
6.3.m: Assuming matted hair in the form of a dwarf, praised by the best of the twice-born, / taking on that divine form, traversing the earth with his strides,

6.3.s:
kṛtavāṃśca baliṃ paścātpātālatalavāsinam .
sthāpayitvā surān sarvān gato viṣṇuḥ svakaṃ puram .. 151.13 ..
6.3.d:
कृतवांश्च बलिं पश्चात्पातालतलवासिनम् .
स्थापयित्वा सुरान् सर्वान् गतो विष्णुः स्वकं पुरम् .. 151.13 ..
6.3.m: and subsequently making Bali a dweller on the floor of Pātāla, / Viṣṇu, having reinstated all the gods, went to his own abode.

6.3.s:
jamadagnisuto rāmo bhūtvā śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ .
kṣatriyān pṛthivīpālānavadhīddhaihayādikān .. 151.14 ..
6.3.d:
जमदग्निसुतो रामो भूत्वा शस्त्रभृतां वरः .
क्षत्रियान् पृथिवीपालानवधीद्धैहयादिकान् .. 151.14 ..
6.3.m: Becoming Rāma, the son of Jamadagni, the best of weapon-bearers, / he slew the kṣatriyas, the rulers of the earth, the Haihayas and others.

6.3.s:
kaśyapāya mahīṃ dattvā saparvatavanākarām .
tapastapati deveśo mahendre'dyāpi bhārata .. 151.15 ..
6.3.d:
कश्यपाय महीं दत्त्वा सपर्वतवनाकराम् .
तपस्तपति देवेशो महेन्द्रेऽद्यापि भारत .. 151.15 ..
6.3.m: Having given the earth with its mountains, forests, and mines to Kaśyapa, / the lord of the gods performs austerity on Mahendra even today, O descendant of Bharata.

6.3.s:
tato dāśarathī rāmo rāvaṇaṃ devakaṇṭakam .
sagaṇaṃ samare hatvā rājyaṃ dattvā vibhīṣaṇe .. 151.16 ..
6.3.d:
ततो दाशरथी रामो रावणं देवकण्टकम् .
सगणं समरे हत्वा राज्यं दत्त्वा विभीषणे .. 151.16 ..
6.3.m: Then Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, having slain in battle the thorn of the gods, Rāvaṇa, / together with his retinue, and having given the kingdom to Vibhīṣaṇa,

6.3.s:
pālayitvā nayādbhūmiṃ makhaiḥ saṃtarpya devatāḥ .
svargaṃ gato mahātejā rāmo rājīvalocanaḥ .. 151.17 ..
6.3.d:
पालयित्वा नयाद्भूमिं मखैः संतर्प्य देवताः .
स्वर्गं गतो महातेजा रामो राजीवलोचनः .. 151.17 ..
6.3.m: having protected the earth with justice and gratified the deities with sacrifices, / lotus-eyed Rāma of great splendor went to heaven.

6.3.s:
vasudevagṛhe bhūyaḥ saṃkarṣaṇasahāyavān .
avatīrṇo jagannātho vāsudevo yudhiṣṭhira .. 151.18 ..
6.3.d:
वसुदेवगृहे भूयः संकर्षणसहायवान् .
अवतीर्णो जगन्नाथो वासुदेवो युधिष्ठिर .. 151.18 ..
6.3.m: Again, accompanied by Saṃkarṣaṇa, the lord of the world, Vāsudeva, / descended in the house of Vasudeva, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

6.3.s:
so'vadhīttava sāmarthyādvadhārthaṃ duṣṭabhūbhṛtām .
cāṇūrakaṃsakeśīnāṃ jarāsaṃdhasya bhārata .. 151.19 ..
6.3.d:
सोऽवधीत्तव सामर्थ्याद्वधार्थं दुष्टभूभृताम् .
चाणूरकंसकेशीनां जरासंधस्य भारत .. 151.19 ..
6.3.m: Through your power he slew, for the purpose of destroying wicked kings, / Cāṇūra, Kaṃsa, Keśin, and Jarāsaṃdha, O descendant of Bharata.

6.3.s:
tena tvaṃ susahāyena hatvā śatrūnnareśvara .
bhokṣyase pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha saṃbhṛtām .. 151.20 ..
6.3.d:
तेन त्वं सुसहायेन हत्वा शत्रून्नरेश्वर .
भोक्ष्यसे पृथिवीं सर्वां भ्रातृभिः सह संभृताम् .. 151.20 ..
6.3.m: With him as your noble helper, having slain your enemies, O ruler of men, / you will enjoy the entire earth along with your brothers, gathered [under your rule].

6.3.s:
tathā buddhatvamaparaṃ navamaṃ prāpsyate'cyutaḥ .
śāntimāndevadeveśo madhuhantā madhupriyaḥ .. 151.21 ..
6.3.d:
तथा बुद्धत्वमपरं नवमं प्राप्स्यतेऽच्युतः .
शान्तिमान्देवदेवेशो मधुहन्ता मधुप्रियः .. 151.21 ..
6.3.m: Likewise, Acyuta, the peaceful one, the god of the lords of gods, / the slayer of Madhu, who loves spring, will assume a ninth [form]—that of the Buddha.

6.3.s:
tena buddhasvarūpeṇa devena parameṣṭhinā .
bhaviṣyati jagatsarvaṃ mohitaṃ sacarācaram .. 151.22 ..
6.3.d:
तेन बुद्धस्वरूपेण देवेन परमेष्ठिना .
भविष्यति जगत्सर्वं मोहितं सचराचरम् .. 151.22 ..
6.3.m: By that god, the supreme lord, in the form of the Buddha, / the entire universe, with its mobile and immobile beings, will be deluded.

6.3.s:
na śroṣyanti pituḥ putrāstadāprabhṛti bhārata .
na gurorbāndhavāḥ śiṣyā bhaviṣyatyadharottaram .. 151.23 ..
6.3.d:
न श्रोष्यन्ति पितुः पुत्रास्तदाप्रभृति भारत .
न गुरोर्बान्धवाः शिष्या भविष्यत्यधरोत्तरम् .. 151.23 ..
6.3.m: From then on, O descendant of Bharata, sons will not listen to their father, / nor relatives and pupils to their guru; topsy-turviness will come to be.

6.3.s:
jito dharmo hyadharmeṇa cāsatyena ṛtaṃ jitam .
jitāścauraiśca rājānaḥ strībhiśca puruṣā jitāḥ .. 151.24 ..
6.3.d:
जितो धर्मो ह्यधर्मेण चासत्येन ऋतं जितम् .
जिताश्चौरैश्च राजानः स्त्रीभिश्च पुरुषा जिताः .. 151.24 ..
6.3.m: Dharma will be overcome by adharma, and truth will be overcome by untruth; / kings will be overcome by thieves, and men will be overcome by women.

6.3.s:
sīdanti cāgnihotrāṇi gurau pūjā praṇaśyati .
sīdanti mānavā dharmāḥ kalau prāpte yudhiṣṭhira .. 151.25 ..
6.3.d:
सीदन्ति चाग्निहोत्राणि गुरौ पूजा प्रणश्यति .
सीदन्ति मानवा धर्माः कलौ प्राप्ते युधिष्ठिर .. 151.25 ..
6.3.m: Agnihotra offerings will falter, worship of the guru will vanish, / and the laws of Manu will deteriorate when Kali has arrived, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

6.3.s:
dvādaśe daśame varṣe nārī garbhavatī bhavet .
kanyāstatra prasūyante brāhmaṇo haripiṅgalaḥ .. 151.26 ..
6.3.d:
द्वादशे दशमे वर्षे नारी गर्भवती भवेत् .
कन्यास्तत्र प्रसूयन्ते ब्राह्मणो हरिपिङ्गलः .. 151.26 ..
6.3.m: A woman will become pregnant in her twelfth or tenth year; / daughters will be born there, and the brahmin will have yellowish hair.

6.3.s: bhaviṣyati tataḥ kalkirdaśame janmani prabhuḥ .. 151.27 ..
6.3.d: भविष्यति ततः कल्किर्दशमे जन्मनि प्रभुः .. 151.27 ..
6.3.m: Then the lord will become Kalki in his tenth incarnation.

6.3.s:
etatte kathitaṃ rājandevasya parameṣṭhinaḥ .
kāraṇaṃ daśa janmanāṃ sarvapāpakṣayaṃkaram .. 151.28 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe śvetavārāhatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmaikapañcāśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 152
6.3.d:
एतत्ते कथितं राजन्देवस्य परमेष्ठिनः .
कारणं दश जन्मनां सर्वपापक्षयंकरम् .. 151.28 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे श्वेतवाराहतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामैकपञ्चाशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 152
6.3.m:
This has been told to you, O king: the purpose of the ten incarnations / of the supreme lord, bringing about the destruction of all sins.
Thus ends the one hundred and fifty-first chapter, named the Description of the Greatness of the Śvetavārāha Sacred Ford, in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 152

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gaccheddharāpāla bhārgaleśvaramuttamam .
śaṅkaraṃ jagataḥ prāṇaṃ smṛtamātrāghanāśanam .. 152.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेद्धरापाल भार्गलेश्वरमुत्तमम् .
शङ्करं जगतः प्राणं स्मृतमात्राघनाशनम् .. 152.1 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then one should go, O protector of the earth, to the supreme Bhārgaleśvara, / to Śaṅkara, the life-breath of the world, who destroys sins merely upon being remembered.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ snātvā pūjayetparameśvaram .
aśvamedhasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ .. 152.2 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः स्नात्वा पूजयेत्परमेश्वरम् .
अश्वमेधस्य यज्ञस्य फलं प्राप्नोति मानवः .. 152.2 ..
6.3.m: A person who bathes at that sacred ford and worships the Supreme Lord / obtains the fruit of an aśvamedha sacrifice.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ kaścitprāṇatyāgaṃ kariṣyati .
anivartikā gatistasya rudralokādasaṃśayam .. 152.3 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe bhārgaleśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma dvipañcāśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 153
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः कश्चित्प्राणत्यागं करिष्यति .
अनिवर्तिका गतिस्तस्य रुद्रलोकादसंशयम् .. 152.3 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे भार्गलेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम द्विपञ्चाशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 153
6.3.m:
Whoever abandons their life at that sacred ford, / their path is without return from Rudra's realm; there is no doubt.
Thus ends the one hundred and fifty-second chapter, named "Description of the Greatness of the Bhārgaleśvara Sacred Ford", in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth [khaṇḍa], the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the Skandapurāṇa comprising eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 153

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tasyaivānantaraṃ cānyadravitīrthamanuttamam .
yasya saṃdarśanādeva mucyante pātakairnarāḥ .. 153.1 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
तस्यैवानन्तरं चान्यद्रवितीर्थमनुत्तमम् .
यस्य संदर्शनादेव मुच्यन्ते पातकैर्नराः .. 153.1 ..
6.3.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Immediately after that is another, the unsurpassed Ravitīrtha, / simply by the sight of which human beings are freed from sins.

6.3.s:
ravitīrthe tu yaḥ snātvā naraḥ paśyati bhāskaram .
tasya yatphalamuddiṣṭaṃ svayaṃ devena tacchṛṇu .. 153.2 ..
6.3.d:
रवितीर्थे तु यः स्नात्वा नरः पश्यति भास्करम् .
तस्य यत्फलमुद्दिष्टं स्वयं देवेन तच्छृणु .. 153.2 ..
6.3.m: The man who, having bathed at Ravitīrtha, beholds the Sun— / hear that fruit which was indicated by the god himself:

6.3.s:
nāndho na mūko badhiraḥ kule bhavati kaścana .
kurūpaḥ kunakhī vāpi tasya janmāni ṣoḍaśa .. 153.3 ..
6.3.d:
नान्धो न मूको बधिरः कुले भवति कश्चन .
कुरूपः कुनखी वापि तस्य जन्मानि षोडश .. 153.3 ..
6.3.m: No one in his lineage is blind, mute, deaf, / deformed, or having diseased nails for sixteen births.

6.3.s:
dadrucitrakakuṣṭhāni maṇḍalāni vicarcikā .
naśyanti devabhaktasya ṣaṇmāsānnātra saṃśayaḥ .. 153.4 ..
6.3.d:
दद्रुचित्रककुष्ठानि मण्डलानि विचर्चिका .
नश्यन्ति देवभक्तस्य षण्मासान्नात्र संशयः .. 153.4 ..
6.3.m: Ringworm, variegated leprosy, blotches, and scabies / perish for the devotee of the god after six months; there is no doubt about this.

6.3.s:
caritaṃ tasya devasya purāṇe yacchrutaṃ mayā .
na tatkathayituṃ śakyaṃ saṃkṣepeṇa nṛpottama .. 153.5 ..
6.3.d:
चरितं तस्य देवस्य पुराणे यच्छ्रुतं मया .
न तत्कथयितुं शक्यं संक्षेपेण नृपोत्तम .. 153.5 ..
6.3.m: The deed of that god which I heard in the Purāṇa / cannot be told in brief, O best of kings.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaddānaṃ ravimuddiśya dīyate .
vidhinā pātraviprāya tasyānto nāsti karhicit .. 153.6 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यद्दानं रविमुद्दिश्य दीयते .
विधिना पात्रविप्राय तस्यान्तो नास्ति कर्हिचित् .. 153.6 ..
6.3.m: Whatever gift is given at that sacred ford intended for the Sun, / according to rule, to a worthy brahmin, there is never any end to it.

6.3.s:
ayane viṣuve caiva candrasūryagrahe tathā .
ravitīrthe pradattānāṃ dānānāṃ phalamuttamam .. 153.7 ..
6.3.d:
अयने विषुवे चैव चन्द्रसूर्यग्रहे तथा .
रवितीर्थे प्रदत्तानां दानानां फलमुत्तमम् .. 153.7 ..
6.3.m: At a solstice, at an equinox, and during an eclipse of the moon or the sun, / the fruit of gifts given at Ravitīrtha is supreme.

6.3.s:
saṃkrāntau yāni dānāni havyakavyāni bhārata .
apāmiva samudrasya teṣāmanto na labhyate .. 153.8 ..
6.3.d:
संक्रान्तौ यानि दानानि हव्यकव्यानि भारत .
अपामिव समुद्रस्य तेषामन्तो न लभ्यते .. 153.8 ..
6.3.m: Whatever gifts, oblations to the gods, and offerings to the ancestors [are made] at a transit, O Bhārata, / their end cannot be found, just like that of the waters of the ocean.

6.3.s:
yena yena yadā dattaṃ yena yena yadā hutam .
tasya tasya tadā kāle savitā pratidāyakaḥ .. 153.9 ..
6.3.d:
येन येन यदा दत्तं येन येन यदा हुतम् .
तस्य तस्य तदा काले सविता प्रतिदायकः .. 153.9 ..
6.3.m: By whomsoever whatever is given, by whomsoever whatever is offered in sacrifice, / to each person at that time Savitṛ gives in return.

6.3.s:
sapta janmāni tānyeva dadātyarkaḥ punaḥ punaḥ .
śatamindukṣaye dānaṃ sahasraṃ tu dinakṣaye .. 153.10 ..
6.3.d:
सप्त जन्मानि तान्येव ददात्यर्कः पुनः पुनः .
शतमिन्दुक्षये दानं सहस्रं तु दिनक्षये .. 153.10 ..
6.3.m: For seven births the Sun repeatedly gives those very things. / A gift on the new-moon day [yields] a hundredfold, but a thousandfold on a solar day's end;

6.3.s: saṃkrāntau śatasāhasraṃ vyatīpāte tvanantakam .. 153.11 ..
6.3.d: संक्रान्तौ शतसाहस्रं व्यतीपाते त्वनन्तकम् .. 153.11 ..
6.3.m: a hundred thousandfold on a transit, but infinite on a vyatīpāta.

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
ravitīrthaṃ kathaṃ tāta puṇyātpuṇyataraṃ smṛtam .
vistareṇa mamākhyāhi śravaṇau mama lampaṭau .. 153.12 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
रवितीर्थं कथं तात पुण्यात्पुण्यतरं स्मृतम् .
विस्तरेण ममाख्याहि श्रवणौ मम लम्पटौ .. 153.12 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / How is Ravitīrtha remembered as holier than the holy, O dear father? / Tell me in full; my ears are eager [to hear].

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
śṛṇuṣvāvahito bhūtvā hyādityeśvaramuttamam .
uttare narmadākūle sarvavyādhivināśanam .. 153.13 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
शृणुष्वावहितो भूत्वा ह्यादित्येश्वरमुत्तमम् .
उत्तरे नर्मदाकूले सर्वव्याधिविनाशनम् .. 153.13 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Listen attentively about the supreme Ādityeśvara / on the northern bank of the Narmadā, which destroys all diseases.

6.3.s:
purā kṛtayugasyādau jābālirbrāhmaṇo'bhavat .
vasiṣṭhānvayasambhūto vedaśāstrārthapāragaḥ .. 153.14 ..
6.3.d:
पुरा कृतयुगस्यादौ जाबालिर्ब्राह्मणोऽभवत् .
वसिष्ठान्वयसम्भूतो वेदशास्त्रार्थपारगः .. 153.14 ..
6.3.m: Long ago, at the beginning of the Kṛta age, there was a brahmin named Jābāli, / born in the lineage of Vasiṣṭha, who had mastered the meaning of the Vedas and treatises.

6.3.s:
pativratā sādhuśīlā tasya bhāryā manasvinī .
ṛtukāle tu sā gatvā bhartāramidamabravīt .. 153.15 ..
6.3.d:
पतिव्रता साधुशीला तस्य भार्या मनस्विनी .
ऋतुकाले तु सा गत्वा भर्तारमिदमब्रवीत् .. 153.15 ..
6.3.m: His wife was devoted to her husband, virtuous in conduct, and high-minded. / Approaching her husband at the fertile time, she spoke this:

6.3.s:
vartate ṛtukālo me bhartāraṃ tvāmupasthitā .
bhaja māṃ prītisaṃyuktaḥ putrakāmāṃ tu kāminīm .. 153.16 ..
6.3.d:
वर्तते ऋतुकालो मे भर्तारं त्वामुपस्थिता .
भज मां प्रीतिसंयुक्तः पुत्रकामां तु कामिनीम् .. 153.16 ..
6.3.m: "My fertile time has arrived, and I have approached you, my husband; / unite with me with love, for I am a passionate woman desiring a son."

6.3.s:
evamukto dvijaḥ prāha priye'dyāhaṃ vratānvitaḥ .
gacchedānīṃ varārohe dāsya ṛtvantare punaḥ .. 153.17 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्तो द्विजः प्राह प्रियेऽद्याहं व्रतान्वितः .
गच्छेदानीं वरारोहे दास्य ऋत्वन्तरे पुनः .. 153.17 ..
6.3.m: Addressed thus, the twice-born said: "My dear, today I am engaged in a religious observance. / Go now, O fair-hipped woman; I will give [it] at another fertile period."

6.3.s:
punardvitīye samprāpte ṛtukāle'pyupasthitā .
punaḥ sā chanditā tena vratastho'dyeti bhārata .. 153.18 ..
6.3.d:
पुनर्द्वितीये सम्प्राप्ते ऋतुकालेऽप्युपस्थिता .
पुनः सा छन्दिता तेन व्रतस्थोऽद्येति भारत .. 153.18 ..
6.3.m: When a second fertile time arrived, she approached him again. / Again she was deferred by him, [saying,] "I am observing a vow today," O Bhārata.

6.3.s:
itthaṃ vā bahuśastena chanditā ca punaḥ punaḥ .
nirāśā cābhavattatra bhartāraṃ prati bhāminī .. 153.19 ..
6.3.d:
इत्थं वा बहुशस्तेन छन्दिता च पुनः पुनः .
निराशा चाभवत्तत्र भर्तारं प्रति भामिनी .. 153.19 ..
6.3.m: When thus repeatedly deferred many times by him, / the proud woman became completely hopeless regarding her husband.

6.3.s:
duḥkhena mahatāviṣṭā vidhāyānaśanaṃ mṛtā .
tena bhrūṇahatenaiva pāpena sahasā dvijaḥ .. 153.20 ..
6.3.d:
दुःखेन महताविष्टा विधायानशनं मृता .
तेन भ्रूणहतेनैव पापेन सहसा द्विजः .. 153.20 ..
6.3.m: Overwhelmed by great sorrow, she undertook fasting and died. / By that very sin of foeticide, suddenly the twice-born...

6.3.s:
śīrṇaghrāṇāṅghrirabhavattapaḥ sarvaṃ nanāśa ca .
dṛṣṭvātmānaṃ sa kuṣṭhena vyāptaṃ brāhmaṇasattamaḥ .. 153.21 ..
6.3.d:
शीर्णघ्राणाङ्घ्रिरभवत्तपः सर्वं ननाश च .
दृष्ट्वात्मानं स कुष्ठेन व्याप्तं ब्राह्मणसत्तमः .. 153.21 ..
6.3.m: His nose and feet decayed, and all his austerity was destroyed. / Seeing himself afflicted with leprosy, that best of brahmins,

6.3.s:
viṣādaṃ paramaṃ gatvā narmadātaṭamāśritaḥ .
apṛcchadbhāskaraṃ tīrthaṃ dvijebhyo dvijasattamaḥ .. 153.22 ..
6.3.d:
विषादं परमं गत्वा नर्मदातटमाश्रितः .
अपृच्छद्भास्करं तीर्थं द्विजेभ्यो द्विजसत्तमः .. 153.22 ..
6.3.m: fell into extreme despair and took refuge on the bank of the Narmadā. / That best of brahmins asked other brahmins about the Bhāskara sacred ford:

6.3.s:
ārogyaṃ bhāskarādicchediti saṃcintya cetasi .
kutastadbhāskaraṃ tīrthaṃ bho dvijāḥ kathyatāṃ mama .. 153.23 ..
6.3.d:
आरोग्यं भास्करादिच्छेदिति संचिन्त्य चेतसि .
कुतस्तद्भास्करं तीर्थं भो द्विजाः कथ्यतां मम .. 153.23 ..
6.3.m: Reflecting in his mind, "One should seek health from the Sun," / [he asked,] "Where is that Bhāskara sacred ford, O brahmins? Tell me!

6.3.s: tapastapyāmyahaṃ gatvā tasmiṃstīrthe subhāvitaḥ .. 153.24 ..
6.3.d: तपस्तप्याम्यहं गत्वा तस्मिंस्तीर्थे सुभावितः .. 153.24 ..
6.3.m: I will go and perform austerity at that sacred ford, well-concentrated."

6.3.s:
dvijā ūcuḥ .
revāyā uttare kūle ādityeśvaranāmataḥ .
vidyate bhāskaraṃ tīrthaṃ sarvavyādhivināśanam .. 153.25 ..
6.3.d:
द्विजा ऊचुः .
रेवाया उत्तरे कूले आदित्येश्वरनामतः .
विद्यते भास्करं तीर्थं सर्वव्याधिविनाशनम् .. 153.25 ..
6.3.m: The brahmins said: / "On the northern bank of the Revā, known by the name Ādityeśvara, / there is the Bhāskara sacred ford, which destroys all diseases.

6.3.s:
tatra yāhyavicāreṇa gantuṃ cecchakyate tvayā .
evamukto dvijairvipro gantuṃ tatra pracakrame .. 153.26 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र याह्यविचारेण गन्तुं चेच्छक्यते त्वया .
एवमुक्तो द्विजैर्विप्रो गन्तुं तत्र प्रचक्रमे .. 153.26 ..
6.3.m: Go there without hesitation, if you are able to go." / Thus addressed by the brahmins, the brahmin set out to go there.

6.3.s:
vyādhinā paribhūtastu ghoreṇa prāṇahāriṇā .
yadā gantuṃ na śaknoti tadā tena vicintitam .. 153.27 ..
6.3.d:
व्याधिना परिभूतस्तु घोरेण प्राणहारिणा .
यदा गन्तुं न शक्नोति तदा तेन विचिन्तितम् .. 153.27 ..
6.3.m: However, overcome by the terrible disease that threatened his life, / when he was unable to walk, he then reflected:

6.3.s:
sāmarthyaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ hi vidyate bhuvanatraye .
liṅgapātaḥ kṛto viprairdevadevasya śūlinaḥ .. 153.28 ..
6.3.d:
सामर्थ्यं ब्राह्मणानां हि विद्यते भुवनत्रये .
लिङ्गपातः कृतो विप्रैर्देवदेवस्य शूलिनः .. 153.28 ..
6.3.m: "Indeed, the power of brahmins exists throughout the three worlds! / The fall of the liṅga of the god of gods, the wielder of the trident, was brought about by brahmins;

6.3.s:
samudraḥ śoṣito viprairvindhyaścāpi nivāritaḥ .
ahamapyatra saṃsthastu hyānayiṣyāmi bhāskaram .. 153.29 ..
6.3.d:
समुद्रः शोषितो विप्रैर्विन्ध्यश्चापि निवारितः .
अहमप्यत्र संस्थस्तु ह्यानयिष्यामि भास्करम् .. 153.29 ..
6.3.m: the ocean was dried up by brahmins, and Vindhya was halted. / Remaining right here, I too will bring the Sun,

6.3.s:
tapobalena mahatā hyādityeśvarasaṃjñitam .
iti niścitya manasā hyugre tapasi saṃsthitaḥ .. 153.30 ..
6.3.d:
तपोबलेन महता ह्यादित्येश्वरसंज्ञितम् .
इति निश्चित्य मनसा ह्युग्रे तपसि संस्थितः .. 153.30 ..
6.3.m: named Ādityeśvara, by the great power of my austerity." / Having thus resolved in his mind, he engaged in severe austerity.

6.3.s:
vāyubhakṣo nirāhāro grīṣme pañcāgnimadhyagaḥ .
śiśire toyamadhyastho varṣāsvaprāvṛtākṛtiḥ .. 153.31 ..
6.3.d:
