वायुभक्षो निराहारो ग्रीष्मे पञ्चाग्निमध्यगः .
शिशिरे तोयमध्यस्थो वर्षास्वप्रावृताकृतिः .. 153.31 ..
6.3.m: Subsisting on wind, taking no food, standing amidst five fires in summer, / standing in water during the cold season, and unprotected against rain during the monsoon,

6.3.s: sāgre varṣaśate pūrṇe ravistuṣṭo'bravīdidam .. 153.32 ..
6.3.d: साग्रे वर्षशते पूर्णे रविस्तुष्टोऽब्रवीदिदम् .. 153.32 ..
6.3.m: when a full century of years had elapsed, the Sun, being pleased, said this:

6.3.s:
sūrya uvāca -
varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te kiṃ te manasi vāñchitam .
adeyamapi dāsyāmi brūhi māṃ tvaṃ ciraṃ kṛthāḥ .. 153.33 ..
6.3.d:
सूर्य उवाच -
वरं वरय भद्रं ते किं ते मनसि वाञ्छितम् .
अदेयमपि दास्यामि ब्रूहि मां त्वं चिरं कृथाः .. 153.33 ..
6.3.m: Sūrya said: / "Choose a boon, blessings to you! What is desired in your mind? / I will grant even what should not be given; speak to me, do not delay.

6.3.s: kimasādhyaṃ hi te vipra idānīṃ tapasi sthitaḥ .. 153.34 ..
6.3.d: किमसाध्यं हि ते विप्र इदानीं तपसि स्थितः .. 153.34 ..
6.3.m: Indeed, what is impossible for you, O brahmin, now established in austerity?"

6.3.s:
jābāliruvāca -
yadi tuṣṭo'si deveśa yadi deyo varo mama .
mama pratijñā deveśa hyādityeśvaradarśane .. 153.35 ..
6.3.d:
जाबालिरुवाच -
यदि तुष्टोऽसि देवेश यदि देयो वरो मम .
मम प्रतिज्ञा देवेश ह्यादित्येश्वरदर्शने .. 153.35 ..
6.3.m: Jābāli said: / "If you are pleased, O Lord of gods, if a boon is to be granted to me: / my vow was made, O Lord of gods, to obtain the darśana of Ādityeśvara,

6.3.s:
kṛtā tāṃ pārituṃ deva na śakto vyādhinā vṛtaḥ .
śuklatīrthe'tra tiṣṭha tvamādityeśvaramūrtidhṛk .. 153.36 ..
6.3.d:
कृता तां पारितुं देव न शक्तो व्याधिना वृतः .
शुक्लतीर्थेऽत्र तिष्ठ त्वमादित्येश्वरमूर्तिधृक् .. 153.36 ..
6.3.m: yet, afflicted by disease, O God, I was unable to fulfill it. / Remain here at Śuklatīrtha, assuming the form of Ādityeśvara."

6.3.s:
evamukte tu deveśo bahurūpo divākaraḥ .
uttare narmadākūle kṣaṇādeva vyadṛśyata .. 153.37 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्ते तु देवेशो बहुरूपो दिवाकरः .
उत्तरे नर्मदाकूले क्षणादेव व्यदृश्यत .. 153.37 ..
6.3.m: When this was said, the Lord of gods, the multiform Sun, / appeared in an instant upon the northern bank of the Narmadā.

6.3.s:
tadāprabhṛti bhūpāla taddhi tīrthaṃ pracakṣate .
sarvapāpaharaṃ proktaṃ sarvaduḥkhavināśanam .. 153.38 ..
6.3.d:
तदाप्रभृति भूपाल तद्धि तीर्थं प्रचक्षते .
सर्वपापहरं प्रोक्तं सर्वदुःखविनाशनम् .. 153.38 ..
6.3.m: From that time forward, O king, they proclaim that very sacred ford; / it is declared to remove all sins and destroy all sorrows.

6.3.s:
yastu saṃvatsaraṃ pūrṇaṃ nityamādityavāsare .
snātvā pradakṣiṇāḥ sapta dattvā paśyati bhāskaram .. 153.39 ..
6.3.d:
यस्तु संवत्सरं पूर्णं नित्यमादित्यवासरे .
स्नात्वा प्रदक्षिणाः सप्त दत्त्वा पश्यति भास्करम् .. 153.39 ..
6.3.m: Whoever, for one full year, constantly on Sundays, / having bathed and performed seven circumambulations, beholds the Sun—

6.3.s:
yatphalaṃ labhate tena tacchṛṇuṣva mayoditam .
prasuptaṃ maṇḍalānīha dadrukuṣṭhavicarcikāḥ .. 153.40 ..
6.3.d:
यत्फलं लभते तेन तच्छृणुष्व मयोदितम् .
प्रसुप्तं मण्डलानीह दद्रुकुष्ठविचर्चिकाः .. 153.40 ..
6.3.m: listen to that fruit obtained by him, as declared by me: / dormant skin eruptions, ringworm, leprosy, and eczema

6.3.s:
naśyanti satvaraṃ rājaṃstūlarāśirivānale .
dhanaputrakalatrāṇāṃ pūrayedvatsaratrayāt .. 153.41 ..
6.3.d:
नश्यन्ति सत्वरं राजंस्तूलराशिरिवानले .
धनपुत्रकलत्राणां पूरयेद्वत्सरत्रयात् .. 153.41 ..
6.3.m: quickly perish, O king, like a heap of cotton in fire. / Within three years, he will fulfill his desires for wealth, sons, and wives.

6.3.s:
yastu śrāddhapradastatra pitḥnuddiśya saṃkrame .
tṛpyanti pitarastasya pitṛdevo hi bhāskaraḥ .. 153.42 ..
6.3.d:
यस्तु श्राद्धप्रदस्तत्र पित्ःनुद्दिश्य संक्रमे .
तृप्यन्ति पितरस्तस्य पितृदेवो हि भास्करः .. 153.42 ..
6.3.m: And whoever offers a śrāddha there dedicated to the ancestors during a transit of the sun, / his ancestors are satisfied, for the Sun is indeed the deity of the ancestors.

6.3.s:
iti te kathitaṃ sarvamādityeśvaramuttamam .
sarvapāpaharaṃ divyaṃ sarvarogavināśanam .. 153.43 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe ādityeśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma tripañcāśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 154
6.3.d:
इति ते कथितं सर्वमादित्येश्वरमुत्तमम् .
सर्वपापहरं दिव्यं सर्वरोगविनाशनम् .. 153.43 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे आदित्येश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम त्रिपञ्चाशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 154
6.3.m:
Thus all of this supreme [māhātmya] of Ādityeśvara has been told to you, / which removes all sins, is divine, and destroys all diseases.
Thus ends the one hundred fifty-third chapter, entitled "Description of the Māhātmya of the Ādityeśvara Sacred Ford," in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compilation of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 154

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
narmadādakṣiṇe kūle tīrthaṃ kalakaleśvaram .
vikhyātaṃ sarvalokeṣu svayaṃ devena nirmitam .. 154.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
नर्मदादक्षिणे कूले तीर्थं कलकलेश्वरम् .
विख्यातं सर्वलोकेषु स्वयं देवेन निर्मितम् .. 154.1 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / "On the southern bank of the Narmadā is the Kalakaleśvara sacred ford, / renowned in all the worlds, fashioned by the God himself.

6.3.s:
andhakaṃ samare hatvā devadevo maheśvaraḥ .
sahito devagandharvaiḥ kinnaraiśca mahoragaiḥ .. 154.2 ..
6.3.d:
अन्धकं समरे हत्वा देवदेवो महेश्वरः .
सहितो देवगन्धर्वैः किन्नरैश्च महोरगैः .. 154.2 ..
6.3.m: Having slain Andhaka in battle, the great Lord, the god of gods, / accompanied by gods, gandharvas, kinnaras, and great serpents,

6.3.s:
śaṅkhatūryaninādaiśca mṛdaṅgapaṇavādibhiḥ .
vīṇāveṇuravaiścānyaiḥ stutibhiḥ puṣkalādibhiḥ .. 154.3 ..
6.3.d:
शङ्खतूर्यनिनादैश्च मृदङ्गपणवादिभिः .
वीणावेणुरवैश्चान्यैः स्तुतिभिः पुष्कलादिभिः .. 154.3 ..
6.3.m: amidst the blasts of conches and trumpets, with mṛdaṅgas, paṇavas, and other drums, / with the sounds of vīṇās and flutes, and with abundant hymns of praise,

6.3.s:
gāyanti sāmāni yajūṃṣi cānye chandāṃsi cānye ṛcamudgiranti .
stotrairanekairapare gṛṇanti maheśvaraṃ tatra mahānubhāvāḥ .. 154.4 ..
6.3.d:
गायन्ति सामानि यजूंषि चान्ये छन्दांसि चान्ये ऋचमुद्गिरन्ति .
स्तोत्रैरनेकैरपरे गृणन्ति महेश्वरं तत्र महानुभावाः .. 154.4 ..
6.3.m: some singing the Sāman hymns, others the Yajus hymns, others reciting the metres and the Ṛg verses, / while other exalted ones praised Maheśvara there with manifold hymns—

6.3.s:
pramathānāṃ ninādena kalkalena ca bandinām .
yasmātpratiṣṭhitaṃ liṅgaṃ tasmājjātaṃ tadākhyayā .. 154.5 ..
6.3.d:
प्रमथानां निनादेन कल्कलेन च बन्दिनाम् .
यस्मात्प्रतिष्ठितं लिङ्गं तस्माज्जातं तदाख्यया .. 154.5 ..
6.3.m: because the liṅga was established amidst the roaring of the Pramathas / and the tumultuous acclaim of the bards, it came to be known by that name.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ snātvā vīkṣetkalakaleśvaram .
vājapeyātparaṃ puṇyaṃ sa labhenmānavo bhuvi .. 154.6 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः स्नात्वा वीक्षेत्कलकलेश्वरम् .
वाजपेयात्परं पुण्यं स लभेन्मानवो भुवि .. 154.6 ..
6.3.m: Whoever, having bathed at that sacred ford, beholds Kalakaleśvara, / that human being on earth attains merit superior to that of a Vājapeya sacrifice.

6.3.s:
tena puṇyena pūtātmā prāṇatyāgāddivaṃ vrajet .
ārūḍhaḥ paramaṃ yānaṃ gīyamāno'psarogaṇaiḥ .. 154.7 ..
6.3.d:
तेन पुण्येन पूतात्मा प्राणत्यागाद्दिवं व्रजेत् .
आरूढः परमं यानं गीयमानोऽप्सरोगणैः .. 154.7 ..
6.3.m: Purified in self by that merit, upon relinquishing his breath he goes to heaven, / having mounted an excellent aerial vehicle, sung of by hosts of apsarases.

6.3.s:
upabhujya mahābhogānkālena mahatā tataḥ .
martyaloke mahātmāsau jāyate vimale kule .. 154.8 ..
6.3.d:
उपभुज्य महाभोगान्कालेन महता ततः .
मर्त्यलोके महात्मासौ जायते विमले कुले .. 154.8 ..
6.3.m: Having enjoyed immense delights there for a long time, / that great-souled one is subsequently born into a pure family in the mortal world.

6.3.s:
brāhmaṇaḥ subhago loke vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ .
vyādhiśokavinirmukto jīvecca śaradāṃ śatam .. 154.9 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe kalakaleśvaratīrthaphalamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma catuḥpañcāśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
6.3.d:
ब्राह्मणः सुभगो लोके वेदवेदाङ्गपारगः .
व्याधिशोकविनिर्मुक्तो जीवेच्च शरदां शतम् .. 154.9 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे कलकलेश्वरतीर्थफलमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम चतुःपञ्चाशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः ..
6.3.m:
A fortunate brahmin in the world, a master of the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas, / freed from disease and grief, he lives for a hundred autumns."
Thus ends the one hundred fifty-fourth chapter, entitled "Description of the Fruit and Māhātmya of the Kalakaleśvara Sacred Ford," in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compilation of eighty-one thousand verses.

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi sarvatīrthādanuttamam .
uttare narmadākūle śuklatīrthaṃ yudhiṣṭhira .. 155.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि सर्वतीर्थादनुत्तमम् .
उत्तरे नर्मदाकूले शुक्लतीर्थं युधिष्ठिर .. 155.1 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Hereafter I shall proclaim Śuklatīrtha on the northern bank of the Narmadā, / the highest of all sacred fords, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

6.3.s:
tasya tīrthasya cānyāni puṇyatvācchubhadarśanāt .
pṛthivyāṃ sarvatīrthāni kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm .. 155.2 ..
6.3.d:
तस्य तीर्थस्य चान्यानि पुण्यत्वाच्छुभदर्शनात् .
पृथिव्यां सर्वतीर्थानि कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीम् .. 155.2 ..
6.3.m: Due to its holiness and auspicious sight, all other sacred fords / on earth do not equal a sixteenth part of that sacred ford.

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
tasya tīrthasya māhātmyaṃ śrotumicchāmi tattvataḥ .
bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitaḥ sarvaistathānyairdvijasattamaiḥ .. 155.3 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
तस्य तीर्थस्य माहात्म्यं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः .
भ्रातृभिः सहितः सर्वैस्तथान्यैर्द्विजसत्तमैः .. 155.3 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / I desire to hear the māhātmya of that sacred ford in truth, / together with all my brothers and also other best brahmins.

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
śuklatīrthasya cotpattimākarṇaya nareśvara .
yasya saṃdarśanādeva brahmahatyā pralīyate .. 155.4 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
शुक्लतीर्थस्य चोत्पत्तिमाकर्णय नरेश्वर .
यस्य संदर्शनादेव ब्रह्महत्या प्रलीयते .. 155.4 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Hear of the origin of Śuklatīrtha, O ruler of men, / by the mere sight of which the murder of a brahmin is dissolved.

6.3.s:
narmadā saritāṃ śreṣṭhā sarvapāpapraṇāśinī .
yacca bālyaṃ kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ darśanādeva naśyati .. 155.5 ..
6.3.d:
नर्मदा सरितां श्रेष्ठा सर्वपापप्रणाशिनी .
यच्च बाल्यं कृतं पापं दर्शनादेव नश्यति .. 155.5 ..
6.3.m: The Narmadā is the foremost among rivers, destroying all sins; / whatever sin was committed in childhood is destroyed merely by seeing it.

6.3.s:
mokṣadāni na sarvatra śuklatīrthamṛte nṛpa .
śuklatīrthasya māhātmyaṃ purāṇe yacchrutaṃ mayā .. 155.6 ..
6.3.d:
मोक्षदानि न सर्वत्र शुक्लतीर्थमृते नृप .
शुक्लतीर्थस्य माहात्म्यं पुराणे यच्छ्रुतं मया .. 155.6 ..
6.3.m: They do not grant liberation everywhere except for Śuklatīrtha, O king. / The māhātmya of Śuklatīrtha that was heard by me in the Purāṇa,

6.3.s:
samāgame munīnāṃ tu devānāṃ hi tathaiva ca .
kathitaṃ devadevena śitikaṇṭhena bhārata .
kailāse parvataśreṣṭhe tatte saṃkathayāmyaham .. 155.7 ..
6.3.d:
समागमे मुनीनां तु देवानां हि तथैव च .
कथितं देवदेवेन शितिकण्ठेन भारत .
कैलासे पर्वतश्रेष्ठे तत्ते संकथयाम्यहम् .. 155.7 ..
6.3.m: as it was related by Śitikaṇṭha, the god of gods, / at an assembly of sages and likewise of the gods, on the excellent mountain Kailāsa, / that I shall relate to you, O Bhārata.

6.3.s:
purā kṛtayugasyādau toṣituṃ girijāpatim .
tapaścacāra vipulaṃ viṣṇurvarṣasahasrakam .
vāyubhakṣo nirāhāraḥ śuklatīrthe vyavasthitaḥ .. 155.8 ..
6.3.d:
पुरा कृतयुगस्यादौ तोषितुं गिरिजापतिम् .
तपश्चचार विपुलं विष्णुर्वर्षसहस्रकम् .
वायुभक्षो निराहारः शुक्लतीर्थे व्यवस्थितः .. 155.8 ..
6.3.m: Formerly, at the beginning of the Kṛta Yuga, Viṣṇu performed vast austerity / for a thousand years in order to please the husband of Girijā, / subsisting on wind, taking no food, settled at Śuklatīrtha.

6.3.s:
tataḥ pratyakṣatāmāgāddevadevo maheśvaraḥ .
prādurbhūtastu sahasā tatra tīrthe narādhipa .. 155.9 ..
6.3.d:
ततः प्रत्यक्षतामागाद्देवदेवो महेश्वरः .
प्रादुर्भूतस्तु सहसा तत्र तीर्थे नराधिप .. 155.9 ..
6.3.m: Then Maheśvara, the god of gods, became visible; / he suddenly manifested at that sacred ford, O ruler of men.

6.3.s:
krośadvayamidaṃ cakre bhuktimuktipradāyakam .
tasmiṃstīrthe naraḥ snātvā mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ .. 155.10 ..
6.3.d:
क्रोशद्वयमिदं चक्रे भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायकम् .
तस्मिंस्तीर्थे नरः स्नात्वा मुच्यते सर्वकिल्बिषैः .. 155.10 ..
6.3.m: He made this [expanse of] two krośas the bestower of enjoyment and liberation. / Having bathed at that sacred ford, a person is freed from all misdeeds.

6.3.s:
gaṅgā kanakhale puṇyā kurukṣetre sarasvatī .
grāme vā yadi vāraṇye puṇyā sarvatra narmadā .. 155.11 ..
6.3.d:
गङ्गा कनखले पुण्या कुरुक्षेत्रे सरस्वती .
ग्रामे वा यदि वारण्ये पुण्या सर्वत्र नर्मदा .. 155.11 ..
6.3.m: The Gaṅgā is holy at Kanakhala, the Sarasvatī at Kurukṣetra; / whether in a village or in a forest, the Narmadā is holy everywhere.

6.3.s:
sarvauṣadhīnāmaśanaṃ pradhānaṃ sarveṣu peyeṣu jalaṃ pradhānam .
nidrā sukhānāṃ pramadā ratīnāṃ sarveṣu gātreṣu śiraḥ pradhānam .. 155.12 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वौषधीनामशनं प्रधानं सर्वेषु पेयेषु जलं प्रधानम् .
निद्रा सुखानां प्रमदा रतीनां सर्वेषु गात्रेषु शिरः प्रधानम् .. 155.12 ..
6.3.m: Among all herbs, food is foremost; among all drinks, water is foremost; / sleep is foremost among pleasures, a woman among sensual delights, the head is foremost among all limbs;

6.3.s:
snātasyāpi yathā puṇyaṃ lalāṭaṃ nṛpasattama .
śuklatīrthaṃ tathā puṇyaṃ narmadāyāṃ yudhiṣṭhira .. 155.13 ..
6.3.d:
स्नातस्यापि यथा पुण्यं ललाटं नृपसत्तम .
शुक्लतीर्थं तथा पुण्यं नर्मदायां युधिष्ठिर .. 155.13 ..
6.3.m: and just as the forehead is the auspicious part of one who has bathed, O best of kings, / so is Śuklatīrtha holy upon the Narmadā, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

6.3.s:
saritāṃ ca yathā gaṅgā devatānāṃ janārdanaḥ .
śuklatīrthaṃ tathā puṇyaṃ narmadāyāṃ vyavasthitam .. 155.14 ..
6.3.d:
सरितां च यथा गङ्गा देवतानां जनार्दनः .
शुक्लतीर्थं तथा पुण्यं नर्मदायां व्यवस्थितम् .. 155.14 ..
6.3.m: And as Gaṅgā is foremost of rivers, as Janārdana is of deities, / even so is Śuklatīrtha, established upon the Narmadā, sacred.

6.3.s:
catuṣpadānāṃ surabhirvarṇānāṃ brāhmaṇo yathā .
pradhānaṃ sarvatīrthānāṃ śuklatīrthaṃ tathā nṛpa .. 155.15 ..
6.3.d:
चतुष्पदानां सुरभिर्वर्णानां ब्राह्मणो यथा .
प्रधानं सर्वतीर्थानां शुक्लतीर्थं तथा नृप .. 155.15 ..
6.3.m: As Surabhi is among four-footed beasts, as the brahmin is among social classes, / so too is Śuklatīrtha the chief of all sacred fords, O king.

6.3.s:
grahāṇāṃ tu yathādityo nakṣatrāṇāṃ yathā śaśī .
śiro vā sarvagātrāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ satyamiṣyate .. 155.16 ..
6.3.d:
ग्रहाणां तु यथादित्यो नक्षत्राणां यथा शशी .
शिरो वा सर्वगात्राणां धर्माणां सत्यमिष्यते .. 155.16 ..
6.3.m: As the sun is among the planets, as the moon is among the lunar mansions, / or the head among all limbs, truth is held to be the foremost among dharmas.

6.3.s:
tathaiva pārtha tīrthānāṃ śuklatīrthamanuttamam .
durvijñeyo yathā loke paramātmā sanātanaḥ .. 155.17 ..
6.3.d:
तथैव पार्थ तीर्थानां शुक्लतीर्थमनुत्तमम् .
दुर्विज्ञेयो यथा लोके परमात्मा सनातनः .. 155.17 ..
6.3.m: Even so, O son of Pṛthā, Śuklatīrtha is unsurpassed among sacred fords. / Just as the eternal Supreme Self is difficult to perceive in the world,

6.3.s:
susūkṣmatvādanirdeśyaḥ śuklatīrthaṃ tathā nṛpa .
mandaprajñatvamāpanne mahāmohasamanvitaḥ .. 155.18 ..
6.3.d:
सुसूक्ष्मत्वादनिर्देश्यः शुक्लतीर्थं तथा नृप .
मन्दप्रज्ञत्वमापन्ने महामोहसमन्वितः .. 155.18 ..
6.3.m: and indescribable on account of its extreme subtlety, so is Śuklatīrtha, O king. / A man who has fallen into foolishness and is full of great delusion

6.3.s:
śuklatīrthaṃ nā jānāti narmadātaṭasaṃsthitam .
bahunātra kimuktena dharmaputra punaḥ punaḥ .. 155.19 ..
6.3.d:
शुक्लतीर्थं ना जानाति नर्मदातटसंस्थितम् .
बहुनात्र किमुक्तेन धर्मपुत्र पुनः पुनः .. 155.19 ..
6.3.m: does not know Śuklatīrtha situated on the bank of the Narmadā. / What more is to be said here repeatedly, O son of Dharma?

6.3.s:
śuklatīrthaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ samprāptaṃ kalmaṣakṣayāt .
yo'tra datte śucirbhūtvā ekaṃ revājalāñjalim .. 155.20 ..
6.3.d:
शुक्लतीर्थं महापुण्यं सम्प्राप्तं कल्मषक्षयात् .
योऽत्र दत्ते शुचिर्भूत्वा एकं रेवाजलाञ्जलिम् .. 155.20 ..
6.3.m: The highly sacred Śuklatīrtha is reached by the exhaustion of sins. / He who, having become pure, offers here a single handful of water from the Revā,

6.3.s: kalpakoṭisahasrāṇi pitarastena tarpitāḥ .. 155.21 ..
6.3.d: कल्पकोटिसहस्राणि पितरस्तेन तर्पिताः .. 155.21 ..
6.3.m: by him the ancestors are propitiated for thousands of kotis of kalpas.

6.3.s:
ekaḥ putro dharāpṛṣṭhe pitḥṇāmārtināśanaḥ .
cāṇakyo nāma rājābhūcchuklatīrthaṃ ca veda saḥ .. 155.22 ..
6.3.d:
एकः पुत्रो धरापृष्ठे पित्ःणामार्तिनाशनः .
चाणक्यो नाम राजाभूच्छुक्लतीर्थं च वेद सः .. 155.22 ..
6.3.m: There was a singular son on the face of the earth who destroyed the distress of his ancestors; / he was a king named Cāṇakya, and he knew Śuklatīrtha.

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
ko'sau dvijavaraśreṣṭha cāṇakyo nāma nāmataḥ .
śuklatīrthasya yo vettā nānyo vettā hi kaścana .. 155.23 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
कोऽसौ द्विजवरश्रेष्ठ चाणक्यो नाम नामतः .
शुक्लतीर्थस्य यो वेत्ता नान्यो वेत्ता हि कश्चन .. 155.23 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / Who is this one named Cāṇakya, O best among the foremost of the twice-born, / who was the knower of Śuklatīrtha, and indeed no one else was a knower?

6.3.s:
kenopāyena tattīrthaṃ tena jñātaṃ dharātale .
tadahaṃ śrotumicchāmi paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me .. 155.24 ..
6.3.d:
केनोपायेन तत्तीर्थं तेन ज्ञातं धरातले .
तदहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि परं कौतूहलं हि मे .. 155.24 ..
6.3.m: By what means was that sacred ford known by him on the earth's surface? / I wish to hear that, for great indeed is my curiosity.

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
ikṣvākuprabhavo rājā naptā śuddhodanasya ca .
cāṇakyo nāma rājarṣirbubhuje pṛthivīmimām .. 155.25 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
इक्ष्वाकुप्रभवो राजा नप्ता शुद्धोदनस्य च .
चाणक्यो नाम राजर्षिर्बुभुजे पृथिवीमिमाम् .. 155.25 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / A king arisen from Ikṣvāku, and the grandson of Śuddhodana, / a royal sage named Cāṇakya ruled over this earth.

6.3.s:
vikrānto matimāñchūraḥ sarvalokairavañcitaḥ .
vañcitaḥ sahasā dhūrtavāyasābhyāṃ nṛpottamaḥ .. 155.26 ..
6.3.d:
विक्रान्तो मतिमाञ्छूरः सर्वलोकैरवञ्चितः .
वञ्चितः सहसा धूर्तवायसाभ्यां नृपोत्तमः .. 155.26 ..
6.3.m: Valiant, intelligent, heroic, undeceived by anyone in all the worlds, / that best of kings was suddenly tricked by two rogue crows.

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
kathaṃ sa vañcito rājā vāyasābhyāṃ kuto'thavā .
purā yena pratijñātaṃ dhīgarbheṇa mahātmanā .. 155.27 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
कथं स वञ्चितो राजा वायसाभ्यां कुतोऽथवा .
पुरा येन प्रतिज्ञातं धीगर्भेण महात्मना .. 155.27 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / How was that king deceived by two crows, or whence did it occur? / By whom of old, a great-souled one endowed with wisdom, it had been resolved:

6.3.s:
na jīve vañcito'nyena prāṇāṃstyakṣye na saṃśayaḥ .
etanme vada viprendra paraṃ kautūhalaṃ mama .. 155.28 ..
6.3.d:
न जीवे वञ्चितोऽन्येन प्राणांस्त्यक्ष्ये न संशयः .
एतन्मे वद विप्रेन्द्र परं कौतूहलं मम .. 155.28 ..
6.3.m: 'I shall not live if deceived by another; I will abandon my life, there is no doubt.' / Tell me this, O foremost of vipras, for my curiosity is great.

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
ātmānaṃ vañcitaṃ jñātvā tadā saṃgṛhya vāyasau .
preṣayāmāsa tīvreṇa daṇḍena yamasādanam .. 155.29 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
आत्मानं वञ्चितं ज्ञात्वा तदा संगृह्य वायसौ .
प्रेषयामास तीव्रेण दण्डेन यमसादनम् .. 155.29 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Knowing himself to be tricked, he seized the two crows then, / and sent them by severe punishment to the abode of Yama.

6.3.s:
vāyasāvūcatuḥ .
sundopasundayoḥ putrāvāvāṃ kākatvamāgatau .
mā vadhīstvaṃ mahābhāga kasmiṃścitkāraṇāntare .. 155.30 ..
6.3.d:
वायसावूचतुः .
सुन्दोपसुन्दयोः पुत्रावावां काकत्वमागतौ .
मा वधीस्त्वं महाभाग कस्मिंश्चित्कारणान्तरे .. 155.30 ..
6.3.m: The two crows said: / 'We are the sons of Sunda and Upasunda, arrived into crowhood. / Do not kill us, O fortunate one, for the sake of some different reason!

6.3.s:
tāvāvāṃ kṛtasaṃkalpau tvayā kopena mānada .
nirastāvanirastau vā yāsyāvaḥ paramāṃ gatim .. 155.31 ..
6.3.d:
तावावां कृतसंकल्पौ त्वया कोपेन मानद .
निरस्तावनिरस्तौ वा यास्यावः परमां गतिम् .. 155.31 ..
6.3.m: Both of us have made our resolution; O giver of honor, whether expelled / or unexpelled by you in anger, we shall attain the supreme state.

6.3.s:
tadādeśaya rājendra kṛtvā tava mahatpriyam .
muktaśāpau bhaviṣyāvo brahmaṇo vacanaṃ tathā .. 155.32 ..
6.3.d:
तदादेशय राजेन्द्र कृत्वा तव महत्प्रियम् .
मुक्तशापौ भविष्यावो ब्रह्मणो वचनं तथा .. 155.32 ..
6.3.m: Therefore, command us, O supreme king, so that, having done what is exceedingly pleasing to you, / we two may become freed from the curse; such is the word of Brahmā.'

6.3.s:
tacchrutvā kākavacanaṃ cāṇakyo nṛpasattamaḥ .
nāhaṃ jīve viditvaivaṃ vañcitaḥ kena karhicit .. 155.33 ..
6.3.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा काकवचनं चाणक्यो नृपसत्तमः .
नाहं जीवे विदित्वैवं वञ्चितः केन कर्हिचित् .. 155.33 ..
6.3.m: Hearing that speech of the crows, Cāṇakya, the best among kings, said: / 'Knowing this, I cannot live having been ever tricked by anyone.

6.3.s:
tasmāttīrthaṃ vijānītaṃ yamasya sadane dvijau .
preṣayāmi yathānyāyaṃ śrutvā tatkathayiṣyathaḥ .. 155.34 ..
6.3.d:
तस्मात्तीर्थं विजानीतं यमस्य सदने द्विजौ .
प्रेषयामि यथान्यायं श्रुत्वा तत्कथयिष्यथः .. 155.34 ..
6.3.m: Therefore, you two birds, find out about the sacred ford in the abode of Yama! / I dispatch you duly; having heard of it, you shall tell it to me.'

6.3.s:
tenaiva muktau tau kākau srakcandanavibhūṣitau .
śīghragau preṣayāmāsa yamasya sadanaṃ prati .. 155.35 ..
6.3.d:
तेनैव मुक्तौ तौ काकौ स्रक्चन्दनविभूषितौ .
शीघ्रगौ प्रेषयामास यमस्य सदनं प्रति .. 155.35 ..
6.3.m: Released by him, those two swift-flying crows, adorned with garlands and sandalwood paste, / were dispatched towards the abode of Yama.

6.3.s:
rājovāca -
tatra dharmapuraṃ gatvā vicarantāvitastataḥ .
yadi pṛcchati dharmātmā yamaḥ saṃyamano mahān .. 155.36 ..
6.3.d:
राजोवाच -
तत्र धर्मपुरं गत्वा विचरन्तावितस्ततः .
यदि पृच्छति धर्मात्मा यमः संयमनो महान् .. 155.36 ..
6.3.m:
The king said:
"Having gone to the City of Dharma and wandering there, here and there, / if the righteous Yama, the great Restrainer, asks:

6.3.s:
kuto vāmāgataṃ brūtaṃ kena vā bhūṣitāvubhau .
madīyā bhāratī tasya kathanīyā hyaśaṅkitam .. 155.37 ..
6.3.d:
कुतो वामागतं ब्रूतं केन वा भूषितावुभौ .
मदीया भारती तस्य कथनीया ह्यशङ्कितम् .. 155.37 ..
6.3.m: 'Tell [me], from where have you two come, or by whom are you both adorned?' / then my word must indeed be spoken to him without fear:

6.3.s:
ikṣvākusaṃbhavo rājā cāṇakyo nāma dhārmikaḥ .
dvādaśāhe mṛtasyāsya tarpitāvaśanādinā .. 155.38 ..
6.3.d:
इक्ष्वाकुसंभवो राजा चाणक्यो नाम धार्मिकः .
द्वादशाहे मृतस्यास्य तर्पितावशनादिना .. 155.38 ..
6.3.m: 'A righteous king born of Ikṣvāku's race named Cāṇakya / has died; on his twelfth day, we two were satiated with food and offerings.'"

6.3.s:
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ rājño gatau tau yamasādanam .
krīḍitau prāṅgaṇe tasya srakcandanavibhūṣitau .
dharmarājena tau dṛṣṭau pṛṣṭau dhṛṣṭau ca vāyasau .. 155.39 ..
6.3.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं राज्ञो गतौ तौ यमसादनम् .
क्रीडितौ प्राङ्गणे तस्य स्रक्चन्दनविभूषितौ .
धर्मराजेन तौ दृष्टौ पृष्टौ धृष्टौ च वायसौ .. 155.39 ..
6.3.m: Having heard those words of the king, the two went to Yama's dwelling. / They frolicked in his courtyard, adorned with garlands and sandalwood paste. / Seen by the King of Dharma, the two bold crows were questioned.

6.3.s:
yama uvāca -
kutaḥ sthānātsamāyātau kena vā bhūṣitāvubhau .
vṛttaṃ vai kathyatāmetadvāyasāvaviśaṅkayā .. 155.40 ..
6.3.d:
यम उवाच -
कुतः स्थानात्समायातौ केन वा भूषितावुभौ .
वृत्तं वै कथ्यतामेतद्वायसावविशङ्कया .. 155.40 ..
6.3.m:
Yama said:
"From what place have you two arrived, or by whom are you both adorned? / O two crows, tell this account indeed without hesitation."

6.3.s:
kākāvūcatuḥ .
ikṣvākusambhavo rājā cāṇakyo nāma dhārmikaḥ .
dvādaśāhe mṛtasyāsya tarpitāvaśanādibhiḥ .. 155.41 ..
6.3.d:
काकावूचतुः .
इक्ष्वाकुसम्भवो राजा चाणक्यो नाम धार्मिकः .
द्वादशाहे मृतस्यास्य तर्पितावशनादिभिः .. 155.41 ..
6.3.m:
The two crows said:
"A righteous king born of Ikṣvāku's race named Cāṇakya / has died; on his twelfth day, we were satiated with food and offerings."

6.3.s:
tayostadvacanaṃ śrutvā sadā vaivasvato yamaḥ .
citraguptaṃ kaliṃ kālaṃ vīkṣyatāmidamabravīt .. 155.42 ..
6.3.d:
तयोस्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सदा वैवस्वतो यमः .
चित्रगुप्तं कलिं कालं वीक्ष्यतामिदमब्रवीत् .. 155.42 ..
6.3.m: Having heard that statement of the two, the eternal Vaivasvata Yama, / having looked at Chitragupta, Kali, and Kāla, said this:

6.3.s:
aṇḍajasvedajātīnāṃ bhūtānāṃ sacarācare .
vihitaṃ lokakartḥṇāṃ sānnidhyaṃ brahmaṇā mama .. 155.43 ..
6.3.d:
अण्डजस्वेदजातीनां भूतानां सचराचरे .
विहितं लोककर्त्ःणां सान्निध्यं ब्रह्मणा मम .. 155.43 ..
6.3.m: "Of beings born of eggs and sweat among the moving and unmoving, / by Brahmā, the presence of the makers of the worlds has been assigned to me.

6.3.s:
gataḥ kutra durācāraścāṇakyo nāmatastviha .
anviṣyatāṃ purāṇeṣu tvitihāseṣu yā gatiḥ .. 155.44 ..
6.3.d:
गतः कुत्र दुराचारश्चाणक्यो नामतस्त्विह .
अन्विष्यतां पुराणेषु त्वितिहासेषु या गतिः .. 155.44 ..
6.3.m: Where has the wicked one named Cāṇakya gone from here? / Let the destiny that is [recorded] in the Purāṇas and Itihāsas be investigated!"

6.3.s:
tatastairdharmapālaistu dharmarājapracoditaiḥ .
nirīkṣitā purāṇoktā karmajā gatirāgatiḥ .. 155.45 ..
6.3.d:
ततस्तैर्धर्मपालैस्तु धर्मराजप्रचोदितैः .
निरीक्षिता पुराणोक्ता कर्मजा गतिरागतिः .. 155.45 ..
6.3.m: Then, by those guardians of dharma urged by the King of Dharma, / the arrival and destiny born of karma as spoken in the Purāṇas was examined.

6.3.s:
tataḥ provāca vacanaṃ dharmo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ .
śṛṇvatāṃ dharmapālānāṃ meghagambhīrayā girā .. 155.46 ..
6.3.d:
ततः प्रोवाच वचनं धर्मो धर्मभृतां वरः .
शृण्वतां धर्मपालानां मेघगम्भीरया गिरा .. 155.46 ..
6.3.m: Then Dharma, the foremost of the maintainers of dharma, / spoke a statement in a voice deep as a thundercloud while the guardians of dharma listened:

6.3.s:
śuklatīrthe mṛtānāṃ tu narmadāvimale jale .
aṇḍajasvedajātīnāṃ na gatirmama sannidhau .. 155.47 ..
6.3.d:
शुक्लतीर्थे मृतानां तु नर्मदाविमले जले .
अण्डजस्वेदजातीनां न गतिर्मम सन्निधौ .. 155.47 ..
6.3.m: "Of those who die at Śuklatīrtha, in the clear water of the Narmadā, / among those born of eggs or sweat, there is no going to my presence.

6.3.s:
tattīrthaṃ dhārmikaṃ loke brahmaviṣṇumaheśvaraiḥ .
nirmitaṃ parayā bhaktyā lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā .. 155.48 ..
6.3.d:
तत्तीर्थं धार्मिकं लोके ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वरैः .
निर्मितं परया भक्त्या लोकानां हितकाम्यया .. 155.48 ..
6.3.m: That righteous sacred ford in the world was fashioned by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara / with supreme devotion, wishing for the welfare of the worlds.

6.3.s:
pāpopapātakairyuktā ye narā narmadājale .
śuklatīrthe mṛtāḥ śuddhā na te madviṣayāḥ kvacit .. 155.49 ..
6.3.d:
पापोपपातकैर्युक्ता ये नरा नर्मदाजले .
शुक्लतीर्थे मृताः शुद्धा न ते मद्विषयाः क्वचित् .. 155.49 ..
6.3.m: Men who are joined with sins and minor sins, / who die purified in the water of the Narmadā at Śuklatīrtha, are never my subjects."

6.3.s:
etacchrutvā tu vacanaṃ tau kākau yamabhāṣitam .
āgatau śīghragau pārtha dṛṣṭvā yamapuraṃ mahat .. 155.50 ..
6.3.d:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचनं तौ काकौ यमभाषितम् .
आगतौ शीघ्रगौ पार्थ दृष्ट्वा यमपुरं महत् .. 155.50 ..
6.3.m: Having heard this speech uttered by Yama, / those two swift-flying crows, having seen the great city of Yama, returned, O Pārtha.

6.3.s:
pṛṣṭau tau praṇatau rājñā yathāvṛttaṃ yathāśrutam .
kathayāmāsatuḥ pārtha dānavau kākatāṃ gatau .. 155.51 ..
6.3.d:
पृष्टौ तौ प्रणतौ राज्ञा यथावृत्तं यथाश्रुतम् .
कथयामासतुः पार्थ दानवौ काकतां गतौ .. 155.51 ..
6.3.m: Questioned by the king as they bowed, as it happened and as it was heard, / the two Dānavas who had become crows spoke, O Pārtha:

6.3.s:
asmātsthānādgatāvāvāṃ yamasya puramuttamam .
pṛthivyā dakṣiṇe bhāge hyatītya bahuyonijam .. 155.52 ..
6.3.d:
अस्मात्स्थानाद्गतावावां यमस्य पुरमुत्तमम् .
पृथिव्या दक्षिणे भागे ह्यतीत्य बहुयोनिजम् .. 155.52 ..
6.3.m: "From this place, we two went to the excellent city of Yama, / in the southern quarter of the earth, passing beyond many [destinies] born of wombs.

6.3.s:
tatpuraṃ kāmagaṃ divyaṃ svarṇaprākāratoraṇam .
anekagṛhasambādhaṃ maṇikāñcanabhūṣitam .. 155.53 ..
6.3.d:
तत्पुरं कामगं दिव्यं स्वर्णप्राकारतोरणम् .
अनेकगृहसम्बाधं मणिकाञ्चनभूषितम् .. 155.53 ..
6.3.m: That city moves at will, celestial, with golden ramparts and archways, / crowded with countless houses, adorned with jewels and gold,

6.3.s:
catuṣpathaiścatvaraiśca ghaṇṭāmārgopaśobhitam .
udyānavanasaṃchannaṃ padminīkhaṇḍamanditam .. 155.54 ..
6.3.d:
चतुष्पथैश्चत्वरैश्च घण्टामार्गोपशोभितम् .
उद्यानवनसंछन्नं पद्मिनीखण्डमन्दितम् .. 155.54 ..
6.3.m: graced with crossroads, squares, and ringing thoroughfares, / covered with parks and woods, ornamented with clusters of lotus ponds,

6.3.s:
haṃsasārasasaṃghuṣṭaṃ kokilākulasaṃkulam .
siṃhavyāghragajākīrṇamṛkṣavānarasevitam .. 155.55 ..
6.3.d:
हंससारससंघुष्टं कोकिलाकुलसंकुलम् .
सिंहव्याघ्रगजाकीर्णमृक्षवानरसेवितम् .. 155.55 ..
6.3.m: resounding with swans and sāra-cranes, teeming with multitudes of cuckoos, / filled with lions, tigers, and elephants, frequented by bears and monkeys,

6.3.s:
naranārīsamākīrṇaṃ nityotsavavibhūṣitam .
śaṃkhadundubhirnirghoṣairvīṇāveṇunināditam .. 155.56 ..
6.3.d:
नरनारीसमाकीर्णं नित्योत्सवविभूषितम् .
शंखदुन्दुभिर्निर्घोषैर्वीणावेणुनिनादितम् .. 155.56 ..
6.3.m: crowded with men and women, adorned with perpetual festivals, / resounding with the sounds of conches and drums, and with the melodies of viṇas and flutes.

6.3.s:
yamamārge'pi vihitaṃ svargalokamivāparam .
gatau tatra punaścānyairyamadūtairyamājñayā .. 155.57 ..
6.3.d:
यममार्गेऽपि विहितं स्वर्गलोकमिवापरम् .
गतौ तत्र पुनश्चान्यैर्यमदूतैर्यमाज्ञया .. 155.57 ..
6.3.m: Even on the path of Yama it is constructed like another heavenly world. / Having gone there, again by other messengers of Yama by Yama's order,

6.3.s:
viditau preṣitau tatra yatra devo jagatprabhuḥ .
prāṇasya bhītyā dṛṣṭo'sau siṃhāsanagataḥ prabhuḥ .. 155.58 ..
6.3.d:
विदितौ प्रेषितौ तत्र यत्र देवो जगत्प्रभुः .
प्राणस्य भीत्या दृष्टोऽसौ सिंहासनगतः प्रभुः .. 155.58 ..
6.3.m: we were announced and sent to where the god, the lord of the universe, was. / Out of fear for our lives, that lord was seen seated upon a lion-throne:

6.3.s:
mahākāyo mahājaṅgho mahāskandho mahodaraḥ .
mahāvakṣā mahābāhurmahāvaktrekṣaṇo mahān .. 155.59 ..
6.3.d:
महाकायो महाजङ्घो महास्कन्धो महोदरः .
महावक्षा महाबाहुर्महावक्त्रेक्षणो महान् .. 155.59 ..
6.3.m: huge-bodied, huge-shanked, huge-shouldered, huge-bellied, / huge-chested, huge-armed, with a huge face and huge eyes, great,

6.3.s:
mahāmahiṣamārūḍho mahāmukuṭabhūṣitaḥ .
tatrānyaśca kaliḥ kālaścitragupto mahāmatiḥ .. 155.60 ..
6.3.d:
महामहिषमारूढो महामुकुटभूषितः .
तत्रान्यश्च कलिः कालश्चित्रगुप्तो महामतिः .. 155.60 ..
6.3.m: mounted upon a huge buffalo, adorned with a great crown. / And there other [figures were seen]: Kali, Kāla, and the wise Citragupta,

6.3.s:
samāgatau tadā dṛṣṭau madhye jvalitapāvakau .
puṇyapāpāni jantūnāṃ śrutismṛtyarthapāragau .. 155.61 ..
6.3.d:
समागतौ तदा दृष्टौ मध्ये ज्वलितपावकौ .
पुण्यपापानि जन्तूनां श्रुतिस्मृत्यर्थपारगौ .. 155.61 ..
6.3.m: who had arrived and were seen with blazing fire between them, / masters of the meaning of the Śrutis and Smṛtis, [examining] the merits and sins of living beings.

6.3.s:
vicārayantau satataṃ tiṣṭhāte tau divāniśam .
tato hyāvāṃ praṇāmānte yamena yamamūrtinā .. 155.62 ..
6.3.d:
विचारयन्तौ सततं तिष्ठाते तौ दिवानिशम् .
ततो ह्यावां प्रणामान्ते यमेन यममूर्तिना .. 155.62 ..
6.3.m: Constantly deliberating, those two stand day and night. / Then, at the conclusion of our salutation, by Yama in the form of the Restrainer,

6.3.s:
pṛṣṭāvāgamane hetuṃ tamabrūva śṛṇuṣva tat .
ujjayinyāṃ mahīpālaścāṇakyo'bhūtpratāpavān .. 155.63 ..
6.3.d:
पृष्टावागमने हेतुं तमब्रूव शृणुष्व तत् .
उज्जयिन्यां महीपालश्चाणक्योऽभूत्प्रतापवान् .. 155.63 ..
6.3.m: we were asked the cause of our arrival. We spoke to him—hear that: / 'In Ujjayinī there was a glorious king named Cāṇakya.

6.3.s:
dvādaśāhe mṛtasyāsya bhuktvā prāptau yamālayam .
tato'smākaṃ vacaḥ śrutvā kampayitvā śiro yamaḥ .. 155.64 ..
6.3.d:
द्वादशाहे मृतस्यास्य भुक्त्वा प्राप्तौ यमालयम् .
ततोऽस्माकं वचः श्रुत्वा कम्पयित्वा शिरो यमः .. 155.64 ..
6.3.m: He died, and on his twelfth day, having eaten, we reached the abode of Yama.' / Then, having heard our words, shaking his head, Yama

6.3.s:
uvāca vacanaṃ satyaṃ sabhāmadhye hasanniva .
asti tatkāraṇaṃ yena cāṇakyaḥ pāpapūruṣaḥ .. 155.65 ..
6.3.d:
उवाच वचनं सत्यं सभामध्ये हसन्निव .
अस्ति तत्कारणं येन चाणक्यः पापपूरुषः .. 155.65 ..
6.3.m: spoke a true statement in the midst of the assembly, smiling as it were: / 'There is a reason by which Cāṇakya, a man of sin,

6.3.s:
nāyāto mama loke tu sarvapāpabhayaṃkare .
śuklatīrthe mṛtānāṃ tu narmadāyāṃ paraṃ padam .. 155.66 ..
6.3.d:
नायातो मम लोके तु सर्वपापभयंकरे .
शुक्लतीर्थे मृतानां तु नर्मदायां परं पदम् .. 155.66 ..
6.3.m: has not come to my realm, which is terrible to all sins. / For those who die at Śuklatīrtha on the Narmadā, the supreme abode

6.3.s:
jāyate sarvajantūnāṃ nātra kācidvicāraṇā .
avaśaḥ svavaśo vāpi jantustatkṣetramaṇḍale .. 155.67 ..
6.3.d:
जायते सर्वजन्तूनां नात्र काचिद्विचारणा .
अवशः स्ववशो वापि जन्तुस्तत्क्षेत्रमण्डले .. 155.67 ..
6.3.m: arises for all living creatures; there is no doubt about this. / Helpless or master of himself, when a creature dies in the circle of that sacred field,

6.3.s:
mṛtaḥ sa vai na sandeho rudrasyānucaro bhavet .
taddharmavacanaṃ śrutvā nirgatya nagarādbahiḥ .. 155.68 ..
6.3.d:
मृतः स वै न सन्देहो रुद्रस्यानुचरो भवेत् .
तद्धर्मवचनं श्रुत्वा निर्गत्य नगराद्बहिः .. 155.68 ..
6.3.m: he surely becomes an attendant of Rudra—there is no doubt.' / Having heard that righteous word, having gone outside the city,

6.3.s:
paśyantau vividhāṃ ghorāṃ narake lokayātanām .
triṃśatkoṭyo hi ghorāṇāṃ narakāṇāṃ nṛpottama .. 155.69 ..
6.3.d:
पश्यन्तौ विविधां घोरां नरके लोकयातनाम् .
त्रिंशत्कोट्यो हि घोराणां नरकाणां नृपोत्तम .. 155.69 ..
6.3.m: seeing the various dreadful torments of the worlds in hell— / for there are thirty crores of dreadful hells, O best of kings—

6.3.s:
dṛṣṭā bhītau parāmārtigatau tatra mahāpathi .
narako rauravastatra mahāraurava eva ca .. 155.70 ..
6.3.d:
दृष्टा भीतौ परामार्तिगतौ तत्र महापथि .
नरको रौरवस्तत्र महारौरव एव च .. 155.70 ..
6.3.m: we, being terrified, reached the greatest distress there on the great highway. / The hell Raurava was there, and also Mahāraurava,

6.3.s:
peṣaṇaḥ śoṣaṇaścaiva kālasūtro'sthibhañjanaḥ .
tāmisraścāndhatāmisraḥ kṛmipūtivahastathā .. 155.71 ..
6.3.d:
पेषणः शोषणश्चैव कालसूत्रोऽस्थिभञ्जनः .
तामिस्रश्चान्धतामिस्रः कृमिपूतिवहस्तथा .. 155.71 ..
6.3.m: Peṣaṇa, Śoṣaṇa, and Kālasūtra, Asthibhañjana, / Tāmisra, Andhatāmisra, and Kṛmipūtivaha,

6.3.s:
dṛṣṭaścānyo mahājvālastatraiva viṣabhojanaḥ .
narakau daṃśamaśakau tathā yamalaparvatau .. 155.72 ..
6.3.d:
दृष्टश्चान्यो महाज्वालस्तत्रैव विषभोजनः .
नरकौ दंशमशकौ तथा यमलपर्वतौ .. 155.72 ..
6.3.m: and another, Mahājvāla, was seen right there, and Viṣabhojana, / the two hells Daṃśamaśaka, and likewise the Twin Mountains.

6.3.s:
nadī vaitaraṇī dṛṣṭā sarvapāpapraṇāśinī .
śītalaṃ salilaṃ yatra pibanti hyamṛtopamam .. 155.73 ..
6.3.d:
नदी वैतरणी दृष्टा सर्वपापप्रणाशिनी .
शीतलं सलिलं यत्र पिबन्ति ह्यमृतोपमम् .. 155.73 ..
6.3.m: The river Vaitaraṇī was seen, destroyer of all sins, / where [the virtuous] drink cool water resembling nectar,

6.3.s:
tadeva nīraṃ pāpānāṃ śoṇitaṃ parivartate .
asipatravanaṃ cānyaddṛṣṭānyā mahatī śilā .. 155.74 ..
6.3.d:
तदेव नीरं पापानां शोणितं परिवर्तते .
असिपत्रवनं चान्यद्दृष्टान्या महती शिला .. 155.74 ..
6.3.m: yet that same water turns into blood for sinners. / And another, the Asipatravana forest, was seen, and another huge stone,

6.3.s:
agnipuṃjanibhākārā viśālā śālmalī parā .
ityādayastathaivānye śatasāhasrasaṃjñitāḥ .. 155.75 ..
6.3.d:
अग्निपुंजनिभाकारा विशाला शाल्मली परा .
इत्यादयस्तथैवान्ये शतसाहस्रसंज्ञिताः .. 155.75 ..
6.3.m: resembling a mass of fire, and another vast Śālmalī tree. / These and others designated in the hundreds and thousands,

6.3.s:
ghoraghoratarā dṛṣṭāḥ kliśyante yatra mānavāḥ .
vācikairmānasaiḥ pāpaiḥ karmajaiśca pṛthagvidhaiḥ .. 155.76 ..
6.3.d:
घोरघोरतरा दृष्टाः क्लिश्यन्ते यत्र मानवाः .
वाचिकैर्मानसैः पापैः कर्मजैश्च पृथग्विधैः .. 155.76 ..
6.3.m: dreadful and more dreadful, were seen, where human beings are tormented / on account of verbal and mental sins, and various kinds born of action,

6.3.s:
ahaṃkārakṛtairdoṣairmāyāvacanapūrvakaiḥ .
pitā mātā gururbhrātā anāthā vikalendriyāḥ .. 155.77 ..
6.3.d:
अहंकारकृतैर्दोषैर्मायावचनपूर्वकैः .
पिता माता गुरुर्भ्राता अनाथा विकलेन्द्रियाः .. 155.77 ..
6.3.m: faults caused by egotism preceded by deceitful words: / father, mother, guru, brother, the helpless, and the disabled,

6.3.s:
bhramanti noddhṛtā yeṣāṃ gatisteṣāṃ hi raurave .
tatra te dvādaśābdāni kṣapitvā raurave'dhamāḥ .. 155.78 ..
6.3.d:
भ्रमन्ति नोद्धृता येषां गतिस्तेषां हि रौरवे .
तत्र ते द्वादशाब्दानि क्षपित्वा रौरवेऽधमाः .. 155.78 ..
6.3.m: who wander and have not been rescued—such people's destination is indeed in Raurava. / Having spent twelve years there in Raurava, those vile ones

6.3.s:
iha mānuṣyake loke dīnāndhāśca bhavanti te .
devabrahmasvahartḥṇāṃ narāṇāṃ pāpakarmaṇām .. 155.79 ..
6.3.d:
इह मानुष्यके लोके दीनान्धाश्च भवन्ति ते .
देवब्रह्मस्वहर्त्ःणां नराणां पापकर्मणाम् .. 155.79 ..
6.3.m: In this human world, they become wretched and blind. / For men of evil deeds who rob the property of the gods and brahmins,

6.3.s:
mahārauravamāśritya dhruvaṃ vāso yamālaye .
tataḥ kālena mahatā pāpāḥ pāpena veṣṭitāḥ .. 155.80 ..
6.3.d:
महारौरवमाश्रित्य ध्रुवं वासो यमालये .
ततः कालेन महता पापाः पापेन वेष्टिताः .. 155.80 ..
6.3.m: dwelling in Yama's abode, consigned to Mahāraurava, is certain. / Then, after a long time, the sinful ones, wrapped up in their sin,

6.3.s:
jāyante kaṇṭakairbhinnāḥ kośe vā kośakārakāḥ .
mṛgapakṣivihaṅgānāṃ ghātakā māṃsabhakṣakāḥ .. 155.81 ..
6.3.d:
जायन्ते कण्टकैर्भिन्नाः कोशे वा कोशकारकाः .
मृगपक्षिविहङ्गानां घातका मांसभक्षकाः .. 155.81 ..
6.3.m: are born pierced by thorns, or as silkworms within cocoons. / Killers of deer, birds, and winged creatures, and eaters of flesh,

6.3.s:
peṣaṇaṃ narakaṃ yānti śoṣaṇaṃ jīvabandhanāt .
tatratyāṃ yātanāṃ ghorāṃ sahitvā śāstracoditām .. 155.82 ..
6.3.d:
पेषणं नरकं यान्ति शोषणं जीवबन्धनात् .
तत्रत्यां यातनां घोरां सहित्वा शास्त्रचोदिताम् .. 155.82 ..
6.3.m: go to the Peṣaṇa hell, and Śoṣaṇa from binding living beings. / Having endured the terrible torment there ordained by the scriptures,

6.3.s:
iha mānuṣyatāṃ prāpya paṅgvandhabadhirā narāḥ .
gavārthe brāhmaṇārthe ca hyanṛtaṃ vadatāmiha .. 155.83 ..
6.3.d:
इह मानुष्यतां प्राप्य पङ्ग्वन्धबधिरा नराः .
गवार्थे ब्राह्मणार्थे च ह्यनृतं वदतामिह .. 155.83 ..
6.3.m: and attaining humanity here, men become lame, blind, and deaf. / For those speaking untruths in this world for the sake of cattle or a brahmin,

6.3.s:
patanaṃ jāyate puṃsāṃ narake kālasūtrake .
tatratyā yātanā ghorā vihitā śāstrakartṛbhiḥ .. 155.84 ..
6.3.d:
पतनं जायते पुंसां नरके कालसूत्रके .
तत्रत्या यातना घोरा विहिता शास्त्रकर्तृभिः .. 155.84 ..
6.3.m: a fall into the Kālasūtraka hell occurs for men. / Having experienced the terrible torment there ordained by the authors of the scriptures,

6.3.s:
bhuktvā samāgatā hyatra te yāsyantyantyajāṃ gatim .
bandhayanti ca ye jīvāṃstyaktvātmakulasantatim .. 155.85 ..
6.3.d:
भुक्त्वा समागता ह्यत्र ते यास्यन्त्यन्त्यजां गतिम् .
बन्धयन्ति च ये जीवांस्त्यक्त्वात्मकुलसन्ततिम् .. 155.85 ..
6.3.m: and having returned here, they shall attain an outcaste birth. / And those who bind living beings, abandoning the lineage of their own family,

6.3.s:
patanti nātra sandeho narake te'sthibhañjane .
tatra varṣaśatasyānta iha mānuṣyatāṃ gatāḥ .. 155.86 ..
6.3.d:
पतन्ति नात्र सन्देहो नरके तेऽस्थिभञ्जने .
तत्र वर्षशतस्यान्त इह मानुष्यतां गताः .. 155.86 ..
6.3.m: fall, without a doubt, into the Asthibhañjana hell. / There, at the end of a hundred years, having attained humanity here,

6.3.s:
kubjā vāmanakāḥ pāpā jāyante duḥkhabhāginaḥ .
ye tyajanti svakāṃ bhāryāṃ mūḍhāḥ paṇḍitamāninaḥ .. 155.87 ..
6.3.d:
कुब्जा वामनकाः पापा जायन्ते दुःखभागिनः .
ये त्यजन्ति स्वकां भार्यां मूढाः पण्डितमानिनः .. 155.87 ..
6.3.m: those sinners are born as hunchbacks and dwarfs, experiencing sorrow. / Those foolish men considering themselves learned who abandon their own wives,

6.3.s:
te yānti narakaṃ ghoraṃ tāmisraṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ .
tatra varṣaśatasyānte iha mānuṣyatāṃ gatāḥ .. 155.88 ..
6.3.d:
ते यान्ति नरकं घोरं तामिस्रं नात्र संशयः .
तत्र वर्षशतस्यान्ते इह मानुष्यतां गताः .. 155.88 ..
6.3.m: go to the terrible hell Tāmisra; there is no doubt of this. / There, at the end of a hundred years, having attained humanity here,

6.3.s:
duścarmāṇo durbhagāśca jāyante mānavā hi te .
mānakūṭaṃ tulākūṭaṃ kūṭakaṃ tu vadanti ye .. 155.89 ..
6.3.d:
दुश्चर्माणो दुर्भगाश्च जायन्ते मानवा हि ते .
मानकूटं तुलाकूटं कूटकं तु वदन्ति ये .. 155.89 ..
6.3.m: those men are indeed born with skin diseases and misfortune. / But those who speak false measures, false balances, and falsehoods,

6.3.s:
narake te'ndhatāmisre prapacyante narādhamāḥ .
śatasāhasrikaṃ kālamuṣitvā tatra te narāḥ .. 155.90 ..
6.3.d:
नरके तेऽन्धतामिस्रे प्रपच्यन्ते नराधमाः .
शतसाहस्रिकं कालमुषित्वा तत्र ते नराः .. 155.90 ..
6.3.m: those lowest of men are cooked in the Andhatāmisra hell. / Having dwelt there for a period of a hundred thousand years, those men,

6.3.s:
iha śatrugṛhe tvandhā bhramante dīnamūrtayaḥ .
pitṛdevadvijebhyo'nnamadattvā ye'tra bhuñjate .. 155.91 ..
6.3.d:
इह शत्रुगृहे त्वन्धा भ्रमन्ते दीनमूर्तयः .
पितृदेवद्विजेभ्योऽन्नमदत्त्वा येऽत्र भुञ्जते .. 155.91 ..
6.3.m: wretched in form, wander blind here in an enemy's house. / Those who eat here without offering food to ancestors, gods, and twice-born,

6.3.s:
narake kṛmibhakṣye te patanti svātmapoṣakāḥ .
tataḥ prasūtikāle hi kṛmibhuktaśca savraṇaḥ .. 155.92 ..
6.3.d:
नरके कृमिभक्ष्ये ते पतन्ति स्वात्मपोषकाः .
ततः प्रसूतिकाले हि कृमिभुक्तश्च सव्रणः .. 155.92 ..
6.3.m: those nourishers of their own selves fall into the Kṛmibhakṣya hell. / Then, at the time of rebirth, eaten by worms and full of sores,

6.3.s:
jāyate'śucigandho'tra parabhāgyopajīvakaḥ .
svakarmavicyutāḥ pāpā varṇāśramavivarjitāḥ .. 155.93 ..
6.3.d:
जायतेऽशुचिगन्धोऽत्र परभाग्योपजीवकः .
स्वकर्मविच्युताः पापा वर्णाश्रमविवर्जिताः .. 155.93 ..
6.3.m: such a person is born foul-smelling here, living off the fortune of others. / The sinners fallen from their proper duties, devoid of caste and stage of life,

6.3.s:
narake pūyasampūrṇe kliśyante hyayutaṃ samāḥ .
pūrṇe tatra tataḥ kāle prāpya mānuṣyakaṃ bhavam .. 155.94 ..
6.3.d:
नरके पूयसम्पूर्णे क्लिश्यन्ते ह्ययुतं समाः .
पूर्णे तत्र ततः काले प्राप्य मानुष्यकं भवम् .. 155.94 ..
6.3.m: suffer in the hell filled with pus for ten thousand years. / Then, when that time is completed, having attained a human rebirth,

6.3.s:
udvejanīyā bhūtānāṃ jāyante vyādhibhirvṛtāḥ .
agnido garadaścaiva lobhamohānvito naraḥ .. 155.95 ..
6.3.d:
उद्वेजनीया भूतानां जायन्ते व्याधिभिर्वृताः .
अग्निदो गरदश्चैव लोभमोहान्वितो नरः .. 155.95 ..
6.3.m: they are born repellent to living beings and afflicted with diseases. / An arsonist, a poisoner, and a man filled with greed and delusion,

6.3.s:
narake viṣasampūrṇe nimajjati durātmavān .
tatra varṣaśatātkālādunmajjanamavasthitaḥ .. 155.96 ..
6.3.d:
नरके विषसम्पूर्णे निमज्जति दुरात्मवान् .
तत्र वर्षशतात्कालादुन्मज्जनमवस्थितः .. 155.96 ..
6.3.m: that evil-minded person sinks into the hell filled with poison. / Remaining there, he emerges from that time after a hundred years;

6.3.s:
bhuvi mānuṣatāṃ prāpya kṛpaṇo jāyate punaḥ .
pādukopānahau chatraṃ śayyāṃ prāvaraṇāni ca .. 155.97 ..
6.3.d:
भुवि मानुषतां प्राप्य कृपणो जायते पुनः .
पादुकोपानहौ छत्रं शय्यां प्रावरणानि च .. 155.97 ..
6.3.m: having attained humanity on earth, he is born miserable again. / For not giving sandals, shoes, an umbrella, a bed, and coverings,

6.3.s:
adattvā daṃśamaśakairbhakṣyante janyasaptatim .
piturdravyāpahartārastāḍanakrośane ratāḥ .. 155.98 ..
6.3.d:
अदत्त्वा दंशमशकैर्भक्ष्यन्ते जन्यसप्ततिम् .
पितुर्द्रव्यापहर्तारस्ताडनक्रोशने रताः .. 155.98 ..
6.3.m: they are eaten by gadflies and mosquitoes for seventy lifetimes. / Those who seize a father's wealth, engaged in beating and reproaching [him],

6.3.s:
pīḍanaṃ kriyate teṣāṃ yatra tau yugmaparvatau .
yā sā vaitaraṇī ghorā nadī raktapravāhinī .. 155.99 ..
6.3.d:
पीडनं क्रियते तेषां यत्र तौ युग्मपर्वतौ .
या सा वैतरणी घोरा नदी रक्तप्रवाहिनी .. 155.99 ..
6.3.m: their crushing is done where those two twin mountains are. / As for that terrible Vaitaraṇī, the river flowing with blood,

6.3.s:
pibanti rudhiraṃ tatra ye'bhiyānti rajasvalām .
asipatravane ghore pīḍyante pāpakāriṇaḥ .. 155.100 ..
6.3.d:
पिबन्ति रुधिरं तत्र येऽभियान्ति रजस्वलाम् .
असिपत्रवने घोरे पीड्यन्ते पापकारिणः .. 155.100 ..
6.3.m: those who approach a menstruating woman drink blood there. / In the terrible Asipatravana, the evildoers are tormented—

6.3.s:
parapīḍākarā nityaṃ ye naro'ntyajagāminaḥ .
gurudāraratānāṃ tu mahāpātakināmapi .. 155.101 ..
6.3.d:
परपीडाकरा नित्यं ये नरोऽन्त्यजगामिनः .
गुरुदाररतानां तु महापातकिनामपि .. 155.101 ..
6.3.m: those men who perpetually cause torment to others and have intercourse with outcaste women. / And for those great sinners delighting in the wife of a guru,

6.3.s:
śilāvagūhanaṃ teṣāṃ jāyate janmasaptatim .
jvalantīmāyasīṃ ghorāṃ bahukaṇṭakasaṃvṛtām .. 155.102 ..
6.3.d:
शिलावगूहनं तेषां जायते जन्मसप्ततिम् .
ज्वलन्तीमायसीं घोरां बहुकण्टकसंवृताम् .. 155.102 ..
6.3.m: embracing a stone pillar occurs for seventy lifetimes. / A blazing, dreadful iron tree covered with many thorns—

6.3.s:
śālmalīṃ te'vagūhanti paradāraratā hi ye .
parasya yoṣitaṃ hṛtvā brahmasvamapahṛtya ca .. 155.103 ..
6.3.d:
शाल्मलीं तेऽवगूहन्ति परदाररता हि ये .
परस्य योषितं हृत्वा ब्रह्मस्वमपहृत्य च .. 155.103 ..
6.3.m: the Śālmalī—is embraced by those who delight in another's wife. / Having abducted another's woman and stolen a brahmin's property,

6.3.s:
araṇye nirjale deśe sa bhavetkrūrarākṣasaḥ .
devasvaṃ brāhmaṇasvaṃ ca lobhenaivāharecca yaḥ .. 155.104 ..
6.3.d:
अरण्ये निर्जले देशे स भवेत्क्रूरराक्षसः .
देवस्वं ब्राह्मणस्वं च लोभेनैवाहरेच्च यः .. 155.104 ..
6.3.m: he will become a cruel rākṣasa in a waterless wilderness. / And he who seizes the property of gods and of brahmins through greed,

6.3.s:
sa pāpātmā pare loke gṛdhrocchiṣṭena jīvati .
evamādīni pāpāni bhuñjante yamaśāsanāt .. 155.105 ..
6.3.d:
स पापात्मा परे लोके गृध्रोच्छिष्टेन जीवति .
एवमादीनि पापानि भुञ्जन्ते यमशासनात् .. 155.105 ..
6.3.m: that sinful-souled one lives on the leavings of vultures in the other world. / Such and other punishments of sins they experience by Yama's decree,

6.3.s:
yeṣāṃ tu darśanādeva śravaṇājjāyate bhayam .
tathā dānaphalaṃ cānye bhuñjānā yamamandire .. 155.106 ..
6.3.d:
येषां तु दर्शनादेव श्रवणाज्जायते भयम् .
तथा दानफलं चान्ये भुञ्जाना यममन्दिरे .. 155.106 ..
6.3.m: the mere sight of which, and the hearing of which, produces dread. / Likewise, others enjoying the fruit of gifts in Yama's palace

6.3.s:
dṛṣṭāḥ śrutaṃ kathayatāṃ dūtānāṃ ca yamājñayā .
rathairanye gajairanye kecidvājibhirāvṛtāḥ .. 155.107 ..
6.3.d:
दृष्टाः श्रुतं कथयतां दूतानां च यमाज्ञया .
रथैरन्ये गजैरन्ये केचिद्वाजिभिरावृताः .. 155.107 ..
6.3.m: were seen, and heard of as the messengers related by Yama's order: / some accompanied by chariots, others by elephants, and some by horses,

6.3.s:
dṛṣṭāstatra mahābhāga tapaḥsaṃcayasaṃsthitāḥ .
godātā svarṇadātā ca bhūmiratnapradā narāḥ .. 155.108 ..
6.3.d:
दृष्टास्तत्र महाभाग तपःसंचयसंस्थिताः .
गोदाता स्वर्णदाता च भूमिरत्नप्रदा नराः .. 155.108 ..
6.3.m: were seen there, O noble one, established in their accumulated austerities. / The giver of cows, the giver of gold, and men who give land and gems—

6.3.s:
śayyāśanagṛhādīnāṃ sa lokaḥ kāmado nṛṇām .
annaṃ pānīyasahitaṃ dadate ye'tra mānavāḥ .. 155.109 ..
6.3.d:
शय्याशनगृहादीनां स लोकः कामदो नृणाम् .
अन्नं पानीयसहितं ददते येऽत्र मानवाः .. 155.109 ..
6.3.m: that world grants the desires of mortals regarding beds, food, houses, and the like. / Those men who give food accompanied by water here,

6.3.s:
tatra tṛptāḥ susaṃtuṣṭāḥ krīḍante yamasādane .
atra yaddīyate dānamapi vālāgramātrakam .. 155.110 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तृप्ताः सुसंतुष्टाः क्रीडन्ते यमसादने .
अत्र यद्दीयते दानमपि वालाग्रमात्रकम् .. 155.110 ..
6.3.m: rejoice there, sated and fully contented, in Yama's abode. / Whatever gift is given here, even the measure of the tip of a hair,

6.3.s:
tadakṣayaphalaṃ sarvaṃ śuklatīrthe nṛpottama .
etatte kathitaṃ sarvaṃ yaddṛṣṭaṃ yacca vai śrutam .. 155.111 ..
6.3.d:
तदक्षयफलं सर्वं शुक्लतीर्थे नृपोत्तम .
एतत्ते कथितं सर्वं यद्दृष्टं यच्च वै श्रुतम् .. 155.111 ..
6.3.m: all that has imperishable fruit at Śuklatīrtha, O best of kings. / All this has been related to you—what was seen and what was heard.

6.3.s:
kuruṣva yadabhipretaṃ yadi śaknoṣi mucyatām .
tayostadvacanaṃ śrutvā cāṇakyo hṛṣṭamānasaḥ .. 155.112 ..
6.3.d:
कुरुष्व यदभिप्रेतं यदि शक्नोषि मुच्यताम् .
तयोस्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा चाणक्यो हृष्टमानसः .. 155.112 ..
6.3.m: Do what is intended, if you are able to be released.' / Having heard the word of the two, Cāṇakya, joyful in mind,

6.3.s:
visarjayāmāsa khagāvabhinandya punaḥpunaḥ .
tābhyāṃ gatābhyāṃ sarvasvaṃ dattvā vipreṣu bhārata .. 155.113 ..
6.3.d:
विसर्जयामास खगावभिनन्द्य पुनःपुनः .
ताभ्यां गताभ्यां सर्वस्वं दत्त्वा विप्रेषु भारत .. 155.113 ..
6.3.m: dismissed the two birds, honouring them again and again. / When the two had departed, giving away all his wealth to the brahmins, O descendant of Bharata,

6.3.s:
kāmakrodhau parityajya jagāmāmaraparvatam .
tatra baddhvoḍupaṃ gāḍhaṃ kṛṣṇarajjvāvalambitam .. 155.114 ..
6.3.d:
कामक्रोधौ परित्यज्य जगामामरपर्वतम् .
तत्र बद्ध्वोडुपं गाढं कृष्णरज्ज्वावलम्बितम् .. 155.114 ..
6.3.m: and abandoning desire and anger, he went to Amaraparvata. / Fastening firmly a small boat there, suspended by a black cord,

6.3.s:
plavamāno jagāmā'śu dhyāyandevaṃ janārdanam .
ārogyaṃ bhāskarādiccheddhanaṃ vai jātavedasaḥ .. 155.115 ..
6.3.d:
प्लवमानो जगामाऽशु ध्यायन्देवं जनार्दनम् .
आरोग्यं भास्करादिच्छेद्धनं वै जातवेदसः .. 155.115 ..
6.3.m: he quickly set out floating, meditating upon Lord Janārdana. / One should desire health from the sun, and wealth indeed from fire;

6.3.s:
prāpnoti jñānamīśānānmokṣaṃ prāpnoti keśavāt .
nīlaṃ raktaṃ tadabhavanmecakaṃ yaddhi sūtrakam .. 155.116 ..
6.3.d:
प्राप्नोति ज्ञानमीशानान्मोक्षं प्राप्नोति केशवात् .
नीलं रक्तं तदभवन्मेचकं यद्धि सूत्रकम् .. 155.116 ..
6.3.m: one attains knowledge from Īśāna, and attains liberation from Keśava. / The cord that was blue, red, and dark-coloured,

6.3.s:
śuddhasphaṭikasaṅkāśaṃ dṛṣṭvā rajjuṃ mahāmatiḥ .
āplutya vimale toye gato'sau vaiṣṇavaṃ padam .. 155.117 ..
6.3.d:
शुद्धस्फटिकसङ्काशं दृष्ट्वा रज्जुं महामतिः .
आप्लुत्य विमले तोये गतोऽसौ वैष्णवं पदम् .. 155.117 ..
6.3.m: seeing the rope resembling pure crystal, the wise one / plunged into the spotless water and went to the realm of Viṣṇu.

6.3.s:
gāyanti yadvedavidaḥ purāṇaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ śāśvatamacyutāhvayam .
prāptaḥ sa taṃ rājasuto mahātmā nikṣipya dehaṃ śubhaśuklatīrthe .. 155.118 ..
6.3.d:
गायन्ति यद्वेदविदः पुराणं नारायणं शाश्वतमच्युताह्वयम् .
प्राप्तः स तं राजसुतो महात्मा निक्षिप्य देहं शुभशुक्लतीर्थे .. 155.118 ..
6.3.m: That eternal Nārāyaṇa, called Acyuta, the ancient one whom knowers of the Veda sing, / that high-souled king's son attained, having cast off his body at the auspicious Śuklatīrtha.

6.3.s:
eṣā te kathitā rājansiddhiścāṇakyabhūbhṛtaḥ .
tathānyattava vakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣvaikāgramānasaḥ .. 155.119 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe cāṇakyasiddhiprāptivarṇanaṃ nāma pañcapañcāśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 156
6.3.d:
एषा ते कथिता राजन्सिद्धिश्चाणक्यभूभृतः .
तथान्यत्तव वक्ष्यामि शृणुष्वैकाग्रमानसः .. 155.119 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे चाणक्यसिद्धिप्राप्तिवर्णनं नाम पञ्चपञ्चाशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 156
6.3.m:
This attainment of perfection of King Cāṇakya has been told to you, O king. / Likewise I shall tell you another; listen with focused mind.
Thus ends the one hundred and fifty-fifth chapter, named 'The Description of Cāṇakya's Attainment of Perfection', in the Revākhaṇḍa of the Avantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].
Chapter 156

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
nāsti lokeṣu tattīrthaṃ pṛthivyāṃ yannareśvara .
śuklatīrthena sadṛśamupamānena gīyate .. 156.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
नास्ति लोकेषु तत्तीर्थं पृथिव्यां यन्नरेश्वर .
शुक्लतीर्थेन सदृशमुपमानेन गीयते .. 156.1 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / "There is no sacred ford in the worlds upon earth, O ruler of men, / that is sung of as being comparable to Śuklatīrtha.

6.3.s:
śuklatīrthaṃ mahātīrthaṃ narmadāyāṃ vyavasthitam .
prāgudakpravaṇe deśe munisaṅghaniṣevitam .. 156.2 ..
6.3.d:
शुक्लतीर्थं महातीर्थं नर्मदायां व्यवस्थितम् .
प्रागुदक्प्रवणे देशे मुनिसङ्घनिषेवितम् .. 156.2 ..
6.3.m: Śuklatīrtha is a great sacred ford situated on the Narmadā, / in a place sloping towards the northeast, frequented by hosts of sages.

6.3.s:
vaiśākhe ca tathā māsi kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśī .
kailāsādumayā sārddhaṃ svayamāyāti śaṅkaraḥ .. 156.3 ..
6.3.d:
वैशाखे च तथा मासि कृष्णपक्षे चतुर्दशी .
कैलासादुमया सार्द्धं स्वयमायाति शङ्करः .. 156.3 ..
6.3.m: Moreover, on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight in the month of Vaiśākha, / Śaṃkara himself comes from Kailāsa along with Umā.

6.3.s:
madhyāhnasamaye snātvā paśyatyātmānamātmanā .
brahmaviṣṇvindrasahitaḥ śuklatīrthe samāhitaḥ .. 156.4 ..
6.3.d:
मध्याह्नसमये स्नात्वा पश्यत्यात्मानमात्मना .
ब्रह्मविष्ण्विन्द्रसहितः शुक्लतीर्थे समाहितः .. 156.4 ..
6.3.m: Having bathed at midday, composed in mind, together with Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Indra, / he beholds himself by himself at Śuklatīrtha.

6.3.s:
kārttikyāṃ tu viśeṣeṇa vaiśākhyāṃ ca narottama .
brahmaviṣṇumahādevān snātvā paśyati taddine .. 156.5 ..
6.3.d:
कार्त्तिक्यां तु विशेषेण वैशाख्यां च नरोत्तम .
ब्रह्मविष्णुमहादेवान् स्नात्वा पश्यति तद्दिने .. 156.5 ..
6.3.m: Especially on the full moon of Kārttika and that of Vaiśākha, O best of men, / having bathed, one beholds Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Mahādeva on that day.

6.3.s:
devarājaḥ suraiḥ sārddhaṃ vāyumārgavyavasthitaḥ .
kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśyāṃ snātvā paśyati śaṅkaram .. 156.6 ..
6.3.d:
देवराजः सुरैः सार्द्धं वायुमार्गव्यवस्थितः .
कृष्णपक्षे चतुर्दश्यां स्नात्वा पश्यति शङ्करम् .. 156.6 ..
6.3.m: The king of the gods, together with the deities, positioned in the aerial path, / having bathed on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, beholds Śaṃkara.

6.3.s:
gandharvāpsaraso yakṣāḥ siddhavidyādharoragāḥ .
taddine te'pi deveśaṃ dṛṣṭvā muñcanti kilbiṣam .. 156.7 ..
6.3.d:
गन्धर्वाप्सरसो यक्षाः सिद्धविद्याधरोरगाः .
तद्दिने तेऽपि देवेशं दृष्ट्वा मुञ्चन्ति किल्बिषम् .. 156.7 ..
6.3.m: Gandharvas, apsarases, yakṣas, siddhas, vidyādharas, and serpents— / they too, on that day, beholding the Lord of gods, cast off sin.

6.3.s:
ardhayojanavistāraṃ tadarddhenaiva cāyatam .
śuklatīrthaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam .. 156.8 ..
6.3.d:
अर्धयोजनविस्तारं तदर्द्धेनैव चायतम् .
शुक्लतीर्थं महापुण्यं महापातकनाशनम् .. 156.8 ..
6.3.m: Śuklatīrtha is half a yojana in extent and half of that in breadth, / exceedingly sacred, destroying great sins."

6.3.s:
yatra sthitaiḥ pradṛśyante vṛkṣāgrāṇi narottamaiḥ .
tatra sthitā mahāpāpairmucyante pūrvasaṃcitaiḥ .. 156.9 ..
6.3.d:
यत्र स्थितैः प्रदृश्यन्ते वृक्षाग्राणि नरोत्तमैः .
तत्र स्थिता महापापैर्मुच्यन्ते पूर्वसंचितैः .. 156.9 ..
6.3.m: Where the tree-tops are seen by the best of men standing [there], / standing there they are freed from great sins accumulated in the past.

6.3.s:
pāpopapātakairyukto naraḥ snātvā pramucyate .
upārjitā vinaśyeta bhrūṇahatyāpi dustyajā .. 156.10 ..
6.3.d:
पापोपपातकैर्युक्तो नरः स्नात्वा प्रमुच्यते .
उपार्जिता विनश्येत भ्रूणहत्यापि दुस्त्यजा .. 156.10 ..
6.3.m: A man afflicted with sins and minor offenses is freed upon bathing; / even the acquired killing of an embryo, so hard to get rid of, is destroyed.

6.3.s:
yasmāttatraiva deveśa umayā saha tiṣṭhati .
vaiśākhyāṃ ca viśeṣeṇa kailāsādeti śaṅkaraḥ .. 156.11 ..
6.3.d:
यस्मात्तत्रैव देवेश उमया सह तिष्ठति .
वैशाख्यां च विशेषेण कैलासादेति शङ्करः .. 156.11 ..
6.3.m: Because right there the lord of gods abides together with Umā, / and especially on the full moon of Vaiśākha, Śaṃkara arrives from Kailāsa.

6.3.s:
tena tīrthaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam .
kathitaṃ brahmaṇā pūrvaṃ mayā tava tathā nṛpa .. 156.12 ..
6.3.d:
तेन तीर्थं महापुण्यं सर्वपातकनाशनम् .
कथितं ब्रह्मणा पूर्वं मया तव तथा नृप .. 156.12 ..
6.3.m: Therefore the sacred ford is supremely holy and destroys all sins; / it was told by Brahmā in ancient times, and likewise by me to you, O king.

6.3.s:
rajakena yathā dhautaṃ vastraṃ bhavati nirmalam .
tathā tatra vapuḥsnānaṃ puruṣasya bhavecchuci .. 156.13 ..
6.3.d:
रजकेन यथा धौतं वस्त्रं भवति निर्मलम् .
तथा तत्र वपुःस्नानं पुरुषस्य भवेच्छुचि .. 156.13 ..
6.3.m: Just as a garment washed by a washerman becomes spotless, / so does a man's body become pure by bathing there.

6.3.s:
pūrve vayasi pāpāni kṛtvā puṣṭāni mānavaḥ .
ahorātroṣito bhūtvā śuklatīrthe vyapohati .. 156.14 ..
6.3.d:
पूर्वे वयसि पापानि कृत्वा पुष्टानि मानवः .
अहोरात्रोषितो भूत्वा शुक्लतीर्थे व्यपोहति .. 156.14 ..
6.3.m: A mortal who has committed heavy sins in his early life / removes them by fasting for a day and a night at Śuklatīrtha.

6.3.s:
śuklatīrthe mahārāja rākāṃ revājalāñjalim .
kalpakoṭisahasrāṇi dattvā syuḥ pitaraḥ śivāḥ .. 156.15 ..
6.3.d:
शुक्लतीर्थे महाराज राकां रेवाजलाञ्जलिम् .
कल्पकोटिसहस्राणि दत्त्वा स्युः पितरः शिवाः .. 156.15 ..
6.3.m: Offering a palmful of Revā's water at the full moon at Śuklatīrtha, O great king, / the ancestors will be blessed for thousands of crores of kalpas.

6.3.s:
na mātā na pitā bandhuḥ patanaṃ narakārṇave .
uddharanti yathā puṇyaṃ śuklatīrthe nareśvara .. 156.16 ..
6.3.d:
न माता न पिता बन्धुः पतनं नरकार्णवे .
उद्धरन्ति यथा पुण्यं शुक्लतीर्थे नरेश्वर .. 156.16 ..
6.3.m: Neither mother, nor father, nor kin rescues one falling into the ocean of hell, / as does the merit [earned] at Śuklatīrtha, O lord of men.

6.3.s:
tapasā brahmacaryeṇa na tāṃ gacchanti sadgatim .
śuklatīrthe mṛto janturdehatyāgena yāṃ labhet .. 156.17 ..
6.3.d:
तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण न तां गच्छन्ति सद्गतिम् .
शुक्लतीर्थे मृतो जन्तुर्देहत्यागेन यां लभेत् .. 156.17 ..
6.3.m: They do not reach by austerity or celibacy that noble destination / which a creature dying at Śuklatīrtha attains by casting off the body.

6.3.s:
kārttikasya tu māsasya kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśīm .
ghṛtena snāpayeddevamupoṣya prayato naraḥ .. 156.18 ..
6.3.d:
कार्त्तिकस्य तु मासस्य कृष्णपक्षे चतुर्दशीम् .
घृतेन स्नापयेद्देवमुपोष्य प्रयतो नरः .. 156.18 ..
6.3.m: On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Kārttika, / having fasted, a restrained man should bathe the god with clarified butter.

6.3.s:
snātvā prabhāte revāyāṃ dadyātsaghṛtakambalam .
sahiraṇyaṃ yathāśakti devamuddiśya śaṅkaraṃ .. 156.19 ..
6.3.d:
स्नात्वा प्रभाते रेवायां दद्यात्सघृतकम्बलम् .
सहिरण्यं यथाशक्ति देवमुद्दिश्य शङ्करं .. 156.19 ..
6.3.m: Having bathed in the morning in the Revā, he should offer a blanket anointed with clarified butter, / along with gold, according to his means, dedicated to the god Śaṃkara.

6.3.s:
devasya pūraṇaṃ kuryādghṛtena ghṛtakambalam .
sa gacchati mahātejāḥ śivalokaṃ mṛto naraḥ .. 156.20 ..
6.3.d:
देवस्य पूरणं कुर्याद्घृतेन घृतकम्बलम् .
स गच्छति महातेजाः शिवलोकं मृतो नरः .. 156.20 ..
6.3.m: He should cover the god with clarified butter, [offering] a blanket of ghee; / dying, that man of great splendor goes to the world of Śiva.

6.3.s:
ekaviṃśakulopeto yāvadābhūtasamplavam .
śuklatīrthe naraḥ snātvā hyumāṃ rudraṃ ca yo'rcayet .. 156.21 ..
6.3.d:
एकविंशकुलोपेतो यावदाभूतसम्प्लवम् .
शुक्लतीर्थे नरः स्नात्वा ह्युमां रुद्रं च योऽर्चयेत् .. 156.21 ..
6.3.m: Endowed with twenty-one generations until the universal dissolution of elements, / the man who, having bathed at Śuklatīrtha, indeed worships Umā and Rudra

6.3.s:
gandhapuṣpādidhūpaiśca so'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet .
māsopavāsaṃ yaḥ kuryāttatra tīrthe nareśvara .. 156.22 ..
6.3.d:
गन्धपुष्पादिधूपैश्च सोऽश्वमेधफलं लभेत् .
मासोपवासं यः कुर्यात्तत्र तीर्थे नरेश्वर .. 156.22 ..
6.3.m: with perfumes, flowers, and incenses, obtains the fruit of a horse-sacrifice. / O lord of men, he who observes a month-long fast at that sacred ford

6.3.s:
mucyate sa mahatpāpaiḥ saptajanmasusaṃcitaiḥ .
uṣṭrīkṣīramavikṣīraṃ navaśrāddhe ca bhojanam .. 156.23 ..
6.3.d:
मुच्यते स महत्पापैः सप्तजन्मसुसंचितैः .
उष्ट्रीक्षीरमविक्षीरं नवश्राद्धे च भोजनम् .. 156.23 ..
6.3.m: is freed from great sins well-accumulated over seven births: / [drinking] camel's milk, sheep's milk, and eating at an initial funeral feast,

6.3.s:
vṛṣalīgamanaṃ caiva tathābhakṣyasya bhakṣaṇam .
avikraye'nṛte pāpaṃ māhiṣe'yājyayājake .. 156.24 ..
6.3.d:
वृषलीगमनं चैव तथाभक्ष्यस्य भक्षणम् .
अविक्रयेऽनृते पापं माहिषेऽयाज्ययाजके .. 156.24 ..
6.3.m: approaching a low-caste woman, and likewise eating forbidden food, / the sin in selling what should not be sold, lying, [selling] buffaloes, officiating for the unworthy,

6.3.s:
vārddhuṣye paṅktigarade devabrāhmaṇadūṣake .
evamādīni pāpāni tathānyānyapi bhārata .. 156.25 ..
6.3.d:
वार्द्धुष्ये पङ्क्तिगरदे देवब्राह्मणदूषके .
एवमादीनि पापानि तथान्यान्यपि भारत .. 156.25 ..
6.3.m: usury, administering poison in a line of diners, reviling gods and brahmins — / these and other sins as well, O Bhārata,

6.3.s:
cāndrāyaṇena naśyanti śuklatīrthe na saṃśayaḥ .
śuklatīrthe tu yaḥ snātvā tarpayetpitṛdevatāḥ .. 156.26 ..
6.3.d:
चान्द्रायणेन नश्यन्ति शुक्लतीर्थे न संशयः .
शुक्लतीर्थे तु यः स्नात्वा तर्पयेत्पितृदेवताः .. 156.26 ..
6.3.m: are destroyed by a lunar penance at Śuklatīrtha, no doubt. / Moreover, whoever, having bathed at Śuklatīrtha, offers libations to the ancestral gods,

6.3.s:
tasya te dvādaśābdāni tṛptiṃ yānti sutarpitāḥ .
pādukopānahau chatraṃ śayyāmāsanameva ca .. 156.27 ..
6.3.d:
तस्य ते द्वादशाब्दानि तृप्तिं यान्ति सुतर्पिताः .
पादुकोपानहौ छत्रं शय्यामासनमेव च .. 156.27 ..
6.3.m: they, well-satisfied, remain content for twelve years. / Wooden sandals, leather shoes, an umbrella, a bed, and a seat,

6.3.s:
suvarṇaṃ dhanadhānyaṃ ca śrāddhaṃ yuktahalaṃ tathā .
annaṃ pānīyasaṃhitaṃ tasmiṃstīrthe dadanti ye .. 156.28 ..
6.3.d:
सुवर्णं धनधान्यं च श्राद्धं युक्तहलं तथा .
अन्नं पानीयसंहितं तस्मिंस्तीर्थे ददन्ति ये .. 156.28 ..
6.3.m: gold, wealth, grain, a funeral feast, a yoked plough, / food together with drinking water — those who give [these] at that sacred ford,

6.3.s:
hṛṣṭāḥ puṣṭā mṛtā yānti śivalokaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .
tatra tīrthe tu yo bhaktyā śivamuddiśya bhārata .. 156.29 ..
6.3.d:
हृष्टाः पुष्टा मृता यान्ति शिवलोकं न संशयः .
तत्र तीर्थे तु यो भक्त्या शिवमुद्दिश्य भारत .. 156.29 ..
6.3.m: joyful and thriving, go to the world of Śiva when dead, without doubt. / O Bhārata, whoever at that sacred ford, with devotion dedicated to Śiva,

6.3.s:
bhikṣāmātraṃ tathānnaṃ ye te'pi svaryānti vai narāḥ .
yajvināṃ vratināṃ caiva tatra tīrthanivāsinām .. 156.30 ..
6.3.d:
भिक्षामात्रं तथान्नं ये तेऽपि स्वर्यान्ति वै नराः .
यज्विनां व्रतिनां चैव तत्र तीर्थनिवासिनाम् .. 156.30 ..
6.3.m: offers even mere alms-food, those men also go to heaven. / For sacrificers and observers of vows dwelling at that sacred ford,

6.3.s:
api vālāgramātraṃ hi dattaṃ bhavati cākṣayam .
agnipraveśaṃ yaḥ kuryācchuklatīrthe samāhitaḥ .. 156.31 ..
6.3.d:
अपि वालाग्रमात्रं हि दत्तं भवति चाक्षयम् .
अग्निप्रवेशं यः कुर्याच्छुक्लतीर्थे समाहितः .. 156.31 ..
6.3.m: even [a gift] measuring the tip of a hair becomes imperishable. / He who, concentrated in mind, enters fire at Śuklatīrtha,

6.3.s:
rāgadveṣavinirmukto hṛdi dhyātvā janārdanam .
sarvakāmasusampūrṇaḥ sa gacchedvāruṇaṃ puram .. 156.32 ..
6.3.d:
रागद्वेषविनिर्मुक्तो हृदि ध्यात्वा जनार्दनम् .
सर्वकामसुसम्पूर्णः स गच्छेद्वारुणं पुरम् .. 156.32 ..
6.3.m: freed from passion and hatred, meditating on Janārdana in his heart, / completely fulfilled in all desires, goes to the city of Varuṇa.

6.3.s:
na rogo na jarā tatra yatra devo'ṃbhasāṃ patiḥ .
anāśakaṃ tu yaḥ kuryāttasmiṃstīrthe yudhiṣṭhira .. 156.33 ..
6.3.d:
न रोगो न जरा तत्र यत्र देवोऽंभसां पतिः .
अनाशकं तु यः कुर्यात्तस्मिंस्तीर्थे युधिष्ठिर .. 156.33 ..
6.3.m: There is neither disease nor old age there where the god is the lord of waters. / But he who undertakes a fast unto death at that sacred ford, O Yudhiṣṭhira,

6.3.s:
anivartikā gatistasya rudralokādasaṃśayam .
avaśaḥ svavaśo vāpi jantustatkṣetramaṇḍale .. 156.34 ..
6.3.d:
अनिवर्तिका गतिस्तस्य रुद्रलोकादसंशयम् .
अवशः स्ववशो वापि जन्तुस्तत्क्षेत्रमण्डले .. 156.34 ..
6.3.m: his destination from the world of Rudra has no return, without doubt. / Whether helpless or in control of himself, any creature in the circle of that sacred field

6.3.s:
mṛtaḥ sa tu na sandeho rudrasyānucaro bhavet .
śuklatīrthe tu yaḥ kanyāṃ śaktyā dadyādalaṃkṛtām .. 156.35 ..
6.3.d:
मृतः स तु न सन्देहो रुद्रस्यानुचरो भवेत् .
शुक्लतीर्थे तु यः कन्यां शक्त्या दद्यादलंकृताम् .. 156.35 ..
6.3.m: who dies becomes an attendant of Rudra, there is no doubt. / Whoever gives away an adorned maiden at Śuklatīrtha according to his means,

6.3.s:
vidhinā yo nṛpaśreṣṭha kurute vṛṣamokṣaṇam .
tasya yatphalamuddiṣṭaṃ purāṇe rudrabhāṣitam .. 156.36 ..
6.3.d:
विधिना यो नृपश्रेष्ठ कुरुते वृषमोक्षणम् .
तस्य यत्फलमुद्दिष्टं पुराणे रुद्रभाषितम् .. 156.36 ..
6.3.m: and he who performs the release of a bull according to rule, O best of kings — / the fruit of that declared in the Purāṇa as spoken by Rudra,

6.3.s:
tadahaṃ sampravakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣvaikamanā nṛpa .
yāvanto romakūpāḥ syuḥ sarvāṅgeṣu pṛthakpṛthak .. 156.37 ..
6.3.d:
तदहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणुष्वैकमना नृप .
यावन्तो रोमकूपाः स्युः सर्वाङ्गेषु पृथक्पृथक् .. 156.37 ..
6.3.m: that I will explain fully; listen with an attentive mind, O king: / as many hair-pores as there are across all his limbs separately,

6.3.s:
tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi rudraloke mahīyate .
śuklatīrthe tu yaddattaṃ grahaṇe candrasūryayoḥ .. 156.38 ..
6.3.d:
तावद्वर्षसहस्राणि रुद्रलोके महीयते .
शुक्लतीर्थे तु यद्दत्तं ग्रहणे चन्द्रसूर्ययोः .. 156.38 ..
6.3.m: for that many thousands of years he is exalted in the world of Rudra. / Whatever is given at Śuklatīrtha during an eclipse of the moon or the sun

6.3.s:
vardhate tadguṇaṃ tāvaddināni daśa pañca ca .
śuklatīrthe śucirbhūtvā yaḥ karoti pradakṣiṇam .. 156.39 ..
6.3.d:
वर्धते तद्गुणं तावद्दिनानि दश पञ्च च .
शुक्लतीर्थे शुचिर्भूत्वा यः करोति प्रदक्षिणम् .. 156.39 ..
6.3.m: multiplies by that factor for fifteen days. / Having become pure, whoever circumambulates Śuklatīrtha,

6.3.s:
pṛthvī pradakṣiṇā tena kṛtā yattasya tatphalam .
śobhanaṃ mithunaṃ yastu rudramuddiśya pūjayet .. 156.40 ..
6.3.d:
पृथ्वी प्रदक्षिणा तेन कृता यत्तस्य तत्फलम् .
शोभनं मिथुनं यस्तु रुद्रमुद्दिश्य पूजयेत् .. 156.40 ..
6.3.m: the earth has been circumambulated by him — such is the fruit he attains. / But he who worships an auspicious couple, dedicating [it] to Rudra,

6.3.s:
sapta janmāni tasyaiva viyogo na ca vai kvacit .
etatte kathitaṃ rājan saṃkṣepeṇa phalaṃ mahat .. 156.41 ..
6.3.d:
सप्त जन्मानि तस्यैव वियोगो न च वै क्वचित् .
एतत्ते कथितं राजन् संक्षेपेण फलं महत् .. 156.41 ..
6.3.m: for him there is never any separation across seven births. / This great fruit has been told to you in brief, O king,

6.3.s:
śuklatīrthasya yatpuṇyaṃ yathā devācchrutaṃ mayā .
ya idaṃ śṛṇuyādbhaktyā purāṇe vihitaṃ phalam .. 156.42 ..
6.3.d:
शुक्लतीर्थस्य यत्पुण्यं यथा देवाच्छ्रुतं मया .
य इदं शृणुयाद्भक्त्या पुराणे विहितं फलम् .. 156.42 ..
6.3.m: the merit of Śuklatīrtha, as heard by me from the god. / Whoever hears this fruit enjoined in the Purāṇa with devotion,

6.3.s:
sa labhennātra sandehaḥ satyaṃ satyaṃ punaḥ punaḥ .
putrārthī labhate putraṃ dhanārthī labhate dhanam .. 156.43 ..
6.3.d:
स लभेन्नात्र सन्देहः सत्यं सत्यं पुनः पुनः .
पुत्रार्थी लभते पुत्रं धनार्थी लभते धनम् .. 156.43 ..
6.3.m: he shall obtain it, there is no doubt here; it is true, true again and again. / One desiring a son obtains a son; one desiring wealth obtains wealth;

6.3.s:
mokṣārthī labhate mokṣaṃ snānadānaphalaṃ mahat .. 156.44 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe śuklatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma ṣaṭpañcāśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 157
6.3.d:
मोक्षार्थी लभते मोक्षं स्नानदानफलं महत् .. 156.44 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे शुक्लतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम षट्पञ्चाशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 157
6.3.m:
one desiring liberation obtains liberation, the great fruit of bathing and giving.
Thus ends the one hundred fifty-sixth chapter, named the Description of the Greatness of Śuklatīrtha, in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth, Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the great Skanda Purāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].
Chapter 157

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tasyaivānantaraṃ rājañchuklatīrthasamīpataḥ .
vāsudevasya tīrthaṃ tu sarvalokeṣu pūjitam .. 157.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
तस्यैवानन्तरं राजञ्छुक्लतीर्थसमीपतः .
वासुदेवस्य तीर्थं तु सर्वलोकेषु पूजितम् .. 157.1 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Immediately after that, O king, near Śuklatīrtha, / is the sacred ford of Vāsudeva, revered across all the worlds.

6.3.s:
taddhi puṇyaṃ suvikhyātaṃ narmadāyāṃ purātanam .
yatra huṅkāramātreṇa revā krośaṃ jagāma sā .. 157.2 ..
6.3.d:
तद्धि पुण्यं सुविख्यातं नर्मदायां पुरातनम् .
यत्र हुङ्कारमात्रेण रेवा क्रोशं जगाम सा .. 157.2 ..
6.3.m: It is indeed holy, celebrated, and ancient on the Narmadā, / where by a mere roar the Revā receded by a krośa.

6.3.s:
yadā prabhṛti rājendra huṅkāreṇa gatā sarit .
tadāprabhṛti sa svāmī huṅkāraḥ śabdito budhaiḥ .. 157.3 ..
6.3.d:
यदा प्रभृति राजेन्द्र हुङ्कारेण गता सरित् .
तदाप्रभृति स स्वामी हुङ्कारः शब्दितो बुधैः .. 157.3 ..
6.3.m: From the time the river receded by the roar, O chief of kings, / from that time that lord has been called 'Huṅkāra' by the wise.

6.3.s:
huṅkāratīrthe yaḥ snātvā paśyatyavyayamacyutam .
sa mucyate naraḥ pāpaiḥ saptajanma kṛtairapi .. 157.4 ..
6.3.d:
हुङ्कारतीर्थे यः स्नात्वा पश्यत्यव्ययमच्युतम् .
स मुच्यते नरः पापैः सप्तजन्म कृतैरपि .. 157.4 ..
6.3.m: Having bathed at Huṅkāratīrtha, whoever looks upon the imperishable Acyuta, / that man is freed from sins, even those committed over seven births.

6.3.s:
saṃsārārṇavamagnānāṃ narāṇāṃ pāpakarmiṇām .
naivoddhartā jagannāthaṃ vinā nārāyaṇaṃ paraḥ .. 157.5 ..
6.3.d:
संसारार्णवमग्नानां नराणां पापकर्मिणाम् .
नैवोद्धर्ता जगन्नाथं विना नारायणं परः .. 157.5 ..
6.3.m: For men who commit sins and are sunk in the ocean of worldly existence, / there is no other savior except Nārāyaṇa, the lord of the universe.

6.3.s:
sā jihvā yā hariṃ stauti taccittaṃ yattadarpitam .
tāveva kevalau ślāghyau yau tatpūjākarau karau .. 157.6 ..
6.3.d:
सा जिह्वा या हरिं स्तौति तच्चित्तं यत्तदर्पितम् .
तावेव केवलौ श्लाघ्यौ यौ तत्पूजाकरौ करौ .. 157.6 ..
6.3.m: That tongue alone is [true] which praises Hari; that mind alone is [true] which is offered to him. / Those two hands alone are truly praiseworthy which perform his worship.

6.3.s:
sarvadā sarvakāryeṣu nāsti teṣāmamaṅgalam .
yeṣāṃ hṛdistho bhagavānmaṅgalāyatano hariḥ .. 157.7 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वदा सर्वकार्येषु नास्ति तेषाममङ्गलम् .
येषां हृदिस्थो भगवान्मङ्गलायतनो हरिः .. 157.7 ..
6.3.m: At all times, in all undertakings, no inauspiciousness exists for those / within whose hearts abides the blessed Lord Hari, the abode of auspiciousness.

6.3.s:
yadanyaddevatārcāyāḥ phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ .
sāṣṭāṅgapraṇipātena tatphalaṃ labhate hareḥ .. 157.8 ..
6.3.d:
यदन्यद्देवतार्चायाः फलं प्राप्नोति मानवः .
साष्टाङ्गप्रणिपातेन तत्फलं लभते हरेः .. 157.8 ..
6.3.m: Whatever other fruit a mortal obtains from worshipping deities, / one obtains that fruit of Hari merely by prostrating oneself with the eight limbs.

6.3.s:
reṇuguṇṭhitagātrasya yāvanto'sya rajaḥkaṇāḥ .
tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi viṣṇuloke mahīyate .. 157.9 ..
6.3.d:
रेणुगुण्ठितगात्रस्य यावन्तोऽस्य रजःकणाः .
तावद्वर्षसहस्राणि विष्णुलोके महीयते .. 157.9 ..
6.3.m: As many particles of dust as cling to a body covered with dust [in prostration], / for that many thousands of years he is honoured in Viṣṇu's world.

6.3.s:
sammārjanābhyukṣaṇalepanena tadālaye naśyati sarvapāpam .
nārī narāṇāṃ parayā tu bhaktyā dṛṣṭvā tu revāṃ narasattamasya .. 157.10 ..
6.3.d:
सम्मार्जनाभ्युक्षणलेपनेन तदालये नश्यति सर्वपापम् .
नारी नराणां परया तु भक्त्या दृष्ट्वा तु रेवां नरसत्तमस्य .. 157.10 ..
6.3.m: By sweeping, sprinkling, and smearing [with cow dung] in his temple, all sin is destroyed / for a woman or for men, through supreme devotion, having beheld the Revā, O best of men.

6.3.s:
yenārcito bhagavānvāsudevo janmārjitaṃ naśyati tasya pāpam .
sa yāti lokaṃ garuḍadhvajasya vidhūtapāpaḥ surasaṅghapūjyatām .. 157.11 ..
6.3.d:
येनार्चितो भगवान्वासुदेवो जन्मार्जितं नश्यति तस्य पापम् .
स याति लोकं गरुडध्वजस्य विधूतपापः सुरसङ्घपूज्यताम् .. 157.11 ..
6.3.m: One by whom the blessed Vāsudeva has been worshipped has the sin acquired over lifetimes destroyed. / Cleansed of sin, he goes to the world of him whose banner bears Garuḍa, worshipped by the host of gods.

6.3.s:
śāṭhyenāpi namaskāraṃ prayuñjaṃścakrapāṇinaḥ .
saptajanmārjitaṃ pāpaṃ gacchatyāśu na saṃśayaḥ .. 157.12 ..
6.3.d:
शाठ्येनापि नमस्कारं प्रयुञ्जंश्चक्रपाणिनः .
सप्तजन्मार्जितं पापं गच्छत्याशु न संशयः .. 157.12 ..
6.3.m: Even if offering bow to the wielder of the discus deceitfully, / the sin accumulated over seven lifetimes swiftly departs; there is no doubt.

6.3.s:
pūjāyāṃ prīyate rudro japahomairdivākaraḥ .
śaṅkhacakragadāpāṇiḥ praṇipātena tuṣyati .. 157.13 ..
6.3.d:
पूजायां प्रीयते रुद्रो जपहोमैर्दिवाकरः .
शङ्खचक्रगदापाणिः प्रणिपातेन तुष्यति .. 157.13 ..
6.3.m: Rudra is pleased by worship, the Sun-maker by recitation and fire offerings; / he who holds the conch, discus, and mace in hand is delighted by prostration.

6.3.s:
bhavajaladhigatānāṃ dvandvavātāhatānāṃ sutaduhitṛkalatratrāṇabhārārditānām .
viṣamaviṣayatoye majjatāmaplavānāṃ bhavati śaraṇameko viṣṇupoto narāṇām .. 157.14 ..
6.3.d:
भवजलधिगतानां द्वन्द्ववाताहतानां सुतदुहितृकलत्रत्राणभारार्दितानाम् .
विषमविषयतोये मज्जतामप्लवानां भवति शरणमेको विष्णुपोतो नराणाम् .. 157.14 ..
6.3.m: For mortals plunged into the ocean of worldly existence, buffeted by the winds of dualities, oppressed by the burden of protecting sons, daughters, and wives, / sinking into the perilous waters of sense objects without a raft, the boat of Viṣṇu alone is the refuge.

6.3.s:
huṅkāratīrthe rājendra śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham .
yatkṛtaṃ puruṣavyāghra tannaśyati na karhicit .. 157.15 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe huṅkārasvāmitīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma saptapañcāśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 158
6.3.d:
हुङ्कारतीर्थे राजेन्द्र शुभं वा यदि वाशुभम् .
यत्कृतं पुरुषव्याघ्र तन्नश्यति न कर्हिचित् .. 157.15 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे हुङ्कारस्वामितीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम सप्तपञ्चाशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 158
6.3.m:
At the Huṅkāratīrtha, O king of kings, whether good or evil, / whatever is done, O tiger among men, never perishes.
Thus ends the one hundred fifty-seventh chapter, entitled the description of the māhātmya of the Huṅkārasvāmitīrtha, in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth [part], the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skandapurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 158

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gacchetparaṃ tīrthaṃ saṅgameśvaramuttamam .
narmadādakṣiṇe kūle sarvapāpabhayāpaham .. 158.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेत्परं तीर्थं सङ्गमेश्वरमुत्तमम् .
नर्मदादक्षिणे कूले सर्वपापभयापहम् .. 158.1 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then one should go to the supreme sacred ford, the excellent Saṅgameśvara, / on the southern bank of the Narmadā, which removes all sins and fears.

6.3.s:
dhanadastatra viśrānto muhūrtaṃ nṛpasattama .
pitṛlokātsamāyātaḥ kailāsaṃ dharaṇīdharam .. 158.2 ..
6.3.d:
धनदस्तत्र विश्रान्तो मुहूर्तं नृपसत्तम .
पितृलोकात्समायातः कैलासं धरणीधरम् .. 158.2 ..
6.3.m: Kubera rested there for a moment, O best of kings, / having come from the realm of the ancestors on his way to Mount Kailāsa.

6.3.s:
pratyayārthaṃ nṛpaśreṣṭha hyadyāpi dharaṇītale .
kṛṣṇavarṇā hi pāṣāṇā dṛśyante sphaṭikojjvalāḥ .. 158.3 ..
6.3.d:
प्रत्ययार्थं नृपश्रेष्ठ ह्यद्यापि धरणीतले .
कृष्णवर्णा हि पाषाणा दृश्यन्ते स्फटिकोज्ज्वलाः .. 158.3 ..
6.3.m: As proof of this, O best of kings, even today on the earth's surface / black stones are seen shining like crystal.

6.3.s:
vindhyanirjharaniṣkrāntā puṇyatoyā saridvarā .
praviṣṭā narmadātoye sarvapāpapraṇāśane .. 158.4 ..
6.3.d:
विन्ध्यनिर्झरनिष्क्रान्ता पुण्यतोया सरिद्वरा .
प्रविष्टा नर्मदातोये सर्वपापप्रणाशने .. 158.4 ..
6.3.m: Coming forth from the waterfalls of the Vindhya, an excellent river of holy waters / entered into the water of the Narmadā, which destroys all sins.

6.3.s:
saṅgame tatra yaḥ snātvā pūjayetsaṅgameśvaram .
aśvamedhasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnotyasaṃśayam .. 158.5 ..
6.3.d:
सङ्गमे तत्र यः स्नात्वा पूजयेत्सङ्गमेश्वरम् .
अश्वमेधस्य यज्ञस्य फलं प्राप्नोत्यसंशयम् .. 158.5 ..
6.3.m: Having bathed at that confluence, whoever worships Saṅgameśvara / undoubtedly obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.

6.3.s:
ghaṇṭāpatākāvitanaṃ yo dadetsaṅgameśvare .
haṃsayuktavimānastho divyastrīśatasaṃvṛtaḥ .. 158.6 ..
6.3.d:
घण्टापताकावितनं यो ददेत्सङ्गमेश्वरे .
हंसयुक्तविमानस्थो दिव्यस्त्रीशतसंवृतः .. 158.6 ..
6.3.m: Whoever donates a bell, flags, and an awning at Saṅgameśvara, / seated in an aerial chariot harnessed with swans and surrounded by a hundred celestial women,

6.3.s:
sa rudrapadamāpnoti rudrasyānucaro bhavet .
dadhi bhakte na devasya yaḥ kuryālliṅgapūraṇam .. 158.7 ..
6.3.d:
स रुद्रपदमाप्नोति रुद्रस्यानुचरो भवेत् .
दधि भक्ते न देवस्य यः कुर्याल्लिङ्गपूरणम् .. 158.7 ..
6.3.m: attains the state of Rudra and becomes an attendant of Rudra. / Whoever covers the liṅga of the god with curd and cooked rice,

6.3.s:
sikthasaṃkhyaṃ śive loke sa vasetkālamīpsitam .
śrīphalaiḥ pūrayelliṅgaṃ niḥsvo bhūtvā bhavasya tu .. 158.8 ..
6.3.d:
सिक्थसंख्यं शिवे लोके स वसेत्कालमीप्सितम् .
श्रीफलैः पूरयेल्लिङ्गं निःस्वो भूत्वा भवस्य तु .. 158.8 ..
6.3.m: dwells in the world of Śiva for a desired length of time equal to the number of grains of boiled rice. / And having become destitute, if one covers the liṅga of Bhava with wood-apple fruits,

6.3.s:
so'pi tatphalamāpnoti gataḥ svarge nareśvara .
akṣayā santatistasya jāyate saptajanmasu .. 158.9 ..
6.3.d:
सोऽपि तत्फलमाप्नोति गतः स्वर्गे नरेश्वर .
अक्षया सन्ततिस्तस्य जायते सप्तजन्मसु .. 158.9 ..
6.3.m: he too attains that fruit, having gone to heaven, O lord of men; / his lineage becomes imperishable throughout seven births.

6.3.s:
snapanaṃ devadevasya dadhnā madhughṛtena vā .
yaḥ karoti vidhānena tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu .. 158.10 ..
6.3.d:
स्नपनं देवदेवस्य दध्ना मधुघृतेन वा .
यः करोति विधानेन तस्य पुण्यफलं शृणु .. 158.10 ..
6.3.m: Whoever performs the ceremonial bath of the god of gods with curds, honey, or clarified butter / according to the prescribed rule, hear the meritorious fruit of that person:

6.3.s:
dhṛtakṣīravahā nadyo yatra vṛkṣā madhusravāḥ .
tatra te mānavā yānti suprasanne maheśvare .. 158.11 ..
6.3.d:
धृतक्षीरवहा नद्यो यत्र वृक्षा मधुस्रवाः .
तत्र ते मानवा यान्ति सुप्रसन्ने महेश्वरे .. 158.11 ..
6.3.m: Where rivers flow with clarified butter and milk, and where trees exude honey, / there those mortals go when Maheśvara is well pleased.

6.3.s:
