patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ toyaṃ yastu dadyānmaheśvare .
tatsarvaṃ saptajanmāni hyakṣayaṃ phalamaśnute .. 158.12 ..
6.3.d:
पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यस्तु दद्यान्महेश्वरे .
तत्सर्वं सप्तजन्मानि ह्यक्षयं फलमश्नुते .. 158.12 ..
6.3.m: Whoever offers a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water to Maheśvara, / enjoys the imperishable fruit of all that throughout seven births.

6.3.s:
sarveṣāmeva pātrāṇāṃ mahāpātraṃ maheśvaraḥ .
tasmātsarvaprayatnena pūjanīyo maheśvaraḥ .. 158.13 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वेषामेव पात्राणां महापात्रं महेश्वरः .
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन पूजनीयो महेश्वरः .. 158.13 ..
6.3.m: Among all worthy recipients, Maheśvara is the greatest recipient; / therefore, with every effort, Maheśvara is to be worshipped.

6.3.s:
brahmacaryasthito nityaṃ yastu pūjayate śivam .
iha jīvansa deveśo mṛto gacchedanāmayam .. 158.14 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रह्मचर्यस्थितो नित्यं यस्तु पूजयते शिवम् .
इह जीवन्स देवेशो मृतो गच्छेदनामयम् .. 158.14 ..
6.3.m: Whoever, established in celibacy, constantly worships Śiva, / lives here as a lord of gods, and on dying goes to the disease-free realm.

6.3.s:
śive tu pūjite pārtha yatphalaṃ prāpyate budhaiḥ .
yogīndre caiva tatpārtha pūjite labhate phalam .. 158.15 ..
6.3.d:
शिवे तु पूजिते पार्थ यत्फलं प्राप्यते बुधैः .
योगीन्द्रे चैव तत्पार्थ पूजिते लभते फलम् .. 158.15 ..
6.3.m: The fruit which is obtained by the wise when Śiva is worshipped, O son of Pṛthā, / that same fruit one obtains, O son of Pṛthā, when a lord of yogins is worshipped.

6.3.s:
te dhanyāste mahātmānasteṣāṃ janma sujīvitam .
yeṣāṃ gṛheṣu bhuñjanti śivabhaktiratā narāḥ .. 158.16 ..
6.3.d:
ते धन्यास्ते महात्मानस्तेषां जन्म सुजीवितम् .
येषां गृहेषु भुञ्जन्ति शिवभक्तिरता नराः .. 158.16 ..
6.3.m: Blessed are they, great-souled are they, well-lived is their life, / in whose homes men devoted to the devotion of Śiva take food.

6.3.s:
saṃnirudhyendriyagrāmaṃ yatrayatra vasenmuniḥ .
tatra tatra kurukṣetraṃ naimiṣaṃ puṣkarāṇi ca .. 158.17 ..
6.3.d:
संनिरुध्येन्द्रियग्रामं यत्रयत्र वसेन्मुनिः .
तत्र तत्र कुरुक्षेत्रं नैमिषं पुष्कराणि च .. 158.17 ..
6.3.m: Wherever a sage may dwell, having restrained the collection of senses, / there are Kurukṣetra, Naimiṣa, and the Puṣkaras.

6.3.s:
yatphalaṃ vedaviduṣi bhojite śatasaṃkhyayā .
tatphalaṃ jāyate pārtha hyekena śivayoginā .. 158.18 ..
6.3.d:
यत्फलं वेदविदुषि भोजिते शतसंख्यया .
तत्फलं जायते पार्थ ह्येकेन शिवयोगिना .. 158.18 ..
6.3.m: The fruit that arises when one hundred knowers of the Veda are fed, / that fruit arises, O son of Pṛthā, through a single Śiva-yogin.

6.3.s:
yatra bhuñjati bhasmāṅgī mūrkho vā yadi paṇḍitaḥ .
tatra bhuñjati deveśaḥ sapatnīko vṛṣadhvajaḥ .. 158.19 ..
6.3.d:
यत्र भुञ्जति भस्माङ्गी मूर्खो वा यदि पण्डितः .
तत्र भुञ्जति देवेशः सपत्नीको वृषध्वजः .. 158.19 ..
6.3.m: Wherever one whose limbs are smeared with ashes eats, whether a fool or a scholar, / there eats the lord of the gods, the bull-bannered god, along with his consort.

6.3.s:
viprāṇāṃ vedaviduṣāṃ koṭiṃ saṃbhojya yatphalam .
bhikṣāmātrapradānena tatphalaṃ śivayoginām .. 158.20 ..
6.3.d:
विप्राणां वेदविदुषां कोटिं संभोज्य यत्फलम् .
भिक्षामात्रप्रदानेन तत्फलं शिवयोगिनाम् .. 158.20 ..
6.3.m: The fruit of feeding ten million brahmins who know the Vedas / is attained merely by giving alms to Śiva-yogins.

6.3.s:
saṅgameśvaramāsādya prāṇatyāgaṃ karoti yaḥ .
na tasya punarāvṛttiḥ śivalokātkadācana .. 158.21 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe saṅgameśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmāṣṭapañcāśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
6.3.d:
सङ्गमेश्वरमासाद्य प्राणत्यागं करोति यः .
न तस्य पुनरावृत्तिः शिवलोकात्कदाचन .. 158.21 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे सङ्गमेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामाष्टपञ्चाशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः ..
6.3.m:
Whoever gives up his life after reaching Saṅgameśvara, / for him there is never any return from the world of Śiva.
Thus ends the one hundred fifty-eighth chapter, entitled the description of the māhātmya of the Saṅgameśvaratīrtha, in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth [part], the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skandapurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gacchenmahārāja tīrthaṃ paramapāvanam .
narmadāyāṃ suduṣprāpaṃ siddhaṃ hyanarakeśvaram .. 159.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेन्महाराज तीर्थं परमपावनम् .
नर्मदायां सुदुष्प्रापं सिद्धं ह्यनरकेश्वरम् .. 159.1 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then, O great king, one should go to the supremely purifying sacred ford / on the Narmadā, very difficult to attain, the perfected Anarakeśvara.

6.3.s:
tasmiṃstīrthe naraḥ snātvā pāpakarmāpi bhārata .
na paśyati mahāghoraṃ narakadvārasaṃjñikam .. 159.2 ..
6.3.d:
तस्मिंस्तीर्थे नरः स्नात्वा पापकर्मापि भारत .
न पश्यति महाघोरं नरकद्वारसंज्ञिकम् .. 159.2 ..
6.3.m: Having bathed in that sacred ford, O descendant of Bharata, even a doer of sinful deeds / does not see the very terrible [place] called the gate of hell.

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
śubhāśubhaphalaistāta bhuktabhogā narāstviha .
jāyante lakṣaṇairyaistu tāni me vada sattama .. 159.3 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
शुभाशुभफलैस्तात भुक्तभोगा नरास्त्विह .
जायन्ते लक्षणैर्यैस्तु तानि मे वद सत्तम .. 159.3 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / Having experienced their fruits through good and bad results, dear sir, / by what signs are men born here [in this world]? Tell me those, O best of good men.

6.3.s:
yathā nirgacchate jīvastyaktvā dehaṃ na paśyati .
tathā gacchanpunardehaṃ pañcabhūtasamanvitaḥ .. 159.4 ..
6.3.d:
यथा निर्गच्छते जीवस्त्यक्त्वा देहं न पश्यति .
तथा गच्छन्पुनर्देहं पञ्चभूतसमन्वितः .. 159.4 ..
6.3.m: Just as the individual soul departs having abandoned the body, and sees it not, / so, entering a body again, joined with the five gross elements,

6.3.s:
tvagasthimāṃsamedo'sṛkkeśasnāyuśataiḥ saha .
viṇmūtraretaḥsaṅghāte kā saṃjñā jāyate nṛṇām .. 159.5 ..
6.3.d:
त्वगस्थिमांसमेदोऽसृक्केशस्नायुशतैः सह .
विण्मूत्ररेतःसङ्घाते का संज्ञा जायते नृणाम् .. 159.5 ..
6.3.m: together with hundreds of skin, bones, flesh, fat, blood, hair, and sinews— / in this mass of feces, urine, and semen, what consciousness arises for men?

6.3.s:
evamuktaḥ sa mārkaṇḍaḥ kathayāmāsa yogavit .
dhyātvā sanātanaṃ sarvaṃ devadevaṃ maheśvaram .. 159.6 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्तः स मार्कण्डः कथयामास योगवित् .
ध्यात्वा सनातनं सर्वं देवदेवं महेश्वरम् .. 159.6 ..
6.3.m: Addressed thus, that knower of yoga, Mārkaṇḍeya, spoke, / having meditated on the eternal, all[-pervading] Maheśvara, the god of gods.

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
śṛṇu pārtha mahāpraśnaṃ kathayāmi yathāśrutam .
sakāśādbrahmaṇaḥ pūrvamṛṣidevasamāgame .. 159.7 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
शृणु पार्थ महाप्रश्नं कथयामि यथाश्रुतम् .
सकाशाद्ब्रह्मणः पूर्वमृषिदेवसमागमे .. 159.7 ..
6.3.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Listen, O son of Pṛthā, to the great question; I shall tell it as it was heard / of old in the presence of Brahmā at the assembly of seers and gods.

6.3.s:
gururātmavatāṃ śāstā rājā śāstā durātmanām .
iha pracchannapāpānāṃ śāstā vaivasvato yamaḥ .. 159.8 ..
6.3.d:
गुरुरात्मवतां शास्ता राजा शास्ता दुरात्मनाम् .
इह प्रच्छन्नपापानां शास्ता वैवस्वतो यमः .. 159.8 ..
6.3.m: The teacher is the chastiser of the self-controlled; the king is the chastiser of the wicked; / in this world, of secret sins, the chastiser is Yama, son of Vivasvat.

6.3.s:
acīrṇaprāyaścittānāṃ yamaloke hyanekadhā .
yātanābhirviyuktānāmanekāṃ jīvasantatim .. 159.9 ..
6.3.d:
अचीर्णप्रायश्चित्तानां यमलोके ह्यनेकधा .
यातनाभिर्वियुक्तानामनेकां जीवसन्ततिम् .. 159.9 ..
6.3.m: For those who have not performed atonement, indeed in various ways in Yama's realm, / having experienced manifold series of lives through tortures,

6.3.s:
gatvā manuṣyabhāve tu pāpacihnā bhavanti te .
tatte'haṃ sampravakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣvaikamanā nṛpa .. 159.10 ..
6.3.d:
गत्वा मनुष्यभावे तु पापचिह्ना भवन्ति ते .
तत्तेऽहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणुष्वैकमना नृप .. 159.10 ..
6.3.m: when they arrive at human existence, they bear the marks of sin. / I shall explain that to you; listen with an attentive mind, O king.

6.3.s:
sahitvā yātanāṃ sarvāṃ gatvā vaivasvatakṣayam .
vistīrṇayātanā ye tu lokamāyānti cihnitāḥ .. 159.11 ..
6.3.d:
सहित्वा यातनां सर्वां गत्वा वैवस्वतक्षयम् .
विस्तीर्णयातना ये तु लोकमायान्ति चिह्निताः .. 159.11 ..
6.3.m: Having endured all tortures and gone to the abode of the son of Vivasvat, / those whose tortures are exhausted come to the world marked [by signs].

6.3.s:
gadgado'nṛtavādī syānmūkaścaiva gavānṛte .
brahmahā jāyate kuṣṭhī śyāvadantastu madyapaḥ .. 159.12 ..
6.3.d:
गद्गदोऽनृतवादी स्यान्मूकश्चैव गवानृते .
ब्रह्महा जायते कुष्ठी श्यावदन्तस्तु मद्यपः .. 159.12 ..
6.3.m: A liar becomes a stammerer, and one who lies about cows becomes mute. / A killer of a brahmin is born a leper, and a drinker of liquor has black teeth.

6.3.s:
kunakhī svarṇaharaṇādduḥścarmā gurutalpagaḥ .
saṃyogī hīnayoniḥ syāddaridro'dattadānataḥ .. 159.13 ..
6.3.d:
कुनखी स्वर्णहरणाद्दुःश्चर्मा गुरुतल्पगः .
संयोगी हीनयोनिः स्याद्दरिद्रोऽदत्तदानतः .. 159.13 ..
6.3.m: A stealer of gold has diseased nails; a violator of the teacher's bed has bad skin. / One who has improper sexual union is born from a low womb; a miser becomes poor.

6.3.s:
grāmaśūkaratāṃ yāti hyayājyayājako nṛpa .
kharo vai bahuyājī syācchvānimantritabhojanāt .. 159.14 ..
6.3.d:
ग्रामशूकरतां याति ह्ययाज्ययाजको नृप .
खरो वै बहुयाजी स्याच्छ्वानिमन्त्रितभोजनात् .. 159.14 ..
6.3.m: One who sacrifices for those unfit to sacrifice becomes a village pig, O king. / One who sacrifices for many becomes an ass; from eating at an invitation [improperly], a dog.

6.3.s:
aparīkṣitabhojī syādvānaro vijane vane .
vitarjako'tha mārjāraḥ khadyotaḥ kakṣadāhataḥ .. 159.15 ..
6.3.d:
अपरीक्षितभोजी स्याद्वानरो विजने वने .
वितर्जकोऽथ मार्जारः खद्योतः कक्षदाहतः .. 159.15 ..
6.3.m: One who eats uninspected [food] becomes a monkey in a lonely forest. / A slanderer becomes a cat; one who sets fire to brush becomes a firefly.

6.3.s:
avidyāṃ yaḥ prayaccheta balīvardo bhaveddhi saḥ .
annaṃ paryuṣitaṃ vipre dadānaḥ klībatāṃ vrajet .. 159.16 ..
6.3.d:
अविद्यां यः प्रयच्छेत बलीवर्दो भवेद्धि सः .
अन्नं पर्युषितं विप्रे ददानः क्लीबतां व्रजेत् .. 159.16 ..
6.3.m: He who teaches false knowledge surely becomes an ox. / One who gives stale food to a brahmin falls into impotency.

6.3.s:
mātsaryādatha jātyandho janmāndhaḥ pustakaṃ haran .
phalānyāharato'patyaṃ mriyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 159.17 ..
6.3.d:
मात्सर्यादथ जात्यन्धो जन्मान्धः पुस्तकं हरन् .
फलान्याहरतोऽपत्यं म्रियते नात्र संशयः .. 159.17 ..
6.3.m: From envy one is born blind; one who steals a book is blind from birth. / The child of one who steals fruits dies—of this there is no doubt.

6.3.s:
mṛto vānaratāṃ yāti tanmukto'tha galāḍavān .
adattvā bhakṣayaṃstāni hyanapatyo bhavennaraḥ .. 159.18 ..
6.3.d:
मृतो वानरतां याति तन्मुक्तोऽथ गलाडवान् .
अदत्त्वा भक्षयंस्तानि ह्यनपत्यो भवेन्नरः .. 159.18 ..
6.3.m: Having died, he becomes a monkey; freed from that, he has an enlarged goitre. / A man who eats those [fruits] without giving [to others] becomes childless.

6.3.s:
haranvastraṃ bhavedgodhā garadaḥ pavanāśanaḥ .
pravrājī gamanādrājan bhavenmarupiśācakaḥ .. 159.19 ..
6.3.d:
हरन्वस्त्रं भवेद्गोधा गरदः पवनाशनः .
प्रव्राजी गमनाद्राजन् भवेन्मरुपिशाचकः .. 159.19 ..
6.3.m: One who steals clothing becomes an iguana; a poisoner becomes an eater of wind (a snake). / From intercourse with an ascetic woman, O king, one becomes a piśāca of the desert.

6.3.s:
vātako jalahartā ca dhānyahartā ca mūṣakaḥ .
aprāptayauvanāṃ gacchan bhavetsarpa iti śrutiḥ .. 159.20 ..
6.3.d:
वातको जलहर्ता च धान्यहर्ता च मूषकः .
अप्राप्तयौवनां गच्छन् भवेत्सर्प इति श्रुतिः .. 159.20 ..
6.3.m: A stealer of water becomes a diver-bird, and a stealer of grain a rat. / Having intercourse with a girl who has not reached puberty, one becomes a snake—so states the tradition.

6.3.s:
gurudārābhilāṣī ca kṛkalāso bhavecciram .
jalaprasravaṇaṃ yastu bhindyānmatsyo bhavennaraḥ .. 159.21 ..
6.3.d:
गुरुदाराभिलाषी च कृकलासो भवेच्चिरम् .
जलप्रस्रवणं यस्तु भिन्द्यान्मत्स्यो भवेन्नरः .. 159.21 ..
6.3.m: One who covets the teacher's wife becomes a chameleon for a long time. / A man who breaks a water-reservoir becomes a fish.

6.3.s:
avikreyān vikrayan vai vikaṭākṣo bhavennaraḥ .
ayonigo vṛko hi syādulūkaḥ krayavañcanāt .. 159.22 ..
6.3.d:
अविक्रेयान् विक्रयन् वै विकटाक्षो भवेन्नरः .
अयोनिगो वृको हि स्यादुलूकः क्रयवञ्चनात् .. 159.22 ..
6.3.m: A man who sells things that should not be sold becomes one with deformed eyes. / One who engages in unnatural intercourse becomes a wolf, and an owl from cheating in a purchase.

6.3.s:
mṛtasyaikādaśāhe tu bhuñjānaḥ śvopajāyate .
pratiśrutya dvijāyārthamadadanmadhuko bhavet .. 159.23 ..
6.3.d:
मृतस्यैकादशाहे तु भुञ्जानः श्वोपजायते .
प्रतिश्रुत्य द्विजायार्थमददन्मधुको भवेत् .. 159.23 ..
6.3.m: One who eats on the eleventh day after a person's death is born as a dog. / Having promised wealth to a twice-born man and not giving it, one becomes an insect.

6.3.s:
rājñīgamādbhavedduṣṭataskaro viḍvarāhakaḥ .
parivādī dvijātīnāṃ labhate kācchapīṃ tanum .. 159.24 ..
6.3.d:
राज्ञीगमाद्भवेद्दुष्टतस्करो विड्वराहकः .
परिवादी द्विजातीनां लभते काच्छपीं तनुम् .. 159.24 ..
6.3.m: From intercourse with a queen one becomes a wicked thief, [then] a dung-eating boar. / A slanderer of twice-born men receives the body of a tortoise.

6.3.s:
vrajeddevalako rājanyoniṃ cāṇḍālasaṃjñitām .
durbhagaḥ phalavikretā vṛściko vṛṣalīpatiḥ .. 159.25 ..
6.3.d:
व्रजेद्देवलको राजन्योनिं चाण्डालसंज्ञिताम् .
दुर्भगः फलविक्रेता वृश्चिको वृषलीपतिः .. 159.25 ..
6.3.m: An attendant on idols, O king, enters the womb called cāṇḍāla. / A seller of fruits becomes unfortunate; the husband of a śūdra woman becomes a scorpion.

6.3.s:
mārjāro'gniṃ padā spṛṣṭvā rogavānparamāṃsabhuk .
sodaryāgamanātṣaṇḍho durgandhaśca sugandhahṛt .. 159.26 ..
6.3.d:
मार्जारोऽग्निं पदा स्पृष्ट्वा रोगवान्परमांसभुक् .
सोदर्यागमनात्षण्ढो दुर्गन्धश्च सुगन्धहृत् .. 159.26 ..
6.3.m: One who touches fire with his foot becomes a cat; one who eats meat [unlawfully] becomes diseased. / From intercourse with a sister one becomes a eunuch, and a thief of fragrant scents becomes foul-smelling.

6.3.s:
grāmabhaṭṭo divākīrtirdaivajño gardabho bhavet .
kupaṇḍitaḥ syānmārjāro bhaṣaṇo vyāsa eva ca .. 159.27 ..
6.3.d:
ग्रामभट्टो दिवाकीर्तिर्दैवज्ञो गर्दभो भवेत् .
कुपण्डितः स्यान्मार्जारो भषणो व्यास एव च .. 159.27 ..
6.3.m: A village bard, a candāla, and an astrologer become asses. / A pseudo-scholar becomes a cat, and a barking dog indeed is Vyāsa [in improper speech].

6.3.s:
sa eva dṛśyate rājanprakāśātparamarmaṇām .
yadvā tadvāpi pārakyaṃ svalpaṃ vā yadi vā bahu .. 159.28 ..
6.3.d:
स एव दृश्यते राजन्प्रकाशात्परमर्मणाम् .
यद्वा तद्वापि पारक्यं स्वल्पं वा यदि वा बहु .. 159.28 ..
6.3.m: That very [mark] is seen, O king, from the revealing of another's secrets. / Whatever belongs to another, whether little or much,

6.3.s:
kṛtvā vai yonimāpnoti tairaścīṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ .
evamādīni cānyāni cihnāni nṛpasattama .. 159.29 ..
6.3.d:
कृत्वा वै योनिमाप्नोति तैरश्चीं नात्र संशयः .
एवमादीनि चान्यानि चिह्नानि नृपसत्तम .. 159.29 ..
6.3.m: having taken it, one attains an animal womb—there is no doubt about this. / These and other signs, O best of kings,

6.3.s:
svakarmavihitānyeva dṛśyante yaistu mānavāḥ .
tato janma tato mṛtyuḥ sarvajantuṣu bhārata .. 159.30 ..
6.3.d:
स्वकर्मविहितान्येव दृश्यन्ते यैस्तु मानवाः .
ततो जन्म ततो मृत्युः सर्वजन्तुषु भारत .. 159.30 ..
6.3.m: ordained by their own karma, are those by which human beings are recognized. / Thence comes birth, thence death among all living beings, O descendant of Bharata;

6.3.s:
jāyate nātra sandehaḥ samībhūte śubhāśubhe .
strīpuṃsoḥ samprayogeṇa viṣuddhe śukraśoṇite .. 159.31 ..
6.3.d:
जायते नात्र सन्देहः समीभूते शुभाशुभे .
स्त्रीपुंसोः सम्प्रयोगेण विषुद्धे शुक्रशोणिते .. 159.31 ..
6.3.m: it arises—there is no doubt here—when good and bad karma become balanced, / through the union of man and woman, when semen and blood are purified.

6.3.s:
pañcabhūtasamopetaḥ saṣaṣṭhaḥ parameśvaraḥ .
indriyāṇi manaḥ prāṇā jñānamāyuḥ sukhaṃ dhṛtiḥ .. 159.32 ..
6.3.d:
पञ्चभूतसमोपेतः सषष्ठः परमेश्वरः .
इन्द्रियाणि मनः प्राणा ज्ञानमायुः सुखं धृतिः .. 159.32 ..
6.3.m: Endowed with the five elements, the supreme lord is the sixth: / sense faculties, mind, vital breaths, knowledge, lifespan, pleasure, steadfastness,

6.3.s:
dhāraṇaṃ preraṇaṃ duḥkhamicchāhaṅkāra eva ca .
prayatna ākṛtirvarṇaḥ svaradveṣau bhavābhavau .. 159.33 ..
6.3.d:
धारणं प्रेरणं दुःखमिच्छाहङ्कार एव च .
प्रयत्न आकृतिर्वर्णः स्वरद्वेषौ भवाभवौ .. 159.33 ..
6.3.m: retention, impulse, pain, desire, egoism, / effort, form, complexion, voice, aversion, existence, and non-existence—

6.3.s:
tasyedamātmanaḥ sarvamanāderādimicchataḥ .
prathame māsi sa kledabhūto dhātuvimūrchitaḥ .. 159.34 ..
6.3.d:
तस्येदमात्मनः सर्वमनादेरादिमिच्छतः .
प्रथमे मासि स क्लेदभूतो धातुविमूर्छितः .. 159.34 ..
6.3.m: all this belongs to that beginningless self desiring a beginning. / In the first month, it becomes liquid, mingled with the bodily humours.

6.3.s:
māsyarbudaṃ dvitīye tu tṛtīye cendriyairyutaḥ .
ākāśāllāghavaṃ saukṣmyaṃ śabdaṃ śrotrabalādikam .
vāyostu sparśanaṃ ceṣṭāṃ dahanaṃ raukṣyameva ca .. 159.35 ..
6.3.d:
मास्यर्बुदं द्वितीये तु तृतीये चेन्द्रियैर्युतः .
आकाशाल्लाघवं सौक्ष्म्यं शब्दं श्रोत्रबलादिकम् .
वायोस्तु स्पर्शनं चेष्टां दहनं रौक्ष्यमेव च .. 159.35 ..
6.3.m: In the second month it is a mass of tissue, and in the third endowed with sense faculties. / From space [comes] lightness, subtlety, sound, and the capacity of hearing; / from wind [comes] touch, motion, combustion, and dryness;

6.3.s:
pittāttu darśanaṃ paktimauṣṇyaṃ rūpaṃ prakāśanam .
salilādrasanāṃ śaityaṃ snehaṃ kledaṃ samārdavam .. 159.36 ..
6.3.d:
पित्तात्तु दर्शनं पक्तिमौष्ण्यं रूपं प्रकाशनम् .
सलिलाद्रसनां शैत्यं स्नेहं क्लेदं समार्दवम् .. 159.36 ..
6.3.m: from bile [comes] sight, digestion, heat, form, and illumination; / from water [comes] taste, coolness, moisture, wetness, and softness;

6.3.s:
bhūmergandhaṃ tathā ghrāṇaṃ gauravaṃ mūrtimeva ca .
ātmā gṛhṇātyajaḥ pūrvaṃ tṛtīye spandate ca saḥ .. 159.37 ..
6.3.d:
भूमेर्गन्धं तथा घ्राणं गौरवं मूर्तिमेव च .
आत्मा गृह्णात्यजः पूर्वं तृतीये स्पन्दते च सः .. 159.37 ..
6.3.m: from earth [comes] smell, the sense of smell, heaviness, and bodily form. / The unborn self assumes these first, and in the third month it stirs.

6.3.s:
daurhṛdasyāpradānena garbho doṣamavāpnuyāt .
vairūpyaṃ maraṇaṃ vāpi tasmātkāryaṃ priyaṃ striyāḥ .. 159.38 ..
6.3.d:
दौर्हृदस्याप्रदानेन गर्भो दोषमवाप्नुयात् .
वैरूप्यं मरणं वापि तस्मात्कार्यं प्रियं स्त्रियाः .. 159.38 ..
6.3.m: By not granting pregnancy cravings, the fetus may incur a defect, / deformity, or even death; therefore, what pleases the woman should be done.

6.3.s:
sthairyaṃ caturthe tvaṅgānāṃ pañcame śoṇitodbhavaḥ .
ṣaṣṭhe balaṃ ca varṇaśca nakharomṇāṃ ca sambhavaḥ .. 159.39 ..
6.3.d:
स्थैर्यं चतुर्थे त्वङ्गानां पञ्चमे शोणितोद्भवः .
षष्ठे बलं च वर्णश्च नखरोम्णां च सम्भवः .. 159.39 ..
6.3.m: In the fourth month there is stability of the limbs, and in the fifth the generation of blood. / In the sixth comes strength, complexion, and the appearance of nails and hair.

6.3.s:
manasā cetanāyukto nakharomaśatāvṛtaḥ .
saptame cāṣṭame caiva tvacāvān smṛtivānapi .. 159.40 ..
6.3.d:
मनसा चेतनायुक्तो नखरोमशतावृतः .
सप्तमे चाष्टमे चैव त्वचावान् स्मृतिवानपि .. 159.40 ..
6.3.m: Endowed with consciousness through the mind, covered with hundreds of nails and hairs, / in the seventh and in the eighth month it has skin and memory.

6.3.s:
punargarbhaṃ punardhātrīmenastasya pradhāvati .
aṣṭame māsyato garbho jātaḥ prāṇairviyujyate .. 159.41 ..
6.3.d:
पुनर्गर्भं पुनर्धात्रीमेनस्तस्य प्रधावति .
अष्टमे मास्यतो गर्भो जातः प्राणैर्वियुज्यते .. 159.41 ..
6.3.m: Now to the fetus, now to the mother does its vitality flow back and forth. / Therefore a fetus born in the eighth month is deprived of life.

6.3.s:
navame daśame vāpi prabalaiḥ sūtimārutaiḥ .
nirgacchate bāṇa iva yantracchidreṇa sajvaraḥ .. 159.42 ..
6.3.d:
नवमे दशमे वापि प्रबलैः सूतिमारुतैः .
निर्गच्छते बाण इव यन्त्रच्छिद्रेण सज्वरः .. 159.42 ..
6.3.m: In the ninth or the tenth month, by the powerful winds of delivery, / it emerges like an arrow through the opening of a machine, full of agony.

6.3.s:
śarīrāvayavairyukto hyaṅgapratyaṅgasaṃyutaḥ .
aṣṭottaraṃ marmaśataṃ tatrāsthā tu śatatrayam .. 159.43 ..
6.3.d:
शरीरावयवैर्युक्तो ह्यङ्गप्रत्यङ्गसंयुतः .
अष्टोत्तरं मर्मशतं तत्रास्था तु शतत्रयम् .. 159.43 ..
6.3.m: Equipped with bodily limbs and provided with major and minor appendages, / there are one hundred and eight vital points and three hundred bones.

6.3.s:
sapta śiraḥkapālāni vihitāni svayambhuvā .
tisraḥ koṭyo'rdhakoṭī ca romṇāmaṅgeṣu bhārata .. 159.44 ..
6.3.d:
सप्त शिरःकपालानि विहितानि स्वयम्भुवा .
तिस्रः कोट्योऽर्धकोटी च रोम्णामङ्गेषु भारत .. 159.44 ..
6.3.m: Seven cranial bones were ordained by the self-manifest [creator]. / There are three and a half crores of hairs on the limbs, O Bhārata.

6.3.s:
dvāsaptatisahasrāṇi hṛdayādabhinisṛtāḥ .
hitānāma hi tā nāḍyastāsāṃ madhye śaśiprabhā .. 159.45 ..
6.3.d:
द्वासप्ततिसहस्राणि हृदयादभिनिसृताः .
हितानाम हि ता नाड्यस्तासां मध्ये शशिप्रभा .. 159.45 ..
6.3.m: Seventy-two thousand [channels] issue forth from the heart; / those channels are called the hitā, and among them is the moon-bright one.

6.3.s:
evaṃ pravartate cakraṃ bhūtagrāme caturvidhe .
utpattiśca vināśaśca bhavataḥ sarvadehinām .. 159.46 ..
6.3.d:
एवं प्रवर्तते चक्रं भूतग्रामे चतुर्विधे .
उत्पत्तिश्च विनाशश्च भवतः सर्वदेहिनाम् .. 159.46 ..
6.3.m: Thus the cycle turns among the fourfold classes of living beings; / birth and destruction occur for all embodied souls.

6.3.s:
gatirūrdhvā ca dharmeṇa hyadharmeṇa tvadhogatiḥ .
jāyate sarvavarṇānāṃ svadharmacalanānnṛpa .. 159.47 ..
6.3.d:
गतिरूर्ध्वा च धर्मेण ह्यधर्मेण त्वधोगतिः .
जायते सर्ववर्णानां स्वधर्मचलनान्नृप .. 159.47 ..
6.3.m: An upward course comes by righteousness, while a downward course comes by unrighteousness. / It arises for all social classes from falling away from one's own duty, O king.

6.3.s:
devatve mānavatve ca dānabhogādikāḥ kriyāḥ .
dṛśyante yā mahārāja tatsarvaṃ karmajaṃ phalam .. 159.48 ..
6.3.d:
देवत्वे मानवत्वे च दानभोगादिकाः क्रियाः .
दृश्यन्ते या महाराज तत्सर्वं कर्मजं फलम् .. 159.48 ..
6.3.m: In the state of godhood and the state of manhood, actions such as gifts and enjoyments / that are seen, O great king, all that is the fruit born of action.

6.3.s:
svakarma vihite ghore kāmaksodhārjite śubhe .
nimajjennarake ghore yasyottāro na vidyate .. 159.49 ..
6.3.d:
स्वकर्म विहिते घोरे कामक्सोधार्जिते शुभे .
निमज्जेन्नरके घोरे यस्योत्तारो न विद्यते .. 159.49 ..
6.3.m: When one's actions are performed in a terrible manner, earned through lust and anger [or] virtuous, / [if sinful] one may sink into a terrifying hell from which there is no crossing over.

6.3.s:
uttāraṇāya jantūnāṃ narmadātaṭasaṃsthitam .
evametanmahātīrthaṃ narakeśvaramuttamam .. 159.50 ..
6.3.d:
उत्तारणाय जन्तूनां नर्मदातटसंस्थितम् .
एवमेतन्महातीर्थं नरकेश्वरमुत्तमम् .. 159.50 ..
6.3.m: For the rescue of living creatures, situated on the bank of the Narmadā, / is this great sacred ford, the supreme Narakeśvara.

6.3.s:
narakāpahaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam .
tattīrthaṃ sarvatīrthānāmuttamaṃ bhuvi durlabham .. 159.51 ..
6.3.d:
नरकापहं महापुण्यं महापातकनाशनम् .
तत्तीर्थं सर्वतीर्थानामुत्तमं भुवि दुर्लभम् .. 159.51 ..
6.3.m: It removes hell, grants great religious merit, and destroys heinous sins; / that sacred ford is the best of all sacred fords, hard to attain on earth.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ snātvā pūjayeta maheśvaram .
mahāpātakayukto'pi narakaṃ naiva paśyati .. 159.52 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः स्नात्वा पूजयेत महेश्वरम् .
महापातकयुक्तोऽपि नरकं नैव पश्यति .. 159.52 ..
6.3.m: Having bathed at that sacred ford, he who worships the Great Lord, / even if possessed of heinous sins, never sees hell.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yo dadyāddhenuṃ vaitaraṇīṃ śubhām .
sa mucyate sukhenaiva vaitaraṇyāṃ na saṃśayaḥ .. 159.53 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यो दद्याद्धेनुं वैतरणीं शुभाम् .
स मुच्यते सुखेनैव वैतरण्यां न संशयः .. 159.53 ..
6.3.m: He who gives an auspicious Vaitaraṇī cow at that sacred ford / is freed with ease at the Vaitaraṇī river; of this there is no doubt.

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
yamadvāre mahāghore yā sā vaitaraṇī nadī .
kiṃrūpā kiṃpramāṇā sā kathaṃ sā vahati dvija .. 159.54 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
यमद्वारे महाघोरे या सा वैतरणी नदी .
किंरूपा किंप्रमाणा सा कथं सा वहति द्विज .. 159.54 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / That river Vaitaraṇī at the terrible door of Yama, / what is its form, what is its extent, and how does it flow, O twice-born?

6.3.s:
kathaṃ tasyāḥ pramucyante keṣāṃ vāsastu saṃtatam .
keṣāṃ tu sānukūlā sā hyetadvistarato vada .. 159.55 ..
6.3.d:
कथं तस्याः प्रमुच्यन्ते केषां वासस्तु संततम् .
केषां तु सानुकूला सा ह्येतद्विस्तरतो वद .. 159.55 ..
6.3.m: How are [men] delivered from it, and whose dwelling is there perpetually? / To whom is it favorable? Tell me this in detail.

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
dharmaputra mahābāho śṛṇu sarvaṃ mayoditam .
yā sā vaitaraṇī nāma yamadvāre mahāsarit .. 159.56 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
धर्मपुत्र महाबाहो शृणु सर्वं मयोदितम् .
या सा वैतरणी नाम यमद्वारे महासरित् .. 159.56 ..
6.3.m: Glorious Mārkaṇḍeya said: / O son of Dharma, O mighty-armed one, hear everything spoken by me / concerning that great river named Vaitaraṇī at the door of Yama.

6.3.s:
agādhā pārarahitā dṛṣṭamātrā bhayāvahā .
pūyaśoṇitatoyā sā māṃsakardamanirmitā .. 159.57 ..
6.3.d:
अगाधा पाररहिता दृष्टमात्रा भयावहा .
पूयशोणिततोया सा मांसकर्दमनिर्मिता .. 159.57 ..
6.3.m: It is unfathomable, shoreless, and frightful as soon as it is seen. / Its waters are pus and blood, and it is made of flesh and mud.

6.3.s:
tattoyaṃ bhramate tūrṇaṃ tāpīmadhye ghṛtaṃ yathā .
kṛmibhiḥ saṅkulaṃ pūyaṃ vajratuṇḍairayomukhaiḥ .. 159.58 ..
6.3.d:
तत्तोयं भ्रमते तूर्णं तापीमध्ये घृतं यथा .
कृमिभिः सङ्कुलं पूयं वज्रतुण्डैरयोमुखैः .. 159.58 ..
6.3.m: Its water swirls rapidly like clarified butter in a frying vessel; / the pus is swarming with worms with adamantine beaks and iron mouths,

6.3.s:
śiśumāraiśca makarairvajrakartarisaṃyutaiḥ .
anyaiśca jalajīvaiḥ sā suhiṃsrairmarmabhedibhiḥ .. 159.59 ..
6.3.d:
शिशुमारैश्च मकरैर्वज्रकर्तरिसंयुतैः .
अन्यैश्च जलजीवैः सा सुहिंस्रैर्मर्मभेदिभिः .. 159.59 ..
6.3.m: and with porpoises and crocodiles equipped with adamantine shears, / and with other exceedingly cruel aquatic creatures that pierce the vitals.

6.3.s:
tapanti dvādaśādityāḥ pralayānta ivolbaṇāḥ .
patanti tatra vai martyāḥ krandanto bhṛśadāruṇam .. 159.60 ..
6.3.d:
तपन्ति द्वादशादित्याः प्रलयान्त इवोल्बणाः .
पतन्ति तत्र वै मर्त्याः क्रन्दन्तो भृशदारुणम् .. 159.60 ..
6.3.m: Twelve fierce suns scorch it, as if at the end of a cosmic dissolution; / mortals fall therein, crying out most dreadfully.

6.3.s:
hā bhrātaḥ putra hā mātaḥ pralapanti muhurmuhuḥ .
asipattravane ghore patantaṃ yo'bhirakṣati .. 159.61 ..
6.3.d:
हा भ्रातः पुत्र हा मातः प्रलपन्ति मुहुर्मुहुः .
असिपत्त्रवने घोरे पतन्तं योऽभिरक्षति .. 159.61 ..
6.3.m: "Alas, brother! Son! Alas, mother!" they wail repeatedly. / [Consider] who protects one falling in the terrible sword-leaved forest!

6.3.s:
prataranti nimajjanti glāniṃ gacchanti jantavaḥ .
caturvidhaiḥ prāṇigaṇairdraṣṭavyā sā mahānadī .. 159.62 ..
6.3.d:
प्रतरन्ति निमज्जन्ति ग्लानिं गच्छन्ति जन्तवः .
चतुर्विधैः प्राणिगणैर्द्रष्टव्या सा महानदी .. 159.62 ..
6.3.m: Creatures try to swim across, sink down, and faint with exhaustion. / That great river must be seen by the four classes of living beings.

6.3.s:
taranti tasyāṃ saddānairanyathā tu patanti te .
mātaraṃ ye na manyante hyācāryaṃ gurumeva ca .. 159.63 ..
6.3.d:
तरन्ति तस्यां सद्दानैरन्यथा तु पतन्ति ते .
मातरं ये न मन्यन्ते ह्याचार्यं गुरुमेव च .. 159.63 ..
6.3.m: They cross over it through good gifts; otherwise, they fall. / Those who do not respect their mother, teacher, and preceptor,

6.3.s:
avajānanti mūḍhā ye teṣāṃ vāsastu saṃtatam .
pativratāṃ sādhuśīlāmūḍhāṃ dharmeṣu niścalām .. 159.64 ..
6.3.d:
अवजानन्ति मूढा ये तेषां वासस्तु संततम् .
पतिव्रतां साधुशीलामूढां धर्मेषु निश्चलाम् .. 159.64 ..
6.3.m: and the fools who show them contempt—their dwelling is there perpetually. / A devoted and virtuous wife, properly wedded and steadfast in duties—

6.3.s:
parityajanti ye pāpāḥ saṃtataṃ tu vasanti te .
viśvāsapratipannānāṃ svāmimitratapasvinām .. 159.65 ..
6.3.d:
परित्यजन्ति ये पापाः संततं तु वसन्ति ते .
विश्वासप्रतिपन्नानां स्वामिमित्रतपस्विनाम् .. 159.65 ..
6.3.m: those wicked men who abandon her dwell there perpetually. / Of those who have placed their trust—masters, friends, and ascetics—

6.3.s:
strībālavṛddhadīnānāṃ chidramanveṣayanti ye .
pacyante tatra madhye vai krandamānāḥ supāpinaḥ .. 159.66 ..
6.3.d:
स्त्रीबालवृद्धदीनानां छिद्रमन्वेषयन्ति ये .
पच्यन्ते तत्र मध्ये वै क्रन्दमानाः सुपापिनः .. 159.66 ..
6.3.m: and of women, children, the elderly, and the wretched, those who seek faults / are cooked in the middle of it, screaming, being great sinners.

6.3.s:
śrāntaṃ bubhukṣitaṃ vipraṃ yo vighnayati durmatiḥ .
kṛmibhirbhakṣyate tatra yāvatkalpaśatatrayam .. 159.67 ..
6.3.d:
श्रान्तं बुभुक्षितं विप्रं यो विघ्नयति दुर्मतिः .
कृमिभिर्भक्ष्यते तत्र यावत्कल्पशतत्रयम् .. 159.67 ..
6.3.m: The evil-minded one who obstructs a tired and hungry brahmin / is devoured there by worms for three hundred cosmic ages.

6.3.s:
brāhmaṇāya pratiśrutya yo dānaṃ na prayacchati .
āhūya nāsti yo brūte tasya vāsastu saṃtatam .. 159.68 ..
6.3.d:
ब्राह्मणाय प्रतिश्रुत्य यो दानं न प्रयच्छति .
आहूय नास्ति यो ब्रूते तस्य वासस्तु संततम् .. 159.68 ..
6.3.m: He who promises a gift to a brahmin and does not give it, / or having called him says "there is nothing," his dwelling is perpetual.

6.3.s:
agnido garadaścaiva rājagāmī ca paiśunī .
kathābhaṅgakaraścaiva kūṭasākṣī ca madyapaḥ .. 159.69 ..
6.3.d:
अग्निदो गरदश्चैव राजगामी च पैशुनी .
कथाभङ्गकरश्चैव कूटसाक्षी च मद्यपः .. 159.69 ..
6.3.m: The arsonist, the poisoner, the informer to the king, the slanderer, / the interrupter of holy tales, the false witness, and the drinker of spirits;

6.3.s:
vajravidhvaṃsakaścaiva svayaṃdattāpahārakaḥ .
sukṣetrasetubhedī ca paradārapradharṣakaḥ .. 159.70 ..
6.3.d:
वज्रविध्वंसकश्चैव स्वयंदत्तापहारकः .
सुक्षेत्रसेतुभेदी च परदारप्रधर्षकः .. 159.70 ..
6.3.m: the breaker of diamond-hard [pledges], the usurper of what he himself gave, / the destroyer of dams in good fields, and the violator of another's wife;

6.3.s:
brāhmaṇo rasavikretā vṛṣalīpatireva ca .
gokulasya tṛṣārtasya pālībhedaṃ karoti yaḥ .. 159.71 ..
6.3.d:
ब्राह्मणो रसविक्रेता वृषलीपतिरेव च .
गोकुलस्य तृषार्तस्य पालीभेदं करोति यः .. 159.71 ..
6.3.m: a brahmin who sells juices and spices, a husband of a Śūdra woman, / and he who breaks the embankment of a herd of cows afflicted with thirst;

6.3.s:
kanyābhidūṣakaścaiva dānaṃ dattvā tu tāpakaḥ .
śūdrastu kapilāpānī brāhmaṇo māṃsabhojanī .. 159.72 ..
6.3.d:
कन्याभिदूषकश्चैव दानं दत्त्वा तु तापकः .
शूद्रस्तु कपिलापानी ब्राह्मणो मांसभोजनी .. 159.72 ..
6.3.m: the defiler of maidens, the one who torments [the recipient] after giving a gift, / a Śūdra who drinks the milk of a brown cow, and a brahmin who eats meat—

6.3.s:
ete vasanti satataṃ mā vicāraṃ kṛthā nṛpa .
sānukūlā bhavedyena tacchṛṇuṣva narādhipa .. 159.73 ..
6.3.d:
एते वसन्ति सततं मा विचारं कृथा नृप .
सानुकूला भवेद्येन तच्छृणुष्व नराधिप .. 159.73 ..
6.3.m: these reside there perpetually; have no doubt of it, O king. / Hear, O ruler of men, how it may become favorable [to someone]:

6.3.s:
ayane viṣuve caiva vyatīpāte dinakṣaye .
anyeṣu puṇyakāleṣu dīyate dānamuttamam .. 159.74 ..
6.3.d:
अयने विषुवे चैव व्यतीपाते दिनक्षये .
अन्येषु पुण्यकालेषु दीयते दानमुत्तमम् .. 159.74 ..
6.3.m: At a solstice, at an equinox, during Vyatīpāta, on the conjunction day of the moon, / and at other meritorious times, the supreme gift should be given.

6.3.s:
kṛṣṇāṃ vā pāṭalāṃ vāpi kuryādvaitaraṇīṃ śubhām .
svarṇaśṛṅgīṃ rūpyakhurāṃ kāṃsyapātrasya dohinīm .. 159.75 ..
6.3.d:
कृष्णां वा पाटलां वापि कुर्याद्वैतरणीं शुभाम् .
स्वर्णशृङ्गीं रूप्यखुरां कांस्यपात्रस्य दोहिनीम् .. 159.75 ..
6.3.m: One should make an auspicious Vaitaraṇī [cow], either black or reddish-brown, / with golden horns, silver hooves, and milked into a bell-metal vessel,

6.3.s:
kṛṣṇavastrayugācchannāṃ saptadhānyasamanvitām .
kuryātsadroṇaśikhara āsīnāṃ tāmrabhājane .. 159.76 ..
6.3.d:
कृष्णवस्त्रयुगाच्छन्नां सप्तधान्यसमन्विताम् .
कुर्यात्सद्रोणशिखर आसीनां ताम्रभाजने .. 159.76 ..
6.3.m: covered with a pair of black garments, accompanied by the seven grains; / one should place it, seated on a copper vessel, with the height of a droṇa measure.

6.3.s:
yamaṃ haimaṃ prakurvīta lohadaṇḍasamanvitam .
ikṣudaṇḍamayaṃ baddhvā hyuḍupaṃ paṭṭabandhanaiḥ .. 159.77 ..
6.3.d:
यमं हैमं प्रकुर्वीत लोहदण्डसमन्वितम् .
इक्षुदण्डमयं बद्ध्वा ह्युडुपं पट्टबन्धनैः .. 159.77 ..
6.3.m: One should fashion a golden Yama equipped with an iron staff, / and having tied a raft made of sugarcane stalks with silk cords,

6.3.s:
uḍupopari tāṃ dhenuṃ sūryadehasamudbhavām .
kṛtvā prakalpayedvidvāñchattropānadyugānvitām .. 159.78 ..
6.3.d:
उडुपोपरि तां धेनुं सूर्यदेहसमुद्भवाम् .
कृत्वा प्रकल्पयेद्विद्वाञ्छत्त्रोपानद्युगान्विताम् .. 159.78 ..
6.3.m: and having placed that cow born from the body of the sun upon the raft, / the wise man should furnish it with an umbrella and a pair of sandals.

6.3.s:
aṅgulīyakavāsāṃsi brāhmaṇāya nivedayet .
imamuccārayenmantraṃ saṃgṛhyāsyāśca pucchakam .. 159.79 ..
6.3.d:
अङ्गुलीयकवासांसि ब्राह्मणाय निवेदयेत् .
इममुच्चारयेन्मन्त्रं संगृह्यास्याश्च पुच्छकम् .. 159.79 ..
6.3.m: He should present a finger-ring and garments to a brahmin, / and holding the tail of this [cow], he should recite this mantra:

6.3.s:
oṃ yamadvāre mahāghore yā sā vaitaraṇī nadī .
tartukāmo dadāmyenāṃ tubhyaṃ vaitaraṇi namaḥ .
ityadhivāsanamantraḥ .. 159.80 ..
6.3.d:
ओं यमद्वारे महाघोरे या सा वैतरणी नदी .
तर्तुकामो ददाम्येनां तुभ्यं वैतरणि नमः .
इत्यधिवासनमन्त्रः .. 159.80 ..
6.3.m: "Om. That river Vaitaraṇī at the terrible door of Yama— / desiring to cross it, I give this [cow]; homage to you, O Vaitaraṇī!" / Such is the consecration mantra.

6.3.s:
gāvo me cāgrataḥ santu gāvo me santu pṛṣṭhataḥ .
gāvo me hṛdaye santu gavāṃ madhye vasāmyaham .. 159.81 ..
6.3.d:
गावो मे चाग्रतः सन्तु गावो मे सन्तु पृष्ठतः .
गावो मे हृदये सन्तु गवां मध्ये वसाम्यहम् .. 159.81 ..
6.3.m: "May cows be in front of me; may cows be behind me; / may cows be in my heart; I dwell in the midst of cows."

6.3.s:
oṃ viṣṇurūpa dvijaśreṣṭha bhūdeva paṅktipāvana .
sadakṣiṇā mayā dattā tubhyaṃ vaitaraṇi namaḥ .
iti dānamantraḥ .. 159.82 ..
6.3.d:
ओं विष्णुरूप द्विजश्रेष्ठ भूदेव पङ्क्तिपावन .
सदक्षिणा मया दत्ता तुभ्यं वैतरणि नमः .
इति दानमन्त्रः .. 159.82 ..
6.3.m: "Om. O best of the twice-born, whose form is Viṣṇu, O god on earth, sanctifier of assemblies, / [this cow] is given by me along with a priestly gift; homage to you, O Vaitaraṇī!" / Such is the donation mantra.

6.3.s:
brāhmaṇaṃ dharmarājaṃ ca dhenuṃ vaitaraṇīṃ śivām .
sarvaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya brāhmaṇāya nivedayet .. 159.83 ..
6.3.d:
ब्राह्मणं धर्मराजं च धेनुं वैतरणीं शिवाम् .
सर्वं प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य ब्राह्मणाय निवेदयेत् .. 159.83 ..
6.3.m: Having circumambulated the brahmin, Dharmarāja, / and the auspicious Vaitaraṇī cow, he should offer everything to the brahmin,

6.3.s: pucchaṃ saṃgṛhya surabheragre kṛtvā dvijaṃ tataḥ .. 159.84 ..
6.3.d: पुच्छं संगृह्य सुरभेरग्रे कृत्वा द्विजं ततः .. 159.84 ..
6.3.m: holding the tail of the cow and placing the twice-born in front; then:

6.3.s:
dhenuke tvaṃ pratīkṣasva yamadvāre mahābhaye .
uttitīrṣurahaṃ dheno vaitaraṇyai namo'stu te .
ityanuvrajamantraḥ .. 159.85 ..
6.3.d:
धेनुके त्वं प्रतीक्षस्व यमद्वारे महाभये .
उत्तितीर्षुरहं धेनो वैतरण्यै नमोऽस्तु ते .
इत्यनुव्रजमन्त्रः .. 159.85 ..
6.3.m: "O cow, wait for me at the terrifying door of Yama; / wishing to cross over, O cow, homage be to you, O Vaitaraṇī!" / Such is the mantra for following after.

6.3.s:
anuvrajeta gacchantaṃ sarvaṃ tasya gṛhaṃ nayet .
evaṃ kṛte mahīpāla saritsyātsukhavāhinī .. 159.86 ..
6.3.d:
अनुव्रजेत गच्छन्तं सर्वं तस्य गृहं नयेत् .
एवं कृते महीपाल सरित्स्यात्सुखवाहिनी .. 159.86 ..
6.3.m: One should accompany him as he walks away, and take everything to his house. / When this is done, O king, that river becomes one of pleasant flow.

6.3.s:
tārayate tayā dhenvā sā sarijjalavāhinī .
sarvānkāmānavāpnoti ye divyā ye ca mānuṣāḥ .. 159.87 ..
6.3.d:
तारयते तया धेन्वा सा सरिज्जलवाहिनी .
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति ये दिव्या ये च मानुषाः .. 159.87 ..
6.3.m: By means of that cow, that river flowing with water carries [him] across. / He obtains all desires, both celestial and human.

6.3.s:
rogī rogādvimuktaḥ syācchāmyanti paramāpadaḥ .
svasthe sahasraguṇitamāture śatasaṃmitam .. 159.88 ..
6.3.d:
रोगी रोगाद्विमुक्तः स्याच्छाम्यन्ति परमापदः .
स्वस्थे सहस्रगुणितमातुरे शतसंमितम् .. 159.88 ..
6.3.m: A sick person is freed from illness, and the greatest calamities are pacified. / [Given] when healthy, [the fruit] is a thousandfold; when afflicted, it is equivalent to a hundredfold.

6.3.s:
mṛtasyaiva tu yaddānaṃ parokṣe tatsamaṃ smṛtam .
svahastena tato deyaṃ mṛte kaḥ kasya dāsyati .
iti matvā mahārāja svadattaṃ syānmahāphalam .. 159.89 ..
6.3.d:
मृतस्यैव तु यद्दानं परोक्षे तत्समं स्मृतम् .
स्वहस्तेन ततो देयं मृते कः कस्य दास्यति .
इति मत्वा महाराज स्वदत्तं स्यान्महाफलम् .. 159.89 ..
6.3.m: The gift given on behalf of one who has died, in his absence, is regarded as equal [to ordinary fruit]. / Therefore one should give it with one's own hand; once dead, who will give to whom? / Considering this, O great king, what is given by oneself yields great fruit.

6.3.s:
ityevamuktaṃ tava dharmasūno dānaṃ mayā vaitaraṇīsamuttham .
śṛṇoti bhaktyā paṭhatīha samyaksa yāti viṣṇoḥ padamaprameyam .. 159.90 ..
6.3.d:
इत्येवमुक्तं तव धर्मसूनो दानं मया वैतरणीसमुत्थम् .
शृणोति भक्त्या पठतीह सम्यक्स याति विष्णोः पदमप्रमेयम् .. 159.90 ..
6.3.m: Thus has the gift pertaining to the Vaitaraṇī been declared to you by me, O son of Dharma. / Whoever hears or recites it properly with devotion here goes to the immeasurable realm of Viṣṇu.

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
prāpte cāśvayuje māsi tasminkṛṣṇā caturdaśī .
snātvā kṛtvā tataḥ śrāddhaṃ sampūjya ca maheśvaram .. 159.91 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
प्राप्ते चाश्वयुजे मासि तस्मिन्कृष्णा चतुर्दशी .
स्नात्वा कृत्वा ततः श्राद्धं सम्पूज्य च महेश्वरम् .. 159.91 ..
6.3.m: Glorious Mārkaṇḍeya said: / When the month of Āśvayuja arrives, on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, / having bathed, performed the śrāddha, and worshipped Maheśvara,

6.3.s:
pitṛbhyo dīyate dānaṃ bhaktiśraddhāsamanvitaiḥ .
paścājjāgaraṇaṃ kuryātsatkathāśravaṇādibhiḥ .. 159.92 ..
6.3.d:
पितृभ्यो दीयते दानं भक्तिश्रद्धासमन्वितैः .
पश्चाज्जागरणं कुर्यात्सत्कथाश्रवणादिभिः .. 159.92 ..
6.3.m: a gift is given to the ancestors by those endowed with devotion and faith. / Afterwards, one should keep a vigil by listening to holy stories and other means.

6.3.s:
tataḥ prabhātasamaye snātvā vai narmadājale .
tarpaṇaṃ vidhivatkṛtvā pitḥṇāṃ devapūrvakam .. 159.93 ..
6.3.d:
ततः प्रभातसमये स्नात्वा वै नर्मदाजले .
तर्पणं विधिवत्कृत्वा पित्ःणां देवपूर्वकम् .. 159.93 ..
6.3.m: Then at daybreak, having bathed in the waters of the Narmadā / and duly performed the water libation to the ancestors preceded by the gods,

6.3.s:
sauvarṇe ghṛtasaṃyuktaṃ dīpaṃ dadyāddvijātaye .
paścātsaṃbhojayedviprān svayaṃ caiva vimatsaraḥ .. 159.94 ..
6.3.d:
सौवर्णे घृतसंयुक्तं दीपं दद्याद्द्विजातये .
पश्चात्संभोजयेद्विप्रान् स्वयं चैव विमत्सरः .. 159.94 ..
6.3.m: one should give a lamp with clarified butter in a golden vessel to a twice-born. / Afterwards, free from malice, he should feed the brahmins and himself.

6.3.s:
evaṃ kṛte naraśreṣṭha na janturnarakaṃ vrajet .
avaśyameva manujairdraṣṭavyā nārakī sthitiḥ .. 159.95 ..
6.3.d:
एवं कृते नरश्रेष्ठ न जन्तुर्नरकं व्रजेत् .
अवश्यमेव मनुजैर्द्रष्टव्या नारकी स्थितिः .. 159.95 ..
6.3.m: When this is done, O best of men, a living being does not go to hell. / A stay in hell must inevitably be seen by men.

6.3.s:
anena vidhinā kṛtvā na paśyennarakānnaraḥ .
tatra tīrthe mṛtānāṃ tu narāṇāṃ vidhinā nṛpa .. 159.96 ..
6.3.d:
अनेन विधिना कृत्वा न पश्येन्नरकान्नरः .
तत्र तीर्थे मृतानां तु नराणां विधिना नृप .. 159.96 ..
6.3.m: Having acted according to this rite, a man does not see the hells. / For men who die in that sacred ford according to the rite, O king,

6.3.s:
manvantaraṃ śive loke vāso bhavati durlabhe .
vimānenārkavarṇena kiṃkiṇīśataśobhinā .. 159.97 ..
6.3.d:
मन्वन्तरं शिवे लोके वासो भवति दुर्लभे .
विमानेनार्कवर्णेन किंकिणीशतशोभिना .. 159.97 ..
6.3.m: there is a stay for a manvantara in the world of Śiva, which is hard to attain. / In an aerial chariot having the colour of the sun, adorned with hundreds of small bells,

6.3.s:
sa gacchati mahābhāga sevyamāno'psarogaṇaiḥ .
bhunakti vividhānbhogānuktakālaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .. 159.98 ..
6.3.d:
स गच्छति महाभाग सेव्यमानोऽप्सरोगणैः .
भुनक्ति विविधान्भोगानुक्तकालं न संशयः .. 159.98 ..
6.3.m: he goes, O fortunate one, served by hosts of apsarases. / He enjoys various pleasures for the stated time; there is no doubt.

6.3.s:
pūrṇe caiva tataḥ kāla iha mānuṣyatāṃ gataḥ .
sarvavyādhivinirmukto jīvecca śaradāṃ śatam .. 159.99 ..
6.3.d:
पूर्णे चैव ततः काल इह मानुष्यतां गतः .
सर्वव्याधिविनिर्मुक्तो जीवेच्च शरदां शतम् .. 159.99 ..
6.3.m: And when that time is fulfilled, having attained human status here, / free from all diseases, he would live for a hundred autumns.

6.3.s:
prāpya cāśvayuje māsi kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśīm .
ahorātroṣito bhūtvā pūjayitvā maheśvaram .
mahāpātakayukto'pi mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 159.100 ..
6.3.d:
प्राप्य चाश्वयुजे मासि कृष्णपक्षे चतुर्दशीम् .
अहोरात्रोषितो भूत्वा पूजयित्वा महेश्वरम् .
महापातकयुक्तोऽपि मुच्यते नात्र संशयः .. 159.100 ..
6.3.m: Having reached the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight in the month of Āśvayuja, / having fasted for a day and night and worshipped Maheśvara, / even if joined with great sins, one is liberated; of this there is no doubt.

6.3.s:
aṣṭāviṃśatikoṭyo vai narakāṇāṃ yudhiṣṭhira .
vimuktā narakairduḥkhaiḥ śivalokaṃ vrajanti te .. 159.101 ..
6.3.d:
अष्टाविंशतिकोट्यो वै नरकाणां युधिष्ठिर .
विमुक्ता नरकैर्दुःखैः शिवलोकं व्रजन्ति ते .. 159.101 ..
6.3.m: There are indeed twenty-eight crores of hells, O Yudhiṣṭhira. / Freed from the miseries of hell, they go to the world of Śiva.

6.3.s:
tatra bhuktvā mahābhogāndivyaiśvaryasamanvitān .
labhante mānuṣaṃ janma durlabhaṃ bhuvi mānavāḥ .. 159.102 ..
.. iti śrīskande mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe'narakeśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmaikonaṣaṣṭyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 160
6.3.d:
तत्र भुक्त्वा महाभोगान्दिव्यैश्वर्यसमन्वितान् .
लभन्ते मानुषं जन्म दुर्लभं भुवि मानवाः .. 159.102 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कन्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डेऽनरकेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामैकोनषष्ट्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 160
6.3.m:
Having enjoyed great pleasures there, endowed with celestial sovereignty, / men obtain human birth, which is hard to attain on earth.
Thus ends the one hundred and fifty-ninth chapter, entitled "The Description of the Māhātmya of the Anarakeśvara Sacred Ford", in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth Āvantyakhaṇḍa in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Chapter 160

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gacchetpāṇḍuputra mokṣatīrthamanuttamam .
sevitaṃ devagandharvairmunibhiśca tapodhanaiḥ .. 160.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेत्पाण्डुपुत्र मोक्षतीर्थमनुत्तमम् .
सेवितं देवगन्धर्वैर्मुनिभिश्च तपोधनैः .. 160.1 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then one should go, O son of Pāṇḍu, to the unexcelled Mokṣatīrtha, / frequented by gods, gandharvas, and sages rich in austerity.

6.3.s:
bahavastanna jānanti viṣṇumāyāvimohitāḥ .
yatra siddhā mahābhāgā ṛṣayaḥ satapodhanāḥ .. 160.2 ..
6.3.d:
बहवस्तन्न जानन्ति विष्णुमायाविमोहिताः .
यत्र सिद्धा महाभागा ऋषयः सतपोधनाः .. 160.2 ..
6.3.m: Many do not know of it, deluded by the māyā of Viṣṇu, / where the highly fortunate seers rich in austerity attained perfection:

6.3.s:
pulastyaḥ pulaho vidvānkratuścaiva mahāmatiḥ .
prācetaso vasiṣṭhaśca dakṣo nārada eva ca .. 160.3 ..
6.3.d:
पुलस्त्यः पुलहो विद्वान्क्रतुश्चैव महामतिः .
प्राचेतसो वसिष्ठश्च दक्षो नारद एव च .. 160.3 ..
6.3.m: Pulastya, the wise Pulaha, and Kratu of great intellect, / the son of Pracetas, Vasiṣṭha, Dakṣa, and Nārada as well—

6.3.s:
ete cānye mahābhāgāḥ saptasāhasrasaṃjñitāḥ .
mokṣaṃ gatāḥ saha sutaistattīrthaṃ tena mokṣadam .. 160.4 ..
6.3.d:
एते चान्ये महाभागाः सप्तसाहस्रसंज्ञिताः .
मोक्षं गताः सह सुतैस्तत्तीर्थं तेन मोक्षदम् .. 160.4 ..
6.3.m: these and other highly fortunate ones, known as the seven thousand, / attained liberation along with their sons; therefore that sacred ford bestows liberation.

6.3.s:
tatra pravāhamadhye tu patitā tamahā nadī .
tatra tatsaṅgamaṃ tīrthaṃ sarvapāpakṣayaṃkaram .. 160.5 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र प्रवाहमध्ये तु पतिता तमहा नदी .
तत्र तत्सङ्गमं तीर्थं सर्वपापक्षयंकरम् .. 160.5 ..
6.3.m: There into the midst of the stream fell that great river; / there is that confluence ford, which effects the destruction of all sins.

6.3.s:
ṛgyajuḥsāmasaṃjñānāmabhyastānāṃ tu yatphalam .
samyagjaptvā tu vidhinā gāyatrīṃ tatra tallabhet .. 160.6 ..
6.3.d:
ऋग्यजुःसामसंज्ञानामभ्यस्तानां तु यत्फलम् .
सम्यग्जप्त्वा तु विधिना गायत्रीं तत्र तल्लभेत् .. 160.6 ..
6.3.m: Whatever fruit is attained by the study of those known as Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma [Vedas], / one obtains that there by properly reciting the Gāyatrī according to rule.

6.3.s:
tatra dattaṃ hutaṃ japtaṃ tīrthasevārjitaṃ phalam .
sarvamakṣayatāṃ yāti mokṣasādhanamuttamam .. 160.7 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र दत्तं हुतं जप्तं तीर्थसेवार्जितं फलम् .
सर्वमक्षयतां याति मोक्षसाधनमुत्तमम् .. 160.7 ..
6.3.m: What is given there, offered into the fire, recited, and the fruit acquired by attending upon the sacred ford, / all becomes imperishable, an excellent means to liberation.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe mṛtānāṃ tu saṃnyāsena dvijanmanām .
anivartikā gatisteṣāṃ mokṣatīrthaprabhāvataḥ .. 160.8 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे मृतानां तु संन्यासेन द्विजन्मनाम् .
अनिवर्तिका गतिस्तेषां मोक्षतीर्थप्रभावतः .. 160.8 ..
6.3.m: For twice-born men who die at that sacred ford in renunciation, / their state is non-returning, through the power of Mokṣatīrtha.

6.3.s:
eṣa te vidhiruddiṣṭaḥ saṃkṣepeṇa mayānagha .
vyuṣṭistīrthasya mahatī purāṇe yābhidhīyate .. 160.9 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe mokṣatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma ṣaṣṭyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 161
6.3.d:
एष ते विधिरुद्दिष्टः संक्षेपेण मयानघ .
व्युष्टिस्तीर्थस्य महती पुराणे याभिधीयते .. 160.9 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे मोक्षतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम षष्ट्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 161
6.3.m:
This rule has been briefly explained to you by me, O sinless one. / Great is the efficacy of the sacred ford which is proclaimed in the Purāṇa.
Thus ends the one hundred and sixtieth chapter, named the Description of the Greatness of Mokṣatīrtha, in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses].
Chapter 161

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gacchenmahārāja sarpatīrthamanuttamam .
yatra siddhā mahāsarpāstapastaptvā yudhiṣṭhira .. 161.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेन्महाराज सर्पतीर्थमनुत्तमम् .
यत्र सिद्धा महासर्पास्तपस्तप्त्वा युधिष्ठिर .. 161.1 ..
6.3.m: The glorious Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then, O great king, one should go to the unexcelled Sarpatīrtha, / where great serpents became perfected by performing austerity, O Yudhiṣṭhira:

6.3.s:
vāsukistakṣako ghoraḥ sārpa airāvatastathā .
kāliyaśca mahābhāgaḥ karkoṭakadhanaṃjayau .. 161.2 ..
6.3.d:
वासुकिस्तक्षको घोरः सार्प ऐरावतस्तथा .
कालियश्च महाभागः कर्कोटकधनंजयौ .. 161.2 ..
6.3.m: Vāsuki, the terrible Takṣaka, Sārpa, Airāvata likewise, / the highly fortunate Kāliya, Karkoṭaka, and Dhanañjaya;

6.3.s:
śaṅkhacūḍo mahātejā dhṛtarāṣṭro vṛkodaraḥ .
kuliko vāmanaścaiva teṣāṃ ye putrapautriṇaḥ .. 161.3 ..
6.3.d:
शङ्खचूडो महातेजा धृतराष्ट्रो वृकोदरः .
कुलिको वामनश्चैव तेषां ये पुत्रपौत्रिणः .. 161.3 ..
6.3.m: Śaṅkhacūḍa of great majesty, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Vṛkodara, / Kulika, and Vāmana, and those who are their sons and grandsons.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe mahāpuṇye tapastaptvā suduṣkaram .
bhuñjanti vividhānbhogānkrīḍanti ca yathāsukham .. 161.4 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे महापुण्ये तपस्तप्त्वा सुदुष्करम् .
भुञ्जन्ति विविधान्भोगान्क्रीडन्ति च यथासुखम् .. 161.4 ..
6.3.m: Having performed very difficult austerity at that most holy sacred ford, / they enjoy various pleasures and disport themselves at will.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ snātvā tarpayetpitṛdevatāḥ .
vājapeyaphalaṃ tasya purā provāca śaṅkaraḥ .. 161.5 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः स्नात्वा तर्पयेत्पितृदेवताः .
वाजपेयफलं तस्य पुरा प्रोवाच शङ्करः .. 161.5 ..
6.3.m: Śaṅkara formerly proclaimed that he who bathes at that sacred ford / and makes libations to the ancestors and gods gains the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice.

6.3.s:
snātānāṃ sarpatīrthe tu narāṇāṃ bhuvi bhārata .
sarpavṛścikajātibhyo na bhayaṃ vidyate kvacit .. 161.6 ..
6.3.d:
स्नातानां सर्पतीर्थे तु नराणां भुवि भारत .
सर्पवृश्चिकजातिभ्यो न भयं विद्यते क्वचित् .. 161.6 ..
6.3.m: For men who have bathed at Sarpatīrtha, O Bhārata, / there is never any fear in the world from species of snakes and scorpions.

6.3.s:
mṛto bhogavatīṃ gatvā pūjyamāno mahoragaiḥ .
nāgakanyāparivṛto mahābhogapatirbhavet .. 161.7 ..
6.3.d:
मृतो भोगवतीं गत्वा पूज्यमानो महोरगैः .
नागकन्यापरिवृतो महाभोगपतिर्भवेत् .. 161.7 ..
6.3.m: When he dies, he goes to Bhogavatī, worshipped by the great serpents; / surrounded by snake maidens, he becomes a lord of great enjoyment.

6.3.s:
mārgaśīrṣasya māsasya kṛṣṇapakṣe ca yāṣṭamī .
sopavāsaḥ śucirbhūtvā liṅgaṃ sampūrayettilaiḥ .
yathāvibhavasāreṇa gandhapuṣpaiḥ samarcayet .. 161.8 ..
6.3.d:
मार्गशीर्षस्य मासस्य कृष्णपक्षे च याष्टमी .
सोपवासः शुचिर्भूत्वा लिङ्गं सम्पूरयेत्तिलैः .
यथाविभवसारेण गन्धपुष्पैः समर्चयेत् .. 161.8 ..
6.3.m: On the eighth day in the dark fortnight of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, / having fasted and become pure, one should cover the liṅga with sesame seeds / and worship it with fragrant pastes and flowers according to one's wealth.

6.3.s:
evaṃ vidhāya vidhivatpraṇipatya kṣamāpayet .
tasya yatphalamuddiṣṭaṃ tacchṛṇuṣva nareśvara .. 161.9 ..
6.3.d:
एवं विधाय विधिवत्प्रणिपत्य क्षमापयेत् .
तस्य यत्फलमुद्दिष्टं तच्छृणुष्व नरेश्वर .. 161.9 ..
6.3.m: Having performed this according to the rule, bowing down, one should ask for forgiveness. / Hear the fruit that is declared for him, O ruler of men:

6.3.s:
tilāstatra ca yatsaṃkhyāḥ patrapuṣpaphalāni ca .
tāvatsvargapure rājanmodate kālamīpsitam .. 161.10 ..
6.3.d:
तिलास्तत्र च यत्संख्याः पत्रपुष्पफलानि च .
तावत्स्वर्गपुरे राजन्मोदते कालमीप्सितम् .. 161.10 ..
6.3.m: As many as the sesame seeds are there, and the leaves, flowers, and fruits, / for that much desired time he rejoices in the city of heaven, O king.

6.3.s:
tataḥ svargātparibhraṣṭo jāyate vimale kule .
surūpaḥ subhagaścaiva dhanakoṭipatirbhavet .. 161.11 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe sarpatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmaikaṣaṣṭyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 162
6.3.d:
ततः स्वर्गात्परिभ्रष्टो जायते विमले कुले .
सुरूपः सुभगश्चैव धनकोटिपतिर्भवेत् .. 161.11 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे सर्पतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामैकषष्ट्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 162
6.3.m:
Then, falling from heaven, he is born in a stainless family; / handsome and fortunate, he becomes master of ten million pieces of wealth.
Thus ends the one hundred and sixty-first chapter, named the Description of the Greatness of Sarpatīrtha, in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses].
Chapter 162

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
gopeśvaraṃ tato gacchetsarpakṣetrādanantaram .
yatra snānena caikena mucyante pātakairnarāḥ .. 162.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
गोपेश्वरं ततो गच्छेत्सर्पक्षेत्रादनन्तरम् .
यत्र स्नानेन चैकेन मुच्यन्ते पातकैर्नराः .. 162.1 ..
6.3.m: The glorious Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then, immediately after the sacred field of the serpents, one should go to Gopeśvara, / where men are freed from sins by a single ritual ablution.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ snātvā kurute prāṇasaṃkṣayam .
sa gacchedyadi yukto'pi pāpena śivamandiram .. 162.2 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः स्नात्वा कुरुते प्राणसंक्षयम् .
स गच्छेद्यदि युक्तोऽपि पापेन शिवमन्दिरम् .. 162.2 ..
6.3.m: He who, having bathed at that sacred ford, brings about the end of his life, / goes to Śiva's abode, even if joined with sin.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ snātvā pūjayeddevamīśvaram .
mucyate sarvapāpaiśca rudralokaṃ sa gacchati .. 162.3 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः स्नात्वा पूजयेद्देवमीश्वरम् .
मुच्यते सर्वपापैश्च रुद्रलोकं स गच्छति .. 162.3 ..
6.3.m: He who, having bathed at that sacred ford, worships the god Īśvara, / is freed from all sins and goes to the realm of Rudra.

6.3.s:
krīḍitvā ca yathākāmaṃ rudraloke mahātapāḥ .
iha mānuṣyatāṃ prāpya rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ .. 162.4 ..
6.3.d:
क्रीडित्वा च यथाकामं रुद्रलोके महातपाः .
इह मानुष्यतां प्राप्य राजा भवति धार्मिकः .. 162.4 ..
6.3.m: Having sported at will in the realm of Rudra, the performer of great austerities, / obtaining human birth here, becomes a righteous king.

6.3.s:
hastyaśvarathasampanno dāsīdāsasamanvitaḥ .
pūjyamāno narendraiśca jīvedvarṣaśataṃ sukhī .. 162.5 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe gopeśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma dviṣaṣṭyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 163
6.3.d:
हस्त्यश्वरथसम्पन्नो दासीदाससमन्वितः .
पूज्यमानो नरेन्द्रैश्च जीवेद्वर्षशतं सुखी .. 162.5 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे गोपेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम द्विषष्ट्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 163
6.3.m:
Endowed with elephants, horses, and chariots, accompanied by female and male servants, / and worshipped by rulers of men, he lives happily for a hundred years.
Thus ends the one hundred and sixty-second chapter, named the Description of the Greatness of Gopeśvaratīrtha, in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses].
Chapter 163

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gacchenmahārāja nāgatīrthamanuttamam .
āśvinasya site pakṣe pañcamyāṃ niyataḥ śuciḥ .. 163.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेन्महाराज नागतीर्थमनुत्तमम् .
आश्विनस्य सिते पक्षे पञ्चम्यां नियतः शुचिः .. 163.1 ..
6.3.m: The glorious Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then, O great king, one should go to the unexcelled Nāgatīrtha. / On the fifth day of the bright fortnight of Āśvina, self-restrained and pure,

6.3.s:
rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kṛtvā gandhadhūpanivedanaiḥ .
prabhāte vimale snātvā śrāddhaṃ kṛtvā yathāvidhi .. 163.2 ..
6.3.d:
रात्रौ जागरणं कृत्वा गन्धधूपनिवेदनैः .
प्रभाते विमले स्नात्वा श्राद्धं कृत्वा यथाविधि .. 163.2 ..
6.3.m: keeping a vigil at night with offerings of fragrances and incense, / having bathed in the stainless morning and performed a śrāddha according to the rule,

6.3.s:
mucyate sarvapāpebhyo nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .
tatra tīrthe tu yo rājanprāṇatyāgaṃ kariṣyati .. 163.3 ..
6.3.d:
मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो नात्र कार्या विचारणा .
तत्र तीर्थे तु यो राजन्प्राणत्यागं करिष्यति .. 163.3 ..
6.3.m: he is freed from all sins; no doubt should be entertained here. / Whoever, O king, shall cast off his life at that sacred ford,

6.3.s:
anivartikā gatistasya provāceti śivaḥ svayam .. 163.4 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe nāgatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma triṣaṣṭyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 164
6.3.d:
अनिवर्तिका गतिस्तस्य प्रोवाचेति शिवः स्वयम् .. 163.4 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे नागतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम त्रिषष्ट्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 164
6.3.m:
his state is non-returning; so said Śiva himself.
Thus ends the one hundred and sixty-third chapter, named the Description of the Greatness of Nāgatīrtha, in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses].
Chapter 164

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gacchenmahārāja sāṃvauraṃ tīrthamuttamam .
yatra saṃnihito bhānuḥ pūjyamānaḥ surāsuraiḥ .. 164.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेन्महाराज सांवौरं तीर्थमुत्तमम् .
यत्र संनिहितो भानुः पूज्यमानः सुरासुरैः .. 164.1 ..
6.3.m: The glorious Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then, O great king, one should go to the excellent Sāṃvaura sacred ford, / where the sun is present, worshipped by gods and asuras.

6.3.s:
tatra ye paṅgutāṃ prāptāḥ śīrṇaghrāṇanakhā narāḥ .
dadrumaṇḍalabhinnāṅgā makṣikākṛmisaṃkulāḥ .. 164.2 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र ये पङ्गुतां प्राप्ताः शीर्णघ्राणनखा नराः .
दद्रुमण्डलभिन्नाङ्गा मक्षिकाकृमिसंकुलाः .. 164.2 ..
6.3.m: Men who have become lame there, whose noses and nails are decayed, / whose bodies are shattered by rings of ringworm, afflicted by flies and worms,

6.3.s:
mātāpitṛbhyāṃ rahitā bhrātṛbhāryāvivarjitāḥ .
anāthā vikalā vyaṅgā magnā ye duḥkhasāgare .. 164.3 ..
6.3.d:
मातापितृभ्यां रहिता भ्रातृभार्याविवर्जिताः .
अनाथा विकला व्यङ्गा मग्ना ये दुःखसागरे .. 164.3 ..
6.3.m: bereft of father and mother, abandoned by brothers and wives, / helpless, crippled, deformed, sunk in an ocean of sorrow—

6.3.s:
teṣāṃ nātho jagadyonirnarmadātaṭamāśritaḥ .
sāṃvauranātho lokānāmārtihā duḥkhanāśanaḥ .. 164.4 ..
6.3.d:
तेषां नाथो जगद्योनिर्नर्मदातटमाश्रितः .
सांवौरनाथो लोकानामार्तिहा दुःखनाशनः .. 164.4 ..
6.3.m: their protector is the source of the world, residing on the bank of the Narmadā: / the Lord of Sāṃvaura, who dispels the distress and destroys the sorrow of all worlds.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ snātvā māsamekaṃ nirantaram .
pūjayedbhāskaraṃ devaṃ tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu .. 164.5 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः स्नात्वा मासमेकं निरन्तरम् .
पूजयेद्भास्करं देवं तस्य पुण्यफलं शृणु .. 164.5 ..
6.3.m: For him who, having bathed at that sacred ford, worships the sun god / continuously for one month, hear the fruit of that merit:

6.3.s:
yatphalaṃ cottare pārtha tathā vai pūrvasāgare .
dakṣiṇe paścime snātvā tatra tīrthe tu tatphalam .. 164.6 ..
6.3.d:
यत्फलं चोत्तरे पार्थ तथा वै पूर्वसागरे .
दक्षिणे पश्चिमे स्नात्वा तत्र तीर्थे तु तत्फलम् .. 164.6 ..
6.3.m: Whatever fruit [comes from] bathing in the northern and in the eastern ocean, O son of Pṛthā, / and likewise in the southern and western, that same fruit is obtained at that sacred ford.

6.3.s:
kaumāre yauvane pāpaṃ vārddhake yacca saṃcitam .
tatpraṇaśyati sāṃvaure snānamātrānna saṃśayaḥ .. 164.7 ..
6.3.d:
कौमारे यौवने पापं वार्द्धके यच्च संचितम् .
तत्प्रणश्यति सांवौरे स्नानमात्रान्न संशयः .. 164.7 ..
6.3.m: The sin accumulated in childhood, in youth, and in old age, / is destroyed simply by bathing at Sāṃvaura, without a doubt.

6.3.s:
na vyādhirnaiva dāridryaṃ na caiveṣṭaviyojanam .
saptajanmāni rājendra sāṃvauraparisevanāt .. 164.8 ..
6.3.d:
न व्याधिर्नैव दारिद्र्यं न चैवेष्टवियोजनम् .
सप्तजन्मानि राजेन्द्र सांवौरपरिसेवनात् .. 164.8 ..
6.3.m: There is no disease, nor poverty, nor separation from dear ones / for seven births, O king of kings, from attendance upon Sāṃvaura.

6.3.s:
saptamyāmupavāsena taddine cāpyupoṣite .
sa tatphalamavāpnoti tatra snātvā na saṃśayaḥ .. 164.9 ..
6.3.d:
सप्तम्यामुपवासेन तद्दिने चाप्युपोषिते .
स तत्फलमवाप्नोति तत्र स्नात्वा न संशयः .. 164.9 ..
6.3.m: By fasting on the seventh lunar day, and having fasted on that day, / he obtains that fruit by bathing there; there is no doubt.

6.3.s:
raktacandanamiśreṇa yadarghyeṇa phalaṃ smṛtam .
tatra tīrthe nṛpaśreṣṭha snātvā tatphalamāpnuyāt .. 164.10 ..
6.3.d:
रक्तचन्दनमिश्रेण यदर्घ्येण फलं स्मृतम् .
तत्र तीर्थे नृपश्रेष्ठ स्नात्वा तत्फलमाप्नुयात् .. 164.10 ..
6.3.m: The fruit that is remembered as arising from an oblation mixed with red sandalwood— / by bathing at that sacred ford, O best of kings, he attains that fruit.

6.3.s:
narmadāsalilaṃ ramyaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam .
nirīkṣitaṃ viśeṣeṇa sāṃvaureṇa mahātmanā .. 164.11 ..
6.3.d:
नर्मदासलिलं रम्यं सर्वपातकनाशनम् .
निरीक्षितं विशेषेण सांवौरेण महात्मना .. 164.11 ..
6.3.m: The charming water of the Narmadā, destroying all sins, / is especially beheld by the great-souled [god] of Sāṃvaura.

6.3.s:
te dhanyāste mahātmānasteṣāṃ janma sujīvitam .
snātvā paśyanti deveśaṃ sāṃvaureśvaramuttamam .. 164.12 ..
6.3.d:
ते धन्यास्ते महात्मानस्तेषां जन्म सुजीवितम् .
स्नात्वा पश्यन्ति देवेशं सांवौरेश्वरमुत्तमम् .. 164.12 ..
6.3.m: Fortunate are they, great-souled are they, and well-lived is their life, / who, having bathed, behold the supreme Lord of the gods, Sāṃvaureśvara.

6.3.s:
sūryaloke vasettāvadyāvadābhūtasamplavam .. 164.13 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe sāṃvaureśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma catuḥṣaṣṭyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 165
6.3.d:
सूर्यलोके वसेत्तावद्यावदाभूतसम्प्लवम् .. 164.13 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे सांवौरेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम चतुःषष्ट्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 165
6.3.m:
He shall dwell in the world of the sun until the dissolution of all beings.
Thus ends the one hundred and sixty-fourth chapter, named the Description of the Greatness of Sāṃvaureśvaratīrtha, in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses].
Chapter 165

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
narmadādakṣiṇe kūle siddheśvaramiti śrutam .
tīrthaṃ paraṃ mahārāja siddhaiḥ kṛtamiti prabho .. 165.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
नर्मदादक्षिणे कूले सिद्धेश्वरमिति श्रुतम् .
तीर्थं परं महाराज सिद्धैः कृतमिति प्रभो .. 165.1 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / On the southern bank of the Narmadā is that sacred ford famed as Siddheśvara, / an supreme sacred ford, O great king, created by the Siddhas, O lord.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ sarvatīrtheṣu pāvanam .
narmadāyā mahārāja dakṣiṇaṃ kūlamāśritam .. 165.2 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थं महापुण्यं सर्वतीर्थेषु पावनम् .
नर्मदाया महाराज दक्षिणं कूलमाश्रितम् .. 165.2 ..
6.3.m: There lies a greatly holy sacred ford, purifying among all sacred fords, / situated upon the southern bank of the Narmadā, O great king.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe naraḥ snātvā tarpayetpitṛdevatāḥ .
śrāddhaṃ tatraiva yo dadyātpitḥnuddiśya bhārata .. 165.3 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे नरः स्नात्वा तर्पयेत्पितृदेवताः .
श्राद्धं तत्रैव यो दद्यात्पित्ःनुद्दिश्य भारत .. 165.3 ..
6.3.m: Having bathed in that sacred ford, a person should offer libations to the ancestors and gods. / Whoever performs a śrāddha right there dedicated to the ancestors, O descendant of Bharata,

6.3.s:
tṛpyanti pitarastasya dvādaśābdānna saṃśayaḥ .
tatra tīrthe tu yo bhaktyā snātvā pūjayate śivam .. 165.4 ..
6.3.d:
तृप्यन्ति पितरस्तस्य द्वादशाब्दान्न संशयः .
तत्र तीर्थे तु यो भक्त्या स्नात्वा पूजयते शिवम् .. 165.4 ..
6.3.m: his ancestors remain satisfied for twelve years, there is no doubt. / Moreover, whoever, having bathed with devotion in that sacred ford, worships Śiva,

6.3.s:
rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kṛtvā paṭhetpaurāṇikīṃ kathām .
tataḥ prabhāte vimale snānaṃ kuryādyathāvidhi .. 165.5 ..
6.3.d:
रात्रौ जागरणं कृत्वा पठेत्पौराणिकीं कथाम् .
ततः प्रभाते विमले स्नानं कुर्याद्यथाविधि .. 165.5 ..
6.3.m: observing a night vigil and reciting a purāṇic tale, / and then, at pure dawn, performs a ritual ablution according to rule,

6.3.s:
vīkṣate girijākāntaṃ sa gacchetparamāṃ gatim .
purā siddhā mahābhāgāḥ kapilādyā maharṣayaḥ .. 165.6 ..
6.3.d:
वीक्षते गिरिजाकान्तं स गच्छेत्परमां गतिम् .
पुरा सिद्धा महाभागाः कपिलाद्या महर्षयः .. 165.6 ..
6.3.m: and beholds the beloved of Girijā, he goes to the supreme state. / In ancient times, the greatly fortunate Siddhas, Kapila and the other great seers,

6.3.s:
japantaśca paraṃ brahma yogasiddhā mahāvratāḥ .
siddhiṃ te paramāṃ prāptā narmadāyāḥ prabhāvataḥ .. 165.7 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe siddheśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma pañcaṣaṣṭyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 166
6.3.d:
जपन्तश्च परं ब्रह्म योगसिद्धा महाव्रताः .
सिद्धिं ते परमां प्राप्ता नर्मदायाः प्रभावतः .. 165.7 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे सिद्धेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम पञ्चषष्ट्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 166
6.3.m:
reciting the supreme Brahman, perfected in yoga and of great vows, / attained supreme perfection through the power of the Narmadā.
Thus ends the one hundred sixty-fifth chapter, named 'The Description of the Greatness of Siddheśvaratīrtha', in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses].
Chapter 166

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tataḥ siddheśvarī devī vaiṣṇavī pāpanāśinī .
ānandaṃ paramaṃ prāptā dṛṣṭvā sthānaṃ suśobhanam .. 166.1 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततः सिद्धेश्वरी देवी वैष्णवी पापनाशिनी .
आनन्दं परमं प्राप्ता दृष्ट्वा स्थानं सुशोभनम् .. 166.1 ..
6.3.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then the goddess Siddheśvarī, Vaiṣṇavī, destroyer of sins, / attained supreme joy upon beholding that very beautiful place.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe naraḥ snātvā pūjayetpitṛdevatāḥ .
devīṃ paśyati yo bhaktyā mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ .. 166.2 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे नरः स्नात्वा पूजयेत्पितृदेवताः .
देवीं पश्यति यो भक्त्या मुच्यते सर्वपातकैः .. 166.2 ..
6.3.m: Having bathed in that sacred ford, a person should worship the ancestors and gods. / Whoever beholds the goddess with devotion is freed from all sins.

6.3.s:
mṛtavatsā tu yā nārī vandhyā strījananī tathā .
putraṃ sā labhate nārī śīlavantaṃ guṇānvitam .. 166.3 ..
6.3.d:
मृतवत्सा तु या नारी वन्ध्या स्त्रीजननी तथा .
पुत्रं सा लभते नारी शीलवन्तं गुणान्वितम् .. 166.3 ..
6.3.m: A woman whose children have died, or a barren woman, or one who gives birth only to daughters, / that woman obtains a son endowed with good character and virtues.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ snātvā paśyeddevīṃ subhaktitaḥ .
aṣṭamyāṃ vā caturdaśyāṃ sarvakāle'thavā nṛpa .. 166.4 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः स्नात्वा पश्येद्देवीं सुभक्तितः .
अष्टम्यां वा चतुर्दश्यां सर्वकालेऽथवा नृप .. 166.4 ..
6.3.m: Whoever, having bathed in that sacred ford, beholds the goddess with profound devotion / on the eighth or the fourteenth [lunar day], or at any time, O king,

6.3.s:
saṅgame tu tataḥ snātā nārī vā puruṣo'pi vā .
putraṃ dhanaṃ tathā devī dadāti paritoṣitā .. 166.5 ..
6.3.d:
सङ्गमे तु ततः स्नाता नारी वा पुरुषोऽपि वा .
पुत्रं धनं तथा देवी ददाति परितोषिता .. 166.5 ..
6.3.m: whether a woman or a man who has bathed at the confluence there, / the goddess, well-pleased, grants them a son and wealth.

6.3.s:
gotrarakṣāṃ prakurute dṛṣṭā devī supūjitā .
prajāṃ ca pāti satataṃ pūjyamānā na saṃśayaḥ .. 166.6 ..
6.3.d:
गोत्ररक्षां प्रकुरुते दृष्टा देवी सुपूजिता .
प्रजां च पाति सततं पूज्यमाना न संशयः .. 166.6 ..
6.3.m: Beheld and well-worshipped, the goddess protects the lineage; / continually worshipped, she protects offspring, there is no doubt.

6.3.s:
navamyāṃ ca mahārāja snātvā devīmupoṣitaḥ .
pūjayetparayā bhaktyā śraddhāpūtena cetasā .. 166.7 ..
6.3.d:
नवम्यां च महाराज स्नात्वा देवीमुपोषितः .
पूजयेत्परया भक्त्या श्रद्धापूतेन चेतसा .. 166.7 ..
6.3.m: And having fasted and bathed on the ninth [day], O great king, / one should worship the goddess with supreme devotion and a mind purified by faith.

6.3.s:
sa gacchetparamaṃ lokaṃ yaḥ surairapi durlabhaḥ .. 166.8 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe siddheśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma ṣaṭṣaṣṭyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 167
6.3.d:
स गच्छेत्परमं लोकं यः सुरैरपि दुर्लभः .. 166.8 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे सिद्धेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम षट्षष्ट्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 167
6.3.m:
He goes to the supreme realm, which is difficult even for the gods to attain.
Thus ends the one hundred sixty-sixth chapter, named 'The Description of the Greatness of Siddheśvaratīrtha', in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses].
Chapter 167

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
narmadādakṣiṇe kūle tvaccihnenopalakṣitam .
tīrthametanmamākhyāhi sambhavaṃ ca mahāmune .. 167.1 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
नर्मदादक्षिणे कूले त्वच्चिह्नेनोपलक्षितम् .
तीर्थमेतन्ममाख्याहि सम्भवं च महामुने .. 167.1 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / On the southern bank of the Narmadā is a sacred ford marked by your sign; / tell me of this sacred ford and its origin, O great sage.

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
purā kṛtayugasyādau dakṣiṇe girimuttamam .
vindhyaṃ sarvaguṇopetaṃ niyato niyatāśanaḥ .. 167.2 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
पुरा कृतयुगस्यादौ दक्षिणे गिरिमुत्तमम् .
विन्ध्यं सर्वगुणोपेतं नियतो नियताशनः .. 167.2 ..
6.3.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Long ago, at the beginning of the Kṛta Yuga, on the excellent southern mountain, / the Vindhya, endowed with all virtues, self-restrained and limited in food,

6.3.s:
ṛṣisaṅghaiḥ kṛtātithyo daṇḍake nyavasaṃ ciram .
uṣitvā suciraṃ kālaṃ varṣāṇāmayutaṃ sukhī .. 167.3 ..
6.3.d:
ऋषिसङ्घैः कृतातिथ्यो दण्डके न्यवसं चिरम् .
उषित्वा सुचिरं कालं वर्षाणामयुतं सुखी .. 167.3 ..
6.3.m: offered hospitality by hosts of seers, I lived for a long time in Daṇḍaka. / Having resided there for a very long time, for ten thousand years, happy,

6.3.s:
tānṛṣīn samanujñāpya śiṣyairanugatastataḥ .
nivṛttaḥ sumahābhāga narmadākūlamāgataḥ .. 167.4 ..
6.3.d:
तानृषीन् समनुज्ञाप्य शिष्यैरनुगतस्ततः .
निवृत्तः सुमहाभाग नर्मदाकूलमागतः .. 167.4 ..
6.3.m: having taken leave of those seers and followed by disciples, / I departed, O greatly fortunate one, and came to the bank of the Narmadā,

6.3.s:
puṇyaṃ ca ramaṇīyaṃ ca sarvapāpavināśanam .
kṛtvāhamāspadaṃ tatra dvijasaṃghasamāyutaḥ .. 167.5 ..
6.3.d:
पुण्यं च रमणीयं च सर्वपापविनाशनम् .
कृत्वाहमास्पदं तत्र द्विजसंघसमायुतः .. 167.5 ..
6.3.m: which is holy, delightful, and the destroyer of all sins. / Having made my dwelling there, accompanied by a host of twice-born,

6.3.s:
brahmacāribhirākīrṇaṃ gārhasthye supratiṣṭhitaiḥ .
vānaprasthaiśca yatibhiryatāhārairyatātmabhiḥ .. 167.6 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रह्मचारिभिराकीर्णं गार्हस्थ्ये सुप्रतिष्ठितैः .
वानप्रस्थैश्च यतिभिर्यताहारैर्यतात्मभिः .. 167.6 ..
6.3.m: crowded with celibate students, those well-established in householdership, / forest dwellers, and ascetics of controlled diet and restrained self,

6.3.s:
tapasvibhirmahābhāgaiḥ kāmakrodhavivarjitaiḥ .
tatrāhaṃ varṣamayutaṃ tapaḥ kṛtvā sudāruṇam .. 167.7 ..
6.3.d:
तपस्विभिर्महाभागैः कामक्रोधविवर्जितैः .
तत्राहं वर्षमयुतं तपः कृत्वा सुदारुणम् .. 167.7 ..
6.3.m: greatly fortunate practitioners of austerities, free from desire and anger, / I performed very severe austerity there for ten thousand years,

6.3.s:
ārādhayaṃ vāsudevaṃ prabhuṃ kartāramīśvaram .
japaṃstapobhirniyamairnarmadākūlamāśritaḥ .. 167.8 ..
6.3.d:
आराधयं वासुदेवं प्रभुं कर्तारमीश्वरम् .
जपंस्तपोभिर्नियमैर्नर्मदाकूलमाश्रितः .. 167.8 ..
6.3.m: worshipping Vāsudeva, the lord, the creator, Īśvara, / with silent recitations, austerities, and observances, resorting to the bank of the Narmadā.

6.3.s:
tatastau varadau devau samāyātau yudhiṣṭhira .
pratyakṣau bhāskarau rājannumāśrībhyāṃ vibhūṣitau .. 167.9 ..
6.3.d:
ततस्तौ वरदौ देवौ समायातौ युधिष्ठिर .
प्रत्यक्षौ भास्करौ राजन्नुमाश्रीभ्यां विभूषितौ .. 167.9 ..
6.3.m: Then those two boon-granting gods arrived, O Yudhiṣṭhira, / manifest like two suns, O king, adorned by Umā and Śrī.

6.3.s:
praṇamyāhaṃ tato devau bhaktiyukto vaco'bruvam .
bhavantau prārthayāmi sma varārhau varadau śivau .. 167.10 ..
6.3.d:
प्रणम्याहं ततो देवौ भक्तियुक्तो वचोऽब्रुवम् .
भवन्तौ प्रार्थयामि स्म वरार्हौ वरदौ शिवौ .. 167.10 ..
6.3.m: Having bowed down then to the two gods, endowed with devotion, I spoke these words: / 'I pray to you both, worthy of granting boons, boon-bestowing, auspicious,

6.3.s:
dharmasthitiṃ mahābhāgau bhaktiṃ vānuttamāṃ yuvām .
ajaro vyādhirahitaḥ pañcaviṃśativarṣavat .
asminsthāne sadā stheyaṃ saha devairasaṃśayam .. 167.11 ..
6.3.d:
धर्मस्थितिं महाभागौ भक्तिं वानुत्तमां युवाम् .
अजरो व्याधिरहितः पञ्चविंशतिवर्षवत् .
अस्मिन्स्थाने सदा स्थेयं सह देवैरसंशयम् .. 167.11 ..
6.3.m: for the preservation of dharma, O greatly fortunate ones, and for unexcelled devotion to you both; / [that I remain] free of old age and disease, as if twenty-five years old, / and that you always remain in this place along with the gods, without doubt.'

6.3.s:
evamuktau mayā pārtha tau devau kṛṣṇaśaṅkarau .
māmūcatuḥ prahṛṣṭau tau nivāsārthaṃ yudhiṣṭhira .. 167.12 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्तौ मया पार्थ तौ देवौ कृष्णशङ्करौ .
मामूचतुः प्रहृष्टौ तौ निवासार्थं युधिष्ठिर .. 167.12 ..
6.3.m: Being thus addressed by me, O Pārtha, those two gods, Kṛṣṇa and Śaṅkara, / greatly pleased, spoke to me regarding their dwelling, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

6.3.s:
devāvūcatuḥ .
asminsthāne sthitau viddhi saha devaiḥ savāsavaiḥ .
evamuktvā tato devau tatraivāntaradhīyatām .. 167.13 ..
6.3.d:
देवावूचतुः .
अस्मिन्स्थाने स्थितौ विद्धि सह देवैः सवासवैः .
एवमुक्त्वा ततो देवौ तत्रैवान्तरधीयताम् .. 167.13 ..
6.3.m: The two gods said: / 'Know that we remain in this place along with the gods and Indra.' / Having spoken thus, the two gods then vanished right there.

6.3.s:
ahaṃ ca sthāpayitvā tau śaṅkaraṃ kṛṣṇamavyayam .
kṛtakṛtyastato jātaḥ sampūjya susamāhitaḥ .. 167.14 ..
6.3.d:
अहं च स्थापयित्वा तौ शङ्करं कृष्णमव्ययम् .
कृतकृत्यस्ततो जातः सम्पूज्य सुसमाहितः .. 167.14 ..
6.3.m: And having established them both, Śaṅkara and the imperishable Kṛṣṇa, / and worshipped them with complete concentration, I was then fulfilled.

6.3.s:
tasmiṃstīrthe naraḥ snātvā pūjayetparameśvaram .
mārkaṇḍeśvaranāmnā vai viṣṇuṃ tribhuvaneśvaram .. 167.15 ..
6.3.d:
तस्मिंस्तीर्थे नरः स्नात्वा पूजयेत्परमेश्वरम् .
मार्कण्डेश्वरनाम्ना वै विष्णुं त्रिभुवनेश्वरम् .. 167.15 ..
6.3.m: A person having bathed in that sacred ford should worship the supreme lord, / Viṣṇu, lord of the three worlds, under the name Mārkaṇḍeśvara.

6.3.s:
sa gacchetparamaṃ sthānaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ śaivameva ca .
ghṛtena payasā vātha dadhnā ca madhunā tathā .. 167.16 ..
6.3.d:
स गच्छेत्परमं स्थानं वैष्णवं शैवमेव च .
घृतेन पयसा वाथ दध्ना च मधुना तथा .. 167.16 ..
6.3.m: He goes to the supreme realm, both Vaiṣṇava and Śaiva. / With ghee, milk, or curd and honey,

6.3.s:
nārmadenodakenātha gandhadhūpaiḥ suśobhanaiḥ .
puṣpopahāraiśca tathā naivedyairniyatātmavān .. 167.17 ..
6.3.d:
नार्मदेनोदकेनाथ गन्धधूपैः सुशोभनैः .
पुष्पोपहारैश्च तथा नैवेद्यैर्नियतात्मवान् .. 167.17 ..
6.3.m: and with water from the Narmadā, with very beautiful scents and incenses, / offerings of flowers, and food offerings, self-controlled,

6.3.s:
evaṃ viṣṇoḥ prakurvīta jāgaraṃ bhaktitatparaḥ .
snānādīni tathā rājanprayataḥ śucimānasaḥ .. 167.18 ..
6.3.d:
एवं विष्णोः प्रकुर्वीत जागरं भक्तितत्परः .
स्नानादीनि तथा राजन्प्रयतः शुचिमानसः .. 167.18 ..
6.3.m: thus devoted to Viṣṇu, he should keep a vigil with intent devotion; / likewise [performing] ritual ablutions and the like, O king, restrained and of pure mind.

6.3.s:
jyeṣṭhe māsi site pakṣe caturdaśyāmupoṣitaḥ .
dvādaśyāṃ kārayeddevapūjanaṃ vaiṣṇavo naraḥ .. 167.19 ..
6.3.d:
ज्येष्ठे मासि सिते पक्षे चतुर्दश्यामुपोषितः .
द्वादश्यां कारयेद्देवपूजनं वैष्णवो नरः .. 167.19 ..
6.3.m: Having fasted on the fourteenth of the bright half in the month of Jyeṣṭha, / a Vaiṣṇava man should have worship of the gods performed on the twelfth.

6.3.s:
evaṃ kṛtvā caturdaśyāmekādaśyāṃ narottama .
vaiṣṇavaṃ lokamāpnoti viṣṇutulyo bhavennaraḥ .. 167.20 ..
6.3.d:
एवं कृत्वा चतुर्दश्यामेकादश्यां नरोत्तम .
वैष्णवं लोकमाप्नोति विष्णुतुल्यो भवेन्नरः .. 167.20 ..
6.3.m: Having done so on the fourteenth or the eleventh, O best of men, / a man attains the realm of Viṣṇu and becomes equal to Viṣṇu.

6.3.s:
māheśvare ca rājendra gaṇavanmodate pure .
śrāddhaṃ ca kurute tatra pitṝnuddiśya susthiraḥ .. 167.21 ..
6.3.d:
माहेश्वरे च राजेन्द्र गणवन्मोदते पुरे .
श्राद्धं च कुरुते तत्र पितॄनुद्दिश्य सुस्थिरः .. 167.21 ..
6.3.m: And in the city of Maheśvara, O king of kings, he rejoices like a gaṇa. / And if, steadfast, he performs a śrāddha there dedicated to his ancestors,

6.3.s:
tasya te hyakṣayāṃ tṛptiṃ prāpnuvanti na saṃśayaḥ .
narmadāyāṃ dvijaḥ snātvā maunī niyatamānasaḥ .. 167.22 ..
6.3.d:
तस्य ते ह्यक्षयां तृप्तिं प्राप्नुवन्ति न संशयः .
नर्मदायां द्विजः स्नात्वा मौनी नियतमानसः .. 167.22 ..
6.3.m: they obtain inexhaustible satisfaction, there is no doubt. / A twice-born, having bathed in the Narmadā, silent, with restrained mind,

6.3.s:
upāsya sandhyāṃ tatrastho japaṃ kṛtvā suśobhanam .
tarpayitvā pitṝndevānmanuṣyāṃśca yathāvidhi .. 167.23 ..
6.3.d:
उपास्य सन्ध्यां तत्रस्थो जपं कृत्वा सुशोभनम् .
तर्पयित्वा पितॄन्देवान्मनुष्यांश्च यथाविधि .. 167.23 ..
6.3.m: having observed the twilight devotion while standing there, performing excellent recitation, / and having offered libations to ancestors, gods, and men according to rule,

6.3.s:
kṛṣṇasya purataḥ sthitvā mārkaṇḍeśasya vā punaḥ .
ṛgyajuḥsāmamantrāṃśca japedatra prayatnataḥ .. 167.24 ..
6.3.d:
कृष्णस्य पुरतः स्थित्वा मार्कण्डेशस्य वा पुनः .
ऋग्यजुःसाममन्त्रांश्च जपेदत्र प्रयत्नतः .. 167.24 ..
6.3.m: standing before Kṛṣṇa or Mārkaṇḍeśa, / should diligently recite verses from the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma Vedas here.

6.3.s:
ṛcamekāṃ japedyastu ṛgvedasya phalaṃ labhet .
yajurvedasya yajuṣā sāmnā sāmaphalaṃ labhet .. 167.25 ..
6.3.d:
ऋचमेकां जपेद्यस्तु ऋग्वेदस्य फलं लभेत् .
यजुर्वेदस्य यजुषा साम्ना सामफलं लभेत् .. 167.25 ..
6.3.m: Whoever chants a single ṛc obtains the fruit of the Ṛgveda; / through a yajus, [the fruit] of the Yajurveda; through a sāman, he obtains the fruit of the Sāmaveda.

6.3.s:
ekasminbhojite vipre koṭirbhavati bhojitā .
mṛtaprajā tu yā nārī vandhyā strījananī tathā .. 167.26 ..
6.3.d:
एकस्मिन्भोजिते विप्रे कोटिर्भवति भोजिता .
मृतप्रजा तु या नारी वन्ध्या स्त्रीजननी तथा .. 167.26 ..
6.3.m: When a single vipra is fed, ten million are fed. / A woman whose children have died, or who is barren, or who gives birth only to daughters,

6.3.s:
rudrāṃstu vidhivajjaptvā brāhmaṇo vedatattvavit .
liṅgasya dakṣiṇe pārśve sthāpayetkalaśaṃ śivam .. 167.27 ..
6.3.d:
रुद्रांस्तु विधिवज्जप्त्वा ब्राह्मणो वेदतत्त्ववित् .
लिङ्गस्य दक्षिणे पार्श्वे स्थापयेत्कलशं शिवम् .. 167.27 ..
6.3.m: — for her, a brahmin knowing the truth of the Veda, having properly recited the Rudra [mantras], / should set up an auspicious water pot on the right side of the liṅga.

6.3.s:
rudraikādaśabhirmantraiḥ snāpayetkalaśāmbhasā .
putramāpnoti rājendra dīrghāyuṣamakalmaṣam .. 167.28 ..
6.3.d:
रुद्रैकादशभिर्मन्त्रैः स्नापयेत्कलशाम्भसा .
पुत्रमाप्नोति राजेन्द्र दीर्घायुषमकल्मषम् .. 167.28 ..
6.3.m: He should bathe [it] with the water from the pot using the eleven Rudra mantras. / [Then] she obtains, O king of kings, a long-lived and faultless son.

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeśvaravṛkṣānyo dūrasthānapi paśyati .
brahmahatyādipāpebhyo mucyate śaṅkaro'bravīt .. 167.29 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेश्वरवृक्षान्यो दूरस्थानपि पश्यति .
ब्रह्महत्यादिपापेभ्यो मुच्यते शङ्करोऽब्रवीत् .. 167.29 ..
6.3.m: Whoever sees the trees of Mārkaṇḍeśvara, even from afar, / is freed from sins such as killing a brahmin; so Śaṃkara declared.

6.3.s:
ya idaṃ śṛṇuyādbhaktyā paṭhedvā nṛpasattama .
sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 167.30 ..
6.3.d:
य इदं शृणुयाद्भक्त्या पठेद्वा नृपसत्तम .
सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा जायते नात्र संशयः .. 167.30 ..
6.3.m: Whoever hears this with devotion or recites it, O best of kings, / becomes purified of all sins; of this there is no doubt.

6.3.s:
idaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ dhanyaṃ duḥkhapraṇāśanam .
paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ vāpi sarvapāpapramocanam .. 167.31 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe mārkaṇḍeśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma saptaṣaṣṭyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
adhyāya 168
6.3.d:
इदं यशस्यमायुष्यं धन्यं दुःखप्रणाशनम् .
पठतां शृण्वतां वापि सर्वपापप्रमोचनम् .. 167.31 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे मार्कण्डेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम सप्तषष्ट्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः ..
अध्याय 168
