परा सिद्धिरनुप्राप्ता द्वादशादित्यसंज्ञितैः .
स्थापितश्च जगद्धाता तस्मिंस्तीर्थे दिवाकरः .. 191.10 ..
6.3.m: known as the twelve Ādityas, supreme perfection was achieved. / And the Sun, creator of the world, was installed at that sacred ford 191.10

6.3.s:
svakīyāṃśavibhāgena dvādaśādityasaṃjñitaiḥ .
tadāprabhṛti tattīrthaṃ rājankhyātiṃ gataṃ bhuvi .. 191.11 ..
6.3.d:
स्वकीयांशविभागेन द्वादशादित्यसंज्ञितैः .
तदाप्रभृति तत्तीर्थं राजन्ख्यातिं गतं भुवि .. 191.11 ..
6.3.m: by those known as the twelve Ādityas through the division of their own portions. / Thenceforth, O king, that sacred ford became renowned on earth. 191.11

6.3.s:
pralaye samanuprāpte hyādityā dvādaśaiva te .
dvādaśādityato rājan sambhavanti yugakṣaye .. 191.12 ..
6.3.d:
प्रलये समनुप्राप्ते ह्यादित्या द्वादशैव ते .
द्वादशादित्यतो राजन् सम्भवन्ति युगक्षये .. 191.12 ..
6.3.m: When dissolution arrives, those twelve Ādityas indeed / arise from Dvādaśāditya at the end of the age, O king. 191.12

6.3.s:
indrastapati pūrveṇa dhātā caivāgnigocare .
gabhastipatirvai yāmye tvaṣṭā nairṛtadiṅmukhaḥ .. 191.13 ..
6.3.d:
इन्द्रस्तपति पूर्वेण धाता चैवाग्निगोचरे .
गभस्तिपतिर्वै याम्ये त्वष्टा नैरृतदिङ्मुखः .. 191.13 ..
6.3.m: Indra shines in the east, and Dhātṛ in the southeast; / Gabhastipati shines in the south, Tvaṣṭṛ facing the southwest; 191.13

6.3.s:
varuṇaḥ paścime bhāge mitrastu vāyave tathā .
viṣṇuśca saumyadigbhāge vivasvānīśagocare .. 191.14 ..
6.3.d:
वरुणः पश्चिमे भागे मित्रस्तु वायवे तथा .
विष्णुश्च सौम्यदिग्भागे विवस्वानीशगोचरे .. 191.14 ..
6.3.m: Varuṇa in the western quarter, and Mitra in the northwest; / Viṣṇu in the northern quarter, and Vivasvat in the northeast; 191.14

6.3.s:
ūrdhvataścaiva savitā hyadhaḥ pūṣā viśoṣayan .
aṃśumāṃstu tathā viṣṇurmukhato nirgataṃ jagat .. 191.15 ..
6.3.d:
ऊर्ध्वतश्चैव सविता ह्यधः पूषा विशोषयन् .
अंशुमांस्तु तथा विष्णुर्मुखतो निर्गतं जगत् .. 191.15 ..
6.3.m: Savitṛ above, and below Pūṣan desiccating [all]; / Aṃśumat and Viṣṇu—[all] issued forth from the mouth of the universe, 191.15

6.3.s:
pradahanvai naraśreṣṭha babhramuśca itastataḥ .
yathaiva te mahārāja dahanti sakalaṃ jagat .. 191.16 ..
6.3.d:
प्रदहन्वै नरश्रेष्ठ बभ्रमुश्च इतस्ततः .
यथैव ते महाराज दहन्ति सकलं जगत् .. 191.16 ..
6.3.m: burning [everything], O best of men, and roamed here and there. / Just as they burn the entire universe, O great king, 191.16

6.3.s:
tathaiva dvādaśādityā bhaktānāṃ bhāvasādhanāḥ .
prātarutthāya yaḥ snātvā dvādaśādityasaṃjñitam .. 191.17 ..
6.3.d:
तथैव द्वादशादित्या भक्तानां भावसाधनाः .
प्रातरुत्थाय यः स्नात्वा द्वादशादित्यसंज्ञितम् .. 191.17 ..
6.3.m: so the twelve Ādityas accomplish the heartfelt desires of their devotees. / Having risen at dawn and bathed, whoever beholds the lord of the gods, 191.17

6.3.s:
paśyate devadeveśaṃ śṛṇu tasyaiva yatphalam .
vācikaṃ mānasaṃ pāpaṃ karmajaṃ yatpurākṛtam .. 191.18 ..
6.3.d:
पश्यते देवदेवेशं शृणु तस्यैव यत्फलम् .
वाचिकं मानसं पापं कर्मजं यत्पुराकृतम् .. 191.18 ..
6.3.m: who is known as Dvādaśāditya—hear the fruit thereof! / Vocal, mental, or born of action—whatever sin was committed in the past 191.18

6.3.s:
naśyate tatkṣaṇādeva dvādaśādityadarśanāt .
pradakṣiṇaṃ tu yaḥ kuryāttasya devasya bhārata .. 191.19 ..
6.3.d:
नश्यते तत्क्षणादेव द्वादशादित्यदर्शनात् .
प्रदक्षिणं तु यः कुर्यात्तस्य देवस्य भारत .. 191.19 ..
6.3.m: perishes at that very moment upon the darśana of Dvādaśāditya. / And whoever performs circumambulation of that deity, O descendant of Bharata, 191.19

6.3.s:
pradakṣiṇīkṛtā tena pṛthivī nātra saṃśayaḥ .
tatra tīrthe tu saptamyāmupavāsena yatphalam .. 191.20 ..
6.3.d:
प्रदक्षिणीकृता तेन पृथिवी नात्र संशयः .
तत्र तीर्थे तु सप्तम्यामुपवासेन यत्फलम् .. 191.20 ..
6.3.m: by him the earth has been circumambulated, without doubt. / Whatever fruit is obtained by fasting on the seventh lunar day at that sacred ford, 191.20

6.3.s:
anyatra saptasaptamyāṃ labhanti na labhanti ca .
ṣaṣṭhyāṃ vāre dainakare dvādaśādityadarśanāt .. 191.21 ..
6.3.d:
अन्यत्र सप्तसप्तम्यां लभन्ति न लभन्ति च .
षष्ठ्यां वारे दैनकरे द्वादशादित्यदर्शनात् .. 191.21 ..
6.3.m: one may or may not obtain elsewhere even in seven seventh lunar days. / On a Sunday that coincides with a sixth lunar day, by the darśana of Dvādaśāditya, 191.21

6.3.s:
pradakṣiṇaṃ tu yaḥ kuryāttasya pāpaṃ tu naśyati .
arogī saptajanmāni bhavedvai nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 191.22 ..
6.3.d:
प्रदक्षिणं तु यः कुर्यात्तस्य पापं तु नश्यति .
अरोगी सप्तजन्मानि भवेद्वै नात्र संशयः .. 191.22 ..
6.3.m: the sin of whoever performs circumambulation is destroyed. / For seven lifetimes he will be free from disease, without doubt. 191.22

6.3.s:
yastu pradakṣiṇaśataṃ dadyādbhaktyā dine dine .
dadrūpiṭakakuṣṭhāni maṇḍalāni vicarcikāḥ .. 191.23 ..
6.3.d:
यस्तु प्रदक्षिणशतं दद्याद्भक्त्या दिने दिने .
दद्रूपिटककुष्ठानि मण्डलानि विचर्चिकाः .. 191.23 ..
6.3.m: And he who devoutly gives a hundred circumambulations day after day— / ringworm, boils, leprosy, blotches, and scabies: 191.23

6.3.s:
naśyanti vyādhayaḥ sarve garuḍeneva pannagāḥ .
putraprāptirbhavettasya ṣaṣṭyā vāsarasevanāt .. 191.24 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe dvādaśādityatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmaikanavatyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
6.3.d:
नश्यन्ति व्याधयः सर्वे गरुडेनेव पन्नगाः .
पुत्रप्राप्तिर्भवेत्तस्य षष्ट्या वासरसेवनात् .. 191.24 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे द्वादशादित्यतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामैकनवत्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः ..
6.3.m:
all diseases perish, as serpents by Garuḍa. / He obtains a son by serving [the deity] on the sixth lunar day. 191.24
Thus ends the one hundred and ninety-first chapter, named 'The Description of the Māhātmya of Dvādaśādityatīrtha', in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses].

6.3.s:
adhyāya 192
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tasyaivānantaraṃ tāta devatīrthamanuttamam .
dṛṣṭvā tu śrīpatiṃ pāpairmucyate mānavo bhuvi .. 192.1 ..
6.3.d:
अध्याय 192
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
तस्यैवानन्तरं तात देवतीर्थमनुत्तमम् .
दृष्ट्वा तु श्रीपतिं पापैर्मुच्यते मानवो भुवि .. 192.1 ..
6.3.m:
Chapter 192
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Immediately next to it, my dear, is Devatīrtha, second to none. / Having seen the Lord of Śrī, a mortal on earth is freed from sins. 192.1

6.3.s: maharṣestasya jāmātā bhṛgordevo janārdanaḥ .. 192.2 ..
6.3.d: महर्षेस्तस्य जामाता भृगोर्देवो जनार्दनः .. 192.2 ..
6.3.m: The god Janārdana is the son-in-law of that great seer Bhṛgu. 192.2

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
ko'yaṃ śriyaḥ patirdevo devānāmadhipo vibhuḥ .
kathaṃ janmābhavattasya deveṣu triṣu vā mune .. 192.3 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
कोऽयं श्रियः पतिर्देवो देवानामधिपो विभुः .
कथं जन्माभवत्तस्य देवेषु त्रिषु वा मुने .. 192.3 ..
6.3.m:
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
Who is this god, the Lord of Śrī, sovereign ruler of the gods, the all-pervading lord? / How did his birth come about among the three gods, O sage? 192.3

6.3.s:
sambandhī ca kathaṃ jāto bhṛguṇā saha keśavaḥ .
etadvistarato brahman vaktumarhasi bhārgava .. 192.4 ..
6.3.d:
सम्बन्धी च कथं जातो भृगुणा सह केशवः .
एतद्विस्तरतो ब्रह्मन् वक्तुमर्हसि भार्गव .. 192.4 ..
6.3.m: And how did Keśava become a relation of Bhṛgu? / You ought to tell this in detail, O holy descendant of Bhṛgu. 192.4

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
saṃkṣepātkathayiṣyāmi sādhyasya caritaṃ mahat .
na hi vistarato vaktuṃ śaktāḥ sarve maharṣayaḥ .. 192.5 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
संक्षेपात्कथयिष्यामि साध्यस्य चरितं महत् .
न हि विस्तरतो वक्तुं शक्ताः सर्वे महर्षयः .. 192.5 ..
6.3.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
I shall tell briefly the great life of the Sādhya; / for not all the great seers together are capable of narrating it in full detail. 192.5

6.3.s:
nārāyaṇasya nābhyabjājjāto devaścaturmukhaḥ .
tasya dakṣo'ṅgajo rājan dakṣiṇāṅguṣṭhasambhavaḥ .. 192.6 ..
6.3.d:
नारायणस्य नाभ्यब्जाज्जातो देवश्चतुर्मुखः .
तस्य दक्षोऽङ्गजो राजन् दक्षिणाङ्गुष्ठसम्भवः .. 192.6 ..
6.3.m: From the navel-lotus of Nārāyaṇa was born the four-faced god [Brahmā]. / Born of his limb was Dakṣa, O king, originating from the right thumb. 192.6

6.3.s:
dharmaḥ stanāntātsaṃjātastasya putro'bhavatkila .
nārāyaṇasahāyo'sāvajo'pi bharatarṣabha .. 192.7 ..
6.3.d:
धर्मः स्तनान्तात्संजातस्तस्य पुत्रोऽभवत्किल .
नारायणसहायोऽसावजोऽपि भरतर्षभ .. 192.7 ..
6.3.m: From the area of his chest Dharma was born, who became his son. / He is the companion of Nārāyaṇa, though unborn, O bull of the Bharatas. 192.7

6.3.s:
marutvatī vasurjñānā lambā bhānumatī satī .
saṃkalpā ca muhūrtā ca sādhyā viśvāvatī kakup .. 192.8 ..
6.3.d:
मरुत्वती वसुर्ज्ञाना लम्बा भानुमती सती .
संकल्पा च मुहूर्ता च साध्या विश्वावती ककुप् .. 192.8 ..
6.3.m: Marutvatī, Vasu, Jñānā, Lambā, Bhānumatī, Satī, / Saṃkalpā, and Muhūrtā, Sādhyā, Viśvāvatī, [and] Kakubh— 192.8

6.3.s:
dharmapatnyo daśaivaitā dākṣāyaṇyo mahāprabhāḥ .
tāsāṃ sādhyā mahābhāgā putrānajanayannṛpa .. 192.9 ..
6.3.d:
धर्मपत्न्यो दशैवैता दाक्षायण्यो महाप्रभाः .
तासां साध्या महाभागा पुत्रानजनयन्नृप .. 192.9 ..
6.3.m: these ten daughters of Dakṣa of great splendour were the wives of Dharma. / Among them, the highly blessed Sādhyā gave birth to sons, O king. 192.9

6.3.s:
naro nārāyaṇaścaiva hariḥ kṛṣṇastathaiva ca .
viṣṇoraṃśāṃśakā hyete catvāro dharmasūnavaḥ .. 192.10 ..
6.3.d:
नरो नारायणश्चैव हरिः कृष्णस्तथैव च .
विष्णोरंशांशका ह्येते चत्वारो धर्मसूनवः .. 192.10 ..
6.3.m: Nara, Nārāyaṇa, Hari, and likewise Kṛṣṇa: / these are the four sons of Dharma, portions of a portion of Viṣṇu.

6.3.s:
tathā nārāyaṇanarau gandhamādanaparvate .
ātmanyātmānamādhāya tepatuḥ paramaṃ tapaḥ .. 192.11 ..
6.3.d:
तथा नारायणनरौ गन्धमादनपर्वते .
आत्मन्यात्मानमाधाय तेपतुः परमं तपः .. 192.11 ..
6.3.m: Then Nārāyaṇa and Nara, on Mount Gandhamādana, / fixing the self upon the Self, performed supreme austerity,

6.3.s:
dhyāyamānāvanaupamyaṃ svaṃ kāraṇamakāraṇam .
vāsudevamanirdeśyamapratarkyamanantaram .. 192.12 ..
6.3.d:
ध्यायमानावनौपम्यं स्वं कारणमकारणम् .
वासुदेवमनिर्देश्यमप्रतर्क्यमनन्तरम् .. 192.12 ..
6.3.m: Meditating on their own uncaused cause, incomparable, / Vāsudeva, undefinable, unthinkable, without boundary,

6.3.s:
yogayuktau mahātmānāvāsthitāvurutāpasau .
tayostapaḥprabhāveṇa na tatāpa divākaraḥ .. 192.13 ..
6.3.d:
योगयुक्तौ महात्मानावास्थितावुरुतापसौ .
तयोस्तपःप्रभावेण न तताप दिवाकरः .. 192.13 ..
6.3.m: Engaged in yoga, the two great souls stood firm in intense austerity. / Through the power of their austerity, the sun did not burn hot,

6.3.s:
vavāha śaṅkito vāyuḥ sukhasparśo hyaśaṅkitaḥ .
śiśiro'bhavadatyarthaṃ jvalannapi vibhāvasuḥ .. 192.14 ..
6.3.d:
ववाह शङ्कितो वायुः सुखस्पर्शो ह्यशङ्कितः .
शिशिरोऽभवदत्यर्थं ज्वलन्नपि विभावसुः .. 192.14 ..
6.3.m: The wind blew timidly, yet felt pleasant to the touch when untroubled; / and fire, though blazing, became exceedingly cool.

6.3.s:
siṃhavyāghrādayaḥ saumyāśceruḥ saha mṛgairgirau .
tayorgauriva bhārārtā pṛthivī pṛthivīpate .. 192.15 ..
6.3.d:
सिंहव्याघ्रादयः सौम्याश्चेरुः सह मृगैर्गिरौ .
तयोर्गौरिव भारार्ता पृथिवी पृथिवीपते .. 192.15 ..
6.3.m: Lions, tigers, and other beasts roamed peacefully together with deer on the mountain. / Oppressed by their weight, O lord of the earth, the earth [groaned] like a cow;

6.3.s:
ceruśca bhūdharāścaiva cukṣubhe ca mahodadhiḥ .
devāśca sveṣu dhiṣṇyeṣu niṣprabheṣu hataprabhāḥ .
babhūvuravanīpāla paramaṃ kṣobhamāgatāḥ .. 192.16 ..
6.3.d:
चेरुश्च भूधराश्चैव चुक्षुभे च महोदधिः .
देवाश्च स्वेषु धिष्ण्येषु निष्प्रभेषु हतप्रभाः .
बभूवुरवनीपाल परमं क्षोभमागताः .. 192.16 ..
6.3.m: The mountains trembled, and the great ocean was agitated. / The gods in their abodes, robbed of their luster and grown dim, / fell into great agitation, O protector of the earth.

6.3.s:
devarājastathā śakraḥ saṃtaptastapasā tayoḥ .
yuyojāpsarasastatra tayorvighnacikīrṣayā .. 192.17 ..
6.3.d:
देवराजस्तथा शक्रः संतप्तस्तपसा तयोः .
युयोजाप्सरसस्तत्र तयोर्विघ्नचिकीर्षया .. 192.17 ..
6.3.m: Then Śakra, king of the gods, tormented by their austerity, / dispatched the apsarases there, wishing to cause an obstacle to them both.

6.3.s:
indra uvāca -
rambhe tilottame kubje ghṛtāci lalite śubhe .
pramloce subhru sumloce saurabheyi mahoddhate .. 192.18 ..
6.3.d:
इन्द्र उवाच -
रम्भे तिलोत्तमे कुब्जे घृताचि ललिते शुभे .
प्रम्लोचे सुभ्रु सुम्लोचे सौरभेयि महोद्धते .. 192.18 ..
6.3.m: Indra said: / 'O Rambhā, Tilottamā, Kubjā, Ghṛtācī, Lalitā, Śubhā, / Pramlocā, O fair-browed Sumlocā, Saurabheyī, highly proud one,

6.3.s:
alambuṣe miśrakeśi puṇḍarīke varūthini .
vilokanīyaṃ bibhrāṇā vapurmanmathabodhanam .. 192.19 ..
6.3.d:
अलम्बुषे मिश्रकेशि पुण्डरीके वरूथिनि .
विलोकनीयं बिभ्राणा वपुर्मन्मथबोधनम् .. 192.19 ..
6.3.m: Alambuṣā, Miśrakeśī, Puṇḍarīkā, Varūthinī! / Displaying a lovely form that awakens love,

6.3.s:
gandhamādanamāsādya kurudhvaṃ vacanaṃ mama .
naranārāyaṇau tatra tapodīkṣānvitau dvijau .. 192.20 ..
6.3.d:
गन्धमादनमासाद्य कुरुध्वं वचनं मम .
नरनारायणौ तत्र तपोदीक्षान्वितौ द्विजौ .. 192.20 ..
6.3.m: Go to Gandhamādana and do my bidding. / There Nara and Nārāyaṇa, two twice-born consecrated to austerity,

6.3.s:
tepāte dharmatanayau tapaḥ paramaduścaram .
tāvasmākaṃ varārohāḥ kurvāṇau paramaṃ tapaḥ .. 192.21 ..
6.3.d:
तेपाते धर्मतनयौ तपः परमदुश्चरम् .
तावस्माकं वरारोहाः कुर्वाणौ परमं तपः .. 192.21 ..
6.3.m: The two sons of Dharma, are performing austerity exceedingly difficult to practice. / For us, O fair-hipped women, they, practicing supreme austerity,

6.3.s:
karmātiśayaduḥkhārtipradāvāyatināśanau .
tadgacchata na bhīḥ kāryā bhavatībhiridaṃ vacaḥ .. 192.22 ..
6.3.d:
कर्मातिशयदुःखार्तिप्रदावायतिनाशनौ .
तद्गच्छत न भीः कार्या भवतीभिरिदं वचः .. 192.22 ..
6.3.m: Inflict suffering and anguish through the excess of their rites, destroying our future. / Therefore go; you should feel no fear. [Hear] this word:

6.3.s:
smaraḥ sahāyo bhavitā vasantaśca varāṅganāḥ .
rūpaṃ vayaḥ samālokya madanoddīpanaṃ param .
kandarpavaśamabhyeti vivaśaḥ ko na mānavaḥ .. 192.23 ..
6.3.d:
स्मरः सहायो भविता वसन्तश्च वराङ्गनाः .
रूपं वयः समालोक्य मदनोद्दीपनं परम् .
कन्दर्पवशमभ्येति विवशः को न मानवः .. 192.23 ..
6.3.m: Smara will be your ally, and the spring season too, O lovely women! / Seeing your beauty and youth, which supremely kindle passion, / what man does not succumb helplessly to the power of Kandarpa?'

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
ityuktvā devarājena madanena samaṃ tadā .
jagmurapsarasaḥ sarvā vasantaśca mahīpate .. 192.24 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
इत्युक्त्वा देवराजेन मदनेन समं तदा .
जग्मुरप्सरसः सर्वा वसन्तश्च महीपते .. 192.24 ..
6.3.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having been thus addressed by the king of the gods, along with Madana, / all the apsarases and Spring went forth at that time, O lord of the earth.

6.3.s:
gandhamādanamāsādya puṃskokilakulākulam .
cacāra mādhavo ramyaṃ protphullavanapādapam .. 192.25 ..
6.3.d:
गन्धमादनमासाद्य पुंस्कोकिलकुलाकुलम् .
चचार माधवो रम्यं प्रोत्फुल्लवनपादपम् .. 192.25 ..
6.3.m: Arriving at Gandhamādana, teeming with flocks of male cuckoos, / Spring ranged through the lovely [mountain] whose forest trees were in full bloom.

6.3.s:
pravavau dakṣiṇāśāyāṃ malayānugato'nilaḥ .
bhṛṅgamālārutaravai ramaṇīyamabhūdvanam .. 192.26 ..
6.3.d:
प्रववौ दक्षिणाशायां मलयानुगतोऽनिलः .
भृङ्गमालारुतरवै रमणीयमभूद्वनम् .. 192.26 ..
6.3.m: In the southern quarter, a breeze blew from the Malaya hills; / the forest became delightful with the buzzing sounds of swarms of bees.

6.3.s:
gandhaśca surabhiḥ sadyo vanarājisamudbhavaḥ .
kinnaroragayakṣāṇāṃ babhūva ghrāṇatarpaṇaḥ .. 192.27 ..
6.3.d:
गन्धश्च सुरभिः सद्यो वनराजिसमुद्भवः .
किन्नरोरगयक्षाणां बभूव घ्राणतर्पणः .. 192.27 ..
6.3.m: And a fragrant scent, rising freshly from the forest groves, / brought delight to the nostrils of Kinnaras, Uragas, and Yakṣas.

6.3.s:
varāṅganāśca tāḥ sarvā naranārāyaṇāvṛṣī .
vilobhayitumārabdhā vāgaṅgalalitasmitaiḥ .. 192.28 ..
6.3.d:
वराङ्गनाश्च ताः सर्वा नरनारायणावृषी .
विलोभयितुमारब्धा वागङ्गललितस्मितैः .. 192.28 ..
6.3.m: And all those lovely women began to entice / the two seers, Nara and Nārāyaṇa, with words, bodily charms, and graceful smiles.

6.3.s:
jagau manoharaṃ kācinnanarta tatra cāpsarāḥ .
avādayattathaivānyā manoharataraṃ nṛpa .. 192.29 ..
6.3.d:
जगौ मनोहरं काचिन्ननर्त तत्र चाप्सराः .
अवादयत्तथैवान्या मनोहरतरं नृप .. 192.29 ..
6.3.m: One sang charmingly, and an apsaras danced there; / another played [instruments] still more delightfully, O king.

6.3.s:
hāvairbhāvaiḥ sṛtairhāsyaistathānyā valgubhāṣitaiḥ .
tayoḥ kṣobhāya tanvaṅgyaścakrurudyamamaṅganāḥ .. 192.30 ..
6.3.d:
हावैर्भावैः सृतैर्हास्यैस्तथान्या वल्गुभाषितैः .
तयोः क्षोभाय तन्वङ्ग्यश्चक्रुरुद्यममङ्गनाः .. 192.30 ..
6.3.m: With coquettish gestures, emotional expressions, flowing smiles, and sweet speech, / the slender-limbed women made an effort to agitate them both.

6.3.s:
tathāpi na tayoḥ kaścinmanasaḥ pṛthivīpate .
vikāro'bhavadadhyātmapārasamprāptacetasoḥ .. 192.31 ..
6.3.d:
तथापि न तयोः कश्चिन्मनसः पृथिवीपते .
विकारोऽभवदध्यात्मपारसम्प्राप्तचेतसोः .. 192.31 ..
6.3.m: Even so, no perturbation arose in the minds of the two, / O lord of the earth, their consciousness having reached the far shore of the Self.

6.3.s:
nivātasthau yathā dīpāvakampau nṛpa tiṣṭhataḥ .
vāsudevārpaṇasvasthe tathaiva manasī tayoḥ .. 192.32 ..
6.3.d:
निवातस्थौ यथा दीपावकम्पौ नृप तिष्ठतः .
वासुदेवार्पणस्वस्थे तथैव मनसी तयोः .. 192.32 ..
6.3.m: Just as two lamps standing in a windless place remain steady, O king, / so the minds of both remained at peace, surrendered to Vāsudeva.

6.3.s:
pūryamāṇo'pi cāmbhobhirbhuvamanyāṃ mahodadhiḥ .
yathā na yāti saṃkṣobhaṃ tathā tanmānasaṃ kvacit .. 192.33 ..
6.3.d:
पूर्यमाणोऽपि चाम्भोभिर्भुवमन्यां महोदधिः .
यथा न याति संक्षोभं तथा तन्मानसं क्वचित् .. 192.33 ..
6.3.m: And as the great ocean, though filled by waters, does not overflow into other land, / so their mind was nowhere agitated.

6.3.s:
sarvabhūtahitaṃ brahma vāsudevamayaṃ param .
manyamānau na rāgasya dveṣasya ca vaśaṃgatau .. 192.34 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वभूतहितं ब्रह्म वासुदेवमयं परम् .
मन्यमानौ न रागस्य द्वेषस्य च वशंगतौ .. 192.34 ..
6.3.m: Regarding supreme Brahman, beneficent to all beings, as consisting of Vāsudeva, / they fell under the sway of neither passion nor hatred.

6.3.s:
smaro'pi na śaśākātha praveṣṭuṃ hṛdayaṃ tayoḥ .
vidyāmayaṃ dīpayutamandhakāra ivālayam .. 192.35 ..
6.3.d:
स्मरोऽपि न शशाकाथ प्रवेष्टुं हृदयं तयोः .
विद्यामयं दीपयुतमन्धकार इवालयम् .. 192.35 ..
6.3.m: Smara could not enter their hearts, / just as darkness cannot enter an abode full of lights and radiant with knowledge.

6.3.s:
puṣpojjvalāṃstaruvarān vasantaṃ dakṣiṇānilam .
tāścaivāpsarasaḥ sarvāḥ kandarpaṃ ca mahāmunī .. 192.36 ..
6.3.d:
पुष्पोज्ज्वलांस्तरुवरान् वसन्तं दक्षिणानिलम् .
ताश्चैवाप्सरसः सर्वाः कन्दर्पं च महामुनी .. 192.36 ..
6.3.m: The excellent trees glowing with blossoms, Spring, the southern breeze, / all those apsarases, and Kandarpa—the two great sages

6.3.s:
yaccārabdhaṃ tapastābhyāmātmānaṃ gandhamādanam .
dadarśāte'khilaṃ rūpaṃ brahmaṇaḥ puruṣarṣabha .. 192.37 ..
6.3.d:
यच्चारब्धं तपस्ताभ्यामात्मानं गन्धमादनम् .
ददर्शातेऽखिलं रूपं ब्रह्मणः पुरुषर्षभ .. 192.37 ..
6.3.m: And the austerity begun by them, themselves, and Gandhamādana— / beheld it all as the form of Brahman, O bull among men.

6.3.s:
dāhāya nāmalo vahnernāpaḥ kledāya cāmbhasaḥ .
taddravyameva taddravyavikārāya na vai yataḥ .. 192.38 ..
6.3.d:
दाहाय नामलो वह्नेर्नापः क्लेदाय चाम्भसः .
तद्द्रव्यमेव तद्द्रव्यविकाराय न वै यतः .. 192.38 ..
6.3.m: The blaze of fire is not for burning [fire], nor is water for moistening water; / for a substance itself cannot cause a change in that very substance.

6.3.s:
tato vijñāya vijñāya paraṃ brahma svarūpataḥ .
madhukandarpayoṣitsu vikāro nābhavattayoḥ .. 192.39 ..
6.3.d:
ततो विज्ञाय विज्ञाय परं ब्रह्म स्वरूपतः .
मधुकन्दर्पयोषित्सु विकारो नाभवत्तयोः .. 192.39 ..
6.3.m: Therefore, repeatedly recognizing supreme Brahman in its essential nature, / no disturbance arose in them on account of Spring, Kandarpa, or the women.

6.3.s:
tato gurutaraṃ yatnaṃ vasantamadanau nṛpa .
cakrāte tāśca tanvaṅgyastatkṣobhāya punaḥpunaḥ .. 192.40 ..
6.3.d:
ततो गुरुतरं यत्नं वसन्तमदनौ नृप .
चक्राते ताश्च तन्वङ्ग्यस्तत्क्षोभाय पुनःपुनः .. 192.40 ..
6.3.m: Then Spring and Madana made an even greater effort, O king, / and those slender-limbed women [did likewise] again and again to agitate them.

6.3.s:
atha nārāyaṇo dhairyaṃ saṃdhāyodīrṇamānasaḥ .
ūrorutpādayāmāsa varāṅgīmabalāṃ tadā .. 192.41 ..
6.3.d:
अथ नारायणो धैर्यं संधायोदीर्णमानसः .
ऊरोरुत्पादयामास वराङ्गीमबलां तदा .. 192.41 ..
6.3.m: Then Nārāyaṇa, having composed his fortitude with an exalted mind, / created from his thigh a woman of beautiful limbs.

6.3.s:
trailokyasundarīratnamaśeṣamavanīpate .
guṇairlāghavamabhyeti yasyāḥ saṃdarśanādanu .. 192.42 ..
6.3.d:
त्रैलोक्यसुन्दरीरत्नमशेषमवनीपते .
गुणैर्लाघवमभ्येति यस्याः संदर्शनादनु .. 192.42 ..
6.3.m: Every jewel among beauties in the three worlds, O protector of the earth, / fell into insignificance beside her qualities upon seeing her.

6.3.s:
tāṃ vilokya mahīpāla cakampe manasānilaḥ .
vasanto vismayaṃ yātaḥ smaraḥ sasmāra kiṃcana .. 192.43 ..
6.3.d:
तां विलोक्य महीपाल चकम्पे मनसानिलः .
वसन्तो विस्मयं यातः स्मरः सस्मार किंचन .. 192.43 ..
6.3.m: Beholding her, O king, the wind trembled in its heart, / Spring was struck with wonder, and Smara became bewildered.

6.3.s:
rambhātilottamādyāśca vailakṣyaṃ devayoṣitaḥ .
na rejuravanīpāla tallakṣyahṛdayekṣaṇāḥ .. 192.44 ..
6.3.d:
रम्भातिलोत्तमाद्याश्च वैलक्ष्यं देवयोषितः .
न रेजुरवनीपाल तल्लक्ष्यहृदयेक्षणाः .. 192.44 ..
6.3.m: Rambhā, Tilottamā, and the other celestial women were embarrassed; / they lost their radiance, O lord of the earth, their hearts and eyes fixed on her.

6.3.s:
tataḥ kāmo vasantaśca pārthivāpsarasaśca tāḥ .
praṇamya bhagavantau tau tuṣṭuvurmunisattamau .. 192.45 ..
6.3.d:
ततः कामो वसन्तश्च पार्थिवाप्सरसश्च ताः .
प्रणम्य भगवन्तौ तौ तुष्टुवुर्मुनिसत्तमौ .. 192.45 ..
6.3.m: Then Kāma, Spring, and those celestial apsarases, O king, / bowed down to the two blessed ones, the best of sages, and praised them.

6.3.s:
vasantakāmāpsarasa ūcuḥ .
prasīdatu jagaddhātā yasya devasya māyayā .
mohitāḥ sma vijānīmo nāntaraṃ vidyate dvayoḥ .. 192.46 ..
6.3.d:
वसन्तकामाप्सरस ऊचुः .
प्रसीदतु जगद्धाता यस्य देवस्य मायया .
मोहिताः स्म विजानीमो नान्तरं विद्यते द्वयोः .. 192.46 ..
6.3.m: Spring, Kāma, and the apsarases said: / 'May the creator of the world be pleased, by whose divine māyā / we have been deluded; we know that there is no difference between you two.

6.3.s:
prasīdatu sa vāṃ devo yasya rūpamidaṃ dvidhā .
dhāmabhūtasya lokānāmanāderapratiṣṭhataḥ .. 192.47 ..
6.3.d:
प्रसीदतु स वां देवो यस्य रूपमिदं द्विधा .
धामभूतस्य लोकानामनादेरप्रतिष्ठतः .. 192.47 ..
6.3.m: May that god be pleased with you both, whose twofold form this is, / who is the abode of the worlds, beginningless, and self-supported.

6.3.s:
naranārāyaṇau devau śaṅkhacakrāyudhāvubhau .
āstāṃ prasādasumukhāvasmākamaparādhinām .. 192.48 ..
6.3.d:
नरनारायणौ देवौ शङ्खचक्रायुधावुभौ .
आस्तां प्रसादसुमुखावस्माकमपराधिनाम् .. 192.48 ..
6.3.m: May the two gods, Nara and Nārāyaṇa, both bearing the conch and discus as weapons, / show gracious faces unto us who have transgressed.

6.3.s:
nidhānaṃ sarvavidyānāṃ sarvapāpavanānalaḥ .
nārāyaṇo'to bhagavān sarvapāpaṃ vyapohatu .. 192.49 ..
6.3.d:
निधानं सर्वविद्यानां सर्वपापवनानलः .
नारायणोऽतो भगवान् सर्वपापं व्यपोहतु .. 192.49 ..
6.3.m: The treasury of all knowledge, a fire to the forest of all sins, / may Lord Nārāyaṇa therefore remove all our sins!

6.3.s:
śārṅgacihnāyudhaḥ śrīmānātmajñānamayo'naghaḥ .
naraḥ samastapāpāni hatātmā sarvadehinām .. 192.50 ..
6.3.d:
शार्ङ्गचिह्नायुधः श्रीमानात्मज्ञानमयोऽनघः .
नरः समस्तपापानि हतात्मा सर्वदेहिनाम् .. 192.50 ..
6.3.m: Bearing the bow Śārṅga as his emblem and weapon, glorious, consisting of self-knowledge, sinless, / may Nara destroy all sins of all embodied souls!

6.3.s:
jaṭākalāpabaddho'yamanayornaḥ kṣamāvatoḥ .
saumyāsyadṛṣṭiḥ pāpāni hantuṃ janmārjitāni vai .. 192.51 ..
6.3.d:
जटाकलापबद्धोऽयमनयोर्नः क्षमावतोः .
सौम्यास्यदृष्टिः पापानि हन्तुं जन्मार्जितानि वै .. 192.51 ..
6.3.m: May this [pair] bound with matted hair, patient, / with gentle faces and looks, destroy our sins accumulated through lifetimes,

6.3.s:
tathātmavidyādoṣeṇa yo'parādhaḥ kṛto mahān .
trailokyavandyau yau nāthau vilobhayitumāgatāḥ .. 192.52 ..
6.3.d:
तथात्मविद्यादोषेण योऽपराधः कृतो महान् .
त्रैलोक्यवन्द्यौ यौ नाथौ विलोभयितुमागताः .. 192.52 ..
6.3.m: And likewise the great transgression committed through the defect of self-conceit, / since we came to entice the two lords worshipped by the three worlds.'

6.3.s:
prasīda deva vijñānadhana mūḍhadṛśāmiva .
bhavanti santaḥ satataṃ svadharmaparipālakāḥ .. 192.53 ..
6.3.d:
प्रसीद देव विज्ञानधन मूढदृशामिव .
भवन्ति सन्तः सततं स्वधर्मपरिपालकाः .. 192.53 ..
6.3.m: Be gracious, O Lord rich in wisdom! As towards those of dull vision, / the virtuous are ever the upholders of their own duty.

6.3.s:
dṛṣṭvaitannaḥ samutpannaṃ yathā strīratnamuttamam .
tvayi nārāyaṇotpannā śreṣṭhā pāravatī matiḥ .. 192.54 ..
6.3.d:
दृष्ट्वैतन्नः समुत्पन्नं यथा स्त्रीरत्नमुत्तमम् .
त्वयि नारायणोत्पन्ना श्रेष्ठा पारवती मतिः .. 192.54 ..
6.3.m: Having seen this best jewel of women produced by us, / [yet] the highest, transcendent mind arose in you, O Nārāyaṇa.

6.3.s:
tena satyena satyātmanparamātmansanātana .
nārāyaṇa prasīdeśa sarvalokaparāyaṇa .. 192.55 ..
6.3.d:
तेन सत्येन सत्यात्मन्परमात्मन्सनातन .
नारायण प्रसीदेश सर्वलोकपरायण .. 192.55 ..
6.3.m: By that truth, O eternal Supreme Soul, whose self is truth, / O Nārāyaṇa, Lord, refuge of all the worlds, be gracious!

6.3.s:
prasannabuddhe śāntātmanprasannavadanekṣaṇa .
prasīda yogināmīśa nara sarvagatācyuta .. 192.56 ..
6.3.d:
प्रसन्नबुद्धे शान्तात्मन्प्रसन्नवदनेक्षण .
प्रसीद योगिनामीश नर सर्वगताच्युत .. 192.56 ..
6.3.m: O one of clear intellect, of peaceful soul, with gracious face and eyes, / be gracious, O Lord of yogins, Nara, all-pervading and infallible!

6.3.s:
namasyāmo naraṃ devaṃ tathā nārāyaṇaṃ harim .
namo narāya namyāya namo nārāyaṇāya ca .. 192.57 ..
6.3.d:
नमस्यामो नरं देवं तथा नारायणं हरिम् .
नमो नराय नम्याय नमो नारायणाय च .. 192.57 ..
6.3.m: We bow down to the god Nara, and likewise to Hari, Nārāyaṇa; / salutations to Nara who is worthy of homage, and salutations to Nārāyaṇa!

6.3.s:
prasannānāmanāthānāṃ tathā nāthavatāṃ prabho .
śaṃ karotu naro'smākaṃ śaṃ nārāyaṇa dehi naḥ .. 192.58 ..
6.3.d:
प्रसन्नानामनाथानां तथा नाथवतां प्रभो .
शं करोतु नरोऽस्माकं शं नारायण देहि नः .. 192.58 ..
6.3.m: To those who are well-disposed, helpless, or have protectors, O Lord: / may Nara bring well-being to us; O Nārāyaṇa, grant us peace!

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
evamabhyarcitaḥ stutyā rāgadveṣādivarjitaḥ .
prāheśaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ madhye nārāyaṇo nṛpa .. 192.59 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
एवमभ्यर्चितः स्तुत्या रागद्वेषादिवर्जितः .
प्राहेशः सर्वभूतानां मध्ये नारायणो नृप .. 192.59 ..
6.3.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Thus praised with a hymn, free from attachment and aversion, / Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of all beings, spoke in their midst, O king:

6.3.s:
nārāyaṇa uvāca -
svāgataṃ mādhave kāme bhavatvapsarasāmapi .
yatkāryamāgatānāṃ ca ihāsmābhistaducyatām .. 192.60 ..
6.3.d:
नारायण उवाच -
स्वागतं माधवे कामे भवत्वप्सरसामपि .
यत्कार्यमागतानां च इहास्माभिस्तदुच्यताम् .. 192.60 ..
6.3.m: Nārāyaṇa said: / Welcome to Spring, to Love, and to the apsarases as well! / Whatever business you have come for here, let it be stated to us.

6.3.s:
yūyaṃ saṃsiddhaye nūnamasmākaṃ balaśatruṇā .
saṃpreṣitāstato'smākaṃ nṛtyayogādidarśanam .. 192.61 ..
6.3.d:
यूयं संसिद्धये नूनमस्माकं बलशत्रुणा .
संप्रेषितास्ततोऽस्माकं नृत्ययोगादिदर्शनम् .. 192.61 ..
6.3.m: Surely you have been sent by the enemy of Bala to test our success; / hence our witnessing of your dance-performance and the like.

6.3.s:
na vayaṃ gītanṛtyena nāṅgaceṣṭādibhāṣitaiḥ .
lubdhā vai viṣayairmanye viṣayā dāruṇātmakāḥ .. 192.62 ..
6.3.d:
न वयं गीतनृत्येन नाङ्गचेष्टादिभाषितैः .
लुब्धा वै विषयैर्मन्ये विषया दारुणात्मकाः .. 192.62 ..
6.3.m: We are not enticed by song or dance, nor by gestures and words of the limbs, / nor indeed by sensory objects; I deem sensory objects to be terrible by nature.

6.3.s:
śabdādisaṅgaduṣṭāni yadā nākṣāṇi naḥ śubhāḥ .
tadā nṛtyādayo bhāvāḥ kathaṃ lobhapradāyinaḥ .. 192.63 ..
6.3.d:
शब्दादिसङ्गदुष्टानि यदा नाक्षाणि नः शुभाः .
तदा नृत्यादयो भावाः कथं लोभप्रदायिनः .. 192.63 ..
6.3.m: When our senses are not corrupted by contact with sound and the like, O auspicious ones, / then how could dancing and other emotional states cause desire?

6.3.s:
te siddhāḥ sma na vai sādhyā bhavatīnāṃ smarasya ca .
mādhavasya ca śākro'pi svāsthyaṃ yātvaviśaṅkitāḥ .. 192.64 ..
6.3.d:
ते सिद्धाः स्म न वै साध्या भवतीनां स्मरस्य च .
माधवस्य च शाक्रोऽपि स्वास्थ्यं यात्वविशङ्किताः .. 192.64 ..
6.3.m: We have attained perfection; we cannot be subdued by you, or Love, / or Spring. Let Indra also regain his composure, free from anxiety.

6.3.s:
yo'sau paraśca paramaḥ puruṣaḥ parameśvaraḥ .
paramātmā samastasya sthāvarasya carasya ca .. 192.65 ..
6.3.d:
योऽसौ परश्च परमः पुरुषः परमेश्वरः .
परमात्मा समस्तस्य स्थावरस्य चरस्य च .. 192.65 ..
6.3.m: That highest, supreme Person, the Supreme Lord, / the Supreme Soul of everything unmoving and moving,

6.3.s:
utpattiheturete ca yasminsarvaṃ pralīyate .
sarvāvāsīti devatvādvāsudevetyudāhṛtaḥ .. 192.66 ..
6.3.d:
उत्पत्तिहेतुरेते च यस्मिन्सर्वं प्रलीयते .
सर्वावासीति देवत्वाद्वासुदेवेत्युदाहृतः .. 192.66 ..
6.3.m: the cause of origin of these, in whom everything dissolves, / because as a divinity he abides in all, he is called Vāsudeva.

6.3.s:
vayamaṃśāṃśakāstasya caturvyūhasya māninaḥ .
tadādeśitavārtmānau jagadbodhāya dehinām .. 192.67 ..
6.3.d:
वयमंशांशकास्तस्य चतुर्व्यूहस्य मानिनः .
तदादेशितवार्त्मानौ जगद्बोधाय देहिनाम् .. 192.67 ..
6.3.m: We are portions of portions of him, holding the dignity of the fourfold emanation, / walking on the path directed by him for the awakening of embodied beings in the world.

6.3.s:
tatsarvabhūtaṃ sarveśaṃ sarvatra samadarśinam .
kutaḥ paśyantau rāgādīnkariṣyāmo vibhedinaḥ .. 192.68 ..
6.3.d:
तत्सर्वभूतं सर्वेशं सर्वत्र समदर्शिनम् .
कुतः पश्यन्तौ रागादीन्करिष्यामो विभेदिनः .. 192.68 ..
6.3.m: Seeing that Lord of all, identical with all beings, looking equally everywhere, / how could the two of us form divisive passions and hatreds?

6.3.s:
vasante mayi cendre ca bhavatīṣu tathā smare .
yadā sa eva bhūtātmā tadā dveṣādayaḥ katham .. 192.69 ..
6.3.d:
वसन्ते मयि चेन्द्रे च भवतीषु तथा स्मरे .
यदा स एव भूतात्मा तदा द्वेषादयः कथम् .. 192.69 ..
6.3.m: When in Spring, in me, in Indra, in you, and likewise in Love / there is only that Soul of all beings, how then could there be hatred and the like?

6.3.s:
tanmayānyavibhaktāni yadā sarveṣu jantuṣu .
sarveśvareśvaro viṣṇuḥ kuto rāgādayastataḥ .. 192.70 ..
6.3.d:
तन्मयान्यविभक्तानि यदा सर्वेषु जन्तुषु .
सर्वेश्वरेश्वरो विष्णुः कुतो रागादयस्ततः .. 192.70 ..
6.3.m: When all living beings are composed of him and undivided, / and Viṣṇu is the Lord of all lords, whence then could come passion and the rest?

6.3.s:
brahmāṇamindramīśānamādityamaruto'khilān .
viśvedevānṛṣīn sādhyānvasūnpitṛgaṇāṃstathā .. 192.71 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रह्माणमिन्द्रमीशानमादित्यमरुतोऽखिलान् .
विश्वेदेवानृषीन् साध्यान्वसून्पितृगणांस्तथा .. 192.71 ..
6.3.m: Brahmā, Indra, Īśāna, all the Ādityas and Maruts, / the Viśvedevas, seers, Sādhyas, Vasus, and the hosts of ancestors,

6.3.s:
yakṣarākṣasabhūtādīnnāgānsarpānsarīsṛpān .
manuṣyapakṣigorūpagajasiṃhajalecarān .. 192.72 ..
6.3.d:
यक्षराक्षसभूतादीन्नागान्सर्पान्सरीसृपान् .
मनुष्यपक्षिगोरूपगजसिंहजलेचरान् .. 192.72 ..
6.3.m: yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas and others, nāgas, serpents, reptiles, / humans, birds, forms of cattle, elephants, lions, aquatic animals,

6.3.s:
makṣikāmaśakāndaṃśāñchalabhāñjalajān kṛmīn .
gulmavṛkṣalatāvallītvaksāratṛṇajātiṣu .. 192.73 ..
6.3.d:
मक्षिकामशकान्दंशाञ्छलभाञ्जलजान् कृमीन् .
गुल्मवृक्षलतावल्लीत्वक्सारतृणजातिषु .. 192.73 ..
6.3.m: flies, mosquitoes, gnats, locusts, water-born worms, / among clumps, trees, creepers, spreading plants, bamboos, and species of grass,

6.3.s:
yacca kiṃcidadṛśyaṃ vā dṛśyaṃ vā tridaśāṅganāḥ .
manyadhvaṃ jātamekasya tatsarvaṃ paramātmanaḥ .. 192.74 ..
6.3.d:
यच्च किंचिददृश्यं वा दृश्यं वा त्रिदशाङ्गनाः .
मन्यध्वं जातमेकस्य तत्सर्वं परमात्मनः .. 192.74 ..
6.3.m: and whatever is invisible or visible, O women of the gods: / understand all that to be born of the one Supreme Soul!

6.3.s:
jāyamānaḥ kathaṃ viṣṇumātmānaṃ paramaṃ ca yat .
rāgadveṣau tathā lobhaṃ kaḥ kuryādamarāṅganāḥ .. 192.75 ..
6.3.d:
जायमानः कथं विष्णुमात्मानं परमं च यत् .
रागद्वेषौ तथा लोभं कः कुर्यादमराङ्गनाः .. 192.75 ..
6.3.m: Being born, who would feel passion, hatred, or greed / toward Viṣṇu, who is also the supreme self, O women of the gods?

6.3.s:
sarvabhūtamaye viṣṇau sarvage sarvadhātari .
nipātya taṃ pṛthagbhūte kuto rāgādiko guṇaḥ .. 192.76 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वभूतमये विष्णौ सर्वगे सर्वधातरि .
निपात्य तं पृथग्भूते कुतो रागादिको गुणः .. 192.76 ..
6.3.m: Viṣṇu being identical with all beings, all-pervading, the supporter of all— / having placed him into something separate, whence could any quality like passion arise?

6.3.s:
evamasmāsu yuṣmāsu sarvabhūteṣu cābalāḥ .
tanmathaikatvabhūteṣu rāgādyavasaraḥ kutaḥ .. 192.77 ..
6.3.d:
एवमस्मासु युष्मासु सर्वभूतेषु चाबलाः .
तन्मथैकत्वभूतेषु रागाद्यवसरः कुतः .. 192.77 ..
6.3.m: Thus in us, in you, and in all beings, O women, / who are united in his oneness, what room is there for passion and the like?

6.3.s:
samyagdṛṣṭiriyaṃ proktā samastaikyāvalokinī .
pṛthagvijñānamātraiva lokasaṃvyavahāravat .. 192.78 ..
6.3.d:
सम्यग्दृष्टिरियं प्रोक्ता समस्तैक्यावलोकिनी .
पृथग्विज्ञानमात्रैव लोकसंव्यवहारवत् .. 192.78 ..
6.3.m: This is declared to be the right vision, beholding unity in all; / cognition of separateness is only like worldly transaction.

6.3.s:
bhūtendriyāntaḥ karaṇapradhānapuruṣātmakam .
jagadvai hyetadakhilaṃ tadā bhedaḥ kimātmakaḥ .. 192.79 ..
6.3.d:
भूतेन्द्रियान्तः करणप्रधानपुरुषात्मकम् .
जगद्वै ह्येतदखिलं तदा भेदः किमात्मकः .. 192.79 ..
6.3.m: Composed of elements, sense-organs, the inner faculty, primordial nature, and the soul, / this entire world exists; then what is the nature of distinction?

6.3.s:
bhavanti layamāyānti samudrasalilormayaḥ .
na vāribhedato bhinnāstathaivaikyādidaṃ jagat .. 192.80 ..
6.3.d:
भवन्ति लयमायान्ति समुद्रसलिलोर्मयः .
न वारिभेदतो भिन्नास्तथैवैक्यादिदं जगत् .. 192.80 ..
6.3.m: The waves of ocean water arise and dissolve; / they are not separate through difference of water; just so is this world due to unity.

6.3.s:
yathāgnerarciṣaḥ pītāḥ piṅgalāruṇadhūsarāḥ .
tathāpi nāgnito bhinnāstathaitadbrahmaṇo jagat .. 192.81 ..
6.3.d:
यथाग्नेरर्चिषः पीताः पिङ्गलारुणधूसराः .
तथापि नाग्नितो भिन्नास्तथैतद्ब्रह्मणो जगत् .. 192.81 ..
6.3.m: Just as the flames of a fire may be yellow, reddish-brown, red, or grey, / yet are not separate from the fire, so is this world from Brahman.

6.3.s:
bhavatībhiśca yatkṣobhamasmākaṃ sa puraṃdaraḥ .
kārayatyasadetacca vivekācāracetasām .. 192.82 ..
6.3.d:
भवतीभिश्च यत्क्षोभमस्माकं स पुरंदरः .
कारयत्यसदेतच्च विवेकाचारचेतसाम् .. 192.82 ..
6.3.m: And that Purandara seeks to cause agitation in us through you— / that is unworthy of those whose minds possess discernment and good conduct.

6.3.s:
bhavantyaḥ sa ca devendro lokāśca sasurāsurāḥ .
samudrādrivanopetā maddehāntaragocarāḥ .. 192.83 ..
6.3.d:
भवन्त्यः स च देवेन्द्रो लोकाश्च ससुरासुराः .
समुद्राद्रिवनोपेता मद्देहान्तरगोचराः .. 192.83 ..
6.3.m: You, and that king of gods, and the worlds with the suras and asuras, / endowed with oceans, mountains, and forests, exist within the scope of my body.

6.3.s:
yatheyaṃ cārusarvāṅgī bhavatīnāṃ mayāgrataḥ .
darśitā darśayiṣyāmi tathā caivākhilaṃ jagat .. 192.84 ..
6.3.d:
यथेयं चारुसर्वाङ्गी भवतीनां मयाग्रतः .
दर्शिता दर्शयिष्यामि तथा चैवाखिलं जगत् .. 192.84 ..
6.3.m: Just as this woman, beautiful in all her limbs, has been shown / by me before you, in the same way I can show the entire universe.

6.3.s:
prayātu śakro mā garvamindratvaṃ kasya susthiram .
yūyaṃ ca mā smayaṃ yāta santi rūpānvitāḥ striyaḥ .. 192.85 ..
6.3.d:
प्रयातु शक्रो मा गर्वमिन्द्रत्वं कस्य सुस्थिरम् .
यूयं च मा स्मयं यात सन्ति रूपान्विताः स्त्रियः .. 192.85 ..
6.3.m: Let Indra not fall into pride; for whom is the status of Indra ever stable? / And you must not feel haughty; there are women possessed of beauty.

6.3.s:
kiṃ surūpaṃ kurūpaṃ vā yadā bhedo na dṛśyate .
tāratamyaṃ surūpatve satataṃ bhinnadarśanāt .. 192.86 ..
6.3.d:
किं सुरूपं कुरूपं वा यदा भेदो न दृश्यते .
तारतम्यं सुरूपत्वे सततं भिन्नदर्शनात् .. 192.86 ..
6.3.m: What is handsome or ugly, when no difference is seen? / A gradation in beauty arises constantly from seeing difference.

6.3.s:
bhavatīnāṃ smayaṃ matvā rūpaudāryaguṇodbhavam .
mayeyaṃ darśitā tanvī tatastu śamameṣyatha .. 192.87 ..
6.3.d:
भवतीनां स्मयं मत्वा रूपौदार्यगुणोद्भवम् .
मयेयं दर्शिता तन्वी ततस्तु शममेष्यथ .. 192.87 ..
6.3.m: Thinking of your pride born of the qualities of beauty and magnanimity, / this slender woman was shown by me, so that you may attain tranquility.

6.3.s:
yasmānmadūrorniṣpannā tviyamindīvarekṣaṇā .
urvaśī nāma kalyāṇī bhaviṣyati varāpsarāḥ .. 192.88 ..
6.3.d:
यस्मान्मदूरोर्निष्पन्ना त्वियमिन्दीवरेक्षणा .
उर्वशी नाम कल्याणी भविष्यति वराप्सराः .. 192.88 ..
6.3.m: Since this blue-lotus-eyed woman was produced from my thigh, / she shall be an auspicious, excellent apsaras named Urvaśī.

6.3.s:
tadiyaṃ devarājasya nīyatāṃ varavarṇinī .
bhavatyastena cāsmākaṃ preṣitāḥ prītimicchatā .. 192.89 ..
6.3.d:
तदियं देवराजस्य नीयतां वरवर्णिनी .
भवत्यस्तेन चास्माकं प्रेषिताः प्रीतिमिच्छता .. 192.89 ..
6.3.m: Therefore, let this fair-complexioned woman be taken to the king of gods; / and you were sent by him because he desired [our] favour.

6.3.s:
vaktavyaśca sahasrākṣo nāsmākaṃ bhogakāraṇāt .
tapaścaryā na vāprāpyaphalaṃ prāptumabhīpsatā .. 192.90 ..
6.3.d:
वक्तव्यश्च सहस्राक्षो नास्माकं भोगकारणात् .
तपश्चर्या न वाप्राप्यफलं प्राप्तुमभीप्सता .. 192.90 ..
6.3.m: And the thousand-eyed one must be told: 'Our practice of austerity / is not for the sake of enjoyment, nor from a desire to obtain unattainable fruit.

6.3.s:
sanmārgamasya jagato darśayiṣye karomyaham .
tathā nareṇa sahito jagataḥ pālanodyataḥ .. 192.91 ..
6.3.d:
सन्मार्गमस्य जगतो दर्शयिष्ये करोम्यहम् .
तथा नरेण सहितो जगतः पालनोद्यतः .. 192.91 ..
6.3.m: I shall show and prepare the good path of this world, / and together with Nara, I am engaged in the protection of the universe.

6.3.s:
yadi kaścittavābādhāṃ karoti tridaśeśvara .
tamahaṃ vārayiṣyāmi nivṛtto bhava vāsava .. 192.92 ..
6.3.d:
यदि कश्चित्तवाबाधां करोति त्रिदशेश्वर .
तमहं वारयिष्यामि निवृत्तो भव वासव .. 192.92 ..
6.3.m: If anyone causes trouble to you, O Lord of the gods, / I shall check him; be at ease, O Vāsava!

6.3.s:
kartāsi cettvamābādhāṃ na duṣṭasyeha kasyacit .
taṃ cāpi śāstā tadahaṃ pravartiṣyāmyasaṃśayam .. 192.93 ..
6.3.d:
कर्तासि चेत्त्वमाबाधां न दुष्टस्येह कस्यचित् .
तं चापि शास्ता तदहं प्रवर्तिष्याम्यसंशयम् .. 192.93 ..
6.3.m: If you do not cause trouble to anyone who is wicked here, / then I, as the chastiser, shall take action against him without doubt.

6.3.s:
etajjñātvā na santāpastvayā kāryo hi māṃ prati .
upakārāya jagatāmavatīrṇo'smi vāsava .. 192.94 ..
6.3.d:
एतज्ज्ञात्वा न सन्तापस्त्वया कार्यो हि मां प्रति .
उपकाराय जगतामवतीर्णोऽस्मि वासव .. 192.94 ..
6.3.m: Knowing this, you should feel no anguish towards me; / I have descended for the benefit of the worlds, O Vāsava!

6.3.s:
yā ceyamurvaśī mattaḥ samudbhūtā puraṃdara tretāgnihetubhūteyaṃ evaṃ prāpya bhaviṣyati .. 192.95 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe narmadāmāhātmye śrīpatyutpattivarṇanaṃ nāma dvinavatyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
6.3.d:
या चेयमुर्वशी मत्तः समुद्भूता पुरंदर त्रेताग्निहेतुभूतेयं एवं प्राप्य भविष्यति .. 192.95 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे नर्मदामाहात्म्ये श्रीपत्युत्पत्तिवर्णनं नाम द्विनवत्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः ..
6.3.m:
And this Urvaśī who has sprung from me, O Purandara, / having been obtained in this manner, shall become the cause of the threefold sacrificial fire.'"
Thus ends the one hundred and ninety-second chapter, titled "Description of the Origin of the Lord of Śrī," in the Revākhaṇḍa of the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, within the Narmadāmāhātmya of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

6.3.s:
adhyāya 193
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
ityukte'psarasaḥ sarvāḥ praṇipatya punaḥ punaḥ .
ūcurnārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ taddarśanasamīhayā .. 193.1 ..
6.3.d:
अध्याय 193
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
इत्युक्तेऽप्सरसः सर्वाः प्रणिपत्य पुनः पुनः .
ऊचुर्नारायणं देवं तद्दर्शनसमीहया .. 193.1 ..
6.3.m:
Chapter 193
Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said:
When this was said, all the apsarases bowed down again and again / and spoke to the god Nārāyaṇa, desiring to see him. // 193.1

6.3.s:
vasantakāmāpsarasa ūcuḥ .
bhagavanbhavatā yo'yamupadeśo hitārthinā .
proktaḥ sa sarvo vijñāto māhātmyaṃ viditaṃ ca te .. 193.2 ..
6.3.d:
वसन्तकामाप्सरस ऊचुः .
भगवन्भवता योऽयमुपदेशो हितार्थिना .
प्रोक्तः स सर्वो विज्ञातो माहात्म्यं विदितं च ते .. 193.2 ..
6.3.m:
Vasanta, Kāma, and the apsarases said:
O Lord, this instruction spoken by you, desiring our welfare, / has all been understood, and your glory is known. // 193.2

6.3.s:
yattvetadbhavatā proktaṃ prasannenāntarātmanā .
darśiteyaṃ viśālākṣī darśayiṣyāmi vo jagat .. 193.3 ..
6.3.d:
यत्त्वेतद्भवता प्रोक्तं प्रसन्नेनान्तरात्मना .
दर्शितेयं विशालाक्षी दर्शयिष्यामि वो जगत् .. 193.3 ..
6.3.m: Indeed, what was spoken by you with a pleased inner self— / "This large-eyed woman was shown [to you]; I shall show you the universe"— // 193.3

6.3.s:
tatrārthe sarvabhāvena prapannānāṃ jagatpate .
darśayātmānamakhilaṃ darśiteyaṃ yathorvaśī .. 193.4 ..
6.3.d:
तत्रार्थे सर्वभावेन प्रपन्नानां जगत्पते .
दर्शयात्मानमखिलं दर्शितेयं यथोर्वशी .. 193.4 ..
6.3.m: for that purpose, show your entire self to us who have surrendered with all our being, O Lord of the universe, / just as this Urvaśī was shown. // 193.4

6.3.s:
yadi devāparādhe'pi nāsmāsu kupitaṃ tava .
namaste jagatāmīśa darśayātmānamātmanā .. 193.5 ..
6.3.d:
यदि देवापराधेऽपि नास्मासु कुपितं तव .
नमस्ते जगतामीश दर्शयात्मानमात्मना .. 193.5 ..
6.3.m: If, O Lord, despite our offense, you are not angry with us, / homage to you, O Lord of the worlds; show yourself through yourself! // 193.5

6.3.s:
nārāyaṇa uvāca -
paśyatehākhilāṃllokānmama dehe surāṅganāḥ .
madhuṃ madanamātmānaṃ yaccānyaddraṣṭumicchatha .. 193.6 ..
6.3.d:
नारायण उवाच -
पश्यतेहाखिलांल्लोकान्मम देहे सुराङ्गनाः .
मधुं मदनमात्मानं यच्चान्यद्द्रष्टुमिच्छथ .. 193.6 ..
6.3.m:
Nārāyaṇa said:
Behold here all the worlds in my body, O celestial damsels: / Madhu, Madana, yourselves, and whatever else you wish to see! // 193.6

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
ityuktvā bhagavāndevastadā nārāyaṇo nṛpa .
uccairjahāsa svanavattatrābhūdakhilaṃ jagat .. 193.7 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान्देवस्तदा नारायणो नृप .
उच्चैर्जहास स्वनवत्तत्राभूदखिलं जगत् .. 193.7 ..
6.3.m:
Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Having spoken thus, the divine Lord Nārāyaṇa then, O king, / laughed aloud resoundingly; and right there appeared the entire universe: // 193.7

6.3.s:
brahmā prajāpatiḥ śakraḥ saha rudraiḥ pinākadhṛk .
ādityā vasavaḥ sādhyā viśvedevā maharṣayaḥ .. 193.8 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रह्मा प्रजापतिः शक्रः सह रुद्रैः पिनाकधृक् .
आदित्या वसवः साध्या विश्वेदेवा महर्षयः .. 193.8 ..
6.3.m: Brahmā the Prajāpati, Śakra, the wielder of the Pināka along with the Rudras, / the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Sādhyas, the Viśvedevas, the great seers, // 193.8

6.3.s:
nāsatyadasrāvanilaḥ sarvaśaśca tathāgnayaḥ .
yakṣagandharvasiddhāśca piśācoragakinnarāḥ .. 193.9 ..
6.3.d:
नासत्यदस्रावनिलः सर्वशश्च तथाग्नयः .
यक्षगन्धर्वसिद्धाश्च पिशाचोरगकिन्नराः .. 193.9 ..
6.3.m: Nāsatya and Dasra, the wind, and all the fires in every quarter, / the yakṣas, gandharvas, siddhas, piśācas, serpents, and kinnaras, // 193.9

6.3.s:
samastāpsaraso vidyāḥ sāṅgā vedāstaduktayaḥ .
manuṣyāḥ paśavaḥ kīṭāḥ pakṣiṇaḥ pādapāstathā .. 193.10 ..
6.3.d:
समस्ताप्सरसो विद्याः साङ्गा वेदास्तदुक्तयः .
मनुष्याः पशवः कीटाः पक्षिणः पादपास्तथा .. 193.10 ..
6.3.m: all the apsarases, the sciences, the Vedas with their auxiliary limbs and their expositions, / human beings, animals, insects, birds, as well as trees, // 193.10

6.3.s:
sarīsṛpāścātha sūkṣmā yaccānyajjīvasaṃjñitam .
samudrāḥ sakalāḥ śailāḥ saritaḥ kānanāni ca .. 193.11 ..
6.3.d:
सरीसृपाश्चाथ सूक्ष्मा यच्चान्यज्जीवसंज्ञितम् .
समुद्राः सकलाः शैलाः सरितः काननानि च .. 193.11 ..
6.3.m: reptiles and subtle [creatures], and whatever else is known as a living being, / all the oceans, mountains, rivers, and forests, // 193.11

6.3.s:
dvīpānyaśeṣāṇi tathā tathā sarvasarāṃsi ca .
nagaragrāmapūrṇā ca medinī medinīpate .
devāṅganābhirdevasya dehe dṛṣṭaṃ mahātmanaḥ .. 193.12 ..
6.3.d:
द्वीपान्यशेषाणि तथा तथा सर्वसरांसि च .
नगरग्रामपूर्णा च मेदिनी मेदिनीपते .
देवाङ्गनाभिर्देवस्य देहे दृष्टं महात्मनः .. 193.12 ..
6.3.m: all the continents, and likewise all the lakes, / and the earth filled with cities and villages, O lord of the earth— / [all this] was seen by the celestial damsels in the body of the great-souled god. // 193.12

6.3.s:
nakṣatragrahatārābhiḥ susampūrṇaṃ nabhastalam .
dadṛśustāḥ sucārvaṅgyastasyāntarviśvaṃ rūpiṇaḥ .. 193.13 ..
6.3.d:
नक्षत्रग्रहताराभिः सुसम्पूर्णं नभस्तलम् .
ददृशुस्ताः सुचार्वङ्ग्यस्तस्यान्तर्विश्वं रूपिणः .. 193.13 ..
6.3.m: The vault of heaven completely filled with constellations, planets, and stars— / those women of beautiful limbs beheld the universe within him, the cosmic-formed one. // 193.13

6.3.s:
ūrdhvaṃ na tiryaṅnādhastādyadāntastasya dṛśyate .
tamanantamanādiṃ ca tatastāstuṣṭuvuḥ prabhum .. 193.14 ..
6.3.d:
ऊर्ध्वं न तिर्यङ्नाधस्ताद्यदान्तस्तस्य दृश्यते .
तमनन्तमनादिं च ततस्तास्तुष्टुवुः प्रभुम् .. 193.14 ..
6.3.m: When neither above, nor across, nor below an end of him was seen, / they then praised that endless and beginningless Lord. // 193.14

6.3.s:
madanena samaṃ sarvā madhunā ca varāṅganāḥ .
sasādhvasā bhaktiparāḥ paraṃ vismayamāgatāḥ .. 193.15 ..
6.3.d:
मदनेन समं सर्वा मधुना च वराङ्गनाः .
ससाध्वसा भक्तिपराः परं विस्मयमागताः .. 193.15 ..
6.3.m: Together with Madana and Madhu, all the excellent women, / filled with trepidation, devoted to bhakti, attained supreme wonder. // 193.15

6.3.s:
vasantakāmāpsarasa ūcuḥ .
paśyāma nādiṃ tava deva nāntaṃ na madhyamavyākṛtarūpapāram .
parāyaṇaṃ tvāṃ jagatāmanantaṃ natāḥ sma nārāyaṇamātmabhūtam .. 193.16 ..
6.3.d:
वसन्तकामाप्सरस ऊचुः .
पश्याम नादिं तव देव नान्तं न मध्यमव्याकृतरूपपारम् .
परायणं त्वां जगतामनन्तं नताः स्म नारायणमात्मभूतम् .. 193.16 ..
6.3.m:
Vasanta, Kāma, and the apsarases said:
We see no beginning, O Lord, no end, and no middle of you, whose unmanifest form is limitless; / we bow to you, Nārāyaṇa, the ultimate refuge of the worlds, the endless one who has become the Self! // 193.16

6.3.s:
mahīnabhovāyujalāgnayastvaṃ śabdādirūpastu parāparātman .
tvatto bhavatyacyute sarvametadbhedādirūpo'si vibho tvamātman .. 193.17 ..
6.3.d:
महीनभोवायुजलाग्नयस्त्वं शब्दादिरूपस्तु परापरात्मन् .
त्वत्तो भवत्यच्युते सर्वमेतद्भेदादिरूपोऽसि विभो त्वमात्मन् .. 193.17 ..
6.3.m: You are earth, sky, wind, water, and fire, and the form of sound and the rest, O Self of higher and lower! / From you, O Acyuta, all this comes into being; you exist in forms of differentiation and the like, O omnipresent Self! // 193.17

6.3.s:
draṣṭāsi rūpasya parasya vettā śrotā ca śabdasya hare tvamekaḥ .
sraṣṭā bhavān sarvagato'khilasya ghrātā ca gandhasya pṛthakśarīrī .. 193.18 ..
6.3.d:
द्रष्टासि रूपस्य परस्य वेत्ता श्रोता च शब्दस्य हरे त्वमेकः .
स्रष्टा भवान् सर्वगतोऽखिलस्य घ्राता च गन्धस्य पृथक्शरीरी .. 193.18 ..
6.3.m: You are the seer of highest form, the knower, and the sole hearer of sound, O Hari; / you are the omnipresent creator of all, the smeller of fragrance, embodied in distinct forms! // 193.18

6.3.s:
sureṣu sarveṣu na so'sti kaścinmanuṣyalokeṣu na so'sti kaścit .
paśvādivargeṣu na so'sti kaścidyo nāṃśabhūtastava devadeva .. 193.19 ..
6.3.d:
सुरेषु सर्वेषु न सोऽस्ति कश्चिन्मनुष्यलोकेषु न सोऽस्ति कश्चित् .
पश्वादिवर्गेषु न सोऽस्ति कश्चिद्यो नांशभूतस्तव देवदेव .. 193.19 ..
6.3.m: Among all the gods there is no one, in the worlds of men there is no one, / and among the classes of animals and the rest there is no one who is not a portion of you, O God of gods! // 193.19

6.3.s:
brahmāmbudhīndupramukhāni saumya śakrādirūpāṇi tavottamāni .
samudrarūpaṃ tava dhairyavatsu tejaḥ svarūpeṣu ravistathāgniḥ .. 193.20 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रह्माम्बुधीन्दुप्रमुखानि सौम्य शक्रादिरूपाणि तवोत्तमानि .
समुद्ररूपं तव धैर्यवत्सु तेजः स्वरूपेषु रविस्तथाग्निः .. 193.20 ..
6.3.m: Brahmā, the ocean, the moon, and the forms of Śakra and the rest, O gentle one, are your superior [forms]; / your form is that of the ocean among the resolute, and the sun and fire among forms of fiery brilliance! // 193.20

6.3.s:
kṣamādhaneṣu kṣitirūpamagryaṃ śīghro balavatsu vāyuḥ .
manuṣyarūpaṃ tava rājaveṣo mūḍheṣu sarveśvara pādapo'si .. 193.21 ..
6.3.d:
क्षमाधनेषु क्षितिरूपमग्र्यं शीघ्रो बलवत्सु वायुः .
मनुष्यरूपं तव राजवेषो मूढेषु सर्वेश्वर पादपोऽसि .. 193.21 ..
6.3.m: You are the foremost form of the earth among those rich in forbearance, and the swift wind among the powerful; / the appearance of a king is your human form; among the foolish, O Lord of all, you are a tree! // 193.21

6.3.s:
sarvānayeṣvacyuta dānavastvaṃ sanatsajātaśca vivekavatsu .
rasasvarūpeṇa jalasthito'si gandhasvarūpaṃ bhavato dharitryām .. 193.22 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वानयेष्वच्युत दानवस्त्वं सनत्सजातश्च विवेकवत्सु .
रसस्वरूपेण जलस्थितोऽसि गन्धस्वरूपं भवतो धरित्र्याम् .. 193.22 ..
6.3.m: Among all unrighteous ones, O Acyuta, you are the Dānava, and Sanatsujāta among the discerning; / you reside in water in the form of taste, and your form is fragrance in the earth! // 193.22

6.3.s:
dṛśyasvarūpaśca hutāśanastvaṃ sparśasvarūpaṃ bhavataḥ samīre .
śabdādikaṃ te nabhasi svarūpaṃ mantavyarūpo manasi prabho tvam .. 193.23 ..
6.3.d:
दृश्यस्वरूपश्च हुताशनस्त्वं स्पर्शस्वरूपं भवतः समीरे .
शब्दादिकं ते नभसि स्वरूपं मन्तव्यरूपो मनसि प्रभो त्वम् .. 193.23 ..
6.3.m: And you are the fire whose form is visible; your form is touch in the wind; / your form in the sky consists of sound and the rest; you are the object of thought in the mind, O Lord! // 193.23

6.3.s:
bodhasvarūpaśca matau tvamekaḥ sarvatra sarveśvara sarvabhūta .
paśyāmi te nābhisarojamadhye brahmāṇamīśaṃ ca haraṃ bhṛkuṭyām .. 193.24 ..
6.3.d:
बोधस्वरूपश्च मतौ त्वमेकः सर्वत्र सर्वेश्वर सर्वभूत .
पश्यामि ते नाभिसरोजमध्ये ब्रह्माणमीशं च हरं भृकुट्याम् .. 193.24 ..
6.3.m: And you alone are the form of awareness in the intellect, omnipresent, Lord of all, who have become all beings! / We see Brahmā in the middle of your navel-lotus, and the Lord Hara on your eyebrow! // 193.24

6.3.s:
tavāśvinau karṇagatau samastāstavāsthitā bāhuṣu lokapālāḥ .
ghrāṇo'nilo netragatau ravīndu jihvā ca te nātha sarasvatīyam .. 193.25 ..
6.3.d:
तवाश्विनौ कर्णगतौ समस्तास्तवास्थिता बाहुषु लोकपालाः .
घ्राणोऽनिलो नेत्रगतौ रवीन्दु जिह्वा च ते नाथ सरस्वतीयम् .. 193.25 ..
6.3.m: The two Aśvins are situated in your ears; all the world-protectors abide in your arms; / the wind is your breath, the sun and moon are in your eyes, and this Sarasvatī is your tongue, O Master! // 193.25

6.3.s:
pādau dharitrī jaṭharaṃ samastāṃllokān hṛṣīkeśa vilokayāmaḥ .
jaṅghe vayaṃ pādatalāṅgulīṣu piśācayakṣoragasiddhasaṅghāḥ .. 193.26 ..
6.3.d:
पादौ धरित्री जठरं समस्तांल्लोकान् हृषीकेश विलोकयामः .
जङ्घे वयं पादतलाङ्गुलीषु पिशाचयक्षोरगसिद्धसङ्घाः .. 193.26 ..
6.3.m: Your feet are the earth, and in your belly we behold all the worlds, O Hṛṣīkeśa; / we are the shanks; and the hosts of piśācas, yakṣas, serpents, and siddhas are on the toes of your feet! // 193.26

6.3.s:
puṃstve prajānāṃ patiroṣṭhayugme pratiṣṭhitāste kratavaḥ samastāḥ .
sarve vayaṃ te daśaneṣu deva daṃṣṭrāsu devā hyabhavaṃśca dantāḥ .. 193.27 ..
6.3.d:
पुंस्त्वे प्रजानां पतिरोष्ठयुग्मे प्रतिष्ठितास्ते क्रतवः समस्ताः .
सर्वे वयं ते दशनेषु देव दंष्ट्रासु देवा ह्यभवंश्च दन्ताः .. 193.27 ..
6.3.m: The Lord of creatures resides in your manhood; all the sacrifices are established in your two lips; / we all are in your teeth, O Lord, and the gods are in your fangs and teeth! // 193.27

6.3.s:
romāṇyaśeṣāstava devasaṅghā vidyādharā nātha tavāṅghrirekhāḥ .
sāṅgāḥ samastāstava deva vedāḥ samāsthitāḥ sandhiṣu bāhubhūtāḥ .. 193.28 ..
6.3.d:
रोमाण्यशेषास्तव देवसङ्घा विद्याधरा नाथ तवाङ्घ्रिरेखाः .
साङ्गाः समस्तास्तव देव वेदाः समास्थिताः सन्धिषु बाहुभूताः .. 193.28 ..
6.3.m: Your hairs are the hosts of all gods; the vidyādharas, O Master, are the lines on your feet; / all the Vedas with their auxiliary limbs, O Lord, are stationed in your joints, having become your arms! // 193.28

6.3.s:
varāhabhūtaṃ dharaṇīdharaste nṛsiṃharūpaṃ ca sadā karālam .
paśyāma te vājiśirastathoccaistrivikrame yacca tadāprameyam .. 193.29 ..
6.3.d:
वराहभूतं धरणीधरस्ते नृसिंहरूपं च सदा करालम् .
पश्याम ते वाजिशिरस्तथोच्चैस्त्रिविक्रमे यच्च तदाप्रमेयम् .. 193.29 ..
6.3.m: We see the bearer of the earth who took the form of the Boar, and your Man-Lion form which is ever dreadful, / and likewise the horse-headed form high above, and that which was immeasurable in the Three Strides! // 193.29

6.3.s:
amī samudrāstava deva dehe maurvālayaḥ śailadharāstathāmī .
imāśca gaṅgāpramukhāḥ sravantyo dvīpāṇyaśeṣāṇi vanādideśāḥ .. 193.30 ..
6.3.d:
अमी समुद्रास्तव देव देहे मौर्वालयः शैलधरास्तथामी .
इमाश्च गङ्गाप्रमुखाः स्रवन्त्यो द्वीपाण्यशेषाणि वनादिदेशाः .. 193.30 ..
6.3.m: These oceans, O Lord, are in your body, the abode of submarine fire, and so are these mountain-bearing [regions], / and these rivers headed by the Gaṅgā, all the continents, and tracts of forest and the like! // 193.30

6.3.s:
stuvanti ceme munayastaveśa dehe sthitāstvanmahimānamagryam .
tvāmīśitāraṃ jagatāmanantaṃ yajanti yajñaiḥ kila yajñino'mī .. 193.31 ..
6.3.d:
स्तुवन्ति चेमे मुनयस्तवेश देहे स्थितास्त्वन्महिमानमग्र्यम् .
त्वामीशितारं जगतामनन्तं यजन्ति यज्ञैः किल यज्ञिनोऽमी .. 193.31 ..
6.3.m: And these sages situated in your body, O Lord, praise your supreme greatness; / indeed, these sacrificers worship you, the endless ruler of the worlds, with sacrifices! // 193.31

6.3.s:
tvattohi saumyaṃ jagatīha kiṃcittvatto na raudraṃ ca samastamūrte .
tvatto na śītaṃ ca na keśavoṣṇaṃ sarvasvarūpātiśayī tvameva .. 193.32 ..
6.3.d:
त्वत्तोहि सौम्यं जगतीह किंचित्त्वत्तो न रौद्रं च समस्तमूर्ते .
त्वत्तो न शीतं च न केशवोष्णं सर्वस्वरूपातिशयी त्वमेव .. 193.32 ..
6.3.m: For there is nothing gentler than you in this world, nor anything fiercer than you, O you whose form is everything! / There is nothing cooler than you, nor hotter, O Keśava; you alone surpass all forms! // 193.32

6.3.s:
prasīda sarveśvara sarvabhūta sanātanātmaparameśvareśa .
tvanmāyayā mohitamānasābhiryatte'parāddhaṃ tadidaṃ kṣamasva .. 193.33 ..
6.3.d:
प्रसीद सर्वेश्वर सर्वभूत सनातनात्मपरमेश्वरेश .
त्वन्मायया मोहितमानसाभिर्यत्तेऽपराद्धं तदिदं क्षमस्व .. 193.33 ..
6.3.m: Be gracious, O Lord of all, you who have become all beings, eternal Self, Supreme Lord and Master! / Forgive this offense of ours whose minds were bewildered by your māyā! // 193.33

6.3.s:
kiṃ vāparāddhaṃ tava devadeva yanmāyayā no hṛdayaṃ tavāpi .
māyābhiśaṅkipraṇatārtihantarmano hi no vihvalatāmupaiti .. 193.34 ..
6.3.d:
किं वापराद्धं तव देवदेव यन्मायया नो हृदयं तवापि .
मायाभिशङ्किप्रणतार्तिहन्तर्मनो हि नो विह्वलतामुपैति .. 193.34 ..
6.3.m: Or what offense could be done to you, O God of gods, when by your māyā our heart, and even your own, [is veiled]? / For our mind, suspicious of your māyā, goes into bewilderment, O destroyer of the distress of those who bow! // 193.34

6.3.s:
na te'parāddhaṃ yadi te'parāddhamasmābhirunmārgavivartinībhiḥ .
tatkṣamyatāṃ sṛṣṭikṛtastavaiva devāparādhaḥ sṛjato vivekam .. 193.35 ..
6.3.d:
न तेऽपराद्धं यदि तेऽपराद्धमस्माभिरुन्मार्गविवर्तिनीभिः .
तत्क्षम्यतां सृष्टिकृतस्तवैव देवापराधः सृजतो विवेकम् .. 193.35 ..
6.3.m: If we who strayed onto the wrong path committed an offense against you, it was no offense to you. / Therefore let it be forgiven; the offense belongs only to you, the creator, who produces discrimination, O God.

6.3.s:
namo namaste govinda nārāyaṇa janārdana .
tvannāmasmaraṇātpāpamaśeṣaṃ naḥ praṇaśyatu .. 193.36 ..
6.3.d:
नमो नमस्ते गोविन्द नारायण जनार्दन .
त्वन्नामस्मरणात्पापमशेषं नः प्रणश्यतु .. 193.36 ..
6.3.m: Obeisance, obeisance to you, Govinda, Nārāyaṇa, Janārdana! / By remembering your name, may our sin perish completely!

6.3.s:
namo'nanta namastubhyaṃ viśvātmanviśvabhāvana .
tvannāmasmaraṇātpāpamaśeṣaṃ naḥ praṇaśyatu .. 193.37 ..
6.3.d:
नमोऽनन्त नमस्तुभ्यं विश्वात्मन्विश्वभावन .
त्वन्नामस्मरणात्पापमशेषं नः प्रणश्यतु .. 193.37 ..
6.3.m: Obeisance to the Infinite One, obeisance to you, Soul of the universe, Source of the universe! / By remembering your name, may our sin perish completely!

6.3.s:
vareṇya yajñapuruṣa prajāpālana vāmana .
tvannāmasmaraṇātpāpamaśeṣaṃ naḥ praṇaśyatu .. 193.38 ..
6.3.d:
वरेण्य यज्ञपुरुष प्रजापालन वामन .
त्वन्नामस्मरणात्पापमशेषं नः प्रणश्यतु .. 193.38 ..
6.3.m: O Choicest One, Puruṣa of the sacrifice, Protector of creatures, Vāmana! / By remembering your name, may our sin perish completely!

6.3.s:
namo'stu te'bjanābhāya prajāpatikṛte hara .
tvannāmasmaraṇātpāpamaśeṣaṃ naḥ praṇaśyatu .. 193.39 ..
6.3.d:
नमोऽस्तु तेऽब्जनाभाय प्रजापतिकृते हर .
त्वन्नामस्मरणात्पापमशेषं नः प्रणश्यतु .. 193.39 ..
6.3.m: Obeisance be to you whose navel is a lotus, Maker of the Lord of Creatures, Hara! / By remembering your name, may our sin perish completely!

6.3.s:
saṃsārārṇavapotāya namastubhyamadhokṣaja .
tvannāmasmaraṇātpāpamaśeṣaṃ naḥ praṇaśyatu .. 193.40 ..
6.3.d:
संसारार्णवपोताय नमस्तुभ्यमधोक्षज .
त्वन्नामस्मरणात्पापमशेषं नः प्रणश्यतु .. 193.40 ..
6.3.m: Obeisance to you, the ship upon the ocean of worldly existence, Adhokṣaja! / By remembering your name, may our sin perish completely!

6.3.s:
namaḥ parasmai śrīśāya vāsudevāya vedhase .
svecchayā guṇayuktāya sargasthityantakāriṇe .. 193.41 ..
6.3.d:
नमः परस्मै श्रीशाय वासुदेवाय वेधसे .
स्वेच्छया गुणयुक्ताय सर्गस्थित्यन्तकारिणे .. 193.41 ..
6.3.m: Obeisance to the Supreme, the Lord of Śrī, Vāsudeva, the Creator, / who by his own will assumes the guṇas, who brings about creation, preservation, and dissolution.

6.3.s:
upasaṃhara viśvātmanrūpametatsanātanam .
vardhamānaṃ na no draṣṭuṃ samarthaṃ cakṣurīśvara .. 193.42 ..
6.3.d:
उपसंहर विश्वात्मन्रूपमेतत्सनातनम् .
वर्धमानं न नो द्रष्टुं समर्थं चक्षुरीश्वर .. 193.42 ..
6.3.m: Withdraw this eternal form, O Soul of the universe! / Our eye is not capable of beholding it as it grows, O Lord.

6.3.s:
pralayāgnisahasrasya samā dīptistavācyuta .
pramāṇena diśo bhūmirgaganaṃ ca samāvṛtam .. 193.43 ..
6.3.d:
प्रलयाग्निसहस्रस्य समा दीप्तिस्तवाच्युत .
प्रमाणेन दिशो भूमिर्गगनं च समावृतम् .. 193.43 ..
6.3.m: Your brilliance is equal to thousands of fires of dissolution, O Acyuta! / By its measure the directions, the earth, and the sky are enveloped.

6.3.s:
na vidmaḥ kutra vartāmo bhavānnāthopalakṣyate .
sarvaṃ jagadiaikasthaṃ piṇḍitaṃ lakṣayāmahe .. 193.44 ..
6.3.d:
न विद्मः कुत्र वर्तामो भवान्नाथोपलक्ष्यते .
सर्वं जगदिऐकस्थं पिण्डितं लक्षयामहे .. 193.44 ..
6.3.m: We do not know where we are; you alone are perceived as Lord. / We perceive the entire universe condensed and standing in one single place.

6.3.s:
kiṃ varṇayāmo rūpaṃ te kiṃ pramāṇamidaṃ hare .
māhātmyaṃ kiṃ nu te deva yajjihvāyā na gocare .. 193.45 ..
6.3.d:
किं वर्णयामो रूपं ते किं प्रमाणमिदं हरे .
माहात्म्यं किं नु ते देव यज्जिह्वाया न गोचरे .. 193.45 ..
6.3.m: How can we describe your form, or what is this measure of it, O Hari? / Or what indeed is your greatness, O God, which is not within the range of the tongue?

6.3.s:
vaktāro vāyutenāpi buddhīnāmayutāyutaiḥ .
guṇanirvarṇanaṃ nātha kartuṃ tava na śakyate .. 193.46 ..
6.3.d:
वक्तारो वायुतेनापि बुद्धीनामयुतायुतैः .
गुणनिर्वर्णनं नाथ कर्तुं तव न शक्यते .. 193.46 ..
6.3.m: Even with ten thousand speakers or myriads of intellects, / it is impossible to describe your attributes, O Lord.

6.3.s:
tadetaddarśitaṃ rūpaṃ prasādaḥ paramaḥ kṛtaḥ .
chandato jagatāmīśa tadetadupasaṃhara .. 193.47 ..
6.3.d:
तदेतद्दर्शितं रूपं प्रसादः परमः कृतः .
छन्दतो जगतामीश तदेतदुपसंहर .. 193.47 ..
6.3.m: Since this form has been shown, supreme grace has been granted. / By your will, O Lord of the worlds, withdraw it now.

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
ityevaṃ saṃstutastābhirapsarobhirjanārdanaḥ .
divyajñānopapannānāṃ tāsāṃ pratyakṣamīśvaraḥ .. 193.48 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
इत्येवं संस्तुतस्ताभिरप्सरोभिर्जनार्दनः .
दिव्यज्ञानोपपन्नानां तासां प्रत्यक्षमीश्वरः .. 193.48 ..
6.3.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Thus praised by those apsarases, Janārdana, the Lord, / directly visible to those who had attained divine knowledge,

6.3.s:
viveśa sarvabhūtāni svairaṃśairbhūtabhāvanaḥ .
taṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvabhūteṣu līyamānamadhokṣajam .. 193.49 ..
6.3.d:
विवेश सर्वभूतानि स्वैरंशैर्भूतभावनः .
तं दृष्ट्वा सर्वभूतेषु लीयमानमधोक्षजम् .. 193.49 ..
6.3.m: the creator of beings entered all beings with portions of himself. / Seeing Adhokṣaja merging into all beings,

6.3.s:
vismayaṃ paramaṃ cakruḥ samastā devayoṣitaḥ .
sa ca sarveśvaraḥ śailānpādapānsāgarānbhuvam .. 193.50 ..
6.3.d:
विस्मयं परमं चक्रुः समस्ता देवयोषितः .
स च सर्वेश्वरः शैलान्पादपान्सागरान्भुवम् .. 193.50 ..
6.3.m: all the women of the gods felt supreme astonishment. / And that Lord of all entered the mountains, trees, oceans, and earth,

6.3.s:
jalamagniṃ tathā vāyumākāśaṃ ca viveśa ha .
kāle dikṣvatha sarvātma hyātmanaścānyathāpi ca .. 193.51 ..
6.3.d:
जलमग्निं तथा वायुमाकाशं च विवेश ह .
काले दिक्ष्वथ सर्वात्म ह्यात्मनश्चान्यथापि च .. 193.51 ..
6.3.m: water, fire, and wind, and the sky. / In time, in the directions, as the Soul of all, in himself and also elsewhere,

6.3.s:
ātmarūpasthitaṃ svena mahimnā bhāvayañjagat .
devadānavarakṣāṃsi yakṣīvidyādharoragāḥ .. 193.52 ..
6.3.d:
आत्मरूपस्थितं स्वेन महिम्ना भावयञ्जगत् .
देवदानवरक्षांसि यक्षीविद्याधरोरगाः .. 193.52 ..
6.3.m: maintaining the universe situated in his own form by his own greatness— / gods, Dānavas, Rakṣases, Yakṣīs, Vidyādharas, and serpents,

6.3.s:
manuṣyapaśukīṭādimṛgapaśvantarikṣagāḥ .
ye'ntarikṣe tathā bhūmau divi ye ca jalāśrayāḥ .. 193.53 ..
6.3.d:
मनुष्यपशुकीटादिमृगपश्वन्तरिक्षगाः .
येऽन्तरिक्षे तथा भूमौ दिवि ये च जलाश्रयाः .. 193.53 ..
6.3.m: humans, domestic animals, insects, and others, wild beasts, cattle, birds, / those that dwell in the atmosphere, on earth, in heaven, and in water—

6.3.s:
tānviveśa sa viśvātmā punastadrūpamāsthitaḥ .
nareṇa sārdhaṃ yattābhirdṛṣṭapūrvamarindama .. 193.54 ..
6.3.d:
तान्विवेश स विश्वात्मा पुनस्तद्रूपमास्थितः .
नरेण सार्धं यत्ताभिर्दृष्टपूर्वमरिन्दम .. 193.54 ..
6.3.m: that Soul of the universe entered them, and then assumed that form / together with Nara, which had been seen by them before, O vanquisher of foes.

6.3.s:
tāḥ paraṃ vismayaṃ jagmuḥ sarvāstridaśayoṣitaḥ .
praṇemuḥ sādhvasātpāṇḍuvadanā nṛpasattama .. 193.55 ..
6.3.d:
ताः परं विस्मयं जग्मुः सर्वास्त्रिदशयोषितः .
प्रणेमुः साध्वसात्पाण्डुवदना नृपसत्तम .. 193.55 ..
6.3.m: All those women of the gods were filled with supreme amazement; / their faces pale with awe, they bowed down, O best of kings.

6.3.s: nārāyaṇo'pi bhagavānāha tāstridaśāṅganāḥ .. 193.56 ..
6.3.d: नारायणोऽपि भगवानाह तास्त्रिदशाङ्गनाः .. 193.56 ..
6.3.m: The blessed Nārāyaṇa also spoke to those women of the gods.

6.3.s:
nārāyaṇa uvāca -
nīyatāmurvaśī bhadrā yatrāsau tridaśeśvaraḥ .
bhavatīnāṃ hitārthāya sarvabhūteṣvasāviti .. 193.57 ..
6.3.d:
नारायण उवाच -
नीयतामुर्वशी भद्रा यत्रासौ त्रिदशेश्वरः .
भवतीनां हितार्थाय सर्वभूतेष्वसाविति .. 193.57 ..
6.3.m: Nārāyaṇa said: / Let the auspicious Urvaśī be taken to where the Lord of the thirty [gods] is. / For your benefit, [it was shown] that he exists within all beings;

6.3.s:
jñānamutpāditaṃ bhūyo layaṃ bhūteṣu kurvatā .
tadgacchadhvaṃ samasto'yaṃ bhūtagrāmo madaṃśakaḥ .. 193.58 ..
6.3.d:
ज्ञानमुत्पादितं भूयो लयं भूतेषु कुर्वता .
तद्गच्छध्वं समस्तोऽयं भूतग्रामो मदंशकः .. 193.58 ..
6.3.m: knowledge was again produced by merging into beings. / Therefore go! This entire aggregate of beings is a part of me.

6.3.s:
ahamadyātmabhūtasya vāsudevasya yoginaḥ .
asmātparataraṃ nāsti yo'nantaḥ paripathyate .. 193.59 ..
6.3.d:
अहमद्यात्मभूतस्य वासुदेवस्य योगिनः .
अस्मात्परतरं नास्ति योऽनन्तः परिपथ्यते .. 193.59 ..
6.3.m: I today belong to Vāsudeva, the yogin who has become the Self. / There is nothing higher than him who is recited as the Infinite One.

6.3.s:
tamajaṃ sarvabhūteśaṃ jānīta paramaṃ padam .
ahaṃ bhavatyo devāśca manuṣyāḥ paśavaśca ye .
etatsarvamanantasya vāsudevasya vai kṛtam .. 193.60 ..
6.3.d:
तमजं सर्वभूतेशं जानीत परमं पदम् .
अहं भवत्यो देवाश्च मनुष्याः पशवश्च ये .
एतत्सर्वमनन्तस्य वासुदेवस्य वै कृतम् .. 193.60 ..
6.3.m: Know him, the unborn Lord of all beings, to be the supreme state. / I, you, the gods, humans, and domestic animals— / all this is indeed made by the infinite Vāsudeva.

6.3.s:
evaṃ jñātvā samaṃ sarvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam .
sapaśvādiguṇaṃ caiva draṣṭavyaṃ tridaśāṅganāḥ .. 193.61 ..
6.3.d:
एवं ज्ञात्वा समं सर्वं सदेवासुरमानुषम् .
सपश्वादिगुणं चैव द्रष्टव्यं त्रिदशाङ्गनाः .. 193.61 ..
6.3.m: Knowing thus, everything, with gods, Asuras, and humans, / along with the attributes of beasts and others, is to be seen as equal, O women of the gods.

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
ityuktāstena devena samastāstāḥ surastriyaḥ .
praṇamya tau samadanāḥ savasantāśca pārthiva .. 193.62 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
इत्युक्तास्तेन देवेन समस्तास्ताः सुरस्त्रियः .
प्रणम्य तौ समदनाः सवसन्ताश्च पार्थिव .. 193.62 ..
6.3.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Addressed thus by that God, all those women of the gods, / having bowed to the two, together with Madana and Vasanta, O king,

6.3.s:
ādāya corvaśīṃ bhūyo devarājamupāgatāḥ .
ācakhyuśca yathāvṛttaṃ devarājāya tattathā .. 193.63 ..
6.3.d:
आदाय चोर्वशीं भूयो देवराजमुपागताः .
आचख्युश्च यथावृत्तं देवराजाय तत्तथा .. 193.63 ..
6.3.m: and taking Urvaśī, returned to the king of the gods. / And they reported to the king of the gods what had happened exactly as it was.

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tathā tvamapi rājendra sarvabhūteṣu keśavam .
cintayansamatāṃ gaccha samataiva hi muktaye .. 193.64 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
तथा त्वमपि राजेन्द्र सर्वभूतेषु केशवम् .
चिन्तयन्समतां गच्छ समतैव हि मुक्तये .. 193.64 ..
6.3.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Likewise, O best of kings, contemplating Keśava in all beings, / attain equanimity, for equanimity leads to liberation.

6.3.s:
rājannevaṃ viśeṣeṇa bhūteṣu parameśvaram .
vāsudeva kathaṃ doṣāṃllobhādīnna prahāsyasi .. 193.65 ..
6.3.d:
राजन्नेवं विशेषेण भूतेषु परमेश्वरम् .
वासुदेव कथं दोषांल्लोभादीन्न प्रहास्यसि .. 193.65 ..
6.3.m: O King, seeing the Supreme Lord in beings in this specific manner, / as Vāsudeva, how will you not abandon faults such as greed?

6.3.s:
sarvabhūtāni govindādyadā nānyāni bhūpate .
tadā vairādayo bhāvāḥ kriyatāṃ na tu putraka .. 193.66 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वभूतानि गोविन्दाद्यदा नान्यानि भूपते .
तदा वैरादयो भावाः क्रियतां न तु पुत्रक .. 193.66 ..
6.3.m: When all beings are none other than Govinda, O ruler of the earth, / then, my son, let not feelings such as enmity be harbored.

6.3.s:
iti paśya jagatsarvaṃ vāsudevātmakaṃ nṛpa .
etadeva hi kṛṣṇena rūpamāviṣkṛtaṃ nṛpa .. 193.67 ..
6.3.d:
इति पश्य जगत्सर्वं वासुदेवात्मकं नृप .
एतदेव हि कृष्णेन रूपमाविष्कृतं नृप .. 193.67 ..
6.3.m: See the whole universe as made of Vāsudeva in this way, O king. / For this was the very form manifested by Kṛṣṇa, O king.

6.3.s:
parameśvareti yadrūpaṃ tadetatkathitaṃ tava .
janmādibhāvarahitaṃ tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam .. 193.68 ..
6.3.d:
परमेश्वरेति यद्रूपं तदेतत्कथितं तव .
जन्मादिभावरहितं तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् .. 193.68 ..
6.3.m: That form known as 'Supreme Lord'—this has been recounted to you. / Free from states such as birth, that is Viṣṇu's supreme abode.

6.3.s:
saṃkṣepeṇātha bhūpāla śrūyatāṃ yadvadāmi te .
yanmataṃ puruṣaḥ kṛtvā paraṃ nirvāṇamṛcchati .. 193.69 ..
6.3.d:
संक्षेपेणाथ भूपाल श्रूयतां यद्वदामि ते .
यन्मतं पुरुषः कृत्वा परं निर्वाणमृच्छति .. 193.69 ..
6.3.m: Now hear in brief, O protector of the earth, what I say to you, / which view having adopted, a person attains supreme nirvāṇa.

6.3.s:
sarvo viṣṇusamāso hi bhāvābhāvau ca tanmayau .
sadasatsarvamīśo'sau mahādevaḥ paraṃ padam .. 193.70 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वो विष्णुसमासो हि भावाभावौ च तन्मयौ .
सदसत्सर्वमीशोऽसौ महादेवः परं पदम् .. 193.70 ..
6.3.m: For everything is an aggregate of Viṣṇu, and existence and non-existence are composed of him. / He is the real and unreal, all, the Lord, the Great God, the supreme state.

6.3.s:
bhavajaladhigatānāṃ dvandvavātāhatānāṃ sutaduhitṛkalatratrāṇabhārārditānām .
viṣamaviṣayatoye majjatāmaplavānāṃ bhavati śaraṇameko viṣṇupoto narāṇām .. 193.71 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe śrīpatimāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma trinavatyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
6.3.d:
भवजलधिगतानां द्वन्द्ववाताहतानां सुतदुहितृकलत्रत्राणभारार्दितानाम् .
विषमविषयतोये मज्जतामप्लवानां भवति शरणमेको विष्णुपोतो नराणाम् .. 193.71 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे श्रीपतिमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम त्रिनवत्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः ..
6.3.m:
For men who have fallen into the ocean of worldly existence, beaten by the winds of the dualities, / afflicted by the burden of protecting sons, daughters, and wives, / sinking into the perilous waters of sense objects without a raft, / the single ship of Viṣṇu becomes their refuge.
Thus ends the one hundred and ninety-third chapter, named 'Description of the Greatness of the Lord of Śrī,' in the Revākhaṇḍa of the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.

6.3.s:
adhyāya 194
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tacchrutvānāntadevena viśvarūpamudāhṛtam .
devarājastathā devāḥ paraṃ vismayamāgatāḥ .. 194.1 ..
6.3.d:
अध्याय 194
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
तच्छ्रुत्वानान्तदेवेन विश्वरूपमुदाहृतम् .
देवराजस्तथा देवाः परं विस्मयमागताः .. 194.1 ..
6.3.m: Chapter 194. / Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having heard that universal form described by the infinite God, / the king of the gods and the gods were filled with supreme wonder.

6.3.s:
dṛṣṭvā cāpsarasaṃ puṇyāmurvaśīṃ kamalānanām .
saṃtrasto vismitaścābhūdindro rājaśriyā vṛtaḥ .. 194.2 ..
6.3.d:
दृष्ट्वा चाप्सरसं पुण्यामुर्वशीं कमलाननाम् .
संत्रस्तो विस्मितश्चाभूदिन्द्रो राजश्रिया वृतः .. 194.2 ..
6.3.m: And seeing the holy apsaras Urvaśī, whose face was like a lotus, / Indra, surrounded by royal splendor, became terrified and astonished.

6.3.s:
na kiṃciduttaraṃ vākyamuktavāñjoṣamāsthitaḥ .
iti vṛttāntabhūtaṃ hi nārāyaṇaviceṣṭitam .. 194.3 ..
6.3.d:
न किंचिदुत्तरं वाक्यमुक्तवाञ्जोषमास्थितः .
इति वृत्तान्तभूतं हि नारायणविचेष्टितम् .. 194.3 ..
6.3.m: He did not speak a single word in reply, remaining silent. / For such was the event, the deed of Nārāyaṇa.

6.3.s:
bhṛgoḥ khātyāṃ(?) samutpannā lakṣmīḥ śrutvā tu vai nṛpa .
vaiśvarūpaṃ paraṃ rūpaṃ vismitācintayattadā .. 194.4 ..
6.3.d:
भृगोः खात्यां(?) समुत्पन्ना लक्ष्मीः श्रुत्वा तु वै नृप .
वैश्वरूपं परं रूपं विस्मिताचिन्तयत्तदा .. 194.4 ..
6.3.m: Hearing of that supreme universal form, Lakṣmī, born from Khyāti and Bhṛgu, / was astonished, O king, and reflected at that time.

6.3.s:
kenopāyena sa syānme bhartā nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ .
vratena tapasā vāpi dānena niyamena ca .. 194.5 ..
6.3.d:
केनोपायेन स स्यान्मे भर्ता नारायणः प्रभुः .
व्रतेन तपसा वापि दानेन नियमेन च .. 194.5 ..
6.3.m: "By what means can that Lord Nārāyaṇa become my husband? / By vow, or by austerity, by gift, or by discipline, // 194.5

6.3.s:
vṛddhānāṃ sevanenātha devatārādhanena vā .
iti cintāparāṃ kanyāṃ satī jñātvā yudhiṣṭhira .. 194.6 ..
6.3.d:
वृद्धानां सेवनेनाथ देवताराधनेन वा .
इति चिन्तापरां कन्यां सती ज्ञात्वा युधिष्ठिर .. 194.6 ..
6.3.m: by serving elders, or by worshipping deities?" / Knowing the maiden to be devoted to such thoughts, O Yudhiṣṭhira, Satī // 194.6

6.3.s:
prāha prāpto mayā bhartā śaṅkarastapasā kila .
prajāpatiśca gāyatryā hyanyābhirabhivāñchitāḥ .. 194.7 ..
6.3.d:
प्राह प्राप्तो मया भर्ता शङ्करस्तपसा किल .
प्रजापतिश्च गायत्र्या ह्यन्याभिरभिवाञ्छिताः .. 194.7 ..
6.3.m: said: "Indeed, through austerity Śaṅkara was obtained by me as husband, / and Prajāpati by Gāyatrī, and [other lords] by other [women] who desired them. // 194.7

6.3.s:
tapasaiva hi te prāpyastasmāttaccara suvrate .
tapastvaṃ hi mahaccograṃ sarvavāñchitadāyakam .. 194.8 ..
6.3.d:
तपसैव हि ते प्राप्यस्तस्मात्तच्चर सुव्रते .
तपस्त्वं हि महच्चोग्रं सर्ववाञ्छितदायकम् .. 194.8 ..
6.3.m: He can only be obtained by you through austerity; therefore perform it, O lady of good vows! / For austere, fierce austerity bestows all desired things." // 194.8

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
sāgarāntaṃ samāsādya lakṣmīḥ parapuraṃjaya .
cacāra vipulaṃ kālaṃ tapaḥ paramaduścaram .. 194.9 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
सागरान्तं समासाद्य लक्ष्मीः परपुरंजय .
चचार विपुलं कालं तपः परमदुश्चरम् .. 194.9 ..
6.3.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having gone to the seashore, O conqueror of enemy cities, / Lakṣmī practiced most difficult austerity for a vast period of time. // 194.9

6.3.s:
sthāṇuvatsaṃsthitā sābhūddivyaṃ varṣasahasrakam .
tata indrādayo devāḥ śaṅkhacakragadādharāḥ .. 194.10 ..
6.3.d:
स्थाणुवत्संस्थिता साभूद्दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रकम् .
तत इन्द्रादयो देवाः शङ्खचक्रगदाधराः .. 194.10 ..
6.3.m: She remained motionless like a pillar for a thousand divine years. / Then the gods, Indra and others, bearing the conch, discus, and mace, // 194.10

6.3.s:
bhūtvā jagmustadarthaṃ te sā tu pṛṣṭavatī surān .
viśvarūpaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ yattaddarśayata māciram .. 194.11 ..
6.3.d:
भूत्वा जग्मुस्तदर्थं ते सा तु पृष्टवती सुरान् .
विश्वरूपं वैष्णवं यत्तद्दर्शयत माचिरम् .. 194.11 ..
6.3.m: went for that purpose having assumed [Viṣṇu's form]. But she asked the gods: / "Show me without delay the universal form belonging to Viṣṇu!" // 194.11

6.3.s:
vilakṣā vrīḍitā devā gatvā nārāyaṇaṃ tadā .
abruvan vaiśvarūpaṃ no śaktā darśayituṃ vayam .. 194.12 ..
6.3.d:
विलक्षा व्रीडिता देवा गत्वा नारायणं तदा .
अब्रुवन् वैश्वरूपं नो शक्ता दर्शयितुं वयम् .. 194.12 ..
6.3.m: Discomfited and ashamed, the gods went then to Nārāyaṇa / and said: "We are unable to show the universal form." // 194.12

6.3.s:
tato yatheṣṭaṃ te jagmuḥ sa ca viṣṇuracintayat .
ugrarūpā sthitā devī dehaṃ dahati bhārgavī .. 194.13 ..
6.3.d:
ततो यथेष्टं ते जग्मुः स च विष्णुरचिन्तयत् .
उग्ररूपा स्थिता देवी देहं दहति भार्गवी .. 194.13 ..
6.3.m: Then they departed wherever they wished, and Viṣṇu reflected: / "The goddess, the daughter of Bhṛgu, assuming a fierce form, is burning her body [with austerities]. // 194.13

6.3.s:
tāṃ tasmāttatra gatvāhaṃ varaṃ dattvā tu vāñchitam .
punastapaḥ kariṣyāmi darśayiṣyāmi vā punaḥ .
vaiṣṇavaṃ viśvarūpaṃ yaddurdaśyaṃ devadānavaiḥ .. 194.14 ..
6.3.d:
तां तस्मात्तत्र गत्वाहं वरं दत्त्वा तु वाञ्छितम् .
पुनस्तपः करिष्यामि दर्शयिष्यामि वा पुनः .
वैष्णवं विश्वरूपं यद्दुर्दश्यं देवदानवैः .. 194.14 ..
6.3.m: Therefore, having gone there and granted her the desired boon, / I shall practice austerity again, or I shall show again / that universal form belonging to Viṣṇu, difficult to see for gods and demons." // 194.14

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gatvā hṛṣīkeśaḥ sāgarāntasthitāṃ śriyam .
prāha tuṣṭo'smi te devi varaṃ vṛṇu yathepsitam .. 194.15 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गत्वा हृषीकेशः सागरान्तस्थितां श्रियम् .
प्राह तुष्टोऽस्मि ते देवि वरं वृणु यथेप्सितम् .. 194.15 ..
6.3.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then, having gone, Hṛṣīkeśa spoke to Śrī stationed at the edge of the sea: / "I am pleased with you, O goddess; choose a boon as you desire!" // 194.15

6.3.s:
śrīruvāca -
yadi tuṣṭo'si me deva prapannāyā janārdana .
tadā darśaya yaddṛṣṭamapsarobhistavānagha .. 194.16 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीरुवाच -
यदि तुष्टोऽसि मे देव प्रपन्नाया जनार्दन .
तदा दर्शय यद्दृष्टमप्सरोभिस्तवानघ .. 194.16 ..
6.3.m: Śrī said: / "If you are pleased with me, O god Janārdana, who have sought refuge, / then show [me], O sinless one, what was seen by your apsarases— // 194.16

6.3.s:
viśvarūpamanantaṃ ca bhūtabhāvana keśava .
gandhamādanamāsādya kṛtaṃ yacca tapastvayā .. 194.17 ..
6.3.d:
विश्वरूपमनन्तं च भूतभावन केशव .
गन्धमादनमासाद्य कृतं यच्च तपस्त्वया .. 194.17 ..
6.3.m: the boundless universal form, O Keśava, source of beings, / and the austerity that was performed by you after reaching Gandhamādana. // 194.17

6.3.s:
tadvadasva vibho viṣṇo na mithyā yadi keśava .
śraddadhāmi na caivāhaṃ rūpasyāsya kathaṃcana .. 194.18 ..
6.3.d:
तद्वदस्व विभो विष्णो न मिथ्या यदि केशव .
श्रद्दधामि न चैवाहं रूपस्यास्य कथंचन .. 194.18 ..
6.3.m: Tell me of that, O all-pervading Viṣṇu, if it is not false, O Keśava! / For I do not put my faith in this form in any way. // 194.18

6.3.s:
bahubhiryakṣarakṣobhirmāyācāripracāribhiḥ .
chanditā mama jānadbhirbhāvamantargataṃ harau .. 194.19 ..
6.3.d:
बहुभिर्यक्षरक्षोभिर्मायाचारिप्रचारिभिः .
छन्दिता मम जानद्भिर्भावमन्तर्गतं हरौ .. 194.19 ..
6.3.m: I was courted by many Yakṣas and Rākṣasas who move by magical illusions, / who knew my inner sentiment directed toward Hari. // 194.19

6.3.s:
bhūtvā viṣṇusvarūpāste cakriṇaśca caturbhujāḥ .
suvrīḍitā gatāḥ sarve viśvarūpo sahāyataḥ .. 194.20 ..
6.3.d:
भूत्वा विष्णुस्वरूपास्ते चक्रिणश्च चतुर्भुजाः .
सुव्रीडिता गताः सर्वे विश्वरूपो सहायतः .. 194.20 ..
6.3.m: Assuming the form of Viṣṇu, four-armed and holding the discus, / they all went away deeply ashamed, because of the help of [your] universal form." // 194.20

6.3.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
nārāyaṇo'tha bhagavāñchaṅkhacakragadābhṛtam .
tayā tathoktastadrūpaṃ muktvā vai surapūjitam .. 194.21 ..
6.3.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच -
नारायणोऽथ भगवाञ्छङ्खचक्रगदाभृतम् .
तया तथोक्तस्तद्रूपं मुक्त्वा वै सुरपूजितम् .. 194.21 ..
6.3.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then Lord Nārāyaṇa, having been addressed thus by her, / set aside that form bearing the conch, discus, and mace, which is worshipped by the gods, // 194.21

6.3.s:
rūpaṃ paraṃ yathoktaṃ vai viśvarūpamadarśayat .
darśayitvā vacaḥ prāha pañcarātravidhānataḥ .. 194.22 ..
6.3.d:
रूपं परं यथोक्तं वै विश्वरूपमदर्शयत् .
दर्शयित्वा वचः प्राह पञ्चरात्रविधानतः .. 194.22 ..
6.3.m: and displayed his supreme universal form as described. / Having shown it, he spoke these words according to the rite of the Pañcarātra: // 194.22

6.3.s:
yo'rcayiṣyati māṃ nityaṃ sa pūjyaḥ sa ca pūjitaḥ .
dhanadhānyasamāyuktaḥ sarvabhogasamanvitaḥ .. 194.23 ..
6.3.d:
योऽर्चयिष्यति मां नित्यं स पूज्यः स च पूजितः .
धनधान्यसमायुक्तः सर्वभोगसमन्वितः .. 194.23 ..
6.3.m: "Whoever worships me daily, he is worthy of worship and is worshipped, / endowed with wealth and grain, and provided with all enjoyments. // 194.23

6.3.s:
mūlaṃ hi sarvadharmāṇāṃ brahmacaryaṃ paraṃ tapaḥ .
tenāhaṃ tatra sthāsyāmi mūlaśrīpatisaṃjñitaḥ .. 194.24 ..
6.3.d:
मूलं हि सर्वधर्माणां ब्रह्मचर्यं परं तपः .
तेनाहं तत्र स्थास्यामि मूलश्रीपतिसंज्ञितः .. 194.24 ..
6.3.m: Celibacy is the supreme austerity, the root indeed of all virtues; / therefore I will dwell there under the name Mūlaśrīpati. // 194.24

6.3.s:
mūlaśrīḥ procyate brāhmī brahmacaryasvarūpiṇī .
sarvayogamayī puṇyā sarvapāpaharī śubhā .. 194.25 ..
6.3.d:
मूलश्रीः प्रोच्यते ब्राह्मी ब्रह्मचर्यस्वरूपिणी .
सर्वयोगमयी पुण्या सर्वपापहरी शुभा .. 194.25 ..
6.3.m: The primordial Fortune (Mūlaśrī) is declared to be the Brāhmī power, having the nature of celibacy, / consisting of all yogas, meritorious, dispelling all sin, and auspicious. // 194.25

6.3.s:
patistasyāḥ prabhurahaṃ varadaḥ prāṇināṃ priye .
revājale naraḥ snātvā yo'rcayenmāṃ yatavrataḥ .. 194.26 ..
6.3.d:
पतिस्तस्याः प्रभुरहं वरदः प्राणिनां प्रिये .
रेवाजले नरः स्नात्वा योऽर्चयेन्मां यतव्रतः .. 194.26 ..
6.3.m: I am her lord and master, granting boons to living beings, O beloved! / That man who, having bathed in the waters of the Revā and restrained his vows, worships me // 194.26

6.3.s:
mūlaśrīpatināmānaṃ vāñchite prāpnuyātphalam .
dānāni tatra yo dadyānmahādānāni ca priye .. 194.27 ..
6.3.d:
मूलश्रीपतिनामानं वाञ्छिते प्राप्नुयात्फलम् .
दानानि तत्र यो दद्यान्महादानानि च प्रिये .. 194.27 ..
6.3.m: named Mūlaśrīpati, shall obtain his desired fruit. / Whoever gives gifts there, and Great Gifts, O beloved, // 194.27

6.3.s:
sahasraguṇitaṃ puṇyamanyasthānādavāpyate .
dṛṣṭaṃ tvayā tatra deśe samyakcaivāvadhāritam .
tadarcitvā parān kāmānāpsyasi tvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .. 194.28 ..
6.3.d:
सहस्रगुणितं पुण्यमन्यस्थानादवाप्यते .
दृष्टं त्वया तत्र देशे सम्यक्चैवावधारितम् .
