tairdahyamānā bahuśo vilapanti muhurmuhuḥ .. 209.74 ..
6.3.d:
छायां संप्रार्थमानानां भृशं ज्वलति पावकः .
तैर्दह्यमाना बहुशो विलपन्ति मुहुर्मुहुः .. 209.74 ..
6.3.m: for those seeking shade, fire blazes violently. / Burned by these repeatedly, they lament again and again:

6.3.s:
hā bhrātarmātaḥ putreti patanti pathi mūrchitāḥ .
itthaṃbhūtena mārgeṇa sa gīto yamakiṃkaraiḥ .. 209.75 ..
6.3.d:
हा भ्रातर्मातः पुत्रेति पतन्ति पथि मूर्छिताः .
इत्थंभूतेन मार्गेण स गीतो यमकिंकरैः .. 209.75 ..
6.3.m: 'Alas, brother! Mother! Son!'—and they fall swooning upon the path. / Along such a path was he brought by the servants of Yama

6.3.s:
yatra tiṣṭhati deveśaḥ prajāsaṃyamano yamaḥ .
te dvāradeśe taṃ muktvācakṣuryamakiṃkarāḥ .. 209.76 ..
6.3.d:
यत्र तिष्ठति देवेशः प्रजासंयमनो यमः .
ते द्वारदेशे तं मुक्त्वाचक्षुर्यमकिंकराः .. 209.76 ..
6.3.m: to where Yama, the lord of gods, the restrainer of creatures, resides. / Leaving him at the entrance, the servants of Yama said:

6.3.s:
baddhvā taṃ galapāśena hyāsīnaṃ mitraghātinam .
avadhāraya deveśa budhyasva yadanantaram .. 209.77 ..
6.3.d:
बद्ध्वा तं गलपाशेन ह्यासीनं मित्रघातिनम् .
अवधारय देवेश बुध्यस्व यदनन्तरम् .. 209.77 ..
6.3.m: 'Having bound this murderer of a friend by a noose around his neck, he sits here. / Take notice, O lord of gods, and determine what should follow next.'

6.3.s:
yama uvāca -
na tu pūrvaṃ mukhaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ mayā viśvāsaghātinām .
ye mitradrohiṇaḥ pāpāsteṣāṃ kiṃ śāsanaṃ bhavet .. 209.78 ..
6.3.d:
यम उवाच -
न तु पूर्वं मुखं दृष्टं मया विश्वासघातिनाम् .
ये मित्रद्रोहिणः पापास्तेषां किं शासनं भवेत् .. 209.78 ..
6.3.m: Yama said: / 'Never before have I looked upon the face of betrayers of trust. / As for those wicked ones who harm their friends, what punishment should there be?

6.3.s:
ṛṣayo'tra vicārārthaṃ niyuktā nipuṇāḥ sthitāḥ .
te yatra bruvate tatra kṣipadhvaṃ mā vicāryatām .. 209.79 ..
6.3.d:
ऋषयोऽत्र विचारार्थं नियुक्ता निपुणाः स्थिताः .
ते यत्र ब्रुवते तत्र क्षिपध्वं मा विचार्यताम् .. 209.79 ..
6.3.m: The wise seers appointed for deliberation are present here; / cast him wherever they say—do not hesitate.'

6.3.s:
ityuktāste tamādāya kiṃkarāḥ śīghragāminaḥ .
munīśāṃstatra tānūcustaṃ nivedya yamājñayā .. 209.80 ..
6.3.d:
इत्युक्तास्ते तमादाय किंकराः शीघ्रगामिनः .
मुनीशांस्तत्र तानूचुस्तं निवेद्य यमाज्ञया .. 209.80 ..
6.3.m: Having been spoken to thus, those swift-moving servants, taking him, / presented him by Yama's order and spoke to the great sages there.

6.3.s:
dvijā anena mitraṃ svaṃ prasuptaṃ niśi ghātitam .
viśvastaṃ dhanalobhena ko daṇḍo'sya bhaviṣyati .. 209.81 ..
6.3.d:
द्विजा अनेन मित्रं स्वं प्रसुप्तं निशि घातितम् .
विश्वस्तं धनलोभेन को दण्डोऽस्य भविष्यति .. 209.81 ..
6.3.m:
"O brahmins, by him his own friend, who was asleep at night
and full of trust, was slain out of greed for wealth. What shall his punishment be?"

6.3.s:
munaya ūcuḥ .
adṛṣṭapūrvamasmābhirvadanaṃ mitraghātinām .
kṛtvā paṭāntare hyenaṃ śṛṇvantu gatimasya tām .. 209.82 ..
6.3.d:
मुनय ऊचुः .
अदृष्टपूर्वमस्माभिर्वदनं मित्रघातिनाम् .
कृत्वा पटान्तरे ह्येनं शृण्वन्तु गतिमस्य ताम् .. 209.82 ..
6.3.m:
The sages said:
"Never before have we seen the face of murderers of friends.
Having put him behind a screen, let them hear his destination."

6.3.s:
te śāstrāṇi vicāryātha ṛṣayaśca parasparam .
āhūya yamadūtāṃstānūcurbrāhmaṇapuṃgavāḥ .. 209.83 ..
6.3.d:
ते शास्त्राणि विचार्याथ ऋषयश्च परस्परम् .
आहूय यमदूतांस्तानूचुर्ब्राह्मणपुंगवाः .. 209.83 ..
6.3.m:
Then, having deliberated among themselves over the scriptures,
those seers, foremost among brahmins, summoned the messengers of Yama and said:

6.3.s:
ālokitāni śāstrāṇi vedāḥ sāṅgāḥ smṛtīrapi .
purāṇāni ca mīmāṃsā dṛṣṭamasmābhiratra ca .. 209.84 ..
6.3.d:
आलोकितानि शास्त्राणि वेदाः साङ्गाः स्मृतीरपि .
पुराणानि च मीमांसा दृष्टमस्माभिरत्र च .. 209.84 ..
6.3.m:
"The scriptures have been examined—the Vedas along with their limbs, the Smṛtis,
the Purāṇas, and the Mīmāṃsā—and this has been seen by us here:

6.3.s:
brahmaghne ca surāpe ca steye gurvaṅganāgame .
niṣkṛtirvihitā śāstre kṛtaghne nāsti niṣkṛtiḥ .. 209.85 ..
6.3.d:
ब्रह्मघ्ने च सुरापे च स्तेये गुर्वङ्गनागमे .
निष्कृतिर्विहिता शास्त्रे कृतघ्ने नास्ति निष्कृतिः .. 209.85 ..
6.3.m:
For a slayer of a brahmin, for a drinker of liquor, for theft, and for violation of the guru's bed,
an expiation is prescribed in scripture; for the ungrateful, there is no expiation.

6.3.s:
ye strīghnāśca gurughnāśca ye bālabrahmaghātinaḥ .
vihitā niṣkṛtiḥ śāstre kṛtaghne nāsti niṣkṛtiḥ .. 209.86 ..
6.3.d:
ये स्त्रीघ्नाश्च गुरुघ्नाश्च ये बालब्रह्मघातिनः .
विहिता निष्कृतिः शास्त्रे कृतघ्ने नास्ति निष्कृतिः .. 209.86 ..
6.3.m:
For those who murder women, who murder gurus, and who murder children and brahmins,
an expiation is prescribed in scripture; for the ungrateful, there is no expiation.

6.3.s:
vāpīkūpataḍāgānāṃ bhettāro ye ca pāpinaḥ .
udyānavāṭikānāṃ ca chettāro ye ca durjanāḥ .. 209.87 ..
6.3.d:
वापीकूपतडागानां भेत्तारो ये च पापिनः .
उद्यानवाटिकानां च छेत्तारो ये च दुर्जनाः .. 209.87 ..
6.3.m:
Those sinners who breach cisterns, wells, and tanks,
and those wicked people who fell gardens and groves;

6.3.s:
dāvāgnidāhakā ye ca satataṃ ye'suhiṃsakāḥ .
nyāsāpahāriṇo ye ca garadāḥ svāmivañcakāḥ .. 209.88 ..
6.3.d:
दावाग्निदाहका ये च सततं येऽसुहिंसकाः .
न्यासापहारिणो ये च गरदाः स्वामिवञ्चकाः .. 209.88 ..
6.3.m:
and those who kindle forest fires, those who constantly slay living beings,
those who steal deposits, poisoners, and deceivers of their master;

6.3.s:
mātāpitṛgurūṇāṃ ca tyāgino doṣadāyinaḥ .
svabhartṛvañcanaparā yā strī garbhapraghātinī .. 209.89 ..
6.3.d:
मातापितृगुरूणां च त्यागिनो दोषदायिनः .
स्वभर्तृवञ्चनपरा या स्त्री गर्भप्रघातिनी .. 209.89 ..
6.3.m:
those who abandon their mother, father, and gurus, and cast blame upon them;
the woman intent on deceiving her husband, and she who destroys an embryo;

6.3.s:
vivekarahitā yā strī yāsnātā bhojane ratā .
dvikālabhojanaratāstathā vaiṣṇavavāsare .. 209.90 ..
6.3.d:
विवेकरहिता या स्त्री यास्नाता भोजने रता .
द्विकालभोजनरतास्तथा वैष्णववासरे .. 209.90 ..
6.3.m:
the woman devoid of discrimination, she who is devoted to eating without having bathed,
and likewise those devoted to eating twice on the day of Viṣṇu—

6.3.s:
tāsāṃ strīṇāṃ gatirdṛṣṭā na tu viśvāsaghātinām .
viśvāsaghātināṃ puṃsāṃ mitradrohakṛtāṃ tathā .. 209.91 ..
6.3.d:
तासां स्त्रीणां गतिर्दृष्टा न तु विश्वासघातिनाम् .
विश्वासघातिनां पुंसां मित्रद्रोहकृतां तथा .. 209.91 ..
6.3.m:
for such women a destination is seen, but not for betrayers of trust.
For men who betray trust and who commit treason against friends,

6.3.s:
teṣāṃ gatirna vedeṣu purāṇeṣu ca kā kathā .
iti sthiteṣu pāpeṣu gatireṣāṃ na vidyate .. 209.92 ..
6.3.d:
तेषां गतिर्न वेदेषु पुराणेषु च का कथा .
इति स्थितेषु पापेषु गतिरेषां न विद्यते .. 209.92 ..
6.3.m:
their destination is not [found] in the Vedas—what need to speak of the Purāṇas?
Thus among established sins, no destination is found for these.

6.3.s:
nānyā gatirmitrahanane viśvastaghne ca naḥ śrutam .
ito nītvā yamadūtā enaṃ viśvastaghātinam .. 209.93 ..
6.3.d:
नान्या गतिर्मित्रहनने विश्वस्तघ्ने च नः श्रुतम् .
इतो नीत्वा यमदूता एनं विश्वस्तघातिनम् .. 209.93 ..
6.3.m:
No other destination has been heard by us for the slaying of a friend and the killing of one who trusted.
Taking this betrayer of trust from here, O messengers of Yama,

6.3.s:
kalpakoṭiśataṃ sāgraṃ paryāyeṇa pṛthakpṛthak .
narakeṣu ca sarveṣu triṃśatkoṭiṣu saṃkhyayā .. 209.94 ..
6.3.d:
कल्पकोटिशतं साग्रं पर्यायेण पृथक्पृथक् .
नरकेषु च सर्वेषु त्रिंशत्कोटिषु संख्यया .. 209.94 ..
6.3.m:
for more than a hundred crore kalpas, in turn, one by one,
across all the hells numbering thirty crores,

6.3.s:
kṣipyatāmeṣa mitraghno vicāro mā vidhīyatām .
iti te vacanaṃ śrutvā kiṃkarāstaṃ nigṛhya ca .. 209.95 ..
6.3.d:
क्षिप्यतामेष मित्रघ्नो विचारो मा विधीयताम् .
इति ते वचनं श्रुत्वा किंकरास्तं निगृह्य च .. 209.95 ..
6.3.m:
let this slayer of a friend be cast! Let there be no hesitation!"
Having heard their word, the servants seized him, and

6.3.s:
yatra te narakā ghorāstatra kṣeptuṃ gatāstataḥ .
te tamādāya hi narake ghore rauravasaṃjñite .. 209.96 ..
6.3.d:
यत्र ते नरका घोरास्तत्र क्षेप्तुं गतास्ततः .
ते तमादाय हि नरके घोरे रौरवसंज्ञिते .. 209.96 ..
6.3.m:
went from there to cast him where those terrible hells are.
Taking him, into that dreadful hell called Raurava

6.3.s:
cikṣipustatra pāpiṣṭhaṃ kṣipte rāvo'bhavanmahān .
narakasthitabhūteṣu moktavyo naiṣa pāpakṛt .. 209.97 ..
6.3.d:
चिक्षिपुस्तत्र पापिष्ठं क्षिप्ते रावोऽभवन्महान् .
नरकस्थितभूतेषु मोक्तव्यो नैष पापकृत् .. 209.97 ..
6.3.m:
they threw that most wicked man. When he was thrown, a great cry arose
among the beings residing in the hell: "This evildoer must not be released!

6.3.s:
asya saṃsparśanādeva pīḍā śataguṇā bhavet .
yathā vyathāsikāṣṭhaiśca samiddhairdahanātmakaiḥ .. 209.98 ..
6.3.d:
अस्य संस्पर्शनादेव पीडा शतगुणा भवेत् .
यथा व्यथासिकाष्ठैश्च समिद्धैर्दहनात्मकैः .. 209.98 ..
6.3.m:
From his very touch our torment would become a hundredfold!
Just as pain arises from firebrands of wood ablaze with fire,

6.3.s:
bhavati sparśanāttasya kimetena kṛtāmalam .
yathā durjanasaṃsargātsujano yāti lāghavam .. 209.99 ..
6.3.d:
भवति स्पर्शनात्तस्य किमेतेन कृतामलम् .
यथा दुर्जनसंसर्गात्सुजनो याति लाघवम् .. 209.99 ..
6.3.m:
so it happens from touching him! What has this polluted wretch done?
Just as a good person suffers degradation from contact with the wicked,

6.3.s:
sannidhānāttathāsyāśu kṣate kṣārāvasecanam .
prasādaḥ kriyatāmāśu nīyatāṃ narake'nyataḥ .. 209.100 ..
6.3.d:
सन्निधानात्तथास्याशु क्षते क्षारावसेचनम् .
प्रसादः क्रियतामाशु नीयतां नरकेऽन्यतः .. 209.100 ..
6.3.m:
so from his proximity it is like pouring salt onto a wound!
Show mercy quickly! Let him be taken elsewhere in hell!"

6.3.s:
evamuktāstatastaistu gatāste tvaśuciṃ prati .
tatra te nārakāḥ santi pūrvavatte'pi cukruśuḥ .. 209.101 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्तास्ततस्तैस्तु गतास्ते त्वशुचिं प्रति .
तत्र ते नारकाः सन्ति पूर्ववत्तेऽपि चुक्रुशुः .. 209.101 ..
6.3.m:
Having been spoken to thus by them, they went toward the Impure Hell.
There those denizens of hell were, and they too cried out just as before.

6.3.s:
evaṃ te kiṃkarāḥ sarve paryaṭannarakamaṇḍale .
narake'pi sthitistasya nāsti pāpasya durmateḥ .. 209.102 ..
6.3.d:
एवं ते किंकराः सर्वे पर्यटन्नरकमण्डले .
नरकेऽपि स्थितिस्तस्य नास्ति पापस्य दुर्मतेः .. 209.102 ..
6.3.m:
In this manner all those servants wandered through the realm of hells;
even in hell there was no place for that evil-minded sinner.

6.3.s:
yadā tadā tu te sarve taṃ gṛhya yamasannidhau .
gatvā nivedya tatsarvaṃ yaduktaṃ nārakairnaraiḥ .
narake na sthitiryasya tasya kiṃ kriyatāṃ vada .. 209.103 ..
6.3.d:
यदा तदा तु ते सर्वे तं गृह्य यमसन्निधौ .
गत्वा निवेद्य तत्सर्वं यदुक्तं नारकैर्नरैः .
नरके न स्थितिर्यस्य तस्य किं क्रियतां वद .. 209.103 ..
6.3.m:
Then they all, taking him, went into the presence of Yama,
and reported all that had been said by the people of hell:
"Tell us, what should be done with him who has no place in hell?"

6.3.s:
yama uvāca -
pāpiṣṭha eṣa vai yātu yoniṃ tiryaṅniṣevitām .
kālaṃ munibhiruddiṣṭaḥ tiryagyoniṃ praveśyatām .. 209.104 ..
6.3.d:
यम उवाच -
पापिष्ठ एष वै यातु योनिं तिर्यङ्निषेविताम् .
कालं मुनिभिरुद्दिष्टः तिर्यग्योनिं प्रवेश्यताम् .. 209.104 ..
6.3.m:
Yama said:
"Indeed, let this most sinful one go into a womb frequented by beasts.
For the period of time indicated by the sages, let him be cast into an animal womb."

6.3.s:
evamukte tu vacane prajāsaṃyamanena ca .
sa gataḥ kṛmitāṃ pāpo viṣṭhāsu ca pṛthakpṛthak .. 209.105 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्ते तु वचने प्रजासंयमनेन च .
स गतः कृमितां पापो विष्ठासु च पृथक्पृथक् .. 209.105 ..
6.3.m:
When that word was spoken by the Restrainer of Creatures,
that sinner became a worm, successively in various excrements.

6.3.s:
tato'sau daṃśamaśakān pipīlikasamudbhavān .
yūkāmatkuṇakāḍhyāṃśca gatvā pakṣitvamāgataḥ .. 209.106 ..
6.3.d:
ततोऽसौ दंशमशकान् पिपीलिकसमुद्भवान् .
यूकामत्कुणकाढ्यांश्च गत्वा पक्षित्वमागतः .. 209.106 ..
6.3.m:
Then having gone through [the states of] gadflies, mosquitoes, born as ants,
and full of lice and bedbugs, he attained the state of a bird.

6.3.s:
sthāvaratvaṃ gataḥ paścātpāṣāṇatvaṃ tataḥ param .
sarīsṛpānajagaravarāhamṛgahastinaḥ .. 209.107 ..
6.3.d:
स्थावरत्वं गतः पश्चात्पाषाणत्वं ततः परम् .
सरीसृपानजगरवराहमृगहस्तिनः .. 209.107 ..
6.3.m:
Afterward he attained the state of an immobile plant, and after that the state of a stone;
then serpents, pythons, boars, deer, elephants,

6.3.s:
vṛkaśvānakharoṣṭrāṃśca sūkarīṃ grāmajātikām .
yonimāśvatarīṃ prāpya tathā mahiṣasambhavām .. 209.108 ..
6.3.d:
वृकश्वानखरोष्ट्रांश्च सूकरीं ग्रामजातिकाम् .
योनिमाश्वतरीं प्राप्य तथा महिषसम्भवाम् .. 209.108 ..
6.3.m:
wolves, dogs, donkeys, camels, and village sows,
having attained the womb of a mule and likewise born of a buffalo—

6.3.s:
etāścānyāśca bahvīrvai prāpa yonīḥ krameṇa vai .
sa tā yonīranuprāpya dhuryo'bhūdbhāravāhakaḥ .. 209.109 ..
6.3.d:
एताश्चान्याश्च बह्वीर्वै प्राप योनीः क्रमेण वै .
स ता योनीरनुप्राप्य धुर्योऽभूद्भारवाहकः .. 209.109 ..
6.3.m:
these and many other wombs he indeed attained in succession.
Having passed through those wombs, he became a draft animal carrying loads.

6.3.s:
sa gṛhe pārthiveśasya dhārmikasya yaśasvinaḥ .
sa dṛṣṭvā kārttikīṃ prāptāmekadā nṛpasattamaḥ .. 209.110 ..
6.3.d:
स गृहे पार्थिवेशस्य धार्मिकस्य यशस्विनः .
स दृष्ट्वा कार्त्तिकीं प्राप्तामेकदा नृपसत्तमः .. 209.110 ..
6.3.m:
In the house of a righteous and renowned king,
that best of kings, having seen that the full-moon day of Kārttika had arrived, once

6.3.s:
purohitaṃ samāhūya brāhmaṇāṃśca tathā bahūn .
na gṛhe kārttikīṃ kuryādetanme bahuśaḥ śrutam .. 209.111 ..
6.3.d:
पुरोहितं समाहूय ब्राह्मणांश्च तथा बहून् .
न गृहे कार्त्तिकीं कुर्यादेतन्मे बहुशः श्रुतम् .. 209.111 ..
6.3.m:
summoned his family priest and many brahmins, [saying:]
"One should not observe the Kārttika full-moon at home; this has been heard by me many times.

6.3.s:
sametāḥ kutra yāsyāma iti brūta dvijottamāḥ .
yo gṛhe kārttikīṃ kuryātsnānadānādivarjitaḥ .. 209.112 ..
6.3.d:
समेताः कुत्र यास्याम इति ब्रूत द्विजोत्तमाः .
यो गृहे कार्त्तिकीं कुर्यात्स्नानदानादिवर्जितः .. 209.112 ..
6.3.m:
Where shall we go together? Speak, O best of brahmins!
Whoever spends the Kārttika full-moon at home, devoid of bathing, gifting, and the like,

6.3.s:
saṃvatsarakṛtātpuṇyātsa bahirbhavati śrutiḥ .
tasmātsarvaprayatnena tīrthaṃ sarvaguṇānvitam .. 209.113 ..
6.3.d:
संवत्सरकृतात्पुण्यात्स बहिर्भवति श्रुतिः .
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन तीर्थं सर्वगुणान्वितम् .. 209.113 ..
6.3.m:
falls outside the religious merit accrued over a year, so says the Veda.
Therefore, with every effort, to a sacred ford endowed with all virtues

6.3.s:
sahitāstatra gacchāmaḥ snātuṃ dātuṃ ca śaktitaḥ .
evamukte tu vacane pārthivena dvijottamāḥ .. 209.114 ..
6.3.d:
सहितास्तत्र गच्छामः स्नातुं दातुं च शक्तितः .
एवमुक्ते तु वचने पार्थिवेन द्विजोत्तमाः .. 209.114 ..
6.3.m:
let us go together, to bathe and to give according to our capacity."
When that statement was made by the king, the best of brahmins

6.3.s:
ūcuḥ śreṣṭhaṃ nṛpatheṣṭha revāyā uttare taṭe .
bhāreśvareti vikhyātaṃ muktitīrthaṃ nṛpottama .. 209.115 ..
6.3.d:
ऊचुः श्रेष्ठं नृपथेष्ठ रेवाया उत्तरे तटे .
भारेश्वरेति विख्यातं मुक्तितीर्थं नृपोत्तम .. 209.115 ..
6.3.m:
said, "O best of monarchs, upon the northern bank of the Revā
is the sacred ford of liberation renowned as Bhāreśvara, O foremost of kings.

6.3.s:
tatra yāmo vayaṃ sarve sarvapāpakṣayāvaham .
evamuktaḥ sa nṛpatirgṛhītvā pracuraṃ vasu .. 209.116 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र यामो वयं सर्वे सर्वपापक्षयावहम् .
एवमुक्तः स नृपतिर्गृहीत्वा प्रचुरं वसु .. 209.116 ..
6.3.m:
Let us all go there; it brings about the destruction of all sins."
Being addressed thus, that king took abundant wealth,

6.3.s:
śakaṭaṃ saṃbhṛtaṃ kṛtvā tatra yuktaḥ sa dhūrvahaḥ .
yaḥ kṛtvā mitrahananaṃ goyoniṃ samupāgataḥ .. 209.117 ..
6.3.d:
शकटं संभृतं कृत्वा तत्र युक्तः स धूर्वहः .
यः कृत्वा मित्रहननं गोयोनिं समुपागतः .. 209.117 ..
6.3.m:
and made ready a cart to which was yoked that draft ox
who, having committed the murder of a friend, had entered the bovine womb.

6.3.s:
itthaṃ sa narmadātīre samprāptastīrthamuttamam .
gatvā caturdaśīdine hyupavāsakṛtakṣaṇaḥ .. 209.118 ..
6.3.d:
इत्थं स नर्मदातीरे सम्प्राप्तस्तीर्थमुत्तमम् .
गत्वा चतुर्दशीदिने ह्युपवासकृतक्षणः .. 209.118 ..
6.3.m:
Thus he arrived at the excellent sacred ford on the bank of the Narmadā.
Having gone on the fourteenth day, seizing the moment to fast,

6.3.s:
gatvā sa narmadātīre nāma rudretyanusmaran .
śucipradeśācca mṛdaṃ mantreṇānena gṛhyatām .. 209.119 ..
6.3.d:
गत्वा स नर्मदातीरे नाम रुद्रेत्यनुस्मरन् .
शुचिप्रदेशाच्च मृदं मन्त्रेणानेन गृह्यताम् .. 209.119 ..
6.3.m:
having gone to the bank of the Narmadā, remembering the name 'Rudra',
let clay from a pure spot be taken with this mantra:

6.3.s:
uddhṛtāsi varāheṇa rudreṇa śatabāhunā .
ahamapyuddhariṣyāmi prajayā bandhanena ca .. 209.120 ..
6.3.d:
उद्धृतासि वराहेण रुद्रेण शतबाहुना .
अहमप्युद्धरिष्यामि प्रजया बन्धनेन च .. 209.120 ..
6.3.m:
"You were lifted up by the Boar, by Rudra of a hundred arms;
I too shall lift [you] up, with offspring and with restraint."

6.3.s:
sa evaṃ tāṃ mṛdaṃ nītvā muktvā tīre tathottare .
dadarśa bhāskaraṃ paścānmantreṇānena cālabhet .. 209.121 ..
6.3.d:
स एवं तां मृदं नीत्वा मुक्त्वा तीरे तथोत्तरे .
ददर्श भास्करं पश्चान्मन्त्रेणानेन चालभेत् .. 209.121 ..
6.3.m:
Having thus taken that clay and placed it on the northern bank,
he then looked upon the sun and touched it with this mantra:

6.3.s:
aśvakrānte rathakrānte viṣṇukrānte vasuṃdhare .
mṛttike hara me pāpaṃ janmakoṭiśatārjitam .. 209.122 ..
6.3.d:
अश्वक्रान्ते रथक्रान्ते विष्णुक्रान्ते वसुंधरे .
मृत्तिके हर मे पापं जन्मकोटिशतार्जितम् .. 209.122 ..
6.3.m:
"O earth trodden by horses, trodden by chariots, trodden by Viṣṇu!
O clay, remove my sin accumulated over a hundred crore births!"

6.3.s:
tata evaṃ vigāhyāpo mantrametamudīrayet .
tvaṃ narmade puṇyajale tavāmbhaḥ śaṅkarodbhavam .. 209.123 ..
6.3.d:
तत एवं विगाह्यापो मन्त्रमेतमुदीरयेत् .
त्वं नर्मदे पुण्यजले तवाम्भः शङ्करोद्भवम् .. 209.123 ..
6.3.m:
Then, having thus entered the waters, one should utter this mantra:
'O Narmadā of holy waters, your water arose from Śaṅkara.

6.3.s:
snānaṃ prakurvato me'dya pāpaṃ haratu cārjitam .
sa snātvānena vidhinā saṃtarpya pitṛdevatāḥ .. 209.124 ..
6.3.d:
स्नानं प्रकुर्वतो मेऽद्य पापं हरतु चार्जितम् .
स स्नात्वानेन विधिना संतर्प्य पितृदेवताः .. 209.124 ..
6.3.m:
May it take away the sin accumulated by me as I perform my ritual ablution today.'
Having bathed according to this rule and satiated the ancestors and deities,

6.3.s:
yayau devālayaṃ paścādupahāraiḥ samanvitaḥ .
bhaktyā saṃcintya sānnidhye śaṅkaraṃ lokaśaṅkaram .. 209.125 ..
6.3.d:
ययौ देवालयं पश्चादुपहारैः समन्वितः .
भक्त्या संचिन्त्य सान्निध्ये शङ्करं लोकशङ्करम् .. 209.125 ..
6.3.m:
he then went to the temple accompanied by offerings.
Having with devotion meditated upon Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the world, in his presence,

6.3.s:
purāṇoktavidhānena pūjāṃ samupacakrame .
pūjācatuṣṭayaṃ devi śivarātryāṃ nigadyate .. 209.126 ..
6.3.d:
पुराणोक्तविधानेन पूजां समुपचक्रमे .
पूजाचतुष्टयं देवि शिवरात्र्यां निगद्यते .. 209.126 ..
6.3.m:
he began the worship according to the rite prescribed in the Purāṇas.
Four worships are enjoined on Śivarātri, O goddess:

6.3.s:
saṃsnāpya prathame yāme pañcagavyena śaṅkaram .
ghṛtena pūraṇaṃ paścātkṛtaṃ nṛpavareṇa tu .. 209.127 ..
6.3.d:
संस्नाप्य प्रथमे यामे पञ्चगव्येन शङ्करम् .
घृतेन पूरणं पश्चात्कृतं नृपवरेण तु .. 209.127 ..
6.3.m:
Having bathed Śaṅkara with the five products of the cow in the first watch,
the filling with clarified butter was then performed by the excellent king.

6.3.s:
dhūpadīpanaivedyādyaṃ saṃkalpya ca yathāvidhi .
argheṇānena deveśaṃ mantreṇānena śaṅkaram .. 209.128 ..
6.3.d:
धूपदीपनैवेद्याद्यं संकल्प्य च यथाविधि .
अर्घेणानेन देवेशं मन्त्रेणानेन शङ्करम् .. 209.128 ..
6.3.m:
And having offered incense, lamps, food offerings, and the rest according to rule,
[he worshipped] Śaṅkara, the lord of gods, with this water offering and this mantra:

6.3.s:
namaste devadeveśa śambho paramakāraṇa .
gṛhāṇārghamimaṃ deva saṃsārāghamapākuru .. 209.129 ..
6.3.d:
नमस्ते देवदेवेश शम्भो परमकारण .
गृहाणार्घमिमं देव संसाराघमपाकुरु .. 209.129 ..
6.3.m:
'Homage to you, O lord of the gods of gods, O Śambhu, O supreme cause!
Accept this water offering, O God, and remove the sin of cyclic existence.'

6.3.s:
vittānurūpato dattaṃ suvarṇaṃ mantrakalpitam .
agnirhi devāḥ sarve suvarṇaṃ ca hutāśanāt .. 209.130 ..
6.3.d:
वित्तानुरूपतो दत्तं सुवर्णं मन्त्रकल्पितम् .
अग्निर्हि देवाः सर्वे सुवर्णं च हुताशनात् .. 209.130 ..
6.3.m:
Gold was given according to his wealth, consecrated with mantras.
For all the gods are fire, and gold comes from the fire-eater.

6.3.s:
ataḥ suvarṇadānena prītāḥ syuḥ sarvadevatāḥ .
tadarghaṃ sarvadā dātuḥ prīto bhavatu śaṅkaraḥ .. 209.131 ..
6.3.d:
अतः सुवर्णदानेन प्रीताः स्युः सर्वदेवताः .
तदर्घं सर्वदा दातुः प्रीतो भवतु शङ्करः .. 209.131 ..
6.3.m:
Therefore, through the gift of gold, all the deities become pleased.
May Śaṅkara be pleased with the giver of that water offering forever.

6.3.s:
anena vidhinā tena pūjitaḥ prathame śivaḥ .
yāme dvitīye tu punaḥ pūrvoktavidhinā caret .. 209.132 ..
6.3.d:
अनेन विधिना तेन पूजितः प्रथमे शिवः .
यामे द्वितीये तु पुनः पूर्वोक्तविधिना चरेत् .. 209.132 ..
6.3.m:
According to this rule, Śiva was worshipped by him in the first watch.
In the second watch, however, he should again proceed according to the aforementioned rule.

6.3.s:
snāpayāmāsa dugdhena gavyena tripurāntakam .
taṃdulaiḥ pūraṇaṃ paścātkṛtaṃ liṅgasya śūlinaḥ .. 209.133 ..
6.3.d:
स्नापयामास दुग्धेन गव्येन त्रिपुरान्तकम् .
तंदुलैः पूरणं पश्चात्कृतं लिङ्गस्य शूलिनः .. 209.133 ..
6.3.m:
He bathed the destroyer of Tripura with cow’s milk.
Then the filling of the liṅga of the trident-bearer was performed with rice grains.

6.3.s:
kṛtvā vidhānaṃ pūrvoktaṃ dattaṃ vastrayugaṃ sitam .
śvetavastrayugaṃ yasmācchaṅkarasyātivallabham .. 209.134 ..
6.3.d:
कृत्वा विधानं पूर्वोक्तं दत्तं वस्त्रयुगं सितम् .
श्वेतवस्त्रयुगं यस्माच्छङ्करस्यातिवल्लभम् .. 209.134 ..
6.3.m:
Having performed the aforementioned rite, a pair of white garments was offered,
because a pair of white garments is extremely dear to Śaṅkara.

6.3.s:
prīto bhavati vai śambhurdattena śvetavāsasā .
yāmaṃ tṛtīyaṃ samprāptaṃ dṛṣṭvā nṛpatisattamaḥ .. 209.135 ..
6.3.d:
प्रीतो भवति वै शम्भुर्दत्तेन श्वेतवाससा .
यामं तृतीयं सम्प्राप्तं दृष्ट्वा नृपतिसत्तमः .. 209.135 ..
6.3.m:
Śambhu indeed becomes pleased by the offering of white clothing.
Seeing the third watch arrive, the best of kings,

6.3.s:
devaṃ saṃsnāpya madhunā pūraṇaṃ cakrivāṃstilaiḥ .
tiladroṇapradānaṃ ca kuryānmantramudīrayan .. 209.136 ..
6.3.d:
देवं संस्नाप्य मधुना पूरणं चक्रिवांस्तिलैः .
तिलद्रोणप्रदानं च कुर्यान्मन्त्रमुदीरयन् .. 209.136 ..
6.3.m:
having bathed the God with honey, performed the filling with sesame seeds.
And one should make the donation of a droṇa of sesame seeds while uttering the mantra:

6.3.s:
tilāḥ śvetāstilāḥ kṛṣṇāḥ sarvapāpaharāstilāḥ .
tiladroṇapradānenu saṃsāraśchidyatāṃ mama .. 209.137 ..
6.3.d:
तिलाः श्वेतास्तिलाः कृष्णाः सर्वपापहरास्तिलाः .
तिलद्रोणप्रदानेनु संसारश्छिद्यतां मम .. 209.137 ..
6.3.m:
'Sesame seeds are white, sesame seeds are black, sesame seeds remove all sins.
By the offering of a droṇa of sesame seeds, may my cyclic existence be severed.'

6.3.s:
anena vidhinā rājā yāminīyāmapūjanam .
ativāhya vinodena brahmaghoṣeṇa jāgaram .. 209.138 ..
6.3.d:
अनेन विधिना राजा यामिनीयामपूजनम् .
अतिवाह्य विनोदेन ब्रह्मघोषेण जागरम् .. 209.138 ..
6.3.m:
By this rule, the king carried out the worship for the watches of the night,
passing the vigil pleasantly with the loud recitation of the Vedas.

6.3.s:
cakāra pūjanaṃ śambhorbahupuṇyaprasādhakam .
ye jāgare trinetrasya śivarātryāṃ śivasthitāḥ .. 209.139 ..
6.3.d:
चकार पूजनं शम्भोर्बहुपुण्यप्रसाधकम् .
ये जागरे त्रिनेत्रस्य शिवरात्र्यां शिवस्थिताः .. 209.139 ..
6.3.m:
He performed the worship of Śambhu, which accomplishes great merit.
Those who remain devoted to Śiva during the vigil of the Three-eyed One on Śivarātri—

6.3.s:
te yāṃ gatiṃ gatāḥ pārtha na tāṃ gacchanti yajvinaḥ .
pāpāni yāni kāni syuḥ koṭijanmārjitānyapi .. 209.140 ..
6.3.d:
ते यां गतिं गताः पार्थ न तां गच्छन्ति यज्विनः .
पापानि यानि कानि स्युः कोटिजन्मार्जितान्यपि .. 209.140 ..
6.3.m:
the state that they attain, O Pārtha, sacrificers do not attain.
Whatever sins there may be, even if accumulated across tens of millions of births,

6.3.s:
harakeśavayoḥ snānti jāgare yānti saṃkṣayam .
yāvanto nimiṣā nṛṇāṃ bhavanti niśi jāgratām .. 209.141 ..
6.3.d:
हरकेशवयोः स्नान्ति जागरे यान्ति संक्षयम् .
यावन्तो निमिषा नृणां भवन्ति निशि जाग्रताम् .. 209.141 ..
6.3.m:
perish in the vigil of [those who] bathe Hara and Keśava.
As many moments as there are for men who keep awake in the night,

6.3.s:
nimiṣe nimiṣe rājannaśvamedhaphalaṃ dhruvam .
upavāsaparāṇāṃ ca devāyatanavāsinām .. 209.142 ..
6.3.d:
निमिषे निमिषे राजन्नश्वमेधफलं ध्रुवम् .
उपवासपराणां च देवायतनवासिनाम् .. 209.142 ..
6.3.m:
at every moment, O King, the fruit of a horse sacrifice is certain
for those devoted to fasting and dwelling in the temple of the God,

6.3.s:
śṛṇvatāṃ dharmamākhyānaṃ dhyāyatāṃ harakeśavau .
na tāṃ bahusuvarṇena kratunā gatimāpnuyuḥ .. 209.143 ..
6.3.d:
शृण्वतां धर्ममाख्यानं ध्यायतां हरकेशवौ .
न तां बहुसुवर्णेन क्रतुना गतिमाप्नुयुः .. 209.143 ..
6.3.m:
listening to the righteous narration and meditating on Hara and Keśava.
They could not attain that state even by a sacrifice with abundant gold.

6.3.s:
śivarātristithiḥ puṇyā kārttikī ca viśeṣataḥ .
revāyā uttaraṃ kūlaṃ tīraṃ bhāreśvareti ca .. 209.144 ..
6.3.d:
शिवरात्रिस्तिथिः पुण्या कार्त्तिकी च विशेषतः .
रेवाया उत्तरं कूलं तीरं भारेश्वरेति च .. 209.144 ..
6.3.m:
The lunar day of Śivarātri is meritorious, and especially that of Kārttika,
[and so is] the northern bank of the Revā and the shore called Bhāreśvara.

6.3.s:
jāgṛtaścātiduḥkhena kathaṃ pāpaṃ na hāsyati .
itthaṃsa jāgaraṃ kṛtvā śivarātryāṃ nareśvaraḥ .. 209.145 ..
6.3.d:
जागृतश्चातिदुःखेन कथं पापं न हास्यति .
इत्थंस जागरं कृत्वा शिवरात्र्यां नरेश्वरः .. 209.145 ..
6.3.m:
When one has kept vigil with great exertion, how will sin not leave [him]?
Having thus kept the vigil on Śivarātri, the lord of men,

6.3.s:
prabhāte vimale gatvā narmadātīramuttamam .
snāpitāstena te sarve vāhanāni gajādayaḥ .. 209.146 ..
6.3.d:
प्रभाते विमले गत्वा नर्मदातीरमुत्तमम् .
स्नापितास्तेन ते सर्वे वाहनानि गजादयः .. 209.146 ..
6.3.m:
went at pure dawn to the excellent bank of the Narmadā.
All those mounts, elephants and the rest, were bathed by him.

6.3.s:
yaistu vāhairgatastīrthaṃ snāto'haṃ snāpayāmi tān .
tatra madhyasthitaḥ snātastiryaktvānnirgato vaṇik .. 209.147 ..
6.3.d:
यैस्तु वाहैर्गतस्तीर्थं स्नातोऽहं स्नापयामि तान् .
तत्र मध्यस्थितः स्नातस्तिर्यक्त्वान्निर्गतो वणिक् .. 209.147 ..
6.3.m:
'By which mounts I came to the sacred ford, having bathed, I bathe them.'
Bathed while standing in their midst, the merchant was released from [his] animal condition.

6.3.s:
dānaṃ dadau tānuddiśya kiṃcicchaktyanurūpataḥ .
tena vāhakṛtāddoṣānmukto bhavati mānavaḥ .. 209.148 ..
6.3.d:
दानं ददौ तानुद्दिश्य किंचिच्छक्त्यनुरूपतः .
तेन वाहकृताद्दोषान्मुक्तो भवति मानवः .. 209.148 ..
6.3.m:
He gave a gift on their behalf, a little according to his ability;
by that, a man becomes freed from the fault caused by mounts.

6.3.s:
anyathāsau kṛto lābhaḥ kṛto vrajati tān prati .
saṃsnāpya taṃ tato rājā svayaṃ snātvā vidhānataḥ .. 209.149 ..
6.3.d:
अन्यथासौ कृतो लाभः कृतो व्रजति तान् प्रति .
संस्नाप्य तं ततो राजा स्वयं स्नात्वा विधानतः .. 209.149 ..
6.3.m:
Otherwise, that benefit that is acquired goes to them.
Having bathed it, the king then bathed himself according to rule.

6.3.s:
saṃtarpya pitṛdevāṃśca kṛtvā śrāddhaṃ yathāvidhi .
kṛtvā piṇḍānpitṛbhyaśca vṛṣamutsṛjya lakṣaṇam .. 209.150 ..
6.3.d:
संतर्प्य पितृदेवांश्च कृत्वा श्राद्धं यथाविधि .
कृत्वा पिण्डान्पितृभ्यश्च वृषमुत्सृज्य लक्षणम् .. 209.150 ..
6.3.m:
And having satiated the ancestors and gods, having performed the śrāddha according to rule,
and having made rice balls for the ancestors, he released a bull marked with auspicious signs.

6.3.s:
gatvā devālayaṃ paścāddevaṃ tīrthodakena ca .
saṃsnāpya pañcagavyena tataḥ pañcāmṛtena ca .. 209.151 ..
6.3.d:
गत्वा देवालयं पश्चाद्देवं तीर्थोदकेन च .
संस्नाप्य पञ्चगव्येन ततः पञ्चामृतेन च .. 209.151 ..
6.3.m:
Then, having gone to the temple, having bathed the God with water from the sacred ford,
with the five products of the cow, and then with the five nectars,

6.3.s:
sarvauṣadhijalenaiva tataḥ śuddhodakena ca .
candanena sugandhena samālabhya ca śaṅkaram .. 209.152 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वौषधिजलेनैव ततः शुद्धोदकेन च .
चन्दनेन सुगन्धेन समालभ्य च शङ्करम् .. 209.152 ..
6.3.m:
with water containing all medicinal herbs, and then with pure water,
and having anointed Śaṅkara with fragrant sandalwood paste,

6.3.s:
kuṅkumaiśca sakarpūrairgandhaiśca vividhaistathā .
puṣpaughaiśca sugandhāḍhyaiścaturthaṃ liṅgapūraṇam .. 209.153 ..
6.3.d:
कुङ्कुमैश्च सकर्पूरैर्गन्धैश्च विविधैस्तथा .
पुष्पौघैश्च सुगन्धाढ्यैश्चतुर्थं लिङ्गपूरणम् .. 209.153 ..
6.3.m:
with saffron and camphor, and likewise with various scents,
and with heaps of intensely fragrant flowers, the fourth filling of the liṅga

6.3.s:
kṛtaṃ nṛpavareṇātra kurvatā pūrvakaṃ vidhim .
godānaṃ ca kṛtaṃ paścādvidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā .. 209.154 ..
6.3.d:
कृतं नृपवरेणात्र कुर्वता पूर्वकं विधिम् .
गोदानं च कृतं पश्चाद्विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा .. 209.154 ..
6.3.m:
was performed here by the excellent king carrying out the previous rite.
And the gift of a cow was made afterwards through the rite seen in the rules:

6.3.s:
dhenuke rudrarūpāsi rudreṇa parinirmitā .
asminnagādhe saṃsāre patantaṃ māṃ samuddhara .. 209.155 ..
6.3.d:
धेनुके रुद्ररूपासि रुद्रेण परिनिर्मिता .
अस्मिन्नगाधे संसारे पतन्तं मां समुद्धर .. 209.155 ..
6.3.m:
'O cow, you are of the form of Rudra, fashioned by Rudra;
lift me up, who am falling into this bottomless cyclic existence.'

6.3.s:
dhenuṃ svalaṃkṛtāṃ dadyādanena vidhinā tataḥ .
kṣamāpya devadeveśaṃ brāhmaṇān bhojayedbahūn .. 209.156 ..
6.3.d:
धेनुं स्वलंकृतां दद्यादनेन विधिना ततः .
क्षमाप्य देवदेवेशं ब्राह्मणान् भोजयेद्बहून् .. 209.156 ..
6.3.m:
He should then give a well-adorned cow according to this rule.
Having begged pardon of the lord of the gods of gods, he should feed many brahmins.

6.3.s:
ṣaḍvidhairbhojanairbhakṣyairvāsobhistān samarcayet .
dakṣiṇābhirvicitrābhiḥ pūjayitvā kṣamāpayet .. 209.157 ..
6.3.d:
षड्विधैर्भोजनैर्भक्ष्यैर्वासोभिस्तान् समर्चयेत् .
दक्षिणाभिर्विचित्राभिः पूजयित्वा क्षमापयेत् .. 209.157 ..
6.3.m:
He should honor them with six kinds of meals, foods to chew, and garments;
having worshipped them with various gifts, he should ask their forgiveness.

6.3.s:
sa svayaṃ bubhuje paścātparivārasamanvitaḥ .
tāmeva rajanīṃ tatra nyavasajjagatīpatiḥ .. 209.158 ..
6.3.d:
स स्वयं बुभुजे पश्चात्परिवारसमन्वितः .
तामेव रजनीं तत्र न्यवसज्जगतीपतिः .. 209.158 ..
6.3.m:
He himself ate afterwards accompanied by his retinue.
The lord of the earth resided there for that very night.

6.3.s:
tasya tatroṣitasyaivaṃ niśīthe'tha nareśvara .
ākāśe so'ti śuśrāva divyavāṇīsamīritam .. 209.159 ..
6.3.d:
तस्य तत्रोषितस्यैवं निशीथेऽथ नरेश्वर .
आकाशे सोऽति शुश्राव दिव्यवाणीसमीरितम् .. 209.159 ..
6.3.m:
As he was residing there in this manner, at midnight, O lord of men,
he heard uttered in the sky a celestial voice.

6.3.s:
vāguvāca -
rājansamaṃ tato loke phalaṃ bhavati sāmpratam .
saṃsārasāgare hyatra patitānāṃ durātmanām .. 209.160 ..
6.3.d:
वागुवाच -
राजन्समं ततो लोके फलं भवति साम्प्रतम् .
संसारसागरे ह्यत्र पतितानां दुरात्मनाम् .. 209.160 ..
6.3.m:
The voice said:
'O King, equal fruit now arises in the world
for the evil-minded fallen here into the ocean of cyclic existence.

6.3.s:
yadi saṃnidhimātreṇa phalaṃ tatrocyate katham .
yadi śaṃtanuvaṃśasya tatronmādakaraṃ bhavet .. 209.161 ..
6.3.d:
यदि संनिधिमात्रेण फलं तत्रोच्यते कथम् .
यदि शंतनुवंशस्य तत्रोन्मादकरं भवेत् .. 209.161 ..
6.3.m:
If by mere presence [alone] the fruit is proclaimed there, how [can it be]?
If for the lineage of Śaṃtanu it should cause intoxication there,

6.3.s:
ya eṣa tvadgṛhe voḍhā hyatibhāradhuraṃdharaḥ .
anena mitrahananaṃ pāpaṃ viśvāsaghātanam .. 209.162 ..
6.3.d:
य एष त्वद्गृहे वोढा ह्यतिभारधुरंधरः .
अनेन मित्रहननं पापं विश्वासघातनम् .. 209.162 ..
6.3.m:
this bearer in your house, who carries exceedingly heavy loads—
by him, the sin of slaying a friend, the betrayal of trust,

6.3.s:
kṛtaṃ janmasahasrāṇāmatīte parijanmani .
gatena pāpmanātmānaṃ narakeṣu ca saṃsthitiḥ .. 209.163 ..
6.3.d:
कृतं जन्मसहस्राणामतीते परिजन्मनि .
गतेन पाप्मनात्मानं नरकेषु च संस्थितिः .. 209.163 ..
6.3.m:
was committed in a past previous life a thousand births ago.
Departing with his sin, his dwelling was in hells.

6.3.s:
tato yonisahasreṣu gatistiryakṣu caiva hi .
goyoniṃ samanuprāptastvadgṛhe sa sudurmatiḥ .. 209.164 ..
6.3.d:
ततो योनिसहस्रेषु गतिस्तिर्यक्षु चैव हि .
गोयोनिं समनुप्राप्तस्त्वद्गृहे स सुदुर्मतिः .. 209.164 ..
6.3.m:
Then his path was in thousands of animal wombs.
Having reached the womb of cattle, that wicked-minded one was in your house.

6.3.s:
snāpitaśca tvayā tīrthe hyasmin parvasamāgame .
dṛṣṭvā pūjāṃ tvayā kḷptāṃ kṛtā jāgaraṇakriyā .. 209.165 ..
6.3.d:
स्नापितश्च त्वया तीर्थे ह्यस्मिन् पर्वसमागमे .
दृष्ट्वा पूजां त्वया कॢप्तां कृता जागरणक्रिया .. 209.165 ..
6.3.m:
And he was bathed by you at this sacred ford upon this festive gathering;
seeing the worship arranged by you, the act of keeping vigil was performed.'

6.3.s:
tena niṣkalmaṣo jāto muktvā dehaṃ tavāgrataḥ .
svargaṃ prati vimānasthaḥ so'dya rājangamiṣyati .. 209.166 ..
6.3.d:
तेन निष्कल्मषो जातो मुक्त्वा देहं तवाग्रतः .
स्वर्गं प्रति विमानस्थः सोऽद्य राजन्गमिष्यति .. 209.166 ..
6.3.m: By that he has become free of blemish. Leaving his body before you, / he will go today to heaven, seated in an aerial chariot, O king.

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
evamukte nipatito dhuryaḥ prāṇairvyayujyata .
vimānavaramārūḍhastatkṣaṇātsamadṛśyata .. 209.167 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
एवमुक्ते निपतितो धुर्यः प्राणैर्व्ययुज्यत .
विमानवरमारूढस्तत्क्षणात्समदृश्यत .. 209.167 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having spoken thus, the draft-ox fell and was separated from his vital breaths. / In that very instant he was seen mounted on an excellent aerial chariot.

6.3.s: sa taṃ praṇamya rājendramuvāca prahasanniva .. 209.168 ..
6.3.d: स तं प्रणम्य राजेन्द्रमुवाच प्रहसन्निव .. 209.168 ..
6.3.m: Having bowed to that best of kings, he spoke as if smiling: 209.168

6.3.s:
vṛṣa uvāca -
bhobho nṛpavaraśreṣṭha tīrthamāhātmyamuttamam .
yatra cāsmadvidhastīrthe mucyate pātakairnaraḥ .
mayā jñātamaśeṣeṇa matsamo nāsti pātakī .. 209.169 ..
6.3.d:
वृष उवाच -
भोभो नृपवरश्रेष्ठ तीर्थमाहात्म्यमुत्तमम् .
यत्र चास्मद्विधस्तीर्थे मुच्यते पातकैर्नरः .
मया ज्ञातमशेषेण मत्समो नास्ति पातकी .. 209.169 ..
6.3.m: The bull said: / O best of noble kings! Excellent is the māhātmya of this sacred ford, / the sacred ford where even a man like me is freed from sins. / I have understood it completely; there is no sinner equal to me.

6.3.s:
ataḥ paraṃ kiṃ tu kuryāṃ paraṃ tīrthānukīrtanam .
bhavānmātā bhavanbhrātā bhavāṃścaiva pitāmahaḥ .. 209.170 ..
6.3.d:
अतः परं किं तु कुर्यां परं तीर्थानुकीर्तनम् .
भवान्माता भवन्भ्राता भवांश्चैव पितामहः .. 209.170 ..
6.3.m: Beyond this, what further praise of the sacred ford can I proclaim? / You are my mother, you are my brother, and you are my grandfather.

6.3.s:
kṣantavyaṃ praṇato'smyadya yasmiṃstīrthe hi mādṛśāḥ .
gatimīdṛgvidhāṃ yānti na jāne tava kā gatiḥ .. 209.171 ..
6.3.d:
क्षन्तव्यं प्रणतोऽस्म्यद्य यस्मिंस्तीर्थे हि मादृशाः .
गतिमीदृग्विधां यान्ति न जाने तव का गतिः .. 209.171 ..
6.3.m: I must be forgiven; I bow to you today. In the sacred ford where people like me / attain such an exalted state, I do not know what state awaits you,

6.3.s:
samārādhya maheśānaṃ sampūjya ca yathāvidhi .
kā gatistava saṃbhāṣyā dehyanujñāṃ mama prabho .. 209.172 ..
6.3.d:
समाराध्य महेशानं सम्पूज्य च यथाविधि .
का गतिस्तव संभाष्या देह्यनुज्ञां मम प्रभो .. 209.172 ..
6.3.m: having propitiated Maheśāna and worshipped him according to rule. / What state could be spoken of for you? Grant me permission, O lord.

6.3.s:
tvarayanti ca māṃ hyete divisthāḥ praṇayādgaṇāḥ .
svastyastu te gamiṣyāmītyuktvā so'ntardadhe kṣaṇāt .. 209.173 ..
6.3.d:
त्वरयन्ति च मां ह्येते दिविस्थाः प्रणयाद्गणाः .
स्वस्त्यस्तु ते गमिष्यामीत्युक्त्वा सोऽन्तर्दधे क्षणात् .. 209.173 ..
6.3.m: These attendants residing in heaven are urging me along out of affection. / May good betide you; I shall depart.' Having said this, he vanished in a moment.

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
gate cādarśanaṃ tatra sa rājā vismayānvitaḥ .
tīrthamāhātmyamatulaṃ varṇayansvapuraṃ gataḥ .. 209.174 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
गते चादर्शनं तत्र स राजा विस्मयान्वितः .
तीर्थमाहात्म्यमतुलं वर्णयन्स्वपुरं गतः .. 209.174 ..
6.3.m: Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / And when he had vanished from sight there, that king, filled with wonder, / returned to his city, describing the peerless māhātmya of the sacred ford.

6.3.s:
itthaṃbhūtaṃ hi tattīrthaṃ narmadāyāṃ vyavasthitam .
sarvapāpakṣayakaraṃ sarvaduḥkhaghnamuttamam .. 209.175 ..
6.3.d:
इत्थंभूतं हि तत्तीर्थं नर्मदायां व्यवस्थितम् .
सर्वपापक्षयकरं सर्वदुःखघ्नमुत्तमम् .. 209.175 ..
6.3.m: Such indeed is that sacred ford situated on the Narmadā, / destroying all sins, banishing all sorrow, supreme.

6.3.s:
upapāpāni naśyanti snānamātreṇa bhārata .
kārttikasya caturdaśyāmupavāsaparāyaṇaḥ .. 209.176 ..
6.3.d:
उपपापानि नश्यन्ति स्नानमात्रेण भारत .
कार्त्तिकस्य चतुर्दश्यामुपवासपरायणः .. 209.176 ..
6.3.m: Minor sins are destroyed merely by a ritual ablution, O Bhārata. / Intent on fasting on the fourteenth day of Kārttika,

6.3.s:
caturdhā pūrayelliṅgaṃ tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu .
brahmahatyā surāpānaṃ steyaṃ gurvaṅganāgamaḥ .. 209.177 ..
6.3.d:
चतुर्धा पूरयेल्लिङ्गं तस्य पुण्यफलं शृणु .
ब्रह्महत्या सुरापानं स्तेयं गुर्वङ्गनागमः .. 209.177 ..
6.3.m: one should fill the liṅga fourfold; hear the fruit of that merit: / Killing a brahmin, drinking alcohol, theft, intercourse with the teacher's wife—

6.3.s:
mahāpāpāni catvāri caturbhiryānti saṃkṣayam .
so'śvamedhasya yajñasya labhate phalamuttamam .. 209.178 ..
6.3.d:
महापापानि चत्वारि चतुर्भिर्यान्ति संक्षयम् .
सोऽश्वमेधस्य यज्ञस्य लभते फलमुत्तमम् .. 209.178 ..
6.3.m: these four great sins are destroyed by the four [fillings]. / He obtains the excellent fruit of a horse sacrifice.

6.3.s:
kārttike śuklapakṣasya caturdaśyāmupoṣitaḥ .
svarṇadānācca tattīrthe yajñasya labhate phalam .. 209.179 ..
6.3.d:
कार्त्तिके शुक्लपक्षस्य चतुर्दश्यामुपोषितः .
स्वर्णदानाच्च तत्तीर्थे यज्ञस्य लभते फलम् .. 209.179 ..
6.3.m: Having fasted on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight of Kārttika, / through the gift of gold at that sacred ford, one obtains the fruit of a sacrifice.

6.3.s:
aṣṭamyāṃ vā caturdaśyāṃ vaiśākhe māsi pūrvavat .
dīpaṃ piṣṭamayaṃ kṛtvā pitṝn sarvān vimokṣayet .. 209.180 ..
6.3.d:
अष्टम्यां वा चतुर्दश्यां वैशाखे मासि पूर्ववत् .
दीपं पिष्टमयं कृत्वा पितॄन् सर्वान् विमोक्षयेत् .. 209.180 ..
6.3.m: Or on the eighth or the fourteenth in the month of Vaiśākha, as before, / having made a lamp of dough, one delivers all the ancestors.

6.3.s:
tatra yaddīyate dānamapi vālāgramātrakam .
tadakṣayaphalaṃ sarvamevamāha maheśvaraḥ .. 209.181 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र यद्दीयते दानमपि वालाग्रमात्रकम् .
तदक्षयफलं सर्वमेवमाह महेश्वरः .. 209.181 ..
6.3.m: Whatever gift is given there, even the measure of the tip of a hair, / all of it has imperishable fruit; thus spoke Maheśvara.

6.3.s:
bhārabhūtyāṃ mṛtānāṃ tu narāṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām .
anivartikā gatī rājañchivalokānnirantaram .. 209.182 ..
6.3.d:
भारभूत्यां मृतानां तु नराणां भावितात्मनाम् .
अनिवर्तिका गती राजञ्छिवलोकान्निरन्तरम् .. 209.182 ..
6.3.m: For men of cultivated minds who die at Bhārabhūti, / there is a non-returning state from the world of Śiva forever, O king.

6.3.s:
athavā lokavṛttyarthaṃ martyalokaṃ jigīṣati .
sāṅgavedajñaviprāṇāṃ jāyate vimale kule .. 209.183 ..
6.3.d:
अथवा लोकवृत्त्यर्थं मर्त्यलोकं जिगीषति .
साङ्गवेदज्ञविप्राणां जायते विमले कुले .. 209.183 ..
6.3.m: Or if he desires to go to the mortal world for the sake of worldly conduct, / he is born in the pure lineage of brahmins who know the Vedas with their auxiliary limbs.

6.3.s:
dhanadhānyasamāyukto vedavidyāsamanvitaḥ .
sarvavyādhivinirmukto jīvecca śaradāṃ śatam .. 209.184 ..
6.3.d:
धनधान्यसमायुक्तो वेदविद्यासमन्वितः .
सर्वव्याधिविनिर्मुक्तो जीवेच्च शरदां शतम् .. 209.184 ..
6.3.m: Endowed with wealth and grain, furnished with Vedic knowledge, / freed from all disease, he may live a hundred autumns.

6.3.s: punastattīrthamāsādya hyakṣayaṃ padamāpnuyāt .. 209.185 ..
6.3.d: पुनस्तत्तीर्थमासाद्य ह्यक्षयं पदमाप्नुयात् .. 209.185 ..
6.3.m: Reaching that sacred ford once again, he surely attains the imperishable abode. 209.185

6.3.s:
etatpuṇyaṃ pāpaharaṃ kathitaṃ te nṛpottama .
bhāratedaṃ mahākhyānaṃ śṛṇu caiva tataḥ param .. 209.186 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe bhārabhūtitīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma navādhikadviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
6.3.d:
एतत्पुण्यं पापहरं कथितं ते नृपोत्तम .
भारतेदं महाख्यानं शृणु चैव ततः परम् .. 209.186 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे भारभूतितीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम नवाधिकद्विशततमोऽध्यायः ..
6.3.m:
This meritorious [account] which removes sin has been told to you, O best of kings, / O Bhārata. Now hear the great narrative that comes after this.
Thus ends the two hundred and ninth chapter, named 'Description of the Māhātmya of the Bhārabhūti Sacred Ford', in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.

6.3.s:
adhyāyaḥ 210
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tasyaivānantaraṃ tāta puṅkhilaṃ tīrthamuttamam .
tatra tīrthe purā puṅkhaḥ pārtha siddhimupāgataḥ .. 210.1 ..
6.3.d:
अध्यायः 210
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
तस्यैवानन्तरं तात पुङ्खिलं तीर्थमुत्तमम् .
तत्र तीर्थे पुरा पुङ्खः पार्थ सिद्धिमुपागतः .. 210.1 ..
6.3.m: Chapter 210 / Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Immediately after that, my dear, is the excellent Puṅkhila sacred ford. / In that sacred ford formerly Puṅkha attained perfection, O Pārtha.

6.3.s:
jāmadagnyo mahātejāḥ kṣatriyāntakaraḥ prabhuḥ .
tapaḥ kṛtvā suvipulaṃ narmadottaratīrabhāk .. 210.2 ..
6.3.d:
जामदग्न्यो महातेजाः क्षत्रियान्तकरः प्रभुः .
तपः कृत्वा सुविपुलं नर्मदोत्तरतीरभाक् .. 210.2 ..
6.3.m: The son of Jamadagni, of great splendor, the destroyer of the kṣatriyas, the powerful lord, / having performed immense austerity, took resort on the northern bank of the Narmadā.

6.3.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti vikhyātaṃ puṅkhatīrthaṃ nareśvara .
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ snātvā hyārādhya parameśvaram .. 210.3 ..
6.3.d:
ततः प्रभृति विख्यातं पुङ्खतीर्थं नरेश्वर .
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः स्नात्वा ह्याराध्य परमेश्वरम् .. 210.3 ..
6.3.m: From then on it became celebrated as the Puṅkha sacred ford, O ruler of men. / Having performed a ritual ablution in that sacred ford and having worshipped the Supreme Lord,

6.3.s:
ihaloke balairyuktaḥ pare mokṣamavāpnuyāt .
devānpitḥn samabhyarcya pitḥṇāmanṛṇī bhavet .. 210.4 ..
6.3.d:
इहलोके बलैर्युक्तः परे मोक्षमवाप्नुयात् .
देवान्पित्ःन् समभ्यर्च्य पित्ःणामनृणी भवेत् .. 210.4 ..
6.3.m: one is endowed with strength in this world and attains liberation in the next. / Having worshipped the gods and ancestors, one becomes free of debt to the ancestors.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe naro yastu prāṇatyāgaṃ karoti vai .
anivartikā gatistasya rudralokādasaṃśayam .. 210.5 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे नरो यस्तु प्राणत्यागं करोति वै .
अनिवर्तिका गतिस्तस्य रुद्रलोकादसंशयम् .. 210.5 ..
6.3.m: The man who indeed casts off his life at that sacred ford, / his course is non-returning from the world of Rudra, without a doubt.

6.3.s: tatra tīrthe naraḥ snātvā hayamedhaphalaṃ labhet .. 210.6 ..
6.3.d: तत्र तीर्थे नरः स्नात्वा हयमेधफलं लभेत् .. 210.6 ..
6.3.m: Having performed a ritual ablution in that sacred ford, a man obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice. 210.6

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe naro yastu brāhmaṇān bhojayennṛpa .
ekasmin bhojite vipre koṭirbhavati bhojitā .. 210.7 ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे नरो यस्तु ब्राह्मणान् भोजयेन्नृप .
एकस्मिन् भोजिते विप्रे कोटिर्भवति भोजिता .. 210.7 ..
6.3.m: The man who feeds brahmins at that sacred ford, O king, / when one brahmin is fed, ten million are fed.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ kaścitpūjayedvṛṣabhadhvajam .
vājapeyasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnotyasaṃśayam .. 210.8 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe puṅkhilatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma daśottaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः कश्चित्पूजयेद्वृषभध्वजम् .
वाजपेयस्य यज्ञस्य फलं प्राप्नोत्यसंशयम् .. 210.8 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे पुङ्खिलतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम दशोत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः ..
6.3.m:
Whoever should worship the one whose banner is a bull at that sacred ford, / obtains the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice, without a doubt.
Thus ends the two hundred and tenth chapter, named 'Description of the Māhātmya of the Puṅkhila Sacred Ford', in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.

6.3.s:
adhyāyaḥ 211
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
āścaryabhūtaṃ lokasya devadevena yatkṛtam .
tatte sarvaṃ pravakṣyāmi narmadātaṭavāsinām .. 211.1 ..
6.3.d:
अध्यायः 211
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
आश्चर्यभूतं लोकस्य देवदेवेन यत्कृतम् .
तत्ते सर्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि नर्मदातटवासिनाम् .. 211.1 ..
6.3.m: Chapter 211 / Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: / That wondrous deed of the god of gods done for the world, / I shall tell you all of that, for the dwellers on the banks of the Narmadā.

6.3.s:
dvijān sukṛtpaṇān devaḥ kuṣṭhī bhūtvā yayāca ha .
śrāddhakāle tu samprāpte raktagandhānulepanaḥ .. 211.2 ..
6.3.d:
द्विजान् सुकृत्पणान् देवः कुष्ठी भूत्वा ययाच ह .
श्राद्धकाले तु सम्प्राप्ते रक्तगन्धानुलेपनः .. 211.2 ..
6.3.m: The god, having become a leper smeared with red fragrant ointments, / begged from the twice-born who had staked their good deeds, when the time of the śrāddha had arrived.

6.3.s:
sravadbudbudagātrastu makṣikākṛmisaṃvṛtaḥ .
duścarmā durmukho gandhī praskhalaṃśca pade pade .. 211.3 ..
6.3.d:
स्रवद्बुद्बुदगात्रस्तु मक्षिकाकृमिसंवृतः .
दुश्चर्मा दुर्मुखो गन्धी प्रस्खलंश्च पदे पदे .. 211.3 ..
6.3.m: His limbs were oozing with blisters, covered with flies and worms, / having foul skin, a repulsive face, stinking, and stumbling at every step.

6.3.s:
brāhmaṇāvasathaṃ gatvā skhalandvāre'bravīdidam .
bhobho gṛhapate tvadya brāhmaṇaiḥ saha bhojanam .. 211.4 ..
6.3.d:
ब्राह्मणावसथं गत्वा स्खलन्द्वारेऽब्रवीदिदम् .
भोभो गृहपते त्वद्य ब्राह्मणैः सह भोजनम् .. 211.4 ..
6.3.m: Going to a brahmin's dwelling, faltering at the door, he said this: / 'O master of the house, today a well-prepared meal with the brahmins

6.3.s:
tvadgṛhe kartumicchāmi hyebhiḥ saha susaṃskṛtam .
tatastaṃ brahmāṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā yajamānasamanvitāḥ .. 211.5 ..
6.3.d:
त्वद्गृहे कर्तुमिच्छामि ह्येभिः सह सुसंस्कृतम् .
ततस्तं ब्रह्माणं दृष्ट्वा यजमानसमन्विताः .. 211.5 ..
6.3.m: I wish to eat together with them in your house.' / Then, seeing that brahmin, [the guests] along with the sacrificer

6.3.s:
sravantaṃ sarvagātreṣu dhigdhigityevamabruvan .
nirgacchasvāśu durgandha gṛhācchīghraṃ dvijādhama .. 211.6 ..
6.3.d:
स्रवन्तं सर्वगात्रेषु धिग्धिगित्येवमब्रुवन् .
निर्गच्छस्वाशु दुर्गन्ध गृहाच्छीघ्रं द्विजाधम .. 211.6 ..
6.3.m: oozing on all his limbs, said, 'Fie, fie!' / 'Get out at once, foul-smelling one, quickly from the house, O lowest of the twice-born!

6.3.s:
abhojyametatsarveṣāṃ darśanāttava satkṛtam .
evameva tathetyuktvā devadevo maheśvaraḥ .. 211.7 ..
6.3.d:
अभोज्यमेतत्सर्वेषां दर्शनात्तव सत्कृतम् .
एवमेव तथेत्युक्त्वा देवदेवो महेश्वरः .. 211.7 ..
6.3.m: This [food] prepared for all has become uneatable because of the sight of you!' / Saying only 'So be it,' the god of gods, Maheśvara,

6.3.s:
jagāmākāśamamalaṃ dṛśyamāno dvijottamaiḥ .
gate cādarśanaṃ deve snātvābhyukṣya samantataḥ .. 211.8 ..
6.3.d:
जगामाकाशममलं दृश्यमानो द्विजोत्तमैः .
गते चादर्शनं देवे स्नात्वाभ्युक्ष्य समन्ततः .. 211.8 ..
6.3.m: went into the clear sky, being watched by the best of the twice-born. / When the god had vanished from sight, having bathed and sprinkled [water] all around,

6.3.s:
bhuñjate'sma dvijā rājanyāvatpātre pṛthakpṛthak .
yatrayatra ca paśyanti tatratatra kṛmirbahuḥ .. 211.9 ..
6.3.d:
भुञ्जतेऽस्म द्विजा राजन्यावत्पात्रे पृथक्पृथक् .
यत्रयत्र च पश्यन्ति तत्रतत्र कृमिर्बहुः .. 211.9 ..
6.3.m: as the twice-born ate, O king, each in his own dish, / wherever they looked, there were many worms.

6.3.s:
dṛṣṭvā vismayamāpannāḥ sarve kimiti cābruvan .
tataḥ kaściduvācedaṃ brāhmaṇo guṇavānajaḥ .. 211.10 ..
6.3.d:
दृष्ट्वा विस्मयमापन्नाः सर्वे किमिति चाब्रुवन् .
ततः कश्चिदुवाचेदं ब्राह्मणो गुणवानजः .. 211.10 ..
6.3.m: Having seen that, they fell into astonishment, and all said, 'What is this?' / Then a certain brahmin, virtuous and unswerving, said this: 211.10

6.3.s:
yogīndraḥ śaṅkayā tatra bahuviprasamāgame .
yo'tra pūrvaṃ samāyātaḥ sa yogī parameśvaraḥ .. 211.11 ..
6.3.d:
योगीन्द्रः शङ्कया तत्र बहुविप्रसमागमे .
योऽत्र पूर्वं समायातः स योगी परमेश्वरः .. 211.11 ..
6.3.m: "With hesitation regarding the king of yogins in that great assembly of brahmins, / He who came here previously, that yogin is the Supreme Lord.

6.3.s:
tasyedaṃ krīḍitaṃ manye bhartsitasya vipākajam .
phalaṃ bhavati nānyasya hyatitheḥ śāstraniścayāt .. 211.12 ..
6.3.d:
तस्येदं क्रीडितं मन्ये भर्त्सितस्य विपाकजम् .
फलं भवति नान्यस्य ह्यतिथेः शास्त्रनिश्चयात् .. 211.12 ..
6.3.m: I think this is his sport, born of the ripening of his scolding; / the fruit comes from no other than a guest, according to the certainty of scripture.

6.3.s:
sampūjya paramātmā vai hyatithiśca viśeṣataḥ .
śrāddhakāle tu samprāptamatithiṃ yo na pūjayet .. 211.13 ..
6.3.d:
सम्पूज्य परमात्मा वै ह्यतिथिश्च विशेषतः .
श्राद्धकाले तु सम्प्राप्तमतिथिं यो न पूजयेत् .. 211.13 ..
6.3.m: The Supreme Self is truly worthy of worship, and especially a guest; / but whoever does not worship a guest who has arrived at the time of a śrāddha,

6.3.s:
piśācā rākṣasāstasya tadvilumpantyasaṃśayam .
rūpānvitaṃ virūpaṃ vā malinaṃ malināmbaram .. 211.14 ..
6.3.d:
पिशाचा राक्षसास्तस्य तद्विलुम्पन्त्यसंशयम् .
रूपान्वितं विरूपं वा मलिनं मलिनाम्बरम् .. 211.14 ..
6.3.m: Piśācas and Rākṣasas undoubtedly snatch away his [merit]. / Whether handsome or deformed, filthy or wearing soiled garments,

6.3.s:
yogīndraṃ śvapacaṃ vāpi atithiṃ na vicārayet .
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya yajamānapurogamāḥ .. 211.15 ..
6.3.d:
योगीन्द्रं श्वपचं वापि अतिथिं न विचारयेत् .
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य यजमानपुरोगमाः .. 211.15 ..
6.3.m: Whether a lord of yogins or an outcaste, one should not scrutinize a guest." / Having heard his word, led by the patron of the sacrifice,

6.3.s:
brāhmaṇā dvijamanveṣṭuṃ dhāvitāḥ sarvatodiśam .
tāvatkathaṃcitkenāpi gahanaṃ vanamāśritaḥ .. 211.16 ..
6.3.d:
ब्राह्मणा द्विजमन्वेष्टुं धाविताः सर्वतोदिशम् .
तावत्कथंचित्केनापि गहनं वनमाश्रितः .. 211.16 ..
6.3.m: The brahmins ran in all directions to search for the twice-born man. / Meanwhile, somehow, by someone, he who had entered the deep forest

6.3.s:
dṛṣṭo dṛṣṭa iti proktaṃ tena te sarva āgatāḥ .
tataḥ paśyanti taṃ vipraṃ sthāṇuvanniścalaṃ sthitam .. 211.17 ..
6.3.d:
दृष्टो दृष्ट इति प्रोक्तं तेन ते सर्व आगताः .
ततः पश्यन्ति तं विप्रं स्थाणुवन्निश्चलं स्थितम् .. 211.17 ..
6.3.m: Was seen, and "Seen, seen!" was shouted; by that [shout] they all arrived. / Then they beheld that brahmin standing motionless like a post.

6.3.s:
krandate na calati spandate na ca paśyati .
jalpanti karuṇaṃ kecitstuvanti ca tathāpare .. 211.18 ..
6.3.d:
क्रन्दते न चलति स्पन्दते न च पश्यति .
जल्पन्ति करुणं केचित्स्तुवन्ति च तथापरे .. 211.18 ..
6.3.m: He did not weep, he did not move, he did not twitch, nor did he look. / Some spoke piteously, and others praised [him] likewise.

6.3.s:
vāgbhiḥ satatamiṣṭābhiḥ stūyamānastrilocanaḥ .
kṣudhārditānāṃ deveśa brāhmaṇānāṃ viśeṣataḥ .
vinaṣṭamannaṃ sarveṣāṃ punaḥ saṃkartumarhasi .. 211.19 ..
6.3.d:
वाग्भिः सततमिष्टाभिः स्तूयमानस्त्रिलोचनः .
क्षुधार्दितानां देवेश ब्राह्मणानां विशेषतः .
विनष्टमन्नं सर्वेषां पुनः संकर्तुमर्हसि .. 211.19 ..
6.3.m: Being constantly praised with pleasing words, the Three-eyed One [was addressed]: / "O Lord of gods, especially for the brahmins afflicted by hunger, / whose food is all ruined, you ought to restore it."

6.3.s:
śrutvā tu vacanaṃ teṣāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ yudhiṣṭhira .
parayā kṛpayā devaḥ prasannastānuvāca ha .. 211.20 ..
6.3.d:
श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तेषां ब्राह्मणानां युधिष्ठिर .
परया कृपया देवः प्रसन्नस्तानुवाच ह .. 211.20 ..
6.3.m: Having heard the words of those brahmins, O Yudhiṣṭhira, / the god, pleased through supreme compassion, spoke to them indeed:

6.3.s:
mayā prasannena mahānubhāvāstadeva vo'nnaṃ vihitaṃ sudheva .
bhuñjantu viprāḥ saha bandhubhṛtyairarcantu nityaṃ mama maṇḍalaṃ ca .. 211.21 ..
6.3.d:
मया प्रसन्नेन महानुभावास्तदेव वोऽन्नं विहितं सुधेव .
भुञ्जन्तु विप्राः सह बन्धुभृत्यैरर्चन्तु नित्यं मम मण्डलं च .. 211.21 ..
6.3.m: "O noble ones, by me, being pleased, that very food of yours has been turned into nectar; / let the brahmins eat together with kinsmen and servants, and let them constantly worship my maṇḍala."

6.3.s:
tataścāyatanaṃ pārtha devadevasya śūlinaḥ .
muṇḍināmeti vikhyātaṃ sarvapāpaharaṃ śubham .
kārttikyāṃ tu viśeṣeṇa gayātīrthena tatsamam .. 211.22 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe muṇḍitīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmaikādaśottaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
6.3.d:
ततश्चायतनं पार्थ देवदेवस्य शूलिनः .
मुण्डिनामेति विख्यातं सर्वपापहरं शुभम् .
कार्त्तिक्यां तु विशेषेण गयातीर्थेन तत्समम् .. 211.22 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे मुण्डितीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामैकादशोत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः ..
6.3.m:
Thence arose the auspicious abode of the trident-bearing God of gods, / renowned as Muṇḍin, which removes all sins, / especially on the full-moon day of Kārttika, equal to the sacred ford of Gayā.
Thus ends the two hundred and eleventh chapter, entitled "Description of the māhātmya of Muṇḍitīrtha," in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth book, Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
athānyatsampravakṣyāmi devasya caritaṃ mahat .
śrutamātreṇa yenāśu sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate .. 212.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
अथान्यत्सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि देवस्य चरितं महत् .
श्रुतमात्रेण येनाशु सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते .. 212.1 ..
6.3.m: Glorious Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Now I shall tell another great deed of the god, / by the mere hearing of which one is quickly freed from all sins.

6.3.s:
bhikṣurūpaṃ paraṃ kṛtvā devadevo maheśvaraḥ .
ekaśālāṃ gato grāmaṃ bhikṣārthī kṣutpipāsitaḥ .. 212.2 ..
6.3.d:
भिक्षुरूपं परं कृत्वा देवदेवो महेश्वरः .
एकशालां गतो ग्रामं भिक्षार्थी क्षुत्पिपासितः .. 212.2 ..
6.3.m: Having assumed the supreme form of a mendicant, the God of gods, Maheśvara, / went to the village of Ekaśālā seeking alms, hungry and thirsty,

6.3.s:
akṣasūtrodyatakaro bhasmaguṇṭhitavigrahaḥ .
sphurattriśūlo viśveśo jaṭākuṇḍalabhūṣitaḥ .. 212.3 ..
6.3.d:
अक्षसूत्रोद्यतकरो भस्मगुण्ठितविग्रहः .
स्फुरत्त्रिशूलो विश्वेशो जटाकुण्डलभूषितः .. 212.3 ..
6.3.m: With an akṣa rosary raised in his hand, his body smeared with ashes, / his trident gleaming, the Lord of the universe, adorned with matted locks and ear-rings,

6.3.s:
kṛttivāsā mahākāyo mahāhikṛtabhūṣaṇaḥ .
vādayanvai ḍamarukaṃ ḍiṇḍimapratimaṃ śubham .. 212.4 ..
6.3.d:
कृत्तिवासा महाकायो महाहिकृतभूषणः .
वादयन्वै डमरुकं डिण्डिमप्रतिमं शुभम् .. 212.4 ..
6.3.m: Clad in an animal hide, of immense body, adorned with great serpents, / playing a small ḍamaru drum resembling a splendid ḍiṇḍima,

6.3.s:
kapālapāṇirbhagavānbālakairbahubhirvṛtaḥ .
kvacidgāyanhasaṃścaiva nṛtyanvadan kvacitkvacit .. 212.5 ..
6.3.d:
कपालपाणिर्भगवान्बालकैर्बहुभिर्वृतः .
क्वचिद्गायन्हसंश्चैव नृत्यन्वदन् क्वचित्क्वचित् .. 212.5 ..
6.3.m: The Lord with a skull in hand, surrounded by many boys, / singing somewhere, and laughing, dancing and speaking here and there.

6.3.s:
yatra yatra gṛhe devo līlayā ḍiṇḍamaṃ nyaset .
bhārākrāntaṃ gṛhaṃ pārtha tatratatra vinaśyati .. 212.6 ..
6.3.d:
यत्र यत्र गृहे देवो लीलया डिण्डमं न्यसेत् .
भाराक्रान्तं गृहं पार्थ तत्रतत्र विनश्यति .. 212.6 ..
6.3.m: In whatever house the god playfully placed the ḍiṇḍima drum, / that house, O Pārtha, overwhelmed by weight, perished right there.

6.3.s:
evaṃ sampracaran devo veṣṭito bahubhirjanaiḥ .
dṛśyādṛśyena rūpeṇa nirjagāma bahiḥ prabhuḥ .. 212.7 ..
6.3.d:
एवं सम्प्रचरन् देवो वेष्टितो बहुभिर्जनैः .
दृश्यादृश्येन रूपेण निर्जगाम बहिः प्रभुः .. 212.7 ..
6.3.m: Wandering thus, the god, surrounded by many people, / in a visible and invisible form, the Lord went outside.

6.3.s:
itaścetaśca dhāvantaṃ na paśyanti yadā janāḥ .
vismitāste sthitāḥ śambhurbhaviṣyati tato'stuvan .. 212.8 ..
6.3.d:
इतश्चेतश्च धावन्तं न पश्यन्ति यदा जनाः .
विस्मितास्ते स्थिताः शम्भुर्भविष्यति ततोऽस्तुवन् .. 212.8 ..
6.3.m: When the people did not see him running here and there, / they stood astonished, and thinking, "It must be Śambhu," they praised him.

6.3.s:
teṣāṃ tu stuvatāṃ bhaktyā śaṅkaraṃ jagatāṃ patim .
ḍiṇḍirūpo hi bhagavāṃstadāsau pratyadṛśyata .. 212.9 ..
6.3.d:
तेषां तु स्तुवतां भक्त्या शङ्करं जगतां पतिम् .
डिण्डिरूपो हि भगवांस्तदासौ प्रत्यदृश्यत .. 212.9 ..
6.3.m: While they were praising Śaṃkara, the Lord of the worlds, with devotion, / the Lord then became visible to them in the form of a ḍiṇḍi.

6.3.s:
tadāprabhṛti deveśo ḍiṇḍimeśvara ucyate .
darśanātsparśanādrājan sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate .. 212.10 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe ekaśālaḍiṇḍimeśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma dvādaśottaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
6.3.d:
तदाप्रभृति देवेशो डिण्डिमेश्वर उच्यते .
दर्शनात्स्पर्शनाद्राजन् सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते .. 212.10 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे एकशालडिण्डिमेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम द्वादशोत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः ..
6.3.m:
From then on the Lord of gods is called Ḍiṇḍimeśvara; / by seeing and touching him, O King, one is freed from all sins.
Thus ends the two hundred and twelfth chapter, entitled "Description of the māhātmya of Ekaśāla-Ḍiṇḍimeśvaratīrtha," in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth book, Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
punaranyatpravakṣyāmi devasya caritaṃ mahat .
śrutamātreṇa yenaiva sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate .. 213.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
पुनरन्यत्प्रवक्ष्यामि देवस्य चरितं महत् .
श्रुतमात्रेण येनैव सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते .. 213.1 ..
6.3.m: Glorious Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Again I shall tell another great deed of the god, / by the mere hearing of which one is freed from all sins.

6.3.s:
abālo bālarūpeṇa grāmaṇyairbālakaiḥ saha .
āmalaiḥ krīḍate śambhustatte vakṣyāmi bhārata .. 213.2 ..
6.3.d:
अबालो बालरूपेण ग्रामण्यैर्बालकैः सह .
आमलैः क्रीडते शम्भुस्तत्ते वक्ष्यामि भारत .. 213.2 ..
6.3.m: Though not a child, in the form of a child, along with prominent boys, / Śambhu played with myrobalan fruits; that I shall tell you, O Bhārata.

6.3.s:
sarvaistairāmalāḥ kṣiptā ye te devena pāṇḍava .
ānītāstatkṣaṇādeva tataḥ paścātkṣipeddharaḥ .. 213.3 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वैस्तैरामलाः क्षिप्ता ये ते देवेन पाण्डव .
आनीतास्तत्क्षणादेव ततः पश्चात्क्षिपेद्धरः .. 213.3 ..
6.3.m: Those myrobalan fruits thrown by all of them, O Pāṇḍava, / were brought back at that very instant by the god; then afterwards Hara threw them.

6.3.s:
yāvadgatvā diśo digbhya āgacchanti pṛthakpṛthak .
tāvattamāmalaṃ bhūtaṃ paśyanti parameśvaram .. 213.4 ..
6.3.d:
यावद्गत्वा दिशो दिग्भ्य आगच्छन्ति पृथक्पृथक् .
तावत्तमामलं भूतं पश्यन्ति परमेश्वरम् .. 213.4 ..
6.3.m: As soon as they went off and returned individually from the various directions, / so soon did they see that Supreme Lord turned into a myrobalan fruit.

6.3.s:
tṛtīye caiva yatkarma devadevasya dhīmataḥ .
sthānānāṃ paramaṃ sthānamāmaleśvaramuttamam .. 213.5 ..
6.3.d:
तृतीये चैव यत्कर्म देवदेवस्य धीमतः .
स्थानानां परमं स्थानमामलेश्वरमुत्तमम् .. 213.5 ..
6.3.m: And as for the third deed of the wise God of gods, / supreme among places is the excellent Āmaleśvara.

6.3.s:
tena pūjitamātreṇa prāpyate paramaṃ padam .. 213.6 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe āmaleśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma trayodaśottaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
6.3.d:
तेन पूजितमात्रेण प्राप्यते परमं पदम् .. 213.6 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे आमलेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम त्रयोदशोत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः ..
6.3.m:
By merely worshipping there, the supreme abode is attained.
Thus ends the two hundred and thirteenth chapter, entitled "Description of the māhātmya of Āmaleśvaratīrtha," in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth book, Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
caturthaṃ sampravakṣyāmi devasya caritaṃ mahat .
śrutamātreṇa yenaiva sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate .. 214.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
चतुर्थं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि देवस्य चरितं महत् .
श्रुतमात्रेण येनैव सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते .. 214.1 ..
6.3.m: Glorious Mārkaṇḍeya said: / I shall tell the fourth great deed of the god, / by the mere hearing of which one is freed from all sins:

6.3.s:
kapālī kānthiko bhūtvā yathā sa vyacaranmahīm .
piśācairrākṣasairbhūtairḍākinīyoginīvṛtaḥ .. 214.2 ..
6.3.d:
कपाली कान्थिको भूत्वा यथा स व्यचरन्महीम् .
पिशाचैर्राक्षसैर्भूतैर्डाकिनीयोगिनीवृतः .. 214.2 ..
6.3.m: How, carrying a skull and wearing rags, he wandered the earth, / surrounded by Piśācas, Rākṣasas, Bhūtas, Ḍākinīs, and Yoginīs,

6.3.s:
bhairavaṃ rūpamāsthāya pretāsanaparigrahaḥ .
trailokyasyābhayaṃ dattvā cacāra vipulaṃ tapaḥ .. 214.3 ..
6.3.d:
भैरवं रूपमास्थाय प्रेतासनपरिग्रहः .
त्रैलोक्यस्याभयं दत्त्वा चचार विपुलं तपः .. 214.3 ..
6.3.m: Assuming a terrifying form, taking corpses as his seat, / granting fearlessness to the three worlds, he performed vast austerity.

6.3.s:
āṣāḍhī tu kṛtā tatra hyāṣāḍhīnāma viśrutam .
kanthā muktā tato'nyatra devena parameṣṭhinā .. 214.4 ..
6.3.d:
आषाढी तु कृता तत्र ह्याषाढीनाम विश्रुतम् .
कन्था मुक्ता ततोऽन्यत्र देवेन परमेष्ठिना .. 214.4 ..
6.3.m: A staff called āṣāḍhī was made there, renowned indeed as Āṣāḍhī; / then the patched garment was left elsewhere by the god, the Supreme Lord.

6.3.s:
tadāprabhṛti rājendra sa kantheśvara ucyate .
tasya darśanamātreṇa hyaśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet .. 214.5 ..
6.3.d:
तदाप्रभृति राजेन्द्र स कन्थेश्वर उच्यते .
तस्य दर्शनमात्रेण ह्यश्वमेधफलं लभेत् .. 214.5 ..
6.3.m: From then on, O best of kings, he is called Kantheśvara; / by merely seeing him, one obtains the fruit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice.

6.3.s:
devo mārge punastatra bhramate ca yadṛcchayā .
vikrīṇāti balākāro dṛṣṭvā cokto hareṇa tu .. 214.6 ..
6.3.d:
देवो मार्गे पुनस्तत्र भ्रमते च यदृच्छया .
विक्रीणाति बलाकारो दृष्ट्वा चोक्तो हरेण तु .. 214.6 ..
6.3.m: Then on the road the god wandered at will; / a bangle-maker was selling, and upon seeing him, he was addressed by Hara:

6.3.s:
yadi bhadra na cetkopaṃ karoṣi mayi sāmpratam .
balābhirbhara me liṅgaṃ dadāmi bahu te dhanam .. 214.7 ..
6.3.d:
यदि भद्र न चेत्कोपं करोषि मयि साम्प्रतम् .
बलाभिर्भर मे लिङ्गं ददामि बहु ते धनम् .. 214.7 ..
6.3.m: "Good sir, if you do not get angry with me now, / fill my liṅga with bangles; I will give you much wealth."

6.3.s:
evamukto'tha devena sa vaṇiglobhamohitaḥ .
yojayāmāsa balakā liṅge cottamamadhyamān .. 214.8 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्तोऽथ देवेन स वणिग्लोभमोहितः .
योजयामास बलका लिङ्गे चोत्तममध्यमान् .. 214.8 ..
6.3.m: Thus addressed by the god, that merchant, deluded by greed, / applied bangles—best and middling—upon the liṅga,

6.3.s:
tāvadyāvatkṣayaṃ sarve gatāḥ kāle susaṃcitāḥ .
sthitaṃ samunnataṃ liṅgaṃ dṛṣṭvā śokamupāgamat .. 214.9 ..
6.3.d:
तावद्यावत्क्षयं सर्वे गताः काले सुसंचिताः .
स्थितं समुन्नतं लिङ्गं दृष्ट्वा शोकमुपागमत् .. 214.9 ..
6.3.m: Until in due course all those well-collected [bangles] were exhausted. / Seeing the liṅga still standing lofty, he fell into sorrow.

6.3.s:
kṛtvā tu khaṇḍakhaṇḍāni sa devaḥ parameśvaraḥ .
uvāca prahasanvākyaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā gatasādhvasam .. 214.10 ..
6.3.d:
कृत्वा तु खण्डखण्डानि स देवः परमेश्वरः .
उवाच प्रहसन्वाक्यं तं दृष्ट्वा गतसाध्वसम् .. 214.10 ..
6.3.m: Having broken them into pieces, the Lord, the supreme Īśvara, / seeing that his fear had departed, laughed and said these words:

6.3.s:
na ca me pūritaṃ liṅgaṃ yāsyāmi yadi manyase .
dadāmi tatra vittaṃ te yadi liṅgaṃ prapūritam .. 214.11 ..
6.3.d:
न च मे पूरितं लिङ्गं यास्यामि यदि मन्यसे .
ददामि तत्र वित्तं ते यदि लिङ्गं प्रपूरितम् .. 214.11 ..
6.3.m: "My liṅga has not been filled; I shall depart if you agree. / I will give you wealth there if the liṅga is fully filled."

6.3.s:
vaṇiguvāca -
adhanyaḥ kṛtapuṇyo'haṃ nigrāhyaḥ parameśvara .
tava priyamakurvāṇaḥ śociṣye śāśvatīḥ samāḥ .. 214.12 ..
6.3.d:
वणिगुवाच -
अधन्यः कृतपुण्योऽहं निग्राह्यः परमेश्वर .
तव प्रियमकुर्वाणः शोचिष्ये शाश्वतीः समाः .. 214.12 ..
6.3.m: The merchant said: / "I am unfortunate, having accumulated merit; yet I deserve punishment, O supreme Īśvara, / since, not doing what pleases you, I shall grieve for perpetual years."

6.3.s:
etacchrutvā vacastasya vaṇikputrasya bhārata .
asaṃkṣayaṃ dhanaṃ dattvā sthitastatra maheśvaraḥ .. 214.13 ..
6.3.d:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य वणिक्पुत्रस्य भारत .
असंक्षयं धनं दत्त्वा स्थितस्तत्र महेश्वरः .. 214.13 ..
6.3.m: Hearing these words of that merchant's son, O descendant of Bharata, / Maheśvara gave him inexhaustible wealth and remained right there.

6.3.s:
tadā prabhṛti rājendra balākairiva bhūṣitam .
pratyayārthaṃ sthitaṃ liṅgaṃ lokānugrahakāmyayā .. 214.14 ..
6.3.d:
तदा प्रभृति राजेन्द्र बलाकैरिव भूषितम् .
प्रत्ययार्थं स्थितं लिङ्गं लोकानुग्रहकाम्यया .. 214.14 ..
6.3.m: From then on, O best of kings, as if adorned with cranes, / the liṅga remained there to inspire faith, out of a desire to show grace to the world.

6.3.s:
devena racitaṃ pārtha krīḍayā supratiṣṭhitam .
devamārgamiti khyātaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam .
paśyan prapūjayan vāpi sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate .. 214.15 ..
6.3.d:
देवेन रचितं पार्थ क्रीडया सुप्रतिष्ठितम् .
देवमार्गमिति ख्यातं त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतम् .
पश्यन् प्रपूजयन् वापि सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते .. 214.15 ..
6.3.m: Fashioned in play by the god, O son of Pṛthā, and well-established, / it is known as Devamārga, celebrated in the three worlds. / Beholding it or worshipping it, one is freed from all sins.

6.3.s:
devamārge tu yo gatvā pūjayedbalākeśvaram .
pañcāyatanamāsādya rudralokaṃ sa gacchati .. 214.16 ..
6.3.d:
देवमार्गे तु यो गत्वा पूजयेद्बलाकेश्वरम् .
पञ्चायतनमासाद्य रुद्रलोकं स गच्छति .. 214.16 ..
6.3.m: Going to Devamārga, whoever worships Balākeśvara / and reaches the fivefold shrine goes to the realm of Rudra.

6.3.s:
devamārge mṛtānāṃ tu narāṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām .
na bhavetpunarāvṛttī rudralokātkadācana .. 214.17 ..
6.3.d:
देवमार्गे मृतानां तु नराणां भावितात्मनाम् .
न भवेत्पुनरावृत्ती रुद्रलोकात्कदाचन .. 214.17 ..
6.3.m: For self-purified men who die at Devamārga, / there will never be a return from the realm of Rudra.

6.3.s:
devamārgasya māhātmyaṃ bhaktyā śrutvā narottama .
mucyate sarvapāpebhyo nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 214.18 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe śrīkapālatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma caturdaśottaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
6.3.d:
देवमार्गस्य माहात्म्यं भक्त्या श्रुत्वा नरोत्तम .
मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो नात्र कार्या विचारणा .. 214.18 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे श्रीकपालतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम चतुर्दशोत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः ..
6.3.m:
Having heard with devotion the māhātmya of Devamārga, O best of men, / one is freed from all sins; no doubt should be entertained on this point.
Thus ends the two hundred and fourteenth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Glory of the Sacred Kapālatīrtha,' in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
śṛṅgitīrthaṃ tato gacchenmokṣadaṃ sarvadehinām .
mṛtānāṃ tatra rājendra mokṣaprāptirna saṃśayaḥ .. 215.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
शृङ्गितीर्थं ततो गच्छेन्मोक्षदं सर्वदेहिनाम् .
मृतानां तत्र राजेन्द्र मोक्षप्राप्तिर्न संशयः .. 215.1 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Next, one should proceed to Śṛṅgitīrtha, which grants liberation to all embodied beings. / For those who die there, O best of kings, the attainment of liberation is without doubt.

6.3.s:
tatraiva piṇḍadānena pitṝṇāmanṛṇo bhavet .
tena puṇyena pūtātmā labhedgāṇeśvarīṃ gatim .. 215.2 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe śṛṅgitīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma pañcadaśottaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
6.3.d:
तत्रैव पिण्डदानेन पितॄणामनृणो भवेत् .
तेन पुण्येन पूतात्मा लभेद्गाणेश्वरीं गतिम् .. 215.2 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे शृङ्गितीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम पञ्चदशोत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः ..
6.3.m:
By offering balls of rice right there, one becomes free from debt to the ancestors. / Purified in soul by that merit, one attains the state of a lord of Gaṇas.
Thus ends the two hundred and fifteenth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Glory of Śṛṅgitīrtha,' in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
aṣāḍhītīrthamāgacchettato bhūpālanandana .
kāmikaṃ rūpamāsthāya sthito yatra maheśvaraḥ .. 216.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
अषाढीतीर्थमागच्छेत्ततो भूपालनन्दन .
कामिकं रूपमास्थाय स्थितो यत्र महेश्वरः .. 216.1 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Next, O delight of kings, one should go to Aṣāḍhītīrtha, / where Maheśvara took up a form according to his wish and remained.

6.3.s:
cāturyugamidaṃ tīrthaṃ sarvatīrtheṣvanuttamam .
tatra snātvā naro rājan rudrasyānucaro bhavet .. 216.2 ..
6.3.d:
चातुर्युगमिदं तीर्थं सर्वतीर्थेष्वनुत्तमम् .
तत्र स्नात्वा नरो राजन् रुद्रस्यानुचरो भवेत् .. 216.2 ..
6.3.m: This sacred ford exists in all four yugas and is unsurpassed among all sacred fords. / Having bathed there, O king, a man becomes an attendant of Rudra.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yaḥ kaścitkurute prāṇamokṣaṇam .
anivartikā gatistasya rudralokādasaṃśayam .. 216.3 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe aṣāḍhītīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma ṣoḍaśottaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यः कश्चित्कुरुते प्राणमोक्षणम् .
अनिवर्तिका गतिस्तस्य रुद्रलोकादसंशयम् .. 216.3 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे अषाढीतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम षोडशोत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः ..
6.3.m:
Whoever abandons his life's breath at that sacred ford / attains a state from which there is no return from the realm of Rudra, without doubt.
Thus ends the two hundred and sixteenth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Glory of Aṣāḍhītīrtha,' in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
eraṇḍīsaṅgamaṃ gacchetsurāsuranamaskṛtam .
tattu tīrthaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ mahāpātakanāśanam .. 217.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
एरण्डीसङ्गमं गच्छेत्सुरासुरनमस्कृतम् .
तत्तु तीर्थं महापुण्यं महापातकनाशनम् .. 217.1 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / One should go to the confluence of Eraṇḍī, which is revered by gods and demons. / That sacred ford is exceedingly meritorious, destroying great sins.

6.3.s:
upavāsaparo bhūtvā niyatendriyamānasaḥ .
tatra snātvā vidhānena mucyate brahmahatyayā .. 217.2 ..
6.3.d:
उपवासपरो भूत्वा नियतेन्द्रियमानसः .
तत्र स्नात्वा विधानेन मुच्यते ब्रह्महत्यया .. 217.2 ..
6.3.m: Devoted to fasting, with mind and senses restrained, / bathing there according to rule, one is freed from the murder of a brahmin.

6.3.s:
tatra tīrthe tu yo bhaktyā prāṇatyāgaparo bhavet .
anivartikā gatistasya rudralokādasaṃśayam .. 217.3 ..
.. iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe eraṇḍītīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma saptadaśottaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..
6.3.d:
तत्र तीर्थे तु यो भक्त्या प्राणत्यागपरो भवेत् .
अनिवर्तिका गतिस्तस्य रुद्रलोकादसंशयम् .. 217.3 ..
.. इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे एरण्डीतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम सप्तदशोत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः ..
6.3.m:
Whoever with devotion gives up his life's breath at that sacred ford / attains a state from which there is no return from the realm of Rudra, without doubt.
Thus ends the two hundred and seventeenth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Glory of Eraṇḍītīrtha,' in the Revākhaṇḍa of the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
tato gaccheddharādhīśa tīrthaṃ paramaśobhanam .
jamadagniriti khyātaṃ yatra siddho janārdanaḥ .. 218.1 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
ततो गच्छेद्धराधीश तीर्थं परमशोभनम् .
जमदग्निरिति ख्यातं यत्र सिद्धो जनार्दनः .. 218.1 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Then, O lord of the earth, one should go to the exceedingly auspicious sacred ford / known as Jamadagni, where Janārdana attained perfection.

6.3.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca -
kathaṃ siddho dvijaśreṣṭha vāsudevo jagadguruḥ .
mānuṣaṃ rūpamāsthāya lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā .. 218.2 ..
6.3.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच -
कथं सिद्धो द्विजश्रेष्ठ वासुदेवो जगद्गुरुः .
मानुषं रूपमास्थाय लोकानां हितकाम्यया .. 218.2 ..
6.3.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / How did Vāsudeva, the teacher of the world, having assumed a human form / out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds, attain perfection, O best of the twice-born?

6.3.s:
etatsarvaṃ yathānyāyaṃ devadevasya cakriṇaḥ .
caritaṃ śrotumicchāmi kathyamānaṃ tvayānagha .. 218.3 ..
6.3.d:
एतत्सर्वं यथान्यायं देवदेवस्य चक्रिणः .
चरितं श्रोतुमिच्छामि कथ्यमानं त्वयानघ .. 218.3 ..
6.3.m: I wish to hear this entire deed of the god of gods, the wielder of the discus, / narrated properly by you, O sinless one.

6.3.s:
śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca -
āsītpūrvaṃ mahārāja haihayādhipatirmahān .
kārtavīrya iti khyāto rājā bāhusahasravān .. 218.4 ..
6.3.d:
श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच -
आसीत्पूर्वं महाराज हैहयाधिपतिर्महान् .
कार्तवीर्य इति ख्यातो राजा बाहुसहस्रवान् .. 218.4 ..
6.3.m: The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Formerly, O great king, there was a great ruler of the Haihayas, / a king known as Kārtavīrya, possessing a thousand arms,

6.3.s:
hastyaśvarathasampannaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ .
vedavidyāvratasnātaḥ sarvabhūtābhayapradaḥ .. 218.5 ..
6.3.d:
हस्त्यश्वरथसम्पन्नः सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरः .
वेदविद्याव्रतस्नातः सर्वभूताभयप्रदः .. 218.5 ..
6.3.m: endowed with elephants, horses, and chariots, foremost among all bearers of weapons, / bathed at the completion of vows in Vedic learning, granting safety to all beings,

6.3.s:
māhiṣmatyāḥ patiḥ śrīmānrājā hyakṣauhiṇīpatiḥ .
sa kadācinmṛgānhantuṃ nirjagāma mahābalaḥ .. 218.6 ..
6.3.d:
माहिष्मत्याः पतिः श्रीमान्राजा ह्यक्षौहिणीपतिः .
स कदाचिन्मृगान्हन्तुं निर्जगाम महाबलः .. 218.6 ..
6.3.m: the glorious lord of Māhiṣmatī, a king commanding an akṣauhiṇī. / Once, that mighty one set forth to hunt deer.

6.3.s:
bahubhirdivasaiḥ prāpto bhṛgukacchamanuttamam .
jamadagnirmahātejā yatra tiṣṭhati tāpasaḥ .. 218.7 ..
6.3.d:
बहुभिर्दिवसैः प्राप्तो भृगुकच्छमनुत्तमम् .
जमदग्निर्महातेजा यत्र तिष्ठति तापसः .. 218.7 ..
6.3.m: After many days, he reached the unsurpassed Bhṛgukaccha, / where the ascetic Jamadagni of great fiery radiance resided,

6.3.s:
reṇukāsahitaḥ śrīmānsarvabhūtābhayapradaḥ .
tasya putro'bhavadrāmaḥ sākṣānnārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ .. 218.8 ..
6.3.d:
रेणुकासहितः श्रीमान्सर्वभूताभयप्रदः .
तस्य पुत्रोऽभवद्रामः साक्षान्नारायणः प्रभुः .. 218.8 ..
6.3.m: accompanied by Reṇukā, glorious, granting safety to all beings. / His son was Rāma, the Lord Nārāyaṇa manifest in person,

6.3.s:
sarvakṣatraguṇairyukto brahmavidbrāhmaṇottamaḥ .
toṣayanparayā bhaktyā pitarau paramārthavat .. 218.9 ..
6.3.d:
सर्वक्षत्रगुणैर्युक्तो ब्रह्मविद्ब्राह्मणोत्तमः .
तोषयन्परया भक्त्या पितरौ परमार्थवत् .. 218.9 ..
6.3.m: endowed with all the virtues of a kṣatriya, a knower of the absolute, the best of brahmins, / pleasing his parents with supreme devotion in accordance with the ultimate truth.

6.3.s:
taṃ tadā cārjunaṃ dṛṣṭvā jamadagniḥ pratāpavān .
carantaṃ mṛgayāṃ gatvā hyātithyena nyamantrayat .. 218.10 ..
6.3.d:
तं तदा चार्जुनं दृष्ट्वा जमदग्निः प्रतापवान् .
चरन्तं मृगयां गत्वा ह्यातिथ्येन न्यमन्त्रयत् .. 218.10 ..
6.3.m: Then, seeing that majestic Arjuna roaming about while hunting, / Jamadagni approached and invited him with hospitality.

6.3.s:
tatheti coktvā sa nṛpaḥ sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ .
jagāma cāśramaṃ puṇyamṛṣestasya mahātmanaḥ .. 218.11 ..
6.3.d:
तथेति चोक्त्वा स नृपः सभृत्यबलवाहनः .
जगाम चाश्रमं पुण्यमृषेस्तस्य महात्मनः .. 218.11 ..
6.3.m: Saying 'So be it,' that king, together with his servants, army, and mounts, / went to the sacred hermitage of that great-souled seer.

6.3.s:
tatkṣaṇādeva sampannaṃ śriyā paramayā vṛtam .
vismayaṃ paramaṃ tatra dṛṣṭvā rājā jagāma ha .. 218.12 ..
6.3.d:
तत्क्षणादेव सम्पन्नं श्रिया परमया वृतम् .
विस्मयं परमं तत्र दृष्ट्वा राजा जगाम ह .. 218.12 ..
6.3.m: At that very moment, it became abundant and filled with supreme splendor; / beholding that, the king was filled with utter astonishment.

6.3.s:
gatamātrastu siddhena paramānnena bhojitaḥ .
sabhṛtyabalavānrājā brāhmaṇena yadṛcchayā .
kimetaditi papraccha kāraṇaṃ śaktimeva ca .. 218.13 ..
6.3.d:
गतमात्रस्तु सिद्धेन परमान्नेन भोजितः .
सभृत्यबलवान्राजा ब्राह्मणेन यदृच्छया .
किमेतदिति पप्रच्छ कारणं शक्तिमेव च .. 218.13 ..
6.3.m: As soon as he arrived, the king, together with his servants and army, was fed with prepared / supreme food at will by the brahmin, / and he asked, "What is this? What is the cause and the power?"

6.3.s:
kāmadhenoḥ prabhāvaṃ taṃ jñātvā prāha tato dvijam .
dakṣiṇāṃ dehi me vipra kalmaṣāṃ dhenumuttamām .. 218.14 ..
6.3.d:
कामधेनोः प्रभावं तं ज्ञात्वा प्राह ततो द्विजम् .
दक्षिणां देहि मे विप्र कल्मषां धेनुमुत्तमाम् .. 218.14 ..
6.3.m: Recognizing the power of Kāmadhenu, he then said to the twice-born: / "O wise brahmin, give me the dakṣiṇā—the spotted, excellent cow.

6.3.s:
śataṃ śatasahasrāṇāmayutaṃ niyutaṃ param .
bhūṣitānāṃ ca dhenūnāṃ dadāmi tava cārbudam .. 218.15 ..
6.3.d:
शतं शतसहस्राणामयुतं नियुतं परम् .
भूषितानां च धेनूनां ददामि तव चार्बुदम् .. 218.15 ..
6.3.m: A hundred, a hundred thousand, ten thousand, a hundred thousand more, / and one hundred million adorned cows I will give to you."

6.3.s:
jamadagniruvāca -
ayutaiḥ prayutairnāhaṃ śatakoṭibhiruttamām .
kāmadhenumimāṃ tāta na dadmi pratigamyatām .. 218.16 ..
6.3.d:
जमदग्निरुवाच -
अयुतैः प्रयुतैर्नाहं शतकोटिभिरुत्तमाम् .
कामधेनुमिमां तात न दद्मि प्रतिगम्यताम् .. 218.16 ..
6.3.m: Jamadagni said: / "Not for tens of thousands, nor millions, nor hundreds of millions / do I give this excellent wish-granting cow, my friend. Return home."

6.3.s:
evamuktaḥ sa rājendrastena vipreṇa bhārata .
krodhasaṃraktanayana idaṃ vacanamabravīt .. 218.17 ..
6.3.d:
एवमुक्तः स राजेन्द्रस्तेन विप्रेण भारत .
क्रोधसंरक्तनयन इदं वचनमब्रवीत् .. 218.17 ..
6.3.m: Addressed thus by that twice-born, O best of kings, O descendant of Bharata, / his eyes red with anger, he spoke these words:

6.3.s:
yasyedṛśaḥ kāmacāro mayyapi dvijapāṃsana .
ahaṃ te paśyatastasmānnayāmi surabhiṃ gṛhāt .. 218.18 ..
6.3.d:
यस्येदृशः कामचारो मय्यपि द्विजपांसन .
अहं ते पश्यतस्तस्मान्नयामि सुरभिं गृहात् .. 218.18 ..
6.3.m: "Since you act so willfully even toward me, O disgrace of the twice-born, / I shall take the wish-granting cow from your house before your very eyes!"

6.3.s:
dvija uvāca -
kaḥ krīḍati saroṣeṇa nirbhayo hi mahāhinā .
mṛtyudṛṣṭotareṇāpi mama dhenuṃ nayeta yaḥ .. 218.19 ..
6.3.d:
द्विज उवाच -
कः क्रीडति सरोषेण निर्भयो हि महाहिना .
मृत्युदृष्टोतरेणापि मम धेनुं नयेत यः .. 218.19 ..
6.3.m:
The brahmin said:
